			Sagara has then chosen sixty thousand sons with great enthusiasm and 
			high reputation.

shloka:
प्रदक्षिणमृषिं कृत्वा शिरसाभिप्रणम्य च |
जगाम स्वपुरं राजा सभार्या रघुनन्दन
translation:
"On performing circumambulations to the Sage Bhrigu along with wives, 
			oh, Raghu's scion, also on reverencing him head-bent, the king Sagara 
			proceeded to his own city.

shloka:
अथ काले गते तस्मिन् ज्येष्ठा पुत्रं व्यजायत |
असमंज इति ख्यातं केशिनी सगरात्मजम्
translation:
When the time rolled by then the elder wife Keshini gave birth to the 
			son of Sagara who is reputed by the name Asamanja.

shloka:
सुमतिस्तु नरव्याघ्र गर्भतुंबं व्यजायत |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि तुंबभेदाद्विनिःसृताः
translation:
But the second queen Sumati on part, oh, tigerly-man Rama, verily 
			delivered a round and long egg which is like a single gourd, and on 
			breaking it up sixty thousand sons are issued forth from that cucumber 
			like egg.

shloka:
घृतपूर्णेषु कुंभेषु धात्र्यस्तान् समवर्धयन् |
कालेन महता सर्वे यौवनं प्रतिपेदिरे
translation:
The childminders brought up those siblings in vessels filled with ghee, 
			the clarified butter, and after a protracted time all of the children 
			have attained youthfulness.

shloka:
अथ दीर्घेण कालेन रूपयौवनशालिनः |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि सगरस्याभवंस्तदा
translation:
After a long time the sixty thousand sons of king Sagara have become 
			youthful, and handsome in their aspects.

shloka:
स च ज्येष्ठो नरश्रेष्ठ सगरस्यात्मसंभवः |
बालान् गृहीत्वा तु जले सरय्वा रघुनंदन
translation:
But, oh, best one among men, oh, Rama, the elder son of the king Sagara, 
			namely Asamanja, always used to grab and hurl children into the waters 
			of River Sarayu, and on seeing the drowning children he used to enjoy 
			with laughter. [1-38-20, 21a]

shloka: एवं पापसमाचारः सज्जनप्रतिबाधकः
translation:
This way, when that son Asamanja is with sinister activity, a torturer 
			of goodmen, and delighter in the undesirable activities towards citizens, 
			his father king Sagara expatriated him from the city. [1-38-21b, 22a]

shloka: तस्य पुत्रोंऽशुमान्नाम असमंजस्य वीर्यवान्
translation:
But Asamanja's son is a valorous one, who by name is Anshuman, and who 
			is an acceptable one for all people and who fondly converses with all. 
			[1-38 -22b, 23a]

shloka: ततः कालेन महता मतिः समभिजायत
translation:
"Oh, best one among men, Rama, then after along time a decided thought 
			has occurred to king Sagara that, 'I shall perform a Vedic-ritual.'[1-38-23b, 
			24a]

shloka:
स कृत्वा निश्चयं राजा सोपाध्यायगणस्तदा |
यज्ञकर्मणि वेदज्ञो यष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
translation:
That king Sagara who is an expert in Vedic-procedures has then taken 
			a decision along with the assemblages of his religious-teachers insofar 
			as the procedures of the ritual are concerned, and he commenced to perform 
			the Vedic-ritual. [1-38-24b, c]

shloka:
विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा कथान्ते रघुनंदन |
उवाच परमप्रीतो मुनिं दीप्तमिवानलम्
translation:
On listening the narration of Vishvamitra, Rama, the delighter of Raghu's 
			dynasty is highly rejoiced, and at the end of the episode he spoke to 
			sage whose glow is fire like.

shloka:
श्रोतुमिच्छामि भद्रं ते विस्तरेण कथामिमाम् |
पूर्वजो मे कथं ब्रह्मन् यज्ञं वै समुपाहरत्
translation:
I am interested to listen this episode exhaustively, oh, Brahman, let 
			good betide you, how my ancestor Sagara had completed the Vedic-ritual, 
			really.

shloka:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा कौतूहलसमन्वितः |
विश्वामित्रस्तु काकुत्स्थमुवाच प्रहसन्निव
translation:
On listening the words of Rama that are inclusive of his inquisitiveness, 
			Sage Vishvamitra smilingly spoke to that descendent of Kakutstha, "oh, 
			Rama, let the episode of the great-souled Sagara be listened vividly." 
			Vishvamitra thus commenced to narrate that episode. [1-39-3, 4a]

shloka: शंकरश्वशुरो नाम हिमवानिति विश्रुतः
translation:
The father-in-law of god Shankara who is well-known by the name of 
			Himavan sets eyes on Mt. Vindhya, which stands as loftily as Himalayas, 
			and those two mountains peer at each other. [1-39-4b, 5a]

shloka: तयोर्मध्ये प्रवृत्तोऽभूद्यज्ञः स पुरुषोत्तम
translation:
Oh, best one among men, Rama, that Vedic-ritual of Sagara started 
			in between those two mountains, namely Himalayas and Vindhya ranges, 
			and oh, tigerly-man Rama, that area is renowned for Vedic-rituals, isn't 
			it! [1-39-5b, 6a]

shloka: तस्याश्वचर्यां काकुत्स्थ दृढधन्वा महारथः
translation:
Oh, dear sire Rama, the grandson of Sagara and the son of exiled Asamanja 
			is Amshuman, oh, descendant of Kakutstha, which Anshuman's bow will 
			be unfaltering and who is a top-speeded chariot-rider, and he has escorted 
			ritual-horse released. [1-39-6b, 7a]

shloka: तस्य पर्वणि तं यज्ञं यजमानस्य वासवः
translation:
And on the day of a sacred function calledukthyam, Indra assumed the form of a demon and stole the ritual horse of the 
			chief of the ritual, namely Sagara. [1-39-7b, 8a]

shloka: ह्रियमाणे तु काकुत्स्थ तस्मिन्नश्वे महात्मनः
translation:
While that ritual-horse of the great-souled Sagara is stolen, all the 
			congregations of the Ritviks, the religious-teachers, then spoke to 
			the chief propitiator, namely Sagara. [1-39-8b, 9a]

shloka: अयं पर्वणि वेगेन यज्ञियाश्वोऽपनीयते
translation:
'Oh, Sagara,the descendent of Kakutstha, at this auspicious time the 
			ritual horse is hastily diverted, you kill him who stole the horse, 
			and let that horse be fetched'. [1-39-9b, 10a]

shloka: यज्ञश्च्छिद्रं भवत्येतत्सर्वेषामशिवाय नः
translation:
'This hindrance in Vedic-ritual will become inauspicious for all of 
			us, thereby, oh, king, action may be taken as to how there can be no 
			fault in proceedings of the ritual.' The religious-teachers of Sagara 
			have advised him in this way. [1-39-10b, 11a]

shloka: सोऽपाध्यायवचः श्रुत्वा तस्मिन्सदसि पार्थिवः
translation:
On hearing the words of religious-teachers that king Sagara indeed 
			spoke this much to his sixty thousand sons in that religious-council. 
			[1-39-11b, 12a]

shloka: गतिं पुत्रा न पश्यामि रक्षसां पुरुषर्षभाः
translation:
'Oh, sons, I do not envisage any way in for demons into this ritual, 
			since oh, best ones among men, holy-sanctifiers who themselves are sanctified 
			by the Vedic-hymns are conducting this glorious Vedic-ritual, isn't 
			it. [1-39-12b, 13a]

shloka: तद्गच्छत विचिन्वध्वं पुत्रका भद्रमस्तु वः
translation:
'Oh, sons, you may therefore proceed to search for the horse and its 
			thief on entire earth as far as it is garlanded by the ocean, and safety 
			betides you all.

shloka: एकैकं योजनं पुत्रा विस्तारमभिगच्छत
translation:
'Oh, sons, let each prince advance searching one square yojana of 
			earth, by my order you dig up the earth until the appearance of the 
			horse, while searching for the stealer of that horse. [1-39-14b, 15]

shloka:
दीक्षितः पौत्रसहितः सोपाध्यायगणस्त्वहम् |
इह स्थास्यामि भद्रं वो यावत्तुरगदर्शनम्
translation:
'As for myself, I will stay here only along with my grandson, namely 
			Amshuman, and with the congregation of religious-teachers till the horse 
			appears, as I am under vow of the ritual.' Thus Sagara instructed to 
			his sixty thousand sons and stayed back at the ritual place.

shloka:
ते सर्वे हृष्टमनसो राजपुत्रा महाबलाः |
जग्मुर्महीतलं राम पितुर्वचनयंत्रिताः
translation:
Animated by their father's words those great-mighty princes enthusiastically 
			proceeded onto earth's surface in the preliminary round of search.

shloka:
गत्वा तु पृथिवीं सर्वमदृष्टा तं महबलाः |
योजनायामविस्तारमेकैको धरणीतलम् |
बिभिदुः पुरुषव्याघ्र वज्रस्पर्शसमैर्भुजैः
translation:
But, oh, tigerly-man Rama, on going round the earth in its entirety 
			those great-mighty princes did not find that horse, then as said by 
			their father they mapped the earth to a unit of one square yojana for 
			each of them, and each of them hollowed out each and every area on the 
			surface of earth with their arms that have the touch of the diamonds.

shloka:
शूलैरशनिकल्पैश्च हलैश्चापि सुदारुणैः |
भिद्यमाना वसुमती ननाद रघुनंदन
translation:
Mother Earth bewailed while she is ruptured with spears also that are 
			similar to thunderbolts, besides with very gruelling ploughs.

shloka:
नागानां वध्यमानानामसुराणां च राघव |
राक्षसानां च दुर्धर्षः सत्त्वानां निनदोऽभवत्
translation:
Oh, Raghava, there emerged an unbearable rumpus from the serpents, 
			asura-s, demons, and other beings living underneath the surface of earth, 
			while they are killed during hollowing the earth.

shloka:
योजनानां सहस्राणि षष्टिं तु रघुनंदन |
बिभिदुर्धरणीं राम रसातलमनुत्तमम्
translation:
Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu's dynasty, thus sixty thousand square 
			yojana-s of the earth is dug over, so as to make the earth's outermost 
			plane as the unsurpassedrasaatala, the 
			sixth subterranean and the nethermost plane.

shloka:
एवं पर्वतसंबाधं जम्बूद्वीपं नृपात्मजाः |
खनन्तो नृपशार्दूल सर्वतः परिचक्रमुः
translation:
Oh, the tigerly king Rama, the sons of Sagara have endeavoured everywhere 
			digging over the Jambu Island which is verily congested with mountains 
			in this way.

shloka:
ततो देवाः सगंधर्वाः सासुराः सहपन्नगाः |
संभ्रांतमनसः सर्वे पितामहमुपागमन्
translation:
All the gods along with gandharva-s, asura-s, and reptiles who are 
			distraught at heart for the plight of earth have approached the Forefather, 
			Brahma.

shloka:
ते प्रसाद्य महात्मानं विषण्णवदनास्तदा |
ऊचुः परमसंत्रस्ताः पितामहमिदं वचः
translation:
They the gods who are very highly scared, and who are chap-fallen, 
			then spoke this sentence to the great-souled Forefather Brahma on gaining 
			his grace.

shloka:
भगवन् पृथिवी सर्वा खन्यते सगरात्मजैः |
बहवश्च महात्मानो वध्यन्ते जलचारिणः
translation:
'Oh, god Brahma, the sons of Sagara are digging entire earth, thus 
			aquatic beings and many great-souls are being destroyed.

shloka:
अयं यज्ञ हरोऽस्माकमनेनाश्वोऽपनीयते |
इति ते सर्वभूतानि हिंसन्ति सगरात्मजाः
translation:
" 'This one is the destroyer of our ritual... this one has carried off 
			our ritual horse...' thinking thus and suspecting everyone those sons 
			of Sagara are torturing all the living beings.' Thus all the gods have 
			appealed to Brahma." So said Sage Vishvamitra to Rama and others.

shloka:
देवतानां वचः श्रुत्वा भगवान्वै पितामहः |
प्रत्युवाच सुसंत्रस्तान् कृतान्तबलमोहितान्
translation:
"On hearing the words of gods, the esteemed Forefather Brahma spoke 
			to them, who are very highly scared, and bewildered by the might of 
			Sagara's sons for they are effectuating the end of all beings." Vishvamitra 
			thus continued his narration.

shloka:
यस्येयं वसुधा कृत्स्ना वासुदेवस्य धीमतः|
महिषी माधवस्यैषा स एव भगवान् प्रभुः
translation:
To whom this Mother Earth belongs in all her entirety, he is that 
			prescient Vasudeva, and she is also the consort of that Maadhava, and 
			that Vishnu eternally props up Mother Earth. Hence, that reverential 
			Vishnu donning the semblance of Sage Kapila will burn down the sons 
			of emperor Sagara to ashes in a fire of fury. [1-40-2, 3]

shloka:
पृथिव्याश्चापि निर्भेदो दृष्ट एव सनातनः |
सगरस्य च पुत्राणां विनाशो दीर्घदर्शिनाम्
translation:
'Even the complete cleavage of the earth, and the complete ruination 
			of Sagara's sons as well, are envisaged by the providentially farsighted 
			ancients." So said Brahma to gods.

shloka:
पितामह वचः श्रुत्वा त्रयस्त्रिंशदरिन्दम |
देवाः परमसंहृष्टाः पुनर्जग्मुर्यथागतम्
translation:
On hearing the words of the Forefather Brahma all the thirty three 
			gods went away with utmost satisfaction, as they have came.

shloka:
सगरस्य च पुत्राणां प्रादुरासीन्महास्वनः |
पृथिव्यां भिद्यमानायां निर्घातसमनिःस्वनः
translation:
When the sons of Sagara are digging the earth then there emerged an 
			unbearable noise similar to the crashing of a thunder.

shloka:
ततो भित्त्वा महीं सर्वां कृत्वा चापि प्रदक्षिणम् |
सहिताः सगराः सर्वे पितरं वाक्यमब्रुवन्
translation:
Then on hollowing the entire earth, and on making trips around her 
			without finding the horse, all of the sons of Sagara have come together 
			and on going to their father they spoke these words to him.

shloka:
परिक्रांता मही सर्वा सत्त्ववन्तश्च सूदिताः |
देवदानवरक्षांसि पिशाचोरगपन्नगाः
translation:
'Entire earth is trekked and mighty beings like gods, demons, monsters, 
			evil-spirits, fiends, serpents, naga-s are also eliminated, but we have 
			not seen the ritual-horse or its stealer. What we have to do next. Let 
			a thought be given in this matter. Let safeness betide you.' So said 
			those princes to their father Sagara. [1-40-8, 9]

shloka:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा पुत्राणां राजसत्तमः |
समन्युरब्रवीद्वाक्यं सगरो रघुनंदन
translation:
On hearing that sentence of his sons, oh, Rama, descendent of Raghu, 
			that exalted king Sagara infuriately spoke these words.

shloka:
भूयः खनत भद्रं वो विभेद्य वसुधातलम्
अश्वहर्तारमासाद्य कृतार्थाश्च निवर्तत
translation:
'Let the earth be dug further, may safety be with you, and verily 
			splitting open the surface of the earth you catch hold of the thief 
			of the horse, and on achieving your purpose you may return to me.' In 
			this way Sagara ordered his sons.

shloka:
पितुर्वचनमासाद्य सगरस्य महात्मनः |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि रसातलमभिद्रवन्
translation:
On catching up the words of their father, the great-souled Sagara, 
            his sixty thousand sons rushed towards the surface of therasaatala, 
            the netherworld.

shloka:
खन्यमाने ततस्तस्मिन् ददृशुः पर्वतोपमम् |
दिशागजं विरूपाक्षं धारयन्तं महीतलम्
translation:
While digging the earth there they beheld a mountain similar easterly 
			elephant named Viruupaaksha, which is bearing the eastern side of earth's 
			surface on its head.

shloka:
सपर्वतवनां कृत्स्नां पृथिवीं रघुनंदन |
धारयामास शिरसा विरूपाक्षो महागजः
translation:
Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu, that great easterly elephant Viruupaaksha 
			is bearing the entire eastern earth along with its mountains and forests 
			on its head.

shloka:
यदा पर्वणि काकुत्स्थ विश्रमार्थं महागजः |
खेदाच्चालयते शीर्षं भूमिकंपस्तदा भवेत्
translation:
On certain occasions, oh, Rama of Kakutstha, when that great-elephant 
			moves its head desiring respite in tiresomeness then earthquakes will 
			occur on earth.

shloka:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा दिशापालं महागजम् |
मानयन्तो हि ते राम जग्मुर्भित्त्वा रसातलम्
translation:
They circumambulated the great elephant in supplication, oh Rama, and 
			on worshipping that elephant which is the protector of easterly direction 
			they proceeded to netherworld duly splitting the earth.

shloka:
ततः पूर्वां दिशं भित्त्वा दक्षिणां बिभिदुः पुनः |
दक्षिणस्यामपि दिशि ददृशुस्ते महागजम्
translation:
After splitting the eastern direction then they split opened the southern 
			direction, and even in southern direction they beheld an elephant that 
			is similar to a very great mountain, and that is sustaining southerly 
			side of earth on its head, and on seeing that mammoth elephant of venerable 
			character, namely Mahapadma, they went into an inordinate astonishment. 
			[1-40-17, 18]

shloka:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा सगरस्य महात्मनः |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि पश्चिमां बिभिदुर्दिशम्
translation:
On circumabulating that elephant Mahaapada in supplication, they the 
			sixty thousand sons of great-souled Sagara scooped out the westerly 
			direction.

shloka:
पश्चिमायामपि दिशि महांतमचलोपमम् |
दिशागजं सौमनसं ददृशुस्ते महाबलाः
translation:
Even in the westerly direction those great mighty sons of Sagara beheld 
			an infinite and mountain similar elephant of western direction, called 
			Sumanasa.

shloka:
ते तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पृष्ट्वा चापि निरामयम् |
खनंतः समुपक्रांता दिशं सोमवतीं तदा
translation:
Circumambulating that elephant namely Sumanasa in western side, and 
			even on asking about its well-being, then they reached the northern 
			direction duly digging the earth.

shloka:
उत्तरस्यां रघुश्रेष्ठ ददृशुर्हिमपाण्डुरम् |
भद्रं भद्रेण वपुषा धारयन्तं महीमिमाम्
translation:
In the northern direction, oh, Rama, they beheld Bhadra, a snow-white 
			elephant with an auspicious body bearing northern side of this earth.

shloka:
समालभ्य ततः सर्वे कृत्वा चैनं प्रदक्षिणम् |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि बिभिदुर्वसुधातलम्
translation:
On touching that elephant reverently and also circumambulating it, 
			those sixty thousands sons of Sagara further burrowed to the surface 
			of the earth.

shloka:
ततः प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा सागराः प्रथितां दिशम् |
रोषादभ्यखनन्सर्वे पृथिवीं सगरात्मजाः
translation:
The sons of Sagara have then gone to the auspicious northeast direction,iishaana-digbhaaga, Shiva-sthaana, and 
			all those sons of Sagara have tunnelled the earth rancorously.

shloka:
ते तु सर्वे महत्मानो भीमवेगा महबलाः |
ददृशुः कपिलं तत्र वासुदेवं सनातनम्
translation:
But all those great-souled and great-mighty ones with terrible dash 
			have seen the Infinite Vasudeva in the form of sage Kapila there in 
			the northeast, and oh, descendant of Raghu, they have also seen the 
			ritual-horse moving nearby that sage Kapila, thus all of the sons of 
			Sagara obtained a matchless delight. [1-40-25, 26]

shloka:
ते तं हयहरं ज्ञात्वा क्रोधपर्याकुलेक्षणाः |
खनित्रलांगलधरा नानावृक्षशिलाधराः
translation:
The eyes of the princes are agitated in fury in construing the sage 
			Kapila as the stealer of ritual-horse, and they furiously dashed towards 
			him wielding crowbars, ploughs, and various trees and boulders, and 
			shouting at him, 'stay, stay.' [1-40-27, 28a]

shloka: अस्माकं त्वं हि तुरगं यज्ञियं हृतवानसि
translation:
You the malicious one, you have indeed stolen our ritual-horse, and 
			in fact, you should know that we who arrived here are the sons of Sagara.' 
			Thus Sagara's sons shouted at sage Kapila. [1-40-28b, 29a]

shloka: श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं तेषां कपिलो रघुनंदन
translation:
On hearing their words, oh, Rama, the descendant of Raghu, then sage 
			Kapila is beset with high wrath, and he boomed a 'hum' sound at them. 
			[1-40-29b, 30a]

shloka:
ततस्तेनाप्रमेयेण कपिलेन महात्मना |
भस्मराशीकृताः सर्वे काकुत्स्थ सगरात्मजाः
translation:
"Oh, Rama of Kakutstha, then that great-souled sage Kapila, rather Vishnu 
			with unimaginable power, has rendered all of those sons of Sagara as 
			heaps of ashes by virtue of his 'hum' sound." Thus Sage Vishvamitra 
			is narrating the legend of Sagara to Rama and others. [1-40-30b, c]

shloka:
पुत्रांश्चिरगतान् ज्ञात्वा सगरो रघुनंदन |
नप्तारमब्रवीद्राजा दीप्यमानं स्वतेजसा
translation:
"On observing that his sons have gone long time back in search of ritual-horse, 
			oh, Rama, king Sagara spoke this to his grandson, Amshuman, who is radiant 
			with his own self-resplendence." Thus Vishvamitra continued his narration 
			about Sagara.

shloka:
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च पूर्वैस्तुल्योऽसि तेजसा |
पितृणां गतिमन्विच्छ येन चाश्वोऽपहारितः
translation:
'You are brave one and completed your education in warfare, such as 
			you are, you are a coequal to your paternal-uncles in magnificence, 
			thus you search the course of your paternal uncles, also him by whom 
			the horse is stolen.' Thus King Sagara started speaking to his grandson 
			Amshuman.

shloka:
अन्तर्भौमानि सत्त्वानि वीर्यवन्ति महान्ति च |
तेषां त्वं प्रतिघातार्थं सासिं गृह्णीष्व कार्मुकम्
translation:
The living beings in netherworlds of earth are intrepid and they 
			are extraordinary also, hence you take your bow along with your sword 
			to retaliate them in the event of their attacking you.

shloka:
अभिवाद्याभिवाद्यांस्त्वां हत्वा विघ्नकरानपि |
सिद्धार्थः संनिवर्तस्व मम यज्ञस्य पारगः
translation:
'On saluting them that are worthy for salutations, and on eliminating 
			them that are the causer of obstructions, you shall achieve your purpose 
			of tracking the ritual-horse, and thus you comeback safely and let my 
			Vedic-ritual be crossed over to the other shore of mortality by you.' 
			Thus king Sagara told his grandson Amshuman.

shloka:
एवमुक्तो ंऽशुमान् सम्यक्सगरेण महात्मना |
धनुरादाय खड्गं च जगाम लघुविक्रमः
translation:
When the great-souled king Sagara has thoroughly said in this way, 
			that adroitly agile Amshuman proceeded wielding a bow and a sword.

shloka:
स खातं पितृभिर्मार्गमन्तर्भौमं महात्मभिः |
प्रापद्यत नरश्रेष्ठ तेन राज्ञाभिचोदितः
translation:
Motivated by the King Sagara, oh, Rama, the best one among men, Amshuman 
			progressed on the walkway that was hollowed out by his great-souled 
			paternal-uncles inside the earth.

shloka:
देवदानवरक्षोभिः पिशाचपतगोरगैः |
पूज्यमानं महातेजा दिशागजमपश्यत
translation:
And he that resplendent Amshuman beheld one of the four directional 
			elephant of the earth which is being venerated by gods, monsters, demons, 
			imps, vultures and serpents.

shloka:
स तं प्रदक्षिणं कृत्वा पृष्ट्वा चैव निरामयम् |
पितृन् स परिपप्रच्छ वाजिहर्तारमेव च
translation:
On circumambulating that elephant in supplication, and even on enquiring 
			after its well-being, he that Amshuman has enquired in detail with it 
			for his paternal-uncles and even about the robber of the ritual-horse.

shloka:
दिशागजस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा प्रत्युवाच महामतिः |
आसमंज कृतार्थस्त्वं सहाश्वः शीघ्रमेष्यसि
translation:
On hearing that enquiry of Amshuman that directional elephant with 
			great perception replied on its part saying, 'oh Amshuman, son of Asamanja, 
			on achieving your mission you will return expeditiously along with the 
			horse'.

shloka:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सर्वानेव दिशागजान् |
यथाक्रमं यथान्यायं प्रष्टुं समुपचक्रमे
translation:
On hearing that word of that directional elephant he departed from 
			there, and on sequentially reaching other directional elephants that 
			are abiding in other directions of earth, he commenced to ask the same 
			enquiry which he made with the first, according to the positioning of 
			elephants in directions, and according to the established procedures 
			of their venerability.

shloka:
तैश्च सर्वैर्दिशापालैर्वाक्यज्ञैर्वाक्यकोविदैः |
पूजितः सहयश्चैव गन्तासीत्यभिचोदितः
translation:
All the elephants that safeguard the directions of earth which have 
			the faculties of articulation and eloquence have adored Amshuman and 
			motivated him by saying, 'you will be going from here taking the horse.'

shloka:
तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा जगाम लघुविक्रमः |
भस्मराशीकृता यत्र पितरस्तस्य सागराः
translation:
On hearing that common blessing of all the directional-elephants, he 
			that nimble-footed Amshuman has gone to the place where his paternal-uncles, 
			sons of Sagara, were rendered as mounds of ashes.

shloka:
स दुःखवशमापन्नस्त्वसमंजसुतस्तदा |
चुक्रोश परमार्तस्तु वधात्तेषां सुदुःखितः
translation:
But he on whom the control of anguish has chanced for not physically 
			seeing his paternal-uncles, that son of Asamanja then wept, as he is 
			highly agonised and extremely anguished at their destruction.

shloka:
यज्ञियं च हयं तत्र चरन्तमविदूरतः |
ददर्श पुरुषव्याघ्रो दुःखशोकसमन्वितः
translation:
That tigerly-man Amshuman who is overwhelmed by agony and anguish, 
			also beheld there the horse of Vedic-ritual that is grazing nearby.

shloka:
स तेषां राजपुत्राणां कर्तुकामो जलक्रियाम् |
स जलार्थं महातेजा न चापश्यज्जलाशयम्
translation:
When he that great resplendent Amshuman wanted to offer obsequial waters 
			to the departed sons of Sagara and searched for water he has not found 
			any fount of water.

shloka:
विसार्य निपुणां दृष्टिं ततोऽपश्यत् खगाधिपम् |
पितृणां मातुलं राम सुपर्णमनिलोपमम्
translation:
Spanning his expert glances, oh, Rama, he then saw the rapid-winged 
			king of birds, namely Garuda, the Eagle-vehicle of Vishnu, who is the 
			maternal uncle of his father and other paternal-uncles, and whose flight 
			will be similar to that of the Wind-god.

shloka:
स चैनमब्रवीद्वाक्यं वैनतेयो महाबलः |
मा शुचः पुरुषव्याघ्र वधोऽयं लोकसम्मतः
translation:
That great-mighty son of Lady Vinata, namely Garuda, also spoke this 
			word to Amshuman, 'do not bemoan, oh, tigerly-man, this eradication 
			of your paternal-uncles is worthwhile to the worlds'.

shloka:
कपिलेनाप्रमेयेण दग्धा हीमे महाबलाः |
सलिलं नार्हसि प्राज्ञ दातुमेषां हि लौकिकम्
translation:
In fact, Kapila, the Imponderable Sage, has burnt down those great-mighty 
			paternal-uncles of yours, oh, observant Amshuman, as such it will not 
			be apt of you to offer the mundane obsequial water-oblations to them, 
			indeed.

shloka:
गंगा हिमवतो ज्येष्ठा दुहिता पुरुषर्षभ |
तस्यां कुरु महाबाहो पितॄणां तु जलक्रियाम्
translation:
'Oh, best one among men, River Ganga is the elder daughter of 
			Himavanta, and oh, dextrous one, you have to offer water-oblation to 
			the departed paternal-uncles of yours in her waters, namely the holy 
			waters of River Ganga'.

shloka:
भस्मराशीकृतानेतान् प्लावयेल्लोकपावनी |
तया क्लिन्नमिदं भस्म गंगया लोककान्तया |
षष्टिं पुत्रसहस्राणि स्वर्गलोकं गमिष्यति
translation:
World purifier River Ganga will drift them who are rendered as mounds 
			of ashes to heaven, and when she who is much adored by all worlds drenches 
			this ash, that River Ganga herself will lead the sixty-thousand sons 
			of Sagara to heaven.

shloka:
गच्छ चाश्वं महाभाग संगृह्य पुरुषर्षभ |
यज्ञं पैतामहं वीर निर्वर्तयितुमर्हसि
translation:
'Oh, great fortunate one, oh, best one among men, you may proceed 
			from here with the horse, oh, brave one, it will be apt of you to carry 
			out the Vedic-ritual of your grandfather.' Thus Garuda said to Amshuman.

shloka:
सुपर्णवचनं श्रुत्वा सोंऽशुमानतिवीर्यवान् |
त्वरितं हयमादाय पुनरायान्महायशाः
translation:
On hearing the words of that great-winged eagle, Garuda, he that highly 
			brave and well-renowned Amshuman swiftly took the horse, and returned 
			to the ritual place of his grandfather, king Sagara.

shloka:
ततो राजानमासाद्य दीक्षितं रघुनंदन |
न्यवेदयद्यथावृत्तं सुपर्णवचनं तथा
translation:
Then on reaching the King Sagara, who is under the vow of the ritual, 
			oh, Rama, Amshuman described what all has happened and even the words 
			of Garuda.

shloka:
तच्छ्रुत्वा घोरसंकाशं वाक्यमंशुमतो नृपः |
यज्ञं निर्वर्तयामास यथाकल्पं यथाविधि
translation:
On hearing those unendurable words from Amshuman, the king Sagara firstly 
			completed the Vedic-ritual scripturally and procedurally.

shloka:
स्वपुरं चागमच्छ्रीमानिष्टयज्ञो महीपतिः |
गंगायाश्चागमे राजा निश्चयं नाध्यगच्छत
translation:
On completing the Vedic-ritual King Sagara arrived at his capital, 
			but that king could not arrive at a decision about the arrival of Ganga 
			to the earth.

shloka:
अगत्वा निश्चयं राजा कालेन महता महान् |
त्रिंशद्वर्षसहस्राणि राज्यं कृत्वा दिवं गतः
translation:
"That great king Sagara could not get at any resolve in getting Ganga 
			to earth even after a long time, and on ruling kingdom for thirty-thousand 
			years he went to heaven." Thus Vishvamitra continued his narration about 
			the ancestors of Rama.

shloka:
कालधर्मं गते राम सगरे प्रकृतीजनाः |
राजानं रोचयामासुरंशुमन्तं सुधार्मिकम्
translation:
"When King Sagara passed away owing to the irrefutable virtue of Time, 
			the ministers and subjects of that kingdom are predisposed towards the 
			highly honourable Amshuman to become their king and they enthroned him 
			accordingly." Thus Vishvamitra continued narration about the predecessors 
			of Rama.

shloka:
स राजा सुमहानासीदंशुमान् रघुनंदन |
तस्य पुत्रो महानासीद्दिलीप इति विश्रुतः
translation:
"He that Amshuman turned out to be a very great king, and oh, Rama of 
			Raghu's delight, he begot a marvellous son who is renowned as Dileepa.

shloka:
तस्मै राज्यं समादिश्य दिलीपे रघुनंदन |
हिमवच्छिखरे रम्ये तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्
translation:
Assigning the kingdom to Dileepa, oh, Rama of Raghu's dynasty, Amshuman 
			undertook very stern ascesis on a pleasant peak of Himalayas desiring 
			the descent of River Ganga to earth.

shloka:
द्वात्रिंशच्च सहस्राणि वर्षाणि सुमहायशाः |
तपोवनगतो राजा स्वर्गं लेभे तपोधनः
translation:
On practising ascesis in ascetic-woods for thirty-two thousand years 
			that highly renowned king Amshuman achieved heaven as he acquired only 
			the wealth of practising the ascesis.

shloka:
दिलीपस्तु महातेजाः श्रुत्वा पैतामहं वधम् |
दुःखोपहतया बुद्ध्या निश्चयं नाध्यगच्छत
translation:
The great resplendent Dileepa on hearing the elimination of his grandfathers, 
			the sixty thousand sons of Sagara at the hand of sage Kapila, and with 
			a mind that is marred by the plight of his father Amshuman in absolving 
			the souls of Sagara's sons, he that Dileepa could not arrive at any 
			decision concerning the descent of Ganga.

shloka:
कथं गंगावतरणं कथं तेषां जलक्रिया |
तारयेयं कथं चैतानिति चिंतापरोऽभवत्
translation:
Dileepa became worried as to how River Ganga is to be alighted onto 
			earth from heaven, how water-oblations are to be offered for the souls 
			of Sagara's sons, and how to cross them, the souls, over this mortal 
			world.

shloka:
तस्य चिंतयतो नित्यं धर्मेण विदितात्मनः |
पुत्रो भगीरथो नाम जज्ञे परमधार्मिकः
translation:
To him who is self-mortified and who is always thinking righteously 
			about the alight of Ganga onto earth, to such a Dileepa a most-virtuous 
			son is born who is renowned by his name Bhageeratha.

shloka:
दिलीपस्तु महातेजा यज्ञैर्बहुभिरिष्टवान् |
त्रिंशद्वर्षसहस्राणि राजा राज्यमकारयत्
translation:
That great-resplendent king Dileepa on his part performed numerous 
			Vedic-rituals, and he ruled the kingdom for thirty thousand years - 
			to the delight of each of his subjects, but could not find a way to 
			fetch Ganga.

shloka:
अगत्वा निश्चयं राजा तेषामुद्धरणं प्रति |
व्याधिना नरशार्दूल कालधर्ममुपेयिवान्
translation:
Oh, tigerly-man Rama, that king Dileepa by not attaining any choice 
			towards the uplifting the souls of his grandparents to heaven by bringing 
			Ganga to earth, he took to illness, and he attained the ultimate virtue 
			of Time, namely the demise.

shloka:
इन्द्रलोकं गतो राजा स्वार्जितेनैव कर्मणा |
राज्ये भगीरथं पुत्रमभिषिच्य नरर्षभः
translation:
That best one among men, namely king Dileepa, on anointing his son 
			Bhageeratha in the kingdom went to the abode of Indra, namely the heaven, 
			only by his self-acquired merits of deeds.

shloka:
भगीरथस्तु राजर्षिर्धार्मिको रघुनंदन |
अनपत्यो महाराजः प्रजाकामः स च प्रजाः
translation:
Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu, but on his part that self-righteous 
			and kingly-sage Bhageeratha is childless, and that great king longed-for 
			offspring.

shloka:
मंत्रिष्वाधाय तद्राज्यं गङ्गावतरणे रतः|
तपो दीर्घं समातिष्ठद्गोकर्णे रघुनंदन
translation:
Interested in the alighting of River Ganga on earth, oh, Rama, the 
			descendent of Raghu, king Bhageeratha delegated his kingdom to the custody 
			of his ministers and people and firmed up himself in sustained asceticism 
			on Mt. Gokarna in Himalayas, and he practise ascesis standing amid five-fires, 
			upraising his hands, with a monthly sustenance and with his sense conquered. 
			[1-42-12, 13a]

shloka: तस्य वर्षसहस्राणि घोरे तपसि तिष्ठतः
translation:
Thousands of years have rolled by while Bhageeratha stood practising 
			his severe ascesis, oh, dextrous Rama, and then the lord and master 
			of all beings, namely god Brahma, is well pleased with that great-souled 
			king's ascesis. [1-42-13b, 14]

shloka:
ततः सुरगणैः सार्धमुपागम्य पितामहः |
भगीरथं महात्मानं तप्यमानमथाब्रवीत्
translation:
Forefather Brahma then arrived along with assemblages of gods, and 
			spoke this way to the great-souled Bhageeratha who is deep in the practise 
			of ascesis.

shloka:
भगीरथ महाराग प्रीतस्तेऽहं जनाधिप |
तपसा च सुतप्तेन वरं वरय सुव्रत
translation:
Oh, great king Bhageeratha, oh, lord of the people, I am delighted 
			with the perfectly conducted ascesis of yours, hence oh, truly committed 
			one, you may beseech for a boon.

shloka:
तमुवाच महातेजाः सर्वलोकपितामहम् |
भगीरथो महाबाहुः कृतांजलिपुटः स्थितः
translation:
That great resplendent and highly fortunate king Bhageeratha then remaining 
			with suppliantly adjoined palm fold spoke to him who is the Forefather 
			of all worlds, namely Brahma.

shloka:
यदि मे भगवान्प्रीतो यद्यस्ति तपसः फलम् |
सगरस्यात्मजाः सर्वे मत्तः सलिलस्याप्नुयुः
translation:
Oh, god, if you are satisfied with my ascesis, and if there is any 
			fruition to the ascesis of mine, let all the sons of Sagara get water 
			oblations through me.

shloka:
गङ्गायाः सलिलक्लिन्ने भस्मन्येषां महात्मनाम् |
स्वर्गं गच्छेयुरत्यन्तं सर्वे मे प्रपितामहाः
translation:
While the ashes of these great souls are drenched with the waters 
			of Ganga, let all of those great-grandfathers of mine depart to heaven, 
			eternally.

shloka:
देव याचे ह संतत्यै नावसीदेत्कुलं च नः |
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले देव एष मेऽस्तु वरः परः
translation:
Oh, god, I indeed pray for offspring in our Ikshvaku dynasty, let 
			not our dynasty dwindle as I am issueless, and oh, god, let this be 
			the other boon to me.

shloka:
उक्तवाक्यं तु राजानं सर्वलोकपितामहः |
प्रत्युवाच शुभां वाणीं मधुरं मधुराक्षराम्
translation:
The Forefather of all the worlds, Brahma, then replied the king who 
			has spoken in that way, in an auspicious tongue that is sweet-sounding 
			and sweetly worded, as well.

shloka:
मनोरथो महानेष भगीरथ महारथ |
एवं भवतु भद्रं ते इक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्धन
translation:
Oh, top-speeded chariot-rider Bhageeratha, this aspiration of yours 
			is sublime, and oh, the furtherer of Ikshvaku dynasty, so be it, let 
			safeness betide you.

shloka:
इयं हैमवती ज्येष्ठा गंगा हिमवतः सुता |
तां वै धारयितुं राजन् हरस्तत्र नियुज्यताम्
translation:
This Ganga is the one with snow-broth, the elder daughter of Himavanta, 
			and oh, king Bhageeratha, god Shiva alone is capable to sustain her 
			force in the course of her alighting onto earth, and in fact, he is 
			to be commissioned for that purpose.

shloka:
गंगायाः पतनं राजन् पृथिवी न सहिष्यते |
तां वै धारयितुं राजन् नान्यं पश्यामि शूलिनः
translation:
'Oh, king Bhageeratha, the earth cannot endure the downfall of Ganga 
			and to sustain Ganga, oh, king, indeed I do not behold none other than 
			the Trident-wielder, god Shiva.' Thus Brahma spoke to Bhageeratha.

shloka:
तमेवमुक्त्वा राजानं गङ्गां चाभाष्य लोककृत् |
जगाम त्रिदिवं देवैः सह सर्वैर्मरुद्गणैः
translation:
"Speaking this way to the king Bhageeratha and informally greeting Ganga 
			also, that Creator of Worlds, Brahma, left for heaven along with all 
			the groups of gods and Wind-gods." Thus Vishvamitra continued narration 
			about the arrival of River Ganga to earth.

shloka:
देवदेवे गते तस्मिन् सोंऽगुष्ठाग्रनिपीडिताम् |
कृत्वा वसुमतीं राम वत्सरं समुपासत
translation:
"When the god of gods Brahma left from there Bhageeratha stood on the 
			tip of his big-toe praying for the mercy of Lord Shiva for one year, 
			while that tip of his big-toe pressurised the earth." Thus Vishvamitra 
			continued his narration about Bhageeratha's effort to bring Ganga to 
			earth.

shloka:
अथ संवत्सरे पूर्णे सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः |
उमापतिः पशुपती राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
translation:
On completion of one year, he who is venerated by all worlds, the consort 
			of Uma and the god of animals from insects to humans, that god Shiva 
			revealed himself and spoke this to the king.

shloka:
प्रीतस्तेऽहं नरश्रेष्ठ करिष्यामि तव प्रियम् |
शिरसा धारयिष्यामि शैलराजसुतामहम्
translation:
Oh, best one among humans, I am delighted with your unwavering effort, 
			and I will fulfil your cherish. I will therefore sustain Ganga, the 
			daughter of king of mountains by my head.

shloka:
ततो हैमवती ज्येष्ठा सर्वलोकनमस्कृता |
तदा सातिमहद्रूपं कृत्वा वेगं च दुःसहम्
translation:
Afterwards, she who is reverenced by all the worlds and who is the 
			elder daughter of Himavanta, that Ganga assuming an unendurable form 
			and an insupportable rapidity, they say, then plunged from the sky onto 
			the auspicious head of Shiva. [1-43-4, 5a]

shloka: अचिन्तयच्च सा देवी गङ्गा परमदुर्धरा
translation:
She who is an extremely unendurable river that goddess Ganga even speculated 
			saying to herself, 'let me enter netherworld, indeed whisking Shiva 
			with my streams.' [1-43-5b, 6a]

shloka: तस्या वलेपनं ज्ञात्वा क्रुद्धस्तु भगवान् हरः
translation:
Discerning her egotism god Shiva is infuriated, and then on his part 
			that Three-eyed god Shiva thought to pent her up in the tufts of his 
			head-hair. [1-43-6b, 7a]

shloka: सा तस्मिन् पतिता पुण्या पुण्ये रुद्रस्य मूर्धनि
translation:
And oh, Rama, she that holy River Ganga swooped down into the cavernous 
			curls of matted hair-tufts on the holy head of God Shiva, and she became 
			a detainee in them. [1-43-7b, 8a]

shloka: सा कथञ्चिन्महीं गन्तुं नाशक्नोद्यत्नमास्थिता
translation:
Though she strove hard in one way or another to reach the earth that 
			Ganga is rendered incapable, as she could not gain access for an outlet 
			from any edge of the coils of matted hair-tufts of Shiva, hence she 
			is held there in durance vile. [1-43-8b, 9a]

shloka: तत्रैवाबंभ्रमद्देवी संवत्सरगणान्बहून्
translation:
Goddess Ganga whirled round and round in the coils of tufts alone for 
			many number of years, and when Ganga's emanation from those coils is 
			intangible Bhageeratha again firmed up in a marvellous penance in the 
			matter of her descent to earth. [1-43-9b, 10a]

shloka: स तेन तोषितश्चासीदत्यन्तं रघुनंदन
translation:
Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu, with that ascesis of Bhageeratha god 
			Shiva is very much delighted, and thereupon he has also released Ganga 
			aiming at Bindu Lake in Himalayas. [1-43-10b, 11a]

shloka: तस्यां विसृज्यमानायां सप्त स्रोतंसि जज्ञिरे
translation:
While god Shiva released Ganga into Bindu Lake seven streams have emerged 
			out of it, and thus three auspicious Ganga-s with holy waters have cruised 
			eastward which are known as Hlaadini, Paavani, and Nalini. [1-43-11b, 
			12]

shloka:
सुचक्षुश्चैव सीता च सिन्धुश्चैव महानदी |
तिस्रस्त्वेता दिशं जग्मुः प्रतीचीं तु शुभोदकाः
translation:
Also thus Sucakshu, Seetha, and the excellent river Sindhu are the 
			other three rivers which streamed to the westward direction with their 
			holy waters.

shloka:
सप्तमी चान्वगात्तासां भगीरथरथं तदा |
भगीरथोऽपि रजर्षिर्दिव्यं स्यंदनमास्थितः
translation:
Of them the seventh Ganga flowed towards the path of Bhageeratha' chariot, 
			and that great-resplendent and kingly sage Bhageeratha sitting in a 
			divine chariot moved ahead and even Ganga followed him. [1-43-14, 15a]

shloka: गगनाच्छङ्करशिरस्ततो धरणिमागता
translation:
Thus Ganga came from heavens onto Shankara's head and from there onto 
			the earth, and there on earth her waters advanced with a tumultuous 
			sound advancing them. [1-43-15b, 16a]

shloka: मत्स्यकच्छपसंघैश्च शिंशुमारगणैस्तथा
translation:
The earth then verily shone forth with the shoals of fish, schools 
			of tortoises, and scores of porpoises and other aquatic beings that 
			have already fallen and that are still falling in step with the spates 
			of Ganga. [1-43-16b, 17a]

shloka: ततो देवर्षिगंधर्वा यक्षा सिद्धगणास्तथा
translation:
Later, they the gods, sages, gandharva-s, yaksha-s, and the assemblages 
			of siddha-s have then seen there the swoop of Ganga in that way from 
			heaven to earth, with curiosity. [1-43-17b, 18a]

shloka: विमानैर्नगराकारैर्हयैर्गजवरैस्तथा
translation:
Some of the gods with aircrafts that are like cities in their shape 
			and size, and some with horses that are prancing, and some with best 
			elephants that are staggering, at the very sight of plunging Ganga, 
			have entered the firmament at that place. [1-43-18b, 19a]

shloka: तदद्भुततमं लोके गंगापतनमुत्तमम्
translation:
The gods whose animation is unlimited, and who are anxious to see the 
			plunge of Ganga, have come together in assemblages, which plunge is 
			a highest marvel in the universe by a better degree of her illimitable 
			animation than that of gods who came to see, and even benignant to the 
			world in according water and salving souls, which those gods cannot 
			do. [1-43-19b, 20a]

shloka: संपतद्भिः सुरगणैस्तेषां चाभरणौजसा
translation:
"The glitter of the ornaments of hosts of gods who are in stampede, 
			made the cloudless sky to shine as if it is with a hundred of suns. 
			[1-43-20b, 21a]

shloka: शिंशुमारोरगगणैर्मीनैरपि च चंचलैः
translation:
At that time, with the falling and rising of scores of porpoises and 
			reptiles, even with the wriggling fishes, the sky became flashy as if 
			flashes of lightning are strewn over it. [1-43-21b, 22a]

shloka: पाण्डुरैः सलिलोत्पीडैः कीर्यमाणैः सहस्रधा
translation:
Spattered innumerably with the whitish froth from the splashes of Ganga, 
			and stippled with the flights of swans, the sky is as though overspread 
			with silver-clouds of autumn. [1-43-22b, 23a]

shloka: क्वचिद् द्रुततरं याति कुटिलं क्वचिदायतम्
translation:
Somewhere Ganga is coursing precipitately, elsewhere sinuously, somewhere 
			else straightly, elsewhere sloppily, somewhere gushingly, and somewhere 
			else her cruise is leisurely and tardily. [1-43-23b, 24a]

shloka: सलिलेनैव सलिलं क्वचिदभ्याहतं पुनः
translation:
Somewhere her water repeatedly knocking against her own water is recurrently 
			billowing upwards only to make nosedive onto earth. [1-43-24b, 25a]

shloka: तच्छङ्करशिरोभ्रष्टं भ्रष्टं भूमितले पुनः
translation:
That impeccable and immaculate water of Ganga then became outstanding 
			as it has flounced down from heaven primarily onto the head of Shankara, 
			and therefrom it has coasted down onto the earth. [1-43-25b, 26a]

shloka: तत्रर्षिगणगन्धर्वा वसुधातलवासिनः
translation:
And asserting that the water as holy, because it descended touching 
			the body of Shiva, viz., the head of Shiva, the assemblages of sages, 
			gandharva-s, and those that are residents on the plane of earth have 
			sipped that water at that place. [1-43-26b, 27a]

shloka: शापात् प्रपतिता ये च गगनाद्वसुधातलम्
translation:
Also those that have fallen from heaven onto the surface of earth by 
			some curse or the other, they too became blemishless on taking head-bath 
			in the water of Ganga. [1-43-27b, 28a]

shloka: धूतपापाः पुनस्तेन तोयेनाथ शुभान्विता
translation:
When sins are washed away with the hallowing water of Ganga, they again 
			transited skyward and then obtained their own empyrean worlds once again. 
			[1-43-28b, 29a]

shloka: मुमुदे मुदितो लोकस्तेन तोयेन भास्वता
translation:
With her splendorous water people are blissful, and on taking dip-baths 
			in Ganga they are totally removed of the strains of their sins, and 
			they lived blissfully ever after. [1-43-29b, 30a]

shloka: भगीरथोऽपि राजर्षिर्दिव्यं स्यंदनमास्थितः
translation:
In this way, the great-resplendent and kingly sage Bhageeratha sitting 
			in a divine chariot continuously moved ahead and Ganga continually followed 
			him at his behind. [1-43-30b, 31a]

shloka: देवाः सर्षिगणाः सर्वे दैत्यदानवराक्षसाः
translation:
Oh, Rama, all of the gods along with the assemblages of sages, ogres, 
			monsters, demons, and even great reptiles with kinnara-s, and gandharva-s 
			with best yaksha-s, and even serpents and apsara-s, have delightfully 
			moved after Ganga who is following the chariot of Bhageeratha, and why 
			they, in fact, all of the aquatic beings have followed Ganga. [31b, 
			32, 33a]

shloka: यतो भगीरथो राजा ततो गंगा यशस्विनी
translation:
In whichever direction king Bhageeratha has advanced, that glorious 
			River Ganga, who is the prominent river among all the rivers and the 
			complete obliterator of sins, has also moved at his behind in that direction. 
			[1-43-33b, 34a]

shloka: ततो हि यजमानस्य जह्नोरद्भुतकर्मणः
translation:
While in flow she started to completely inundate the field of Vedic-ritual 
			belonging to the great-souled sage Jahnu, who is of marvellous deeds 
			and who is presently an officiator of an ongoing Vedic-ritual. [1-43-34b, 
			35a]

shloka: तस्यावलेपनं ज्ञात्वा क्रुद्धो जह्नुश्च राघव
translation:
But on knowing her hubris, oh, Raghava, that sage Jahnu has become 
			irritated and causing an extreme marvel he drank off all the water of 
			Ganga. [1-43-35b, 36a]

shloka: ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च सुविस्मिताः
translation:
Thereupon, the gods along with gandharva-s and sages at that extremely 
			marvellous feat of Sage Jahnu are highly astounded, and they then started 
			to worship that ablest human and great-souled sage Jahnu, and even deigned 
			for the daughterhood of Ganga to that high-souled sage Jahnu. [1-43-36b, 
			37]

shloka:
ततस्तुष्टो महातेजाः श्रोत्राभ्यामसृजत् प्रभुः |
तस्माज्जह्नुसुता गङ्गा प्रोच्यते जाह्नवीति च
translation:
That greatly radiant and godly sage Jahnu is then delighted and released 
			Ganga from both of his ears. Therefore Ganga became the daughter of 
			sage Jahnu, and she is also renowned as Jahnavi, after the name of that 
			sage.

shloka:
जगाम च पुनर्गङ्गा भगीरथरथानुगा |
सागरं चापि संप्राप्ता सा सरित्प्रवरा तदा
translation:
Even though Ganga again proceeded moving behind the chariot of Bhageeratha 
			and reached the ocean, therefrom she had to wend her way to netherworld, 
			once dug by the sons of Sagara, only to accomplish the mission of Bhageeratha, 
			namely drenching the ashes of Sagara's sons. [1-43-39, 40a]

shloka: भगीरथोऽपि रजार्षिर्गङ्गामादाय यत्नतः
translation:
Even kingly-sage Bhageeratha making every effort ushered Ganga to netherworld, 
			but on seeing his grandparents rendered to ashes he has became doleful. 
			[1-43-40b, 41a]

shloka:
अथ तद्भस्मनां राशिं गङ्गासलिलमुत्तमम् |
प्लावयत् पूतपाप्मानः स्वर्गं प्रप्ता रघूत्तम
translation:
"Oh, Rama, the best of Raghu's dynasty, then Ganga inundated that mound 
			of ashes of Sagara's six-thousand sons, by which those souls obtained 
			heaven, while the sins of souls are cleansed with the water of Ganga." 
			Thus Vishvamitra continued his narration. [1-43-41b, c]

shloka:
स गत्वा सागरं राजा गंगयानुगतस्तदा |
प्रविवेश तलं भूमेर्यत्र ते भस्मसात्कृताः
translation:
"King Bhageeratha followed by Ganga has gone to the ocean-like ditch 
			which is dredged up by the sons of Sagara, and entered the subterranean 
			of earth where the sons of Sagara are rendered to ashes." Thus Vishvamitra 
			continued his narration about the Descent of Ganga.

shloka:
भस्मन्यथाप्लुते राम गंगायाः सलिलेन वै |
सर्वलोकप्रभुर्ब्रह्मा राजानमिदमब्रवीत्
translation:
While the waters of Ganga are inundating those ashes, oh, Rama, then 
			Brahma, the lord of all worlds, indeed spoke this to the king Bhageeratha.

shloka:
तारिता नरशार्दूल दिवं याताश्च देववत् |
षष्टिः पुत्रसहस्राणि सगरस्य महात्मनः
translation:
Oh, tigerly-man Bhageeratha, the sixty thousands sons of great souled 
			Sagara have crossed over the sea of mortality, and on a par with the 
			gods they have also transited to heaven.

shloka:
सागरस्य जलं लोके यावत् स्थास्यति पार्थिव |
सगरस्यात्मजाः सर्वे दिवि स्थास्यन्ति देववत्
translation:
As long as the water of the ocean abides in the world, oh, king, 
			so long the sons of Sagara will abide in heaven like gods.

shloka:
इयं च दुहिता ज्येष्ठा तव गंगा भविष्यति |
त्वत्कृतेन च नाम्नाथ लोके स्थास्यति विश्रुता
translation:
This Ganga will become your eldest daughter and hereafter she will 
			remain renowned in the world with the name associated with your deed 
			of bringing her onto earth.

shloka:
गंगा त्रिपथगा नाम दिव्या भागीरथीति च |
त्रीन्पथो भावयन्तीति तस्मत्त्रिपथगा स्मृता
translation:
Henceforth heavenly Ganga will be renowned as 'Triple-path-cruiser' 
			and 'Bhaageerathi,' as well, and as this river is sanctifying three 
			worlds, namely,svarga, bhuu, paataala loka-s, 
			'heaven, earth and netherworld' she will be remembered as the traveller 
			on triple path.

shloka:
पितामहानां सर्वेषां त्वमत्र मनुजाधिप |
कुरुष्व सलिलं राजन् प्रतिज्ञामपवर्जय
translation:
You may now offer water-oblations to all of your forefathers in the 
			waters of Ganga, oh, king, the lord of people, thus you may fulfil and 
			do away with the pledge of your requiescat.

shloka:
पूर्वकेण हि ते राजंस्तेनातियशसा तदा |
धर्मिणां प्रवरेणाथ नैष प्राप्तो मनोरथः
translation:
Your ancestor Sagara is a highly glorious one and a best one 
			among righteous persons, oh, king, even then he has not achieved this 
			aspiration of alighting Ganga in his lifetime, but you have achieved 
			it.

shloka:
तथैवांशुमता वत्स लोकेऽप्रतिमतेजसा |
गङ्गां प्रार्थयता नेतुं प्रतिज्ञा नापवर्जिता
translation:
Like that, your grandfather Amshuman, who is unequalled in his resplendence 
			in this world and who had been praying for the descent of Ganga, he 
			also could not dispense with this vow on fulfilling it.

shloka:
राजर्षिणा गुणवता महर्षिसमतेजसा |
मत्तुल्यतपसा चैव क्षत्रधर्मे स्थितेन च
translation:
Oh, impeccable Bhageeratha, even by the kingly-sage Dileepa whose 
			resplendence is kindred to great sages, who is equal to me in his ascesis, 
			who is abided by the observances of ruling Kshatriya class, even by 
			such a highly fortunate and highly resplendent father of yours it was 
			impossible to bring Ganga in his turn, even though he had been supplicating 
			for the descent of Ganga throughout his lifetime. [1-44-10, 11]

shloka:
सा त्वया समतिक्रान्ता प्रतिज्ञा पुरुषर्षभ |
प्राप्तोऽसि परमं लोके यशः परमसंमतम्
translation:
But, you have accomplished that pledge, oh, the best one among men, 
			and in the world you have achieved highest renown which is highly adorable 
			by all.

shloka:
तच्च गंगावतरणं त्वया कृतमरिन्दम |
अनेन च भवान् प्राप्तो धर्मस्यायतनं महत्
translation:
That 'Descent of Ganga' is perfected by you, oh, enemy-represser, 
			and by this you have acquired a genuine basis for righteousness in this 
			world, and thereby a base for yourself in my world, namely Abode of 
			Brahma.

shloka:
प्लावयस्व त्वमात्मानं नरोत्तम सदोचिते |
सलिले पुरुषश्रेष्ठ शुचिः पुण्यफलो भव
translation:
Oh, phenomenal one, you may always take dip-baths in the holy water 
			of Ganga and oh, persona grata, thereby get purified of sins and thus 
			let your merit be fructified.

shloka:
पितामहानां सर्वेषां कुरुष्व सलिलक्रियाम् |
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि स्वं लोकं गम्यतां नृप
translation:
'You may now perform water-oblations to your forefathers with the 
			water of Ganga, let there be wellbeing to you, and oh, king, here I 
			go to my abode and you too may depart to yours.' Thus Brahma said to 
			Bhageeratha.

shloka:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा देवेशः सर्वलोकपितामहः |
यथागतं तथागच्छद्देवलोकं महायशाः
translation:
On saying in this way, the forefather of all the worlds, and the great 
			glorious lord of all gods, namely Brahma, went away to his empyrean 
			world as he has came.

shloka:
भगीरथस्तु राजर्षिः कृत्वा सलिलमुत्तमम् |
यथाक्रमं यथान्यायं सागराणां महायशाः
translation:
On according those best water-oblations that endow superior realms 
			to the souls of sons of Sagara, according to precedency and the rationale 
			of scriptures, and even on offering water-oblations to other manes that 
			kingly-sage and greatly renowned Bhageeratha is sanctified, and then 
			only that king re-entered his own city, indeed when his purpose is completely 
			achieved, and oh, outstanding man Rama, thus that king Bhageeratha ruled 
			his kingdom well. [1-44-17, 18]

shloka:
प्रमुमोद च लोकस्तं नृपमासाद्य राघव |
नष्टशोकः समृद्धार्थो बभूव विगतज्वरः
translation:
On regaining him as their king the subjects of the kingdom are overjoyed, 
			and oh, Raghava, that king Bhageeratha too is relieved of his febrility 
			as his purpose is achieved and he is happy when devoid of haunting grief 
			of getting Ganga to earth.

shloka:
एष ते राम गंगाया विस्तरोऽभिहितो मया |
स्वस्ति प्राप्नुहि भद्रं ते संध्याकालोऽतिवर्तते
translation:
Oh, Rama, this way I described to you about 'The Decent of Ganga' in 
			detail, thus you be blest and prosperous, and as the visceral time is 
			elapsing no more questions from you for now, and let us meditate on 
			Gayatri. But listen to the fruits of listening the legend ofganga avataraNa,'The Descent of Ganga'

shloka:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं पुत्र्यं स्वर्ग्यमथापि च |
यः श्रावयति विप्रेषु क्षत्रियेष्वितरेषु च
translation:
This legend is conducive to achieve prosperity, fame, longevity, progeny 
			and even heaven, and he who narrates this legend to others, whether 
			he is from Brahmans or from Kshatriya-s, or for that matter of fact 
			from any other class, his manes will be satisfied, and gods too will 
			be gladdened. [1-44-21, 22a]

shloka: इदमाख़्यनमायुष्यं गंगावतरणं शुभम्
translation:
"Oh, Rama of Kakutstha-s, he who listens to this auspicious legend named 
			'The Descent of Gang,' which is an endower of longevity, all his wishes 
			are achieved, all his sins are obliterated, and his reputation and longevity 
			are also enhanced." Thus Vishvamitra concluded the episode of 'The Descent 
			of Ganga.' [1-44-22b, 23]

shloka:
विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा राघवः सहलक्ष्मणः |
विस्मयं परमं गत्वा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्
translation:
On listening the narration of Sage Vishwamitra about Ganga's descent along with 
Lakshmana, Rama went into a great astonishment, and then addressed Vishvamitra.

shloka:
अत्यद्भुतमिदं ब्रह्मन् कथितं परमं त्वया |
गंगावतरणं पुण्यं सागरस्यापि पूरणम्
translation:
The blessed legend you have narrated about the digging of an ocean at the behest 
of Sagara, Ganga's alighting, and Bhageeratha filling it with the water of Ganga 
is sacrosanct and even highly amazing.

shloka:
क्षणभूतेव नौ रात्रिः संवृत्तेयं परंतप |
इमां चिंतयतोः सर्वां निखिलेन कथां तव
translation:
Oh, enemy-inflamer, for two of us entire night rolled by as if it is a single moment 
while we were thinking about the episode you have narrated in its entirety.

shloka:
तस्य सा शर्वरी सर्वा मम सौमित्रिणा सह |
जगाम चिंतयानस्य विश्वामित्रकथां शुभाम्
translation:
While thinking about the auspicious legend of Ganga along with Lakshmana, oh, friend 
of the universe, Vishvamitra, whole night rolled by." Thus Rama is addressing Vishvamitra.

shloka:
ततः प्रभाते विमले विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम्|
उवाच राघवो वाक्यं कृताह्निकमरिन्दमः
translation:
Thereafter on the next fresh dawn the enemy-oppressor Raghava spoke these words 
to sage Vishvamitra, whose affluence is nothing but asceticism, and who by now has 
performed his daily chores of rituals.

shloka:
गता भगवती रात्रिः श्रोतव्यं परमं श्रुतम् |
तराम सरितं श्रेष्ठं पुण्यां त्रिपथगां नदीम्
translation:
We have listened the praiseworthy legend of River Ganga, and the deific night 
has also passed by while listening such a legend, we may now cross over the very 
same prominent and merited River Ganga, the tri-path-cruiser.

shloka:
नौरेषा हि सुखास्तीर्णा ऋषीणां पुण्यकर्मणाम् |
भगवन्तमिह प्राप्तं ज्ञात्वा त्वरितमागता
translation:
"This boat which is suitable for the embarkation of the sages whose deeds are pious, 
and which is comfortably blanketed with mats in its deck has come here, and indeed 
on knowing about the visit of your holiness to this place the sages have fetched 
it." Thus Rama spoke to Vishvamitra.

shloka:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः |
संतारं कारयामास सर्षिसंघस्य कौशिकः
translation:
Hearing the words of great-souled Raghava, Vishvamitra of Kusha dynasty, started 
to cross over the River Ganga along with the assemblage of sages, and with both 
the Raghava-s.

shloka:
उत्तरं तीरमासाद्य संपूज्यर्षिगणं ततः |
गंगाकूले निविष्टास्ते विशालां ददृशुः पुरिम्
translation:
Arriving at the northern bank of River Ganga they have honoured the group of sages 
who ferried them up to here and sent them off. Then sojourning on the riverbank 
of Ganga they have seen the city called Vishaala.

shloka:
ततो मुनिवरस्तूर्णं जगाम सहराघवः |
विशालां नगरीं रम्यां दिव्यां स्वर्गोपमां तदा
translation:
The great sage Vishvamitra then quickly started along with Rama and Lakshmana to 
the charming and admirable city Vishaala, which in comparison is like heaven.

shloka:
अथ रामो महाप्राज्ञो विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् |
पप्रच्छ प्रांजलिर्भूत्वा विशालामुत्तमां पुरीम्
translation:
Then Rama, whose flair for knowing everything is high, became suppliant duly adjoining 
his palms, and enquired about the prominent city Vishala with the great Sage Vishvamitra.

shloka:
कतमो राजवंशोऽयं विशालायां महामुने |
श्रोतुमिच्छामि भद्रं ते परं कौतूहलं हि मे
translation:
"Oh, great sage, which dynasty of kings is ruling from this city of Vishaala? Let 
safeness betide you, I am interested to hear of it and indeed I am highly inquisitive 
about it." Thus Rama spoke to Vishvamitra. [1- 45-12]

shloka:
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा रामस्य मुनिपुंगवः |
आख्यातुं तत्समारेभे विशालस्य पुरातनम्
translation:
Hearing that sentence of Rama then the eminent sage Vishvamitra has commenced to 
narrate the legend of ancient Vishaala.

shloka:
श्रूयतां राम शक्रस्य कथां कथयतः श्रुताम् |
अस्मिन् देशे हि यद्वृत्तं शृणु तत्त्वेन राघव
translation:
Oh, Rama, I will tell you about the auspicious legend of Indra as I was told, and 
you listen to it as I tell. Oh, Raghava, indeed you may now listen to the quintessence 
of what has happened in this country.

shloka:
पूर्वं कृतयुगे राम दितेः पुत्रा महाबलाः |
अदितेश्च महाभागा वीर्यवन्तः सुधार्मिकाः
translation:
Once in Krita era, oh, Rama, the sons of Lady Diti were extremely energetic, whereas 
the sons of her younger sister Lady Aditi were vigorous and highly righteous.

shloka:
ततस्तेषां नरव्याघ्र बुद्धिरासीन्महात्मनाम् |
अमरा निर्जराश्चैव कथं स्यामो निरामयाः
translation:
"Oh, tigerly-man, Rama, then those great-souls speculated as to 'how we can thrive 
without ageing, illness, and likewise without death.'

shloka:
तेषां चिंतयतां तत्र बुद्धिरासीद्विपश्चिताम् |
क्षीरोदमथनं कृत्वा रसं प्राप्स्याम तत्र वै
translation:
A thought occurred to those masterminds who were thinking on that matter clueing 
them up, 'we indeed can get elixir of life by churning the Milky Ocean.'

shloka:
ततो निश्चित्य मथनं योक्त्रं कृत्वा च वासुकिम् |
मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा ममन्थुरमितौजसः
translation:
Deciding upon to churn the Milky Ocean then made Vasuki, Thousand-headed King of 
Snakes, as the churning rope and Mt. Mandara as stirrer, and those brothers whose 
energy is unlimited have started churning the Milky Ocean thoroughly.

shloka:
अथ वर्षसहस्रेण योक्त्रं सर्पशिरांसि च |
वमन्त्यतिविषं तत्र ददंशुर्दशनैः शिलाः
translation:
After a thousand years, the Thousand-headed serpent Vaasuki, which is being 
used as churning rope, is incapacitated to bear the friction of churning and fanged 
the cliffs of Mt. Mandara. Thereby a great lot of venom is disgorged from the heads 
of that serpent Vaasuki, which venom on melting the rocks of Mt. Mandara became 
the holocaustic poison calledhaalaahala.

shloka:
उत्पपाताग्निसंकाशं हालाहलमहाविषम् |
तेन दग्धं जगत्सर्वं सदेवासुरमानुषम्
translation:
A lethal poison similar to inferno known ashaalaahalahas started to fulminate 
therefrom, by which whole universe of gods, non-gods and humans is burnt down.

shloka:
अथ देवा महादेवं शंकरं शरणार्थिनः |
जग्मुः पशुपतिं रुद्रं त्राहि त्राहीति तुष्टुवुः
translation:
The gods seeking shelter then approached Rudra, the Cardinal God, Endower of Solace, 
and who husbands all the created animals inclusive of human-animals, namely Shiva, 
and they prayed to him saying 'save, save us.'

shloka:
एवमुक्तस्ततो देवैर्देवदेवेश्वरः प्रभुः |
प्रादुरासीत् ततोऽत्रैव शंखचक्रधरो हरिः
translation:
This way while the gods are praying the Lord and God of Gods, namely Shiva, then 
handling his disc and conch-shell Vishnu has also revealed himself at that place.

shloka:
उवाचैनं स्मितं कृत्वा रुद्रं शूलधरं हरिः |
दैवतैर्मथ्यमाने तु तत्पूर्वं समुपस्थितम्
translation:
And Vishnu smilingly spoke to wielder of trident Rudra, 'oh, god the best, whatever 
element that has emerged from the churning of Milk Ocean by gods, that shall belong 
to you, isn't it. By virtue of your position as the foremost god among gods, oh, 
omnicompetent god Shiva, you please accept this poison applying yourself to that 
position of foremost god, and deeming this poison, haalahala, as a foremost oblation 
to your godhood'. [1-45-23, 24]

shloka:
इत्युक्त्वा च सुरश्रेष्ठस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत |
देवतानां भयं दृष्ट्वा श्रुत्वा वाक्यं तु शार्ङ्गिणः
translation:
Saying so Vishnu, the best one among gods, has disappeared then and there only. 
And on observing the scare of gods and also on paying heed to the words of the Wielder 
of Bow calledshaar~Nga, namely Vishnu, god Shiva gulped that lethal poison,haalaahala, as if it is ambrosia. [1-45-25, 26a]

shloka:
देवान् विसृज्य देवेशो जगाम भगवान् हरः॥ १-४५-२६
ततो देवासुराः सर्वे ममन्थू रघुनन्दन।
translation:
The god of gods Hara then left for his abode Kailash parting with other gods, and 
oh, Rama, the joy of Raghu's dynasty, the gods and non-gods have continued to churn 
the Milky Ocean. [1-45-26b, 27a]

shloka:
प्रविवेशाथ पातालं मन्थानः पर्वतोत्तमः॥ १-४५-२७
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः तुष्टुवुर्मधुसूदनम्।
translation:
Now the loftiest mountain that is being used as stirrer, namely Mt. Mandara, has 
caved into the netherworld, thereby the gods along with gandharva-s have prayed 
to Madhusuudana, the other name of Vishnu. [1-45-27b, 28a]

shloka:
त्वं गतिः सर्वभूतानां विशेषेण दिवौकसाम्॥ १-४५-२८
पालयास्मान् महाबाहो गिरिमुद्धर्तुमर्हसि।
translation:
'You alone are the recourse to all beings, especially to the dwellers in heavens, 
oh ambidextrous god Vishnu, you safeguard us, it will be apt of you elevate the 
mountain.' So prayed gods to Vishnu. [1-45-28b, 29a]

shloka:
इति श्रुत्वा हृषीकेशः कामठं रूपमास्थितः॥ १-४५-२९
पर्वतं पृष्ठतः कृत्वा शिश्ये तत्रोदधौ हरिः।
translation:
Hearing the prayer of gods Vishnu, Hrisheekesha, the controller of senses, adopting 
the form of a tortoise and positioning the stirring Mt. Mandara on that tortoiseshell, 
he lay recumbent at the bottom of Milky Ocean as a base to the stirrer. [1-45-29b, 
30a]

shloka:
पर्वताग्रं तु लोकात्मा हस्तेनाक्रम्य केशवः॥ १-४५-३०
देवानां मध्यतः स्थित्वा ममन्थ पुरुषोत्तमः।
translation:
Keshava then reached out his hand and grasped the mountaintop as he is the Cosmic-Soul, 
and thus staying amid gods that Supreme Person Vishnu participated in churning the 
ocean by holding the stirring mountain upright. [1-45-30b, 31a]

shloka:
अथ वर्षसहस्रेण आयुर्वेदमयः पुमान्॥ १-४५-३१
उदतिष्ठत् सुधर्मात्मा सदण्डः सकमण्डलुः।
पूर्वं धन्वन्तरिर्नाम अप्सराश्च सुवर्चसः॥ १-४५-३२
translation:
After a thousand years of churning, then a male personality, an epitome of Life 
Sciences, namelyaayurveda, a highly righteous soul, named Dhanvantari, 
has firstly surfaced with his arm-rest-stick and with his handy water-vessel, and 
then the remarkably elegant Apsara-s, angelic damsels, have emerged next to him 
from the Milky Ocean. [1-45-31b, 32]

shloka:
अप्सु निर्मथनादेव रसात्तस्माद्वरस्त्रियः।
उत्पेतुर्मनुजश्रेष्ठ तस्मादप्सरसोऽभवन्॥ १-४५-३३
translation:
Choicest females have come out an elixir obtained on absolute churning of the waters 
of Milk Ocean, oh, best one among men, Rama, thereby that genera of females became 
Apsara-s.

shloka:
षष्टिः कोट्योऽभवंस्तासामप्सराणां सुवर्चसाम्।
असन्ख्येयास्तु काकुत्स्थ यास्तासां परिचारिकाः॥ १-४५-३४
translation:
Six hundred millions of such Apsara-s with amazing dazzle have emerged from the 
churning of Milky Ocean, oh, descendent of Kakutstha, and their maidservants who 
emerged along with them are innumerable.

shloka:
न ताः स्म प्रतिगृह्णन्ति सर्वे ते देवदानवाः।
अप्रतिग्रहणादेव ता वै साधारणाः स्मृताः॥ १-४५-३५
translation:
Anybody either from gods or demons espoused them, and when none espoused them they 
are virtually reckoned as 'general-purpose' Apsara-females.

shloka:
वरुणस्य ततः कन्या वारुणी रघुनन्दन।
उत्पपात महाभागा मार्गमाणा परिग्रहम्॥ १-४५-३६
translation:
Oh, descendent of Raghu, then the heaven-sent damsel Vaaruni came up from Milky 
Ocean searching for her espousal, who is the daughter of Varuna, the Rain-god, and 
who incidentally is the presiding deity of hard liquors and also called assura.

shloka:
दितेः पुत्रा न तां राम जगृहुर्वरुणात्मजाम्।
अदितेस्तु सुता वीर जगृहुस्तामनिन्दिताम्॥ १-४५-३७
translation:
Oh, Rama, the sons of Diti, namely asuraa-s, have not espoused that daughter of 
Rain-god, but oh, brave Rama, the sons of Aditi on their part, namely sura-s, have 
espoused that impeccable Vaaruni.

shloka:
असुरास्तेन दैतेयाः सुरास्तेनादितेः सुताः।
हृष्टाः प्रमुदिताश्चासन् वारुणीग्रहणात् सुराः॥ १-४५-३८
translation:
Thereby the sons of Diti are calledasuraa-s, and the sons of Aditi are 
calledsuraa-s, and gods are delighted and rejoiced on espousing Vaaruni.

shloka:
उच्चैःश्रवा हयश्रेष्ठो मणिरत्नं च कौस्तुभम्।
उदतिष्ठन्नरश्रेष्ठ तथैवामृतमुत्तमम्॥ १-४५-३९
translation:
Then a best horse called Ucchaishravaa has emerged, oh, Rama, the best among men, 
and then a gem of a jewel, called Kaustubha, and like thatamrita, the 
Supreme ambrosial elixir of gods, have also emerged.

shloka:
अथ तस्य कृते राम महानासीत् कुलक्षयः।
अदितेस्तु ततः पुत्रा दितेः पुत्रानसूदयन्॥ १-४५-४०
translation:
Owing to the dispute regarding the possession of that ambrosia, oh, Rama, then 
there chanced a rampant ethnic havoc, and then the sons of Aditi have havocked the 
sons of Diti.

shloka:
एकतामगमन् सर्वे असुरा राक्षसैः सह।
युद्धमासीन् महाघोरं वीरत्रैलोक्यमोहनम्॥ १-४५-४१
translation:
All the asura-s and demons have come to one side against sura-s, and there occurred 
a very gruesome war which was perplexing to all the triad of universe viz., ethereal, 
real and surreal spheres.

shloka:
यदा क्षयं गतं सर्वं तदा विष्णुर्महाबलः।
अमृतं सोऽहरत्तूर्णं मायामास्थाय मोहिनीम्॥ १-४५-४२
translation:
When everything is wading into annihilation then that omnicompetent Vishnu swiftly 
impounded Amrita, the Divine Elixir, by assuming his illusory power of Mohini.

shloka:
ये गताभिमुखं विष्णुमक्षरं पुरुषोत्तमम्।
संपिष्टास्ते तदा युद्धे विष्णुना प्रभविष्णुना॥ १-४५-४३
translation:
Whoever confronted that Eternal and Supreme Person, namely Vishnu, in that war, 
then Vishnu whose blaze is threefold as manifest in the sun, fire and lightning, 
has pulverised him.

shloka:
अदितेरात्मजा वीरा दितेः पुत्रान्निजघ्‌निरे।
अस्मिन् घोरे महायुद्धे दैतेयादित्ययोर्भृशम्॥ १-४५-४४
translation:
In this horrendous war between the progeny of Diti, namely demons, and the progeny 
of Aditi, namely gods, the sons of Aditi being gods, have altogether massacred the 
demonic sons of Diti.

shloka:
निहत्य दितिपुत्रांश्च राज्यं प्राप्य पुरन्दरः।
शशास मुदितो लोकान् सर्षिसन्घान् सचारणान्॥ १-४५-४५
translation:
"On eliminating the demonic sons of Diti and on acquiring kingdom of heaven, that 
eliminator of enemy cities, namely Indra, happily ruled the worlds that are inclusive 
of sages and caarana-s." Thus Vishvamitra continued his narration about Vishaala 
city and its emergence.

shloka: इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे पञ्चचत्वारिंशः सर्गः

हतेषु तेषु पुत्रेषु दितिः परमदुःखिता |
मारीचं काश्यपं राम भर्तारमिदमब्रवीत्
translation:
"Oh, Rama, Lady Diti was highly anguished for those sons that are killed 
			and said this to her husband, Sage Kashyapa, the son of Sage Maareechi." 
			Thus Vishvamitra continued narration.

shloka:
हतपुत्रास्मि भगवंस्तव पुत्रैर्महाबलैः |
शक्रहन्तारमिच्छामि पुत्रं दीर्घतपोऽर्जितम्
translation:
Oh, god, I am bereaved of my sons who are killed by your great mighty 
			sons, the sons of your second wife Aditi, as such I wish to bear a son, 
			who is achievable by sustained penance, for he shall be the exterminator 
			of Indra.

shloka:
साहं तपश्चरिष्यामि गर्भं मे दातुमर्हसि |
ईश्वरं शक्रहन्तारं त्वमनुज्ञातुमर्हसि
translation:
'Such a bereaved mother as I am, I wish to undertake asceticism for 
			a son who shall become an exterminator of Indra, and who shall be the 
			ruler of worlds. As such, it will be apt of you to permit me for asceticism, 
			and further it will be apt of you to accord me pregnancy with such a 
			son.' Thus Diti spoke to her husband Kaashyapa.

shloka:
तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा मारीचः कश्यपस्तदा |
प्रत्युवाच महातेजा दितिं परमदुःखिताम्
translation:
On hearing her request the great resplendent sage Kaashyapa, the son 
			of Sage Mareechi, replied Diti, who is deeply mournful.

shloka:
एवं भवतु भद्रं ते शुचिर्भव तपोधने |
जनयिष्यसि पुत्रं त्वं शक्रहन्तारमाहवे
translation:
" 'So be it... oh, ascetically wealthy lady, you be blest, if you abide 
			by the propriety of the practises of asceticism, then you will be delivering 
			a son who can become an exterminator of Indra in war.

shloka:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु शुचिर्यदि भविष्यसि |
पुत्रं त्रैलोक्यहन्तारं मत्तस्त्वं जनयिष्यसि
translation:
'If you can complete a thousand years of asceticism punctiliously, 
			by my grace you can deliver a son who can be a husbander of three worlds.' 
			Thus Sage Kaashyapa advised his wife Diti.

shloka:
एवमुक्त्वा महातेजाः पाणिना स ममार्ज ताम् |
तमालभ्य ततः स्वस्तीत्युक्त्वा तपसे ययौ
translation:
Saying thus that great resplendent sage patted her, and then on his 
			touching her she is consecrated, and then that sage Kaashyapa departed 
			for his ascetic practises, saying 'be blest.'

shloka:
गते तस्मिन्नरश्रेष्ठ दितिः परमहर्षिता |
कुशप्लवं सामासाद्य तपस्तेपे सुदारुणम्
translation:
On the exit of Sage Kaashyapa, oh, best one among men Rama, highly 
			elated Diti reached the sacred place called Kushaplava, on which the 
			present City of Vishala is now standing, and practised a highly rigorous 
			asceticism.

shloka:
तपस्तस्यां हि कुर्वत्यां परिचर्यां चकार ह |
सहस्राक्षो नरश्रेष्ठ परया गुणसंपदा
translation:
While she is truly practising asceticism, oh, the best among men Rama, 
			that Thousand-eyed god Indra has indeed rendered services with his abundant 
			and surpassing veracities to her, who is none other than his maternal-aunt.

shloka:
अग्निं कुशान् काष्ठमपः फलं मूलं तथैव च |
न्यवेदयत् सहस्राक्षो यच्चान्यदपि कांक्षितम्
translation:
The Thousand-eyed god Indra made available fire, firewood, water, the 
			sacred Kusha grass, fruits and like that tubers also, and whatever other 
			items she required in her ascetic practise.

shloka:
गात्रसंवाहनैश्चैव श्रमापनयनैस्तथा |
शक्रः सर्वेषु कालेषु दितिं परिचचार ह
translation:
All the time Indra indeed served Diti by massaging her body, and other 
			means of removing her bodily strain resulting from her arduous practises.

shloka:
पूर्णे वर्षसहस्रे तु दशोने रघुनंदन |
दितिः परमसंहृष्टा सहस्राक्षमथाब्रवीत्
translation:
Oh, Rama, the descendent of Raghu, when ten years are less to complete 
			the thousand years span of her ascetics, Diti is highly rejoiced as 
			her ambition is going to fructify in just ten more years, and then she 
			spoke to the Thousand-eyed god, Indra.

shloka:
तपश्चरन्त्या वर्षाणि दश वीर्यवतां वर |
अवशिष्टानि भद्रं ते भ्रातरं द्रक्ष्यसे ततः
translation:
Oh, best one among the valiant ones, Indra, to me who am practising 
			asceticism ten years are remaining to complete, then you can see your 
			brother, you be safe.

shloka:
यमहं त्वत्कृते पुत्र तमाधास्ये जयोत्सुकम् |
त्रैलोक्यविजयं पुत्र सह भोक्ष्यसि विज्वरः
translation:
Oh, son Indra, whom I am bringing up for your reason, I will bring 
			him up as a victory-enthusiast, and oh, son, Indra, along with him conquering 
			the three worlds you can enjoy them, without febrility from your enemies.

shloka:
याचितेन सुरश्रेष्ट पित्रा तव महात्मना |
वरो वर्षसहस्रान्ते मम दत्तः सुतं प्रति
translation:
Oh, best one among gods, Indra, on my prayer your high-souled father 
			Sage Kaashyapa bestowed this boon on me for a son, which materialises 
			at the end of thousand years, and only ten more years are to slip by.

shloka:
इत्युक्त्वा च दितिस्तत्र प्राप्ते मध्यन्दिनेश्वरे |
निद्रयापहृता देवी पादौ कृत्वाथ शीर्षतः
translation:
When Diti was saying thus, the noontime sun was reigning high that 
			lady is stolen over by sleep keeping her feet headward.

shloka:
दृष्ट्वा तामशुचिं शक्रः पादयोः कृतमूर्धजाम् |
शिरःस्थाने कृतौ पादौ जहास च मुमोद च
translation:
On observing her who has become impious by placing her head at feet-side 
			and braid falling on feet, Indra is gladdened and laughed at her failed 
			asceticism.

shloka:
तस्याः शरीरविवरं प्रविवेश पुरंदरः |
गर्भं च सप्तधा राम चिच्छेद परमात्मवान्
translation:
Oh, Rama, being a highly courageous one, Indra the destroyer of enemy 
			fastnesses, entered the body of Diti through her vaginal aperture and 
			rent her foetus asunder into seven fragments.

shloka:
भिद्यमानस्ततो गर्भो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा |
रुरोद सुस्वरं राम ततो दितिरबुध्यत
translation:
Oh, Rama, then that foetus wailed clamorously while being sliced with 
			Thunderbolt that has hundred cutting edges, and then Diti woke up.

shloka:
मा रुदो मा रुदश्चेति गर्भं शक्रोऽभ्यभाषत |
बिभेद च महातेजा रुदन्तमपि वासवः
translation:
'Do not scream, do not scream...' thus Indra was coaxing the foetus, 
			and even though that foetus is screaming piteously the great resplendent 
			Indra has gone on fragmenting it.

shloka:
न हन्तव्यं न हन्तव्यमित्येवं दितिरब्रवीत् |
निष्पपात ततः शक्रो मातुर्वचनगौरवात्
translation:
'Unkillable, unkillable is my foetus...' thus Diti raved in that way, 
			and then Indra fell out of the womb honouring his stepmother's entreaty.

shloka:
प्रांजलिर्वज्रसहितो दितिं शक्रोऽभ्यभाषत |
अशुचिर्देवि सुप्तासि पादयोः कृतमूर्धजा
translation:
Indra humbly folding his palms that are still handling his bloody Thunderbolt 
			spoke to Diti, 'oh, lady, you have become impious when your braid touched 
			your feet and when you have gone to sleep in midday, and you vow is 
			thwarted.'

shloka:
तदन्तरमहं लब्ध्वा शक्रहन्तारमाहवे |
अभिदं सप्तधा देवि तन्मे त्वम् क्षन्तुमर्हसि
translation:
"Thereby I gained a chance to eliminate him who can eliminate Indra 
			in a battle. Hence I fragmented your foetus into seven fragments, and 
			it will be apt of you to pardon me for that act of mine." So said 
			Indra to lady Diti. Thus, Sage Vishvamitra continued narration about 
			City of Vishaala.

shloka:
सप्तधा तु कृते गर्भे दितिः परमदुःखिता |
सहस्राक्षं दुराधर्षं वाक्यं सानुनयाब्रवीत्
translation:
"Diti was highly anguished when her foetus is rendered into sevenfold, and spoke these 
appeasing words to the indomitable Thousand-eyed Indra." Thus Vishvamitra continued his narration about 
City Vishala.

shloka:
ममापराधाद्गर्भोऽयं सप्तधा शकलीकृतः |
नापराधो हि देवेश तवात्र बलसूदन
translation:
'Oh, Indra, the eliminator of demon Bala, this foetus of mine is sliced into seven 
segments owing to my own misdeed, oh, ruler of gods, Indra, indeed there is no iniquity of yours in 
this matter.' Thus Diti started speaking to Indra.

shloka:
प्रियं त्वत्कृतमिच्छामि मम गर्भविपर्यये |
मरुतां सप्तसप्तानां स्थानपाला 
भवन्तु ते
translation:
Though a reversal has happened against my thinking in the matter of my pregnancy, 
let these seven segments become your seven Wind-gods, the rulers of seven ethereal-places, under your 
ruler-ship.

shloka:
वातस्कंधा इमे सप्त चरन्तु दिवि पुत्रक |
मारुता इति विख्याता दिव्यरूपा ममात्मजाः
translation:
Oh, son Indra, let these seven sons of mine become the seven presiding deities of 
Cosmic Air Divisions and let them move in heaven with heavenly forms.

shloka:
ब्रह्मलोकं चरत्वेक इन्द्रलोकं तथापरः |
दिव्यवायुरिति ख्यातः तृतीयोऽपि 
महायशाः
translation:
One from the seven may permeate Brahma's abode, likewise another may permeate the 
heaven of Indra, and even the third one, let him become a greatly celebrated and reputed as Divine Wind, 
and he may circulate in entire universe.

shloka:
चत्वारस्तु सुरश्रेष्ठ दिशो वै तव शासनात् |
संचरिष्यन्ति भद्रं ते कलेन हि ममात्मजाः
translation:
'Oh, chief of gods, Indra, let four of my sons permeate four directions according to 
time and at your command, let safety betide you, and let them be renowned verily by the name given by 
you as 'Marut,' because you have coaxed the crying fragments of foetus saying, 'maa ruda, maa ruda, 
'do not cry, do not cry...' Thus Diti said to Indra. [1-47-6, 7a]

shloka: तस्यास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सहस्राक्षः पुरंदरः
translation:
On hearing her words, the Thousand-eyed destroyer of enemy's citadels and a demon named 
Bala, namely Indra, spoke this word to Diti, humbly adjoining his palms. [1-47-7b, 8a]

shloka: सर्वमेतद्यथोक्तं ते भविष्यति न संशयः
translation:
" 'All this will happen as you have said, undoubtedly, and your offspring, the Maaruta-s, 
would be pervading in the forms of gods, you be safe.' Thus Indra assured Diti. Those two, the stepmother 
Diti and the stepson Indra, on arriving at a decision in that ascetic forest, departed to heaven fulfilling 
their purposes. Thus we heard the legend." Thus Vishvamitra continued his narration. [1-47-8b, 9, 10a]

shloka: एष देशः स काकुत्स्थ महेन्द्राध्युषितः पुरा
translation:
Oh, Rama of Kakutstha, this province is that one which was once presided over by Indra, 
and where he rendered services to that accomplished one in her asceticism, namely lady Diti. [1-47-10b, 
11a]

shloka: इक्ष्वाकोस्तु नरव्याघ्र पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः
translation:
To king Ikshvaku of Vishaala, oh, tigerly-man Rama, a highly righteous son was born 
through queen Alambusa, and he was renowned as Vishaala. There is a city in this place constructed by 
him and known by his own name, Vishaala. [1-47-11b, 12]

shloka:
विशालस्य सुतो राम हेमचन्द्रो महाबलः |
सुचन्द्र इति विख्यातो हेमचन्द्रादनंतरः
translation:
"Oh, Rama, Vishaala's son is the great-mighty Hemachandra, and Hemachandra's son is highly 
renowned as Suchandra..

shloka:
सुचन्द्रतनयो राम धूम्राश्व इति विश्रुतः |
धूम्राश्वतनयश्चापि सृंजयः समपद्यत
translation:
"The son of Suchandra became famous as Dhuumraashva, and oh, Rama, Dhuumraashva derived 
his son named Srinjaya.

shloka:
सृंजयस्य सुतः श्रीमान् सहदेवः प्रतापवान् |
कुशाश्वः सहदेवस्य पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः
translation:
The fortunate and valorous son of Srinjaya is Sahadeva, and the son of Sahadeva is the 
most righteous Kushaashva.

shloka:
कुशाश्वस्य महातेजाः सोमदत्तः प्रतापवान् |
सोमदत्तस्य पुत्रस्तु काकुत्स्थ इति 
विश्रुतः
translation:
The highly resplendent and dauntless Somadatta is the son of Kushaashva and Somadatta's 
son is highly reputed as Kakutstha.

shloka:
तस्य पुत्रो महातेजाः संप्रत्येष पुरीमिमाम् |
आवसत्परमप्रख्यः सुमतिर्नाम दुर्जयः
translation:
Presently that Kakutstha's son named Sumati, who is a great-resplendent one, an unconquerable 
one, and a highly celebrated one is dwelling in this city.

shloka:
इक्ष्वाकोस्तु प्रसादेन सर्वे वैशालिका नृपाः |
दीर्घायुषो महात्मानो वीर्यवन्तः 
सुधार्मिकाः
translation:
By the grace of Ikshvaku, the successive kings of Vishaala have longevity, intrepidity, 
well-off in generosity, and they were great-souled ones.

shloka:
इहाद्य रजनीमेकां सुखं स्वप्स्यामहे वयम् |
श्वः प्रभाते नरश्रेष्ठ जनकं द्रष्टुमर्हसि
translation:
"Today we may gladly go to sleep here for a night, and oh, best one among men, and it 
will be apt of you to see Janaka, the King of Mithila tomorrow morning." Thus Sage Vishvamitra spoke 
to Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka:
सुमतिस्तु महातेजा विश्वामित्रमुपागतम् |
श्रुत्वा नरवरश्रेष्ठः प्रत्यागच्छन् 
महायशाः
translation:
The best one among best men, a widely reputed and the highly resplendent king of Vishaala, 
namely Sumati, having heard that Vishvamitra has arrived at the precincts of the city, came to him for 
a warm welcome.

shloka:
पूजां च परमां कृत्वा सोपाध्यायः सबान्धवः |
प्रांजलिः कुशलं पृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रमथाब्रवीत्
translation:
King Sumati arrived along with his mentors and family members, offered an excellent veneration 
to Vishvamitra, and then spoke to the sage with adjoined palms enquiring about his well being.

shloka:
धन्योऽस्म्यनुगृहीतोऽस्मि यस्य मे विषयं मुने |
संप्राप्तो दर्शनं चैव नास्ति 
धन्यतरो मम
translation:
"To which province you have visited that happens to be mine, thereby I could get an audience 
of yours without stirring myself from my country, hence none will be more fortunate than me." So said 
king Sumati to Vishvamitra.

shloka:
पृष्ट्वा तु कुशलं तत्र परस्परसमागमे |
कथान्ते सुमतिर्वाक्यं व्याजहार महामुनिम्
translation:
When those two, Vishvamitra and Sumati, have met one another there at that place, 
king Sumati raised the topic of Rama and Lakshmana, after exchanging greetings and 
enquiring about the well-being of the great-saint Vishvamitra.

shloka:
इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देवतुल्यपराक्रमौ |
गजसिंहगती वीरौ शार्दूलवृषभोपमौ
translation:
"These two youngsters, oh, sage, let safety betide you, striding like audacious 
elephants and arrogant lions, bearing a similitude to adventurous tigers and adamantine 
bulls, and wielding quivers, swords, and bows, are valorous with their valour matching 
that of Vishnu, and with their eyes broad like lotus-petals and with youthfulness 
in the offing they look like the exceptionally beautiful twin-gods, Ashwin-brothers,
