"Women, like you, on the other hand who are endowed with virtues, who look with
detachment on prosperity and adversity in this world, therefore dwell in heaven as those who
performed meritorious deeds."

shloka:
तदेवमेनम् त्वमनुच्रता सती |
पतिव्रतानाम् समयानुवर्तिनी |
भव स्वभर्तुः सहधर्मचारिणी |
यश्श्च धर्मम् च ततः समाप्स्यसि
translation:
"Thus devoted to your lord, loyal to your husband, following established rules, you
become an honest wife to your husband and obtain merit and renown."

shloka:
सा तु एवम् उक्ता वैदेही अनसूयान् असूयया |
प्रतिपूज्य वचो मन्दम् प्रवक्तुम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
Anasuya having spoken thus, Seetha without any jealousy, full of reverence for her,
addressed her gently as follows:

shloka:
न एतद् आश्चर्यम् आर्याया यन् माम् त्वम् अनुभाषसे |
विदितम् तु मम अप्य् एतद् यथा नार्याः पतिर् गुरुः
translation:
"It is not a surprise that a venerable woman like a you, talk to me like this, for,
I know well that a husband is a respectable person for a woman."

shloka:
यद्य् अप्य् एष भवेद् भर्ता मम आर्ये वृत्त वर्जितः |
अद्वैधम् उपवर्तव्यः तथा अप्य् एष मया भवेत्
translation:
"O, venerable woman! Even if my husband be without fortune, he should unhesitatingly
be obeyed by me."

shloka:
किम् पुनर् यो गुण श्लाघ्यः सानुक्रोशो जित इन्द्रियः |
स्थिर अनुरागो धर्म आत्मा मातृ वर्ती पितृ प्रियः
translation:
"How much more, if he be renowned for his virtues, compassionate, master of my
heart, who is ever affectionate, a religious person, manifests the tenderness of a mother and a
father to me."

shloka:
याम् वृत्तिम् वर्तते रामः कौसल्यायाम् महा बलः |
ताम् एव नृप नारीणाम् अन्यासाम् अपि वर्तते
translation:
The exceedingly strong Rama bears himself to all other Queens, as he exercises his
behaviour towards his mother, Kausalya."

shloka:
सकृद् दृष्टासु अपि स्त्रीषु नृपेण नृप वत्सलः |
मातृवद् वर्तते वीरो मानम् उत्सृज्य धर्मवित्
translation:
"The valiant and pious Rama who is devoted to Dasartha and free from all sense of
importance treats all those women as his mothers on whom Dasaratha has even once bestowed a single
glance."

shloka:
आगग्च्छन्त्याः च विजनम् वनम् एवम् भय आवहम् |
समाहितम् हि मे श्वश्र्वा हृदये यत् स्थितम् महत्
translation:
"While departing for the lonely and fearful forest, my mother-in-law imparted a
great message to me, which I have inscribed in my heart."

shloka:
प्राणि प्रदान काले च यत् पुरा तु अग्नि सम्निधौ |
अनुशिष्टा जनन्या अस्मि वाक्यम् तद् अपि मे धृतम्
translation:
"What my mother taught me when witnessed by the fire, earlier at the time of my
marriage with Rama, I shall always remember them."

shloka:
नवी कृतम् तु तत् सर्वम् वाक्यैः ते धर्म चारिणि |
पति शुश्रूषणान् नार्याः तपो न अन्यद् विधीयते
translation:
"O, virtuous woman! By your words, all that is being renewed. No austerity, other
than obedience to one's husband is decreed for a woman."

shloka: सावित्री पति शुश्रूषाम् कृत्वा स्वर्गे महीयते
translation:
Savitri* is now highly honoured in heaven, for having served her lord faithfully
heaven, You too, having followed this, will proceed to heaven, in showing obedience to your
husband."

shloka:
वरिष्ठा सर्व नारीणाम् एषा च दिवि देवता |
रोहिणी च विना चन्द्रम् मुहूर्तम् अपि दृश्यते
translation:
"This goddess Rohini, the excellent among all women, is not seen without the moon
even for a single moment in the sky."

shloka:
एवम् विधाः च प्रवराः स्त्रियो भर्तृ दृढ व्रताः |
देव लोके महीयन्ते पुण्येन स्वेन कर्मणा
translation:
"Such excellent women, devoted to their husbands, and by their meritorious deeds,
are highly honoured in heaven."

shloka:
ततो अनसूया सम्हृष्टा श्रुत्वा उक्तम् सीतया वचः |
शिरस्य् आघ्राय च उवाच मैथिलीम् हर्षयन्त्य् उत
translation:
Hearing the words of Seetha, Anasuya was very much pleased, kissed on Seetha's
forehead and spoke delightfully (as follows)

shloka:
नियमैर् विविधैर् आप्तम् तपो हि महद् अस्ति मे |
तत् संश्रित्य बलम् सीते चन्दये त्वाम् शुचि व्रते
translation:
"O, Seetha with a bright smile! There is a great merit acquired by me in virtue of
my various pious observances. Through that power, I wish to confer a boon on you."

shloka:
उपपन्नम् च युक्तम् च वचनम् तव मैथिलि |
प्रीता च अस्म्य् उचितम् किम् ते करवाणि ब्रवीह्यहम्
translation:
"O, Seetha! Your words are suitable for the occasion and are charming too. I am
satisfied. Tell me what good I may do for you."

shloka:
तस्यास्तद्वचनम् श्रुत्वा विस्मिता मन्दविस्मया |
कृतम् इत्य् अब्रवीत् सीता तपो बल समन्विताम्
translation:
Hearing those words of Anasuya, Seetha was surprised and with a gentle smile spoke
to her, who was richly endowed with the power of askesis, saying; "Everything stands fulfilled (by
your grace).

shloka:
सा तु एवम् उक्ता धर्मज्ना तया प्रीततरा अभवत् |
सफलम् च प्रहर्षम् ते हन्त सीते करोम्यहम्
translation:
Thus spoken by Seetha, the pious-minded Anasuya became more delighted and said: "O,
Seetha! Alas! I will create a great joy for you, which will be to your advantage."

shloka:
इदम् दिव्यम् वरम् माल्यम् वस्त्रम् आभरणानि च |
अन्ग रागम् च वैदेहि महा अर्हम् अनुलेपनम्
translation:
"O, Seetha, the daughter of Videha kingdom! Here are divine gifts: a garland, an
apparel, jewels, a scented cosmetic and rare body-cream. These are all given by me to adorn your
limbs. They will be ever worthy of your and will remain in tact (even after constant use)."

shloka:
अन्ग रागेण दिव्येन लिप्त अन्गी जनक आत्मजे |
शोभयिष्यामि भर्तारम् यथा श्रीर् विष्णुम् अव्ययम्
translation:
"O, Seetha! Your body, anointed with these heavenly cosmetics, will cause your
husband to look beautiful, as Lakshmi (the goddess of fortune and beauty) does the imperishable
Vishnu (the Lord of Preservation)."

shloka:
सा वस्त्रम् अन्ग रागम् च भूषणानि स्रजः तथा |
मैथिली प्रतिजग्राह प्रीति दानम् अनुत्तमम्
translation:
Seetha accepted the apparel, the scented cosmetic, the jewels and the garlands as
unsurpassed gifts of love.

shloka:
प्रतिगृह्य च तत् सीता प्रीति दानम् यशस्विनी |
श्लिष्ट अन्जलि पुटा धीरा समुपास्त तपो धनाम्
translation:
Having accepted those gifts of love, the illustrious Seetha with joined palms, sat
near that female ascetic.

shloka:
तथा सीताम् उपासीनाम् अनसूया दृढ व्रता |
वचनम् प्रष्टुम् आरेभे कांचिद् त्प्रियाम् कथामनु
translation:
To inquire about a lovely tale of once upon a time, Anasuya who was firm in
austerity, started asking the following words to Seetha who was sitting near her in that
manner.

shloka:
स्वयम् वरे किल प्राप्ता त्वम् अनेन यशस्विना |
राघवेण इति मे सीते कथा श्रुतिम् उपागता
translation:
"O, Seetha! It is so said that you were won by the illustrious Rama through a
process of your self-choosing (svayamvara)*. This report has reached my ear."

shloka:
ताम् कथाम् श्रोतुम् इग्च्छामि विस्तरेण च मैथिलि |
यथा अनुभूतम् कार्त्स्न्येन तन् मे त्वम् वक्तुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"O, Seetha! I wish to hear that narrative in detail. Hence, tell me that tale in
full as you experienced it."

shloka:
एवम् उक्ता तु सा सीता ताम् ततो धर्म चारिणीम् |
श्रूयताम् इति च उक्त्वा वै कथयाम् आस ताम् कथाम्
translation:
Then, Seetha obediently answered, saying "Hear me" and began to truly narrate that
tale of Svayamvara to the virtuous woman, Anasuya."

shloka:
मिथिला अधिपतिर् वीरो जनको नाम धर्मवित् |
क्षत्र धर्मण्य् अभिरतो न्यायतः शास्ति मेदिनीम्
translation:
"A king of Mithila kingdom, named Janaka who was valiant and a knower of
righteousness, was devoted to the duty of his warrior class and was ruling the earth in a fitting
manner."

shloka:
तस्य लान्गल हस्तस्य कर्षतः क्षेत्र मण्डलम् |
अहम् किल उत्थिता भित्त्वा जगतीम् नृपतेः सुता
translation:
"While he was furrowing a territory of land, holding a plough in his hand, it is so
said that I came forth, splitting up the land, as a daughter of that king."

shloka:
स माम् दृष्ट्वा नर पतिर् मुष्टि विक्षेप तत् परः |
पांशु गुण्ठित सर्व अन्गीम् विस्मितो जनको अभवत्
translation:
"The king Janaka, who was absorbed in scattering handfuls of seeds was surprised to
see me, with all my limbs covered with dust."

shloka:
अनपत्येन च स्नेहाद् अन्कम् आरोप्य च स्वयम् |
मम इयम् तनया इत्य् उक्त्वा स्नेहो मयि निपातितः
translation:
"Placing me personally in his lap with affection, that childless king Janaka called
one as his daughter, and was very fond of me since then."

shloka:
अन्तरिक्षे च वाग् उक्ता अप्रतिमा मानुषी किल |
एवम् एतन् नर पते धर्मेण तनया तव
translation:
"It is said that voice resembling that of a human being in the air above me rang
out, saying": "O, King! Let it be so. This divine child without a match is a daughter to you,
rightly."

shloka:
ततः प्रहृष्टो धर्म आत्मा पिता मे मिथिला अधिपः |
अवाप्तो विपुलाम् ऋद्धिम् माम् अवाप्य नर अधिपः
translation:
"Thereafter, my father the pious mind the lord of men and the king of Mithila
kingdom was rejoiced in my possession and acquired extensive property."

shloka:
दत्त्वा च अस्मि इष्टवद् देव्यै ज्येष्ठायै पुण्य कर्मणा |
तया सम्भाविता च अस्मि स्निग्धया मातृ सौहृदात्
translation:
"That king performing auspicious acts gave me into the care of the chief Queen. She
nourished me fondly and with maternal affection."

shloka:
पति सम्योग सुलभम् वयो दृष्ट्वा तु मे पिता |
चिन्ताम् अभ्यगमद् दीनो वित्त नाशाद् इव अधनः
translation:
"Seeing my age to be such, when union with a husband can be easily had, my father
fell a prey to anxiety like an indigent man, feeling miserable by the loss of all his
possessions."

shloka:
सदृशाच् च अपकृष्टाच् च लोके कन्या पिता जनात् |
प्रधर्षणाम् अवाप्नोति शक्रेण अपि समो भुवि
translation:
"Eventhough the father of an unmarried girl be like Indra himself on earth, suffers
indignity in the world from the suitor's men, no matter whether they are equal or inferior to
him."

shloka:
ताम् धर्षणाम् अदूरस्थाम् संदृश्य आत्मनि पार्थिवः |
चिन्न्ता अर्णव गतः पारम् न आससाद अप्लवो यथ
translation:
"Perceiving that ill-treatment threatening him at no distant date, the king Janaka
was plunged into an ocean of anxiety and did not reach its end any more than a man without a bark
would reach the end of a sea."

shloka:
अयोनिजाम् हि माम् ज्नात्वा न अध्यगग्च्छत् स चिन्तयन् |
सदृशम् च अनुरूपम् च मही पालः पतिम् मम
translation:
"Knowing me to be the one not emerged from a mother's womb, the king after a deep
reflection, was unable to find a suitable and worthy husband for me."

shloka:
तस्य बुद्धिर् इयम् जाता चिन्तयानस्य सम्ततम् |
स्वयम् वरम् तनूजायाः करिष्यामि इति धीमतः
translation:
"After reflecting thus deeply, the thought came to him, 'I shall inaugurate a
Svayamvara, a process of self-choosing marriage, for my daughter."

shloka:
महा यज्ने तदा तस्य वरुणेन महात्मना |
दत्तम् धनुर् वरम् प्रीत्या तूणी च अक्षय्य सायकौ
translation:
"In ancient days, Janaka received with affection from Varuna the rain-god, an
excellent bow with two quivers that should never lack arrows."

shloka:
असंचाल्यम् मनुष्यैः च यत्नेन अपि च गौरवात् |
तन् न शक्ता नमयितुम् स्वप्नेषु अपि नर अधिपाः
translation:
"That bow was so heavy in weight that no man could lift it up nor any of the kings
were bale to bend it even in their dreams."

shloka:
तद् धनुः प्राप्य मे पित्रा व्याहृतम् सत्य वादिना |
समवाये नर इन्द्राणाम् पूर्वम् आमन्त्र्य पार्थिवान्
translation:
"My truthful father called all the princes first and informed them in a meeting
about the bow to be lifted."

shloka:
इदम् च धनुर् उद्यम्य सज्यम् यः कुरुते नरः |
तस्य मे दुहिता भार्या भविष्यति न संशयः
translation:
"Whoever is able to lift up and string this bow, I will bestow my daughter in
marriage on him. There is no doubt about it."

shloka:
तच् च दृष्ट्वा धनुः श्रेष्ठम् गौरवाद् गिरि सम्निभम् |
अभिवाद्य नृपा जग्मुर् अशक्ताः तस्य तोलने
translation:
"Seeing that excellent bow, resembling a mountain in weight, and being unable to
lift it up, the princes offered salutation to it and went away."

shloka:
सुदीर्घस्य तु कालस्य राघवो अयम् महा द्युतिः |
विश्वामित्रेण सहितो यज्नम् द्रष्टुम् समागतः
translation:
"After a very long time, this Rama born in Raghu dynasty with a great splendour
possessing a true valour, along with his brother Lakshmana together with a sage Visvamitra, came to
witness a sacrifice."

shloka: विश्वामित्रः तु धर्म आत्मा मम पित्रा सुपूजितः
translation:
"The pious-souled Visvamitra, having been received well by my father said to my
father, (as follows):

shloka: सुतौ दशरथस्य इमौ धनुर् दर्शन कान्क्षिणौ
translation:
"These two boys, the sons of Dasaratha wish to see that bow. Show that bow, coming
from gods, to Rama the prince."

shloka: इत्य् उक्तः तेन विप्रेण तद् धनुः समुपानयत्
translation:
"Hearing the words of Vivamitra, Janaka caused the bow to be brought there. The
mighty and the valiant Rama bent that bow merely within an instant and immediately stringed the bow
with the bow-cord and drew the bow to the full."

shloka:
तेन पूरयता वेगान् मध्ये भग्नम् द्विधा धनुः |
तस्य शब्दो अभवद् भीमः पतितस्य अशनेर् इव
translation:
"While Rama was drawing the bow to the full, the bow was broken into two in the
middle due to the resultant jerk. The terrific sound then created was like that of a falling
thunderbolt."

shloka:
ततो अहम् तत्र रामाय पित्रा सत्य अभिसंधिना |
उद्यता दातुम् उद्यम्य जल भाजनम् उत्तमम्
translation:
"Then and there, my father true to his promise decided to bestow me on Rama,
offering him a jar of pure water."

shloka:
दीयमानाम् न तु तदा प्रतिजग्राह राघवः |
अविज्नाय पितुः चन्दम् अयोध्या अधिपतेः प्रभोः
translation:
"But Rama did not consent to accept my hand till the will of his father, the Lord
and the king of Ayodhya had been made known to him."

shloka:
ततः श्वशुरम् आमन्त्र्य वृद्धम् दशरथम् नृपम् |
मम पित्रा अहम् दत्ता रामाय विदित आत्मने
translation:
Thereupon, my father-in-law and the aged Dasaratha was invited to Mithila by my
father and with his approval, I was bestowed on Rama, the knower of the self."

shloka:
मम चैव अनुजा साध्वी ऊर्मिला प्रिय दर्शना |
भार्य अर्थे लक्ष्मणस्य अपि दत्ता पित्रा मम स्वयम्
translation:
"My younger sister Urmila, the virtuous lady of lovely looks was given as a consort
to Lakshmana by my father himself."

shloka:
एवम् दत्ता अस्मि रामाय तदा तस्मिन् स्वयम् वरे |
अनुरक्ता च धर्मेण पतिम् वीर्यवताम् वरम्
translation:
"I was given thus to Rama in that Svayamvara, a process of self-choosing marriage. I
became devoted, by my good works, to my husband who is excellent among men of strength."

shloka:
अनसूया तु धर्मज्ना श्रुत्वा ताम् महतीम् कथाम् |
पर्यष्वजत बाहुभ्याम् शिरस्य् आघ्राय मैथिलीम्
translation:
Hearing that great story, Anasuya the knower of piety kissed Seetha's forehead and
hugged her in her arms.

shloka:
व्यक्त अक्षर पदम् चित्रम् भाषितम् मधुरम् त्वया |
यथा स्वयम् वरम् वृत्तम् तत् सर्वम् हि श्रुतम् मया
translation:
"It was narrated sweetly and amazingly by you, in clear words and syllables. It has
been indeed heard by me how all that Svayamvara, the process of self-choosing marriage took place.
O, the sweet speaking Seetha! I am overjoyed by hearing your story."

shloka: रविर् अस्तम् गतः श्रीमान् उपोह्य रजनीम् शिवाम्
translation:
"O, Fortunate One! While the auspicious night drawing near, the sun has sunk below
horizon. The twittering of the birds can be heard, who, through the day, have sought their
nourishment far and wide and are seeking their shelter for sleep at the time of
evening-twilight."

shloka:
एते च अप्य् अभिषेक आर्द्रा मुनयः फल शोधनाः |
सहिता उपवर्तन्ते सलिल आप्लुत वल्कलाः
translation:
"These ascetics too are returning together, their bark-robes drenched from bathing,
and with uplifted vessels, wet with sprinkled water on them."

shloka:
ऋषीणाम् अग्नि होत्रेषु हुतेषु विधि पुर्वकम् |
कपोत अन्ग अरुणो धूमो दृश्यते पवन उद्धतः
translation:
"From the sacred fire kindled by the sages, according to the scriptural ordinance, a
column of smoke with the hue of a Pigeon's neck, raised by the wind, is seen there."

shloka:
अल्प पर्णा हि तरवो घनी भूताः समन्ततः |
विप्रकृष्टे अपि ये देशे न प्रकाशन्ति वै दिशः
translation:
"Thought their foliage is sparse, the trees look dense all around. The quarters of
the world, by whom the senses are drawn apart, do not shine brilliantly at this place."

shloka:
रजनी रस सत्त्वानि प्रचरन्ति समन्ततः |
तपो वन मृगा ह्य् एते वेदि तीर्थेषु शेरते
translation:
"The animals who wander about at night are ranging everywhere. The deer of the
hermitage are sleeping round the sacred altars."

shloka:
सम्प्रवृत्ता निशा सीते नक्षत्र समलम्कृता |
ज्योत्स्ना प्रावरणः चन्द्रो दृश्यते अभ्युदितो अम्बरे
translation:
"O, Seetha! The night richly adorned with stars has set well in motion. The moon
encircled with light is seen rising in the sky."

shloka:
गम्यताम् अनुजानामि रामस्य अनुचरी भव |
कथयन्त्या हि मधुरम् त्वया अहम् परितोषिता
translation:
"Go now. I give you leave. Be a female companion to Rama. Your sweet conversation
has charmed me."

shloka:
अलम्कुरु च तावत् त्वम् प्रत्यक्षम् मम मैथिलि |
प्रीतिम् जनय मे वत्स दिव्य अलम्काल शोभिनी
translation:
"O, Seetha! O, Dear child! Adorn (with ornaments and apparel gifted by me_ before my
eyes and cause delight to me in embellishing yourself with heavenly jewels."

shloka:
सा तदा समलम्कृत्य सीता सुर सुत उपमा |
प्रणम्य शिरसा तस्यै रामम् तु अभिमुखी ययौ
translation:
Then Seetha, adorning herself, resembled the daughter of a god, and making obeisance
to the feet of Anasuya, she went forward to meet Rama.

shloka:
तथा तु भूषिताम् सीताम् ददर्श वदताम् वरः |
राघवः प्रीति दानेन तपस्विन्या जहर्ष च
translation:
Rama, the most eloquent one, saw Seetha adorned as aforesaid and felt delighted over
the charming gifts of the ascetic.

shloka:
न्यवेदयत् ततः सर्वम् सीता रामाय मैथिली |
प्रीति दानम् तपस्विन्या वसन आभरण स्रजाम्
translation:
Seetha, the daughter of Mithila kingdom then showed to Rama all the apparel, jewels
and garlands the affectionate gifts of Anasuya the hermitess.

shloka:
प्रहृष्टः तु अभवद् रामो लक्ष्मणः च महा रथः |
मैथिल्याः सत्क्रियाम् दृष्ट्वा मानुषेषु सुदुर्लभाम्
translation:
Seeing the respectful treatment, received by Seetha, which was very rare among human
beings, Rama and Lakshmana the great car-warrior felt highly rejoiced.

shloka:
ततः ताम् सर्वरीम् प्रीतः पुण्याम् शशि निभ आननः |
अर्चितः तापसैः सिद्धैर् उवास रघु नन्दनः
translation:
Thereupon, Rama with his face resembling the moon, having been honoured by the holy
ascetics, was delighted and spent that auspicious night there.

shloka:
तस्याम् रात्र्याम् व्यतीतायाम् अभिषिच्य हुत अग्निकान् |
आपृग्च्छेताम् नर व्याघ्रौ तापसान् वन गोचरान्
translation:
While that night passed away, Rama and Lakshmana the tigers among men finished their
ablutions and took leave of the ascetics dwelling the forest, who had just poured oblations into
the sacred fire.

shloka:
ताउ ऊचुः ते वन चराः तापसा धर्म चारिणः |
वनस्य तस्य संचारम् राक्षसैः समभिप्लुतम्
translation:
Those ascetics dwelling in the forest and practising virtue told Rama and Lakshmana
about the region of that forest, which was infested with demons (as follows):

shloka:
रक्षांसि पुरुषादानि नानारूपाणि राघव! |
वसन्त्यस्मिन् महारण्ये व्याळाश्चश्च रुधिराशनाः
translation:
"O, Rama! Various forms of man-eating demons and beasts drinking the blood are
living in this great forest."

shloka:
उच्चिष्टम् वा प्रमत्तम् वा तापसम् धर्मचारिणम् |
अदन्त्यस्मिन् महारण्ये तान्निवारय राघवः
translation:
"O, Rama! They devour an ascetic or a celibate, who has not rinsed his mouth after
finishing his meal or who is inattentive in this great forest. (Pray ward them off!"

shloka:
एष पन्था महर्षीणाम् फलान्य् आहरताम् वने |
अनेन तु वनम् दुर्गम् गन्तुम् राघव ते क्षमम्
translation:
"O, Rama! Here is the path of the great sages, through which they fetch the fruits
in this forest. It is appropriate for you to go by this path in this dangerous forest."

shloka:
इति इव तैः प्रान्जलिभिः तपस्विभिर्
र्द्विजैः कृत स्वस्त्ययनः परम् तपः |
वनम् सभार्यः प्रविवेश राघवः |
सलक्ष्मणः सूर्य इव अभ्र मण्डलम्
translation:
Thus addressed by those Brahmanas having great asceticism, who, with joined palms
paid obedience to him and blessed his journey, Rama the harasser of his foes entered the forest
with his consort along with Lakshmana, as sun enters a mass of clouds.

shloka:
प्रविश्य तु महारण्यं दण्डकारण्यमात्मवान् |
रामो ददर्श दुर्धर्षस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्
translation: On entering the impenetrable Dandaka forest that courageous and unassailable Rama saw a clusters of hermitages of sages.

shloka:
कुशचीरपरिक्षिप्तं ब्राह्म्यां लक्ष्यासमावृतम् |
यथा प्रदीप्तं दुर्दर्शं गगने सूर्यमण्डलम्
translation:
Overspread with Darbha, the sacred grass, and jute clothing, well pervaded with Vedic splendour and well glowing like the 
un-seeable solar arena in the sky, with naked eye.

shloka:
शरण्यं सर्वभूतानां सुसंमृष्टाजिरं सद |
मृगैर्बहुभिराकीर्णं पक्षिसंमैः समातम्
translation:
Those hermitages have well-tidied thresholds on all sides, dense with many deer and teemed with many groups of birds, and 
they are the recourse for all living beings.

shloka:
पूजितं चोपनृत्तं च नित्यमप्सरसाम् गणैः |
विशालैरग्निशरणैः स्रुग्भाण्डैरजिनैः कुशैः
translation:
Those hermitages are always adored by groups of apsarasa-s with their continued dancing, their Holy Fireplaces are very 
broad, and are with oblation items, vessels, deerskins and sacred grass, and they are beaming forth with gigantic trees 
that yield sacred and palatable fruits, and with ritual fuels, and water vessels, tubers and fruits. [3-1-4, 5]

shloka:
बलिहोमार्चितं पुण्यं ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम् |
पुष्पैश्चान्यैः परिक्षिप्तं पद्मिन्या च सपद्मया
translation:
Those hermitages are sacrosanct for Ritual fire is being worshiped with fire-oblations and sacrifices to the reverberating 
Vedic sounds, and they are enwrapped with lotus ponds with lotuses, and even with flowers of forest.

shloka:
फलमूलाशनैर्दान्तैस्चीरकृष्णाजिनाम्बरैः |
सूर्यवैश्वानराभश्च पुराणैर्मुनिभिर्युतम्
translation:
They have age-old saints with controlled senses who are clad in jute cloths and deerskin, and who subsist on fruits and 
tubers alone, ye their resplendence is like that that of the Sun-god or the Fire-god.

shloka:
पुण्यैश्च नियताहारैः शोभितं परमर्षिभिः |
तद् ब्रह्मभवनप्रख्यां ब्रह्मघोषनिनादितम्
translation:
Rama has seen such a cluster of hermitages that is glistening forth just by the presence of holy saints whose sustenance 
is constrained, and that hermitage is distinctive like Brahma's abode, reverberating with the sounds of that Brahma's Vedic 
chants alone.

shloka:
ब्रह्मविर्भिर्महाभागैर्ब्राह्मणैरुपशोभितम् |
तद्दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमांस्तापसाश्रममण्डलम्
translation:
That glorious and great resplendent Rama on seeing those precincts of hermitage that is graced with highly blest Brahmans, 
the knowers of Brahma, neared it, unstringing the bowstring of his great bow. [3-1-9-10a]

shloka: दिव्यज्ञानोपपन्नास्ते रामं दृष्ःट्वा महर्षयः
translation:
Those great sages, the possessors of divine knowledge, are gladdened on seeing Rama and illustrious Seetha, and they moved 
towards them welcomingly. [3-1-10-11a]

shloka: ते तु सोममिवोद्यन्तं द्इष्ट्वा वै धर्मचारिणम्
translation:
But those sages who are austerely committed to vows, on their seeing Rama, the treader on the path of rectitude, and who 
is now arising like moon, and at Lakshmana and at glorious Seetha as well, rendered Vedic blessings and welcomed the trio. 
[3-1-11a-12]

shloka:
रूपसंहननं लक्ष्मीं सौकुमार्यं सुवेषताम् |
ददृशुर्विस्मिताकारा रामस्य वनवासिनः
translation:
Those forest-dwelling sages saw the physical built, its augustness and gracefulness, and his fine attire remaining in astonished 
postures.

shloka:
वैदेहीं लक्ष्मणं रामं नेत्रैरनिमिषैरिव |
आश्चरभूतान् ददृशुः सर्वे ते पनवासिनः
translation:
The forest-dwellers saw Seetha, Lakshmana and Rama, without a wink on their own eyes, as that trio is causing surprise with 
their arrival.

shloka:
आत्रैनं हि महाभागाः सर्वभूतहिते रताः |
अतिथिं पर्णशालायां राघवं संन्यवेशयन्
translation:
Those august sages that are interested in the well being of all beings have indeed accommodated Rama in that hermitage, 
as Rama is their guest a priori.

shloka:
ततो रामस्य सत्कृत्य विधिना पावकोपमाः |
अजह्रुस्ते महाभागाः सलिलं धर्मचारिणः
translation:
Then those august sages who are similar to sacred fire in glow have procedurally accorded guestship to Rama, and fetched 
water for him.

shloka:
मङ्गलानि प्रयुञ्जना मुदा परमया युताः |
मूलं पुष्पं फलं सर्वमाश्रमं च महात्मनः
translation:
On sounding out Vedic blessings those virtuous sages have offered flowers, fruits and tubers, and even the entire hermitage 
to that great soul Rama, and then with their palms adjoined. [3-1-17-18a]

shloka: धर्मपालो जनस्यास्य शरण्यश्च महायशाः
translation:
"The king will have great renown for he is the ruler of the righteousness of these people, a protector, a respectable and 
adorable one, and as he wields the sceptre of justice, he is a revered one too... [3-1-18-19a]

shloka: इन्द्रस्यव चतुर्भागः प्रजा रक्षति राघव
translation:
"The fourth part of Indra is the protector of people, called the king, and hence Oh! Raghava, the king is hailed, and hence 
he enjoys best and delightful fortune... [3-1-19b-20a]

shloka:
ते वयं भवता रक्ष्या भवद्विषयवासिनः |
नगरस्थो वनस्थोवा त्वं नो राजा जनेश्वरः
translation:
"You alone have to protect us as we are the subjects living in your kingdom..May you be in the capital... or in the forest...you 
are our king... [3-1-20b,c]

shloka:
न्यस्तदण्डा वयं राजञ्जितक्रोधा जित्रेन्द्रियाः |
रक्षणीयास्त्वया श्श्वद्गर्भभूतास्तपोधनाः
translation:
"We gave-up punishments, either physically or by the power of curses, conquered are our anger and senses, and our ascesis 
is the only wealth of ours, thus oh! King, we are to be protected by you, like the foetus inside a womb...

shloka:
एवमुक्त्वा फलैर्मुलैह् पुष्पैरन्यैश्च राघवम् |
वन्यैश्च विविधाहारैः सलक्ष्मणमपूजयन्
translation:
Thus saying they worshipped Raghava along with Lakshmana, on giving fruits, tubers, flowers and other varieties of forest 
foods.

shloka:
तथान्ये तापसाः सिद्धा रामं वैश्वानरोपमाः |
न्यायवृत्ता यथान्यायं तर्पयामासुरीश्वरम्
translation:
Thus other saints and sages who are the followers of the virtue, and similar to the Sacred Fire adored Rama, the king, according 
to the wont of custom.

shloka:
कृत आतिथ्योऽथ रामस्तु सूर्यस्य उदयनम् प्रति |
आमंत्र्य स मुनीम् तत् सर्वान् वनम् एव अन्वगाहत
translation:
Then, on receiving the hospitality in that hermitage for that day, and on the next
  day before sunrise, Rama bade farewell to all of the sages, and thus entered the deep forests.

shloka:
नाना मृग गण आकीर्णम् ऋक्ष शार्दूल सेवितम् |
ध्वस्त वृक्ष लता गुल्मम् दुर्दर्श सलिलाशयम्
translation:
Rama followed by Lakshmana has indeed seen that midst of the forest which is
  filled with very many animal herds, where the bears and tigers are frequenting, and whose trees,
  creepers, bushes are ruined, water ponds rendered unsightly, birds song-less, but where the
  swarms of crickets are whistling deafeningly. [3-3-2, 3]

shloka:
सीताया सह काकुत्स्थः तस्मिन् घोर मृग आयुते |
ददर्श गिरि शृङ्ग आभम् पुरुषादम् महास्वनम्
translation:
Therein Rama has seen along with Seetha, a lurid voiced man-eater who is akin to a
  mountain-peak, among horrendous animals.

shloka:
गम्भीर अक्षम् महावक्त्रम् विकटम् विकटोदरम् |
बीभत्सम् विषमम् दीर्घम् विकृतम् घोर दर्शनम्
translation:
Deep eyed, huge mouthed, horrible with a monstrous belly, hideously misshapen, and
  a very soaring one that demon is, an ugly one with a horrendous look.

shloka:
वसानम् चर्म वैयाघ्रम् वस आर्द्रम् रुधिरोक्षितम् |
त्रासनम् सर्व भूतानाम् व्यादितास्यम् इव अन्तकम्
translation:
Wearing tiger's skin that is wetted with fat and dampened with blood, he is
  frightening to all beings like the wide-open mouth of Death.

shloka:
त्रीन् सिंहान् चतुरो व्याघ्रान् द्वौ वृकौ पृषतान् दश |
सविषाणम् वसादिग्धम् गजस्य च शिरो महत्
translation:
He skewered three lions, four tigers, two wolves, ten spotted deer, and a big head
  of an elephant with tusks and fouled with fat on an iron spear, and he is yelling with his
  deafening voice. [3-2-7-8a]

shloka: स रामम् लक्ष्मणम् चैव सीताम् दृष्ट्वा च मैथिलीम्
translation:
He that demon on seeing Rama, Lakshmana and Seetha ran towards them very angrily,
  like the Time, the Eliminator of people. [3-2-8b-9a]

shloka: स कृत्वा भैरवम् नादम् चालयन् इव मेदिनीम्
translation:
He shouted a tremulous blare, as though to tremor the earth, and seized Vaidehi
  with his arms and gone afar, and then said this way. [9b-10a]

shloka: युवाम् जटा चीर धरौ सभार्यौ क्षीण जीवितौ
translation:
"You two wear jute cloths like hermits, but handle arrows, bows and swords like
  warriors, yet entered Dandaka forest with your wife... your lives are on the wane...
  [3-2-10b-11a]

shloka: कथम् तापसयोः युवाम् च वासः प्रमदया सह
translation:
"How saintly are you while living with your wife? You sinful fellows dishonest are
  you ways... who are you... you insulters of sainthood? [3-2-11b-12a]

shloka: अहम् वनम् इदम् दुर्गम् विराघो नाम राक्षसः
translation:
"I am a demon named Viradha and I will be on the rove in this impassable forest
  with weapon, always eating the flesh of sages... [3-2-12b-13a]

shloka: इयम् नारी वरारोहा मम भार्या भविष्यति
translation:
"This best waisted woman will be my wife, and I will drink your blood of you two
  sinful one in a fight with you... [3-2-13b-14a]

shloka: तस्य एवम् ब्रुवतो दुष्टम् विराधस्य दुरात्मनः
translation:
On listening those arrogant words spoken in bad intent by that evil minded
  Viradha, Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, is much panicked. [3-2-14b-15a.]

shloka: सीता प्रावेपिता उद्वेगात् प्रवाते कदली यथा
translation:
Seetha in fear wiggled like a plantain tree in a whirlwind, and on seeing at the
  auspicious lady gone into the arms of Viradha, Raghava spoke this sentence to Lakshmana, with his
  face fully turning to pale. [3-2-15b-16]

shloka:
पश्य सौंय नरेन्द्रस्य जनकस्य अत्म संभवाम् |
मम भार्याम् शुभाचाराम् विराधाङ्के प्रवेशिताम्
translation:
"See! Gentle Lakshmana, see that illustrious princes Seetha, the daughter of
  emperor Janaka, one who is brought up comfortably in immense comfort, and my auspiciously
  traditional wife... now gone into the wretched hands of a demon... [3-2-17-18a]

shloka: यत् अभिप्रेतम् अस्मासु प्रियम् वर वृतम् च यत्
translation:
"That which is desired to befall on us, and that which is the choicest desire of
  Kaikeyi, and that which is concomitant to her boons, oh, Lakshmana, that has come to pass
  quickly, and today only Lakshmana... [3-2-18b-19a]

shloka: या न तुष्यति राज्येन पुत्रार्थे दीर्घ दर्शिनी
translation:
"She who is a foresighted lady, she who is not happy with the kingdom for her son,
  she by whom I, a dear one to all beings, am sent to forests, and she is my middle mother, her
  desire is fulfilled today, nay now itself... [3-2-19b-20]

shloka:
पर स्पर्शात् तु वैदेह्या न दुःखतरम् अस्ति मे |
पितुर् विनाशात् सौमित्रे स्व राज्य हरणात् तथा
translation:
"To me, oh, Soumitri, the grief of others touching Seetha is more, than father's
  demise or grabbing away my kingdom...

shloka:
इति ब्रुवति काकुत्स्थे बाष्प शोक परिप्लुतः |
अब्रवीत् लक्ष्मणः क्रुद्धो रुद्धो नाग इव श्वसन्
translation:
When said thus by Rama, Lakshmana said this with flooding tears of lament, and in
  his anger hissing like a forestalled snake.

shloka:
अनाथ इव भूतानाम् नाथः त्वम् वासवोपमः |
मया प्रेष्येण काकुत्स्थः किम् अर्थम् परितप्यसे
translation:
"Oh, Rama, you being the Indra like lord of all beings, and while you are being
  attended by an adherent like me, what for you worry yourself like a derelict?

shloka:
शरेण निहतस्य अद्य मया क्रुद्धेन रक्षसः |
विराधस्य गत असोः हि मही पास्यति शोणितम्
translation:
"He will now be felled with my arrow as I am enraged at him, and gone are his
  lives now, and indeed the earth shall drink his blood...

shloka:
राज्य कामे मम क्रोधो भरते यो बभूव ह |
तम् विराधे विमोक्ष्यामि वज्री वज्रम् इव अचले
translation:
"Indeed, that which anger was there to me on Bharata when he desired kingdom, that
  anger I will now release on Viradha, as Indra released his Thunderbolt on the mountain...

shloka:
मम भुज बल वेग वेगितः
पततु शरोऽस्य महान् महोरसि |
व्यपनयतु तनोः च जीवितम्
पततु ततः च महीम् विघूर्णितः
translation:
"Accelerated by my shoulder strength this ruinous arrow shall fall on his massive
  chest, thus life from his body shall decamp, and then he shall whirlingly fall onto the earth..."
  So said Lakshmana.

shloka:
अथ उवाच पुनर् वाक्यम् विराधः पूरयन् वनम् |
पृच्छतो मम हि ब्रूतम् कौ युवाम् क्व गमिष्यथः
translation:
Then in his turn that demon Viradha said this sentence filling the forest with his gruesome voice, "I am asking you, really... 
tell me who you are and whereto you wish to go? "

shloka:
तम् उवाच ततो रामो राक्षसम् ज्वलित आननम् |
पृच्छन्तम् सुमहातेजा इक्ष्वाकु कुलम् आत्मनः
translation: Then that highly resplendent Rama said about his Ikshvaku dynasty to the blazing faced demon who is insistent.

shloka:
क्षत्रियौ वृत्त संपन्नौ विद्धि नौ वनगोचरौ |
त्वाम् तु वेदितुम् इच्छावः कः त्वम् चरसि दण्डकान्
translation:
"Know us as Kshatriya-s with ennobled bearing, and we are trekking the forest...but we wish to know about you, who are you 
that move about in Dandaka forest?

shloka:
तम् उवाच विराधः तु रामम् सत्य पराक्रमम् |
हन्त वक्ष्यामि ते राजन् निबोध मम राघव
translation: Viradha said to that truly valiant Rama, "Ah! I'll tell you, oh king, be informed of me, oh Raghava...

shloka:
पुत्रः किल जवस्य अहम् माता मम शतह्रदा |
विराध इति माम् आहुः पृथिव्याम् सर्व राक्षसाः
translation: "I am the son of Java indeed... my mother is Shatahradaa, and all the demons on earth call me Viradha...'

shloka:
तपसा च अभि संप्राप्ता ब्रह्मणो हि प्रसादजा |
शस्त्रेण अवध्यता लोके अच्छेद्य अभेद्यत्वम् एव च
translation:
"On my undertaking ascesis I derived a boon from the beneficence of Brahma, by which I will neither be cut, nor slit, nor 
killed with a weapon in this world..."

shloka:
उत्सृज्य प्रमदाम् एनाम् अनपेक्षौ यथा आगतम् |
त्वरमाणौ पलायेथाम् न वाम् जीवितम् आददे
translation:
"Leave off this lady without any yearning for her, and you expeditiously flee-away as you have come, then your lives will 
not be snatched away...

shloka:
तम् रामः प्रति उवाच इदम् कोप संरक्त लोचनः |
राक्षसम् विकृत आकारम् विराधम् पाप चेतसम्
translation:
Rama in reply said this to that ogre Viradha, whose eyes are fully bloodshot in anger, who is monstrous in his body, and 
evil in intent...

shloka:
क्षुद्र धिक्त्वाम् तु हीनार्थम् मृत्युम् अन्वेषसे ध्रुवम् |
रणे प्राप्स्यसि संतिष्ठ न मे जीवन् विमोक्ष्यसे
translation:
"You knave, fie upon you... you are in quest of you own death for your meanly measures, and definitely you will get it in 
this confrontation. Stay! I will not let you to live...

shloka:
ततः सज्यम् धनुः कृत्वा रामः सुनिशितान् शरान् |
सु शीघ्रम् अभिसंधाय राक्षसम् निजघान ह
translation: Then, stringing his bow Rama indeed darted very sharp arrows, very quickly and well aiming the demon...

shloka:
धनुषा ज्या गुणवता सप्त बाणान् मुमोच ह |
रुक्म पुंखान् महावेगान् सुपर्ण अनिल तुल्य गान्
translation:
Indeed seven arrows are let off with perfectly stringed bow, which have golden vanes, and very fast ones that equal the 
flights of Garuda, the Divine Eagle and the Air-god.

shloka:
ते शरीरम् विराधस्य भित्त्वा बर्हिण वाससः |
निपेतुः शोणिता दिग्धा धरण्याम् पावकोपमाः
translation:
But, they the arrows that are akin to infernos and dressed with peacock feathers as their fins, on piercing the body of 
Viradha they fell onto the ground besmirched with blood.

shloka:
स विद्धो न्यस्य वैदेहीम् शूलम् उद्यंय राक्षसः |
अभ्यद्रवत् सुसंक्रुद्धः तदा रामम् स लक्ष्मणम्
translation:
When that demon is thus struck, then he placed Vaidehi down from his arms, hauled up his spear, and very angrily rushed 
towards Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka:
स विनद्य महानादम् शूलम् शक्र ध्वज उपमम् |
प्रगृह्य अशोभत तदा व्यात्तानन इव अंतकः
translation:
And holding fast his spear that is similar to the Indra's Flagstaff he blaringly yelled a ghastly shriek, and thus he shone 
forth like the wide-mouthed Death, ready-to-gulp.

shloka:
अथ तौ भ्रातरौ दीप्तम् शर वर्षम् ववर्षतुः |
विराधे राक्षसे तस्मिन् कालांतक अयम् उपमे
translation:
Then with an effulgent arrow-rain those two brothers incessantly rained on demon Viradha, who is similar to the terminator 
of lifetime.

shloka:
स प्रहस्य महा रौद्रः स्थित्वा अजृम्भत राक्षसः |
जृंभमाणस्य ते बाणाः कायात् निष्पेतुर् अशुगाः
translation:
He that highly horrendous demon laughed at that arrow-shower, and standing for a while he yawned, and on his yawning and 
stretching his limbs in fatigue those arrows that earlier have gone speedily, spilled out from his body that speedily.

shloka:
स्पर्शात् तु वर दानेन प्राणान् संरोध्य राक्षसः |
विराधः शूलम् उद्यंय राघवौ अभ्यधावत
translation: Demon Viradha held back his lives by the touch of boon, and raising up the spear he ran quickly at Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka:
तत् शूलम् वज्र संकाशम् गगने ज्वलन उपमम् |
द्वाभ्याम् शराभ्याम् चिच्छेद रामः शस्त्रभृताम् वरः
translation:
The best wielder of weaponry Rama ripped that spear apart, which is akin to the Thunderbolt of Indra, and that which is 
like a blaze in the sky, with two arrows in the sky itself.

shloka:
तत् राम विशिखैः छिन्नम् शूलम् तस्य आपतत् भुविः |
पपात अशनिना चिन्नम् मेरोर् इव शिला तलम्
translation:
Shattered by Rama's blazing shafts that spear fallen on ground like the boulder mass of Mt. Meru when it is shattered by 
Indra's Thunderbolt.

shloka:
तौ खड्गौ क्षिप्रम् उद्यंय कृष्ण सर्पौ इव उद्यतौ |
तूर्णम् आपेततुः तस्य तदा प्रहारताम् बलात्
translation:
They quickly upraised their swords and like a pair of up-swinging black-cobras they rapidly crashed on him, and then battered 
him mightily.

shloka:
स वध्यमान सुभृशम् भुजाभ्याम् परिगृह्य तौ |
अप्रकंप्यौ नरव्याघ्रौ रौद्रः प्रस्थातुम् ऐच्छत
translation:
He that demon thus beaten very firmly by Rama and Lakshmana, then on grabbing those unwavering ones and manly tigers with 
his arms, that furious demon wished to carry them away.

shloka:
तस्य अभिप्रायम् अज्ञाय रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत् |
वहतु अयम् अलम् तावत् पथानेन तु राक्षसः
translation: Knowing the thinking of the demon for sure, Rama spoke to Lakshmana, "Let him easily carry us anywhere on his way...

shloka:
यथा च इच्छति सौमित्रे तथा वहतु राक्षसः |
अयम् एव हि नः पन्था येन याति निशाचरः
translation: "Let this demon carry us as he wishes, and Saumitri, by which way this night-walker goes, that alone will be our way...

shloka:
स तु स्व बल वीर्येण समुत्क्षिप्य निशाचरः |
बालाः इव स्कन्ध गतौ चकार अति बलोद्धतः
translation:
But he that night-walker arrogant as he is by his might has uplifted Rama and Lakshmana like babies by that might and courage 
alone, and placed them on his shoulders as one would place babies.

shloka:
तौ आरोप्य ततः स्कन्धम् राघवो रजनी चरः |
विराधो विनदन् घोरम् जगाम अभिमुखो वनम्
translation: That nightwalker Viradha on placing those two Raghava-s on his shoulders gone towards deeper forest yelling very luridly.

shloka:
वनम् महा मेघ निभम् प्रविष्टो
द्रुमैः महद्भिः विविधैः उपेतम् |
नाना विधैः पक्षि कुलैः विचित्रम्
शिव आयुतम् व्याल मृगैः विकीर्णम्
translation:
That demon entered into a baffling forest that is like a very dark cloud in its sheen, where a variety of massive trees 
are contained in, numerous flocks of vulturine birds are overspreading, and where wild jackals and other predaceous animals 
are sprawling around, along with Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka:
ह्रियमाणौ तु काकुत्स्थौ दृष्ट्वा सीता रघूत्तमौ |
उच्चैः स्वरेण चुक्रोश प्रगृह्य सु महाभुजौ
translation:
On seeing those two very dexterous scions of Kakutstha, and the best ones from Raghu dynasty, namely Rama and Lakshmana, 
grabbed and being carried off, Seetha screamed in a high-pitched voice.

shloka:
एष दाशरथी रामः सत्यवान् शीलवान् शुचिः |
रक्षसा रौद्र रूपेण ह्रियते सह लक्ष्मणः
translation:
"He that truth-abiding, virtuous, and the flawless Rama of Dasharatha is carried off along with Lakshmana by the demon with 
a ferocious look...

shloka:
माम् ऋका भक्ष इष्यन्ति शार्दूल द्वीपिनः तथा |
माम् हरः उत्सृज्य काकुत्स्थौ नमस्ते राक्षसोत्तमः
translation:
"Wild bears, tigers and panthers aspire to eat me away... oh, best demon, thieve me instead and release Kakutstha-s... Hail 
to thee..." [Said Seetha.]

shloka:
तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा वैदेह्याः राम लक्ष्मणौ |
वेगम् प्रचक्रतुर् वीरौ वधे तस्य दुरात्मनः
translation:
On hearing Vaidehi's that utterance those valorous ones Rama and Lakshmana speedily busied themselves in eliminating that 
evil-minded demon Viradha.

shloka:
तस्य रौद्रस्य सौमित्रिः सव्यम् बाहुम् बभञ्ज ह |
रामः तु दक्षिणम् बाहुम् तरसा तस्य रक्षसः
translation: Soumitri indeed severed the left arm of that ferocious one, while Rama rent the right arm of that demon with his might.

shloka:
सः भग्न बहुः संविग्नः पपात आशु विमूर्छितः |
धरण्याम् मेघ संकाशो वज्र भिन्न इव अचलः
translation:
When his arms are mutilated that demon similar to a dark-cloud is frustrated, fainted, and fell onto ground, like the mountain 
demolished by the Thunderbolt of Indra.

shloka:
मुष्टिभिर् बाहुभिर् पद्भिः सूदयन्तौ तु राक्षसम् |
उद्यंयोद्यंय च अपि एनम् स्थण्डिले निष्पिपेषतुः
translation:
They battered that demon with their fists, hands and feet, and even by heaving and hurling him again and again they entirely 
pounded on him on the ground.

shloka:
स विद्धो बहुभिर् बाणैः खड्गाभ्याम् च परिक्षतः |
निष्पिष्टो बहुधा भूमौ न ममार स राक्षसः
translation:
Though that demon is battered with many arrows, even sheared off with two swords, and even though he is entirely pounded 
on the ground he is not killed.

shloka:
तम् प्रेक्ष्य रामः सुभृशम् अवध्यम् अचल उपमम् |
भयेषु अभय दः श्रीमान् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
On observing that the mountain-similar demon is ineradicable that easily, then Rama, the sublime one, and the bestower of 
shelter in fear, spoke this sentence to Lakshmana.

shloka:
तपसा पुरुषव्याघ्र राक्षसोऽयम् न शक्यते |
शस्त्रेण युधि निर्जेतुम् राक्षसम् निखनावहे
translation:
"Oh! Manly-tiger Lakshmana, it is impossible to overpower this demon with weapons in a confrontation, hence, let's bury 
this demon...

shloka:
कुंजर्स्य इव रौद्रस्य राक्षसस्य अस्य लक्ष्मण! |
वने अस्मिन् सुमहद् श्वभ्रम् खन्यताम् रौद्रवर्चसः
translation: "Lakshmana, a very deep pit be dug for this furious and ferocious reprobate in this forest, as though for an elephant...

shloka:
इति उक्त्वा लक्ष्मणम् रामः प्रदरः खन्यताम् इति |
तस्थौ विराधम् आक्र्ंय कण्ठे पादेन वीर्यवान्
translation:
On saying to Lakshmana that a trench shall be dug...' then Rama repressively placed his foot on the throat of Viradha, and 
stood by.

shloka:
तत् श्रुत्वा राघवेण उक्तम् राक्षसः प्रश्रितम् वचः |
इदम् प्रोवाच काकुत्स्थम् विराधः पुरुषर्षभम्
translation:
On hearing that said by Raghava, demon Viradha sincerely spoke these humble words to Rama, the finest one from Kakutstha 
dynasty.

shloka:
हतोऽहम् पुरुषव्याघ्रः शक्र तुल्य बलेन वै |
मया तु पूर्वम् त्वम् मोहान् न ज्ञातः पुरुषर्षभः
translation:
"Dead I am, oh! Manly-tiger and a coequal of Indra in your strength... I have fallaciously not identified you earlier... 
oh, best one among men...

shloka:
कौसल्या सुप्रजातः तात रामः त्वम् विदितो मया |
वैदेही च महाभागा लक्ष्मणः च महायशाः
translation:
"Oh, sire, now I have known you to be Rama, the son of Kausalya... and even propitious Seetha and greatly renowned one Lakshmana 
are now known to me...

shloka:
अभि शापाद् अहम् घोरम् प्रविष्टो राक्ष्सीम् तनुम् |
तुंबुरुः नाम गन्धर्वः शप्तो वैश्रवणेन हि
translation: "By curse I had to enter this ghoulish demon's body, but I am a celestial gandharva, named Tumburu and Kubera cursed me...

shloka:
प्रसाद्यमानः च मया सोऽब्रवीत् माम् महायशाः |
यदा दाशरथी रमः त्वाम् वधिष्यति संयुगे
translation:
"When entreated by me, he that greatly renowned Kubera said to me, 'When Dasharatha's Rama kills you in a fight... then 
you will attain your nature of celestial body and you will go to heavens...' [3-4-17, 18a]

shloka: अनुपस्थीयमानो माम् स क्रुद्धो व्याजहार ह
translation:
" King Kubera thus cursed angrily me for not presenting myself in his service when I was interested in a celestial dancer 
Rambha, and indeed he alone said this curse-clearance to me... [3-4-18b, 19a]

shloka: तव प्रसादान् मुक्तो अहम् अभिशापात् सु दारुणात्
translation:
" And by your grace I am released from this utterly hideous cruse, and now I wish to go to my own heavenly abode, oh, firestorm 
of enemies, let safety betide you all... [3-4-19b, 20a]

shloka: इतो वसति धर्मात्मा शरभङ्गः प्रतापवान्
translation:
"Oh, Sire, att one and half yojana-s of distance from here Sage Sharabhanga, a great saint of virtue, and an efficacious 
sage with sun-like resplendence dwells, you shall quickly approach him for he advises you opportunely... [3-4-20-21]

shloka:
अवटे च अपि माम् राम निक्षिप्य कुशली व्रज |
रक्षसाम् गत सत्त्वानाम् एष धर्मः सनातनः
translation:
"Rama you go safely on burying me in a pit... this is the age-old custom for those demons that lost vitality... those that 
are inhumed in pit, to them there will be the worlds of manes..." [3-4-22, 23a]

shloka: एवम् उक्त्वा तु काकुत्स्थम् विराधः शर पीडितः
translation: "And on saying thus to Rama that Viradha who is hurt by arrows became heaven-worthy on leaving his body. [3-4-23b, 24a]

shloka: तत् श्रुत्वा राघवः वाक्यम् लक्ष्मणम् व्यादिदेश ह
translation:
And Raghava on hearing those words of the demon ordered Lakshmana, "Lakshmana, a very deep pit be dug for this furious and 
ferocious reprobate in this forest, as though for an elephant..." On saying to Lakshmana that a trench shall be dug...' 
then Rama repressively placed his foot on the throat of Viradha, and stood by. [3-4-24b, 25, 26]

shloka:
ततः खनित्रम् आदाय लक्ष्मणः श्वभ्रम् उत्तमम् |
अखनत् पार्श्वतः तस्य विराधस्य महात्मनः
translation: Then, on taking a digging tool Lakshmana dug a deep pit beside the great soul Viradha.

shloka:
तम् मुक्त कण्ठम् उत्क्षिप्य शङ्कु कर्णम् महास्वनम् |
विराधम् प्राक्षिपत् श्वभ्रे नदन्तम् भैरव स्वनम्
translation:
On releasing his throat from the stamping of Rama, he that long eared, lurid voiced Viradha is ensconced in that pit while 
he is still blaring with his horrific voice.

shloka:
तम् आहवे दारुणम् आशु विक्रमौ
स्थिरौ उभौ संयति राम लक्ष्मणौ |
मुदान्वितौ चिक्षिपतुर् भयावहम्
नदन्तम् उत्क्षिप्य बिलेन राक्ष्सम्
translation:
Those deftly victorious ones Rama and Lakshmana who compose themselves in a given fight, both have gladly raised that Viradha, 
a ghoulish one in fight, a terrifying demon who is still blaring, with all their might and hurled him into the pit.

shloka:
अवध्यताम् प्रेक्ष्य महासुरस्य तौ
शितेन शस्त्रेण तदा नरर्षभौ |
समर्थ्य च अत्यर्थ विशारदौ उभौ
बिले विरधस्य वधम् प्रचक्रतुः
translation:
On observing the indestructibility of that demon with any weapon, however sharp it might be, those two best ones among men 
that are very expertly skilled have thought over well and undertook the elimination of that great demon in a pit.

shloka:
स्वयम् विराधेन हि मृत्युम् आत्मनः
प्रसह्य रामेण वधार्थम् ईप्सितः |
निवेदितः कानन चारिणा स्वयम्
न मे वधः शस्त्र कृतो भवेत् इति
translation:
Viradha himself preferred his death at the hands of Rama and desired for a long to be killed by Rama and that forest walker 
himself appraised that, "Killing me with any weapon is impossible..."

shloka:
तदेव रामेण निशंय भाषितम्
कृता मतिः तस्य बिल प्रवेशने |
बिलम् च तेन अति बलेन रक्षसा
प्रवेश्यमानेन वनम् विनादितम्
translation:
On listening to that which is said by Viradha, Rama resolved his mind to cast him into pit, and when that mighty demon is 
being flung into the pit the whole forest blared with that demon's cries.

shloka:
प्रहृष्ट रूपौ इव राम लक्ष्मणौ
विराधम् उर्व्याम् प्रदरे निपात्य तम् |
ननन्दतुः वीत भयौ महावने
शिलाभिः अन्तर् दधतुः च राक्षसम्
translation:
Rama and Lakshmana felt happy by way of their look in burying Viradha in the pit of the earth, and on burying him they two 
felt rejoiced for gone is the fear in that great forest, and within the pit they have also concealed him with boulders in 
order to make it a burial-chamber to the departed soul.

shloka:
ततः तु तौ कांचन चित्र कार्मुकौ
निहत्य रक्षः परिगृह्य मैथिलीम् |
विजह्रतुः तौ मुदितौ महावने
दिवि स्थितौ चन्द्र दिवाकरौ इव
translation:
Then they two who have dazzling golden bows have eliminated that demon and retrieved Seetha, and they gladly journeyed on 
in that great forest like the two entities abiding on the skies, namely the Sun and Moon.

shloka:
हत्वा तु तम् भीम बलम् विराधम् राक्षसम् वने |
ततः सीताम् परिष्वज्य समाश्वास्य च वीर्यवान्
translation:
After killing that stupendously mighty demon Viradha in forest, then Rama comfortingly embraced Seetha, and spoke to his 
brother Lakshmana who is beaming forth with resplendence.

shloka: कष्टम् वनम् इदम् दुर्गम् न च स्मो वन गोचराः
translation:
"Difficult is this impassable forest, nor we are forest inhabitants either... let's go quickly to that ascetically rich 
sage Sharabhanga..." [3-5-2b, 3a]

shloka: आश्रमम् शरभन्गस्य राघवोऽभिजगाम ह
translation:
On his approach at the hermitage of Sage Sharabhanga, a sage with a divine effect and the one with a purified soul, saw 
a great wonder at the nearby of that hermitage of Sharabhanga.[3-5-3b, 4]

shloka:
विभ्राजमानम् वपुषा सूर्य वैश्वानर प्रभम् |
रथ प्रवरम् आरूढम् आकाशे विबुध अनुगम्
translation:
Rama has seen Indra, the lord of three worlds, with a radiant body that has the coupled radiance of Sun and Fire, mounted 
on a great chariot that does not touch the earth, wearing greatly brilliant ornaments and attired in spotless dress, while 
the other divinities are attending, and many more selfsame great-souls are worshipping him. [3-5-5, 6, 7a]

shloka: हरितैः वाजिभिर् युक्तम् अंतरिक्ष गतम् रथम्
translation:
Rama saw at his very nearby a chariot yoked with green horses that traverses in firmament, which in its splendour is either 
like the noontime sun, or a cluster of silver clouds, or like the silvern sphere of the moon. [3-5-7b, 8]

shloka:
अपश्यत् विमलम् छत्रम् चित्र माल्य उपशोभितम् |
चामर व्यजने च अग्र्ये रुक्म दण्डे महाधने
translation:
He saw the stainless parasol of Indra, marvellously garlanded and shining forth, and the exemplary and invaluable royal 
fanning instruments with golden handles, which two best female celestials are handling and fanning at Indra's head sides 
with them. [3-5-9, 10a]

shloka: गन्धर्व अमर सिद्धाः च बहवः परम ऋषयः
translation:
And the celestials like gandharva-s, amara-s, siddhaa-s and very many great sages as well are extolling Indra who is abiding 
in firmament. [3-5-10b, 11a]

shloka: सह संभाषमाणे तु शरभंगेन वासवे
translation: On seeing Indra speaking there to sage Sharabhanga, Rama spoke to Lakshmana. [3-5-11b, 12a]

shloka: रामोऽथ रथम् उद्दिश्य भ्रातुर् दर्शयत अद्भुतम्
translation:
Rama then on pointing out the chariot expressed his own amazement saying, "Lakshmana see this wonderful chariot that includes 
effulgence and auspiciousness as well, and that abides in firmament, and highly luminous like the Sun... [3-5-12b, 13]

shloka:
ये हयाः पुरु हूतस्य पुरा शक्रस्य नः श्रुताः |
अन्तरिक्ष गता दिव्याः ते इमे हरयो ध्रुवम्
translation:
"Of which horses we have earlier heard from our teachers telling that they belong to Indra, the Chief Invitee in Vedic rituals, 
they are these divinely green horses that now abide in the firmament, and definitely these must be Indra's horses...

shloka:
इमे च पुरुष व्याघ्र ये तिष्ठन्ति अभितः दिशम् |
शतम् शतम् कुण्डलिनो युवानः खड्ग पाणयः
translation:
"And oh, manly-tiger Lakshmana, those that are there in hundreds and hundreds around Indra, those youthful ones with their 
ear-ornaments and swords in hands, with wide and broad chests, with club shaped arms, and clad in glimmering red garments, 
all are like tigers, all are unapproachable, all of them are wearing ornamental chains on their chest-place that are akin 
to flaring fires, and in their appearance, Soumitri, they always bear a look of twenty-five-year-olds... [3-5-15, 16, 17]

shloka:
एतद्धि किल देवानाम् वयो भवति नित्यदा |
यथा इमे पुरुष व्याघ्रा दृश्यन्ते प्रिय दर्शनाः
translation:
"The age factor of gods remains constant at the age that appears for these nice-looking Tigerly-men, so they say... 
for gods are immortals and they will be ever young...

shloka:
इह एव सह वैदेह्या मुहूर्तम् तिष्ठ लक्ष्मण |
यावत् जानामि अहम् व्यक्तम् क एष द्युतिमान् रथे
translation: "Stay for a moment Lakshmana along with Vaidehi, until I know clearly about that resplendent one on that chariot...

shloka:
तम् एवम् उक्त्वा सौमित्रिम् इह एव स्थीयताम् इति |
अभिचक्राम काकुत्स्थः शरभंग आश्रमम् प्रति
translation: On saying to Lakshmana stay there only...' Rama proceeded towards the hermitage of Sage Sharabhanga..

shloka:
ततः समभिगच्छन्तम् प्रेक्ष्य रामम् शची पतिः |
शरभंगम् अनुज्ञाप्य विबुधान् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Then, on seeing Rama arriving there, Indra, bade farewell to Sage Sharabhanga and said this to the celestials attending 
him.

shloka:
इह उपयाति असौ रामो यावन् माम् न अभिभाषते |
निष्ठाम् नयत तावत् तु ततो मा द्रष्टुम् अर्हति
translation:
"Here comes that Rama...before he talks to me, you lead him towards his vow, after completing the result of his incarnation, 
then only he is eligible to see me... Let him be a victorious and accomplished one, then I will see him very soon...for 
that will happen very soon... A great deed is to be verily performed by him that is highly impossible for others... [3-5-22, 
23

shloka:
अथ वज्री तम् आमंत्र्य मानयित्वा च तापसम् |
रथेन हय युक्तेन ययौ दिवम् अरिन्दमः
translation:
Then that Enemy-destroyer Indra adoringly bade farewell to the sage, and travelled to heavens by the chariot with its green 
horses.

shloka:
प्रयाते तु सहस्राक्षे राघवः सपरिच्छदः |
अग्नि होत्रम् उपासीनम् शरभंगम् उपागमत्
translation:
On the transit of that Thousand-eyed Indra, Raghava with his adherents [namely Lakshmana and Seetha,] came nearby the 
Sage Sharabhanga, who is sitting nearby the altar of fire.

shloka:
तस्य पादौ च संगृह्य रामः सीता च लक्ष्मणः |
निषेदुः तद् अनुज्ञाता लब्ध वासा निमंत्रिताः
translation:
Touching the feet of that Sage Sharabhanga Rama along with Seetha and Lakshmana, and duly permitted and invited by that 
Sage Sharabhanga they sat there, as they obtained a shelter.

shloka:
ततः शक्र उपयानम् तु पर्यपृच्छत राघवः |
शरभंगः च तत् सर्वम् राघवाय न्यवेदयत्
translation: Then, Raghava enquired with sage about the arrival of Indra and Sage Sharabhanga narrated all that to him.

shloka:
माम् एष वरदो राम ब्रह्म लोकम् निनीषति |
जितम् उग्रेण तपसा दुष्प्रापम् अकृत आत्मभिः
translation:
"Oh! Rama, that boon-giver Indra wishes to take me to Brahma's abode, which is achieved by me by my arduous ascesis and 
that which is unattainable for them with their souls unconquered...

shloka:
अहम् ज्ञात्वा नर व्याघ्र वर्तमानम् अदूरतः |
ब्रह्म लोकम् न गच्छामि त्वाम् अदृष्ट्वा प्रिय अतिथिम्
translation:
"On knowing that you are course is nearby, oh! Manly-tiger, and without seeing my dear guest I do not wish to go to Brahma's 
abode...

shloka:
त्वया अहम् पुरुषव्याघ्र धार्मिकेण महत्मनाअ |
समागंय गमिष्यामि त्रिदिवम् च अवरम् परम्
translation:
" Having met with you, a virtuous one and a great soul as you are, oh, manly-tiger, I wish to go through undesirable lesser 
heavens to Brahma's abode, the highest

shloka:
अक्षया नर शार्दूल जितालोका मया शुभाः |
ब्राह्ंयाः च नाक पृष्ठ्याः च प्रतिगृह्णीष्व मामकान्
translation:
"Oh! Tigerly-man, non-diminishing are the abodes achieved by me either in Brahma's abode or yonder than paradise...you take 
them all...that are mine achieved by me ascesis..." So said Sage Sharabhanga to Rama.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तो नरव्याघ्रः सर्व शास्त्र विशारदः |
ऋषिणा शरभंगेन राघवो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Thus said by the Sage Sharabhanga to that Manly-tiger Rama, being the scholar in all the scriptures he spoke this sentence 
to that sage.

shloka:
अहम् एव आहरिष्यामि सर्वान् लोकान् महामुने |
आवासम् तु अहम् इच्छामि प्रदिष्टम् इह कानने
translation:
"I alone can gain all those worlds, oh! Great Saint, I now seek a place to dwell here in this forest as indicated by you... 
[Apparent meaning.]

shloka:
राघवेण एवम् उक्तः तु शक्र तुल्य बलेन वै |
शरभंगो महाप्राज्ञः पुनर् एव अब्रवीत् वचः
translation:
Thus said by Raghava, who is like Indra in strength, that supremely intellectual Sage Sharabhanga again spoke this sentence 
this way.

shloka:
इह राम महातेजाः सुतीक्ष्णो नम धार्मिकः |
वसति अरण्ये नियतः स ते श्रेयो विधास्यति
translation:
"Here, oh! Rama, a great resplendent sage named Suteekshna, lives in this forest...a virtuous and a self-disciplined one, 
and he will do something benignant to you...

shloka:
सुतीक्ष्णम् अभिगच्छ त्वम् शुचौ देशे तपस्विनम् |
रमणीये वनोद्देशे स ते वासम् विधास्यति
translation: "You approach Sage Suteekshna and to you he will arrange housing in his auspicious and dpleasant place woods of hermits...

shloka:
इमाम् मन्दाकिनीम् राम प्रतिस्रोतम् अनुव्रज |
नदीम् पुष्पोडुप वहाम् ततः तत्र गमिष्यसि
translation:
" Following opposite to its flow you may follow this River Mandaakini that carries flower-ferries, then you can reach there 
at Sage Suteekshna's hermitage...]

shloka:
एष पन्था नरव्याघ्र मुहूर्तम् पश्य तात माम् |
यावत् जहामि गात्राणि जीर्णाम् त्वचम् इव उरगः
translation:
"This is the only way, oh, manly-tiger, and oh, sire, see me for a moment, till I forsake these body parts of mine, like 
a snake casting its withered moult...

shloka:
ततो अग्निम् सु समाधाय हुत्वा च आज्येन मंत्रवित् |
शरभंगो महातेजाः प्रविवेश हुताशनम्
translation:
Then that hymnist on invoking the sacred fire and offering oblations with clarified butter into it, that radiant sage Sharabhanga 
entered that sacred fire.

shloka:
तस्य रोमाणि केशाम् च तदा वह्निः महात्मनः |
जीर्णम् त्वचम् तद् अस्थीनि यत् च मांसम् च शोणितम्
translation:
The fire burnt down that great soul Sharabhanga from head-hair to body hair and thus his shrunk skin, bones and whatever 
flesh and blood are there, they are also burnt completely.

shloka:
स च पावक संकाशः कुमारः समपद्यत |
उत्थाय अग्निचयात् तस्मात् शरभंगो व्यरोचत
translation:
He that Sage Sharabhanga, then reappeared as an youngster in the semblance of Fire, o\n resurrecting from that altar of 
fire he shone-forth.

shloka:
स लोकान् आहिताग्नीनाम् ऋषीणाम् च महात्मनाम् |
देवानाम् च व्यतिक्रंय ब्रह्म लोकम् व्यरोहत
translation:
He that Sage Sharabhanga, transcending the ethereal worlds of fire-worshippers, of saints, of great souls, and also of divinities, 
has ascended to Brahma's abode.

shloka:
स पुण्य कर्मा भुवने द्विजर्षभः
पितामहम् सानुचरम् ददर्श ह |
पितामहः च अपि समीक्ष्य तम् द्विजम्
ननन्द सुस्वागतम् इति उवाच ह
translation:
He that meritorious and best Brahman Sharabhanga has seen Brahma in Brahma's abode, and Brahma too, on seeing that Brahman 
happily spoke to him... "Welcome..."

shloka:
शरभङ्गे दिवम् प्राप्ते मुनि संघाः समागताः |
अभ्यगच्छन्त काकुत्स्थम् रामम् ज्वलित तेजसम्
translation:
On Sage Sharabhanga attaining heaven, groups of sages assembled and approached
  Rama of Kakutstha dynasty, who is glowing with resplendence.

shloka:
वैखानसा वालखिल्याः संप्रक्षाला मरीचिपाः |
अश्म कुट्टाः च बहवः पत्र आहाराः च तापसाः
translation:
The sages called Vaikahanasa-s, [who are born out of the nails of Prajaapati, the
  first ruler of mankind,] also Vaalakhilyaa-s, [those born from His hair,] and those from the
  water of His feet-wash, and those that thrive on drinking rays of sun and moon alone, and those
  that pound with stones and others who thrive on leaves alone, are those sages...

shloka:
दन्त उलूखलिनः च एव तथा एव उन्मज्जकाः परे |
गात्र शय्या अशय्याः च तथा एव अनवकाशिकाः
translation:
Some of them use their own teeth to grid the grain they eat, and some who perform
  ascesis in neck-deep water, and some who sleep with their head resting on their shoulders or on
  chests without using any kind of bed, and some who do not use any kind of beds either, and some
  who meditate without any repose sitting in an enclosure without any leg-space.

shloka:
मुनयः सलिल आहारा वायु भक्षाः तथा अपरे |
आकाश निलयाः च एव तथा स्थण्डिल शायिनः
translation:
And some sages whose food is water alone, or air alone to some, like that some who
  meditate staying in sky and some who sleep on bare ground itself.

shloka:
तथा ऊर्थ्व वासिनः दान्ताः तथा आर्द्र पट वाससः |
स जपाः च तपो नित्याः तथा पंच तपोऽन्विताः
translation:
Thus some are dwellers on high-peaked places with their senses controlled, and
  some are wearers of wet cloths, always reciting name or hymn japa and like that some who meditate
  with five kinds of fire around them.

shloka:
सर्वे ब्राह्ंया श्रिया ज्युक्ता दृढ योग समाहिताः |
शरभंग आश्रमे रामम् अभिजग्मुः च तापसाः
translation:
All have Vedic resplendence and firm yogic control, and they have arrived at the
  hermitage of Sage Sharabhanga for Rama.

shloka:
अभिगंय च धर्मज्ञा रामम् धर्म भृताम् वरम् |
ऊचुः परम धर्मज्ञम् ऋषि संघाः समागताः
translation:
Those virtuous sages coming together in groups neared Rama, the best beholder of
  virtue, and said to that supreme one in virtue.

shloka:
त्वम् इक्ष्वाकु कुलस्य अस्य पृथिव्याः च महारथः |
प्रधानः च अपि नाथः च देवानाम् मघवान् इव
translation:
"You are the supreme charioteer born in Ikshvaku dynasty hence you are the
  protector of earth under your control. As with Indra, the ruler of divinities you are a similar
  ruler for us.

shloka: ओर्
translation:
Though born in Ikshvaku dynasty you are the Supreme Charioteer, hence you are the
  same Supreme Charioteer of this Earth and earthlings too, as with Indra who protects divinities,
  you are our protector.

shloka:
विश्रुतः त्रिषु लोकेषु यशसा विक्रमेण च |
पितृ व्रतत्वम् सत्यम् च त्वयि धर्मः च पुष्कलः
translation:
"You are well renowned in all the three worlds by your repute and valour, and in
  you abounding are the virtues like truthfulness and devotion to your father, and even
  righteousness too, is there.

shloka:
त्वाम् आसाद्य महात्मानम् धर्मज्ञम् धर्म वत्सलम् |
अर्थित्वात् नाथ वक्ष्यामः तत् च नः क्षन्तुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"You are the great-souled one, knower of righteousness and a patron of virtue...
  such as you are, on approaching you we beg to state something for which we may please be
  excused...

shloka:
अधार्मः सुमहान् नाथ भवेत् तस्य तु भूपतेः |
यो हरेत् बलि षड् भागम् न च रक्षति पुत्रवत्
translation:
"Oh! , very great a-dharma, wrongness, will occur to that king who takes the sixth
  part of the country's produce as cess, but does not safeguard his subjects like his own sons...

shloka:
युंजानः स्वान् इव प्राणान् प्राणैः इष्टान् सुतान् इव |
नित्य युक्तः सदा रक्षन् सर्वान् विषय वासिनः
translation:
"A king shall treat all the subjects of kingdom as his own sons, and he shall
  protect them as though he is ready to save them at the cost of his own lives, and he who will
  always be endeavouring in that manner will attain permanent renown lasting for many for many
  years to come, and thereby he attains a prosperous place even in Brahma's abode... [3-6-12,
  3]

shloka:
यत् करोति परम् धर्मम् मुनिः मूल फल अशनः |
तत्र राज्ञः चतुर् भागः प्रजा धर्मेण रक्षतः
translation:
"He who righteously protects his subjects will get one fourth of the merit of
  great duty-bound deeds performed by each individual sage, say yajna-s, ascesis, meditation etc.
  performances.

shloka:
सो अयम् ब्राह्मण भूयिष्ठो वानप्रस्थ गणो महान् |
त्वम् नाथो अनाथवत् राम राक्षसैः हन्यते भृशम्
translation:
"O, Rama, though you are there as protector for the hermitages, suchlike this one,
  where the most reverent Brahmans are there numerously, they look as though forsaken, for they are
  being demolished by demons, devastatingly...

shloka:
एहि पश्य शरीराणि मुनीनाम् भावित आत्मनाम् |
हतानाम् राक्षसैः घोरैः बहूनाम् बहुधा वने
translation:
"Come and see many of the bodies of the sages, the contemplative souls, that are
  variously killed by ghastly demons in the forest...

shloka:
पंपा नदी निवासानाम् अनुमन्दाकिनीम् अपि |
चित्रकूट आलयानाम् च क्रियते कदनम् महत्
translation:
"At Pampa riverside, and alongside of River Mandakini, and at the surroundings of
  Mt. Chitrakuta also, this hideous warfare is being done...

shloka:
एवम् वयम् न मृष्यामो विप्रकारम् तपस्विनाम् |
क्रियमाणम् वने घोरम् रक्षोभिः भीम कर्मभिः
translation:
"Thus. we are not able to tolerate this injustice to the sages, being executed in
  this forest by the demons with fiendish deeds, in a ghastly manner...

shloka:
ततः त्वाम् शरणार्थम् च शरण्यम् समुपस्थिताः |
परिपालय नः राम वध्यमानान् निशाचरैः
translation:
"Therefore we present ourselves before you as you are our protector, for the
  purpose of your protecting us that are being killed by nightwalkers... please safe guard us...

shloka:
परा त्वत्तः गतिः वीर पृधिव्यम् न उपपद्यते |
परिपालय नः सर्वान् राक्षसेभ्यो नृपात्मजः
translation:
"Other than you, oh, valorous Rama, no way-out is deducible on this earth, hence
  oh, prince, protect all of us from the demons...

shloka:
एतत् श्रुत्वा तु काकुत्स्थः तापसानाम् तपस्विनाम् |
इदम् प्रोवाच धर्मात्मा सर्वान् एव तपस्विनः
translation:
On hearing all that is said by the sages of great penance, he that virtue souled
  Rama said this unto all of the sages.

shloka:
न एवम् अर्हथ माम् वक्तुम् आज्ञाप्यः अहम् तपस्विनाम् |
केवलेन स्व कार्येण प्रवेष्टव्यम् वनम् मया
translation:
"Unapt is this way of speaking to me...command me, for I am at your behest... just
  for my personal purpose I had to enter the forests....

shloka:
विप्रकारम् अपाक्रष्टुम् राक्षसैः भवताम् इमम् |
पितुः तु निर्देशकरः प्रविष्टो अहम् इदम् वनम्
translation:
"I entered this forest as ordered by my father and even to obliterate the
  unconscionable state of yours owing to the misdeeds of demons.

shloka:
भवताम् अर्थ सिद्ध्यर्थम् आगतोऽहम् यदृच्छया |
तस्य मे अयम् वने वासो भविष्यति महाफलः | ३-६-२४
translation:
"Perchance I have come for the achievement of your purpose, such as I am, dwelling
  in this forest will immensely be fruitful to me...

shloka:
तपस्विनाम् रणे शत्रून् हन्तुम् इच्छामि राक्षसान् |
पश्यन्तु वीर्यम् ऋषयः सः ब्रातुर् मे तपोधनाः
translation:
"I wish to eliminate demons, the enemies of sages, in war... let the sages behold
  my valour, and my brother's valour in doing so..." Thus Rama promised the sages.

shloka:
दत्त्वा अभयम् च अपि तपो धनानाम्
धर्मे धृइत आत्मा सह लक्ष्मणेन |
तपो धनैः च अपि सह आर्य दत्तः
सुतीक्ष्णम् एव अभिजगाम वीरः
translation:
Thus giving his aegis to the sages, that valiant Rama who is firmly virtue-souled,
  journeyed towards Sage Suteekshna with Lakshmana and the sages, and along with the one given by
  Honourable Janaka, namely Seetha.

shloka:
रामः तु सहितः भ्रात्रा सीतया च परंतपः |
सुतीक्ष्णस्य आश्रम पदम् जगाम सह तैः द्विजैः
translation:
Rama, the enemy-scorcher, has gone towards the threshold of the hermitage of Sage Suteekshna 
along with his brother Lakshmana and Seetha, also along with those Brahmans who accompanied him all 
the way.

shloka:
स गत्वा दीर्घम् अध्वानम् नदीः तीर्त्वा बहु उदकाः |
ददर्श विमलम् शैलम् महा मेरुम् 
इव उन्नतम्
translation:
He travelling on a long way, and on crossing rivers with plenty of waters has seen a 
tranquil mountain towering like great Mt. Meru.

shloka:
ततः तद् इक्ष्वाकु वरौ सततम् विविधैः द्रुमैः |
काननम् तौ विविशतुः सीतया सह राघवौ
translation:
Then those best ones from Ikshvaku dynasty, those two Raghava-s along with Seetha have 
entered the forest which will always be full with diverse trees.

shloka:
प्रविष्टः तु वनम् घोरम् बहु पुष्प फल द्रुमम् |
ददर्श आश्रमम् एकान्ते चीर माला 
परिष्कृतम्
translation:
Entering that perilous forest with its many a flower and fruit bearing trees, they have 
seen the hermitage in a reclusive place adorned with rows of jute cloths as though garlanding it.

shloka:
तत्र तापसम् आसीनम् मल पङ्कज धारिणम् |
रामः सुतीक्ष्णम् विधिवत् तपोधनम् अभाषत
translation:
There on seeing the ascetically rich Sage Suteekshna sitting in yogic posture with his 
body bearing lotus-like blotches of soil, Rama dutifully spoke to him.

shloka:
रामोऽहम् अस्मि भगवन् भवन्तम् द्रष्टुम् आगतः |
तत् मा अभिवद धर्मज्ञ महर्षे सत्य 
विक्रम
translation:
"Oh! godly sage I am Rama, I have come to see you, hence oh, knower of virtue, oh, great 
sage, oh, one with truthfulness as your courage, please talk to me..."

shloka:
स निरीक्ष्य ततः धीरो रामम् धर्मभृताम् वरम् |
समाश्लिष्य च बाहुभ्याम् इदम् वचनम् 
अब्रवीत्
translation:
Then that sage having seen that brave and best proponent of virtue, Rama, embraced him 
with both of his hands, and spoke this sentence.

shloka:
स्वागतम् ते रघु श्रेष्ठ राम सत्यभृताम् वर |
आश्रमओ अयम् त्वया आक्रान्तः सनाथ 
इव सांप्रतम्
translation:
"Welcome to you Rama, best of Raghu dynasty and the best patron of truth, and when you 
presently caught this hermitage unprepared this has become a well-lorded one...

shloka:
प्रतीक्षमाणः त्वाम् एव न आरोहे अहम् महायशः |
देव लोकम् इतो वीर देहम् त्यक्त्वा 
महीतले
translation:
"I am awaiting for you only, oh, greatly renowned one, without my ascent to heavens by 
casting off this body on the earth's plane, oh, brave one, for I have heard that you have arrived at 
Chitrakuta after you are repudiated from your kingdom...

shloka: इह उपयातः काकुत्स्थः देवराजः शततक्रतुः
translation:
"The king of gods and the chief invitee in hundred sacrifices Indra approached me, and 
that great deity said me that I have conquered all the worlds by my meritorious deeds... [3-7-10, 11]

shloka:
तेषु देव ऋषि जुष्टेषु जितेशु तपसा मया |
मत् प्रसादात् स भार्यः त्वम् विहरस्व 
स लक्ष्मणः
translation:
"Let me bequeath those worlds that are cherished by gods and sages alike, but which are 
won over by me by my ascesis, and you enjoy in them with your wife and with your brother Lakshmana...

shloka:
तम् उग्र तपसम् दीप्तम् महर्षिम् सत्य वादिनम् |
प्रत्युवाच आत्मवान् रामो ब्रह्माणम् 
इव वासवः
translation:
That self-respecting Rama replied the radiant sage with intense asceticism, a great soul 
and an advocate of truth by himself, as Indra would reply to Brahma.

shloka:
अहम् एव आहरिष्यामि स्वयम् लोकान् महामुने |
आवासम् तु अहम् इच्छामि प्रदिष्टम् 
इह कानने
translation:
"I alone can gain all those worlds, oh, great saint, I now seek a place to dwell here 
in this forest as indicated by you...

shloka:
भवान् सर्वत्र कुशलः सर्वभूत हिते रतः |
आख्यातः शरभंगेन गौतमेन महात्मना
translation:
"You are an expert in all affairs, and you are interested in the welfare of all the beings, 
so said the great souled Sage Sharabhanga of Sage Gautama's dynasty..." [So said Rama to the sage.]

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण महर्षिः लोक विश्रुतः |
अब्रवीत् मधुरम् वाक्यम् हर्षेण महता 
युतः
translation:
When said thus by Rama, that great sage with world renown spoke sweet worded sentence 
with great pleasure.

shloka:
अयम् एव आश्रमो राम गुणवान् रंयताम् इति |
ऋषि संघ अनुचरितः सदा मूल फलैर् युतः
translation:
"You can take delight in this good featured hermitage alone, for groups of sages will 
always be moving here, and this always contains tubers and fruits..." Thus said Sage Suteekshna.

shloka:
इमम् आश्रमम् आगंय मृग संघा महीयसः |
अहत्वा प्रतिगच्छन्ति लोभयित्वा अकुतोभयाः
translation:
"But herds of very large animals will be coming to this hermitage, they return after 
scaring us, of course without killing anyone, and they fear none...

shloka:
ना अन्यो दोषो भवेत् अत्र मृगेभ्यः अन्यत्र विद्धि वै |
तत् श्रुत्वा वचनम् तस्य 
महर्षेः लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
translation:
"Know that no other problem is there other than the animals..." So said the sage. On 
hearing those words of that great sage, that brave elder brother of Lakshmana taking bow and arrow said 
this sentence. [3-7-19, 20a]

shloka: तान् अहम् सुमहाभाग मृगसंघान् समागतान्
translation:
"I will eradicate them, oh, greatly blessed one, those animals that will come collectively 
in herds with sharp edged, curve-end arrows... [3-7-20b, 21a]

shloka: भवान् तत्र अभिषज्येत किम् स्यात् कृच्छ्र तरम् ततः
translation:
"But you may be more interested in those animals mercifully, then what will be there 
more painful to you, hence I deem our staying in this hermitage for along will be unbefitting..." So 
said Rama. [3-7-21b, 22a]

shloka: तम् एवम् उक्त्वा उपरमम् रामः संध्याम् उपागमत्
translation:
On saying thus to the sage then Rama came by the twilight, and he paused at it. On worshipping 
the westward vesperal time, Rama arranged a stay for himself along with Seetha and Lakshmana, there 
in that delightful hermitage of Sage Suteekshna. [3-7-22b, 23]

shloka:
ततः शुभम् तापस अन्नम्
स्वयम् सुतीक्ष्णः पुरुषर्षभाभ्याम् |
ताभ्याम् सुसत्कृत्य 
ददौ महात्मा
संध्या निवृत्तौ रजनीम् समीक्ष्य
translation:
Then the great soul Sage Suteekshna on completing his evening rituals and on observing 
the fall of night he himself courteously served food that is auspicious and worthy of sages to two of 
the best men, Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka:
रामः तु सह सौमित्रिः सुतीक्ष्णेन अभिपूजितः |
परिणांय निशाम् तत्र प्रभाते प्रत्यबुध्यत
translation:
Rama along with Soumitri is well revered by Sage Suteekhsna, spent that night there and awoken in the 
morning.

shloka:
उत्थाय च यथा कालम् राघवः सह सीतया |
उपस्पृश्य सु शीतेन तोयेन उत्पल गंधिना
translation:
Rama got up according to time along with Seetha and touched finely cool water with lotus-fragrance for 
morning bath.

shloka:
अथ ते अग्निम् सुराम् च एव वैदेही राम लक्ष्मणौ |
काल्यम् विधिवत् अभ्यर्च्य तपस्वि शरणे वने
translation:
Then they all, Vaidehi, Rama and Lakshmana, on worshipping sacred fire and deities dutifully in the 
shelter of the sages in that forest and on seeing the dawning sun, they are reft of their blemishes, 
and then they approached Sage Suteekshna speaking this sentence gently. [3-8-3, 4]

shloka:
सुखोषिताः स्म भगवन् त्वया पूज्येन पूजिताः |
आपृच्छामः प्रयास्यामो मुनयः त्वरयन्ति नः
translation:
"We stayed here happily, oh, god, venerated by a venerable one like you, and here we come to ask your 
permission as we wish to journey on, as the sages are hastening us...

shloka:
त्वरामहे वयम् द्रष्टुम् कृत्स्नम् आश्रम मण्डलम् |
ऋषीणाम् पुण्य शीलानाम् दण्डकारण्य वासिनाम्
translation:
"We make haste to see the habitats of hermitages in their entirety, and even wish to see the sages with 
meritorious selves living in Dandaka forest...

shloka:
अभ्यनुज्ञातुम् इच्छामः सह एभिः मुनिपुङ्गवैः |
धर्म नित्यैः तपो दान्तैः विशिखैः इव पावकैः
translation:
"We wish to have your permission, and that of these eminent sages, who are ever virtuous, self-controlled 
by their ascesis, and who look like the veritable tongues of sacred fire...

shloka:
अविषह्य आतपो यावत् सूर्यो न अति विराजते |
अमार्गेण आगताम् लक्ष्मीम् प्राप्य इव अन्वय वर्जितः
translation:
"We wish to proceed before sun attains an intolerable glare, like an unworthy person of unworthy lineage 
attains wealth in an improper way with much glare..." saying so Rama with Seetha and Lakshmana venerated 
at the feet of that sage Suteekshna. [3-8-8, 9]

shloka:
तौ सम् स्पृशंतौ चरणौ उत्थाप्य मुनिपुंगवः |
गाढम् आश्लिष्य सस्नेहम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
That eminent sage lifted them that are touching his feet, embraced them tightly, and said this sentence 
in all his friendliness.

shloka:
अरिष्टम् गच्छ पन्थानम् राम सौमित्रिणा सह |
सीतया च अनया सार्धम् छाय एव अनुवृत्तया
translation:
"Proceed in an invulnerable way, Rama, along with Lakshmana, and with this Seetha while she follows 
you closely like a shadow...

shloka:
पश्य आश्रम पदम् रंयम् दण्डकारण्य वासिनाम् |
एषाम् तपस्विनाम् वीर तपसा भावित आत्मनाम्
translation:
"See the pleasant thresholds of the hermitages of the dwellers in the forests of Dandaka, oh! Valiant 
one, whose souls are consecrated just by their ascesis...

shloka:
सुप्राज्य फल मूलानि पुष्पितानि वनानि च |
प्रशस्त मृग यूथानि शान्त पक्षि गणानि च
translation:
"See the well-flowered woodlands with well-grown fruits and tubers, with herds of best animals and 
peaceful bird flocks... tranquil waters with spreading clusters of bloomed lotuses and water-birds in 
the pools and lakes... eye-pleasing rapids from mountains and you can see pleasant forests loaded with 
the hearty screams of precooks... [3-8-13, 14, 15]

shloka:
गंयताम् वत्स सौमित्रे भवान् अपि च गच्छतु |
आगन्तव्यम् च ते दृष्ट्वा पुनः एव आश्रमम् प्रति
translation:
"My dear Rama, you may go and Soumitri you too also may go... but come again towards this hermitage 
after seeing all of them...

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तथा इति उक्त्वा काकुत्स्थः सह लक्ष्मणः |
प्रदक्षिणम् मुनिम् कृत्वा प्रस्थातुम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
Thus said by the sage, Rama in his turn said to him, "so be it..." and having performed circumambulations 
around the sage he started to journey on.

shloka:
ततः शुभतरे तूणी धनुषी च आयतेक्षणा |
ददौ सीता तयोः भ्रात्रोः खड्गौ च विमलौ ततः
translation:
Then the broad eyed Seetha gave auspicious quivers and bows to those brothers and then spotless swords 
too.

shloka:
आबध्य च शुभे तूणी चापे च आदाय सस्वने |
निष्क्रान्तौ आश्रमात् गन्तुम् उभौ तौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
Both of those two Rama and Lakshmana tied their beautiful quivers well on their backs, and took the 
twangy bows and exited from that hermitage to go on their way.

shloka:
शीघ्रम् तौ रूपसंपन्नौ अनुज्ञातौ महर्षिणा |
प्रस्थितौ धृत चापा असी सीतया सह राघवौ
translation:
Those two Raghava-s, the handsome princes, have swiftly set out when permitted by that august sage, 
wielding bows and swords, and along with Seetha.

shloka:
सुतीक्ष्णेन अभ्यनुज्ञातम् प्रस्थितम् रघु नन्दनम् |
हृद्यया स्निग्धया वाचा भर्तारम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
To Rama, the scion of Raghu and her husband, who started out when permitted by Sage Suteekshna, Vaidehi 
spoke this with friendly words.

shloka:
अधर्मम् तु सुसूक्ष्मेण विधिना प्राप्यते महान् |
निवृत्तेन च शक्यो अयम् व्यसनात् कामजाद् इह
translation:
"Gross unjust will accrue to any in an abstruse way if his indulgence is enkindled merely by his own 
desire, and in this world it is possible to fend them off, to have a recourse to justness...

shloka:
त्रीणि एव व्यसनानि अत्र कामजानि भवन्ति उत |
मिथ्या वाक्यम् तु परमम् तस्मात् गुरुतरा उभौ
translation:
"Only three self-gratifications, the definite products of desire, are there: one is speaking fallacious 
utterances, which itself is worse, and worst than the other two malefic self-gratifications, where the 
other two are the fascination for other's wife, and the cruelness without enmity... [3-9-3, 4a]

shloka: मिथ्या वाक्यम् न ते भूतम् न भविष्यति राघव
translation:
"The habit of telling specious words is not there with you in the past nor it will be there in future, 
oh, Raghava, then wherefrom the virtue-ruining desire for other's women can be there... [3-9-4b, 5a]

shloka: तव नास्ति मनुष्येन्द्र न च आभूत् ते कदाचन
translation:
"Oh, king, earlier this vile desire for other's women is absent in you, nor it is there now, unobserved 
is such a desire in any corner of your heart oh, prince, for you are always interested in your own wife... 
[3-9-5, 6]

shloka:
धर्मिष्टः सत्य सन्धः च पितुः निर्देश कारकः |
त्वयि धर्मः च सत्यम् च त्वयि सर्वम् प्रतिष्टितम्
translation:
"You are conscientious, adherent of truth, and obliging father's orders, and in you virtue and truth, 
nay everything is established in you...

shloka:
तच्च सर्वम् महाबाहो शक्यम् वोढुम् जितेइन्द्रियैः |
तव वश्य इन्द्रियत्वम् च जानामि शुभदर्शन
translation:
"Oh, dextrous one, all this can possibly be shouldered by one with controlled senses, and oh, graceful 
one for a gaze, I am also aware of your sense control...

shloka:
तृतीयम् यद् इदम् रौद्रम् पर प्राण अभिहिंसनम् |
निर्वैरम् क्रियते मोहात् तत् च ते समुपस्थितम्
translation:
"That third tendency to torture others' lives without enmity, that which will usually be effectuated 
unwarily, has now suddenly chanced before you...

shloka:
प्रतिज्ञातः त्वया वीर दण्डकारण्य वासिनाम् |
ऋषीणाम् रक्षणार्थाय वधः संयति रक्षसाम्
translation:
"Intending to safeguard the sages you have promised the dwellers in Dandaka forest, oh, valiant one, 
that you would eliminate demons in a fight...

shloka:
एतन् निमित्तम् च वनम् दण्डका इति विश्रुतम् |
प्रस्थितः त्वम् सह भ्रात्रा धृत बाण शराअसनः
translation:
"Only in this respect you have started towards the well-known Dandaka forest along with your brother, 
and wielding bow and arrows...

shloka:
ततः त्वाम् प्रस्थितम् दृष्ट्वा मम चिन्त आकुलम् मनः |
त्वत् वृत्तम् चिन्तयन्त्या वै भवेत् निःश्रेयसम् 
हितम्
translation:
"Then on seeing your starting my mind is apprehensively upset, on verily reflecting about your bearing 
there appears to be no beneficial good for you...

shloka:
न हि मे रोचते वीरः गमनम् दण्डकान् प्रति |
कारणम् तत्र वक्ष्यामि वदन्त्याः श्रूयताम् मम
translation:
"Oh, brave one, your going towards Dandaka forest is not delightful to me, I tell the cause for that 
and listen to it as I tell...

shloka:
त्वम् हि बाण धनुष्पाणिः भ्रात्रा सह वनम् गतः |
दृष्ट्वा वन चरान् सर्वान् कच्चित् कुर्याः शर व्ययम्
translation:
