"Indeed on entering the forest along with your brother, and wielding bow and arrows, seeing the forest 
ramblers there, won't you deplete arrows on all of them...

shloka:
क्षत्रियाणाम् इह धनुर् हुताशस्य इन्धनानि च |
समीपतः स्थितम् तेजो बलम् उच्छ्ह्रयते भृशम्
translation:
"The bow of warrior and the fuel of a burning fire if available within their reach, they immensely enhance 
their strength...

shloka:
पुरा किल महाबाहो तपस्वी सत्य वाक् शुचिः |
कस्मिन् चित् अभवत् पुण्ये वने रत मृग द्विजे
translation:
"Once upon a time, oh, dextrous one, there was a pious and true worded hermit in some merited forest 
that was wonted by animals and birds...

shloka:
तस्य एव तपसो विघ्नम् कर्तुम् इन्द्रः शचीपतिः |
खड्ग पाणिः अथ आगच्छ्हत् आश्रमम् भट रूप धृक्
translation:
"Then Indra came to that hermitage handling a sword, and donning a soldier's guise, to cause hindrance 
to that hermit's ascesis...

shloka:
तस्मिन् तत् आश्रम पदे निहितः खड्ग उत्तमः |
स न्यास विधिना दत्तः पुण्ये तपसि तिष्ठतः
translation:
"Indra gave that best sword to store, there in that hermitage to that sage who is lasting in his ascesis, 
on a redeemable basis...

shloka:
स तत् शस्त्रम् अनुप्राप्य न्यास रक्षण तत्परः |
वने तु विचरति एव रक्षन् प्रत्ययम् आत्मनः
translation:
"On receiving that sword, he who is duteous in guarding the entrustment, moved about in the forest always 
handling the sword, to safeguard the confidence reposed in him...

shloka:
यत्र गच्छ्हति उपादातुम् मूलानि च फलानि च |
न विना याति तम् खड्गम् न्यास रक्षण तत्परः
translation:
"Wherever that dedicated guardian of that entrustment goes, even to obtain tubers or fruits, he did 
not go without that sword...

shloka:
नित्यम् शस्त्रम् परिवहन् क्रमेण स तपोधनः |
चकार रौद्रीम् स्वाम् बुद्धिम् त्यक्त्वा तपसि निश्चयम्
translation:
"Carrying that sword always, that hermit slowly made his own faculty infuriated, loosing determination 
in ascesis...

shloka:
ततः स रौद्र अभिरतः प्रमत्तो अधर्म कर्षितः |
तस्य शस्त्रस्य संवासात् जगाम नरकम् मुनिः
translation:
"Then with the constant association of that weapon that sage gradually became inadvertent, and smitten 
by vice he went to hell...

shloka:
एवम् एतत् पुरा वृत्तम् शस्त्र संयोग कारणम् |
अग्नि संयोगवत् हेतुः शस्त्र संयोग उच्यते
translation:
"Thus, all this happened earlier, only owing the reason of associating with a weapon constantly, and 
the sequel of constant association with weapon is as good as constant association with fire...

shloka:
स्नेहात् च बहुमानात् च स्मारये त्वाम् न शिक्षये |
न कथंचन सा कार्या गृहीत धनुषा त्वया
translation:
"In affinity and in respect I am reminding but not tutoring you, and in anyway improper is that thought 
of yours to wield your bow to kill the demons dwelling in Dandaka without any enmity, oh, brave one, 
undesirable is the killing of offenceless... [3-9-24, 25]

shloka:
क्षत्रियाणाम् तु वीराणाम् वनेषु नियतात्मनाम् |
धनुषा कार्यम् एतावत् आर्तानाम् अभिरक्षणम्
translation:
"For the valiant Kshatriya-s who are inclined in forests heartily, the purpose of the bow is this much 
'safeguarding the sufferers...'

shloka:
क्व च शस्त्रम् क्व च वनम् क्व च क्षात्रम् तपः क्व च |
व्याविद्धम् इदम् अस्माभिः देश धर्मः तु पूज्यताम्
translation:
"Where that weapon? Where this forest? Where the principles of Kshatriya? And where is sageness? All 
this is inconsistent... let us esteem the laws of the land...

shloka:
तदार्य कलुषा बुद्धिः जायते शस्त्र सेवनात् |
पुनर् गत्वात् तत् अयोध्यायाम् क्षत्र धर्मम् चरिष्यसि
translation:
"Weapon admiring mind becomes maligned with avariciousness, you may therefore follow the tenet of Kshatriya-s 
on going to Ayodhya again...

shloka:
अक्षया तु भवेत् प्रीतिः श्वश्रू श्वशुरयोः मम |
यदि राज्यम् हि संन्यस्य भवेत् त्वम् निरतो मुनिः
translation:
"Everlasting satisfaction will be there to my father-in-law and mothers-in-laws, on your becoming a 
devout sage even after forfeiture of kingdom...

shloka:
धर्मात् अर्थः प्रभवति धर्मात् प्रभवते सुखम् |
धर्मेण लभते सर्वम् धर्म सारम् इदम् जगत्
translation:
"From virtuousness prosperity emanates, from righteousness happiness, and by honourableness all are 
achieved, and this universe is the essence of probity...

shloka:
आत्मानम् नियमैः तैः तैः कर्षयित्वा प्रयत्नतः |
प्राप्यते निपुणैः धर्मो न सुखात् लभते सुखम्
translation:
"Experts will make efforts to exhaust their own selves with those and those principles, thus they realise 
sublimity... unachievable is pleasure by pleasuring alone...

shloka:
नित्यम् शुचि मतिः सौम्य चर धर्मम् तपो वने |
सर्वम् हि विदितम् तुभ्यम् त्रैलोक्यम् अपि तत्त्वतः
translation:
"Always tread along the righteousness with a pure mind, oh, gentle one, and specially in these sagely 
forests... you know everything in all the three worlds, in all its nuances...

shloka:
स्त्री चापलात् एतत् उदाहृतम् मे
धर्मम् च वक्तुम् तव कः समर्थः |
विचार्य बुद्ध्या तु सह अनुजेन
यत् रोचते तत् कुरु म अचिरेण
translation:
"I cite all this with my womanly waver, and who is capable to talk to you about dharma? Ponder mindfully 
along with your brother, and what that is appropriate, you do it...but not belatedly...

shloka:
वाक्यम् एतत् तु वैदेह्या व्याहृतम् भर्तृ भक्त्या |
श्रुत्वा धर्मे स्थितो रामः प्रत्युवाच जानकीम्
translation:
On hearing all of the words said by Vaidehi, in adoration of her husband, he who abides by virtue alone 
that Rama replied Janaki.

shloka:
हितम् उक्तम् त्वया देवि स्निग्धया सदृशम् वचः |
कुलम् व्यपदिशन्त्या च धर्मज्ञे जनक आत्मजे
translation:
"You have said beneficial, friendlily words that are seemlier to your disposition, oh, lady, which 
are apt to speak of your familial brought up, for you are the daughter of virtue-knowing Janaka.

shloka:
किम् नु वक्ष्यामि अहम् देवि त्वया एव उक्तम् इदम् वचः |
क्षत्रियैः धार्यते चापो न आर्त शब्दो भवेद् 
इति
translation:
"What more shall I say, oh, lady, since it is said that 'a warrior handles a bow so that misery's tears 
cease to flow...' and this saying is iterated even by you...

shloka:
ते च आर्ता दण्डकारण्ये मुनयः संशित व्रताः |
माम् सीते स्वयम् आगम्य शरण्याः शरणम् गताः
translation:
"Oh! Seetha, those shleterable sages of Dandaka forest have approached me sombrely on their own, and 
thus they came into my refuge...

shloka:
वसन्तः काल कालेषु वने मूल फल अशनाः |
न लभन्ते सुखम् भीरु राक्षसैः क्रूर कर्मभिः
translation:
"Subsisting on fruits and tubers, living at all the time in forests those sages are not getting quietude, 
as they are scared by the demons with invidious deeds...

shloka:
भक्ष्यन्ते राक्षसैः भीमैः नर मांसोपजीविभिः |
ते भक्ष्यमाणा मुनयो दण्डकारण्य वासिनः
translation:
"The sages dwelling in Dandaka forest are being eaten away by fiendish demons that subsist on human 
flesh, and while being eaten away like that those eminent Brahmans have said to me, "please come to 
our rescue..." [4-10-6,7a]

shloka: मया तु वचनम् श्रुत्वा तेषाम् एवम् मुखात् च्युतम्
translation:
"This way when I have heard the words voiced by them, I comforted them verbally and avouched this way, 
"Be gracious to me... you all... by which reason I am being addressed this way by this kind of eminent 
Brahmans, whom I should have actually addressed my self, this indeed is a dishonour for me... [4-10-7b, 
8, 9a]

shloka: किम् करोमि इति च मया व्याहृतम् द्विज संनिधौ
translation:
"Then I said before the Brahmans, "what shall I do?" All of them thus thronged and spoke this word. 
[4-10-9b, 10a]

shloka: राक्षसैः दण्डकारण्ये बहुभिः काम रूपिभिः
translation:
"Many of the guise changing demons are outrightly torturing us in Dandaka forest, hence in that context 
you shall protect us... [4-10-10b, 11a]

shloka: होम काले तु संप्राप्ते पर्व कालेषु च अनघ
translation:
"Those resistless carnivorous demons, oh, merited Rama, will descend exactly at the time of fire oblations, 
or on propitious times like full or new moons to persecute us... [4-10-11b, 12a]

shloka: राक्षसैः धर्षितानाम् च तापसानाम् तपस्विनाम्
translation:
"We the ascetics being assaulted thus are aggrieved, and when we searched for a recourse you chanced 
as our ultimate course... [4-10-12b, 13a]

shloka: कामम् तपः प्रभावेण शक्ता हन्तुम् निशाचरान्
translation:
"We by the efficacy of our ascesis are surely capable to eradicate those demons, but we do not wish 
to shorten the effect of our long earned merit of ascesis... [4-10-13b, 14a]

shloka: बहु विघ्नम् तपो नित्यम् दुःश्चरम् चैव राघव
translation:
"Many hurdles are always there in our practice of ascesis, and even the ascesis have become impracticable, 
oh, Raghava, thus though being eaten away by the demons we are not issuing any curse... [4-10-14b, 15a]

shloka: तद् अर्द्यमानान् रक्षोभिः दण्डकारण्य वासिभिः
translation:
"Thereby, you along with your brother protect us that are being persecuted by the demons dwelling in 
Dandaka forest as you alone are the protector of ours in these forests...'so said sages to me... [4-10-15b, 
16a]

shloka: मया च एतत् वचः श्रुत्वा कार्त्स्न्येन परिपालनम्
translation:
"On hearing all those words, oh, Seetha, I promised complete protection to the sages of Dandaka forests... 
[4-10-16b, 17a]

shloka: संश्रुत्य न च शक्ष्यामि जीवमानः प्रतिश्रवम्
translation:
"Having promised to the sages it is incapable of me to implement it otherwise while I am alive... truth 
is dearer to me, isn't it... [4-10-17b, 18a]

shloka: अपि अहम् जीवितम् जह्याम् त्वाम् वा सीते स लक्ष्मणाम्
translation:
"I may forfeit my life, forgo Lakshmana, or even forsake you but not a promise, that too especially 
made to Brahmans, and having promised I can never go back... [4-10-18b, 19a]

shloka: तत् अवश्यम् मया कार्यम् ऋषीणाम् परिपालनम्
translation:
"By that reason, oh, Seetha, even if I am unasked, safeguarding sages is definitely to be done by me, 
how then it is undone when given a promise... [4-10-19b, 20a]

shloka: मम स्नेहात् च सौहार्दात् इदम् उक्तम् त्वया वचः
translation:
"With your friendship and good-heartedness you say these words, oh, Seetha, I am contended... uninterested 
ones do not forewarn, indeed... [4-10-20b, 21a]

shloka:
सदृशम् च अनुरूपम् च कुलस्य तव शोभने |
सधर्म चारिणी मे त्वम् प्राणेभ्यो अपि गरीयसी
translation:
"Appropriate and seemly is your word of caution to your bloodline, oh, graceful Seetha, you are the 
co-pursuer in dharma with me, hence you are loftier to me than my own lives..." So said Rama to Seetha. 
[4-10-21b, c]

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्त्वा वचनम् महात्मा
सीताम् प्रियाम् मैथिल राज पुत्रीम् |
रामो धनुष्मान् सह लक्ष्मणेन
जगाम रम्याणि तपो वनानि
translation:
That exalted soul Rama on saying those words to Seetha, his dear wife and the daughter of Janaka, wielding 
his bow proceeded further with Lakshmana to the picturesque woodlands of hermits.

shloka:
अग्रतः प्रययौ रामः सीता मध्ये सुशोभना |
पृष्ठतः तु धनुष्पाणिः लक्ष्मणः अनुजगाम ह
translation:
Rama travelled ahead while the glorious Seetha in middle, and wielding bow Lakshmana followed them on 
the rear.

shloka:
तौ पश्यमानौ विविधान् शैल प्रस्थान् वनानि च |
नदीः च विविधा रम्या जग्मतुः सह सीतया
translation:
They proceeded while seeing diverse mountain terraces, forests, and diversely enchanting rivers too, 
along with Seetha.

shloka:
सारसान् चक्रवाकां च नदी पुलिन चारिणः |
सरांसि च सपद्मानि युतानि जलजैः खगैः
translation:
Beholding the rivers that have water-birds like saarasa, chakravaaka that move on their sandbanks, and 
also the lakes that contain lotuses and water born birds, they moved on.

shloka:
यूथ बद्धाम् च पृषतान् मद उन्मत्तान् विषाणिनः |
महिषाम् च वराहाम् च गजाम् च द्रुम वैरिणः
translation:
The moved on watching spotted deer banded in herds, the wild boars, large horned buffaloes maddened 
in virility, and the ruttish elephants rending trees like their enemies.

shloka:
ते गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम् लंबमाने दिवाकरे |
ददृशुः सहिता रंयम् तटाकम् योजन आयुतम्
translation:
On going far on their way, and when the sun is dangling in the western skiy, together they saw a charming 
lake of one yojana width fully overloaded with red and white lotuses, overspread with sporting elephants, 
and over-flurried with waterfowls like saarasa birds, kaadamba birds, swans and with others kinds too. 
[4-11-5, 6]

shloka:
प्रसन्न सलिले रम्ये तस्मिन् सरसि शुश्रुवे |
गीत वादित्र निर्घोषो न तु कश्चन दृश्यते
translation:
Out of the tranquil and enchanting waters of that lake audible are the melodies of singing and musical 
instruments, but none is visible.

shloka:
ततः कौतूहलात् रामो लक्ष्मणः च महारथः |
मुनिम् धर्मभृतम् नाम प्रष्टुम् समुपचक्रमे
translation:
Then Rama and also Lakshmana, the great charioteer, inquisitively started to ask the Sage named Dharmabhrita 
about it.

shloka:
इदम् अत्यद्भुतम् श्रुत्वा सर्वेषाम् नो महामुने |
कौतूहलम् महत् जातम् किम् इदम् साधु कथ्यताम्
translation:
"On hearing this greatly amazing music from lake, oh, great saint, intensive inquisitiveness is created 
in all of us, why this, please tell us clearly about it." Thus Rama asked.

shloka:
तेन एवम् उक्तो धर्मात्मा राघवेण मुनिः तदा |
प्रभावम् सरसः क्षिप्रम् आख्यातुम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
Thus said by that Raghava then that virtuous sage quickly started to tell about the efficacy of that 
lake.

shloka:
इदम् पंच अप्सरो नाम तटाकम् सार्व कालिकम् |
निर्मितम् तपसा राम मुनिना माण्डकर्णिना
translation:
"Oh, Rama, this is an all-time lake built by the ascetic power of the sage Mandakarni, known as Five 
Apsara Lake.

shloka:
स हि तेपे तपः तीव्रम् माण्डकर्णिः महामुनिः |
दश वर्ष सहस्राणि वायु भक्षो जलाशये
translation:
"He that great saint Mandakarni practiced rigorous ascesis for ten thousand years staying in the waters 
of the lake, and consuming air alone.

shloka:
ततः प्रव्यथिताः सर्वे देवाः स अग्नि पुरोगमाः |
अब्रुवन् वचनम् सर्वे परस्पर समागताः
translation:
"Then all the gods are worried and met together with Fire-god at the helm of affairs, and they all conversed 
among themselves.

shloka:
अस्मकम् कस्यचित् स्थानम् एष प्रार्थयते मुनिः |
इति संविग्न मनसः सर्वे तत्र दिवौकसः
translation:
"This sage is praying for someone's place among us," thus all of those heaven-dwellers are perturbed 
at heart.

shloka:
ततः कर्तुम् तपो विघ्नम् सर्व देवैः नियोजिताः |
प्रधान अप्सरसः पंच विद्युत् चलित वर्चसः
translation:
"Then all gods assigned five important Apsara-s, the celestial courtesans, whose shine is like the sprint 
of the lightning, to effectuate hindrance in that sage's ascesis.

shloka:
अप्सरोभिः ततः ताभिः मुनिः दृष्ट परावरः |
नीतो मदन वश्यत्वम् देवानाम् कार्य सिद्धये
translation:
Then those five celestial beauties have led that sage astray who discerned the nature of this and the 
other world, or good and bad, or the nature of Absolute-Soul and Body- bound Soul, towards the passional 
restraint by, as though to achieve god's task.

shloka:
ताः चैव अप्सरसः पंच मुनेः पत्नीत्वम् आगताः |
तटाके निर्मितम् तासाम् तस्मिन् अन्तर्हितम् गृहम्
translation:
"Also thus, those five celestial apsara-s attained wifehood of that sage, and for them he built a house 
in there, concealed inside that lake.

shloka:
तत्र एव अप्सरसः पंच निवसन्त्यो यथा सुखम् |
रमयन्ति तपोयोगात् मुनिम् यौवनम् आस्थितम्
translation:
"While those five celestial apsara-s are living in there, they are gratifying that sage according to 
his delight as youthfulness came upon that sage owing to his power of asceticism.

shloka:
तासाम् संक्रीड मानानाम् एष वादित्र निःस्वनः |
श्रूयते भूषण उन्मिश्रः गीत शब्दः मनोहरः
translation:
"These musical sounds we hear are emerging out as played on their instruments, mingled with the tinkling 
of their ornaments, and mixed with their delightful singing of melodies." So said sage Dharmabhrita 
to Rama.

shloka:
आश्चर्यम् इति तस्य एतद् वचनम् भावितात्मनः |
राघवः प्रतिजग्राह सह भ्रात्रा महा यशाः
translation:
That highly renowned Raghava together with his brother acknowledged the sage Dharmabhrita's account, 
exclaiming it as "amazing is this..."

shloka:
एवम् कथयमानः स ददर्श आश्रम मण्डलम् |
कुश चीर परिक्षिप्तम् ब्राह्म्या लक्ष्म्या समावृतम्
translation:
While saying thus Raghava has seen a cluster of hermitages nearby, encircled with sacred grass, jute 
cloths, and even encompassed with Vedic solemness, and he entered that hermitage along with Seetha and 
Lakshmana. [4-11-21, 22a]

shloka: तदा तस्मिन् स काकुत्स्थः श्रीमति आश्रम मण्डले
translation:
Rama happily stayed in that august cluster of hermitages duly venerated by those great saints for sometime, 
and then that expert in great missiles Rama went to the hermitages of those sages with whom he stayed 
earlier, for another round. [4-11-22, 23, 24a]

shloka: क्वचित् परिदशान् मासान् एक संवत्सरम् क्वचित्
translation:
Rama stayed there for nearly ten months at some place, elsewhere for one year, at somewhere else for 
four months, and for five, and six months at elsewhere, even at somewhere else for more than a month, 
and for more than one and half months elsewhere. [4-11-24, 25, 26a]

shloka: तत्र संवसतः तस्य मुनीनाम् आश्रमेषु वै
translation:
While Raghava stayed comfortably taking delight in those hermitages of sages, indeed ten years have 
smoothly elapsed. [4-11-26b, 27a]

shloka: परिसृत्य च धर्मज्ञः राघवः सह सीतया
translation:
Thus that virtue-knowing glorious Rama on going around those hermitages along with Seetha indeed went 
to the hermitage of Sage Suteekshna again. [4-11-27b, 28a]

shloka: स तम् आश्रमम् आगम्य मुनिभिः परिपूजितः
translation:
On coming at that hermitage that enemy destroyer is adored by sages, and he resided there for some time. 
[4-11-28b, 29a]

shloka: अथ आश्रमस्थो विनयात् कदाचित् तम् महामुनिम्
translation:
Then on one day while staying in that hermitage Rama submissively said this to that sage Suteekshna 
who is sitting nearby. [4-11-29b, 30a]

shloka: अस्मिन् अरण्ये भगवन् अगस्त्यो मुनिसत्तमः
translation:
"I have always heard through the narratives narrated by other sages that the godly and eminent sage 
Agastya is residing in this forest. [4-11-30b, 31a]

shloka: न तु जानामि तम् देशम् वनस्य अस्य महत्तया
translation:
"But due to the vastness of this forest I have not known that place, where is the pious hermitage of 
that astute sage? [4-11-31b, 32a]

shloka: प्रसाद अर्थम् भगवतः सानुजः सह सीतया
translation:
"I wish to approach that sage seeking that godly sage's graciousness, along with my brother and Seetha 
to venerate him. [4-11-32b, 33a]

shloka: मनोरथो महान् एष हृदि परिवर्तते
translation:
"Can I personally propitiate that supreme sage -- is my high ambition, and it is recurrent in my heart." 
So said Rama to Suteekshna. [4-11-33b, 34a]

shloka: इति रामस्य स मुनिः श्रुत्वा धर्मात्मनो वचः
translation:
Sage Suteekshna on hearing that particular request of that virtue-minded Rama is gladdened and said 
this to him. [4-11-34b, 35a]

shloka: अहम् अपि एतद् एव त्वाम् वक्तु कामः स लक्ष्मणम्
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, even I wished to say this to you, that you may approach Agastya along with Lakshmana and 
Seetha. [4-1-35b, 36a]

shloka: दिष्ट्या तु इदानीम् अर्थे अस्मिन् स्वयम् एव ब्रवीषि माम्
translation:
"But providentially you alone raised this topic with me, Rama, I will tell you where that great sage 
Agastya is. [4-11-36b, 37a]

shloka:
योजनानि आश्रमात् तात याहि चत्वारि वै ततः |
दक्षिणेन महान् श्रीमान् अगस्त्य भ्रातुर् आश्रमः
translation:
"On your going four yojana-s from this hermitage, oh, dear Rama, there is the great and glorious hermitage 
of Agastya's brother on the southern side. [4-11-37b, c]

shloka:
स्थली प्राय वनोद्देशे पिप्पली वन शोभिते |
बहु पुष्प फले रम्ये नाना विहग नादिते
translation:
"That hermitage is there on a plateau in a spectacular place of that forest which is adorned with many 
flowers and fruits, thickets of long pepper, and reechoed with the callings of various birds.

shloka:
पद्मिन्यो विविधाः तत्र प्रसन्न सलिल आशयाः |
हंस कारण्डव आकीर्णाः चक्रवाक उपशोभिताः
translation:
"There are diverse lakes that are receptacles for tranquil waters, that are teeming with swans and partridges, 
beautified with ruddy geese, and Rama staying there for a night you may proceed in the next morning. 
[4-11-39, 40a]

shloka: दक्षिणाम् दिशम् आस्थाय वन षण्डस्य पार्श्वतः
translation:
"On going one yojana beyond, taking the southward course on the side of the forest clump you will find 
Agastya's hermitage. [4-11-40b, 41a]

shloka: रमणीये वनोद्देशे बहु पादप शोभिते
translation:
"Seetha and Lakshmana will enjoy those woodlands adorned with diverse pleasant trees, as the woodlands 
abounding with diverse trees will naturally be delightful, isn't it. [4-11-41b, 42]

shloka:
यदि बुद्धिः कृता द्रष्टुम् अगस्त्यम् तम् महामुनिम् |
अद्य एव गमने बुद्धिम् रोचयस्व महामते
translation:
"If your mind is made up to see that great sage Agastya, oh, great ingenious Rama, resolve your thinking 
in going only today." So said Sage Suteekshna to Rama.

shloka:
इति रामो मुनेः श्रुत्वा सह भ्रात्रा अभिवाद्य च |
प्रतस्थे अगस्त्यम् उद्दिश्य सानुगः सह सीतया
translation:
On listening that which is said by the sage, Rama revered that sage along with his brother, and then 
he journeyed with Seetha and his follower Lakshmana aiming to reach Agastya.

shloka:
पश्यन् वनानि चित्राणि पर्वतां च अभ्र संनिभान् |
सरांसि सरितः चैव पथि मार्ग वश अनुगतान्
translation:
While viewing beautiful forests, cloud-like mountains, lakes, and rivers that are flowing following 
the pathways, Rama happily journeyed on the pathway indicated by sage Suteekshna, then he gladly spoke 
this sentence to Lakshmana. [4-11-45, 46]

shloka:
एतद् एव आश्रम पदम् नूनम् तस्य महात्मनः |
अगस्त्यस्य मुनेर् भ्रातुर् दृश्यते पुण्य कर्मणः
translation:
"Definitely this alone appears to be the hermitage of Sage Agastya's brother, one with great soul and 
pious deeds.

shloka:
यथा हि इमे वनस्य अस्य ज्ञाताः पथि सहस्रशः |
संनताः फल भरेण पुष्प भारेण च द्रुमाः
translation:
"As how thousands of trees are bowing under the weight of flowers and fruit on the pathway, thereby 
I perceive it to be the hermitage of Agastya's bother.

shloka:
पिप्पलीनाम् च पक्वानाम् वनाद् अस्माद् उपागतः |
गन्धो अयम् पवन उत्क्षिप्तः सहसा कटुकोदयः
translation: "Upraised by the wind the sour-smell of pippali fruits is suddenly coming closer from the forest.

shloka:
तत्र तत्र च दृश्यन्ते संक्षिप्ताः काष्ठ संचयाः |
लूनाः च परिदृश्यन्ते दर्भा वैदूर्य वर्चसः
translation:
"Here and there visible are the well heaped heaps of firewood, and all over appearing is the sacred 
grass snipped at its top and gemlike in its tinge.

shloka:
एतत् च वन मध्यस्थम् कृष्ण अभ्र शिखर उपमम् |
पावकस्य आश्रमस्थस्य धूमाग्रम् संप्रदृश्यते
translation:
"From inside the hermitage in the midst of this forest the vertex of smoke from ritual fire is clearly 
visible as high as the vertex of a black rainy cloud.

shloka:
विविक्तेषु च तीर्थेषु कृत स्नाना द्विजातयः |
पुष्प उपहारम् कुर्वन्ति कुसुमैः स्वयम् आर्जितैः
translation: "On performing bathing in sacred streams the Brahmans are making flower offerings to gods, calledpuSpa bali, with the flowers that are personally collected by them.

shloka:
ततः सुतीक्ष्णस्य वचनम् यथा सौम्य मया श्रुतम् |
अगस्त्यस्य आश्रमो भ्रातुर् नूनम् एष भविष्यति
translation:
"Thus by the words of Sage Suteekshna as I have heard, oh, gentle Lakshmana, this hermitage shall definitely 
be that of Sage Agastya's brother.

shloka:
निगृह्य तरसा मृत्युम् लोकानाम् हित काम्यया |
यस्य भ्रात्रा कृता इयम् दिक् शरण्या पुण्य कर्मणा
translation:
"Whose brother is Sage Agastya with meritorious deeds, who wishing well-being of the world controlled 
death by his efficacy, and who made this southern region a liveable region, this must be the hermitage 
of such a sage, such Agatya's brother.

shloka:
इह एकदा किल क्रूरो वातापिः अपि च इल्वलः |
भ्रातरौ सहितौ आस्ताम् ब्राह्मणघ्नौ महा असुरौ
translation:
"Once upon a time verily cruel demon brothers Vaataapi and Ilvala were here together, and they the dreadful 
demons, they say, used to be Bhraman-killers.

shloka:
धारयन् ब्राह्मणम् रूपम् इल्वलः संस्कृतम् वदन् |
आमंत्रयति विप्रान् स श्राद्धम् उद्दिश्य निर्घृणः
translation:
"Disguising in Bhraman's semblance and speaking sophisticatedly that Ilvala used to invite Brahmans 
for the purpose of obsequial ceremonies, where Brahman are fed after usual ceremony to appeases their 
manes.

shloka:
भ्रातरम् संस्कृतम् कृत्वा ततः तम् मेष रूपिणम् |
तान् द्विजान् भोजयामास श्राद्ध दृष्टेन कर्मणा
translation:
Then Ilvala used to make his brother Vaataapi into a ram, perfect that ram's meat into deliciously cooked 
food, and used to feed Brahmans according to obsequial rites and deeds.

shloka:
ततो भुक्तवताम् तेषाम् विप्राणाम् इल्वलो अब्रवीत् |
वातापे निष्क्रमस्व इति स्वरेण महता वदन्
translation:
"When those Brahmans are surfeited with that ram's meat, then Ilvala used to shout loudly, "oh, Vaataapi, 
you may come out."

shloka:
ततो भ्रातुर् वचः श्रुत्वा वातापिः मेषवत् नदन् |
भित्त्वा भित्वा शरीराणि ब्राह्मणानाम् विनिष्पतत्
translation:
"Then on listening his brother's words Vaataapi used to lunge out bleating like a ram, tearing and rending 
the bodies of those Brahmans.

shloka:
ब्राह्मणानाम् सहस्राणि तैः एवम् काम रूपिभिः |
विनाशितानि संहत्य नित्यशः पिशित अशनैः
translation:
"This way they the guise changing demons always ruined thousands of Brahmans together, greedy for raw-flesh 
as they are.

shloka:
अगस्त्येन तदा देवैः प्रार्थितेन महर्षिणा |
अनुभूय किल श्राद्धे भक्षितः स महा असुरः
translation:
"Then by Sage Agastya, whom gods have prayed to end this demonic menace, and whom demon Ilvala invited 
to feast during obsequial rites, he that Agastya having relished the fiendish demon in the form of ram, 
they say, had finished him off.

shloka:
ततः संपन्नम् इति उक्त्वा दत्त्वा हस्ते अवनेजनम् |
भ्रातरम् निष्क्रमस्व इति च इल्वलः समभाषत
translation:
"Then Ilvala while giving lateral hand wash into the palms of Agastya entered in the routine conversation 
of obsequies asking, "Is this rite fulfilled..." and he furthered it in calling his brother to come 
out.

shloka:
स तदा भाषमाणम् तु भ्रातरम् विप्र घातिनम् |
अब्रवीत् प्रहसन् धीमान् अगस्त्यो मुनि सत्तमः
translation:
Then that wise and eminent sage Agastya spoke mockingly to Ilvala who is conversing that way to his 
brother to come out.

shloka:
कुतो निष्क्रमितुम् शक्तिर् मया जीर्णस्य रक्षसः |
भ्रातुः ते मेष रूपस्य गतस्य यम सादनम्
translation:
"Where is the energy for that ram shaped demon brother of yours to come out as I digested and sent him 
to the hellish residence of Terminator.

shloka:
अथ तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा भ्रातुर् निधन संश्रितम् |
प्रधर्षयितुम् आरेभे मुनिम् क्रोधात् निशा चरः
translation:
"Then on hearing the words of sage Agastya affirming brother's demise, that night-walking demon furiously 
commenced to assault the sage.

shloka:
सो अभ्यद्रवत् द्विजेंद्रम् तम् मुनिना दीप्त तेजसा |
चक्षुषा अनल कल्पेन निर्दग्धो निधनम् गतः
translation:
"When that demon rushed towards that best Bhraman to kill, he that sage glowing with his own refulgence 
burnt him down just by his flame-like eyes and doomed him to death.

shloka:
तस्य अयम् आश्रमो भ्रातुः तटाक वन शोभितः |
विप्र अनुकंपया येन कर्म इदम् दुष्करम् कृतम्
translation:
"This hermitage embellishing with lake and woods belongs to the brother of Sage Agastya who has done 
this impossible deed just by his compassion towards Brahmans." So said Rama to Lakshmana and Seetha 
about Agastya.

shloka:
एवम् कथयमानस्य तस्य सौमित्रिणा सह |
रामस्य अस्तम् गतः सूर्यः संध्या कालो अभ्यवर्तत
translation: While Rama narrated that way to Lakshmana sun went into dusk and the vesperal time came close of him.

shloka:
उपास्य पश्चिमाम् संध्याम् सह भ्रात्रा यथा विधि |
प्रविवेश आश्रम पदम् तम् ऋषिम् च अभ्यवादयत्
translation: Worshipping sunset along with brother as per custom, Rama entered that hermitage and greeted that sage.

shloka:
सम्यक् प्रतिगृहीतः तु मुनिना तेन राघवः |
न्यवसत् ताम् निशाम् एकाम् प्राश्य मूल फलानि च
translation: Raghava spent one night there when that sage received him well and when they dined on tubers and fruits.

shloka:
तस्याम् रात्र्याम् व्यतीतायाम् उदिते रवि मण्डले |
भ्रातरम् तम् अगस्त्यस्य आमंत्रयत राघवः
translation:
Raghava spent that night there and when sun rose in solar orbit he took leave of the brother of Sage 
Agastya saying the following.

shloka:
अभिवादये त्वाम् भगवन् सुखम् स्म उष्यतो निशाम् |
आमंत्रये त्वाम् गच्छ्हामि गुरुम् ते द्रष्टुम् अग्रजम्
translation:
"Oh, godly sage, we stayed in the night comfortably, I now make an obeisance and bid farewell to you, 
as I wish to proceed to see your mentor and elder brother Agastya.

shloka:
गम्यताम् इति तेन उक्तो जगाम रघु नन्दनः |
यथा उद्दिष्टेन मार्गेण वनम् तत् च अवलोकयन्
translation:
When the brother of Agastya said, "you may go," Rama the legatee of Raghu journeyed on the pathways 
as directed by Suteekshna, and on observing those woodlands.

shloka:
नीवारान् पनसान् सालान् वन्जुलान् तिनिशान् तथा |
चिरि बिल्वान् मधूकान् च बिल्वान् अथ च तिन्दुकान्
translation:
On observing the wild grass that grows on its own giving wild grain, Jack-fruit trees, sala trees, Ashoka 
trees, lemons trees, saplings of bilva trees and also madhuka and bilva trees he journeyed.

shloka:
पुष्पितान् पुष्पित अग्राभिर् लताभिर् उपशोभितान् |
ददर्श रामः शतशः तत्र कान्तार पादपान्
translation:
Rama has seen hundreds of flowered forest trees that are battered by the trunks of elephants, that are 
adorned with monkeys, reverberated by hundreds of lusty bird folks, and that are enriched by the flowered 
climbers whorled around them. [4-11-75, 76]

shloka:
ततो अब्रवीत् समीपस्थम् रामो राजीव लोचनः |
पृष्ठतो अनुगतम् वीरम् लक्ष्मणम् लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्
translation:
Then the lotus-eyed Rama said this to his follower Lakshmana who is a valiant and glory-enriching one 
and who is near at hand.

shloka:
स्निग्ध पत्रा यथा वृक्षा यथा क्षान्ता मृग द्विजाः |
आश्रमो न अतिदूरस्थो महर्षेर् भावित आत्मनः
translation:
"As to how the trees are appearing with velvety leaves, and as to how the animals and birds appear unwearied, 
thus gauging by this it appears that the hermitage of that contemplative soul Agastya is situated not 
very far from here.

shloka:
अगस्त्य इति विख्यातो लोके स्वेन एव कर्मणा |
आश्रमो दृश्यते तस्य परिश्रान्त श्रम अपहः
translation:
"He who by his own deed is renowned in the world as Agastya, the stopper of mountain, it appears to 
be his hermitage that alleviates the weary of wearied ones.

shloka:
प्राज्य धूम आकुल वनः चीर माला परिष्कृतः |
प्रशान्त मृग यूथः च नाना शकुनि नादितः
translation:
"The forest nearby this hermitage is overrun by huge smoke from altars of fire, overstuffed with the 
garlands of jute cloth, overcrowded with the herds of peaceful deer, and also overloaded with sonority 
of the birds.

shloka:
निगृह्य तरसा मृत्युम् लोकानाम् हित काम्यया |
दक्षिणा दिक् कृता येन शरण्या पुण्य कर्मणा
translation:
"He who impeding death by his yogic might and wishing well-being for worlds made this southern extent 
a liveable province by his pious deeds, his hermitage is this.

shloka:
तस्य इदम् आश्रम पदम् प्रभावाद् यस्य राक्षसैः |
दिक् इयम् दक्षिणा त्रासाद् दृश्यते न उपभुज्यते
translation:
"Under whose influence the demons behold this southern quarter appallingly, and they do not even venture 
to live here, such a sage Agastya's hermitage is this.

shloka:
यदा प्रभृति च आक्रान्ता दिग् इयम् पुण्य कर्मणा |
तदा प्रभृति निर् वैराः प्रशान्ता रजनी चराः
translation:
"And from when that pious deeded Agastya took possession of this quarter, from then on the night walkers 
are calmed down and remained without feud.

shloka:
नाम्ना च इयम् भगवतो दक्षिणा दिक् प्रदक्षिणा |
प्रथिता त्रिषु लोकेषु दुर्धर्षा क्रूर कर्मभिः
translation:
"This very worthy southern quarter is known in the name of that godly saint Agastya and this remained 
unattackable to the demons with cruel deeds.

shloka:
मार्गम् निरोद्धुम् सततम् भास्करस्य अचल उत्तमः |
संदेशम् पालयन् तस्य विंध्य शैलो न वर्धते
translation:
"Complying which sage's directive Mt. Vindhya ceased to heighten in order not to obstruct the path of 
the sun, such sage's hermitage is this who is renowned in the world by his deeds and whose longevity 
is inestimable, hence this glorious hermitage is adored by well-behaved animals and humans as well. 
[4-11-85, 86]

shloka:
एष लोक अर्चितः साधुः हिते नित्यम् रतः सताम् |
अस्मान् अधिगतान् एष श्रेयसा योजयिष्यति
translation:
"He that gentle sage who is always interested in the respect of sagacious ones is thus an esteemed one 
in the world, and for us when we approach him he accords beneficence.

shloka:
आराधयिष्यामि अत्र अहम् अगस्त्यम् तम् महामुनिम् |
शेषम् च वन वासस्य सौम्य वत्स्यामि अहम् प्रभो
translation:
"Oh, adept Lakshmana, I wish to worship that great saint Agastya therein that hermitage, and oh, gentle 
one, I think of living the remainder of forest living here only.

shloka:
अत्र देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाः च परम ऋषयः |
अगस्त्यम् नियत आहाराः सततम् पर्युपासते
translation:
"There gods with gandharva-s, siddha-s, exalted sages will be worshipping Agastya who is self-regulating 
self-disciplinary.

shloka:
न अत्र जीवेत् मृषावादी क्रूरो वा यदि वा शठः |
नृशंसः पाप वृत्तो वा मुनिः एष तथा विधः
translation:
"There no liar can live, nor a savage, nor even a deceiver, nor a man-torturer, nor one with sinful 
behaviour, for that sage is of that nature.

shloka:
अत्र देवाः च यक्षाः च नागाः च पतगैः सह |
वसन्ति नियत आहारा धर्मम् आराधयिष्णवः
translation: "There the gods, celestials, reptiles, birds live together wishing to worship the Absolute with self-discipline.

shloka:
अत्र सिद्धा महात्मानो विमानैः सूर्य सन्निभैः |
त्यक्त्वा देहान् नवैर् देहैः स्वर् याताः परम ऋषयः
translation:
"There the blest and great souls of accomplished ascesis rode to heavens by aircrafts similar to sun 
in resplendence, on relinquishing their mortal bodies here and on obtaining new bodies.

shloka:
यक्षत्वम् अमरत्वम् च राज्यानि विविधानि च |
अत्र देवाः प्रयच्छ्हन्ति भूतैः आराधिताः शुभैः
translation:
"There gods will endow the state of celestials or immortals, or many realms of divine living to those 
auspicious beings that worship them.

shloka:
आगताः स्म आश्रम पदम् सौमित्रे प्रविश अग्रतः |
निवेदय इह माम् प्राप्तम् ऋषये सह सीतया
translation:
"We arrived at the threshold of the hermitage, oh, Soumitri, you enter firstly and submit to Sage Agastya 
about my arrival at this place along with Seetha.

shloka:
स प्रविश्य आश्रम पदम् लक्ष्मणो राघव अनुजः |
अगस्त्य शिष्यम् आसाद्य वाक्यम् एतद् उवाच ह
translation:
On entering the hermitage Lakshmana, the younger brother of Raghava, reached Agastya's disciple and 
spoke this sentence to him.

shloka:
राजा दशरथो नाम ज्येष्ठः तस्य सुतो बली |
रामः प्राप्तो मुनिम् द्रष्टुम् भार्यया सह सीतया
translation:
"A king named Dasharatha was there, his eldest son and the dynamic one, Rama has arrived along with 
his wife Seetha to see the sage.

shloka:
लक्ष्मणो नाम तस्य अहम् भ्राता तु अवरजो हितः |
अनुकूलः च भक्तः च यदि ते श्रोत्रम् आगतः
translation:
"I am his loyal, dedicated, and adherent younger brother named Lakshmana, if ever you have heard of 
us.

shloka:
ते वयम् वनम् अत्युग्रम् प्रविष्टाः पितृ शासनात् |
द्रष्टुम् इच्छ्हामहे सर्वे भगवन्तम् निवेद्यताम्
translation:
"Such as we are, we entered the awful forest at the decree of our father, and we wiush to see the godly 
sage, let this be informed to him." Said Lakshmana to the disciple of Agastya.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणस्य तपोधनः |
तथा इति उक्त्वा अग्नि शरणम् प्रविवेश निवेदितुम्
translation:
On hearing that sentence of Lakshmana that disciple who is ascetically rich replied 'agreed, ' and he 
entered the sanctum of Ritual-fire to submit the same to Agastya.

shloka:
स प्रविश्य मुनिश्रेष्ठम् तपसा दुष्प्रधर्षणम् |
कृत अंजलिः उवाच इदम् राम आगमनम् अञ्जसा
translation:
He that agreeable disciple of sage quickly approached the irrefutable sage by his asceticism, made palm-fold 
and said this to the eminent sage about about the arrival of Rama, exactly as said by Lakshmana. [3-12-6, 
7a]

shloka: पुत्रौ दशरथस्य इमौ रामो लक्ष्मण एव च
translation:
"Sons of King Dasharatha, Rama and also thus Lakshmana have entered the threshold of hermitage along 
with the wife of Rama, namely Seetha. [3-12-7b, 8a]

shloka: द्रष्टुम् भवन्तम् आयातौ शुश्रूषार्थम् अरिन्दमौ
translation:
"Those two enemy-destroyers have come cherishing to see and serve you, hence it will be apt of you to 
order what next is to be done in this regard." Said disciple to the sage. [3-12-8b, 9a]

shloka: ततः शिष्यात् उपश्रुत्य प्राप्तम् रामम् स लक्ष्मणम्
translation:
Having heard from the disciple that Rama has arrived with Lakshmana and with highly fortunate Seetha 
the sage said this to him. [3-12-9b, 10a]

shloka: दिष्ट्या रामः चिरस्य अद्य द्रष्टुम् माम् समुपागतः
translation:
"My heart is indeed yearning for his arrival, and after this long a time Rama providentially came to 
see me." [3-12-10b, 11a]

shloka: गम्यताम् सत्कृतो रामः स भार्यः सह लक्ष्मणः
translation:
"Go forth and make welcome to Rama, Lakshmana and to Seetha, and they be entered here, why you have 
not invited them as yet? [3-12-11b, 12a]

shloka: एवम् उक्तः तु मुनिना धर्मज्ञेन महात्मना
translation:
Thus said by the great-souled sage and the knower of virtue, the disciple adored him with palm-fold 
saying that "as you say." [3-12-12b, 13a]

shloka: तदा निष्क्रम्य संभ्रान्तः शिष्यो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Then that disciple went out with a little perplexity and said this to Lakshmana, "Where is this Rama? 
He may come to see the sage and let him enter hermitage on his own." Said that disciple to Lakshmana. 
[3-12-13b, 14a]

shloka: ततो गत्वा आश्रम पदम् शिष्येण सह लक्ष्मणः
translation:
Then on going out to the exterior of that hermitage along with that disciple, Lakshmana has shown him 
Rama and Janaka's daughter Seetha. [3-12-14b, 15a]

shloka: तम् शिष्यः प्रश्रितम् वाक्यम् अगस्त्य वचनम् ब्रुवन्
translation:
While that disciple repeated the obliging words of Agastya entered that reception-worthy Rama into hermitage 
on receiving him well. [3-12-15b, 16a]

shloka: प्रविवेश ततो रामः सीतया सह लक्ष्मणः
translation:
And then Rama entered the hermitage with Seetha and Lakshmana looking over it which is overspread with 
docile deer. [ 3-12-16b, 17a]

shloka: स तत्र ब्रह्मणः स्थानम् अग्नेः स्थानम् तथैव च
translation:
Rama entered inside the hermitage and saw therein the sanctus of Brahma, Fire-god, Vishnu, Indra, Vivasvat 
- the Sun-god, Soma - the Moon-god, Bhaga - one among the twelve Suns, and the sanctusms of Kubera, 
[Wealth-Management-god, are seen and passed by the three of them, sanctums of Dhaata, Vidhaata - Vedic 
deities created by Brahma to help Svayambhuu Manu, santucm of Vaayu - the Air-god, and also like that 
the sanctum of great-soloed VaruNa - the Rain-god who also wields noose, and the sanctum of Gayatri 
- the presiding deity of gnosis, sanctum of Vasus - eight of them, and the sanctum of cobra's king - 
aadi sheSa, the divine Thousand-headed serpent that bears this globe on its head, and on which Vishnu 
reclines, and even the sanctum of GaruDa - the Divine Eagle and the vehicle of Vishnu, and the half 
brother of aadi sheSa, and the sanctum of Kaartikeya - chief of gods army, second son of Shiva, and 
the sanctum of Dharma - Dharmaraaja, presiding deity of Virtue-Vice-Time of living beings, in-charge 
of the hell. [17b, 18, 19, 20, 21a]

shloka: ततः शिष्यैः परिवृतो मुनिर् अपि अभिनिष्पतत्
translation:
Then encircled by disciples the sage Agastya came out quickly, and Rama saw him who is glowing brilliant 
before all the other sages. [3-12-21b, 22a]

shloka: अब्रवीत् वचनम् वीरो लक्ष्मणम् लक्ष्मिवर्धनम्
translation:
On seeing the brilliantly glowing sage among those sages, he that bold Rama said this sentence to Lakshmana, 
the fortifier of fortune, "Here comes the godly sage, Lakshmana, by his eminence I comprehend him as 
a depository of all ascesis." [3-12-22b, 23]

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा महाबाहुः अगस्त्यम् सूर्य वर्चसम् |
जग्राह आपतत् तस्य पादौ च रघुनन्दन
translation:
That dexterous Rama on saying about that sun-like radiant sage Agastya, he that descendent of Raghu 
fell on the feet of Agastya touching them reverentially.

shloka:
अभिवाद्य तु धर्मात्मा तस्थौ रामः कृतांजलिः |
सीतया सह वैदेह्या तदा रामः स लक्ष्मणः
translation:
Then he who is a delight to the on lookers that noble-hearted Rama on revering the sage along with Lakshmana 
and Seetha, the princess from Videha, stood aside with his palms adjoined.

shloka:
प्रतिगृह्य च काकुत्स्थम् अर्चयित्वा आसन उदकैः |
कुशल प्रश्नम् उक्त्वा च आस्यताम् इति सोऽब्रवीत्
translation:
Offering seat and water that sage received Rama, and even on exchanging pleasantries that sage said 
to him, "please be seated."

shloka:
अग्निम् हुत्वा प्रदाय अर्घ्यम् अतिथिन् प्रतिपूज्य च |
वानप्रस्थेन धर्मेण स तेषाम् भोजनम् ददौ
translation:
Having completed his personal worship to Fire-god, and having offered water and other formalities to 
guest, that sage gave viands to guests according to his hermitic observances.

shloka:
प्रथमम् च उपविश्य अथ धर्मज्ञो मुनिपुंगवः |
उवाच रामम् आसीनम् प्रांजलिम् धर्मकोविदम्
translation:
Then that eminent and shrewd sage Agastya in righteousness took his seat at the outset, and spoke to 
prudent Rama of righteousness itself, and who by now is sitting with his palms adjoined.

shloka:
अग्निम् हुत्वा प्रदाय अर्घ्यम् अतिथिम् प्रतिपूजयेत् |
अन्यथा खलु काकुत्स्थ तपस्वी समुदाचरन् |
दुःसाक्षी इव परे लोके स्वानि मांसानि भक्षयेत्
translation:
"Worshipping the fire, giving water and worshipping the guest a hermit should receive a guest and feed 
him, and if a hermit practices contrarily, oh, Rama, he is destined to eat his own flesh like a false 
deponent in other world say, hell.

shloka:
राजा सर्वस्य लोकस्य धर्मचारी महारथः |
पूजनीयः च मान्यः च भवान् प्राप्तः प्रिय अतिथिः
translation:
"You are the king of all the world, the treader in the path of righteousness, great charioteer of probity, 
and you are the venerable and estimable one, and you have arrived as my dear guest.

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा फलैः मूलैः पुष्पैः च अन्यैः च राघवम् |
पूजयित्वा यथा कामम् ततो अगस्त्यः तम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Saying thus, Agastya adored Raghava well with fruits, tubers, flowers and others according to his ardency, 
and then he said this to Rama.

shloka:
इदम् दिव्यम् महत् चापम् हेम वज्र विभूषितम् |
वैष्णवम् पुरुषव्याघ्र निर्मितम् विश्वकर्मणा
translation:
"This sacred bow that is decorated with gold and diamonds is crafted by the divine architect Vishvakarma 
pertains to Vishnu, and these unwasteful arrows equalling sun in their blaze are the gift of Brahma. 
[3-12-32, 33a]

shloka: दत्तो मम महेन्द्रेण तूणी च अक्षय सायकौ
translation:
"Also these two inexhaustible quivers packed with arrows that have the blaze of Ritual-fire, and this 
sword decorated in gold together with its sheath made up of excellent golden are once given to me by 
Indra. [3-12-33b, 34]

shloka:
अनेन धनुषा राम हत्वा संख्ये महासुरान् |
आजहार श्रियम् दीप्ताम् पुरा विष्णुर् दिव ओकसाम्
translation:
"By this bow, oh, Rama, once Vishnu eliminated horrible demons in war and brought back radiant prosperity 
to the celestials.

shloka:
तत् धनुः तौ च तूणि च शरम् खड्गम् च मानद |
जयाय प्रतिगृह्णीष्व वज्रम् वज्रधरो यथा
translation:
"The bow, these two quivers, arrows, and the sword, oh, Rama, the endower of grace, receive and wield 
them to triumph over the demons as Indra would wield Thunderbolt.

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा महा तेजाः समस्तम् तत् वर आयुधम् |
दत्त्वा रामाय भगवान् अगस्त्यः पुनर् अब्रवीत्
translation:
On saying thus that great resplendent and godly sage Agastya, gave all of those best weapons to Rama, 
and again spoke to Rama

shloka:
राम प्रीतो अस्मि भद्रम् ते परितुष्टो अस्मि लक्ष्मण |
अभिवादयितुम् यन् माम् प्राप्तौ स्थः सह सीतया
translation:
" I am delighted Rama, safe you be, oh Lakshmana, well-contended I am for you have
come to pay respects to me along with Seetha.

shloka:
अध्व श्रमेण वाम् खेदो बाधते प्रचुर श्रमः |
व्यक्तम् उत्कण्ठते वा अपि मैथिली जनक आत्मजा
translation:
"The well-worn trail of yours on pathway is strenuousness and painful for you two,
and it is evident from the sweat above your necks, even much more for Janaka's daughter, Maithili.

shloka:
एषा च सुकुमारी च खेदैः च न विमानिता |
प्राअज्य दोषम् वनम् प्रप्ता भर्तृ स्नेह प्रचोदिता
translation:
"She is delicate and not discomforted by such distresses earlier, yet motivated by
her friendship she came to these highly detrimental forests.

shloka:
यथा एषा रमते राम इह सीता तथा कुरु |
दुष्करम् कृतवती एषा वने त्वाम् अभिगच्छ्हती
translation:
"In which way Seetha takes delight in these forests, Rama, that you may ensure
to her, for she has done an impossible deed in following you to forests, an impossible deed for
womenfolk, in general.

shloka:
एषा हि प्रकृतिः स्त्रीणाम् आसृष्टे रघुनंदन |
समस्थम् अनुरंजंते विषमस्थम् त्यजन्ति च
translation:
"From the beginning of creation the nature of women is this way only, oh scion of
Raghu, they devote themselves to their men in good fortune, but they leave them off in ill fortune.

shloka:
शत ह्रदानाम् लोलत्वम् शस्त्राणाम् तीक्ष्णताम् तथा |
गरुड अनिलयोः शैघ्र्यम् अनुगच्छ्हन्ति योषितः
translation:
"With the mercuriality of hundreds of streaks of thunderbolt and with the
incisiveness of a weapon, and with the speediness of an eagle or the gusty wind, the women are
conformable.

shloka:
इयम् तु भवतो भार्या दोषैर् एतैर् विवर्जिताः |
श्लाघ्या च व्यपदेश्या च यथा देवी हि अरुन्धती
translation:
"But she this wife of yours is devoid of all those stigmas, an exemplary and an
estimable lady, like Lady Arundhati.

shloka:
अलंकृतो अयम् देशः च यत्र सौमित्रिणा सह |
वैदेह्या च अनया राम वत्स्यसि त्वम् अरिंदम
translation:
"Where you wish to put up along with Lakshmana and with this Seetha, oh,
enemy-destroyer Rama, that province shall be glorified." So said Sage Agastya to Rama."

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु मुनिना राघवः संयत अंजलिः |
उवाच प्रश्रितम् वाक्यम् ऋषिम् दीप्तम् इव अनलम्
translation:
Thus said by the sage, Raghava spoke amiable this sentence adjoining his palms to
the sage who is glowing like a ritual-fire.

shloka:
धन्योस्मि अनुगृहीतोस्मि यस्य मे मुनि पुंगवः |
गुणैः सभ्रातृ भार्यस्य गुरुः नः परितुष्यति
translation:
"I am privileged and blessed as my mentor and the eminent age is well pleased with
the virtues of my brother and wife which are non-dissimilar to mine.

shloka:
किन्तु व्यादिश मे देशम् स उदकम् बहु काननम् |
यत्र आश्रम पदम् कृत्वा वसेयम् निरतः सुखम्
translation:
"But a place with water and many forests may please be shown, where I can reside
happily and self-composedly on erecting a hermitage." Thus Rama asked the Sage Agastya.

shloka:
ततो अब्रवीत् मुनि श्रेष्ठः श्रुत्वा रामस्य भाषितम् |
ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तम् धर्मात्मा धीरो धीरतरम् वचः
translation:
Then that eminent sage Agastya on contemplating a while about what Rama has said,
that virtuous and confident sage spoke more ideational word to Rama.

shloka:
इतो द्वि योजने तात बहु मूल फल उदकः |
देशो बहु मृगः श्रीमान् पंचवटि अभिविश्रुतः
translation:
"A most prosperous place called Panchavati is there at a distance of two yojana-s
from here, oh, dear Rama, which is abundant with tubers, fruits, water, and many deer." Thus
Agastya started to tell.

shloka:
तत्र गत्वा आश्रम पदम् कृत्वा सौमित्रिणा सह |
रमस्व त्वम् पितुर् वाक्यम् यथा उक्तम् अनुपालयन्
translation:
"On your going there along with Saumitri, and on erecting a hermitage you may
take delight in there complying the decreed order of your father.

shloka:
विदितो हि एष वृत्तांतो मम सर्वः तव अनघ |
तपसः च प्रभावेण स्नेहाद् दशरथस्य च
translation:
"Indeed all of this episode of yours is known to me, oh, merited one, by the
ability of my asceticism, and also by my friendship with Dasharatha.

shloka:
हृदयस्थः च ते छ्हन्दो विज्ञातः तपसा मया |
इह वासम् प्रतिज्ञाय मया सह तपो वने
translation:
"I am in the know of your heartfelt certitude by my ascesis, thereby I wish to
advise you to go to Panchavati, though I said that you may dwell in these ascetic-woods along with
me. [3-13-16, 17a]

shloka: स हि रम्यो वनोद्देशो मैथिली तत्र रंस्यते
translation:
"That woodland will be delightful, isn't it Raghava, for it is praiseworthy and not
very far off from here, and Seetha can take delight in there. [3-13-17b, 18a]

shloka: गोदावर्याः समीपे च मैथिली तत्र रंस्यते
translation:
"There Maithili will take delight nearby River Godavari, and it is with abundant
tubers, fruits, various are its bird flocks, and it is very reclusive too, oh, great dextrous Rama,
further it is meritorious and appealing. [3-13-18b, 19]

shloka:
भवान् अपि सदाचारः च शक्तः च परिरक्षणे |
अपि च अत्र वसन् राम तापसान् पालयिष्यसि
translation:
"Even you, Rama, with your good deportment are capable to safeguard the hermits
while residing there.

shloka:
एतत् आलक्ष्यते वीर मधूकानाम् महत् वनम् |
उत्तरेण अस्य गंतव्यम् न्यग्रोधम् अपि गच्छ्हता
translation:
"Oh, brave one, you see this great forest of flower-liquor trees, you have to
proceed north of it and advance towards a banyan tree.

shloka:
ततः स्थलम् उपारुह्य पर्वतस्य अविदूरतः |
ख्यातः पंचवटी इति एव नित्य पुष्पित काननः
translation:
"Then on climbing up an upland a mountain is seen, that which is also not far away,
and that renowned Panchavati is there in an ever-blooming forest in the valley of that mountain."
Said Sage Agastya to Rama.

shloka:
अगस्त्येन एवम् उक्तः तु रामः सौमित्रिणा सह |
सत्कृत्य आमंत्रयामास तम् ऋषिम् सत्य वादिनम्
translation:
When thus said by Sage Agastya, Rama along with Soumitri venerated and bade farewell
to that truth advocator sage Agastya.

shloka:
तौ तु तेन अभ्यनुज्ञातौ कृत पाद अभिवन्दनौ |
तम् आश्रमम् पंचवटीम् जग्मतुः सह सीतया
translation:
Thus well bidden by Sage Agastya those two Rama and Lakshmana have offered their
venerations at the feet of that sage and proceeded to their prospective hermitage at Panchavati
along with Seetha.

shloka:
गृहीत चापौ तु नराधिप आत्मजौ
विषक्त तूणी समरेषु अकातरौ |
यथा उपदिष्टेन पथा महर्षिणा |
प्रजग्मतुः पंचवटीम् समाहितौ
translation:
Those princes that are dauntless in war took up their bows and braced up their
quivers, and resolutely proceeded to Panchavati on the route apprised by that great sage Agastya.

shloka:
अथ पंचवटीम् गच्चन्न् अन्तरा रघुनन्दनः |
आससाद महाकायम् गृध्रम् भीम पराक्रमम्
translation:
Then while proceeding to Panchavati that Rahu's descendent came across a mammoth eagle with marvellous 
might in midway.

shloka:
तम् दृष्ट्वा तौ महाभागौ वनस्थम् राम लक्ष्मणौ |
मेनाते राक्षसम् पक्षिम् ब्रुवाणौ को भवान् इति
translation:
On seeing such an eagle in the forest those two highly privileged brothers Rama and Lakshmana questioned 
it asking, "Who you are?" presuming it to be a demon.

shloka:
स तौ मधुरया वाचा सौम्यया प्रीणयन्न् इव |
उवाच वत्स माम् विद्धि वयस्यम् पितुर् आत्मनः
translation:
But that eagle with sweet ad soft words spoke to them as though to please them, "oh boy Rama know me 
as your father's friend."

shloka:
स तम् पितृ सखम् मत्वा पूजयामास राघवः |
स तस्य कुलम् अव्यग्रम् अथ पप्रच्छ्ह नाम च
translation:
Accepting that bird as his father's friend Raghava revered it, and he that Rama then asked for that 
eagle's name and lineage.

shloka:
रामस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा कुलम् आत्मानम् एव च |
आचचक्षे द्विजः तस्मै सर्वभूत समुद्भवम्
translation:
On hearing Rama's words that bird said about his ancestry and himself, and in doing so, that eagle also 
narrated the overall genesis of all beings.

shloka:
पूर्वकाले महाबाहो ये प्रजापतयो अभवन् |
तान् मे निगदतः सर्वान् आदितः शृणु राघव
translation:
"Once upon a time there were lords of people, oh dextrous Raghava, and you may listen all about them 
from the beginning, while I narrate

shloka:
कर्दमः प्रथमः तेषाम् विकृतः तद् अनन्तरम् |
शेषः च संश्रयः चैव बहु पुत्रः च वीर्यवान्
translation:
"Of them Kardama was there at first, and afterwards Sesha, and later Samshraya was there with many children 
and a vigorous one he was. Then Sthaanu, Mariichi, Atri, the great mighty one Kratu, Pulasthya, Angira, 
Pracheta and Pulah were there. And oh, Raghava, Daksha, Vivaswan were while the other name of Vivasvan 
is Arishtanemi, and lastly the great resplendent Kashyapa, was there as Prajapati.

shloka:
प्रजापतेः तु दक्षस्य बभूवुर् इति विश्रुतम् |
षष्टिर् दुहितरो राम यशस्विन्यो महायशः
translation: "Oh glorious Rama, there were sixty highly renowned daughters to Daksha, thus we hear.

shloka:
कश्यपः प्रतिजग्राह तासाम् अष्टौ सुमध्यमाः |
अदितिम् च दितिम् चैव दनूम् अपि च कालकाम्
translation:
"Of them Kashyapa accepted eight slender-waisted daughters of Daksha Prajapati, namely Aditi, Diti, 
Danu, Kaalakaa and Taamra, Krodhavasha, also thus Manu and even Anala also as wives. [3-14-11, 12a]

shloka: ताः तु कन्याः ततः प्रीतः कश्यपः पुनर् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"Then Kashyapa is gladdened and said to those young wives, "You all shall deliver sons similar to me 
and who can sustain the three worlds." [3-14-12b, 13a]

shloka: अदितिः तन् मना राम दितिः च दनुर् एव च
translation:
"Oh, dextrous Rama, Aditi, Diti, Kaalakaa and Danu have agreed for that, but others became unheedful 
of Kashyapa's words. [3-14-13b, 14a]

shloka: अदित्याम् जज्ञिरे देवाः त्रयः त्रिंशत् अरिंदम
translation:
"Aditi gave birth to twelve Aditya-s, the Sun-gods, eight Vasu-s, the Terrestrials-gods, eleven Rudraa-s, 
the Fury-gods, and two Ashvinis, the medicine-gods, total thirty-three of them. [3-14-14b, 15a]

shloka: दितिः तु अजनयत् पुत्रान् दैत्याम् तात यशस्विनः
translation:
"Oh, boy Rama, Diti gave birth to well-known Daitya-s, the so-called demons, and earlier this earth 
with forests and oceans belonged to them. [3-14-15b, 16a]

shloka: दनुः तु अजनयत् पुत्रम् अश्वग्रीवम् अरिंदम
translation:
"And oh, enemy-destroyer Rama, Danu gave birth to son Ashvagriiva or also called Hayagriiva, Horse-headed 
god, and Kaalakaa gave birth to Naraka and Kaalaka. [3-14-16b, 17a]

shloka: क्रौन्चीम् भासीम् तथा श्येनीम् धृतराष्ट्रीम् तथा शुकीम्
translation:
"But Taamraa gave birth to five world renowned girls namely, Krounchi, Bhaasii, Shyenii, Dhritaraashtrii, 
and Shukii. [3-14-17b, 18a]

shloka: उलूकान् जनयत् क्रौन्ची भासी भासान् व्यजायत
translation:
"And from each of the five daughters of Taamraa in turn emanated are the other avian species, where 
Kraunchii gave birth to Uluuka-s, the owls, Bhasii-s gave birth to Bhaasaa-s, the vultures, and Shyenii 
gave birth to very sharp eagles and falcons, and then Dhritaraashtrii gave birth to swans and all other 
kinds of graceful water-birds. [3-14-18b, 19]

shloka:
चक्रवाकाम् च भद्रम् ते विजज्ञे सा अपि भामिनी |
शुकी नताम् विजज्ञे तु नताया विनता सुता
translation:
"Dhritaraashtrii gave birth even to Chakravaaka water-birds, and Shukii gave birth to a daughter Nata, 
and Nata's daughter is Vinata.

shloka:
दश क्रोधवशा राम विजज्ञे अपि आत्मसंभवाः |
मृगीम् च मृगमंदाम् च हरीम् भद्रमदाम् अपि
translation:
"Oh, Rama, Krodhavasha gave birth to ten of her self-same daughters namely Mrigi, Mrigamanda, Hari, 
Bhadramanda, Maatangii, Sharduulii, Shweta, Surabhii, and like that to Surasa, who is embodied with 
all giftedness, and even to Kadruva. [3-14-21, 22]

shloka:
अपत्यम् तु मृगाः सर्वे मृग्या नरवरोत्तम |
ऋक्षाः च मृगमंदायाः सृमराः चमराः तथा
translation:
"Children Mrigi are all of the the deer, oh best of the best-men, Rama, and Mrigamnda's progeny is Riksha-s, 
Bears, a kind of antelope, and like that the Himalayan yak like species.

shloka:
ततः तु इरावतीम् नाम जज्ञे भद्रमदा सुताम् |
तस्याः तु ऐरावतः पुत्रो लोकनाथो महागजः
translation:
"Then Bhadramanda gave birth to the girl named Iravati and her son is elephant the great, Airaavata, 
the protector of world.

shloka:
हर्याः च हरयो अपत्यम् वानराः च तपस्विनः |
गोला.ंगूलाः च शार्दूली व्याघ्राम् च अजनयत् सुतान्
translation:
"And Hari's offspring are lions and sagely/mighty monkeys, while Sharduulii gave birth to baboons and 
tigers.

shloka:
मात.ंग्याः तु अथ मातंगाअपत्यम् मनुज ऋषभ |
दिशागजम् तु श्वेत काकुत्स्थ श्वेता व्यजनयत् सुतम्
translation:
"Then Maatangi's childrenm are elephants, oh, best one among men, Rama, and Shweta gave birth to eight 
elephants that are at eight quarters of world, sustaining the world on their head.

shloka:
ततो दुहितरौ राम सुरभिर् द्वे वि अजायत |
रोहिणीम् नाम भद्रम् ते गन्धर्वीम् च यशस्विनीम्
translation:
"Then, oh Rama, Surabhi gave birth to two daughters, one is named as illustrious Rohini, safe you 
be, and the other is Gandharvi.

shloka:
रोहिणि अजनयद् गावो गन्धर्वी वाजिनः सुतान् |
सुरसा अजनयन् नागान् राम कद्रूः च पन्नगान्
translation:
"Rohini gave birth to cows and other livestock, while Surasa gave birth to Naagaa-s, viz., many headed 
serpents, while Kadru gave birth to ordinary serpents.

shloka:
मनुर् मनुष्यान् जनयत् कश्यपस्य महात्मनः |
ब्राह्मणान् क्षत्रियान् वैश्यान् शूद्राम् च मनुजर्षभ
translation:
"Oh, the best among men Rama, the wife of great-soul Kashyapa, lady Manu procreated humans, Brahman--s, 
Kshatriya-s, Vyasya-s, and Shudra-s.

shloka:
मुखतो ब्राह्मणा जाता उरसः क्षत्रियाः तथा |
ऊरुभ्याम् जज्ञिरे वैश्याः पद्भ्याम् शूद्रा इति श्रुतिः
translation:
"The Brahman-s emerged from face, the Kshatriya-s from chest, the Vyasya-s from two thighs, and the 
Shudra-s from two feet, thus we hear from the scriptures viz., Veda, i.e., Rig Veda Purusha Shuukta.

shloka:
सर्वान् पुण्य फलान् वृक्षान् अनला अपि व्यजायत |
विनता च शुकी पौत्री कद्रूः च सुरसा स्वसा
translation:
"All the merited fruit-bearing trees are given birth by Anala, and now I will narrate about Vinata, 
the daughter's daughter of Shukii, and about Kadru, the sister of Surasa.

shloka:
कद्रूर् नाग सहस्रम् तु विजज्ञे धरणीधरन् |
द्वौ पुत्रौ विनतायाः तु गरुडो अरुण एव च
translation:
"Kadru gave birth to a thousand-headed serpent who is the bearer of this earth, and Vinata gave birth 
to two sons namely Garuda and Aruna.

shloka:
तस्मात् जातो अहम् अरुणात् संपातिः च मम अग्रजः |
जटायुर् इति माम् विद्धि श्येनी पुत्रम् अरिंदम
translation:
"Oh enemy-destroyer Rama, I took birth from that Aruna, the charioteer of Sun, and my elder brother 
Sampati too, hence know me as Jatayu, the son of Shyenii.

shloka:
सो अहम् वास सहायः ते भविष्यामि यदि इच्छ्हसि |
इदम् दुर्गम् हि कान्तारम् मृग राक्षस सेवितम्
सीताम् 
च तात रक्षिष्ये त्वयि याते सलक्ष्मणे
translation:
"Such as I am, I can be your helpmate at your residence if only you wish me to... oh, boy, this impassable 
forest is a beloved one to predators and demons, isn't it... as such I can take care of Seetha if you 
and Lakshmana go out..." Thus Jatayu said to Rama.

shloka:
जटायुषम् तु प्रतिपूज्य राघवो
मुदा परिष्वज्य च सन्नतो अभवत् |
पितुर् हि शुश्राव सखित्वम् आत्मवान्
जटायुषा संकथितम् पुनः पुनः
translation:
Raghava revered Jatayu in his turn by gladly hugging and stood by him with his head bent, and that kind-natured 
Rama is indeed regardful of the friendship of his father with Jatayu that is repeatedly said by Jatayu.

shloka:
स तत्र सीताम् परिदाय मैथिलीम्
सह एव तेन अतिबलेन पक्षिणा |
जगाम ताम् पंचवटीम् सलक्ष्मणो
रिपून् 
दिधक्षन् शलभान् इव अनलः
translation:
He that Rama took the princess from Mithila Seetha, and proceeded to Panchavati along with that very 
mighty bird and Lakshmana, as though to incinerate enemies, like fire that burns down grasshoppers.

shloka:
ततः पंचवटीम् गत्वा नाना व्याल मृगायुताम् |
उवाच भ्रातरम् रामो लक्ष्मणम् दीप्त तेजसम्
translation:
Then on going to Panchavati which is full with many serpents and predators, Rama said to splendidly 
brilliant Lakshmana.

shloka:
आगताः स्म यथा उद्दिष्टम् यम् देशम् मुनिः अब्रवीत् |
अयम् पंचवटी देशः सौम्य पुष्पित काननः
translation:
"We arrived at the place as indicated by the sage, oh, gentle Lakshmana, this region with its flowered 
forests is Panchavati."

shloka:
सर्वतः चार्यताम् दृष्टिः कानने निपुणो हि असि |
आश्रमः कतर अस्मिन् नः देशे भवति सम्मतः
translation:
"In which place we have to situate our hermitage for our liking, for that cast your sight all over the 
forest, and indeed you are an expert in such matters.

shloka:
रमते यत्र वैदेही त्वम् अहम् चैव लक्ष्मण |
तादृशो दृश्यताम् देशः संनिकृष्ट जलाशयः
translation:
"In which place Vaidehi, likewise you and me too can take delight, where the woodland is scenic and 
the water is pleasurable, and where a water lake, ritual-firewood, flowers, and the sacred grass are 
available in proximity, oh, Lakshmana, such a place may be searched out. [3-15-4, 5]

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण लक्मणः संयत अंजलिः |
सीता समक्षम् काकुत्स्थम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
When thus said by Rama, Lakshmana adjoined his palms and said this sentence to Rama in the presence 
of Seetha.

shloka:
परवान् अस्मि काकुत्स्थ त्वयि वर्ष शतम् स्थिते |
स्वयम् तु रुचिरे देशे क्रियताम् इति माम् वद
translation:
"I am but a dependent, as long as you are there, may it be for innumerable years, I am your adherent, 
Rama, therefore you yourself tell me to build hermitage in such and such delightful place.

shloka:
सुप्रीतः तेन वाक्येन लक्ष्मणस्य महाद्युतिः |
विमृशन् रोचयामास देशम् सर्व गुण अन्वितम्
translation:
Rama is gladdened by those words of that great resplendent Lakshmana, and he selected a place that comprised 
of all the attributes.

shloka:
स तम् रुचिरम् आक्रम्य देशम् आश्रम कर्मणि |
हस्ते गृहीत्वा हस्तेन रामः सौमित्रिम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
On taking Lakshmana's hand by his hand Rama paced that beautiful place intended for the construction 
of hermitage up and down and spoke to Soumitri this way.

shloka:
अयम् देशः समः श्रीमान् पुष्पितैर् तरुभिर् वृतः |
इह आश्रम पदम् सौम्य यथावत् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"This is an evenly and propitious place surrounded with flowered trees and it is apt of you to erect 
hermitage here, traditionally.

shloka:
इयम् आदित्य संकाशैः पद्मैः सुरभि गंधिभिः |
अदूरे दृश्यते रम्या पद्मिनी पद्म शोभिता
translation:
"This pleasing lake is seen here adjacently, beaming forth with its lotuses that are similar to sun 
in resplendence, and that are scented fragrantly.

shloka:
यथा आख्यातम् अगस्त्येन मुनिना भावितात्मना |
इयम् गोदावरी रम्या पुष्पितैः तरुभिर् वृता
translation:
"This River Godavari is also seen from here, surrounded by blooming trees, spread over with swans, and 
beautified with kaarandava, and chakravaaka birds, as that contemplated soul sage Agastya had said.

shloka: न अतिदूरे न च आसन्ने मृग यूथ निपीडिता
translation:
"Those soaring mountains are appearing beautiful with many caves, surrounded by flowered trees, flurried 
by animal herds, sounded by peacocks, and they are neither far-off nor very nearby. [3-15-13, 14]

shloka:
सौवर्णै राजतैः ताम्रैः देशे देशे च धातुभिः |
गवाक्षिता इव आभान्ति गजाः परम भक्तिभिः
translation:
"Here and there are the golden, silvery and coppery ores on the mountains, and they are shining forth 
like cow-eye ventilators on walls and also like the superb paintings on elephants.

shloka:
सालैः तालैः तमालैः च खर्जूरैः पनसैः द्रुमैः |
नीवारैः तिनिशैः चैव पुन्नागैः च उपशोभिताः
translation:
"These mountains are brightening with trees of Saala, Palmyra, Tamaala, Date Palms, Jackfruit and also 
thus with Punnaagaa. With Chuuta - Sweet Mango; Ashoka, Tialaka, even with Ketaka, Champaka trees, And 
even with Syandana, Sandalwood, Niipa, Paarnasa, Lakuch, dhava, Ashwakarna, Khadira, Shamii, Kimshuka, 
Paatala trees, and entwined are those and those trees with flowered shrubs, and along with climbers, 
and thus they brighten the mountains. [3-15-16, 17, 18]

shloka:
इदम् पुण्यम् इदम् रम्यम् इदम् बहु मृग द्विजम् |
इह वत्स्याम सौमित्रे सार्धम् एतेन पक्षिणा
translation:
"This place is holy, this is delightful and this is with many animals and birds, hence Soumitri, let 
us reside here along with this bird Jatayu." Thus said Rama to Lakshmana.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा |
अचिरेण आश्रमम् भ्रातुः चकार सुमहाबलः
translation:
Thus said by Rama to that remover of foe's valour and one with very great might, namely Lakshmana, he 
briskly erected a hermitage for his brother.

shloka:
पर्णशालाम् सुविपुलाम् तत्र संघात मृत्तिकाम् |
सुस्तंभाम् मस्करैर् दीर्घैः कृत वंशाम् सुशोभनाम्
translation:
Lakshmana built a very spacious straw-cottage there levelling and raising the clay for raised floor 
of the cottage, strongly pillared with long bamboos, thereupon on those pillars excellent rafters are 
made, and the branches of Shamii trees are spread out, twined firmly with twines of jute strands, and 
with the cross-laid bamboos for thatching, and over that blades of Kusha grass and leaves of Kaasha 
are spread and well over-covered for the roof, and thus that very great mighty Lakshmana made that best 
and very spacious straw-cottage with a levelled surface for residence of Raghava in the interests of 
Raghava alone, and it resulted as a feast to the eye. [3-15-21, 22, 23]

shloka:
स गत्वा लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान् नदीम् गोदावरीम् तदा |
स्नात्वा पद्मानि च आदाय सफलः पुनर् आगतः
translation:
On his going to River Godavari that noble Lakshmana bathed and on gathering lotuses and fruits he returned 
to the cottage.

shloka:
ततः पुष्प बलिम् कृत्वा शान्तिम् च स यथाविधि |
दर्शयामास रामाय तद् आश्रम पदम् कृतम्
translation:
Then making flowery offerings and peace-invocations also procedural togR^iha 
pravesha, entering a new house,] started to show the constructed hermitage to Rama.

shloka:
स तम् दृष्ट्वा कृतम् सौम्यम् आश्रमम् सह सीतया |
राघवः पर्णशालायाम् हर्षम् आहारयत् परम्
translation:
On seeing the beautifully constructed hermitage along with Seetha, Rama is highly gladdened in respect 
that straw-cottage.

shloka:
सुसंहृष्टः परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्याम् लक्ष्मणम् तदा |
अति स्निग्धम् च गाढम् च वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Then Rama very highly gladdened Rama embraced Lakshmana tightly by both of his hands, and spoke these 
friendly words to him.

shloka:
प्रीतो अस्मि ते महत् कर्म त्वया कृतम् इदम् प्रभो |
प्रदेयो यन् निमित्तम् ते परिष्व.ंगो मया कृतः
translation:
"Oh, masterful one, I am very happy about you for you have done a great deed, for that reason I am giving 
what I have to give to you a hugging.

shloka:
भावज्ञेन कृतज्ञेन धर्मज्ञेन च लक्ष्मण |
त्वया पुत्रेण धर्मात्मा न संवृत्तः पिता मम
translation:
"You are the knower of others feelings, knower of many skills, and the knower of what is right and honest, 
oh, Lakshmana, such as you are, being with you I deem that my virtue-souled father is not gone and forgotten.

shloka:
एवम् लक्ष्मणम् उक्त्वा तु राघवो लक्ष्मिवर्धनः |
तस्मिन् देशे बहु फले न्यवसत् स सुखम् सुखी
translation:
On saying thus to Lakshmana, Raghava, the enhancer of magnificence comfortably resided in that province 
which is with many a fruit.

shloka:
कंचित् कालम् स धर्मात्मा सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च
अन्वास्यमानो न्यवसत् स्वर्ग लोके यथा अमरः
translation:
While Seetha and Lakshmana devoted themselves to that righteous Rama, he resided in Panchavati like 
a Divinity in heavenly world for sometime to come.

shloka:
वसतः तस्य तु सुखम् राघवस्य महात्मनः |
शरद् व्यपाये हेमंतऋतुर् इष्टः प्रवर्तत
translation:
Pleasanthemantha R^itu, pre-winter season has set in after the passage ofsharat R^itu, 
post-rainy season at Panchavati where the noble souled Rama is staying comfortably.

shloka:
स कदाचित् प्रभातायाम् शर्वर्याम् रघुनंदनः |
प्रययाव अभिषेकार्थम् रम्यम् गोदावरीम् नदीम्
translation: On some day when night faded into dawn Rama started for the delightful River Godavari for a bath.

shloka:
प्रह्वः कलश हसतः तम् सीतया सह वीर्यवान् |
पृष्ठतो अनुव्रजन् भ्राता सौमित्रिर् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
His valorous brother Saumitri following him humbly with a handy vessel, along with Seetha, spoke this 
to Rama.

shloka:
अयम् स कालः संप्राप्तः प्रियो यः ते प्रियंवद |
अलंकृत इव आभाति येन संवत्सरः शुभः
translation:
"Adorned by which season the promising year will be bright, oh, pleasant conversationalist, and which 
season will also be pleasant to you, that hemanta season has set in.

shloka:
नीहार परुषो लोकः पृथिवी सस्य मालिनी |
जलानि अनुपभोग्यानि सुभगो हव्य वाहनः
translation:
"These days the dew is harsh to the bodies of people, earth is overlaid with crops, water is unenjoyable, 
but fire is delightful.

shloka:
नव आग्रयण पूजाभिर् अभ्यर्च्य पितृ देवताः |
कृत आग्रयणकाः काले सन्तो विगत कल्मषाः
translation:
"On appeasing manes with worships during northern solstice and even on performing solstitial rituals 
in time, the righteous people are becoming free from evils.

shloka:
प्राज्यकामा जनपदाः संपन्नतर गो रसाः |
विचरन्ति महीपाला यात्र अर्थम् विजिगीषवः
translation:
"Amply fulfilled are the desires of the villagers with the affluence of milch cows and dairy, and the 
vanquishing kings are make moves for the purposes of their further vanquishes.

shloka:
सेवमाने दृढम् सूर्ये दिशम् अन्तक सेविताम् |
विहीन तिलका इव स्त्री न उत्तरा दिक् प्रकाशते
translation:
"While the sun is steadfastly attending the direction of Time-god Yama, namely southern horizon, the 
northern direction is not brilliant like a woman who lost the vermilion mark on her forehead.

shloka:
प्रकृत्या हिम कोश आढ्यो दूर सूर्याः च सांप्रतम् |
यथार्थ नामा सुव्यक्तम् हिमवान् हिमवान् गिरिः
translation:
"By their very nature Himalayas are the depositories of snow, and presently distanced from the sun they 
are very obviously snowy true to their name.

shloka:
अत्यन्त सुख संचारा मध्याह्ने स्पर्शतः सुखाः |
दिवसाः सुभग आदित्याअः छ्हाया सलिल दुर्भगाः
translation:
"By the way of touch the mid days are comfortable and in these days the daytime is very much comfortable 
for sauntering, thus the sun in daytimes is genial and ungenial are the shades and waters.

shloka:
मृदु सूर्याः सनीहाराः पटु शीताः समारुताः |
शून्य अरण्या हिम ध्वस्ता दिवसा भान्ति सांप्रतम्
translation:
"Overwhelmed by snow presently the noontimes are with soft sun, with bitter cold, with mists and wintry 
breezes, and with them the forests too are bleak in their sheen.

shloka:
निवृत्त आकाश शयनाः पुष्यनीता हिम अरुणाः |
शीता वृद्धतर आयामः त्रि यामा यान्ति सांप्रतम्
translation:
"Precluded is the reclining under open sky as the nights are led by the Pushya constellation, they will 
now be with brownish-grey fog and chilly, and prolonged are the lengths of nights whereby the three 
watches of night will be quickly slipping away.

shloka:
रवि संक्रान्त सौभाग्यः तुषार अरुण मण्डलः |
निःश्वास अन्ध इव आदर्शाः चंद्रमा न प्रकाशते
translation:
"Transgressed is the destiny of moon by the sun as moon lost the chance of keeping people happy with 
his lustrousness in these days, thus the lustreless moon remained in a blushing sphere with fog, just 
like a mirror blinded by the fog of a suspire.

shloka:
ज्योत्स्ना तुषार मलिना पौर्णमास्याम् न राजते |
सीता इव च आतप श्यामा लक्ष्यते न तु शोभते
translation:
"Even on a full moon day the moonlight is unbright blemished by mist, and it is appearing like brightly 
Seetha becoming swarthy by sun's heat, but not brightly.

shloka:
प्रकृत्या शीतल स्पर्शो हिम विद्धाः च सांप्रतम् |
प्रवाति पश्चिमो वायुः काले द्वि गुण शीतलः
translation:
"The western breeze by itself will be cool to touch, but presently charged with snow it is wafting doubly 
chilly in the early hours.

shloka:
बाष्प च्छ्हन्नानि अरण्यानि यव गोधूमवंति च |
शोभन्ते अभ्युदिते सूर्ये नदद्भिः क्रौन्च सारसैः
translation:
"Covered with the dew the forests that already covered with crop fields of barley and wheat are beaming 
forth, together with the callings of waterfowls, at the rise of the sun.

shloka:
खर्जूर पुष्प आकृतिभिः शिरोभिः पूर्ण तण्डुलैः |
शोभन्ते किंचिद् आलंबाः शालयः कनक प्रभाः
translation:
"The paddy crops in fields are gleaming forth with golden lustre, and their heads full with grain and 
a little bent down are shapely like the flowers of date-fruit.

shloka:
मयूखैः उपसर्पद्भिः हिम नीहार संवृतैः |
दूरम् अभ्युदितः सूर्यः शशांक इव लक्ष्यते
translation:
"Though he came up long back, and though his beams are spreading around, besieged by snowy mist the 
sun is appearing as moon.

shloka:
अग्राह्य वीर्यः पूर्वाह्णे मध्याह्ने स्पर्शतः सुखः |
संरक्तः किंचिद् आपाण्डुः आतपः शोभते क्षितौ
translation:
Inappreciable is the warmth of sun in the mornings, but comfortable for touch at noontimes, since the 
reddish but a little palish sunshine is radiating on earth.

shloka:
अवश्याय निपातेन किंचित् प्रक्लिन्न शाद्वला |
वनानाम् शोभते भूमिर् निविष्ट तरुण आतपा
translation:
"The pasturelands are a little moistened with the fall of dewdrops, but the fields of forest are enlivened 
by the radiance of tender sun's warmth.

shloka:
स्पृशन् तु सुविपुलम् शीतम् उदकम् द्विरदः सुखम् |
अत्यन्त तृषितो वन्यः प्रतिसंहरते करम्
translation:
"On easily touching very clear and cold water with its very broad trunk that intensely thirsty wild 
elephant is backing away its trunk for the water is that cold.

shloka:
एते हि समुपासीना विहगा जलचारिणः |
न अवगाहन्ति सलिलम् अप्रगल्भा इव आवहम्
translation: "These waterfowls that are sitting nearby are not entering into waters like cowards not entering battlefields.

shloka:
अवश्याय तमो नद्धा नीहार तमसा आवृताः |
प्रसुप्ता इव लक्ष्यन्ते विपुष्पा वन राजयः
translation:
"Subdued by snowy darkness, enclosed in misty gloom, and reft of flowers these forest ranges appear 
like those that are asleep.

shloka:
बाष्प संचन्न सलिला रुत विज्ञेय सारसाः |
हिमाअर्द्र वालुकैः तीरैः सरितो भान्ति सांप्रतम्
translation:
"Now the rivers are imperceptible as their water is overspread with dewdrops, but their water-birds 
are perceptible only by their callings, thus making that river perceptible, and such rivers are now 
glistening with moist sandbanks and shores.

shloka:
तुषार पतनात् चैव मृदुत्वात् भास्करस्य च |
शैत्यात् अग अग्रस्थम् अपि प्रायेण रसवत् जलम्
translation:
"Owing to the fall of snow, further owing to the softness and coldness of sun, the water deep down the 
wells is generally agreeable for drinking.

shloka:
जरा जर्जरितैः पत्रैः शीर्ण केसर कर्णिकैः |
नाल शेषा हिम ध्वस्ता न भान्ति कमलाकराः
translation:
"Lotus lakes are left alone with stalks of lotuses as their petals are aged and withered, decrepit are 
the fibrils and carpels, thus impaired by cold they are ungracious in look.

shloka:
अस्मिन् तु पुरुषव्याघ्र काले दुःख समन्वितः |
तपश्चरति धर्मात्मा त्वत् भक्त्या भरतः पुरे
translation:
"But during this time, oh, manly-tiger, ushered by anguish that virtue souled one Bharata must be practising 
ascesis in city with adoration to you.

shloka:
त्यक्त्वा राज्यम् च मानम् च भोगांश्च विविधान् बहून् |
तपस्वी नियताहारः शेते शीते महीतले
translation:
"On forsaking kingdom and pride of becoming the king of Ayodhya as well, and varied and various pleasures 
too, he is in self-denial, and with his food regulated he sleeps on chilly surface of earth.

shloka:
सोऽपि वेलाम् इमाम् नूनम् अभिषेक अर्थम् उद्यतः |
वृतः प्रकृतिभिर् नित्यम् प्रयाति सरयूम् नदीम्
translation:
"Even he might always be getting up at this time of the day and proceeding to River Sarayu for a bath 
surrounded by ministers, definite is that.

shloka:
अत्यन्त सुख संवृद्धः सुकुमारो हिमार्दितः |
कथम् तु अपर रात्रेषु सरयूम् अवगाहते
translation:
"But how can he who is brought up in high comfort, a delicate one too, enter the cold-wet waters of 
River Sarayu, in these small hours.

shloka:
पद्मपत्रेक्षणः श्यामः श्रीमान् निरुदरो महान् |
धर्मज्ञः सत्यवादी च ह्री निषेधो जितेन्द्रियः
translation:
"That lotus-petal eyed one with blue-black complexion is an imposing one with lion-like waist, being 
the noblest he is knower of dharma thus an advocate of truth, and thus intolerant of ignominy, and as 
a self-restrained one he talks dearly and sweetly, and he is dextrous and an enemy-destroyer, such as 
he is, that Bharata on forgoing all of his various pleasures he is devoted to you, as you alone are 
his adorable brother. [4-16-31, 32]

shloka:
जितः स्वर्गः तव भ्रात्रा भरतेन महात्मना |
वनस्थम् अपि तापस्ये यः त्वाम् अनुविधीयते
translation:
"Even though you are in forests far away from him, he is following you in the practise of austerities, 
and such a brother of yours, that great-souled Bharata has refused ascent to heaven.

shloka:
न पित्र्यम् अनुवर्न्तन्ते मातृकम् द्विपदा इति |
ख्यातो लोक प्रवादो अयम् भरतेन अन्यथा कृतः
translation:
"  Humans do not derive father's attitude but they take of their mothers' is the well-know maxim in 
the world, but Bharata rendered it otherwise.

shloka:
भर्ता दशरथो यस्याः साधुः च भरतः सुतः |
कथम् नु सा अम्बा कैकेयी तादृशी क्रूरदर्शिनी
translation:
"Whose husband is Dasharatha and whose son is gentle Bharata, how then can she, our mother Kaikeyi, 
is with this sort of cruel disposition, indeed " Thus Lakshmana spoke to Rama on their way to River 
Godavari.

shloka:
इति एवम् लक्ष्मणे वाक्यम् स्नेहात् वदति धर्मिके |
परिवादम् जनन्यः तम् असहन् राघवो अब्रवीत्
translation:
When that upright Lakshmana is speaking those words that way out of his fondness towards Rama, Raghava 
spoke to Lakshmana, intolerant of that slanderous talk about their mother.

shloka:
न ते अम्बा मध्यमा तात गर्हितव्या कथंचन |
ताम् एव इक्ष्वाकु नाथस्य भरतस्य कथाम् कुरु
translation:
"In any way, dear Lakshmana, you are not supposed to deplore another mother of ours, but you go on telling 
the topics of Bharata, the king of Ikshvaku-s.

shloka:
निश्चिता एव हि मे बुद्धिः वन वासे दृढ व्रता |
भरत स्नेह संतप्ता बालिशी क्रियते पुनः
translation:
"My mind is indeed set to dwell only in forest, and it is firmly avowed, but while yearning for Bharata's 
fellowship my fascination to reunite with him is recurring again.

shloka:
संस्मरामि अस्य वाक्यानि प्रियाणि मधुराणि च |
हृद्यानि अमृत कल्पानि मनः प्रह्लादानि च
translation: "I reminisce his words well, that are genial, sweet, heartily, ambrosial and that will gladden the heart.

shloka:
कदा हि अहम् समेष्यामि भरतेन महात्मना |
शत्रुघ्नेन च वीरेण त्वया च रघुनंदन
translation:
"When can I really reunite, oh, Lakshmana, with great-souled Bharata, valorous Shatrughna, and with 
you and Seetha." Thus said Rama to Lakshmana.

shloka:
इति एवम् विलपन् तत्र प्राप्य गोदावरीम् नदीम् |
चक्रे अभिषेकम् काकुत्स्थः सानुजः सह सीतया
translation:
Thus worrying that way while proceeding, there Rama reached River Godavari and performed bathing with 
his younger brother Lakshmana and along with Seetha.

shloka:
तर्पयित्वा अथ सलिलैः तैः पितॄन् दैवतानि च |
स्तुवन्ति स्म उदितम् सूर्यम् देवताअः च तथा अनघाः
translation:
Then on offering water oblations to manes and gods that impeccant trinity extolled the rising sun and 
gods likewise.

shloka:
कृताभिषेकः स रराज रामः
सीता द्वितीयः सह लक्ष्मणेन |
कृत अभिषेको तु अग राज पुत्र्या
रुद्रः स 
नन्दिः भगवान् इव ईशः
translation:
On taking bath in the river along with Seetha and Lakshmana, Rama shone forth like All-controlling god 
Rudra, who will be radiant on taking bath along with his consort Paarvati and with his follower Nandi, 
the Holy Bull.

shloka: एक्ष्तोल्लिंग् सेअसोन्स् इन् एपिच्स्
translation:
The portrayal of seasons in epics with all their delicacies is 
a disputed topic. Ramayana also deals much on these descriptions of seasons. Whether an epic avowed 
to reflect the Vedic import, as said at 1-4-6,vedopabR^ihmaNaarthaaya, and that which is 
pious and meritedpuNyam vedaischa samamatamat 1-1-98, should have accounts on seasons   is 
the question. For this is said that relating niceties of season time and again, is in perfect accord 
with Veda, for the season and time are subservient to all Veda-s as per the ancillary of Veda, the Astrology,veda-anga : jyotiShya. Veda-s themselves say that the year is the soul of the horse of Ashvameda.uShaa 
vaa ashvasya medhasya shiraH | sa~Nvatsara aatmaashvasya medhasya | -- yajurveda bR^ihadaaraNyakaHence time and season are the mind and soul of all Veda-s.

shloka:
कृत अभिषेको रामः तु सीता सौमित्रिर् एव च |
तस्मात् गोदावरी तीरात् ततो जग्मुः स्वम् आश्रमम्
translation:
On taking bath Rama with Seetha and Soumitri, then went to his own hermitage from that bank of River 
Godavari.

shloka:
आश्रमम् तम् उपागम्य राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः |
कृत्वा पौर्वाह्णिकम् कर्म पर्णशालाम् उपागमत्
translation:
Nearing that hermitage Raghava along with Lakshmana performed early morning rituals and then reached 
the cottage.

shloka:
उवास सुखितः तत्र पूज्यमानो महर्षभः|
स रामः पर्ण शालायाम् आसीनः सह सीतया
translation:
There Rama comfortably spent time while being adored by eminent sages when he is with them, and narrating 
many a narrative while sitting in hermitage along with Seetha and his brother Lakshmana, thus he shone 
forth like the moon when with Chitra constellation. [3-1-7-3, 4]

shloka:
तदा आसीनस्य रामस्य कथा संसक्त चेतसः |
तम् देशम् राक्षसी काचिद् आजगाम यदृच्छ्हया
translation:
At one time when Rama is sitting in hermitage and heartily absorbed in telling narratives some demoness 
arrived at that place, fortuitously.

shloka:
सा तु शूर्पणखा नाम दशग्रीवस्य रक्षसः |
भगिनी रामम् आसाद्य ददर्श त्रिदश उपमम्
translation:
She is but the sister of ten-faced demon Ravana, Shuurpanakha by her name and she has seen him on reaching 
the paradisiacal being like Rama.

shloka:
दीप्तास्यम् च महाबाहुम् पद्म पत्रायत ईक्षणम् |
गज विक्रांत गमनम् जटा मण्दल धारिणम्
translation:
