He whose face is radiant, arms lengthy, eyes large like lotus petals, stride like that of an elephant, 
wearing bunches of hair-tufts, delicate yet greatly vigorous, possessor of all kingly aspects, complexion 
deep-blue like blue lotus, similar to Love-god in brilliance and in simile to Indra, the demoness has 
seen such a Rama and became lovesick. [3-17-7, 8, 9a]

shloka: सुमुखम् दुर्मुखी रामम् वृत्त मध्यम् महोदरी
translation:
She that demoness who is facially unpleasant one with that pleasant faced one, pot bellied one with 
the slim-waisted one, wry-eyed one with the broad-eyed one, coppery-haired one with the neatly tressed 
one, ugly featured one with the charming featured one, brassy voiced one with the gentle voiced one, 
deplorably oldish one with the youngish one, crooked talker with the pleasant talker, ill-mannered one 
with the well-mannered one, uncouth one with couth, abominable one with amiable Rama spoke, besieged 
by Love-god. [3-17-9b, 11, 12a]

shloka: जटी तापस रूपेण सभार्यः शर चाप धृक्
translation:
"You are an ascetic yet with a wife, handling bow and arrows yet in the appearance of a sage  what for 
you have come to this province frequented by demons  it will be apt of you to tell the purpose of your 
coming here, in actuality " [3-17-12b, 13]

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु राक्षस्या शूर्पणख्या परंतपः |
ऋजु बुद्धितया सर्वम् आख्यातुम् उपचक्रमे
translation: Thus asked by demoness Shuurpanakha that enemy-scorcher Rama started to inform all about it, straightforwardly.

shloka:
आसीत् दशरथो नाम राजा त्रिदश विक्रमः |
तस्य अहम् अग्रजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
translation:
"A king named Dasharatha was there with his godlike valour, I am his eldest son, and people hear of 
me by name Rama.

shloka:
भ्राता अयम् लक्ष्मणो नाम यवीयान् माम् अनुव्रतः |
इयम् भार्या च वैदेही मम सीतेति विश्रुता
translation:
"He is Lakshmana by his name, my younger brother and a devoted follower of mine, and she is my wife, 
daughter of Videha's king, well-known as Seetha.

shloka:
नियोगात् तु नरेन्द्रस्य पितुर् मातुः च यंत्रितः |
धर्मार्थम् धर्मकांक्षी च वनम् वस्तुम् इह आगतः
translation:
"Desiring to implement the probity in following father's orders and for the sake of establishing probity 
in living an ascetic's life I have come here to forests to dwell, as enjoined by the directives of the 
king and my father, and by my mother, as well.

shloka:
त्वाम् तु वेदितुम् इच्छ्हामि कस्य त्वम् का असि कस्य वा |
त्वम् हि तावन्मनोज्ञा.ंगी राक्षसी प्रतिभासि 
मे
translation:
"I too wish to know about you. Whose wife are you? What is your name? Or, whose daughter are you? By 
the way, you are with a most enthralling personality, and then you must be a demoness.

shloka:
इह वा किम् निमित्तम् त्वम् आगता ब्रूहि तत्त्वतः |
सा अब्रवीत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राक्षसी मदन अर्दिता
translation:
"What for you have come, either, you tell in actuality..." Thus Rama asked her. On hearing the words 
of Rama she that demoness wetted with love said these words.

shloka:
श्रूयताम् राम वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वार्थम् वचनम् मम |
अहम् शूर्पणखा नाम राक्षसी कामरूपिणी
translation:
"I will tell you truth, Rama, nothing but truth, I am a guise-changing demoness named Shuurpanakha, 
and I will be freely moving in this forest in a solitary manner and unnerving all. [3-17-20, 21a]

shloka: रावणो नाम मे भ्राता यदि ते श्रोत्रम् आगतः
translation:
"My brother is valorous and mighty Ravana, the king of demons and the son of Vishravasa, if ever you 
have heard of him. [3-17-21b, 22a]

shloka: प्रवृद्ध निद्रः च सदा कुंभकर्णो महाबलः
translation:
"And the mighty Kumbhakarna who will always be in profound sleep is my brother, and the virtue-souled 
Vibheeshana too is my brother, but he does not behave like a demon, and two more bothers of mine are 
Khara and Duushana who are renowned for their bravery in war. [3-17-22b, 23

shloka:
तान् अहम् समतिक्रान्ता राम त्वा पूर्व दर्शनात् |
समुपेता अस्मि भावेन भर्तारम् पुरुषोत्तमम्
translation:
"I can excel all of them by my bravery, oh, Rama, and on seeing you for the first time I had a notion 
that you being the choicest among men you alone are my husband, hence I neared you.

shloka:
अहम् प्रभाव संपन्ना स्वच्छ्हंद बल गामिनी |
चिराय भव भर्ता मे सीतया किम् करिष्यसि
translation:
"I am endowed with such preponderances and I can operate with my independent might, as such you become 
my everlasting husband  by the way, what can you bring off with Seetha.

shloka:
विकृता च विरूपा च न सा इयम् सदृशी तव |
अहम् एव अनुरूपा ते भार्या रूपेण पश्य माम्
translation:
"Unlovely and unshapely is this one, such as she is, this Seetha is unworthy to be your wife, and I 
am the lone one worthy to be your wife, hence treat me as your wife.

shloka:
इमाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् करालाम् निर्णत उदरीम् |
अनेन सह ते भ्रात्रा भक्षयिष्यामि मानुषीम्
translation:
"Shall I eat up this disfigured, dishonest, diabolical human female with a hallow stomach along with 
him, that brother of yours to make you free.

shloka:
ततः पर्वत शृ.ंगाणि वनानि विविधानि च |
पश्यन्सहमयाकामीदण्डकान्विचरिष्यसि - यद्वा -
पश्यन् सह मया 
कामी दण्डकान् विचरिष्यसि
translation:
"Afterwards, you can lustily ramble about Dandaka forest along with me while enjoying yourself on various 
mountaintops in the sky and in forests on the earth." So Shuurpanakha said to Rama.

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्तः काकुत्स्थः प्रहस्य मदिर ईक्षणाम् |
इदम् वचनम् आरेभे वक्तुम् वाक्य विशारदः
translation:
When he is said that way Rama chuckled and that wordsmith started to reply her who eyes are besotted 
in lovesickness with this sentence.

shloka:
ताम् तु शूर्पणखाम् रामः काम पाश अवपाशिताम् |
स्वच्छ्हया श्लक्ष्णया वाचा स्मित पूर्वम् अथ अब्रवीत्
translation:
Rama then voicing clearly and softly spoke to her, whom the noose of lust has tethered down, with a 
smile preceding his words.

shloka:
कृत दारो अस्मि भवति भार्या इयम् दयिता मम |
त्वत् विधानाम् तु नारीणाम् सुदुःखा ससपत्नता
translation:
"Oh, honourable one, I am married and this is my dear wife, thus it will be distressing for your sort 
of females to live with a co-wife.

shloka:
अनुजः तु एष मे भ्राता शीलवान् प्रिय दर्शनः |
श्रीमान् अकृत दारः च लक्ष्मणो नाम वीर्यवान्
translation:
"He is my younger brother named Lakshmana, he is with a good conduct, good looking, a promising and 
valiant one, and he is without a wife.

shloka:
अपूर्वी भार्यया च अर्थी तरुणः प्रिय दर्शनः |
अनुरूपः च ते भर्ता रूपस्य अस्य भविष्यति
translation:
"He is without a wife and in need of a wife  he is youthful, good-looking and he can become a fitly 
husband of yours, fit enough to your kind of features.

shloka:
एनम् भज विशालाक्षि भर्तारम् भ्रातरम् मम |
असपत्ना वरारोहे मेरुम् अर्क प्रभा यथा
translation:
"You woo him, oh, board-eyed [bulged-eyed] one, this brother of mine as your husband like sunshine seeking 
the Mt. Meru, then oh, great-waisted [pot-bellied] one, you will be without a co-wife " So said Rama 
to that demoness.

shloka:
इति रामेण सा प्रोक्ता राक्षसी काम मोहिता |
विसृज्य रामम् सहसा ततो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
When Rama clearly told that way to that demoness dazed in lust, discarding Rama quickly then she spoke 
to Lakshmana.

shloka:
अस्य रूपस्य ते युक्ता भार्या अहम् वरवर्णिनी |
मया सह सुखम् सर्वान् दण्डकान् विचरिष्यसि
translation:
"I with my best complexion will be your deserving wife meetly to you charm, you can happily take a jaunt 
all over Dandaka forest along with me." So Shuurpanakha ran after Lakshmana.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सौमित्री राक्षस्या वाक्य कोविदः |
ततः शूर्पणखीम् स्मित्वा लक्ष्मणो युक्तम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Thus said by the demoness that meaningful sentence maker Lakshmana, the son of Sumitra, then smiled 
and appropriately replied Shuurpanakha.

shloka:
कथम् दासस्य मे दासी भार्या भवितुम् इच्छ्हसि |
सो अहम् आर्येण परवान् भ्रात्रा कमल वर्णिनी
translation:
"How you wish to become a female servant, oh, [black] lotus-coloured one, by becoming the wife of a 
servant like me? I am just a vassal of my adorable brother.

shloka:
समृद्ध अर्थस्य सिद्धार्था मुदित अमल वर्णिनी |
आर्यस्य त्वम् विशालाक्षि भार्या भव यवीयसी || ३-१८--१०
translation:
"Oh, goggle eyed one, befitting to your complexion that is un-stainable further you better become the 
wife of my brother Rama who is abounding in means, and on becoming the younger wife of that adorable 
one, you too will achieve your means and thus you will be happy.

shloka:
एनाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् करालाम् निर्णत उदरीम् |
भार्याम् वृद्धाम् परित्यज्य त्वाम् एव एष भजिष्यति
translation:
"On discarding her who is disfigured, dishonest, diabolically deleterious old wife with a hallow stomach 
that Rama will adore you alone.

shloka:
को हि रूपम् इदम् श्रेष्ठम् संत्यज्य वरवर्णिनि |
मानुषेषु वरारोहे कुर्यात् भावम् विचक्षणः
translation:
"Oh, best complexioned one with best waist, is there any wiseacre to simply discard your kind of best 
personality, indeed, in preference to human females?" Lakshmana said so to Shuurpanakha.

shloka:
इति सा लक्ष्मणेन उक्ता कराला निर्णतोदरी |
मन्यते तत् वचः सत्यम् परिहास अविचक्षणा
translation:
Thus said by Lakshmana that despicable one with slouching stomach Shuurpanakha presumed those words 
to be truthful, for she is equivocal of that equivoque.

shloka:
सा रामम् पर्णशालायाम् उपविष्टम् परंतपम् |
सीतया सह दुर्धर्षम् अब्रवीत् काम मोहिता
translation:
She who is fuddle by lust said to that unassailable enemy scorcher Rama who is sitting in the cottage 
along with Seetha.

shloka:
इमाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् करालाम् निर्णतोदरीम् |
वृद्धाम् भार्याम् अवष्टभ्य न माम् त्वम् बहु मन्यसे
translation:
"Tenacious of her who is disfigured, dishonest, diabolical, hallow-stomached old wife of yours you are 
not regarding me high.

shloka:
अद्य इमाम् भक्षयिष्यामि पश्यतः तव मानुषीम् |
त्वया सह चरिष्यामि निःसपत्ना यथा सुखम्
translation:
"Now I wish to eat up this human female right before your very eyes, and then I can blithely make merry 
along with you, without the botheration of a co-wife." Said Shuurpanakha to Rama.

shloka:
इति उक्त्वा मृगशावाक्षीम् अलात सदृश ईक्षणा |
अभ्यधावत् सुसंक्रुद्धा महा उल्का रोहिणीम् इव
translation:
Speaking that way she that torch-eyed Shuurpanakha dashed towards the deer-eyed Seetha in high exasperation 
as a great meteor would dash towards Rohini, the brightest star in the sky.

shloka:
ताम् मृत्यु पाश प्रतिमाम् आपतंतीम् महाबलः |
विगृह्य रामः कुपितः ततो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
By that the great-energetic Rama took umbrage and checking her who is like the noose of death swooping 
down on Seetha said to Lakshmana.

shloka:
क्रूरैः अनार्यैः सौमित्रे परिहासः कथंचन |
न कार्यः पश्य वैदेहीम् कथंचित् सौम्य जीवतीम्
translation:
"Punning in any way with the base and brutish is inapposite, oh, gentle Saumitri, mark note of Vaidehi, 
somehow surviving

shloka:
इमाम् विरूपाम् असतीम् अतिमत्ताम् महोदरीम् |
राक्षसीम् पुरुषव्याघ्र विरूपयितुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"She is freakish, knavish and overtly ruttish, oh, tigerly man, it will be apt of you to deface this 
paunchy demoness " Thus Rama said to Lakshmana.

shloka:
इति उक्तो लक्ष्मणः तस्याः क्रुद्धो रामस्य पश्यतः |
उद्धृत्य खड्गम् चिच्छ्हेद कर्ण नासम् महाबलः
translation:
Thus said to that mighty Lakshmana he infuriately drew sword and chopped off her ears and nose before 
the very eyes of Rama.

shloka:
निकृत्त कर्ण नासा तु विस्वरम् सा विनद्य च |
यथा आगतम् प्रदुद्राव घोरा शूर्पणखा वनम्
translation:
On hewing off her ears and nose she that ghastly Shuurpanakha blared highly and discordantly, and very 
speedily fled into forest as she came.

shloka:
सा विरूपा महाघोरा राक्षसी शोणित उक्षिता |
ननाद विविधान् नादान् यथा प्रावृषि तोयदः
translation:
She that very ghastly demoness when defaced is wetted by blood and blared many a blare like a cloud 
in cloudburst.

shloka:
सा विक्षरंती रुधिरम् बहुधा घोर दर्शना |
प्रगृह्य बाहू गर्जन्ती प्रविवेश महावनम्
translation:
She that gruesome one in her appearance clasped herself and thunderously entered similarly gruesome 
forest while her blood fountained and profusely exuded.

shloka:
ततः तु सा राक्षस संघ सम्वृतम्
खरम् जन स्थान गतम् विरूपिता |
उपेत्य तम् भ्रातरम् उग्र तेजसम्
पपात भूमौ गगनाद् यथा अशनिः
translation:
Then she who is deformed neared her brother Khara who possess violent vigour, who is abiding in Janasthaana 
and who is presently surrounded by his band of his hench-demons, and before him she that Shuurpanakha 
fell onto ground like a thunderbolt from the sky.

shloka:
ततः सभार्यम् भय मोह मूर्चिता
सलक्ष्मणम् राघवम् आगतम् वनम् |
विरूपणम् च आत्मनि शोणित उक्षिता
शशंस सर्वम् भगिनी खरस्य सा
translation:
Then that sister of Khara who is convulsed in the fluster of fear and her body wetted with blood reported 
to her brother Khara, all about Rama's arrival in forest with his wife and Lakshmana, and even about 
his misshaping her.

shloka:
ताम् तथा पतिताम् दृष्ट्वा विरूपाम् शोणित उक्षिताम् |
भगिनीम् क्रोध संतप्तः खरः पप्रच्छ्ह राक्षसः
translation:
On seeing her who fell before him in a misshapen and blood-soaked condition, demon Khara is all stewed 
up and asked her.

shloka:
उत्तिष्ठ तावत् आख्याहि प्रमोहम् जहि संभ्रमम् |
व्यक्तम् आख्याहि केन त्वम् एवम् रूपा विरूपिता
translation:
"Rise up, first tell me clearly putting away your flurry and fluster, who disfigured your form in this 
way.

shloka:
कः कृष्ण सर्पम् असीनम् आशी विषम नागसम् |
तुदति अभिसमापन्नम् अ.ंगुलि अग्रेण लीलया
translation:
"Who for sport is poking his fingertip at a venomously fanged black-cobra that has chanced in his close 
proximity but slouching down inoffensively.

shloka:
काल पाशम् समासज्य कण्ठे मोहात् न जानते |
यः त्वाम् अद्य समासाद्य पीतवान् विषम् उत्तमम्
translation:
"Who on harrowing you is now heedless about his gulping a deadly poison, or about his foolish bracing 
the noose of Time around his own neck.

shloka:
बल विक्रम संपन्ना कामगा काम रूपिणी |
इमाम् अवस्थाम् नीता त्वम् केन अंतक समा गता
translation:
"You are gifted with boldness and braveness, a whimsical rover, a guise changer by your wish, a coequal 
of Terminator, but to whom you have gone and by whom you are led into this kind of plight.

shloka:
देव गन्धर्व भूतानाम् ऋषीणाम् च महात्मनाम् |
को अयम् एवम् महावीर्यः त्वाम् विरूपाम् चकार ह
translation:
"Who is that kind of highly intrepid warper, either from gods, or from celestials or from high-souled 
sages who indeed rendered you shapeless.

shloka:
न हि पश्यामि अहम् लोके यः कुर्यात् मम विप्रियम् |
अमरेषु सहस्राक्षम् महएन्द्रम् पाकशासनम्
translation:
"Indeed, I do not find anyone who causes displeasure to me in this world, even among divinities including 
the thousand eyed Indra, the controller of demon Paaka.

shloka:
अद्य अहम् मार्गणैः प्राणान् आदास्ये जीवितांतगैः |
सलिले क्षीरम् आसक्तम् निष्पिबन् इव सारसः
translation:
"Now, I will take away the lives of that miscreant with my arrows that are terminators of lives, as 
a swan would drink milk to dregs even if it is mingled in water, duly separating milk from water.

shloka:
निहतस्य मया संख्ये शर संकृत्त मर्मणः |
सफेनम् रुधिरम् कस्य मेदिनी पातुम् इच्छ्हसि
translation:
"Whose frothy blood is it that the earth wishes to quaff when I cut off his crucial organs by my arrows 
and drop him dead in a combat.

shloka:
कस्य पत्ररथाः कायात् मांसम् उत्कृत्य संगताः |
प्रहृष्टा भक्षयिष्यन्ति निहतस्य मया रणे
translation:
"Whose body is it from which birds pressing round gladly wish to wring flesh to pieces for eating when 
I slay him in war.

shloka:
तम् न देवा न गंधर्वा न पिशाचा न राक्षसाः |
मया अपकृष्टम् कृपणम् शक्ताः त्रातुम् इह आहवे
translation:
"Now, when I haul him easily on the ground in a battle that villain will be unredeemable either by gods, 
celestials, evil spirits, or by demons.

shloka:
उपलभ्य शनैः संज्ञाम् तम् मे शंसितुम् अर्हसि |
येन त्वम् दुर्विनीतेन वने विक्रम्य निर्जिता
translation:
"It will be apt of you to gather your sensitivity slowly and tell me as to which miscreant attacked 
and worsted you in the forest." Thus Khara spoke to Shuurpanakha.

shloka:
इति भ्रातुर् वचः श्रुत्वा क्रुद्धस्य च विशेषतः |
ततः शूर्पणखा वाक्यम् सबाष्पम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
On hearing this kind of words of her brother, especially who is rancorous, then Shuurpanakha spoke these 
words, tearfully.

shloka:
तरुणौ रूप संपन्नौ सुकूमारौ महाबलौ |
पुण्डरीक विशालाक्षौ चीर कृष्ण अजिन अंबरौ
translation:
"Those two are in adulthood, good-looking, gentle yet greatly mighty, eyes broad like lotuses, dressed 
in jute-cloths and deerskin, subsistent on fruits and tubers, composed, sagacious and celibate, and 
they are the sons of Dasharatha, namely Rama and Lakshmana. [3-19-14,15]

shloka:
गन्धर्व राज प्रतिमौ पार्थिव 
व्यन्जन अन्वितौ |
देवौ वा दानवौ - मानुषौ - वा तौ न तर्कयितुम् उत्सहे
translation:
"Having all the aspects 
of kings they equal the kings of gandharva celestials, and I am ill-disposed to differentiate whether 
they two are gods or demons.

shloka:
तरुणी रूपसंपन्ना सर्वाअभरण 
भूषिता |
दृष्टा तत्र मया नारी तयोर् मध्ये सुमध्यमा
translation:
" I have seen a curvaceous 
lady between those two, a ripely beauty, rich in comeliness, adorned with lots of ornaments.

shloka:
ताभ्याम् उभाभ्याम् संभूय 
प्रमदाम् अधिकृत्य ताम् |
इमाम् अवस्थाम् नीता अहम् यथा अनाथा सती तथा
translation:
"Owing to that woman I am 
led into this sort of situation, together by those two, as with an insecure female.

shloka:
तस्याः च अनृजु वृत्तायाः 
तयोः च हतयोर् अहम् |
सफेनम् पातुम् इच्छ्हामि रुधिरम् रण मूर्धनि
translation:
"Staying in the van of war 
I wish to drink the frothy blood of that guileful Seetha along with that of those two, Rama and Lakshmana, 
when they are killed in war.

shloka:
एष मे प्रथमः कामः कृतः तत्र 
त्वया भवेत् |
तस्याः तयोः च रुधिरम् पिबेयम् अहम् आहवे
translation:
"I shall drink her blood 
and also that of those two in war, this being my prime longing let it be fulfilled by you." Thus wailed 
Shuurpanakha before her brother Khara.

shloka:
इति तस्याम् ब्रुवाणायाम् 
चतुर् दश महाबलान् |
व्यादिदेश खरः क्रुद्धो राक्षसान् अंतकोपमान्
translation:
While she is saying like 
that Khara vengefully summoned fourteen great mighty demons that are similar to the Terminator.

shloka:
मानुषौ शस्त्र संपन्नौ चीर 
कृष्ण अजिन अंबरौ |
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यम् घोरम् प्रमदया सह
translation:
"Wielding weapons and wearing 
jute-cloths and deerskin two humans have got into ghastly forest of Dandaka along with a woman of age." 
Thus Khara is ordering the fourteen demons.

shloka:
तौ हत्वा ताम् च दुर्वृत्ताम् 
उपावर्तितुम् अर्हथ |
इयम् च रुधिरम् तेषाम् भगिनी मम पास्यति
translation:
"You shall return to me only on killing those two and also that 
treacherous woman, and their blood this sister of mine will drink.

shloka:
मनोरथो अयम् इष्टो अस्या भगिन्या मम राक्षसाः |
शीघ्रम् संपद्यताम् 
गत्वा तौ प्रमथ्य स्व तेजसा
translation:
"Oh, demons, on going there swiftly stamp them out by you own 
vigour, thus let the fanciful hearty desire of my sister be achieved.

shloka:
युष्माबिः निर्हतो दृष्ट्वा तौ उभौ भ्रातौ रणे |
इयम् प्रहृष्टा 
मुदिता रुधिरम् युधि पास्यति
translation:
"On seeing your finishing those two brothers flatly in a war she 
this sister of mine will be gladdened, and then she drinks their blood in war, amusingly.

shloka:
इति प्रतिसमादिष्टा राक्षसाः ते चतुर् दश |
तत्र जग्मुः तया सार्धम् 
घना वातेरिताः यथा
translation:
In this way when Khara ordered those fourteen demons, they have 
gone to Panchavati along with Shuurpanakha like black-clouds glided by gales.

shloka:
ततस्तु ते तम् समुदर्ग तेजसम्
तथापि तीक्ष्ण प्रदरा निशाचरा |
न शेकुर् एनम् सहसा प्रमर्दितुम्
वनद्विपा दीप्त्वम् इव अग्निम् उथितम्
translation:
But then, though the nightwalker wielding sharp arrows have become 
ineffectual to trounce Rama like the wild elephants which will become ineffectual to overcome the blazingly 
uprising wildfire.

shloka:
ततः शूर्पणखा घोरा राघव आश्रमम् आगता |
रक्षसान् आचचक्षे तौ भ्रातरौ सह सीतया
translation:
Then on arriving at Raghava's hermitage that ghastly Shuurpanakha has shown the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, 
along with Seetha to the fourteen demons.

shloka:
ते रामम् पर्ण शालायाम् उपविष्टम् महाबलम् |
ददृशुः सीतया सार्धम् लक्ष्मणेन अपि सेवितम्
translation:
They have seen the great-mighty Rama seated in the thatched cottage along with Seetha and Lakshmana 
attending to him.

shloka:
ताम् दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमान् आगताम् ताम् च राक्षसीम् |
अब्रवीत् भ्रातरम् रामो लक्ष्मणम् दीप्त तेजसम्
translation:
On seeing the arrival of the demons, and the demoness Shuurpanakha too, that magnificent Rama of Raghava 
dynasty said to the radiantly brilliant Lakshmana.

shloka:
मुहूर्तम् भव सौमित्रे सीतायाः प्रत्यनंतरः |
इमान् अस्या वधिष्यामि पदवीम् आगतान् इह
translation:
"Oh, Soumitri, briefly tarry at the close of Seetha as I wish to eliminate these demons who have trailed 
the path of that demoness to here.

shloka:
वाक्यम् एतत् ततः श्रुत्वा रामस्य विदित आत्मनः |
तथा इति लक्ष्मणो वाक्यम् रामस्य प्रत्यपूजयत्
translation:
On hearing that word of Rama, then the nimble-souled Lakshmana honoured the word of Rama saying "so 
be it."

shloka:
राघवो अपि महत् चापम् चामीकर विभूषितम् |
चकार सज्यम् धर्मात्मा तानि रक्षांसि च अब्रवीत्
translation:
On taking up his awful bow that is decorated with gold Raghava stringed it with bowstring and even spoke 
the demons as a forewarning.

shloka:
पुत्रौ दशरथस्य आवाम् भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |
प्रविष्टौ सीतया सार्धम् दुश्चरम् दण्डका वनम्
translation:
"We the sons of Dasharatha are brothers named Rama and Lakshmana, and we entered the impenetrable forests 
Dandaka along with Seetha.

shloka:
फल मूल अशनौ दांतौ तापसौ धर्म चारिणौ |
वसन्तौ दण्डकारण्ये किम् अर्थम् उपहिंसथ
translation:
"We the dispassionate subsist on fruits and tubers treading in the path of virtue, and we being the 
sages resident in Dandaka forest what for you outrage us.

shloka:
युष्मान् पाप आत्मकान् हंतुम् विप्रकारान् महाहवे |
ऋषीणाम् तु नियोगेन प्राप्तो अहम् सशर आसनः
translation:
"As assigned by the sages I chanced here with bow and arrows to decimate you evil-souled and unrighteous 
beings in a crucial clash.

shloka:
तिष्ठत एव अत्र संतुष्टा न उपवरितितुम् अर्हथ |
यदि प्राणैः इह अर्थो वो निवर्तध्वम् निशा चराः
translation:
"Stay there obligingly or you should not be able to return, else if you desire your lives, oh, nightwalkers, 
you may return now.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राक्षसाः ते चतुर्दश |
ऊचुर् वाचम् सुसंक्रुद्धा ब्रह्मघ्नः शूल पाणयः
translation:
On hearing that sentence of Rama they the fourteen ghoulish demons who are the slayers of Brahmans and 
handlers of spears have become highly infuriated, and they with their bloodshot eyes and with harsh 
words said these words to Rama, whose eyes are with blood streaks at their ends, and who also is a sweet 
talker, and whose valour is yet unseen by those fourteen demons. [3-20-11, 12]

shloka:
क्रोधम् उत्पाद्य नो भर्तुः खरस्य सुमहात्मनः |
त्वम् एव हास्यसे प्राणान् अद्य अस्माभिर् हतो युधि
translation:
"Killed in conflict by us you alone will set your lives loose as an inciter of fury in our highly great 
souled lord Khara.

shloka:
का हि ते शक्तिर् एकस्य बहूनाम् रण मूर्धनि |
अस्माकम् अग्रतः स्थातुम् किम् पुनर् योद्धुम् आहवे
translation:
"Indeed, what capability you have as a lone one to stand against many of us in the forefront of war, 
and why tell again about your battling ability in a given battle.

shloka:
एभिः बाहु प्रयुक्तैः नः परिघैः शूल पट्टिशैः |
प्राणाम् त्यक्ष्यसि वीर्यम् च धनुः च कर पीडितम्
translation:
"When we launch maces, spears and swords by our might you will forgo your lives, mettle, and even the 
bow now clasped in your hand." So said the demons to Rama.

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्त्वा संरब्धा राक्षसाः ते चतुर्दश |
उद्यत आयुध निस्त्रिंशा रामम् एव अभिदुद्रुवुः
translation:
Thus saying that way clamorously they the fourteen demons, upraising their weapons they unhesitatingly 
rushed towards Rama alone, and they hurled lances towards that unconquerable Raghava. [3-20-16, 17a]

shloka: तानि शूलानि काकुत्स्थः समस्तानि चतुर्दश
translation:
Rama in turn shredded all of those fourteen lances only with as many arrows that are adorned in gold. 
[3-20-17b, 18a]

shloka: ततः पश्चात् महातेजा नाराचान् सूर्य संनिभान्
translation:
Next that great resplendent Rama in high wrath took up fourteen iron bolt like arrows that are whetted 
on whetstone and equalling the sun in their dazzle. [3-20-18b, 19a]

shloka: गृहीत्वा धनुः आयम्य लक्ष्यान् उद्दिश्य राक्षसान्
translation:
Then Raghava took up his bow, arched it, and aiming at the targeted demons released arrows as Indra 
would release his Thunderbolts. [3-20-19b, 20a]

shloka: ते भित्त्वा रक्षसाम् वेगात् वक्षांसि रुधिर आप्लुताः
translation:
And by the force of their speed those arrows gored the chests of those demons, and then on coming out 
bedaubed with blood they swiftly penetrated into earth like snakes into snake pit. [3-20-20b, 21a]

shloka: तैः भग्न हृदया बूमौ छ्हिन्न मूला इव द्रुमाः
translation:
Those arrows bursting their hearts they are blood bathed, mangled, and utterly dead, and like the uprooted 
trees they fell onto the ground. [3-20-21b, 22a]

shloka: तान् भूमौ पतितान् दृष्ट्वा राक्षसी क्रोध मूर्च्छ्हिता
translation:
On seeing the demons falling onto ground that demoness Shuurpanakha is convulsed in rage, and she with 
a blanched aspect returned to the near of Khara in an agonising manner like a creeper exuding resin 
on incision, and fell before him as before. [3-20-22b, 23]

shloka:
भ्रातुः समीपे शोक आर्ता ससर्ज निनदम् महत् |
सस्वरम् मुमोच बाष्पम् विवर्ण वदना तदा
translation:
Then she in the presence of her brother Khara discharged a great outcry, and with a bloodless face she 
spilled tears attuning the strains of a whiner.

shloka:
निपातितान् प्रेक्ष्य रणे तु राक्षसान्
प्रधाविता शूर्पणखा पुनः ततः |
वधम् च तेषाम् निखिलेन रक्षसाम्
शशंस सर्वम् भगिनी खरस्य सा
translation:
Shuurpanakha having seen the fall of demons quickly fled from Panchavati of Rama to trikanTaka, the 
capital of Khara, and she being the sister of Khara she reported to Khara all about the destruction 
of those demons, in its entirety.

shloka:
स पुनः पतिताम् दृष्ट्वा क्रोधात् शूर्पणखाम् खरः |
उवाच व्यक्तता वाचा ताम् अनर्थ अर्थम् आगताम्
translation:
On seeing Shuurpanakha who came back only to wreck havoc on demonic race and again fell before him as 
before, Khara spoke this sentence to her in clear terms in all his fury.

shloka:
मया तु इदानीम् शूराः ते राक्षसा पिशित अशनाः |
त्वत् प्रियार्थम् विनिर्दिष्टाः किम् अर्थम् रुद्यते 
पुनः
translation:
"What for your are howling again when I have just now commanded those fearless flesh eating demons in 
order to fulfill your wish?

shloka:
भक्ताः चैव अनुरक्ताः च हिताः च मम नित्यशः |
हन्यमाना अपि न हन्यन्ते न न कुर्युः वचो मम
translation:
"Those demons are my admirers, adherers and they always remained my well-wishers, hence there is no 
question of their non-accomplishment of my orders.

shloka:
किम् एतत् श्रोतुम् इच्छ्हामि कारणम् यत् कृते पुनः |
हा नाथ इति विनर्दन्ती सर्पवत् चेष्टसे क्षितौ
translation:
"Owing to what you are highly bawling by saying, 'haa, lord' and wriggle on the ground like a snake? 
I would like to know the reason for all this, what is it?

shloka:
अनाथ वत् विलपसि किम् नु नाथे मयि स्थिते |
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ मा मैवम् वैक्लव्यम् त्यज्यताम् इति
translation:
"I am here to take care of you, then why should you really cry out like an uncared-for being, get up...get 
up, and ward off this sort of perplexity." Thus Khara said to Shuurpanakha.

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्ता दुर्धर्षा खरेण परिसान्त्विता |
विमृज्य नयने स अस्रे खरम् भ्रातरम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
She that Shuurpanakha who is otherwise an unassuageable one is wholly pacified when Khara spoke to her 
thus that way, and she on dabbing her tearful eyes then spoke to her brother Khara.

shloka:
अस्मि इदानीम् अहम् प्रप्ता हत श्रवण नासिका |
शोणित ओघ परिक्लिन्ना त्वया च परिसमन्विता
translation:
"I came to you just a while back with my ears and nose chopped off and wet with gushes of blood, and 
you too have comforted me, isn't it.

shloka:
प्रेषिताः च त्वया शूरा राक्षसाः ते चतुर् दश |
निहन्तुम् राघवम् घोराम् मत् प्रियार्थम् स लक्ष्मणम्
translation:
"Oh, valiant brother, for my delight you too have sent fourteen demons to eliminate that atrocious Rama 
along with Lakshmana, isn't it?

shloka:
ते तु रामेण सामर्षाः शूल पट्टिस पाणयः |
समरे निहताः सर्वे सायकैः मर्म भेदिभिः
translation:
"But they all who handled their spears and bolts along with an envious anger are killed in a fight with 
Rama by his arrows that cleave the crucial parts of his opponents.

shloka:
तान् भूमौ पतितान् दृष्ट्वा क्षणेन एव महाजवान् |
रामस्य च महत् कर्म महान् त्रासो अभवन् मम
translation:
"On seeing those highly impetuous demons falling to earth in a trice, and even on seeing the unusual 
deed of Rama in felling them, I am highly alarmed.

shloka:
सा अस्मि भीता समुद्विग्ना विषण्णा च निशाचर |
शरणम् त्वाम् पुनः प्राप्ता सर्वतो भय दर्शिनी
translation:
"Oh me! I am alarmed, fully frenzied, and even despaired, oh, nightwalker Khara, and beholding dread 
everywhere again I have come seeking your refuge.

shloka:
विषाद नक्र अध्युषिते परित्रास ऊर्मि मालिनि |
किम् माम् न त्रायसे मग्नाम् विपुले शोक सागरे
translation:
"Why do not you rescue me when I am drowned in a vast ocean called grief, wherein each pervasive crocodile 
is despair and each swelling wave is fright.

shloka:
एते च निहता भूमौ रामेण निशितैः शरैः |
ये च मे पदवीम् प्राप्ता राक्षसाः पिशित अशनाः
translation:
"Besides, those flesh-eating demons that have followed me are also felled by Rama with his sharp arrows, 
for whom I have a contrite heart.

shloka:
मयि ते यदि अनुक्रोशो यदि रक्षःसु तेषु च |
रामेण यदि शक्तिः ते तेजो वा अस्ति निशा चर
translation:
"If you have mercy on me, and even on those dead demons, and if ability and animation are still left 
in you to cope with Rama, oh, nightwalker, kill that Rama who is a thorn in the side of demons dwelling 
in Dandaka forest. [3-21-14, 15a]

shloka: यदि रामम् अमित्रघ्नम् न त्वम् अद्य वधिष्यसि
translation:
"If you are not going to kill that enemy destroyer Rama now itself, I will give up my life unhesitatingly, 
that too in your fore, that too now itself.

shloka: बुद्ध्या अहम् अनुपश्यामि न त्वम् रामस्य संयुगे
translation:
"I can perceive instinctually that you are incapable of affronting Rama in a given crucial battle, even 
if your are with all your forces on the battlefield, and you assert yourself a valiant, but you are 
just vainglorious. [3-21-16b, 17]

shloka:
अपयाहि जन स्थानात् त्वरितः सह बान्धवः |
जहि त्वम् समरे मूढान् यथा तु कुलपांसन
translation:
"Kill those two, Rama and Lakshmana, as they are just humans, or else, if you are incapable of doing 
so, really what for is your stay here in Janasthaana with your trivial stamina and trifling sinews like 
a stupid blemishing his clan, then get out of this Janasthaana at once along with your hench-demons. 
[3-21-18, 19]

shloka:
राम तेजो अभिभूतो हि त्वम् क्षिप्रम् विनशिष्यसि |
स हि तेजः समायुक्तो रामो दशरथात्मजः
translation:
"You will completely and quickly evanish, indeed, subjugated by resplendence of Rama, for that Dasharatha's 
son Rama possess that kind of resplendence, in effect.

shloka:
भ्राता च अस्य महा वीर्यो येन च अस्मि विरूपिता |
एवम् विलाप्य बहुशो राक्ष्सी प्रदरोदरी
translation:
"And, by whom I am misshapen that brother of Rama too is a highly vigorous one..." in this way on saying 
Shuurpanakha bawled variously in the presence of her brother, Khara, and then anguished by her own affliction 
that demoness with a cave like belly started hitting her paunch with both of her hands, and what is 
more, she swooned. [3-21-21, 22]

shloka:
एवम् आधर्षितः शूरः शूर्पणख्या खरः ततः |
उवाच रक्षसाम् मध्ये खरः खरतरम् वचः
translation:
Thus when Shuurpanakha disparaged that valiant Khara amidst demons he is infuriated and spoke these 
highly hurtful words.

shloka:
तव अपमान प्रभवः क्रोधो अयम् अतुलो मम |
न शक्यते धारयितुम् लवण अंभ इव उल्बणम्
translation:
"This fury of mine originating from the disgrace brought on you is like the highly bitter salt water 
that is impossible to contain when ingested.

shloka:
न रामम् गणये वीर्यान् मानुषम् क्षीण जीवितम् |
आत्म दुश्चरितैः प्राणान् हतो यो अद्य विमोक्ष्यति
translation:
"I do not care the valour of that Rama for he is a human with dwindled lifetime, now going to give up 
his life slain by his own misdoings.

shloka:
बाष्पः संधार्यताम् एष संभ्रमः च विमुच्यताम् |
अहम् रामम् सह भ्रात्रा नयामि यम सादनम्
translation:
"Control your tears and cast off your despair too, for I will send Rama to the abode of the Terminator 
along with his brother.

shloka:
परश्वध हतस्य अद्य मन्द प्राणस्य भू तले |
रामस्य रुधिरम् रक्तम् उष्णम् पास्यसि राक्षसि
translation:
"Now, you demoness, you will swill that Rama's red hot blood when that short-lived one is hewed down 
to earth with an axe." So Khara assured Shuurpanakha.

shloka:
सा प्रहृष्ट्वा वचः श्रुत्वा खरस्य वदनात् च्युतम् |
प्रशशंस पुनर् मौर्ख्यात् भ्रातरम् रक्षसाम् वरम्
translation:
On hearing the words plunged from the mouth of Khara she is very much gladdened and in all her stupidity 
she further praised her brother highly saying, "you are the best among all the demons..."

shloka:
तया परुषितः पूर्वम् पुनर् एव प्रशंसितः |
अब्रवीत् दूषणम् नाम खरः सेना पतिम् तदा
translation:
Though she denounced him earlier she alone praised him now for which Khara is overjoyed, and then he 
ordered his army commander, namely Duushana.

shloka:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि मम चित्त अनुवर्तिनाम् |
रक्षसाम् भीम वेगानाम् समरेषु अनिवर्तिनाम्
translation:
"Those who are the followers of my will, whose hustle will be frightful and who will be unretreating 
in combats, such of those demons are there in fourteen thousand numbers, aren't they.

shloka:
नील जीमूत वर्णानाम् लोक हिंसा विहाराणाम् |
सर्व उद्योगम् उदीर्णानाम् रक्षसाम् सौम्य कारय
translation:
"And oh, gentle Duushana, those domineering demons are with dark-clouds like complexions, and they are 
the pamperers of genocide, as such, cause them for a belligerency, all at once.

shloka:
उपस्थापय मे क्षिप्रम् रथम् सौम्य धनूंषि च |
शरान् च चित्रान् खड्गां च शक्ती च विविधाः शिताः
translation:
"For me, oh, gentle one, promptly position my chariot before me along with bows and arrows, amazing 
swords and diverse sharp power bolts.

shloka:
अग्रे निर्यातुम् इच्छ्हामि पौलस्त्यानाम् महात्मनाम् |
वधार्थम् दुर्विनीतस्य रामस्य रण कोविद
translation:
"Oh, war pert Duushana, I wish to start ahead of all the demons of ours, who are the clans-demons of 
the great souled Paulastya, for the purpose of elimination of that evil-minded Rama." So said Khara 
to Duushana.

shloka:
इति तस्य ब्रुवाणस्य सूर्य वर्णम् महारथम् |
सत् अश्वैः शबलैः युक्तम् आचचक्षे अथ दूषणः
translation:
While Khara is saying thus Duushana heralded saying, "Here comes the great chariot with sun's dazzle, 
yoked with very good horses of variegated colours."

shloka:
तम् मेरु शिखर आकारम् तप्त कांचन भूषणम् |
हेम चक्रम् असंबाधम् वैदूर्यमय कूबरम्
translation:
That chariot which has a roomy cabin with its rooftop like that of the ridge of Mt. Meru, body embellished 
in gold, wheels golden, gem-studded yoke-to-carriage shaft, all around encompassed with golden artefacts 
like fishes, flowers, trees, mountains, sun, moon, and auspicious birds flocks and stars, and even decorated 
with jingle-bells, endowed with flags, swords, and best horses, and such as it is, Khara embarked on 
it with all his rancour. [3-22-13, 14, 15]

shloka:
खरः तु तान् महत् सैन्याम् रथ चर्म आयुध ध्वजान् |
निर्यात इति अब्रवीत् प्रेक्ष्य दूषणः सर्व राक्षसान्
translation:
On overseeing that great army with chariots, skins shields, weaponry and flags, and even at Duushana 
too, Khara charged all those demons saying "proceed."

shloka:
ततः तद् राक्षसम् सैन्यम् घोर चर्म आयुध ध्वजम् |
निर्जगाम जन स्थानात् महानादम् महाजवम्
translation:
Then that demonic force with their ghoulish skin shields, weaponry and flags, issued forth from Janasthaana, 
blaring blatantly and foraying dashingly.

shloka:
मुद्गरैः पट्टिशैः शूलैः सुतीक्ष्णैः च परश्वधैः |
खड्गैः चक्रैः च हस्तस्थैः भ्राजमानैः स तोमरैः
translation:
Wielding maces, dart-bolts, and spears, and also razor-sharp axes, swords and discs, and dreadful power-darts 
and power-bolts that are flashing, iron maces, unusual bows, clubs, scimitars and pounding-shafts, and 
even thunderbolt like weapons that are calamitous in look, that army which comprises fourteen thousand 
fiendish demons that are the followers of Khara's whim, has started from Janasthaana. [3-22-18, 19, 
20]

shloka:
तान् तु निर्धावतो दृष्ट्वा राक्षसान् भीम दर्शनम् |
खरस्य अथ रथः किंचित् जगाम तत् अनन्तरम्
translation:
On seeing the outrush of those demons of diabolic appearance, then Khara's chariot also proceeded a 
little later at their behind.

shloka:
ततः तान् शबलान् अश्वान् तप्त कांचन भूषितान् |
खरस्य मतम् आज्ञाय सारथिः पर्यचोदयत्
translation:
Then the charioteer set spurs on those colourful horses that are adorned in polished gold according 
to the notions of Khara.

shloka:
संचोदितो रथः शीघ्रम् खरस्य रिपु घातिनः |
शब्देन आपूरयामास दिशः स प्रदिशः तथा
translation:
When the chariot of enemy destroyer Khara is driven that impetuously, it has started to swell earth's 
four cardinal quarters and inter-quarters with turbulence.

shloka:
प्रवृद्ध मन्युः तु खरः खर स्वरे
रिपोः वध अर्थम् त्वरितो यथा अंतकः |
अचूचुदत् सारथिम् उन्नदन् पुनर्
महाबलो मेघ इव अश्म वर्षवान्
translation:
He whose voice is thunderous and whose rancour escalated speedily, and who is hastening forward like 
the Terminator intending to destroy his enemy, that Khara repeatedly hurried the charioteer shouting 
at him loudly like a overwhelming cloud that is going to storm stones.

shloka:
तत् प्रयातम् बलम् घोरम् अशिवम् शोणित उदकम् |
अभ्यवर्षत् महा मेघः तुमुलो गर्दभ अरुणः
translation:
A massy and tumultuous ass-coloured cloud rained ill-omened bloody water while that fiendish force is 
advancing.

shloka:
निपेतुः तुरगाः तस्य रथ युक्ता महाजवाः |
समे पुष्पचिते देशे राजमार्गे यदृच्छ्हया
translation:
The highly speedy horses paired to Khara's chariot have tottered in a trice, even though that place 
on the highway is with even surface and spread with flowers.

shloka:
श्यामम् रुधिर पर्यन्तम् बभूव परिवेषणम् |
अलात चक्र प्रतिमम् प्रतिगृह्य दिवाकरम्
translation:
Capturing the sun a blackish corona with blood-red outer circle has formed and nested around it 
like the fiery ring formed by circling a fireball.

shloka:
ततो ध्वजम् उपागम्य हेम दण्डम् समुच्छ्ह्रितम् |
समाक्रम्य महाकायः तस्थौ गृध्रः सुदारुणः
translation:
Then, nearing the golden shaft of the flag of the chariot with a very lofty flagstaff, an awful eagle 
with massive body occupied and perched atop of that golden shaft.

shloka:
जनस्थान समीपे च समाक्रम्य खर स्वनाः |
विस्वरान् विविधान् च चक्रुः मांस आदा मृग पक्षिणः
translation:
Cacophonous and carnivorous predators and vultures took over the nearby places of Janasthaana and they 
made raucous sounds of many kinds.

shloka:
व्याजह्रुः च पदीप्तायाम् दिशि वै भैरव स्वनम् |
अशिवा यातुधानानाम् शिवा घोरा महास्वनाः
translation:
Turning towards the stretch scorched by the sun, fearsome and loud noised jackals have howled emitting 
awful sounds, that which is inauspicious to the demons.

shloka:
प्रभिन्नगजसंकाशतोयशोणितधारिणः | - यद्वा -
प्रभिन्न गज संकाश तोय शोणित धारिणः |
आकाशम् तत् अनाकाशम् 
चक्रुः भीम अंबु वाहकाः
translation:
Then frightening clouds similar to bursting mountains carrying bloodlike water have rendered the firmament 
less of leeway.

shloka:
बभूव तिमिरम् घोरम् उद्धतम् रोम हर्षणम् |
दिशो वा प्रदिशो वा अपि सुव्यक्तम् न चकाशिरे
translation:
There chanced an abominable, cataclysmic, hair-raising darkness whereby the milieus or inter-milieus 
are not very clearly brightened.

shloka:
क्षतज आर्द्र सवर्णाभा संध्या कालम् विना बभौ |
खरम् च अभिमुखम् नेदुः तदा घोरा मृगाः खगाः
translation:
An untimely eventide glistened with a colour similar to the one drenched in blood, and then horrendous 
brutes and birds have clamoured facing Khara directly, and the vultures, jackals and eagles too have 
screamed portending danger. [3-23-9, 10a]

shloka: नित्या अशिव करा युद्धे शिवा घोर निदर्शनाः
translation:
Jackals, that too female jackals, are always the agents of inauspiciousness in wars with demonstrable 
calamities brought forth by their portending howling, and such jackals have now howled in front of Khara's 
army with their snouts spewing blazes.

shloka: कबन्धः परिघ आभासो दृश्यते भास्कर अंतिके
translation:
A spherical object like that of a human trunk is revealed near at the sun, while the sun is rendered 
shineless as though Rahu, the great eclipsing-planet, has eclipsed him inopportunely, and the wind too 
whirled frantically. [3-23-11b, 12]

shloka:
उत्पेतुः च विना रात्रिम् ताराः खद्योतन प्रभाः |
संलीन मीन विहगा नलिन्यः शुष्क पंकजाः
translation:
Stars sprang up with the brilliance of fireflies though it is not night, and at that moment fishes and 
waterfowls stood still in lakes, lotuses have dried up, flowers and fruits have dropped from trees as 
though it is night. [3-23-13, 14a]

shloka: उद्धूतः च विना वातम् रेणुः जलधर अरुणः
translation:
Without any puffing of wind dust in brownish-red colour is heaved up, and there the songbirds like Maina 
started to twitter as 'cii cii kuu cii'. [3-23-14b, 15a]

shloka: उल्काः च अपि स निर्घोषा निपेतुः घोर दर्शनाः
translation:
Meteors horrible in their look have fallen down thunderously, and even the earth together with its mountains, 
woods and forests quaked shakily. [3-23-15b, 16a]

shloka: खरस्य च रथस्थस्य नर्दमानस्य धीमतः
translation:
He who is raving while sitting in his chariot that clever Khara's left shoulder thrilled excessively, 
and his voice too quavered. [3-23-16b, 17a]

shloka: स अस्रा संपद्यते दृष्टिः पश्यमानस्य सर्वतः
translation:
While he is seeing everywhere his eyes spawned tears for no good reason, his forehead ached, but he 
did not retrace his steps owing to his own vanity. [3-23-17b, 18a]

shloka: तान् समीक्ष्य महोत्पातान् उत्थितान् रोम हर्षणान्
translation:
On observing those worst auguries stemming up at that moment with hair-raising nature, Khara laughed 
them off and said this to all of the demons. [3-23-18b, 19a]

shloka: महा उत्पातान् इमान् सर्वान् उत्थितान् घोर दर्शनान्
translation:
"These awful auguries with their horrible nature have arisen, but owing to my own valour I am unbothered 
about all of them as with a mighty one unworried of the mightless. [3-23-19b, 20a]

shloka: तारा अपि शरैः तीक्ष्णैः पातयेयम् नभः तलात्
translation:
"With the excruciating arrows of mine I can hurtle stars from the face of sky, and if highly infuriated, 
I can even enjoin mortality to Death himself. [3-23-20b, 21a]

shloka: राघवम् तम् बल उत्सिक्तम् भ्रातरम् च अस्य लक्ष्मणम्
translation:
"I am reluctant to return without killing that Rama, a haughty one by his might, together with his brother 
Lakshmana, with my incisive arrows. [3-23-21b, 22a]

shloka: यन् निमित्तम् तु रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्य विपर्ययः
translation:
"In whose respect both Rama and Lakshmana behaved perversely, let that sister of mine be contented in 
drinking the blood of those two. [3-23-22b, 23a]

shloka: न क्वचित् प्राप्त पूर्वो मे संयुगेषु पराजयः
translation:
"No defeat has chanced on me in combats at anytime and anywhere, that to you all is obvious and I tell 
no untruth. [3-23-23b, 24a]

shloka: देव राजम् अपि क्रुद्धो मत्त ऐरावत गामिनम्
translation:
"If I am infuriated I can eliminate even the king of gods, wielder of Thunderbolt and a trekker on ruttish 
elephant Iravata, namely Indra in a war, then why talk about these two humans." Thus Khara addressed 
his troops. [3-23-24b, 25a]

shloka: सा तस्य गर्जितम् श्रुत्वा राक्षसाअनाम् महा चमूः
translation:
On hearing that thundering speech of Khara that sizeable army of demons which is tied down by the noose 
of death obtained an incomparable rejoice. [3-23-25b, 26a]

shloka: समेयुः च महात्मानो युद्ध दर्शन कांक्षिणः
translation:
Then desiring to see the war of Khara with Rama, great-souls like sages, gods, gandharva-s along with 
carana-s and siddha-s have come together in firmament. [3-23-26b, 27a]

shloka: समेत्य च ऊचुः सहिताः ते अन्यायम् पुण्यकर्मणः
translation:
On gathering at a place those great souls met one another and said, "let good betide cows, Brahmans 
and those that are held respectful by the people at large." [3-23-27b, 28a]

shloka: जयताम् राघवो युद्धे पौलस्त्यान् रजनी चरान्
translation:
"Let Raghava triumph over these mighty night walkers from the lineage of Pulastya, as with Vishnu who 
once conquered all the mighty demons in war." So said celestials to one another.

shloka: एतत् च अन्यत् च बहुशो ब्रुवाणाः परम ऋषयः
translation:
While the great sages are speaking about this and many other topics, they and the gods abiding in their 
aircrafts have inquisitively seen the flow of army of demons, whose longevity is now beyond hope. [3-23-29, 
30]

shloka:
रथेन तु खरो वेगात् सैन्यस्य अग्रात् विनिःसृतः |
श्येनगामी पृथुग्रीवो यज्ञशत्रुः विहंगमः
translation:
Khara speedily bolted in his chariot to the van of his legions, and on seeing that demon Khara going 
in front other important demons too rushed to fore. They are Shyenagaami, Prithugviira, Yajnashatru, 
Vihamgama and also Durjaya, Karaviiraaksha, Parusha, Kaalakaarmuka, Hemamaali, Mahaamaali, Sarpaasya, 
Rudhiraaksha. These twelve highly valorous demons cruised in a semicircle around Khara.

shloka:
महाकपालः स्थूलाक्षः प्रमाथी त्रिशिराः तथा |
चत्वार एते सेना अग्रे दूषणम् पृष्ठतो अन्वयुः
translation:
Likewsie Mahakapaala, Stuulaaksha, Pramaathii, Trishira are the four commanders of demonic forces and 
they followed Duushana marching at his behind.

shloka:
सा भीम वेगा समर अभिकांक्षिणी
सुदारुणा राक्षस वीर सेना |
तौ राज पुत्रौ सहसा अभ्युपेता
माला ग्रहाणाम् 
इव चन्द्र सूर्यौ
translation:
That army of valiant demons which is highly execrable, infernally speedy, and readily inspirited for 
a battle quickly rushed towards those two princes, Rama and Lakshmana, as though a festoon of planets 
would rush towards the Moon and Sun so as to put them to rout.

shloka:
आश्रमम् प्रति याते तु खरे खर पराक्रमे |
तान् एव औत्पातिकान् रामः सह भ्रात्रा ददर्श ह
translation:
While fiercely valorous Khara proceeded towards Rama's hermitage, Rama along with his brother Lakshmana 
has indeed seen the very same auguries which have earlier appeared to Khara.

shloka:
तान् उत्पातान् महाघोरान् रामो दृष्ट्वा अति अमर्षण |
प्रजानाम् अहितान् दृष्ट्वा वाक्यम् लक्ष्मणम् 
अब्रवीत्
translation:
On looking at those very gruesomely bad omens, and perceiving them to be unpropitious to people, Rama 
spoke this sentence to Lakshmana.

shloka:
इमान् पश्य महाबाहो सर्व भूत अपहारिणः |
समुत्थितान् महा उत्पातान् संहर्तुम् सर्व राक्षसान्
translation:
"Oh, dextrous Lakshmana, for the complete elimination of all the demons these great indications have 
arisen, as though betokening the annihilation of all beings. See them.

shloka:
अमी रुधिर धाराः तु विसृजंतो खर स्वनाः |
व्योम्नि मेघा निवर्तन्ते परुषा गर्दभ अरुणाः
translation:
"On their part these clouds are hovering on the sky with stark reddish-grey tint, thunderously braying 
and copiously showering streams of blood.

shloka:
स धूमाः च शराः सर्वे मम युद्ध अभिनन्दिताः |
रुक्म पृष्ठानि चापानि विचेष्टन्ते विचक्षण
translation:
"All my arrows too are incensed to fuming in an ecstasy towards a war, and dorsally gold-plated bows 
of mine are incessantly spurring to hook up those arrows, telling apart the impeding conflict.

shloka:
यादृशा इह कूजन्ति पक्षिणो वन चारिणः |
अग्रतो नः भयम् प्राप्तम् संशयो जीवितस्य च
translation:
"Judging by the kind of wild birds that are shrieking here, danger is up ahead and coming upon us, along 
with uncertainty of our lives.

shloka:
संप्रहारः तु सुमहान् भविष्यति न संशयः |
अयम् आख्याति मे बाहुः स्फुरमाणो मुहुर् मुहुः
translation:
"This right hand of mine is indicating by its repeated throbbing that a critical and riotous conflict 
is going to occur, no doubt, but oh brave one, our victory and defeat to the enemies are also in vicinity, 
and for sure, your face is also appearing brightish and aglow, which itself is a good omen.  
[3-24-7, 8]

shloka:
उद्यतानाम् हि युद्धार्थम् येषाम् भवति लक्ष्मणः |
निष्प्रभम् वदनम् तेषाम् भवति आयुः परिक्षयः
translation:
"If the faces of those that are poised for a conflict loose lustre, deem that the death is looming large 
on their longevity too.

shloka:
रक्षसाम् नर्दताम् घोरः श्रूयते अयम् महाध्वनिः |
आहतानाम् च भेरीणाम् राक्षसैः क्रूर कर्मभिः
translation:
"This nasty noise which we hear pertains to the uproar of demons, and even to the drumming of war drums 
by the demons of fiendish activities, and this is ear-splitting.

shloka:
अनागत विधानम् तु कर्तव्यम् शुभम् इच्छ्हता |
आपदम् शंकमानेन पुरुषेण विपश्चिता
translation:
"Preventive measures are to be effectuated for any imminent situation by any well-wishing person, or 
by a person with misgivings about a danger, or by a person of talent.

shloka:
तस्मात् गृहीत्वा वैदेहीम् शर पाणिः धनुर् धरः |
गुहाम् आश्रय शैलस्य दुर्गाम् पादप संकुलाम्
translation:
"Hence, wield your bow, keep arrows ready at hand, and taking Vaidehi with you seek shelter in a impassable 
cave of a mountain overgrown with trees.

shloka:
प्रतिकूलितुम् इच्छ्हामि न हि वाक्यम् इदम् त्वया |
शापितो मम पादाभ्याम् गम्यताम् वत्स मा चिरम्
translation:
"I wish you to gainsay me for this word of mine, my boy, have honour on my feet and be gone not before 
long.

shloka:
त्वम् हि शूरः च बलवान् हन्या एतान् न संशयः |
स्वयम् निहन्तुम् इच्छ्हमि सर्वान् एव निशाचरान्
translation:
"You are a stalwart, a forceful one, and for sure you can eliminate them all, it is doubtless, but I 
long to eliminate all of the nightwalkers, personally" Rama said thus to Lakshmana.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः सह सीतया |
शरान् आदाय चापम् च गुहाम् दुर्गाम् समाश्रयत्
translation:
When Rama said to him that way, Lakshmana picked up his bow and arrows, and together with Seetha he 
took shelter in an unreachable cave.

shloka:
तस्मिन् प्रविष्टे तु गुहाम् लक्ष्मणे सह सीतया |
हन्त निर्युक्तम् इति उक्त्वा रामः कवचम् आविशत्
translation:
On Lakshmana's entering into cave along with Seetha, Rama said to himself, "thank goodness, it is a 
good-idea!" and thus saying he donned his shield.

shloka:
स तेन अग्नि निकाशेन कवचेन विभूषितः |
बभूव रामः तिमिरे महान् अग्निर् इव उत्थितः
translation:
Well bedecked in a shield that has fire-like brilliance that Rama shone forth like a fumeless conflagration 
up-shot in utter darkness.

shloka:
स चापम् उद्यम्य महत् शरान् आदाय वीर्यवान् |
संबभूव अवस्थितः तत्र ज्या स्वनैः पूरयन् दिशः
translation:
On raising his imposing bow and drawing arrows, that valorous Rama firmed up and stood there, filling 
all the directions with the tinny sounds of bowstring.

shloka:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाः च सह चारणैः |
समेयुः च महात्मनो युद्ध दर्शन कांक्षया
translation:
Gods with gandharva-s and great-souled siddha-s along with carana-s have then met one another and came 
there aspiring to see the war.

shloka:
ऋषयः च महात्मनो लोके ब्रह्मर्षि सत्तमाः |
समेत्य च ऊचुः सहिताः ते अन्योन्यम् पुण्य कर्मणः
translation:
The great-souled sages and those that are known in worlds as eminent Brahma-sages, on their coming together 
those beings of pious exploits spoke to one another, among themselves.

shloka:
स्वस्ति गो ब्राह्मणानाम् च लोकानाम् च इति संस्थिताः |
जयताम् राघवो युद्धे पौलस्त्यान् रजनी चरान्
translation:
"Let good betide cows, Brahmans and those people that are abiding in all the worlds. Raghava shall be 
victorious in the war over the clansmen of Sage Paulastya, the nightwalkers." Thus they talked among 
themselves.

shloka: एवम् उक्त्वा पुनः प्र ऊचुः आलोक्य च परस्परम्
translation:
Thus speaking they also well-said again, looking at each other "the demons of fiendish deeds are fourteen 
thousand in number and this virtue-souled Rama is solitary... what would be the result of this war!" 
Thus the sages discussed among themselves. [3-24-22b, 23]

shloka:
इति राजर्षयः सिद्धाः स गणाः च द्विजर्षभाः |
जात कौतूहलात् तस्थुर् विमानस्थाः च देवता
translation:
Thus the assemblages of kingly-sages, siddha-s and the eminent Brahmans, along with gods that are staying 
in their aircrafts, tarried there in the firmament peering inquisitively at Rama.

shloka:
आविष्टम् तेजसा रामम् स.ंग्राम शिरसि स्थितम् |
दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि भयात् विव्यथिरे तदा
translation:
Immured in an aura of invincibility Rama is standing up to the war in its vanguard, and then on seeing 
at him all beings went into the throes of dread.

shloka:
रूपम् अप्रतिमम् तस्य रामस्य अक्लिष्ट कर्मणः |
बभूव रूपम् क्रुद्धस्य रुद्रस्य इव महात्मनः
translation:
That nonesuch aspect of Rama whose deeds are unharmful to any, has become the aspect of wrathful supreme-souled 
Rudra.

shloka:
इति संभाष्यमाणो तु देव गंधर्व चारणैः |
ततो गंभीर निर्ह्रादम् घोर चर्म आयुध ध्वजम्
translation:
While gods, gandharva-s, carana-s are conversing thus, then they have seen there the legions of the 
demons arriving from all over with boisterous noises, spouting cries of bravo, handling their grisly 
skins, shields, weaponry and war-flags, and onrushing at each other in disarray. With brassy twanging 
of bows, with the drumming of war drums, and even by their jumping, leaping and bouncing that area is 
filled with very loud and clamorous noise. [3-24-27, 28, 29]

shloka:
तेषाम् सुतुमुलः शब्दः पूरयामास तद् वनम् |
तेन शब्देन वित्रस्ताः श्वापदा वन चारिणः
translation:
When highly brutish cacophony of demons started to fill the forest, that jangling even panicked the 
brutes ranging in that forest, and those beasts dashed off to other places where silence prevailed, 
without looking back. [3-24-30, 31a]

shloka: तत् च अनीकम् महावेगम् रामम् समनुवर्तत
translation:
And that foolhardy army of demons which in simile is like an unnavigable ocean steered towards Rama 
handling many assault weapons. [3-24-31b, 32a]

shloka: रामो अपि चारयन् चक्षुः सर्वतो रण पण्डितः
translation:
Casting his sight all-over even that war-expert Rama has seen that army of Khara lunging at a conflict. 
[3-24-32b, 33a]

shloka: वितत्य च धनुर् भीमम् तूण्याः च उद्धृत्य सायकान्
translation:
Rama stretched his awesome bow to examine the taut of bowstring, and even whipped arrows out of quiver, 
and then adopted a mask of extreme wrath to eliminate all the demons.

shloka:
दुष्प्रेक्ष्यश्चाभवत्क्रुद्धोयुगान्ताग्निरिवज्वलन् - यद्वा -
दुष्प्रेक्ष्यः च अभवत् क्रुद्धो युगान्त 
अग्निः इव ज्वलन्
translation:
And when he is enraged and blazing he became frightful-looking like the blazing Fire at the end of era, 
and on seeing such a Rama when he is pervaded with conflagration like anger, the pastoral deities are 
very much annoyed.

shloka:
तस्य रुष्ट्स्य रूपम् तु रामस्य ददृशे तदा |
दक्षस्य इव क्रतुम् हन्तुम् उद्यतस्य पिनाकिनी
translation:
The all-pacific aspect of that Rama then in his exasperation appeared to be like that of the all-ruinous 
Rudra, the wielder of bow called Pinaki, namely peaceful Shiva when enraged, at the time of Rudra's 
embarking on to ruin the Vedic ritual of Daksha Prajaapati.

shloka:
तत् कार्मुकैः आभरणैः रथैः च
तत् वर्माभिः च अग्नि समान वर्णैः |
बभूव सैन्यम् पिशित अशनिनाम्
सूर्य उदये नीलम् इव अभ्र जालम्
translation:
That army of raw-flesh eaters with their bows, embellishments, and chariots, and also with their armours, 
all glittering with the dazzle of flaming fire, varied into a sky-blue coloured cluster of clouds on 
which the dazzling sunrays will be glittering at the dawning of the sun.

shloka:
अवष्टब्ध धनुम् रामम् क्रुद्धम् च रिपु घातिनम् |
ददर्श आश्रमम् आगम्य खरः सह पुरःसरैः
translation:
Khara on arriving at the hermitage along with forerunning soldiers saw the enemy-eliminator and wrathful 
Rama holding fast to his bow.

shloka:
तम् दृष्ट्वा सगुणम् चापम् उद्यम्य खर निःस्वनम् |
रामस्य अभिमुखम् सूतम् चोद्यताम् इति अचोदयत्
translation:
On seeing Rama that bawling Khara raised his string-taut bow that makes an ass-like braying twang, drove 
his charioteer crazy saying, "drive to the fore of that Rama..."

shloka:
स खरस्य आज्ञया सूतः तुरगान् समचोदयत् |
यत्र रामो महाबाहुः एको धुन्वन् धनुः स्थितः
translation:
On the orders of Khara the charioteer drove the horses to there where the mighty armed Rama is standing 
single-handedly while swaying his bow.

shloka:
तम् तु निष्पतितम् दृष्ट्वा सर्वे ते रजनी चराः |
मुंचमाना महानादम् सचिवाः पर्यवारयन्
translation:
On seeing Khara descending on Rama then all those nightwalkers who are the deputies of Khara encircled 
Khara venting out loud battle cries.

shloka:
स तेषाम् यातुधानानाम् मध्ये रथः गतः खरः |
बभूव मध्ये ताराणाम् लोहिता.ंग इव उदितः
translation:
Khara staying on his chariot in the thick of those demons appeared to be like coppery-red planet Mars 
up-shot in the thick of stars.

shloka:
ततः शर सहस्रेन रामम् अप्रतिम ओजसम् |
अर्दयित्वाअ महानादम् ननाद समरे खरः
translation:
In his proneness to war then Khara assaulted that uniquely forceful Rama with a thousand arrows and 
blared a roaring battle cry.

shloka:
ततः तम् भीम धन्वानम् क्रुद्धाः सर्वे निशाचराः |
रामम् नाना विधैः शस्त्रैः अभ्यवर्षन्त दुर्जयम्
translation:
All of those infuriated nightwalkers then incessantly rained diverse weapons on that invincibleRama 
who is handling a horrific bow.

shloka:
मुद्गरैः आयसैः शूलैः प्रासैः खड्गैः परश्वधैः |
राक्षसाः समरे रामम् निजघ्नू रोष तत्पराः
translation:
Those demons that are already caught up with rancour bombarded Rama with bludgeons, lances, tridents, 
darts and hatchets.

shloka:
ते वलाहक संकाशा महाकाया महाबलाः |
अभ्यधावन्त काकुत्स्थम् रथैः वाजिभिः एव च
translation:
Those massive bodied and exceptionally mighty demons came jostling like immense clouds in their eagerness 
to kill Rama in that war, while some mounted on chariots and horsebacks, and some more riding mountain-ridges 
like elephants rushed in on Rama. [3-25-9,10a]

shloka: ते रामे शर वर्षाणि व्यसृजन् रक्षसाम् गणाः
translation:
And those bands of demons have outpoured arrows on Rama, as with enormous black-clouds disemboguing 
torrents on a lofty mountain. [3-25-10b, 11a]

shloka: सर्वैः परिवृतो रामो राक्षसैः कॄरदर्शिनैः
translation:
When hemmed in with those grisly-looking demons Rama appeared like Rudra surrounded by his divine retinue 
calledprathama gaNa-s, on certain days, whereupon he starts his all-destructive 
cosmic-dance. [3-25-11b, 12a]

shloka: तानि मुक्तानि शस्त्राणि यातुधानैः स राघवः
translation:
That Raghava has pre-empted those arrows discharged by the demons with his excruciatingly pointed arrows 
as an ocean would do with the river's onrush. [3-25-12b, 13a]

shloka: स तैः प्रहरणैः घोरैः भिन्न गात्रो न विव्यथे
translation:
Even if his body is gashed with those gruesome assault weapons Rama is not enfeebled, as with the enormous 
Mt. Meru that can withstand even if battered by very many highly blazing thunderbolts of Indra. [3-25-13, 
14a]

shloka: स विद्धः क्षतज दिग्धः सर्व गात्रेषु राघवः
translation:
Bruised and bedaubed with blood on all his limbs that Rama of Raghu's dynasty took shape of the sun 
enshrouded by cloudscapes at eventide. [3-25-14b, 15a]

shloka: विषेदुर् देव गन्धर्वाः सिद्धाः च परम ऋषयः
translation:
On seeing lone Rama beset by many demons, then the gods, celestials, saints and sublime-sages are dispirited. 
[3-25-15b, 16a]

shloka: ततो रामः तु सुसंक्रुद्धो मण्डली कृत कार्मुकः
translation:
But Rama on becoming highly infuriated curved his bow to a full circularity on stretching the bowstring 
up to his ear, and then jetted out trenchant arrows in hundreds. Why hundreds? He surged them in thousands. 
[3-25-16b, 17a]

shloka: दुरवारान् दुर्विषहान् कालपाश उपमान् रणे
translation:
In that war Rama sportily discharged eagle-feathered arrows adorned in gold which are unstoppable and 
intolerable, and which in simile are the leads of Time-god. [3-25-17b, 18a]

shloka: ते शराः शत्रु सैन्येषु मुक्ता रामेण लीलया
translation:
Those arrows that are playfully discharged on the army of enemy have grabbed the lives of demons like 
the tethers flung by the Time-god. [3-25-18b, 19a]

shloka: भित्त्वा राक्षस देहान् ताम् ते शरा रुधिर आप्लुताः
translation:
On impaling the bodies demons, the arrows swamped in blood have gone into welkin, where they are aglow 
with flares equalling inflamed flames. [3-25-19b, 20a]

shloka: असंख्येयाः तु रामस्य सायकाः चाप मण्डलात्
translation:
Innumerable and highly frightening arrows fusilladed from the nimbus of the bow of Rama that resulted 
as the filchers of the lives of demons. [3-25-20b, 21a]

shloka: तैः धनूंषि ध्वज अग्राणि चर्माणि च शिरांसि च
translation:
In that war, shooting now with hundreds, and now with thousands of such arrows, Rama shredded those 
many bows, pinnacles of war-flags, armours and the like. And even shred are the heads of demons, along 
with their ornamented arms and thighs similar to the trunks of elephants. [3-25-21b, 22]

shloka:
हयान् कांचन सन्नाहान् रथ युक्तान् स सारथीन् |
गजाम् च स गज आरोहान् स हयान् सारधिनः तदा
translation:
With the arrows flung from the bow-bowstring-nimbus of Rama, he indeed shredded and scraped the horses 
hitched with golden harnesses, and the chariots to which they are yoked, and even their charioteers. 
Likewise, he even ripped off the elephants along with their riders, and the horses along with their 
cavaliers. And on eliminating infantrymen in that war Rama led them to the abode of Yama, the Time-god. 
[3-25-23, 24]

shloka:
ततो नालीक नाराचैः तीक्ष्ण अग्रैः विकर्णिभिः |
भीमम् आर्त स्वरम् चक्रुः छ्हिद्यमाना निशाचराः
translation:
While ripped to pieces with tubular arrows, with arrows made of iron, and with sharp-edged and crescent-tipped 
arrows those demons have let out disgusting cries of anguish.

shloka:
तत् सैन्यम् निशितैः बाणैः अर्दितम् मर्म भेदिभिः |
न रामेण सुखम् लेभे शुष्कम् वनम् इव अग्निना
translation:
When those arrows that gore the critical parts are thus harrowing, that army is discomposed like a forest 
burnt to a cinder by wild-fire.

shloka:
केचिद् भीम बलाः शूराः प्रासान् शूलान् परश्वधान् |
चिक्षिपुः परम क्रुद्धा रामाय रजनीचराः
translation:
Some of the grotesquely sinewy and braving nightwalkers are highly enraged and dashed their darts, tridents, 
and hatchets towards Rama.

shloka:
तेषाम् बाणैः महाबाहुः शस्त्राणि आवार्य वीर्यवान् |
जहार समरे प्राणान् चिच्छ्हेद च शिरो धरान्
translation:
On fending off those weapons with his arrows that mighty armed and valorous Rama filched away their 
lives by shearing off their necks in that war.

shloka:
ते छ्हिन्न शिरसः पेतुः छ्हिन्न चर्म शरासनाः |
सुपर्ण वात विक्षिप्ता जगत्याम् पादपा यथा
translation:
Those demons crashed down to earth with their heads severed and shields and bows wrecked, like the trees 
strewn around on earth owing to the gust raised by Garuda, the Divine Eagle, when he takes a sudden 
flight in heavens.

shloka:
अवशिष्टाः च ये तत्र विषण्णाः ते निशाचराः |
खरम् एव अभ्यधावन्त शरणार्थम् शर आहताः
translation:
Those nightwalkers that are battered by those arrows and remaining there, they desperately rushed towards 
Khara alone seeking shelter.

shloka:
तान् सर्वान् धनुर् आदाय समाश्वास्य च दूषणः |
अभ्यधावत सुसंक्रुद्धः क्रुद्धः [रुद्रम्] क्रुद्ध इव 
अन्तकः
translation:
Comforting all of them and taking his bow, very highly infuriated Duushana rushed towards that infuriated 
Rama like the furious Eliminator Yama.

shloka:
निवृत्ताः तु पुनः सर्वे दूषण आश्रय निर्भयाः |
रामम् एव अभ्यधावन्त साल ताल शिल आयुधाः
translation:
Coming under the shelter of Duushana all of those demons are but emboldened and returned, and they once 
again rushed towards Rama with saala trees, palm trees and boulders as their weapons.

shloka:
शूल मुद्गर हस्ताः च पाश हस्ता महाबलाः |
सृजन्तः शर वर्षाणि शस्त्र वर्षाणि संयुगे
translation:
Handling tridents, maces, and leashes those great-mighty demons have created torrents of arrows, missiles, 
trees and boulders, and inundated Rama in that war. [3-25-33, 34a]

shloka: तद् बभूव अद्भुतम् युद्धम् तुमुलम् रोम हर्षणम्
translation:
Again there chanced a highly gruesome war between Rama and those demons that is tumultuous, stunning, 
and a hair-raising. [3-25-34b, 35a]

shloka: ते समन्तात् अभिक्रुद्धा राघवम् पुनर् आर्दयन्
translation:
Those demons have resurfaced from all around pressurising Raghava in high dudgeon. On seeing the reappearance 
of demons from everywhere, with whom all the directions and inter-directions are fully filled, and who 
are storming torrents of arrows, then that exceptionally forceful Rama made a thunderous sound and launched 
an extremely blazing missile among the gather of demons, called gandharva missile. [3-25-35b, 36, 37]

shloka:
ततः शर सहस्राणि निर्ययुः चाप मण्डलात् |
सर्वा दश दिशो बानैः आपूर्यन्त समागतैः
translation:
Then from the nimbus of his bow, arrows in thousand have scurried out, and with them thus arrived all 
the ten sides are cramped up.

shloka:
न आददानाम् शरान् घोरान् विमुंचंतम् शर उत्तमान् |
विकर्षमाणम् पश्यन्ति राक्षसाः ते शर आर्दिताः
translation:
Either the drawing of those supreme arrows from the quiver, or the traction of bowstring on placing 
them, or unloosing them from the bow is unperceived by those demons that are harrowing under those arrows.

shloka:
शर अन्धकारम् आकाशम् आवृणोत् स दिवाकरम् |
बभूव अवस्थितो रामः प्रक्षिपन् इव तान् शरान्
translation:
Darkness caused by the thick of the arrows overspread the sky including its sun, while Rama happened 
to persevere spewing forth his arrows.

shloka:
युगपत् पतमानैः च युगपच्च हतैः भ्रिशम् |
युगपत् पतितैः चैव विकीर्णा वसुधा अभवत्
translation:
Far and wide the earth is scattered with herds that are falling instantaneously, hosts that have fallen 
instantly, and huddles that are already felled with an instantaneity.

shloka:
निहताः पतिताः क्षीणा च्छ्हिन्न भिन्न विदारिताः |
तत्र तत्र स्म दृश्यन्ते राक्षसाः ते सहस्रशः
translation:
Thousands of demons are noticeable hither and yon, killed, fallen and enfeebled, and slashed, gashed 
and ripped.

shloka:
स उष्णीषैः उत्तम अंगैः च स अ.ंगदैः बाहुभिः तथा |
ऊरुभिः बाहुभिः च्छ्हिन्नैः नाना रूपैः विभूषणैः
translation:
Some severed heads still have their headgears and some bare, some arms are with armlets and some bare, 
while some with their arms cut off, some with their thighs cut off, some with their divers patterns 
of ornaments on their bodies have fallen on ground. Numerous horses and elephants are felled. Chariots, 
royal-fans, royal-parasols, war-flags of very many kinds are ravaged in many ways. Hit down by Rama's 
arrows spears and tridents are variously splintered, swords broken to pieces, darts and hatchets shattered 
and strewn around. Also the boulders are pulverised, various amazing arrows have gone to rack and ruin 
in many ways. Spread with such wreckage the earth has become horrifying for a glance. [3-25-43, 44, 
45, 46]

shloka:
तान् दृष्ट्वा निहतान् सर्वे रक्षसाः परम आतुराः |
न तत्र चलितुम् शक्ता रामम् पर पुरंजयम्
translation:
On seeing the killed demons all the surviving demons have become enervated and they are rendered incapable 
to make a move towards Rama, the conqueror of enemy's capitals.

shloka:
दूषणः तु स्वकम् सैन्यम् हन्यमानम् विलोक्य च |
संदिदेश महाबाहुः भीम वेगान् निशाचरान्
translation:
On seeing the shattering of his own forces, Duushana bid five thousand mighty-armed nightwalkers of 
monstrous impetus, and who knew no retreat in war, to attack Rama.

shloka: ते शूलैः पट्टिशैः कदगैः शिला वरषैः द्रुमैः
translation:
And they with spears, scimitars, swords, and with the rains of boulders, trees and arrows rained incessantly 
and inordinately upon Rama from all over. [3-26-2b, 3a]

shloka: तत् द्रुमाणाम् शिलानाम् च वर्षम् प्राण हरम् महत्
translation:
Raghava, the virtue-souled, in his turn has neutralised that ghastly and life-taking storm of boulders 
and trees with his fierce arrows. [3-26-3b, 4a]

shloka: प्रतिगृह्य च तद् वर्षम् निमीलित इव ऋषभः
translation:
Like a bull receiving rain with closed eyes Rama assimilated that storming and then evoked an inordinate 
infuriation for eliminating all of the demons. [3-26-4b, 5a]

shloka: ततः क्रोध समाविष्टः प्रदीप्त इव तेजसा
translation:
Exasperation prevailing on him who appeared to be highly blazing with the blaze of his own virtue, he 
then diffused Duushana and his army with arrows from all over. [3-26-5b, 6a]

shloka: ततः सेना पतिः क्रुद्धो दूषणः शत्रु दूषणः
translation:
And on becoming enraged Duushana, the railer of his rivals and the commander of that army, then virtually 
forestalled Raghava's onslaught with his arrows that are simulative of thunderbolts. [3-26-6b, 7a]

shloka: ततो रामः संक्रुद्धः क्षुरेण अस्य महत् धनुः
translation:
That valiant one in warring Rama is then infuriated and with his crescent-barbed arrow shivered the 
sturdy bow of Duushana, shredding four of his horses with four more arrows. [3-26-7b, 8a]

shloka: हत्वा च अश्वान् शरैः तीक्ष्णैः अर्थ चन्द्रेण सारथे
translation:
On destructing the horses with excruciating arrows, he even fragmented the head of the charioteer with 
a crescent-barbed arrow, and even impaled the chest of demon Duushana with some more arrows. [3-26-8b, 
9a]

shloka: स च्छ्हिन्न धन्वा विरथो हत अश्वो हत सारथिः
translation:
With his bow fractured and chariot shredded, and with horses and charioteer killed, he that Duushana 
grabbed a mace which outranks a peak of mountain and a hair-thriller at its sight, and which girt with 
golden girths once gritted the armies of gods, the head of which is studded with incisive iron spikes 
and saturated with the fat of foes, a coequal of a diamond and a thunderbolt in its hardiness and flashiness, 
and a ransacker of the archways of fortresses of his adversaries. [3-26-9b, 10, 11]

shloka:
तम् महा उरग संकाशम् प्रगृह्य परिघम् रणे |
दूषणो अभ्यपतत् रामम् क्रूर कर्मा निशाचरः
translation:
On firmly gripping that mace which in war is akin to an infernal serpent, and the touch of which tantamount 
to snakebite, rushed that nightwalker Duushana with infernal exerts rushed towards Rama.

shloka:
तस्य अभिपतमानस्य दूषणस्य स राघवः |
द्वाभ्याम् शराभ्याम् चिच्छ्हेद स हस्त आभरणौ भुजौ
translation:
While Duushana came falling on, he that Raghava sheared off his shoulders that have wrist-ornaments 
on his arms with two arrows.

shloka:
भ्रष्टः तस्य महाकायः पपात रण मूर्धनि |
परिघः छ्हिन्न हस्तस्य शक्र ध्वज इव अग्रतः
translation:
When Duushana's arms are thus sheared in the van of war, his gigantic mace slipped and spun in his own 
front, like the flagstaff with flag raised in honour of Indra, and collapsed .

shloka:
कराभ्याम् च विकीर्णाभ्याम् पपात भुवि दूषणः |
विषाणाभ्याम् विशीर्णाभ्याम् मनस्वी इव महागजः
translation:
With both of his arms strewn around Duushana fell down onto earth like a haughty and gigantic elephant 
when both of its tusks are broken down.

shloka:
दृष्ट्वा तम् पतितम् भूमौ दूषणम् निहतम् रणे |
साधु साधु इति काकुत्स्थम् सर्व भूतानि अपूजयन्
translation:
On seeing Duushana eliminated and fallen to ground, all the beings have applauded Rama saying, 'good, 
good...'

shloka:
एतस्मिन् अन्तरे क्रुद्धाः त्रयः सेना अग्र यायिनः |
संहत्य अभ्यद्रवन् रामम् मृत्यु पाश अवपाशिताः
translation:
In the meantime infuriated are the three leading commanders of that army, namely Mahakapaala, Sthulaaksha 
and great mighty Pramaathii, and they collectively ran towards Rama, bound by the rein of death. [3-26-17, 
18a]

shloka: महाकपालो विपुलम् शूलम् उद्यम्य राक्षसः
translation:
Mahakapaala raising a broad trident, Sthulaaksha handling a scimitar, Pramaathi handling an axe rushed 
towards Rama. [3-26-18b, 19a]

shloka: दृष्ट्वा एव आपततः ताम् तु राघवः सायकैः शितैः
translation:
As one would receive guests meeting his basic needs, Raghava too took on these untimely guests of war, 
rather the insurgents, meeting their basic needs which now are no more than highly sharpened acute edged 
arrows, when he saw them coming and falling upon him, inopportunely. [3-26-19b, 20a]

shloka: महाकपालस्य शिरः चिच्छ्हेद रघुनंदनः
translation:
Rama, the legatee of Raghu, chopped off the head of Mahakapaala, with incalculable spates of arrows 
he eliminated Pramaathi, and filled the bulging eyes of Sthulaaksha with arrows by which Sthulaaksha 
is killed and fell down onto ground like a burly tree with its broad branches. Then still infuriated 
Rama forthwith eliminated the five thousand hench-demons of Duushana with five thousand arrows, and 
thus he led them to the residence of Time-god, namely the hell. [3-26-20b, 21, 22, 23a]

shloka: दूषणम् निहतम् श्रुत्वा तस्य च एव पदानुगान्
translation:
On hearing about the killing of Duushana and also thus of the followers of Duushana, Khara irately ordered 
his army captains, under whose captaincy mighty forces are there. [3-26-23b, 24a]

shloka: अयम् विनिहतः संख्ये दूषणः स पदानुगाः
translation:
"Duushana is killed in war along with his followers, hence all you demons, take formidable army, take 
weapons of diverse designs, combat and kill that evil-human Rama..." Thus Khara ordered the remaining 
demons. [3-26-24b, 25]

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा खरः क्रुद्धो रामम् एव अभि दुद्रुवे |
श्येनगामी पृथुग्रीवो यज्ञशत्रुर् विहंगमः
translation:
Saying so Khara himself rushed towards Rama in rage, and Shyenagaami, Prithugriiva, Yajnashatru, Vihangama 
Durjaya, Karaviiraaksha, Parusha, Kaalakaarmuka, Hemamaali, Mahaamaali, Sarpaasya, and Rudhiraaksha 
are the twelve fiendishly atrocious troop leaders of demonic forces, and they too rushed towards Rama 
launching their atrocious arrows. [3-26-26, 27, 28]

shloka:
ततः पावक संकाशैः हेम वज्र विभूषितैः |
जघन शेषम् तेजस्वी तस्य सैन्यस्य सायकैः
translation:
He who is resplendent that Rama then annihilated the remaining demons of that army with his arrows that 
are embellished with gold and diamonds, and that are blazing like ritual-fires.

shloka:
ते रुक्म पुंखा विशिखाः स धूमा इव पावकाः |
निजघ्नुः तानि रक्षांसि वज्रा इव महाद्रुमान्
translation:
With those arrows that have golden tailpieces and sharp barbs, and that are dazzling like fuming ritual 
fires Rama felled the demons, as Thunderbolts of Indra will be felling gigantic trees.

shloka:
रक्षसाम् तु शतम् रामः शतेन एकेन कर्णिना |
सहस्रम् तु सहस्रेण जघान रण मूर्धनि
translation:
With a hundred rudder like arrows Rama hit down a hundred demons, and with a thousand more, thousand 
more demons are hit in the forefront of that war.

shloka:
तैः भिन्न वर्म आभरणाः छ्हिन्न भिन्न शर आसनाः |
निपेतुः शोणित आदिग्धा धरण्याम् रजनीचराः
translation:
Ripped are their shields and armorial-ornaments, ruined and rickety are their bows, and they the nightwalkers 
fell flat on ground, bodies wholly smudged with blood.

shloka:
तैः मुक्त केशैः समरे पतितैः शोणित उक्षितैः |
विस्तीर्णा वसुधा कृत्स्ना महावेदिः कुशैः इव
translation:
With those demons that have fallen down in war, whose hair is tousled and who are drenched in blood, 
entire earth looked like a vast altar of fire overspread with holy grass.

shloka:
तत् क्षणे तु महा घोरम् वनम् निहत राक्षसम् |
बभूव निरय प्रख्यम् मांस शोणित कर्दमम्
translation:
That forest which became sludgy with the flesh and blood of killed demons and very disgusting, in a 
moment it became identical with hell.

shloka:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि रक्षसाम् भीम कर्मणाम् |
हतानि एकेन रामेण मानुषेण पदातिना
translation:
Thus that Rama, a lone one, that too a foot-soldier, has eliminated fourteen thousand demons of frightening 
exploits.

shloka:
तस्य सैन्यस्य सर्वस्य खरः शेषो महारथः |
राक्षसः त्रिशिराः चैव रामः च रिपुसूदनः
translation:
Of his entire army great-charioteer Khara and Trishira are the remaining nightwalkers, and Rama, the 
enemy destroyer, naturally on the other side.

shloka:
शेषा हता महावीर्या राक्षसा रण मूर्धनि |
घोरा दुर्विषहाः सर्वे लक्ष्मणस्य अग्रजेन
translation:
Lakshmana's elder brother Rama eliminated all of the remaining demons in the forefront of war who are 
highly valorous, ghastly and unbearable.

shloka:
ततः तु तद् भीम बलम् महा आहवे
समीक्ष्य रामेण हतम् बलीयसा |
रथेन रामम् महता खरः ततः
समाससाद इन्द्र 
इव उद्यत अशनिः
translation:
Then on surveying that great demonic force which is eliminated by Rama in that staggering war, Khara 
then marched on to reach Rama in a huge chariot, as with Indra who will march upraising his Thunderbolt.

shloka:
खरम् तु राम अभिमुखम् प्रयांतम् वाहिनी पतिः |
राक्षसः त्रिशिरा नाम संनिपत्य इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
But when Khara is about to lunge to the forefront of Rama, nearing him the commander of demonic forces 
named Trishira spoke this to him.

shloka:
माम् नियोजय विक्रांतम् त्वम् निवर्तस्व साहसात् |
पश्य रामम् महाबाहुम् संयुगे विनिपातितम्
translation:
"Desisting from your personal adventure you enjoin me for I am an invader, and then you are certain 
to see me felling that mighty-armed Rama in combat.

shloka:
प्रतिजानामि ते सत्यम् आयुधम् च अहम् आलभे |
यथा रामम् वधिष्यामि वधार्हम् सर्व रक्षसाम्
translation:
"Taking oath on my weapon I promise to you that I truly wish to kill this Rama, as he deserves ill of 
all the demons by killing.

shloka:
अहम् वा अस्य रणे मृत्युः एष वा समरे मम |
विनिवर्त्य रण उत्साहम् मुहूर्तम् प्राश्निको भव
translation:
"Hold back your combative-adventurism and become an examiner to decide whether I am going to become 
his god of death in this combat, or he becomes mine.

shloka:
प्रहृष्टो वा हते रामे जनस्थानम् प्रयास्यसि |
मयि वा निहते रामम् संयुगाय प्रयास्यसि
translation:
"If I were to kill Rama you may gladly proceed to Janasthaana, else if Rama kills me then you can adventurously 
proceed against him for a combat." Thus Trishira spoke to Khara.

shloka:
खरः त्रिशिरसा तेन मृत्यु लोभात् प्रसादितः |
गच्छ्ह युध्य इति अनुज्ञातो राघव अभिमुखो ययौ
translation:
By that death-greedy demon Trishira, Khara is manoeuvred and Khara to him said 'begone... combat...' 
and thus permitted, Trishira proceeded to the forefront of Rama.

shloka:
त्रिशिराः तु रथेन एव वाजि युक्तेन भास्वता |
अभ्यद्रवत् रणे रामम् त्रि शृंग इव पर्वतः
translation:
Trishira with a lustrous chariot that is yoked with equally lustrous horses hurried towards Rama in 
that war, like a tri-peaked mountain, for they say, he is a tri-headed demon.

shloka:
शर धारा समूहान् स महामेघ इव उत्सृजन् |
व्यसृजत् सदृशम् नादम् जल आर्द्रस्य इव दुन्दुभेः
translation:
Discharging hosts of arrow-torrents like a hefty-arrow-cloud, he readily discharged a noise similar 
to the thudding drumbeat when a water-wet war-drum is beaten, rather than a blast from a heated drum.

shloka:
आगच्छ्हंतम् त्रिशिरसम् राक्षसम् प्रेक्ष्य राघवः |
धनुषा प्रतिजग्राह विधुन्वन् सायकान् शितान्
translation:
On seeing the oncoming of that demon Trishira, Raghava welcomed him by speedily winnowing smarting arrows 
from his bow.

shloka:
स संप्रहारः तुमुलो राम त्रिशिरसोः तदा |
संबभूव अतीव बलिनोः सिंह कुं~जरयोः इव
translation:
That grave and tumultuous encounter chanced between Rama and Trishira is like the extremely forceful 
encounter between a loin and an elephant.

shloka:
ततः त्रिशिरसा बाणैः ललाटे ताडितः त्रिभिः |
अमर्षी कुपितो रामः संरब्धम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Later when Trishira smote on the forehead of highly enraged Rama with three arrows, Rama's ire is intensified 
and he franticly said this to that demon.

shloka:
अहो विक्रम शूरस्य राक्षसस्य ईदृशम् बलम् |
पुष्पैः इव शरैः यस्य ललाटे अस्मि परिक्षतः
translation:
"Oho! What an energy of a triumphing adventurer is this! A demon with this sort of energy is adventuring 
me, whose arrows rap my forehead peripherally, like flowers!

shloka:
मम अपि प्रतिगृह्णीष्व शरान् चाप गुण च्युतान् |
एवम् उक्त्वा सुसंरब्धः शरान् आशीविष उपमान्
translation:
"Now you accept arrows plunging from the string of my bow..." saying thus, that infuriated Rama with 
his alacritous swiftness hit the chest of Trishira with fourteen arrows similar to venomous snakes. 
[3-27-13, 14a]

shloka: चतुर्भिः तुरगान् अस्य शरैः संनत पर्वाभिः
translation:
With four of his straight shooting arrows that have hook-like barbs, that resplendent Rama hewed down 
four of the speedy horses of Trishira's chariot. [3-27-14b, 15a]

shloka: अष्टभिः सायकैः सूतम् रथ उपस्थे न्यपातयत्
translation:
With eight arrows Rama felled the charioteer from his settle on the chariot, and with one arrow ripped 
off the high flying flag on that chariot. [3-27-15b, 16a]

shloka: ततो हत रथात् तस्मात् उत्पतंतम् निशाचरम्
translation:
When that nightwalker is vaulting from that smashed chariot Rama with his arrows tore his chest to shreds 
and he that Trishira became inert. [3-27-16b, 17a]

shloka: सायकैः च अप्रमेय आत्मा सामर्षः तस्य रक्षसः
translation:
And with three sharp and rapid arrows, and even with his own exasperation, Rama of inestimable aptitude 
rolled the three heads that demon. [3-27-17b, 18a]
