Kabandha while Lakshmana is hearing. [3-71-20b, 21a]

shloka: रावणेन हृता सीता मम भार्या यशस्विनी
translation:
"Ravana conveniently stole my illustrious wife when myself and my brother exited from Janasthaana... 
[3-71-21b, 22a]

shloka: नाम मात्रम् तु जानामि न रूपम् तस्य रक्षसः
translation:
"I only know his name but not the form of that demon... and we are unaware either of his stronghold 
or of his staying power... [3-71-22b, 23a]

shloka: शोक आर्तानाम् अनाथानाम् एवम् विपरिधावताम्
translation:
"It will be apt of you to show befitting mercy on us who are anguished by agony, running all over helter-skelter 
like unsheltered ones, and we who will be compliant for your restitution... [3-71-23b, 24a]

shloka: काष्ठानि आनीय भग्नानि काले शुष्काणि कुंजरैः
translation:
"Oh, brave Kabandha, on bringing dried up firewood that was rent at times by elephants, and on digging 
a large trench, we will incinerate you in it... [3-71-24b, 25a]

shloka: स त्वम् सीताम् समाचक्ष्व येन वा यत्र वा हृता
translation:
"Such as you are, if you actually know who stole Seetha, or whereto she is stolen, either... you clearly 
inform of her when incinerated, thus you will be rendering a most gracious deed to me, and to all concerned..." 
Thus Rama made clear of his case. [3-71-25b, 26a]

shloka: एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण वाक्यम् दनुः अनुत्तमम्
translation:
When he is said thus that expert articulator Kabandha replied Rama, who is also an expert enunciator, 
with expedient words. [3-71-26b, 27a]

shloka: दिव्यम् अस्ति न मे ज्ञानम् न अभिजानामि मैथिलीम्
translation:
"There is no divine knowledge to me as of now... nor I can identify Maithili... but when I am burnt 
I assume my own original divine form, and then I will be able tell about him, who will find her out... 
[3-71-27b, 28a]

shloka: यो अभिजानाति तद् रक्षः तद् वक्ष्ये राम तत् परम्
translation:
"With this unburnt body, oh, Rama, I indeed have no ability to discern anything, hence oh, lord, I will 
be able to speak about him who can familiarise you with that great mighty demon, by whom your Seetha 
is stolen, only after that incineration... [3-71-28b, 29]

shloka:
विज्ञानम् हि महत् भ्रष्टम् शाप दोषेण राघव |
स्वकृतेन मया प्राप्तम् रूपम् लोक विगर्हितम्
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, utterly distorted is my acumen, indeed, by the blemish of curse... and this form which 
is despicable to world has bechanced only because of my own antics...

shloka:
किम् तु यावत् न याति अस्तम् सविता श्रान्त वाहनः |
तावत् माम् अवटे क्षिप्त्वा दह राम यथा विधि
translation:
"Oh, Rama, soon you have to toss me into trench to burn me customarily, sooner than the Sun's going 
to Mt. Dusk when his horses are fatigued...

shloka:
दग्धः त्वया अहम् अवटे न्यायेन रघुनंदन |
वक्ष्यामि तम् महावीर यः तम् वेत्स्यति राक्षसम्
translation:
"Oh, Rama, the legatee of Raghu, when I am scripturally burnt by you in a trench, oh, great valiant 
Rama, for sure, I will tell of him, who can quiet fathom that demon...

shloka:
तेन सख्यम् च कर्तव्यम् न्याय्य वृत्तेन राघव |
कल्पयिष्यति ते प्रीतः साहाय्यम् लघु विक्रमः
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, you have to befriend him with an amicable comportment... and that valiantly alacritous 
one will be gladdened by the sequel of your friendship, and he will evolve a succour to you...

shloka:
न हि तस्य अस्ति अविज्ञातम् त्रिषु लोकेषु राघव |
सर्वान् परिवृतो लोकान् पुरा वै कारण अन्तरे
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, nothing is there in all the three worlds that is unfamiliar to him, for he circumnavigated 
all worlds once, in a different context...

shloka:
एवम् उक्तौ तु तौ वीरौ कबन्धेन नर ईश्वरौ |
गिरि प्रदरम् आसाद्य पावकम् विससर्जतुः
translation:
When Kabandha said that way, both those brave men and lords of people, on throwing the body of Kabandha 
into a mountain cleft and then embedded it with firewood.

shloka:
लक्ष्मणः तु महा उल्काभिः ज्वलिताभिः समन्ततः |
चिताम् आदीपयामास सा प्रजज्वाल सर्वतः
translation:
On his part Lakshmana started to torch that pyre with highly sparkling torches from all over, and even 
that pyre too suddenly blazed with blazes from all over.

shloka:
तत् शरीरम् कबन्धस्य घृत पिण्ड उपमम् महत् |
मेदसा पच्यमानस्य मन्दम् दहति पावकः
translation:
That massy body of Kabandha is full with fat and while it is being cooked, it is in simile with a massy 
gob of ghee. But the Fire had to stew that body tardily, though that stewed meat is Fire's favourite 
dish, because of that body's massiveness.

shloka:
स विधूय चिताम् आशु विधूमो अग्निर् इव उत्थितः |
अरजे वाससी बिभ्रत् मालाम् दिव्याम् महाबलः
translation:
In a trice that highly dynamic Kabandha zoomed up shoving off that pyre, and he is now attired in lily-white 
vestments and angelic garlands, and appeared like a fumeless fire.

shloka:
ततः चिताया वेगेन भास्वरो विरज अंबरः |
उत्पपात आशु संहृष्टः सर्व प्रत्यंग भूषणः
translation:
Then highly gladdened Kabandha jumped up onto sky from the pyre, and there he is irradiant with unsullied 
clothing, and fineries decorated on every limb.

shloka:
विमाने भास्वरे तिष्ठन् हंस युक्ते यशस् करे |
प्रभया च महातेजा दिशो दश विराजयन्
translation:
On going to firmament Kabandha is now seated in a dazzling celestial aircraft yoked with swans, which 
endows renown because it takes the occupants to the realms of Brahma, and sitting in that celestial 
aircraft he said this sentence to Rama, while his own great glimmer and glitter beamed forth in all 
ten quarters. [3-72-6, 7]

shloka: शृणु राघव तत्त्वेन यथा सीमाम् अवाप्स्यसि
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, how you will regain Seetha, that you listen from me in its essence... oh, Rama, by which 
and which analyses everything will be analysed, six of such ideations are available in this world... 
and when a person is touched down by a spell of nemeses, he shall adore one who is equally in such spell 
of nemesis... [3-72-7b, 8]

shloka:
दश आभाग गतो हीनः त्वम् राम सह लक्ष्मणः |
यत् कृते व्यसनम् प्राप्तम् त्वया दार प्रधर्षणम्
translation:
"Oh, Rama, you along with Lakshmana went into a spell of nemesis, and thus you have become an underprivileged 
one, and that spell alone has obtained you this dire straits, in the form of abducting your wife...

shloka:
तत् अवश्यम् त्वया कार्यः स सुहृत् सुहृदाम् वर |
अकृत्वा न हि ते सिद्धिम् अहम् पश्यामि चिन्तयन्
translation:
"Oh, best among kind-hearted ones, thereby you have to certainly befriend such a soul in similar dire 
straits... however deeply I may think, I am not able to perceive your accomplishment if you do not befriended 
with such a soul...

shloka:
श्रूयताम् राम वक्ष्यामि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः |
भ्रात्रा निरस्तः क्रुद्धेन वालिना शक्र सूनुना
translation:
"Oh, Rama, listen what I tell... a vanara is there by name Sugreeva, who is vengefully reneged by his 
brother Vali, the son of Indra...

shloka:
ऋष्यमूके गिरि वरे पंपा पर्यन्त शोभिते |
निवसति आत्मवान् वीरः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
translation:
"That self-respectful valiant Sugreeva is living on the Mt. Rishyamuka, a best mountain available in 
the lambent fringes of Pampa Lake, along with four other vanara-s.

shloka:
वानरेन्द्रो महावीर्यः तेजोवान् अमित प्रभः |
सत्य संधो विनीतः च धृतिमान् मतिमान् महान्
translation:
"He that Sugreeva is a masterful one among vanara-s, highly mettlesome, self-resplendent, and illimitable 
is his self-radiance... and he is also truth-bound and culture-bound... a mastermind, master-hand and 
a taskmaster...

shloka:
दक्षः प्रगल्भो द्युतिमान् महा बल पराक्रमः |
भ्राता विवासितो वीर राज्य हेतो महात्मना
translation:
"He is a capable adventurer, a courageous exploiter and incomparable one in intrepidity and a brave 
one in incursions, and his personality will be coruscating ever and anon, for he is the son of Sun-god... 
but he is banished by his self-conceited brother owing to the reasons of kingdom...

shloka:
स ते सहायो मित्रम् च सीतायाः परिमार्गणे |
भविष्यति हि ते राम मा च शोके मनः कृधाः
translation:
"Oh, Rama, he will be your associate and an aid in searching for Seetha, and he conducts himself in 
your wellbeing, hence let not your heart yield to agony...

shloka:
भवितव्यम् हि यत् च अपि न तत् शक्यम् इह अन्यथा |
कर्तुम् इक्ष्वाकु शार्दूल कालो हि दुर्रक्रमः
translation:
"Oh, tigerly Ikshvaaku, further nothing can be countermanded in this world which is indeed ineluctable, 
and it is impossible to countervail against Time, isn't it...

shloka:
गच्छ शीघ्रम् इतो वीर सुग्रीवम् तम् महाबलम् |
वयस्यम् तम् कुरु क्षिप्रम् इतो गत्वा अद्य राघव
translation:
"Oh, bold one, you go straight from here to that great mighty Sugreeva, and oh, Raghava, on going from 
here now and promptly you fraternise with Sugreeva... and to not to bode any ill of unfriendliness among 
you two, you make him a friend before blazing Fire, making that Fire as an Attestor of your friendship... 
[3-72-17, 18a]

shloka: न च ते सो अवमन्तव्यः सुग्रीवो वानर अधिपः
translation:
"You shall not look down on that lord of monkeys taking him as a lowly simian, why because that Sugreeva 
is a valiant one, a guise changing wizard and presently he is in the need of a bolsterer, and if you 
render help he will be obligated to you for ever... [3-72-18b, 19]

shloka: शक्तौ हि अद्य युवाम् कर्तुम् कार्यम् तस्य चिकीर्षितम्
translation:
"Now you two are capable enough to effectuate the desired task of Sugreeva, isn't it... whether his 
own purpose is achieved through you or not, he will effectuate your task... [3-72-19b, 20a]

shloka: स ऋक्षरजसः पुत्रः पंपाम् अटति शन्कितः
translation:
"Sugreeva is the son of Riksharaja, and the direct son of the Sun, but Vali trespassed against him. 
Wary of Vali's onslaughts Sugreeva is wandering around Pampa... [3-72-20b, 21a]

shloka: संनिधाय आयुधम् क्षिप्रम् ऋष्यमूक आलयम् कपिम्
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, right away and candidly you make that monkey Sugreeva, a wanderer in the forest, sheltering 
himself on Mt. Rishyamuka, as a friend of yours taking an oath on your weapon besides the Fire-witness... 
[3-72-21b, 22a]

shloka: स हि स्थानानि सर्वाणि कार्त्स्न्येन कपि कुंजरः
translation:
"With his expertise that straightforward monkey Sugreeva is indeed conversant with all of the strongholds 
of anthropophagite demons in the world in their entirety... [3-72-22b, 23a]

shloka: न तस्य अविदितम् लोके किंचित् अस्ति हि राघव
translation:
"Oh, enemy-subjugator Rama, as far as the thousand rayed sun manifestly irradiates the world, oh, Raghava, 
thus far, nothing in the least is unfamiliar to him, isn't it... [3-72-23b, 24a]

shloka: स नदीः विपुलान् शैलान् गिरि दुर्गाणि कंदरान्
translation:
"He makes the monkeys to purposefully rake over the expansive rivers, extensive mountains and their 
impassable cliffs and caves in locating your wife... [3-72-24b, 25a]

shloka: वानरान् च महाकायान् प्रेषयिष्यति राघव
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, he expedites giant bodied monkeys in all directions to search for her, who is agonised 
by your parting, and he quests after the residence of Ravana for that comely lady Maithili... [3-72-25b, 
26]

shloka:
स मेरु शृंग अग्र गताम् अनिंदिताम्
प्रविश्य पाताल तले अपि वा आश्रिताम् |
प्लवंगमानाम् ऋषभः तव प्रियाम्
निहत्य रक्षांसि पुनः प्रदास्यति
translation:
"Whether that unreprovable ladylove of yours, Seetha, is located on the tops of Mt. Meru's peaks, or 
abiding on the planes of nadir of the earth, he that defiant one among fly-jumpers, Sugreeva, on entering 
there and annihilating the demons, he again bestows Seetha to you..." So Kabandha continued his advise 
to Rama regarding Sugreeva.

shloka:
दर्शयित्वा रामाय सीतायाः प्रैमार्गने |
वाक्यम् अन्वर्थम् अर्थज्ञः कबंधः पुनः अब्रवीत्
translation:
On showing a concept for questing after Seetha that context-sensitive Kabandha further spoke this sentence 
which is inclusive of right concept to Rama.

shloka:
एष राम शिवः पंथा यत्र एते पुष्पिता द्रुमाः |
प्रतीचीम् दिशम् आश्रित्य प्रकाशन्ते मनो रमाः
translation:
"Oh, Rama, have a recourse to westward, and where the trees of Rose-apple, Priyaala, Jackfruit, Plaksha, 
Banyan, Tinduka, Pipal, Karnikara, Mango, and others... and even trees like Dhanva, Naaga, Tilaka, Naktamaala, 
blue Ashoka, Kadamba, Karaviira, Agnimukha, Ashoka, red-sandalwood trees and Neem trees will be heart-pleasingly 
shining forth in full blossom, that alone is an optimistic course for you. [3-73-2, 3, 4, 5a]

shloka: तान् आरुह्य अथवा भूमौ पातयित्वा च तान् बलात्
translation:
"On shinning up those trees, or else, even on forcefully pelting those fruits down onto ground, then 
you may pelt over, devouring those ambrosial fruits... [3-73-5b, 6a]

shloka: तत् अतिक्रम्य काकुत्स्थ वनम् पुषित पादपम्
translation:
"On crossing over that parkland, oh, Kakutstha, another parkland with blossomy flowers is there, which 
replicates the heavenly Nandana gardens, and a replica of North-Kuru, an all-endowing province... [3-73-6b, 
7a]

shloka: सर्व काल फला यत्र पादपा मधुर स्रवाः
translation:
"Wherein the trees fruit all-season fruits that transude nectar, why fruits alone, in that parkland 
all seasons are coeval, as they will be in Caitraratha, the celestial gardens of Kubera... [3-73-7b, 
8a]

shloka: फल भार नताः तत्र महा विटप धारिणः
translation:
"In there, the trees bear enormous branches which will be crouching under the weight of their own fruits, 
and everywhere such trees will be shining forth like shiny clouds and shining mountains... [3-73-8b, 
9a]

shloka: तान् आरुह्य अथवा भूमौ पातैत्वा यथा सुखम्
translation:
"Let Lakshmana present those ambrosial fruits to you either by climbing up those trees to pluck them, 
or else by pelting them to ground, according to his convenience... [3-73-9b-10a]

shloka: चङ्क्रमंतौ वरान् शैलान् शैलात् शैलम् वनात् वनम्
translation:
"Peregrinating finest places by trekking from mountain to mountain, from forest to forest, oh, valorous 
ones, you will trek to an auspicious lotus-lake, called Pampa... [3-73-10b, 11a]

shloka: अशर्कराम् अविभ्रंशाम् सम तीर्थम् अशैवलाम्
translation:
"It is un-pebbly, un-slippery, un-weedy thereabouts, oh, Rama, equal are its quaysides and emersed are 
its sandbanks, red and blue lotuses beautify that Pampa Lake... [3-73-11b, 12a]

shloka: तत्र हंसाः प्लवाः क्रौङ्चाः कुरराः चैव राघव
translation:
"There the indwellers of Pampa Lake's waters, oh, Raghava, namely the swans, cranes, Kraunca-s and fish-hawks 
will be letting out peeps in tuneful voice... [3-73-12a, 13b]

shloka: न उद्विजन्ते नरान् दृष्ट्वा वधस्य अकोविदाः शुभाः
translation:
"Thereabout birds will be unflustered on seeing humans, because they are artless to avoid hunting, because 
none kills them, and you may savour them because those birds will be best and burley, similar to ghee-gobs... 
[3-73-13b, 14a]

shloka: रोहितान् वक्र तुण्डान् च नल मीनान् च राघव
translation:
"Oh, Rama in that Pampa Lake there are best fishes, red-carps, and blunt-snouted small porpoises, and 
a sort of sprats, which are neither scraggy, nor with many fish-bones. Lakshmana will reverentially 
offer them to you on skewering them with arrow, and on broiling them on iron rod of arrow after descaling 
and de-finning them. [3-73-14b, 15, 16a]

shloka:
पद्म गन्धि शिवम् वारि सुख शीतम् अनामयम् |
उद्धृत्य स तदा अक्लिष्टम् रूप्य स्फटिक सन्निभम्
translation:
"While you eat those fishes to satiety, Lakshmana will offer you the water of Pampa Lake, which will 
be in the bunches of flowers of that lake, and which will be lotus-scented, pellucid, comfortably cool, 
shiny like silver and crystal, uncontaminated and that way pristine, by lifting it up that water with 
lotus leaf, making that leaf a stoup-like basin... [3-73-16b, 17, 18a]

shloka: स्थूलान् गिरि गुहा शय्यान् वानरान् वन चारिणः
translation:
"Oh, best one among men Rama, at Pampa you will see best shaped Vanara-s who have their bunk bed in 
mountain caves, and who will be coming nearby the lake, greedy as they are for water, and those forest 
movers will be moving about in evening time of the day, bellowing like bulls... oh, Rama, Lakshmana 
will show them to you... [3-73-18b, 19, 20a]

shloka: साय अह्ने विचरन् राम विटपीन् माल्य धारिणः
translation:
"While roving in the evenings, oh, Rama, should you see the serenely water of Pampa, with her trees 
garlanded with their own blooms and twigs, you will discard your own dolour... [3-73-20b, 21a]

shloka: सु मनोभिः चितान् तत्र तिलकान् नक्त मालकान्
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, there you will see highly delightful and wide-ranging trees like Tilaka and Naktamaala, 
and fully bloomed red and blue lotuses, as well... [3-73-21b, 22a]

shloka: न तानि कश्चित् माल्यानि तत्र आरोपयिता नरः
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, there is none someone to inwreathe the garlands of those flowers, and indeed, they neither 
dry up, nor drop down... [3-73-22b, 23a]

shloka: मतंग शिष्याः तत्र आसन् ऋषयः सुसमाहितः
translation:
"Erst there were self-collected sages, the disciples of Sage Matanga, and at one time while they were 
bringing the forest produce as ritual paraphernalia, they were much wearied by its weight and they were 
sweating... and all of those earthbound strings of sweat-drops that quickly dropped from their bodies 
were wafted by air onto trees, and on them they reoccurred as strings of flowers, by the merit of the 
ascesis of those sages... oh, Raghava, since those flowers have emerged from sweat-drops, they are imperishable, 
indeed... [3-73-23b, 24, 25]

shloka:
तेषाम् गतानाम् अद्य अपि दृश्यते परिचारिणी |
श्रमणी शबरी नाम काकुत्स्थ चिर जीविनी
translation:
"Oh, Rama of Kakutstha, albeit the passing of those sages through the pearly gates, their maidservant, 
a long-lived one and an anchoress, named Shabari, can be seen there, even today...

shloka:
त्वाम् तु धर्मे स्थिता नित्यम् सर्व भूत नमस्कृतम् |
दृष्ट्वा देव उपमम् राम स्वर्ग लोकम् गमिष्यति
translation:
"Oh, Rama, she who always stands by probity will depart to the sphere of heaven, on attending to you, 
for you are the referent to god, and a reverent for one and all...

shloka:
ततः तत् राम पंपायाः तीरम् आश्रित्य पश्चिमम् |
आश्रम स्थानम् अतुलम् गुह्यम् काकुत्स्थ पश्यसि
translation:
"Oh, Rama, thereafter on your taking course to that western bank of Pampa Lake, oh, Kakutstha, there 
you will see the unequalled and arcane place of hermitage of sage Matanga...

shloka:
न तत्र आक्रमितुम् नागाः शक्नुवन्ति तद् आश्रमे |
ऋषेः तस्य मतंगस्य विधानात् तत् च काननम्
translation:
"Sage Matanga so methodised that woodland, where even the elephants are rendered incapable to trespass 
in that hermitage of sage Matanga disturbing its serenity...

shloka:
मातंग वनम् इति एव विश्रुतम् रघुनंदन |
तस्मिन् नंदन संकाशे देव अरण्य उपमे वने
translation:
"Oh, the legatee of Raghu, that woodland which in simile is like a godly forest, similar to the heavenly 
Nandana gardens, overspread with divers birds is renowned as 'Matanga woodland', and oh, Rama, you will 
take delight rejoicingly in that woodland... [3-73-30, 31a]

shloka: ऋष्यमूकः तु पंपायाः पुरस्तात् पुष्पित द्रुमः
translation:
"In front of Pampa there is a bountiful but an unclimbable mountain is there with trees in full blossom, 
which is well-protected by baby elephants, and which in earlier times was purposefully created by Brahma, 
and that alone is Mt. Rishyamuka... [3-73-31b, 32]

shloka:
शयानः पुरुषो राम तस्य शैलस्य मूर्धनि |
यत् स्वप्ने लभते वित्तम् तत् प्रबुद्धो अधिगच्छति
translation:
"And should a man sleep on the heights of that mountain, and should he dream of gaining some riches 
in that sleep, he gains that much when he wakes up...

shloka:
यः तु एनम् विषम आचारः पाप कर्मा अधिरोहति |
तत्र एव प्रहरन्ति एनम् सुप्तम् आदाय राक्षसाः
translation:
"But he who is diabolic in his deportment and devilish in comportment, climbs that and hopes to sleep 
soundly, demons capture him while he is in sleep, and rough him up to death, there itself...

shloka:
तत्र अपि शिशु नागानाम् आक्रंदः श्रूयते महान् |
क्रीडताम् राम पंपायाम् मतंग आश्रम वासिनाम्
translation:
"Oh, Rama, there the blaring trumpet-blasts of baby elephants that amuse themselves at Lake Pampa, and 
of those that are the indwellers of Matanga hermitage, even there on Mt. Rishyamuka are audible...

shloka:
सिक्ता रुधिर धाराभिः संहत्य परम द्विपाः |
प्रचरन्ति पृथक् कीर्णा मेघ वर्णाः तरस्विनः
translation:
"The mighty and massy dark-cloud coloured elephants will be hitting head-on, and with dripping blood 
streams on their jumbo heads and temples, they disperse and move about separately, only to come together 
for yet another round of head-to-head collision...

shloka:
ते तत्र पीत्वा पानीयम् विमलम् चारु शोभनम् |
अत्यन्त सुख संस्पर्शम् सर्व गन्ध समन्वितम्
translation:
"There the elephants are quenched on drinking water of Pampa Lake, that is daintily clean, and neatly 
clear, springlike for touch, and in which all scents of flowers of that lake are included, and then 
they will be collectively re-entering the forests, for they are forest ranging elephants... [3-73-37, 
38a]

shloka: ऋक्षाम् च द्विपिनः चैव नील कोमलक प्रभान्
translation:
"On your seeing the bears, also thus the tigers and even the exultant sapphire-blue Rurus with black 
stripes there, you will discard your distress... [3-73-38b, 39a]

shloka: राम तस्य तु शैलस्य महती शोभते गुहा
translation:
"But oh, Rama, a cavernous cave lidded with a boulder stone outshines on that mountain, and oh, Kakutstha, 
problematic is an entry into it... [3-73-39b, 40a]

shloka: तस्या गुहायाः प्राक् द्वारे महान् शीत उदको ह्रदः
translation:
"On its right at its eastern opening a delightful lake with highly coolant waters is there, fringed 
with divers trees and fraught with numerous tubers and fruits... [3-73-40b, 41a]

shloka: तस्याम् वसति सुग्रीवः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
translation:
"Sugreeva dwells in that cave along with four other monkeys, and at times he will be available on the 
peaks of that mountain, even on its bluffs and cliffs, for he is a terrified monkey..." Thus Kabandha 
informed them. [3-73-41b, 42a]

shloka: कबंधः तु अनुशास्य एवम् तौ उभौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
That impressive Kabandha adorned with divine garlands and abiding in sky scintillating with the grandeur 
of the dazzle of the sun has bidden both the brothers, Rama and Lakshmana thus, awaited a bid adieu 
from them. [3-73-42b, 43a]

shloka: तम् तु ख स्थम् महाभागम् कबंधम् राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
Rama and Lakshmana who started off on their peregrination said this sentence to that highly providential 
Kabandha, who is temporising in the sky in their vicinity, thus as "you may proceed..." [3-73-43b, 44a]

shloka: गम्यताम् कार्य सिद्धि अर्थम् इति तौ अब्रवीत् च सः
translation:
On getting the orders for departure from those two brothers who are highly gladdened at the information 
given by Kabandha, he that Kabandha who is ready to exit, he further said to them thus, "proceed for 
the purpose of achieving your task..." [3-73-44b, 45]

shloka:
स तत् कबंधः प्रतिपद्य रूपम्
वृतः श्रिया भास्कर सर्व देहः |
निदर्शयन् रामम् अवेक्ष्य ख स्थः
सख्यम् कुरुष्व इति तदा अभ्युवाच
translation:
Kabandha who redeemed his divine form has now got an aureole around him, and while irradiance is tamping 
whole of his mien, he moved further up on sky and reappeared. And staying in the sky he pointed out 
at the side of Mt. Rishyamuka, and then he reiterated, "you befriend Sugreeva..."and then he vanished.

shloka:
तौ कबन्धेन तम् मार्गम् पम्पाया दर्शितम् वने |
आतस्थतुः दिशम् गृह्य प्रतीचीम् नृ वर आत्मजौ
translation:
Both the sons of that best king Dasharatha, on taking up westerly path in that forest travelled on the 
passage to Pampa as shown by Kabandha.

shloka:
तौ शैलेषु आचित अनेकान् क्षौद्र कल्प फल द्रुमान् |
वीक्षन्तौ जग्मतुः द्रष्टुम् सुग्रीवम् राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
Those two, Rama and Lakshmana, while seeing several of the ticketed trees on mountains which have nectarous 
fruits on them moved forward to see Sugreeva.

shloka:
कृत्वा च शैल पृष्ठे तु तौ वासम् रघु नन्दनौ |
पंपायाः पश्चिमम् तीरम् राघवौ उपतस्थतुः
translation:
Those two legatees of Raghu on making a sojourn on the mountaintop, they the Raghava-s drew nigh of 
the moorland on the westward of Pampa Lake.

shloka:
तौ पुष्करिण्याः पंपायाः तीरम् आसाद्य पश्चिमम् |
अपश्यताम् ततः तत्र शबर्या रम्यम् आश्रमम्
translation:
Then on getting at the westward moorland of that lotus-lake Pampa, there those two have spotted the 
idyllic hermitage of Shabari.

shloka:
तौ तम् आश्रमम् आसाद्य द्रुमैः बहुभिः आवृतम् |
सु रम्यम् अभिवीक्षन्तौ शबरीम् अभ्युपेयतुः
translation:
On getting at that hermitage and on perusing at that picturesque environ that is wreathed round with 
several picturesque trees, those two came nigh of Shabari.

shloka:
तौ दृष्ट्वा तु तदा सिद्धा समुत्थाय कृतांजलिः |
पादौ जग्राह रामस्य लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः
translation:
On seeing them that sublimated yogi Shabari instinctively made palm-fold, got up imperatively, and then 
she braced the feet of Rama, and even that of sagacious Lakshmana, impressively.

shloka:
पाद्यम् आचमनीयम् च सर्वम् प्रददात् यथा विधि |
ताम् उवाच ततो रामः श्रमणीम् धर्म संस्थिताम्
translation:
She gave them water for feet-wash and mouthwash, and other viands customarily affordable to visitants, 
and then Rama asked after that anchoress who is unflinchingly abiding in her duty.

shloka:
कच्चित् ते निर्जिता विघ्नाः कच्चित् ते वर्धते तपः |
कच्चित् ते नियतः कोप आहारः च तपोधने
translation:
"Oh, ascetically wealthy lady, perchance your deterrents in ascesis are completely overcome, somehow... 
your ascetic practises culminating, someway... your annoyances and ailments are adjusted, somewhat... 
isn't it!

shloka:
कच्चित् ते नियमाः प्राप्ताः कच्चित् ते मनसः सुखम् |
कच्चित् ते गुरु शुश्रूषा सफला चारु भाषिणि
translation:
"Oh, suave speaker, mayhap your sacred commitments are achieved, anywise... appeased is your self, anyway... 
and your subservience to your mentors brought to fruition, perchance... isn't it!" Thus Rama enquired 
with Shabari.

shloka:
रामेण तापसी पृष्ठा सा सिद्धा सिद्ध सम्मता |
शशंस शबरी वृद्धा रामाय प्रति अवस्थिता
translation:
When Rama asked her in this way she that Shabari who is a senescent anchoress, sublimated yogin and 
an adherent to the sublimated yogis of higher rank, informed Rama remaining in his vis-�-vis.

shloka:
अद्य प्राप्ता तपः सिद्धिः तव संदर्शनात् मया |
अद्य मे सफलम् जन्म गुरवः च सुपूजिताः
translation:
"Just now, on your pleasing manifestation before me my ascesis is accomplished, and now only my birth 
is fructified, and now only my subservience to my mentors is well hallowed...

shloka:
अद्य मे सफलम् तप्तम् स्वर्गः चैव भविष्यति |
त्वयि देव वरे राम पूजिते पुरुषर्षभ
translation:
"Oh, best one among men, now all my ascesis is fructified when I personally worshiped you, who are none 
other than the best god among gods, thus the heaven will also be there for me...

shloka:
तव अहम् चक्षुषा सौम्य पूता सौम्येन मानद |
गमिष्याम्यक्षयांलोकांस्वत्प्रसादादरिन्दम - यद्वा -
गमिष्यामि 
अक्षयान् लोकान् त्वत् प्रसादात् अरिंदम
translation:
"Oh, kind one, your blessed sight has sanctified me... and oh, endower of respect, by your beneficence 
I wish to go to those returnless worlds because I have subjugated those enemies of yours, viz.,ari SaD varga-sin me, and I think my prayer to you is justified because 
you are a subjugator of such enemies...

shloka:
चित्रकूटम् त्वयि प्राप्ते विमानैः अतुल प्रभैः |
इतः ते दिवम् आरूढा यान् अहम् पर्यचारिषम्
translation:
"Divine aircrafts of unequalled refulgence have lifted those disciples of Sage Matanga in whose tendance 
I was, to welkin on your arriving at Chitrakuta...

shloka:
तैः च अहम् उक्ता धर्म ज्ञैः महाभागैः महर्षिभिः |
आगमिष्यति ते रामः सु पुण्यम् इमम् आश्रमम्
translation:
"Those knowers of probity, highly providential, and eminent-saints have told me, 'Rama will come to 
this highly blest hermitage of yours along with Soumitri... and you have to cordially welcome them as 
your guests, and on your seeing him you will go to best worlds, where merit remains undiminished...' 
[3-74-15, 16]

shloka:
एवम् उक्ता महाभागैः तदा अहम् पुरुषर्षभ |
मया तु विविधम् वन्यम् संचितम् पुरुषर्षभ
translation:
"Oh, best one among men Rama, thus I was told by those highly providential sages, oh, best one among 
men, oh, manly tiger, and I have gleaned various forest fruits and eatables that occur on the moorlands 
of Pampa Lake for your sake..." So said Shabari to Rama.

shloka: एवम् उक्तः स धर्मात्मा शबर्या शबरीम् इदम्
translation:
When that graceful souled Rama is addressed thus by Shabari, he that Raghava enquiringly said this to 
that Shabari who is never ever debarred from esoteric knowledge and gnosis. [3-74-18b, 19a]

shloka: दनोः सकाशात् तत्त्वेन प्रभावम् ते महात्मनः
translation:
"Your and your preceptors' effectiveness is heard in effect from the wraith of the great souled Danu's 
son, Kabandha, and if you feel showing it like I wish to clearly see it, personally..." Thus Rama asked 
her to show hermitage. [3-74-19b, 20a]

shloka: एतत् तु वचनम् श्रुत्वा राम वक्त्रात् विनिःसृतम्
translation: On hearing those words voiced by Rama, Shabari started to show that unique woodland to both of them.

shloka: पश्य मेघ घन प्रख्यम् मृग पक्षि समाकुलम्
translation:
"Oh, Rama the delight of Raghu's lineage... this one comparable to a crammed cloud that would be ever 
ready to yield much cherished cloudbursts, and compacted with animals and birds that are ever ready 
to enjoy seasonable rains, is that hermitage to which you have come, that way this woodland is well 
known as Matanga, meaning a cloud, or an elephant, or an elephantine cloud that showers blessings on 
all... and oh, highly resplendent Rama, you may see this nest, snuggery, where those contemplative souls, 
my teachers, used to conduct oblations into the Ritual-fires, orienting and worshipping them with Vedic 
hymns... [3-74-21b, 22]

shloka:
इयम् प्रत्यक् स्थली वेदी यत्र ते मे सुसत्कृताः |
पुष्प उपहारम् कुर्वन्ति श्रमात् उद् वेपिभिः करैः
translation:
"Where those great sages that are highly revered by me used to offer flowers with their extremely doddery 
hands in the worship the Altar of Fire, this alone is that Altar of Fire raised at western end...

shloka:
तेषाम् तपः प्रभावेन पश्य अद्य अपि रघूत्तम |
द्योतयन्ति दिशः सर्वाः श्रिया वेद्यः अतुल प्रभाः
translation:
"Oh, best one from Raghu-s, by the efficacy of the ascesis of my teachers these Altars of Fire are with 
incomparable irradiance, and even now they are irradiating all of the directions with solemnity... see 
them...

shloka:
अशक्नुवद्भिस्तैर्गन्तुमुपवासश्रमालसैः - यद्वा -
अशक्नुवद्भिः तैः गन्तुम् उपवास श्रम आलसैः |
चिन्तिते 
अभ्यागतान् पश्य समेतान् सप्त सागरान्
translation:
"Enervated by dieting and straining they were incapable to go for sea bathing, and just at their thought 
process all the seven seas came close by, in coalescence... see them...

shloka:
कृत अभिषेकैः तैः न्यस्ता वल्कलाः पादपेषु इह |
अद्य अपि न विशुष्यन्ति प्रदेशे रघुनंदन
translation:
"On performing holy baths those sages have spread their jute cloths on those trees with their own doddering 
hands here at this place and oh, Raghu's legatee, those cloths did not dry even now by the touch of 
their hands...

shloka:
देव कार्याणि कुर्वद्भिः यानि इमानि कृतानि वै |
पुष्पैः कुवलयैः सार्थम् म्लानत्वम् न तु यान्ति वै
translation:
"Which garlands they have knotted together with black-lotuses and other flowers while they were worshiping 
gods, these are really those garlands, and indeed there is no discolouration to them...

shloka:
कृत्स्नम् वनम् इदम् दृष्टम् श्रोतव्यम् च श्रुतम् त्वया |
तत् इच्छामि अभ्यनुज्ञाता त्यक्ष्यामि एतत् 
कलेवरम्
translation:
"You have seen what is seeable and you have listened what is listenable of this woodland in its entirety... 
thereby I wish to become a permittee, where you alone are my permitter, as I wish to castaway this sheathe 
of soul, called my body... to make that soul to move nigh of my teachers feet...

shloka:
तेषाम् इच्छामि अहम् गन्तुम् समीपम् भावित आत्मनाम् |
मुनीनाम् आश्रमो येषाम् अहम् च परिचारिणी
translation:
"Of which sages this hermitage is, and of which sages I am also a maidservant, I soulfully go the proximity 
of those contemplative souls..." Thus, she appealed to Rama.

shloka:
धर्मिष्ठम् तु वचः श्रुत्वा राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः |
प्रहर्सम् अतुलम् लेभे आश्चर्यम् इदम् च अब्रवीत्
translation:
Rama on hearing those duty-congruous words of Shabari along with Lakshmana, obtained a uniquely high 
rejoice and he also said, "astonishing is this..."

shloka:
ताम् उवाच ततो रामः शबरी संश्रित व्रताम् |
अर्चितो अहम् त्वया भद्रे गच्छ कामम् यथा सुखम्
translation:
Then Rama spoke to that Shabari who is firmed up in her faith towards her masters, "oh, saintly lady, 
you treated me with deference... thus may go to your cherished worlds, where you can solace yourself 
with your masters...

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्ता जटिला चीर कृष्ण अजिन अंबरा |
अनुज्ञाता तु रामेण हुत्वा आत्मानम् हुत अशने
translation:
Thus that way said by Rama in consent, she who is wearing tufty-matted hair, jute-cloths, and deerskin 
as her clothing, she offered herself as an oblation into Ritual-fire, and then like a flaring fire, 
she went to heaven alone. [3-74-32, 33a]

shloka: दिव्यम् आभरण संयुक्ता दिव्य माल्य अनुलेपना
translation:
Now she appeared as an angle bejewelled with angelic ornaments, wearing angle's wraparound and angelical 
flowery tassels, and bedaubed with suchlike cosmetics, and as with the scintillations of electric sparks 
she scintillated that province. [3-74-33b, 34]

shloka:
यत्र ते सुकृत आत्मानो विहरन्ति महर्षयः |
तत् पुण्यम् शबरी स्थानम् जगाम आत्म समाधिना
translation:
Shabari who is a perfect yogin with perfected meditative concentration, now went to that sanctum locus 
where the blest souls of those sublime sages, namely her masters, saunter.

shloka:
दिवम् तु तस्याम् यातायाम् शबर्याम् स्वेन तेजसा |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा चिन्तयामास राघवः
translation:
While Shabari ascended to heaven with her own divine self-resplendence, Raghava who is with Lakshmana 
started to cogitate over the magnificence of Matanga disciples.

shloka:
चिंतयित्वा तु धर्मात्मा प्रभावम् तम् महात्मनाम् |
हित कारिणम् एक अग्रम् लक्ष्मणम् राघवो अब्रवीत्
translation:
That noble-souled Raghava on thinking about the efficacy of the disciples of Matanga, said to Lakshmana, 
who is the maintainer of Rama's well being, and who is thinking single-mindedly.

shloka:
दृष्टो मया आश्रमः सौम्य बहु आश्चर्यः कृत आत्मनाम् |
विश्वस्त मृग शार्दूलो नाना विहग सेवितः
translation:
"I have seen a highly astounding hermitage of self-controlled sages, oh, gentle Lakshmana, in which 
the deer and tigers are at home, and which is adored by divers birds...

shloka:
सप्तानाम् च समुद्राणाम् तेषाम् तीर्थेषु लक्ष्मण |
उपस्पृष्टम् च विधिवत् पितरः च अपि तर्पिताः
translation:
"Oh, Lakshmana, holy is our taking a bath in this holy Pampa Lake, for it is formed by the waters of 
seven seas, and even holier is our oblation of this holy waters to manes...

shloka:
प्रणष्टम् अशुभम् यत् नः कल्याणम् समुपस्थितम् |
तेन तु एतत् प्रहृष्टम् मे मनो लक्ष्मण संप्रति
translation:
"What that was unpropitious for us is completely abated by our holy bath and holy oblations, oh, Lakshmana, 
propitiousness is standing en face us, thereby presently this heart of mine is highly gladdening... 
oh, lion-like man, indeed, heart alone hatches hope... [3-75-5, 6a]

shloka: तत् आगच्छ गमिष्यावः पंपाम् ताम् प्रिय दर्शनाम्
translation:
"Thereby, where Mt. Rishyamuka is beaming forth at its nearby, on which that right minded son of the 
Sun, Sugreeva, is living along with four other vanara-s, always frightened by the fear from Vali, we 
will go to her, to that spectacular Lake Pampa, come on, Lakshmana... [3-75-6b, 7, 8a]

shloka: अहम् त्वरे च तम् द्रष्टुम् सुग्रीवम् वानरर्षभम्
translation:
"I am also hasty to see that best one among vanara-s, Sugreeva, for my enterprise called search for 
Seetha is under his aegis, isn't it... [3-75-8b, 9a]

shloka: इति ब्रुवाणम् तम् वीरम् सौमित्रिः इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
To that brave Rama who is speaking thus, Soumitri said this, " my heart too is hastening me, let us 
go there promptly..." [3-75-9b, 10a]

shloka: आश्रमात् तु ततः तस्मात् निष्क्रम्य स विशाम् पतिः
translation:
Then that Lord of People and Lord of Nature on exiting from that hermitage, he then came nigh of Lake 
Pampa along with Lakshmana. [3-75-10b, 11a]

shloka: समीक्षमाणः पुष्प आढ्यम् सर्वतो विपुल द्रुमम्
translation:
Rama on scrutinising that rosy woodland in which everywhere there are outsized and diverse trees that 
are thickset with flowers, and different lakes loaded with the trilling birds like plovers, peacocks, 
waterfowls and suchlike, with which that woodland itself is trilling in much ado, became impassioned 
as he is instantly rendered thus by Love-god, and thus that Rama went towards that lovely Lake Pampa. 
[3-75-11b, 12, 13]

shloka:
स ताम् आसाद्य वै रामो दूरात् पानीय वाहिनीम् |
मतंग सरसम् नाम ह्रदम् समवगाहत
translation:
Rama spotted Pampa Lake from a distance which is plethoric with water, but entered into a lake called 
Matanga Lake on his way to Pampa...

shloka:
तत्र जग्मतुः अव्यग्रौ राघवौ हि समाहितौ |
स तु शोक समाविष्टो रामो दशरथात्मजः
translation:
Though both Raghava-s came there composedly and dispassionately, but Rama, the son of Dasharatha, is 
ensorcelled by anguish on seeing a ladylike lake Pampa.

shloka:
विवेश नलिनीम् रम्याम् पंकजैः च समावृताम् |
तिलकाशोकपुंनागबकुलोद्दालकाशिनीम् - यद्वा -
तिलक अशोक 
पुन्नाग बकुल उद्दाल काशिनीम्
translation:
Rama entered the area of that beautiful lake which is beaming forth with lotuses hemming in from inside, 
and trees like Tilaka, Ashoka, Punnaga, Bakula, Uddala, are hemming it from outside.

shloka:
रम्य उपवन संबाधाम् पद्म संपीडित उदकाम् |
स्फटिक उपम तोय आढ्याम् श्लक्ष्ण वालुक संतताम्
translation:
That lake is huddled with delightful fringe lands and lotuses squeeze it from within, and its water 
is plethoric and crystalline, and its sand is softish all over.

shloka:
मत्स्य कच्छप संबाधाम् तीरस्थ द्रुम शोभिताम् |
सखीभिः इव संयुक्ताम् लताभिः अनुवेष्टिताम्
translation:
That lake is beautified with packs of fishes and tortoises, and packs of trees on its banks, on which 
climber plants are wraparound like the ladyloves of those trees.

shloka:
किंनरोरगगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षससेविताम् -यद्वा - |
किन्नर उरग गन्धर्व यक्ष राक्षस सेविताम् |
नाना द्रुम 
लता आकीर्णाम् शीत वारि निधिम् शुभाम्
translation:
And that is adored by the beings like sylvan, reptilian, celestial, georgic, and elfish beings, and 
it is overcrowded with trees and tendrils, and it is a trove for fairish and clodish water.

shloka:
पद्म सौगन्धिकैः ताम्राम् शुक्लाम् कुमुद मण्डलैः |
नीलाम् कुवलय उद् घाटैः बहु वर्णाम् कुथाम् इव
translation:
The lotuses of the lake are rich in their fragrance, and with the heaps of clusters of reddish, whitish, 
and blackish lotuses, and with such pinkish, whitish, and reddish lotuses the sheet of water is like 
a picturesquely painted canvas and it is surrounded by the orchards of flowered mango trees and sounded 
much by the screams of peacocks. [3-75-20, 21]

shloka:
स ताम् दृष्ट्वा ततः पंपाम् रामः सौमित्रिणा सह |
विललाप च तेजस्वी कामात् दशरथात्मजः
translation:
Then Rama along with Lakshmana on seeing at that Pampa Lake, that self-refulgent son of Dasharatha whimpered 
over, owing to his passionate recollection of Seetha.

shloka:
तिलकैः बीज पूरैः च वटैः शुक्ल द्रुमैः तथा |
पुष्पितैः करवीरैः च पुन्नागैः च सु पुष्पितैः
translation:
That Pampa Lake is wraparound with the trees of Tilaka, Citron-fruits, Banyan, White-trees, likewise 
flowered are flowery trees like Red oleanders, Punnaaga, shrubs of Maalati and Kunda, likewise flowered 
are the trees of Madder, Nicula, Ashoka, and Seven-leaved banana plants, and plants of Mogra and climbers 
of Maadhavii Lata are also flowered, and with them she that Ladylike Pampa shone forth like a pulchritudinous 
lady. [3-75-23, 24]

shloka: अस्याः तीरे तु पूर्व उक्तः पर्वतो धातु मण्डितः
translation:
The aforesaid mountain renowned as Rishyamuka which is abounding with colourful ores and amazingly flowered 
trees is there on the bank of Pampa Lake. [3-75-25b, 26a]

shloka: हरेः ऋक्षरजो नाम्नः पुत्रः तस्य महात्मनः
translation:
A noble soul by his name Risharaja was there and that monkey's son is the highly valiant Sugreeva, thus 
he is renowned, and he presides over that mountain. [3-75-26b, 27b]

shloka: सुग्रीवम् अभिगच्छ त्वम् वानरेन्द्रम् नरर्षभ
translation:
That best one among men Rama, said this way, "oh, Lakshmana, you make a headway for that chief of monkeys, 
Sugreeva..." and further said this to Lakshmana whose valiance is truthfulness alone, "how can I possibly 
live without Seetha..." [3-75-27b, 28]

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्त्वा मदन अभिपीडितः
स लक्ष्मणम् वाक्यम् अनन्य चेतनः |
विवेश पंपाम् नलिनी मनो रमाम्
तम् उत्तमम् शोकम् उदीरयाणः
translation:
Such as he is whose thinking is applying itself to Seetha alone, and who is vocalising his anguish for 
her, to whom aa stymie is laid by the Love-god just at the appearance that lake, that Rama on saying 
that sentence in that way to Lakshmana neared that superb and heart delighting lotus Lake Pampa.

shloka:
क्रमेण गत्वा प्रविलोकयन् वनम्
ददर्श पंपाम् शुभ दर्श काननाम् |
अनेक नाना विध पक्षि संकुलाम्
विवेश रामः सह लक्ष्मणेन
translation:
On going step by step, and on going on seeing ardently and intently at that forest which has picturesque 
visuals of forestry, and which is with hurly-burly birds, not one, but numerous and divers are they, 
and then Rama along with Lakshmana on entering the area of that lake, has seen that Lake Pampa.

shloka:
स ताम् पुष्करिणीम् गत्वा पद्म उत्पल झषाकुलाम् |
रामः सौमित्रि सहितो विललाप अकुलेन्द्रियः
translation:
Rama, on arriving at that Lake of Lotuses called Pampa along with Lakshmana, which is full with lotuses, 
costuses, and fishes, lamented as his emotions are disturbed, on seeing the beauty of the Lake comparable 
with Seetha's face.

shloka:
तत्र दृष्ट्वैवा ताम् हर्षात् इन्द्रियाणि चकम्पिरे |
स कामवशम् आपन्नः सौमित्रिम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
There, on seeing that Lake of Lotuses, thrilled are his senses with gladness, and he engrossed and overcame 
by passion spoke this way to Lakshmana.

shloka:
सौमित्रे शोभते पम्पा वैदूर्य विमल उदका |
फुल्ल पद्म उत्पलवती शोभिता विविधैः द्रुमैः
translation:
"Oh! Soumitri, magnificent is Pampa Lake with its cat's-eye-gem like waters, and she with her fully 
bloomed lotuses and costuses is beaming forth, along with many trees around her.

shloka:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाः काननम् शुभ दर्शनम् |
यत्र राजन्ति शैला वा द्रुमाः स शिखरा इव
translation:
"Oh! Soumitri, see the forest of Pampa, the auspicious one in its appearance... where the mountains 
or trees lustre with their mountainous peaks...

shloka: माम् तु शोकाभि सन्तप्तम् आधयः पीडयन्ति वै
translation:
"But I, who am well seethed by the anguish of Bharata, and even by the abduction of Seetha, am indeed 
distressed by my sensibilities and their distresses...

shloka:
शोकार्तस्य अपि मे पम्पा शोभते चित्र कानना |
व्यवकीर्णा बहु विधैः पुष्पैः शीतोदका शिवा
translation:
"This auspicious Pampa is pleasant to me with its delightful forests overspread with many diverse flowers, 
cool waters, though I am disquieted...

shloka:
नलिनैः अपि संछन्ना हि अत्यर्थ शुभ दर्शना |
सर्प व्याल अनुचरिता मृग द्विज समाकुला
translation:
"Even enwreathed with lotuses this is remarkably sacred in its aspect... rambling snakes and elephants 
and restless are the deer and birds flocks, as well...

shloka:
अधिकम् प्रविभाति एतत् नील पीतम् तु शाद्वलम् |
द्रुमाणाम् विविधैः पुष्पैः परिस्तोमैः इव अर्पितम्
translation:
"All this is shining very much with bluish, yellowish grassland with a variety of trees... and with 
flowers covering it like flowery bed-sheet with variegated colours...

shloka:
पुष्प भार समृद्धानि शिखराणि समन्ततः |
लताभिः पुष्पित अग्राभिः उपगूढानि सर्वतः
translation:
"Everywhere the treetops are fully flowered and the onus of those flowers is on the rise, though they 
are wholly embraced by climbers and their apices.

shloka:
सुख अनिलोऽयम् सौमित्रे कालः प्रचुर मन्मथः |
गन्धवान् सुरभिर् मासो जात पुष्प फल द्रुमः
translation:
"Pleasing is this breeze, oh! Soumitri, and Manmadha, the Love God, prevails at this time, and prideful 
is this month with its fragrance, flowers, fruits and trees... all anew...

shloka:
पश्य रूपाणि सौमित्रे वनानाम् पुष्प शालिनाम् |
सृजताम् पुष्प वर्षाणि वर्षम् तोयमुचाम् इव
translation:
"See this figuration of these forests enriched with these flowers, Soumitri! Outpouring is the flower 
rain, like the rain from rain-clouds...

shloka:
प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः कानन द्रुमाः |
वायु वेग प्रचलिताः पुष्पैः अवकिरन्ति गाम्
translation:
"Also on those appeasing terraces of mountains there are many forest trees... speed of winds are swinging 
them to shower flowers onto ground...

shloka:
पतितैः पतमानैः च पादपस्थैः च मारुतः |
कुसुमैः पश्य सौमित्रे क्रीडतीव समन्ततः
translation:
"These are the flowers already fallen, about to fall, or still on the trees, but everywhere the air 
is playing with these flowers, see that Lakshmana...

shloka:
विक्षिपन् विविधाः शाखा नगानाम् कुसुमोत्कटाः |
मारुतः चलित स्थानैः षट्पदैः अनुगीयते
translation:
"The honeybees are displaced when the wind rapidly moved numerous branches of trees with full of flowers, 
and though displaced those bees are singing as though in accompaniment to the singing breeze...

shloka:
मत्त कोकिल सन्नादैः नर्तयन् इव पादपान् |
शैल कन्दर निष्क्रान्तः प्रगीत इव च अनिलः
translation:
"Breeze coming out from those mountain caves along with the high callings of lusty black cuckoos are 
making the trees to dance, and the air itself is as though singing as an accompaniment to that dancing...

shloka:
तेन विक्षिपता अत्यर्थम् पवनेन समन्ततः |
अमी संसक्त शाखाग्रा ग्रथिता इव पादपाः
translation:
"Entwined are the spires of trees when muchly moved by the air, thus the trees themselves seem to be 
entwined one with the other...

shloka:
स एव सुख संस्पर्शो वाति चन्दन शीतलः |
गन्धम् अभ्यवहन् पुण्यम् श्रम अपनयो अनिलः
translation:
"He, this breeze is thus a happy one for touch, carrying a coolant and the fragrance like that of the 
sandalwood, and this breezing is a merited one and a fatigue remover...

shloka: अमी पवन विक्षिप्ता विनन्दन्ती इव पादपाः |षट्पदैः अनुकूजद्भिः वनेषु मधु गन्धिषु
translation:
"Air is vacillating these trees in this honey scented forest... and the trees appear to be enjoying 
their fluttering dance and seem to be swinging their treetops to appreciate the singing of honeybees 
that are humming in accompaniment to this dance...

shloka:
गिरि प्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पुष्पवद्भिः मनोरमैः |
संसक्त शिखरा शैला विराजन्ति महाद्रुमैः
translation:
"On mountain-planes that are beautiful with fully flowered and pleasant tress that entwine the mountain 
peaks with their high treetops, and thus these mountains indeed liven up with these great trees...

shloka:
पुष्प संछन्न शिखरा मारुतः उत्क्षेप चंचला |
अमी मधुकरोत्तंसाः प्रगीत इव पादपाः
translation:
"Air is moving the treetops fully covered with flowers to swinging and the coronet like honeybees have 
to swing around those treetops, thus these trees themselves appear to be dancing to be dancing and singing...

shloka:
सुपुष्पितांस्तु पश्य एतान् कर्णिकारान् समन्ततः |
हाटक प्रति संच्छन्नान् नरान् पीतांबरान् इव
translation:
"Fully flowered are these Karnikaara plants all over with golden colour flowers at top and yellow coloured 
stems, and they look like men wearing golden ornaments on their upper body, while their loin cloth is 
yellow...

shloka:
अयम् वसन्तः सौमित्रे नाना विहग नादितः |
सीतया विप्रहीणस्य शोक सन्दीपनो मम
translation:
"This spring with the soundings of many birds, oh! Soumitri, is enkindling grief in me, for Seetha is 
disunited...

shloka:
माम् हि शोक समाक्रान्तम् संतापयति मन्मथः |
हृष्टम् प्रवदमानश्च समाह्वयति कोकिलः
translation:
"I, who am already pervaded by grief, am now well sweltered by the Love God, and this cuckoo that has 
happy calls is rather calling me down...

shloka:
एष दाअत्यूहको हृष्टो रम्ये माम् वन निर्झरे |
प्रणदन् मन्मथाविष्टम् शोचयिष्यति लक्ष्मण
translation:
"This gallinule bird happily calling in the forest brooks is making me awesome with its calls, as the 
Love-god has already made me awestricken...

shloka:
श्रुत्वा एतस्य पुरा शब्दम् आश्रमस्था मम प्रिया |
माम् आहूय प्रमुदिता परमम् प्रत्यनन्दत
translation:
"Earlier when we were in hermitage, on hearing this bird's call, dear Seetha used to call me to listen, 
and she herself was highly cheerful at this bird's calls...

shloka:
एवम् विचित्राः पतगा नाना राव विराविणः |
वृक्ष गुल्म लताः पश्य संपतन्ति समन्ततः
translation:
"Very many amusing birds of that kind are flitting all over on trees, bushes, and creepers emitting 
very many sounds... see them, Lakshmana...

shloka:
विमिश्रा विहगाः पुंभिः आत्म व्यूह अभिनन्दिताः |
भृङ्गराज प्रमुदिताः सौमित्रे मधुर स्वराः
translation:
"Well mingled are these female birds with their male ones, for which they are well admired by their 
own flock, oh! Soumitri, and such birds are calling gladsomely together with the pleasing humming of 
king-bees...

shloka:
अस्याः कूले प्रमुदिताः सन्घशः शकुनास्त्विह |
दात्यूहरति विक्रन्दैः पुंस्कोकिल रुतैः अपि | ४-१-२८
स्वनन्ति पादपाः च इमे माम् अनङ्ग प्रदीपकाः |
translation:
"At the shore of this Lake Pampa rejoicing are these birds in groups, and these trees loaded with the 
mating sounds of gallinule birds, and even loaded the callings of the male black cuckoos, are while 
inciting me they are inspiring love in me... [4-1-28, 29a]

shloka: अशोक स्तबक अङ्गारः षट्पद स्वन निस्वनः
translation:
"The fire called spring season will burn me down with its fiery paraphernalia like the clusters of red 
flowers of hellebore that are akin to fireballs, the humming of honeybees that is alike the rustle of 
campfires, and the coppery red colour of tender leaves just sprouted that is identical to burning fire... 
[4-1-29b, 30a]

shloka: न हि ताम् सूक्ष्मपक्ष्माक्षीम् सुकेशीम् मृदु भाषिणीम्
translation:
"And if she with slender eyelids on her eyes, decent hairdo, and a soft spoken one, Oh! Soumitri, if 
she is unseen by me will there be any purposefulness of my life? [4-1-30b, 31a]

shloka: अयम् हि रुचिरः तस्याः कालो रुचिर काननः
translation:
"My dear Seetha has an enchantment for these enchanting woodlands bustling with koels up to their horizons, 
and Lakshmana, similarly enchanting is this vernal season to her... [4-1-31b, 32a]

shloka: मन्मध आयास संभूतो वसन्त गुण वर्धितः
translation:
"This fire of grief born out of the throes of love, and furthered by the attributes of spring season 
will swiftly burn me down in no time...

shloka: अपश्यत ताम् वनिताम् पश्यतो रुचिर द्रुमान्
translation:
"As the one unable to see that lady but able to see beautiful trees the Love-god in me gains intensity... 
[4-1-33b, 34a]

shloka: अदृश्यमाना वैदेही शोकम् वर्धयती इह मे
translation:
"Now, that invisible Seetha is intensifying my agony, and this visible spring season, the remover of 
the touch of sweat too, is doing the same... [4-1-34b, 35a]

shloka: माम् हि सा मृगशाबाक्षी चिन्ता शोक बलात्कृतम्
translation:
"Overwhelmed with the grief of worry about that deer eyed Seetha, such as I am, I am burnt down by this 
cruel vernal breeze of forests...[4-1-35b, 36a]

shloka: अमी मयूराः शोभन्ते प्रनृत्यन्तः ततः ततः
translation:
"And these peacocks that dance here and there are shining forth with crystal like windows on their plumage, 
when up-shoved by the wind...[4-1-36b, 37a]

shloka: शिखिनीभिः परिवृतास्त एते मद मूर्छिताः
translation:
"Those peacocks that are surorounded by their peahens and convulsed in love are intensifying longing 
in me, who am already muffled in love-longing... [4-1-37b, 38a]

shloka: पश्य लक्ष्णम नृत्यन्तम् मयूरम् उपनृत्यति
translation:
"See Lakshmana, on that mountain terrace this peahen longing for love is dancing at the nearby of her 
husband, that peacock... [4-1-38b, 39a]

shloka: ताम् एव मनसा रामाम् मयुरोऽपि अनुधावति
translation:
"Spreading his beautiful wings and screaming as though joking, even that peacock is longingly running 
after his female... [4-1-39b, 40a]

shloka: मयूरस्य वने नूनम् रक्षसा न हृता प्रिया
translation:
"Definitely no demon has abducted that peacock's ladylove, hence he is dancing with her in beautiful 
forests... [4-1-40b, 41a]

shloka: मम त्वयम् विना वासः पुष्पमासे सुदुःसहः
translation:
"Living in this flowering month is unbearable for me... Lakshmana, see the fondness even in those originated 
in animals, thus that peahen in her passion is following her husband... [4-1-41b, 42]

shloka:
माम् अपि एवम् विशालाक्षी जानकी जात संभ्रमा |
मदनेन अभिवर्तेत यदि न अपहृता भवेत्
translation:
"Had she, that broad eyed lady Seetha, not been abducted, she too would have followed me in this way 
with an ecstatic love...

shloka:
पश्य लक्ष्मण पुष्पाणि निष्फलानि भवन्ति मे |
पुष्प भार समृद्धानाम् वनानाम् शिशिरात्यये
translation:
"See Lakshmana, while these forests are abundantly weighty with flowers in wintry season these flowers 
are becoming futile to me...

shloka:
रुचिराणि अपि पुष्पाणि पादपानाम् अतिश्रिया |
निष्फलानि महीम् यान्ति समम् मधुकरोत्करैः
translation:
"Though these flowers on the trees are exceedingly beautiful they are falling onto the earth wastefully, 
along with the swarms of honeybees hovering over them... [4-1-45.]

shloka:
नदन्ति कावम् मुदिताः शकुना सङ्घशः कलम् |
आह्वयन्त इव अन्योन्यम् काम उन्मादकरा मम
translation:
"These blithesome birds appear to be inviting each other in mutual consent, and they are melodious calling 
as they like, and this is causing love madness in me...

shloka:
वसन्तो यदि तत्र अपि यत्र मे वसति प्रिया |
नूनम् परवशा सीता सा अपि शोच्यति अहम् यथा
translation:
"Should this spring season be there too, where my dear one Seetha is living, she with her unrequited 
merriment will definitely be saddened like me...

shloka:
नूनम् न तु वसन्तः तम् देशम् स्पृशति यत्र सा |
कथम् हि असित पद्माक्षी वर्तयेत् सा मया विना
translation:
"Definitely this spring season will not touch that place where she is... and even if this touches that 
place, how can that lady with black-lotus-eyes can possibly comport without me!

shloka:
अथवा वर्तते तत्र वसन्तो यत्र मे प्रिया |
किम् करिष्यति सुश्रोणी सा तु निर् भर्त्सिता परैः
translation:
"Otherwise, even if the spring happens to be there where my dear is, what can that fine waisted lady 
do under threat by others?

shloka:
श्यामा पद्म पलाशाक्षी मृदु भाषा च मेम् प्रिया |
नूनम् वसन्तम् आसाद्य परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्
translation:
"She in midst of her youth, eyes like lotus petals, also soft-spoken one is my dear one... and definitely 
taken by the spring she leaves her life...

shloka:
दृढम् हि हृदये बुधिः मम संप्रतिवर्तते |
न अलम् वर्तयितुम् सीता साध्वी मत् विरहम् गता
translation:
"Indeed in my heart a strong notion is prevailing that the chaste lady Seetha will be unable to live 
separated from me...

shloka:
मयि भावो हि वैदेह्याः तत्त्वतो विनिवेशितः |
मम अपि भावः सीतायाम् सर्वधा विनिवेशितः
translation:
"My thoughts of Seetha alone are well biding in me, and in Seetha also thoughts about me will always 
be abiding... [4-1-52.]

shloka:
एष पुष्पवहो वायुः सुख स्पर्शो हिमावहः |
ताम् विचिन्तयतः कान्ताम् पावक प्रतिमो मम
translation:
"This breeze carrying fragrance of flowers is though pleasant for touch and though coolish like snow, 
this alone is like fire to me as I am very much worried about that lady...

shloka:
सदा सुखम् अहम् मन्ये यम् पुरा सह सीताया |
मारुतः स विना सीताम् शोक संजनओ मम
translation:
"By which breeze I always felt happiness earlier along with Seetha... that breeze alone is increasing 
anguish in me without Seetha...

shloka:
ताम् विन अथ विहङ्गो असौ पक्षी प्रणदितः तदा |
वायसः पादपगतः प्रहृष्टम् अभि कूजति
translation:
"When Seetha was with me, then this crow flew into the sky and cawed much indicating Seetha's departure 
from me, and now sitting on a tree it is cawing agreeably indicating early arrival of Seetha...

shloka:
एष वै तत्र वैदेह्या विहगः प्रतिहारकः |
पक्षी माम् तु विशालाक्ष्याः समीपम् उपनेष्यति
translation:
"This bird alone, then roving in the sky indicated about the abduction of Seetha... and this very same 
bird will now lead me near to that broad eyed one...

shloka:
पश्य लक्ष्मण संनादम् वने मद विवर्धनम् |
पुष्पित अग्रेषु वृक्षेषु द्विजानाम् अवकूजताम्
translation:
"Lakshmana, observe the appealing tonality of birds in the forest that calling out atop the flowered 
trees, that which is indeed furthering one's passion�

shloka:
विक्षिप्ताम् पवनेन एताम् असौ तिलक मञ्जरीम् |
षट्पदः सहसा अभ्येति मद उद्धूताम् इव प्रियाम्
translation:
"That honeybee is quickly reaching these red flowers bouquets of Tilaka that are like his loved ones 
that are raising their faces with vigour�

shloka:
कामिनाम् अयम् अत्यन्तम् अशोकः शोक वर्धनः |
स्तबकैः पवन उत्क्षिप्तैः तर्जयन् इव माम् स्थितः
translation:
"To the impassioned ones that Ashoka tree is very much enhancing grief, and with its bouquets of flowers 
hustled up by the wind it is sanding as though to daunt me...

shloka:
अमी लक्ष्मण दृश्यन्ते चूताः कुसुम शालिनः |
विभ्रम उत्सिक्त मनसः स अङ्गरागा नरा इव
translation:
" Lakshmana, these mango trees bearing greenish yellow flower are appearing like men whose hearts are 
flirtatiously aroused, and who have creamed their bodies with greenish-yellow body cream�

shloka:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाः चित्रासु वन राजिषु |
किंनरा नरशार्दूल विचरन्ति ततः ततः
translation:
"Oh, tigerly man Soumitri, see these Pampa's amazing forests ranges... and therein the nymphs are moving, 
hither and yon...

shloka:
इमानि शुभ गन्धीनि पश्य लक्ष्मण सर्वशः |
नलिनानि प्रकाशन्ते जले तरुण सूर्य वत्
translation:
"See Lakshmana, these fragrant and propitious blue lotuses are everywhere in the waters, glistening 
like tender sun...

shloka:
एषा प्रसन्न सलिला पद्म नील उत्पलायुता |
हंस कारण्डव आकीर्णा पम्पा सौगन्धिका युता
translation:
"This Pampa Lake is shining forth with its tranquil waters, that contain lotuses, blue water-lily's, 
and red lotuses, along with swans and water-birds that permeate it �

shloka:
जले तरुण सूर्याभैः षट्पद आहत केसरैः |
पन्कजैः शोभते पम्पा समन्तात् अभिसंवृता
translation:
"Lotuses with the resplendence of tender sun enwrapping its waters, pollen grain pilfered by honeybees 
enwrapping those lotuses� with them this Pampa is beaming forth�

shloka:
चक्रवाक युता नित्यम् चित्र प्रस्थ वनान्तरा |
मातंग मृग यूथैः च शोभते सलिल अर्थिभिः
translation:
"This Pampa is always bedecked with the ruddy geese, amazing deep areas of the forest, and with water 
thirsty herds of elephants and deer, and with them it gleams forth...

shloka:
पवन आहत वेगाभिः ऊर्मिभिः विमले अंभसि |
पन्कजानि विराजन्ते ताड्यमानानि लक्ष्मण
translation:
"In the tranquil water the speed of wind is throbbing ripples, and the ripples throb the lotuses, thus 
the throbbing and rippling lotuses appear beautiful�

shloka:
पद्म पत्र विशालाक्षीम् सततम् प्रिय पन्कजाम् |
अपश्यतो मे वैदेहीम् जीवितम् न अभिरोचते
translation:
"That one with lotus-petal-like broad eyes, who always holds the lotuses dear...without finding that 
Vaidehi... to me my life is uninteresting...

shloka:
अहो कामस्य वामत्वम् यो गताम् अपि दुर्लभाम् |
स्मारयिष्यति कल्याणीम् कल्याण तर वादिनीम्
translation:
"Aha! Deplorable is the deviousness of Love-god, for he is causing reminisces about that graceful lady 
who articulates that gracefully, even if she is gone away and cannot be regained now...

shloka:
शक्यो धारयितुम् कामो भवेत् अभ्यागतो मया |
यदि भूयो वसन्तो माम् न हन्यात् पुष्पित द्रुमः
translation:
"If this spring with its flowered trees is not going to deaden me... the Love-god is a possible one 
to tolerate, though now he came upon me forcefully...

shloka:
यानि स्म रमणीयानि तया सह भवन्ति मे |
तानि एव अरमणीयानि जायन्ते मे तया विना
translation:
"All those places or objects that were delightful ones to me when she was with me, and they alone are 
now becoming anguishing ones to me...for she parted from me�

shloka:
पद्मकोश पलाशानि द्रष्टुम् दृष्टिः हि मन्यते |
सीताया नेत्र कोशाभ्याम् सदृशान् इति लक्ष्मण
translation:
"To gaze the petals of the lotus buds my sight is fascinated... and in them I perceive the pair of Seetha's 
bud-like eyes...Oh! Lakshmana...and they are alike thus...

shloka:
पद्म केसर संसृष्टो वृक्षान्तर विनिःसृतः |
निःश्वास इव सीताया वाति वायुः मनोहरः
translation:
"This breeze� let out from within the thickets of forests, breezing touching the pollen of lotuses, 
is reminding Seetha's exhale, as such it is heart-stealing�

shloka:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पाया दक्षिणे गिरि सानुषु |
पुष्पितान् कर्णिकारस्य यष्टिम् परम शोभिताम्
translation:
"Soumitri, see those flowered Karnikara trees with their tree-trunks on those southern hill-terraces 
of Pampa, they are highly splendorous...

shloka:
अधिकम् शैल राजोऽयम् धातुभिः तु विभूषितः |
विचित्रम् सृजते रेणुम् वायु वेग विघट्टितम्
translation:
"That one, that kingly mountain which is ornamentally impregnated with ores and minerals is exhausting 
much mass of wondrous dust with the colour of its ores, that is drifted by the wind's speed...

shloka:
गिरि प्रस्थास्तु सौमित्रे सर्वतः संप्रपुष्पितैः |
निष्पत्रैः सर्वतो रम्यैः प्रदीप्ता इव किंशुकैः
translation:
"On the mountainsides, Soumitri, all over fully flowered are the exquisite Kimshuka trees, while their 
leaves are hidden under those reddish flowers, and with them that mountain is as though aglow...

shloka:
पम्पा तीर रुहाः च इमे संसक्ता मधु गन्धिनः |
मालती मल्लिका पद्म करवीराः च पुष्पिताः
translation:
"On the banks of Pampa these jasmines, water-lilies, red oleanders have grown up and they are now flowered 
that is wetted with the fragrance of nectar...

shloka:
केतक्यः सिन्धुवाराः च वासन्त्यः च सुपुष्पिताः |
माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाः च कुंदगुल्माः च सर्वशः
translation:
"The Mogra bushes, Sinduka, Vaasanti are well flowered. Maadhavi, flowers are also fully fragrant, and 
everywhere there are bushes of Jasmine...

shloka:
चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाः च वञ्जुला वकुलाः तथा |
चम्पकाः तिलकाः च एव नागवृक्षाः च पुष्पिताः
translation:
"Charming are the saplings of Bilva, and Madhooka, and plants like Vakula, Champaka, Tilaka, Naaga trees 
are well flowered....

shloka:
पद्मकाः च एव शोभन्ते नील अशोकाः च पुष्पिताः
लोध्राः च गिरि पृष्ठेषु सिंह केसर पिन्जराः
translation:
"Padmaka plants are well flourishing, and like that Neela, Ashoka are also flowered... trees on the 
mountain terraces namely Lodhra trees are brownish like lion's mane...

shloka:
अन्कोलाः च कुरण्टाः च पूर्णकाः पारिभद्रकाः |
चूताः पाटलयः च अपि कोविदाराः च पुष्पिताः
translation:
"The trees of Alangium, Kurntaka, Poornaka, Devadaaru, and also the Mango trees, and like that Patala 
trees, and the trees of Mountain ebony are flowered...

shloka:
मुचुकुंद अर्जुनाः च एव दृश्यन्ते गिरिसानुषु
केतक उद्दालकाः च एव शिरीषाः शिंशुपा धवाः
translation:
"Muchukunda trees, also Arjuna trees are seen on mountain terraces...Date palm trees, Uddaalaka trees 
also... like that the Shiriisha tree, simshupa trees, and dhava trees...

shloka:
शाल्मल्यः किंशुकाः च एव रक्ताः कुरवकाः तथा |
तिनिशा नक्तमालाः च चंदनाः स्यंदनाः तथा
translation:
"Silk cotton trees, palaasha trees also, like that are red mehandi trees, thus are Tinisha and Naktamaala 
trees, sandalwood trees, spandana trees are all thus well flowered...

shloka:
हिन्तालः तिलकाः च एव नाग वृक्षाः च पुष्पिताः |
पुष्पितान् पुष्पित अग्राभिः लताभिः परिवेष्टितान्
translation:
"Flowered are the trees like hintaala, tilaka, and naaga trees, and they are enfolded by the flowered 
climber-plants at their apices...

shloka:
द्रुमान् पश्य इह सौमित्रे पम्पाया रुचिरान् बहून् |
वात विक्षिप्त विटपान् यथा आसन्नान् द्रुमान् इमान्
translation:
"See the splendorous trees of Pampa here, oh! Soumitri...their branches bestirred by wind and bend onto 
other trees, as though these trees are nearby and within the reach of climber-plants... thus the climber-plants 
passionately bear upon those trees, like the doting of passionate women... [ [4-1-84, 85a]

shloka: पादपात् पादपम् गच्छन् शैलात् शैलम् वनात् वनम्
translation:
"And the breeze is perhaps unhappy by savouring only one kind of nectarine aroma, hence it appears to 
be gliding from tree to tree, forest to forest, mountain to mountain... while going from tree to tree, 
mountain to mountain, forest to forest... [4-1-85b, 86a]

shloka: केचित् पर्याप्त कुसुमाः पादपा मधु गन्धिनः
translation:
"Some trees are full with flowers whose nectar is fragrant, and some shine forth with dark colour as 
they are enveloped with buds... [4-1-86b, 87a]

shloka: इदम् मृष्टम् इदम् स्वादु प्रफुल्लम् इदम् इत्यपि
translation:
"And the honeybee on assessing each of the flower as 'this one is pure... this one is delicious... and 
this one is well bloomed...' is plunging into them... [4-1-87b, 88a]

shloka:
निलीय पुनर् उत्पत्य सहसा अन्यत्र गच्छति |
मधु लुब्धो मधुकरः पंपा तीर द्रुमेषु असौ
translation:
"On plunging into the flowers that nectar-avaricious honeybee is again coming up, and quickly going 
elsewhere in the trees on the banks of Pampa...

shloka:
इयम् कुसुम सन्घातैः उपस्तीर्णा सुखा कृता |
स्वयम् निपतितैः भूमिः शयन प्रस्तरैः इव
translation:
"These clusters of flowers that have fallen on their own are spreading out like a bed of flowers laid 
on, with them the ground appears to endow comfort...

shloka:
विविधा विविधैः पुष्पैः तैः एव नगसानुषु |
विस्तेएर्णाः पीत रक्ताभा सौमित्रे प्रस्तराः कृताः
translation:
"On mountain slopes varied flowers are spread out, with them the colour of diverse mountain slabs is 
rendered into yellow-red hue...

shloka:
हिमान्ते पश्य सौमित्रे वृक्षाणाम् पुष्प संभवम् |
पुष्प मासे हि तरवः संघर्षात् इव पुष्पिताः
translation:
"Soumitri see the bloom of flowers in spring after winter, as if the trees have indeed bore the flowers 
in competition with one another...

shloka:
आह्वयन्त इव अन्योन्यम् नगाः षट्पद नादिताः |
कुसुमोत्तंस विटपाः शोभन्ते बहु लक्ष्मण
translation:
"The drones of honeybees among the trees with flowered treetops appear to be the talk of trees, and 
the swinging branches of trees appear to be their invitational gestures to one another, thus those trees 
look highly attractive...

shloka:
एष कारण्डवः पक्षी विगाह्या सलिलम् शुभम् |
रमते कान्ताया सार्थम् कामम् उद्दीपयन् इव
translation:
"Entering the blessed waters this bird, partridge, is rejoicing together with his female, kindling desire 
in me too...

shloka:
मंदकिन्यास्तु यदिदम् रूपम् एतन् मनोररम् |
स्थाने जगति विख्याता गुणाः तस्या मनोरमाः
translation:
"This sort of heart pleasing nature is also available with River Ganga, and that alone reasonably signifies 
the popularity of River Pampa in the world...

shloka:
यदि दृश्येत सा साध्वी यदि च इह वसेम हि |
स्पृहयेयम् न शक्राय न अयोध्यायै रघूत्तम
translation:
"If that devot lady Seetha is found, and also if we were to stay here only, I neither think about Indra's 
throne in Heavens nor Ayodhya's throne, which is like Indra's throne on the earth...

shloka:
न हि एवम् रमणीयेषु शाद्वलेषु तया सह |
रमतो मे भवेत् चिन्ता न स्पृहा अन्येषु वा भवेत्
translation:
"Nay... if I were to take delight this way in these pleasant green meadows along with her, there will 
be no worry to me... nor interest in other things...

shloka:
अमी हि विविधैः पुष्पैः तरवो रुचिर च्छदाः |
कानने अस्मिन् विना कान्ताम् चित्तम् उत्पादयन्ति मे
translation:
"Indeed these beautifully leaved and variously flowered trees are maddening my heart as I am without 
that lady Seetha in this forest...

shloka:
पश्य शीत जलाम् च इमाम् सौमित्रे पुष्कर आयुताम् |
चक्रवाक अनुचरिताम् कारण्डव निषेविताम्
translation:
"See the cool water of this Pampa Lake, Soumitri, filled with blue lotuses, and with ruddy geese well 
moving in, and well venerated by the partridge birds...

shloka:
प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैः च संपूर्णाम् महा मृग निषेविताम् |
अधिकम् शोभते पम्पा विकूजद्भिः विहङ्गमैः
translation:
"Well filled with waterfowls, curlew birds, and adored by great animals, this Pampa glistens much with 
pleasantly calling birds...

shloka:
दीपयन्ती इव मे कामम् विविधा मुदिता द्विजाः |
श्यामाम् चन्द्र मुखीम् स्मृत्वा प्रियाम् पद्म निभ ईक्षणाम्
translation:
"Enkindling passion in me, are these umpteen gladdened birds, reminding me of my dear one who is in 
the mid of her youth, moonfaced, and with the radiance of lotuses in her eyes...

shloka:
पश्य सानुषु चित्रेषु मृगीभिः सहितान् मृगान् |
माम् पुनः मृग शबाक्षी वैदेह्या विरहीकृतम् |
व्यधयन्तीव 
मे चित्तम् संचरन्तः ततः ततः
translation:
"See that female deer along with male deer moving there and there on those wonderful mountainsides... 
and at me, who am weaned away from such a fawn-eyed lady Seetha... and such as I am, my heart is further 
agonised on seeing these wide-eyed deer, and for not seeing her, the wide-eyed Seetha...

shloka:
अस्मिन् सानुनि रम्ये हि मत्त द्विज गणाकुले |
पश्य अयम् यदि ताम् कन्ताम् ततः स्वस्ति भवेत् मम
translation:
"If only I can see that lady on those spectacular terraces filled with impassioned bird groups with 
much ado, then there shall be peace for me...

shloka:
जीवेयम् खलु सौमित्रे मया सह सुमध्यमा |
सेवेत यदि वैदेही पम्पायाः पवनम् शुभम्
translation:
"I live along for sure, Soumitri, if that slender-waisted Vaidehi basks in this benignant breeze of 
Pampa along with me...

shloka:
पद्म सौगन्धिक वहम् शिवम् शोक विनाशनम् |
धन्या लक्ष्मण सेवन्ते पम्पाया वन मरुतम्
translation:
""Lakshmana, the breeze from the greenswards of Pampa that carries the fragrance of lotuses including 
that of red lotuses is an auspicious one, an eliminator of melancholy, and those that adore such a breeze 
are fortunate ones...

shloka:
श्यमा पद्म पलाशाक्षी प्रिया विरहिता मया |
कथम् धरयति प्राणान् विवशा जनकात्मजा
translation:
"That youthful, lotus-petal eyed beloved of mine, that Janaka's daughter... how can that helpless lady 
bear her lives without me...

shloka:
किम् नु वक्ष्यामि धर्मज्ञम् राजानम् सत्य वादिनम् |
जनकम् पृष्ट सीतम् तम् कुशलम् जन संसदि
translation:
"What sort of well-being can I say to that virtuous and truth speaking King Janaka, if he enquires about 
Seetha's well-being among hosts of people?

shloka:
या मम् अनुगता मन्दम् पित्रा प्रस्थापितुम् वनम् |
सीता धर्मम् समास्थय क्व नु सा वर्तते प्रिया
translation:
"She who accompanied me, an unfortunate one whom his father sent to forests, taking up a virtuous course... 
now where will be she, that ladylove of mine, be abiding...

shloka:
तया विहीनः कृपणः कथम् लक्ष्मण धारये |
य माम् अनुगता रज्यात् भ्रष्टम् विहत चेतसम्
translation:
"Whose kingdom is forfeited, and whose soul succumbed to the circumstance at the time of exile, but 
she accompanied suchlike me, and Lakshmana, without her how I can I live on in desolation...

shloka:
तत् चारु अञ्चित पद्माक्षम् सुगन्धि शुभम् अव्रणम् |
अपश्यतो मुखम् तस्याः सीदति इव मतिः मम
translation:
"She who has a pretty and beaming face with lotus-like eyes, that is fragrant, auspicious and scarless, 
and not seeing such a face my mind is as though sinking...

shloka:
स्मित हास्यान्तर युतम् गुणवत् मधुरम् हितम् |
वैदेह्याः वाक्यम् अतुलम् कदा श्रोष्यामि लक्ष्मण
translation:
" Lakshmana, when can I hear that conversation of Vaidehi that will have smiles and wits in between... 
wisdom wise pleasing, friendly and unique one in its own way...

shloka:
प्राप्य दुःखम् वने श्यामा माम् मन्मध विकर्शितम् |
नष्ट दुःखेव हृष्टेव साध्वी साधु अभ्यभाषत
translation:
"That youthful and decent lady though succumbed to suffering in forests used to look as though got rid 
of her sufferings, and as though gladsome woman, and she used to speak to me, one smitten by her love, 
very fondly...

shloka:
किम् नु वक्ष्यामि अयोध्यायाम् कौसल्याम् हि नृपात्मज |
क्व सा स्नुषा इति पृच्छन्तीम् कथम् च अति मनस्विनीम्
translation:
"What can I say in Ayodhya to that kind hearted lady and my mother Kausalya, oh, prince Lakshmana, when 
she asks �where is she, my daughter-in-law? And how is she? '

shloka:
गच्छ लक्ष्मण पश्य त्वम् भरतम् भ्रातृउ वत्सलम् |
न हि अहम् जीवितुम् शक्तः ताम् ऋते जनकात्मजम्
translation:
"Begone! Lakshmana.... you may see Bharata, that affectionate one for his brothers... I may not be able 
to live on leaving off Seetha... isn't so!" [So said Rama to Lakshmana]

shloka:
इति रामम् महात्मानम् विलपन्तम् अनाथ वत् |
उवाच लक्ष्मणो भ्राता वचनम् युक्तम् अव्ययम्
translation:
To that great-souled Rama who is bewailing that way like a waif, his brother Lakshmana said these appropriate 
and infallible words.

shloka:
संस्थम्भ राम भद्रम् ते मा शुचः पुरुषोत्तम |
न ईदृइशानाम् मतिः मन्दा भवति अकलुषात्मनाम्
translation:
"Oh, best one among men, please control yourself Rama, let safety betide you, do not lament, the intellect 
of your kind of unblemished souls does not become languorous...

shloka:
स्मृत्वा वियोगजम् दुःखम् त्यज स्नेहम् प्रिये जने |
अति स्नेह परिष्वन्गात् वर्तिः अर्द्रा अपि दह्यते
translation:
"Recollect the sadness caused by departure of loved ones, and it may please be forsaken for some extent, 
with the embrace of too much of friendship of the water-drenched wick with oil, even that water-drenched 
wick burns in the lamp...

shloka:
यदि गच्छति पतालम् ततो अभ्यऽधिकम् एव वा |
सर्वधा रावणः तात न भविष्यति राघव
translation:
"If Ravana goes to the netherworlds, or still deeper worlds from there, oh my brother, still he will 
not live, Raghava...

shloka:
प्रवृत्तिः लभ्यताम् तावत् तस्य पापस्य रक्षसः |
ततः हास्यति वा सीताम् निधनम् वा गमिष्यति
translation:
"Let the emplacement of that sinning demon e obtained... and then he either cedes Seetha or enters into 
his own doom...

shloka:
यदि याति दितेः गर्भम् रावणः सह सीताया |
तत्र अपि एनम् हनिष्यामि न चेत् दास्यति मैथिलीम्
translation:
"Even if he enters the womb of Diti along with Seetha, and if he does not give away Seetha, even there 
I wish to slay him,...

shloka:
स्वास्थ्यम् भद्रम् भजस्व आर्यः त्यजताम् कृपणा मतिः |
अर्थो हि नष्ट कार्यार्थैः न अयत्ने न अधिगम्यते
translation:
"May you rejuvenate and be secure, oh, revered one, cast-off your pathetic mood... result of purpose 
will be lost indeed, for the endeavourers without a try, thus nothing can be regained by them...

shloka:
उत्साहो बलवान् आर्य नास्ति उत्साहात् परम् बलम् |
सः उत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचित् अपि दुर्लभम्
translation:
"Vehemence is might, oh, noble one, there is no superior might than vehemence and to him with vehemence 
there is no impossibility in the world,... even the slightest...

shloka:
उत्साहवन्तः पुरुषा न अवसीदन्ति कर्मसु |
उत्साह मत्रम् आश्रित्य सीताम् प्रतिलप्स्याम् जनकीम्
translation: "Vehement men do not regress in deeds, and taking hold of vehemence alone we regain Seetha...

shloka:
त्यज्य काम वृत्तत्वम् शोकम् सम् न्यस्य पृष्टतः |
महात्मानम् कृतात्मानम् आत्मानम् न अवबुध्यसे
translation:
"You leave off this enclosure of ardency and pushback that compassion ... you are not able to know your 
great and controlled soul...with these thoughts of self-pity and fondness...

shloka:
एवम् संबोधितः तेन शोकोपहत चेतनः |
त्य्ज्य शोकम् च मोहम् च रामो धैर्यम् उपागमत्
translation:
Thus addressed by Lakshmana, then Rama whose conscience is marred by emotions, got rid of pity and fondness, 
and acquired courage, to perform the deed demanded of his incarnation.

shloka:
सोऽभ्य अतिक्रामत् अव्यग्रः ताम् अचिन्त्य पराक्रमः |
रामः पम्पाम् सु रुचिराम् रम्याम् पारिप्लव द्रुमान्
translation:
He that inestimable valiant Rama strode forward those areas of charming Pampa Lake, with the charm of 
wind-flopped trees, getting rid of grief.

shloka:
निरीक्षमाणः सहसा महात्मा सर्वम् वनम् निर्झर कन्दराम् च |
उद्विग्न चेताः सह लक्ष्मणेन विचार्य दुःखोपहतः 
प्रतस्थे
translation:
That great one Rama on observing all over quickly, all round the forest with its brooks and caves, and 
reviewing with Lakshmana, though agonised at heart that anguished one travelled on.

shloka:
तम् मत्त मातङ्ग विलास गामी गच्छन्तम् अव्यग्र मनाः महात्मा |
स लक्ष्मणो राघवम् अप्रमत्तो ररक्ष धर्मेण 
बलेन च एव
translation:
While that great soul Rama is walking ahead, that great souled Lakshmana whose stride is also like that 
of an elephant, and whose deeds are agreeable to Rama, vigilantly protected Rama with an un-despaired 
mind and even by his virtue and strength.

shloka:
तौ ऋष्यमूकस्य समीप चारी चरन् ददर्श अद्भुत दर्शनीयौ |
शाखा मृगाणाम् अधिपः तरस्वी वितत्रसे नैव चिचेष्ट 
चेष्टाम्
translation:
He who is the chief of Vanara-s, who moves about Mt. Rishyamuka, while he is meandering thereabout he 
happened to see those two who are so amazing for a look, namely Rama and Lakshmana, by which he is so 
frightened that he is petrified.

shloka:
स तौ महात्मा गज मन्द गामि शखा मृगः तत्र चिरन् चरन्तौ |
दृष्ट्वा विषादम् परमम् जगाम चिन्ता परीतो भय 
भार मग्नः
translation:
On seeing those two Rama and Lakshmana who are advancing his way, he that great soul who is a tree-branch 
animal, and he who strides like an elephant, derived profound agony that muffled him in worry, and he 
is engulfed under the weight of his fear.

shloka:
तम् आश्रमम् पुण्य सुखम् शरण्यम् सदैव शाखा मृग सेवितान्तम् |
त्रस्ताः च दृष्ट्वा हरयोः अभिजग्मुः महौजसौ 
राघव लक्ष्मणौ तौ
translation:
On seeing those magnificent two, Rama and Lakshmana, the monkeys are frightened and fled towards the 
pious hermitage of Sage Matanga, which has an inland that is always adored by monkeys for it is consolatory 
and sheltering them.

shloka:
तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महात्मानौ भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |
वर आयुध धरौ वीरौ सुग्रीवः श्ङ्कितोऽभवत्
translation:
On seeing them the wielders of best weapons and audacious ones, two brothers and great souls, namely 
Rama and Lakshmana, Sugreeva became ambiguous.

shloka:
उद्विग्न हृदयः सर्वा दिशः समवलोकयन् |
न व्यतिष्ठत कस्मिन् चित् देशे वानर पुङ्गवः
translation:
Distressed at heart that foremost monkey gazed blankly in all directions and he did not remain at any 
one place.

shloka:
नैव चक्रे मनः स्थातुम् वीक्षमाणो महाबलौ |
कपेः परम भीतस्य चित्तम् व्यवससाद ह
translation:
On seeing those two great mighty ones that monkey has not even made-up his mind steadfast as he is very 
much frightened, and his heart is really sunken. [4- 2- 3]

shloka:
चिन्तयित्वा स धर्मात्मा विमृश्य गुरु लाघवम् |
सुग्रीवः परम उद्विग्नः सर्वैः तैः वानरैः सह
translation:
He that righteous Sugreeva considering his own strength and weakness is much agitated, and along with 
all the other monkeys too are frightened.

shloka:
ततः स सचिवेभ्यः तु सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः |
शशंस परम उद्विग्नः पश्यन् तौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
On seeing Rama and Lakshmana then that chief of monkeys Sugreeva with much dreadfulness said this to 
his ministers. [4- 2- 5]

shloka:
एतौ वनम् इदम् दुर्गम् वालि प्रणिहितौ ध्रुवम् |
छद्मना चीर वसनौ प्रचरन्तौ इह आगतौ
translation:
"Here they come wearing jute cloths and move about in this impassable forest deceitfully, definitely 
Vali must have dispatched them...

shloka:
ततः सुग्रीव सचिवा दृष्ट्वा परम धन्विनौ |
जग्मुः गिरि तटात् तस्माद् अन्यत् शिखरम् उत्तमम्
translation:
Then on seeing the great archers Rama and Lakshmana the ministers of Sugreeva have gone from that mountain 
terrace to another high-peaked mountain. [4- 2- 7]

shloka:
ते क्षिप्रम् अभिगम्य अथ यूथपा यूथपर्षभम् |
हरयो वानर श्रेष्ठम् परिवार्य उपतस्थिरे
translation:
Then the group-leaders of monkeys quickly arrived as they fled, at that lofty monkey group-leader Sugreeva, 
the chieftain of monkeys, gathering around him there they stood at his nearby.

shloka:
एवम् एक आयन गताः प्लवमाना गिरेः गिरिम् |
प्रकंपयन्तो वेगेन गिरीणाम् शिखराणि च
translation:
Thus they reached to one course of return, after hopping from one mountain to the other, shuddering 
mountains and even thir peaks by their trample in hastiness.

shloka:
ततः शाखा मृगाः सर्वे प्लवमाना महाबलाः |
बभंजुः च नगान् तत्र पुष्पितान् दुर्गम् आश्रितान्
translation:
Then all of the tree-branch animals, who are great in their strength, have wrecked down the well-flowered 
trees that are clumped in that forest on that mountain by their swinging. [4- 2- 10]

shloka:
आप्लवन्तो हरिवराः सर्वतः तम् महागिरिम् |
मृग मार्जार शार्दूलान् त्रासयन्तो ययुः तदा
translation:
While those best monkeys hopped everywhere they have frightened deer, wildcats and tigers on that great 
mountain.

shloka:
ततः सुग्रीव सचिवाः पर्वतेन्द्रे समाहिताः |
संगम्य कपि मुख्येन सर्वे प्रांजलयः स्थिताः
translation:
Then the ministers of Sugreeva, assembled on that best mountain and gathered around the chief of monkeys 
Sugreeva, and all stood with their adjoined palms.

shloka:
ततः तु भय संत्रस्तम् वालि किल्बिष शन्कितम् |
उवाच हनुमान् वाक्यम् सुग्रीवम् वाक्य कोविदः
translation:
Then Hanuma, the ablest sentence-maker, said this sentence to Sugreeva who is dismayed with fear doubting 
Vali's mischief.

shloka:
संभ्रमः त्यजताम् एष सर्वैः वालि कृते महान् |
मलयोऽयम् गिरिवरो भयम् न इह अस्ति वालिनः
translation:
