"Perplexity be warded off... all of you discarded that great fear from Vali or his cruelty... there 
is no scare from Vali here on this best mountain, for it is Mt. Malaya...

shloka:
यस्मात् उद्विग्न चेताः त्वम् विद्रुतो हरिपुंगव |
तम् क्रूर दर्शनम् क्रूरम् न इह पश्यामि वालिनम्
translation:
"By whom you are bewildered at heart and running away, oh, the best monkey Sugreeva, I do not see that 
cruel-looking, cruel Vali here... [4- 2-15]

shloka:
यस्मात् तव भयम् सौम्य पूर्वजात् पाप कर्मणः |
स न इह वाली दुष्टात्मा न ते पश्यामि अहम् भयम्
translation:
"From whom your fear is spurted, oh, gentle Sugreeva, that elder brother of yours, who is an evildoer 
and the one with harmful intent... that Vali is not here. Therefore I perceive no fear from him...

shloka:
अहो शाखा मृगत्वम् ते व्यक्तम् एव प्लवंगम |
लघु चित्ततया आत्मानम् न स्थापयसि यो मतौ
translation:
"Aha! You made a monkey of yourself, oh, monkey, and you feel small, thus you are not able to stay firm 
in your mind by that fickleness, and your monkeyshines is clear by it...

shloka:
बुद्धि विज्ञान संपन्न इङ्गितैः सर्वम् आचर |
न हि अबुद्धिम् गतो राजा सर्व भूतानि शास्ति हि
translation:
"Keep your intellect and wisdom firm, and express all your intents rightly in your body language in 
all your undertakings... certainly, a king getting into unintelligence cannot command all his subjects..." 
So said Hanuma to Sugreeva.

shloka:
सुग्रीवः तु शुभम् वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा सर्वम् हनूमतः |
ततः शुभतरम् वाक्यम् हनूमन्तम् उवाच ह
translation:
Sugreeva thus hearing entirely to all the propitious words of Hanuma spoke to Hanuma this opportune 
sentence, positively.

shloka:
दीर्घ बाहू विशालाक्षौ शर चाप असि धारिणौ |
कस्य न स्यात् भयम् दृष्ट्वा हि एतौ सुर सुत उपमौ
translation:
"Lengthy are their arms, broad are their eyes and they are the wielders of arrows, bows and swords... 
and on seeing them, to whom there will be no scare? These two are like the sons of some divinity..." 
Sugreeva thus spoke to Hanuma.

shloka:
वालि प्रणिहितौ एव शन्के अहम् पुरुषोत्तमौ |
राजानो बहु मित्राः च विश्वासो न अत्र हि क्षमः
translation:
"I presume these two... those best of men are abetted by Vali to assault me... for, the kings like Vali 
do have many friends and trusting them absolutely is an unpardonable mistake...

shloka:
अरयः च मनुष्येण विज्ञेयाः छद्म चारिणः |
विश्वस्तानाम् अविश्वस्ताः छिद्रेषु प्रहरन्ति अपि
translation:
"By men the enemies are to be assessed... for, they move in disguise and distrustful enemies will trounce 
the complacently self-assured ones that relax in their own self-confidence on any possible occasion...

shloka:
कृत्येषु वाली मेधावी राजानो बहु दर्शनः |
भवन्ति पर हन्तारः ते ज्ञेयाः प्राकृतैः नरैः
translation:
"In exploits Vali is an ingenious one... and the kings will be observing many aspects of their enemies 
to eliminate them... and they the kings are to be known even by ordinary people... [4- 2- 23]

shloka:
तौ त्वया प्राकृतेन एव गत्वा ज्ञेयौ प्लवंगम |
इङ्गितानाम् प्रकारैः च रूपव्या भाषणेन च
translation:
"Begone to them oh, monkey Hanuma, in a commoner's form, for your monkey-hood is distinguishable by 
Vali's agents, and know the intentions of those two by their conduct, by their semblance, and by their 
conversation, as well...

shloka:
लक्षयस्व तयोः भावम् प्रहृष्ट मनसौ यदि |
विश्वासयन् प्रशंसाभिः इङ्गितैः च पुनः पुनः
translation:
"Aim at their concepts and if they are pleasant-hearted, duly create confidence in them by conducting 
yourself, and also commending them again and again... oh, best of monkeys, Hanuma, set their face towards 
me alone in a compassionate manner, and you inquire about the reason of their entering this forest alone... 
of those bows wielders... [4-2-25, 26]

shloka:
शुद्ध आत्मानौ यदि एतौ जानीहि त्वम् प्लवंगम |
व्याभाषितैः वा रूपैः वा विज्ञेया दुष्टता अनयोः
translation:
"You shall know whether those two are clean at heart or otherwise, or about their evil-mindedness or 
otherwise by conversation..." Thus Sugreeva said to Hanuma.

shloka:
इति एवम् कपिराजेन संदिष्टो मारुतात्मजः |
चकार गमने बुद्धिम् यत्र तौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
Thus this way ordered by Sugreeva, the king of monkeys, Hanuma, the son of Air-god made up his mind 
to go there, where Rama and Lakshmana are.

shloka:
तथा इति संपूज्य वचः तु तस्य
कपेः सुभीतस्य दुरासदस्य |
महानुभावो हनुमान् ययौ तदा
स यत्र रामो 
अतिबली स लक्ष्मणः
translation:
That marvellous monkey Hanuma agreeing for the words of that inaccessible and very much frightened Sugreeva, 
and on respectfully replying him saying that, 'I will do accordingly...' proceeded there where that 
highly mighty Rama is there along with Lakshmana.

shloka:
वचो विज्ञाय हनुमान् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
पर्वतात् ऋष्यमूकात् तु पुप्लुवे यत्र राघवौ
translation:
Mindful of the words of noble-souled Sugreeva, Hanuma took his flight from Mt. Rishyamuka to where Raghavaa-s 
are.

shloka:
कपि रूपम् परित्यज्य हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः |
भिक्षु रूपम् ततो भेजे शठबुद्धितया कपिः
translation:
Casting off his monkey's semblance Air-god's son Hanuma attained the persona of an ascetic, for that 
monkey is incredulous in mind about Raghava-s.

shloka:
ततः च हनुमान् वाचा श्लक्ष्णया सुमनोज्ञया |
विनीतवत् उपागम्य राघवौ प्रणिपत्य च
translation:
Then on nearing Raghava-s that Hanuma voicing softly and well pleasingly like an obedient one, that 
best monkey befittingly hailed, greeted and praised those two valiant ones. [4-3-3, 4a]

shloka: संपूज्य विधिवद् वीरौ हनुमान् वानरोत्तमः
translation:
The best Vanara Hanuma spoke soft-wordily, as desired by Sugreeva, to those candidly resolute ones, 
on making reverent obeisance to both of them. [4-3-4b, 5a]

shloka: राजर्षि देव प्रतिमौ तापसौ संशित व्रतौ
translation:
"You two look like kingly saints, or deities by your build, ascetics with blest vows, but with ideal 
complexions... how come you arrived at this countryside scaring the herds of animals and other inhabitants 
of this forest... [4-3-5b, 6]

shloka:
पम्पा तीर रुहान् वृक्षान् वीक्षमाणौ समंततः |
इमाम् नदीम् शुभ जलाम् शोभयन्तौ तरस्विनौ
translation:
"You mighty ones you are watching the trees grown on the banks of Pampa from all over, and owing to 
your presence on these banks you make this river Pampa with its propitious waters to shine forth... 
but you with your golden hue appear as courageous ones, yet you sigh over repeatedly, you wear jute-cloths, 
yet you look mighty shouldered... who are you that distress all the beings in this forest... [4-3-7, 
8]

shloka:
सिंह विप्रेक्षितौ वीरौ महाबल पराक्रमौ |
शक्र चाप निभे चापे गृहीत्वा शत्रु नाशनौ
translation:
"Dauntless, bold and brave are you with sharp glances of lions, wielding bows like that of Indra's bow 
you are the real enemy destroyers... glorious, splendid, and even impetuous you appear like Sacred Bulls... 
elephant's trunks are your arms... and you foremost among men are self-resplendent... [4-3-9, 10]

shloka:
प्रभया पर्वत इन्द्रः असौ युवयोः अवभासितः |
राज्य अर्हौ अमर प्रख्यौ कथम् देशम् इह आगतौ
translation:
"This lord-like mountain is effulgent with your effulgence, you two look as kingdom-worthy, or worthy 
divinities, but how you have reached this countryside now...

shloka:
पद्म पत्र ईक्षणौ वीरौ जटा मण्डल धारिणौ |
अन्योन्य सदृशौ वीरौ देव लोकात् इह आगतौ
translation:
"Eyes of yours are like fine lotus petals, are you superhuman... nay, you wear tufts and braids, are 
you some undaunted human ascetics... nay, you look clonal, are you from some world of gods... nay, you 
are on earth, does this earth have a chance to receive Sun and Moon on her by her fortune... nay, are 
you some broad-chested deities in human form... lion-shouldered, very vehement and vigorous like Sacred 
Bulls... who you might be... [4-3-12, 13, 14a]

shloka: आयताः च सुवृत्ताः च बाहवः परिघोपमाः
translation:
"Also lengthy are your hands, and spherical are your shoulders similar to clubs... they are worthy for 
decoration with every kind of ornament, for what reason they are undecorated... [4-3-14b, 15a]

shloka: उभौ योग्यौ अहम् मन्ये रक्षितुम् पृथिवीम् इमाम्
translation:
"I deem that each of you are the choicest one to protect the earth adorned with Mt Meru and Vindhya 
range, and with all her oceans and forests... [4-3-15b, 16a]

shloka: इमे च धनुषी चित्रे श्लक्ष्णे चित्र अनुलेपने
translation:
"And these awesome bows are polished with odd things are smooth, and they are brightening like the gilded 
Thunderbolt of Indra.

shloka: संपूर्णाः च शितैः बाणैः तूणाः च शुभ दर्शनाः
translation:
"Full with hazardous, life terminating, fiery snake like sharp arrows are these quivers, admirable in 
their appearance... [4-3-17b, 18a]

shloka: महा प्रमाणौ विपुलौ तप्त हाटक भूषणौ
translation:
"Dazzling are these amply wide, broad and gilded swords like the snakes just released from their moults... 
[4-3-18b, 19a]

shloka: एवम् माम् परिभाषन्तम् कस्माद् वै न अभि भाषतः
translation:
"When I have been talking to you this way, what for you don't speak up... one named Sugreeva, somebody 
virtuous and worthily one among monkeys is expelled by his brother Vali, and he is roaming all over 
the world sorrowfully... [4-3-19b, 20]

shloka:
प्राप्तः अहम् प्रेषितः तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना |
राज्ञा वानर मुख्यानाम् हनुमान् नाम वानरः
translation:
"Delegated by that great soul and the king of important monkeys Sugreeva, I have come here and by name 
I am Hanuma, another Vanara...

shloka:
युवाभ्याम् स हि धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवः सख्यम् इच्छति |
तस्य माम् सचिवम् वित्तम् वानरम् पवनात्मजम्
translation:
"He that righteous Sugreeva is desiring friendship with you two, and know me as a monkey and his minister, 
the son of Air-god... I had to come here from Mt. Rishyamuka in an ascetic's form only to appease that 
Sugreeva, and I can wend my way by my will, and wear any guise as I wish..." Hanuma said so to those 
brothers. [4-3-22, 23]

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु हनुमाम् तौ वीरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्य कुशलः पुनः न उवाच किंचन
translation:
Saying thus to those valorous Rama and Lakshmana, Hanumaan, the sententious wordsmith, spoke nothing 
further.

shloka:
एतत् श्रुत्वा वचः तस्य रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत् |
प्रहृष्ट वदनः श्रीमान् भ्रातरम् पार्श्वतः स्थितम्
translation:
Hearing all those words said by Hanuma, that illustrious Rama is well pleased facially, spoke to his 
brother Lakshmana who is standing at his side.

shloka:
सचिवो अयम् कपीन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
तम् एव काङ्क्षमाणस्य मम अन्तिकम् इह आगतः
translation:
"He is the minister of that noteworthy soul and king of monkeys, Sugreeva... whom alone I cherish, but 
he himself has drew nigh of me, on his own...

shloka:
तम् अभ्यभाष सौमित्रे सुग्रीव सचिवम् कपिम् |
वाक्यज्ञम् मधुरैः वाक्यैः स्नेह युक्तम् अरिन्दम
translation:
"Soumitri, with this minister of Sugreeva, the knower of sententiousness and a pleasant worded one, 
and one with friendliness you exchange pleasantries with that enemy destroyer Hanuma...

shloka:
न अन् ऋग्वेद विनीतस्य न अ\-\-यजुर्वेद धारिणः |
न अ\-\-साम वेद विदुषः शक्यम् एवम् विभाषितुम्
translation:
"Nay...the non-knower of Rig Veda, or the non-rememberer of Yajur Veda, or the non-scholar of Saama 
Veda... can possibly, or truly speak this way...

shloka:
नूनम् व्यकरणम् कृत्स्नम् अनेन बहुधा श्रुतम् |
बहु व्याहरता अनेन न किंचित् अप शब्दितम्
translation:
"Definitely grammar is severally and comprehensively learnt by him... and though much is said by him 
not a single word has gone amiss of verbiage...

shloka:
न मुखे नेत्रयोः च अपि ललाटे च भ्रुवोः तथा |
अन्येषु अपि च सर्वेषु दोषः संविदितः क्वचित्
translation:
"On his face or eyes, or on forehead or brows, or on other faculties of expression no fault is found...even 
at the least...

shloka:
अविस्तरम् असंदिग्धम् अविलम्बितम् अव्यथम् |
उरःस्थम् कण्ठगम् वाक्यम् वर्तते मध्यमे स्वरम्
translation:
"Unexpanded, un-doubtful, un-delaying and non-dissonant is the tenor of his speech, and it comports 
in his chest or throat in a medium tone...

shloka:
संस्कार क्रम संपन्नाम् अद्भुताम् अविलम्बिताम् |
उच्चारयति कल्याणीम् वाचम् हृदय हर्षिणीम्
translation:
"He has orderly refinement in speech that is remarkable and un-delaying, and he speaks propitious words 
that are heart-pleasing...

shloka:
अनया चित्रया वाचा त्रिस्थान व्यंजनस्थयाः |
कस्य न आराध्यते चित्तम् उद्यत् असे अरेः अपि
translation:
"His speech is generated in three places is enthralling... and whose heart is it that is disenchanted, 
even that of an enemy after raising his sword at him, on hearing his speech...

shloka:
एवम् विधो यस्य दूतो न भवेत् पार्थिवस्य तु |
सिद्ध्यन्ति हि कथम् तस्य कार्याणाम् गतयोऽनघ
translation:
"Oh, faultless Lakshmana, if this sort of envoy is not there to a king, really how can that king accomplishes 
his ways and means...

shloka:
एवम् गुण गणैर् युक्ता यस्य स्युः कार्य साधकाः |
तस्य सिद्ध्यन्ति सर्वेऽर्था दूत वाक्य प्रचोदिताः
translation:
"Should a king have this kind of work accomplishers with a variety of virtues, all his objectives will 
be achieved impelled by such an envoy's words..." Rama thus said to Lakshmana.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सौमित्रिः सुग्रीव सचिवम् कपिम् |
अभ्यभाषत वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यज्ञम् पवनात्मजम्
translation:
When said thus by Rama, wise-worded Lakshmana spoke to that monkey and the minister of Sugreeva, namely 
Hanuma, the son of Air-god, who is equally a wise-worded one.

shloka:
विदिता नौ गुणा विद्वन् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
तम् एव च अवाम् मार्गावः सुग्रीवम् प्लवगेश्वरम्
translation:
"The virtues of that great soul Sugreeva are known to us, oh, scholarly monkey, we for our part are 
in search of that lord of fly-jumpers Sugreeva alone...

shloka:
यथा ब्रवीषि हनुमान् सुग्रीव वचनाद् इह |
तत् तथा हि करिष्यावो वचनात् तव सत्तम
translation:
"As you communicated the words of Sugreeva, oh, gentle Hanuma, by them and by your words we indeed wish 
to do accordingly...

shloka:
तत् तस्य वाक्यम् निपुणम् निशम्य
प्रहृष्ट रूपः पवनात्मजः कपिः |
मनः समाधाय जय उपपत्तौ
सख्यम् 
तदा कर्तुम् इयेष ताभ्याम्
translation:
On observing that operative sentence of Lakshmana the monkey Hanuma is gladdened, as seen from his composure, 
and kept his mind at ease at the prospective victory, and then he wished to materialise the pact of 
friendship between Rama ad Sugreeva, at the earliest.

shloka:
ततः प्रहृष्टो हनुमान् कृत्यवान् इति तत् वचः |
श्रुत्वा मधुर भावम् च सुग्रीवम् मनसा गतः
translation:
Then that Hanuma, who has good deeds for his credit, on hearing the words of
Lakshmana, and even knowing that they are finely meaningful, he rejoicingly recalled in his mind
that Sugreeva's effort is going to fructify.

shloka:
भाव्यो राज्यागमः तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
यत् अयम् कृत्यवान् प्राप्तः कृत्यम् च एतत् उपागतम्
translation:
"Conceivable is the retrieval of the kingdom by that great souled Sugreeva...and for
which deed, this purposive Rama has come, and that deed desired by Rama is also achievable by
Sugreeva, and thus all this has came by..." thus thought Hanuma.

shloka:
ततः परम संहृष्टः हनुमान् प्लवगोत्तमः |
प्रति उवाच ततो वाक्यम् रामम् वाक्य विशारदः
translation:
Then Hanuma, the ablest flyer is thus very gladdened...and in turn then spoke to
that very learned one, namely Rama. [4- 4-3]

shloka:
किम् अर्थम् त्वम् वनम् घोरम् पम्पा कानन मण्डितम् |
आगतः सानुजो दुर्गम् नाना व्याल मृग आयुतम्
translation:
"What for you have come into these perilous forests hemming in Pampa Lake along with
your brother, for these are impenetrable forests abounding with many a serpent and animal?" Thus
Hanuma asked Rama.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणो राम चोदितः |
आचचक्षे महात्मानम् रामम् दशरथात्मजम्
translation:
On hearing the words of Hanuma, Lakshmana motivated by Rama, narrated about the
great soul Rama, the son of Dasharatha.

shloka:
राजा दशरथो नाम द्युतिमान् धर्म वत्सलः |
चातुर् वर्ण्यम् स्व धर्मेण नित्यम् एव अभिपालयन्
translation:
"The king named Dasharatha, a resplendent one and the patron of virtue was ruling
the four-caste system with its, and by his own rectitude, for he is also bound within that
four-caste system...

shloka:
न द्वेष्टा विद्यते तस्य स तु द्वेष्टि न कंचन |
स तु सर्वेषु भूतेषु पितामह इव अपरः
translation:
There is none despising him, nor he despised any and for all the living beings he is
like the Grandparent Brahma on earth...

shloka:
अग्निष्टोमादिभिः यज्ञैः इष्टवान् आप्त दक्षिणैः |
तस्य अयम् पूर्वजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः
translation:
"And he, King Dasharatha who performed rituals agniSToma and the like Vedic rituals
wherein he donated liberally, and this one is his eldest son, and he is renowned among people by
the name of Rama...

shloka:
शरण्यः सर्व भूतानाम् पितुः निर्देश पारगः |
ज्येष्टो दशरथस्य अयम् पुत्राणाम् गुणवत्तरः
translation:
"He is the protector of all beings and the follower of father's directives, he is
the eldest one among the sons of King Dasharatha... possessor of high virtues, qualities and royal
fortune befitting to a king... but he is deprived of his kingdom, and came hither to dwell in the
forests... nevertheless, followed by me...[4-4-9, 10]

shloka:
भार्यया च महाभाग सीतया अनुगतो वशी |
दिन क्षये महातेजाः प्रभ एव दिवाकरः
translation:
"With his wife Seetha following him, oh, highly fortunate Hanuma, this
self-controlled and highly resplendent Rama came to forests like the Sun followed by his consort
Prabha, who vanishes when the day is abated...

shloka:
अहम् अस्य अवरः भ्राता गुणैः दास्यम् उपागतः |
कृतज्ञस्य बहुज्ञस्य लक्ष्मणो नाम नामतः
translation:
"I am the one who obtained servitude by the justness of this faithful and
knowledgeable one, and his younger brother, by name I am named as Lakshmana...

shloka:
सुखार्हस्य महार्हस्य सर्वभूत हितात्मनः |
ऐश्वर्येण विहीनस्य वनवासे रतस्य च
translation:
"He who aspires to keep up the well-being of all the beings, and he who is merited
for all comforts and respectability is now devoid of his prosperity and predisposed to forest
dwelling... such as he is, his wife is abducted by a guise changing demon in a lonely place, of
whom we know not... we know not which demon stole his wife... [4-4-13, 14]

shloka:
दनुः नाम दितेः पुत्रः शापात् राक्षसताम् गतः |
आख्यातः तेन सुग्रीवः समर्थो वानराधिपः
translation:
"One named Danu, son of Diti, who acquired demon-hood by curse had said that
Sugreeva, the chief of monkeys, is a capable one, and he even said, "that great valorous Sugreeva
can know about the abductor of your wife..." saying thus that Danu is released from the curse of
his demon-hood, moved skyward and went away to heavens while becoming self-luminous... [4-4-15,
16]

shloka:
एतत् ते सर्वम् आख्यातम् याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः |
अहम् चैव च रामः च सुग्रीवम् शरणम् गतौ
translation:
"All this is informed to you, as it is as you have asked..Myself and Rama, we now
have our recourse to Sugreeva alone...

shloka:
एष दत्त्वा च वित्तानि प्राप्य च अनुत्तमम् यशः |
लोकनाथः पुरा भूत्वा सुग्रीवम् नाथम् इच्छति
translation:
"He who gave away riches in charity, who obtained unequalled renown and who himself
was the lord of this world earlier, now accepts the lordship of Sugreeva...

shloka:
सीता यस्य स्नुषा च आसीत् शरण्यो धर्मवत्सलः |
तस्य पुत्रः शरण्यस्य सुग्रीवम् शरणम् गतः
translation:
"Who was a patron of virtue and who himself was a shelterer, to whom Seetha is the
daughter-in-law, such a shelterer's son Rama is now taking shelter under Sugreeva...

shloka:
सर्व लोकस्य धर्मात्मा शरण्यः शरणम् पुरा |
गुरुर् मे राघवः सोऽयम् सुग्रीवम् शरणम् गतः
translation:
"He who is a virtuous one and protector of all the world, and who is the only refuge
for all in earlier times... such a Raaghava, my mentor, is now seeking refuge with Sugreeva...

shloka:
यस्य प्रसादे सततम् प्रसीदेयुः इमाः प्रजाः |
स रामः वानरेन्द्रस्य प्रसादम् अभिकाङ्क्षते
translation:
"By whose beneficence all these people are always delighted, he that Rama is now
seeking benefaction from the lord of monkeys...

shloka:
येन सर्व गुणोपेताः पृथिव्याम् सर्व पार्थिवाः |
मानिताः सततम् राज्ञा सदा दशरथेन वै
translation:
"By which kingDasharatha, are all the kings with all possible good attributes are
always, and at all the times were esteemed to be safeguarded as defensible kings, such king's
eldest son Rama, renowned in all the three worlds for his own sheltering the needy, has now taken
shelter under monkeys lord Sugreeva... [4-4-22, 23]

shloka:
शोक अभिभूते रामे तु शोक आर्ते शरणम् गते |
कर्तुम् अर्हति सुग्रीवः प्रसादम् सह यूथपैः
translation:
"One who is rebuffed by sadness, and even agonised by it had already sought refuge,
hence it is apt of Sugreeva to do favour in Rama's respect along with other vanara commanders..."
Lakshmana said thus to Hanuma.

shloka:
एवम् ब्रुवाणम् सौमित्रिम् करुणम् स अश्रु पातनम् |
हनुमान् प्रति उवाच इदम् वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारदः
translation:
To Lakshmana, who is telling that piteously with tears falling out, the eminently
lettered Hanumaan said this in his return.

shloka:
ईदृशा बुद्धि संपन्ना जितक्रोधा जितेइन्द्रियाः |
द्रष्टव्या वानरेइन्द्रेण दिष्ट्या दर्शनम् आगताः
translation:
"Intellectuals of your kind, who have conquered anger and senses are to be seen by
the chief of monkeys Sugreeva, for your advent is godsend...

shloka:
स हि राज्यात् च विभ्रष्टः कृत वैरः च वालिना |
हृत दारो वने त्रस्तः भ्रात्रा विनिकृतः भृशम्
translation:
"He who is made as an enemy, very muchinsulted, and abrogated from kingdom by his
own brother Vali, that Sugreeva is roaming about forests fearing him alone, his own brother Vali...

shloka:
करिष्यति स साहाय्यम् युवयोः भास्करात्मजः |
सुग्रीवः सह च अस्माभिः सीतायाः परिमार्गणे
translation:
"He that son of Sun, Sugreeva, will render help to you two, joining forces of our
like Vanara-s in searching Seetha..."

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्त्वा हनुमान् श्लक्ष्णम् मधुरया गिरा |
बभाषे साधु गच्छामः सुग्रीवम् इति राघवम्
translation:
Thus Hanuman on speaking melodious words with politeness, also said to Raghava as,
"good, we may now approach Sugreeva...."

shloka:
एवम् ब्रुवन्तम् धर्मात्मा हनूमन्तम् स लक्ष्मणः |
प्रतिपूज्य यथा न्यायम् इदम् प्रोवाच राघवम्
translation:
Hanuma when said thus virtuous Lakshmana adored him customarily in the way befitting
to an envoy, and spoke this to Rama...

shloka:
कपिः कथयते हृष्टो यथा अयम् मारुतात्मजः |
कृत्यवान् सोऽपि संप्राप्तः कृत कृत्योऽसि राघव
translation:
"Raghava, as to how this monkey seems to be happy in meeting us, by way of his
narration, and he too neared us as an aspirant of some deed to be performed by us, hence joining
them seems to fulfil your mission...

shloka:
प्रसन्न मुख वर्णः च व्यक्तम् हृष्टः च भाषते |
न अनृतम् वक्ष्यते वीरो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः
translation:
"He is talking with a lucid expression and pleasing facial tinge by which he seems
to be gladdened at his heart... needless is telling untruths to such a valiant son of Air-god,
Hanuma, isn't it!" So said Laskhmana to Rama

shloka:
ततः स सुमहाप्राज्ञः हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः |
जगाम आदाय तौ वीरौ हरि राजाय राघवौ
translation:
Then he that very intelligent son of Air-god Hanuma, took those two valorous
Raghava-s to go to the king of monkeys Sugreeva.

shloka:
भिक्षु रूपम् परित्यज्य वानरम् रूपम् आस्थितः |
पृष्टम् आरोप्य तौ वीरौ जगाम कपिकुङ्जरः
translation:
On discarding the ascetic's semblance that estimable monkey Hanuma obtained his own
monkey's form, and mounting those two valiant ones onto his back he proceeded towards Sugreeva.

shloka:
स तु विपुल यशाः कपि प्रवीरः पवनसुतः कृत कृत्यवत् प्रहृष्टः |
गिरि वरम् उरुविक्रमः प्रयातः स शुभमतिः सह राम लक्ष्मणाभ्याम्
translation:
Hanuma, the extensively renowned heroic son of Air-god with pious mind and highly
audacious nature, is then gladdened like the one whose difficult deed is just accomplished, thus he
gladly travelled to that mountain where Sugreeva is abiding, along with Rama and Lakshmana.

shloka:
ऋश्यमूकात् तु हनुमान् गत्वा तम् मलयम् गिरिम् |
आचचक्षे तदा वीरौ कपि राजाय राघवौ
translation:
Hanuma on going from Mt. Rishyamuka to Mt. Malaya, has reported to the king of monkeys Sugreeva, about 
the two valiant Raghava-s.

shloka:
अयम् रामो महाप्राज्ञ संप्राप्तो दृढ विक्रमः |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा रामोऽयम् सत्य विक्रमः
translation:
"Oh! great discerner Sugreeva, this is Rama... oh, stubbornly valiant Sugreeva, this virtuously valiant 
Rama arrived along with his brother Lakshmana...

shloka:
इक्ष्वाकूणाम् कुले जातो रामो दशरथात्मजः |
धर्मे निगदितः च एव पितुर् निर्देश कारकः
translation:
"Rama is the son of king Dasharatha, one born in Ikshvaku dynasty, an adept one in virtue and thus an 
adherent of his father's orders...

shloka:
राजसूय अश्वमेधैः च वह्निः येन अभितर्पितः |
दक्षिणाः च तथा उत्सृष्टा गावः शत सहस्रशः
translation:
"By whom the ritual fire is well worshipped in Vedic rituals like rajasuuya, ashvametha, and thus cows 
in hundreds and thousands are donated in those rituals, by whom this earth is ruled devoutly and truthful 
to his word, such Dasharatha's son is this Rama, who has to come to forests owing to a woman... [4-5-4, 
5]

shloka:
तस्य अस्य वसतो अरण्ये नियतस्य महात्मनः |
रावणेन हृता भार्या स त्वाम् शरणम् आगतः
translation:
"Ravana stole the wife of this principled one and great soul Rama when dwelling in forests, such as 
he is, he came seeking your refuge...

shloka:
भवता सख्य कामौ तौ भ्रातरौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |
प्रगृह्य च अर्चयस्व एतौ पूजनीयतमौ उभौ
translation:
"These two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, are interested to make friendship with you... thus you receive 
these two and worship them, for they are most venerable ones..." Hanuma thus advised Sugreeva.

shloka:
श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यम् सुग्रीवो वानर अधिपः |
दर्शनीयतमो भूत्वा प्रीत्या उवाच राघवम्
translation:
On hearing Hanuma's words Sugreeva, the chief of monkeys has become presentable and gladly spoke to 
Rama.

shloka:
भवान् धर्म विनीतः च सुतपाः सर्व वत्सलः |
आख्याता वायुपुत्रेण तत्त्वतो मे भवद् गुणाः
translation:
"You are a trained one in treading righteous path, best by your scruples, and a kindlier one to all, 
so said Air-god's son Hanuma to me about your attributes, in subtlety...

shloka:
तन् मम एव एष सत्कारो लाभः च एव उत्तमः प्रभो |
यत् त्वम् इच्छसि सौहार्दम् वानरेण मया सह
translation:
"Therefor oh, lord, you wish to make friendship with a monkey like me, thereby this is an honour and 
a best achievement to me alone...

shloka:
रोचते यदि मे सख्यम् बाहुः एष प्रसारितः |
गृह्यताम् पाणिना पाणिः मर्यादा बध्यताम् ध्रुवा
translation:
"If you aspire my friendship here I extend my arm, take this hand of mine into yours, thus let the convention 
be stably made fast..." Thus Sugreeva proffered friendship to Rama.

shloka:
एतत् तु वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य सुभाषितम् |
संप्रहृष्ट मना हस्तम् पीडयामास पाणिना
translation:
Rama is gladdened at heart on listening all those words well said by Sugreeva, and then clutched Sugreeva's 
hand in his, and ardently abiding by the vow of friendship he embraced Sugreeva, grippingly and happily. 
[4-5-12, 13a]

shloka: ततो हनूमान् संत्यज्य भिक्षु रूपम् अरिन्दमः
translation:
Then the destroyer of enemies Hanuma discarding the guise of ascetic assumed his original monkey form, 
and on producing fire with two sticks then made it to glow. decorated, worshipped with flowers, then 
gladly and devoutly placed that fire in between Rama and Sugreeva. [4-5-13b,14,15a]

shloka: ततो अग्निम् दीप्यमानम् तौ चक्रतुः च प्रदक्षिणम्
translation:
Then those two performed circumambulations to that well glowing ritual fire, and thus, Rama and Sugreeva 
entered into the pact of friendship. [4-5-15, 16a]

shloka: ततः सुप्रीत मनसौ तौ उभौ हरि राघवौ
translation:
And then gladdened at heart are those two, that monkey and Raghava, gazed enough at each other eye-to-eye, 
but their hearts did not derive any fraternal satisfaction. [4-5-16b, 17a]

shloka: त्वम् वयस्योऽसि हृद्यः मे हि एकम् दुःखम् सुखम् च नौ
translation:
Sugreeva rejoicingly said to Raghava, "you are the amiable friend of mine, henceforth our mirth or miseries 
are same for us..." [4-5-17b, 18a]

shloka: ततः सुपर्ण बहुलाम् भंक्त्वा शाखाम् सुपुष्पिताम्
translation:
And then Sugreeva snapped off and spread a fully flowered tree-branch of sala tree with many leaves, 
and sat on it along with Rama. [4-5-18b, 19a]

shloka: लक्ष्मनाय अथ संहृष्टो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः
translation:
Then Hanuma the son of Air, gladly gave a well-flowered branch of sandalwood tree to Lakshmana... [4-5-19b, 
20a]

shloka: ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवः श्लक्ष्णम् मधुरया गिरा
translation:
Then that delighted Sugreeva with his sweet words, and with his eyes quavering in happiness, replied 
Rama softly. [4-5-20b, 21a]

shloka: अहम् विनिकृतो राम चरमि इह भय आर्दितः
translation:
"Rama, I am ridiculed, stolen is my wife, I move here about in these forests with dread and fear haunting 
me... I took refuge in this impenetrable forest... [4-5-21b, 22a]

shloka: सोऽहम् त्रस्तो वने भीतो वसामि उद् भ्रान्त चेतनः
translation:
"Oh, Raghava, my brother denounced me, he even made me an enemy of his, such as I am I am living in 
these forests with scare and fear, and with dismayed vitality... [4-5-22b, 23a]

shloka: वालिनो मे महाभाग भय आर्तस्य अभयम् कुरु
translation:
"Oh, highly fortunate Rama, affirm fearlessness to me from Vali by who I am highly intimidated, and 
as to how there will be fearlessness to me from him, it will be apt of you to accomplish that, that 
way... [4-5-23b, 24a]

shloka: एवम् उक्तः तु तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्म वत्सलः
translation:
When thus said, that resplendent and righteous one being the patron of virtue Rama replied Sugreeva, 
as though laughing off. [4-5-24b, 25a]

shloka: उपकार फलम् मित्रम् विदितम् मे महाकपे
translation:
"A friend is the resultant factor of helpfulness... that I know... oh, great monkey I intend eliminate 
that Vali, the abductor of your wife... [4-5-2b, 26a5]

shloka: अमोघोः सूर्य संकाशाः मम इमे निशिताः शराः
translation:
"Unfailing are these arrows of mine, scorchers like sun, sharp ones tied with eagle feathers, similar 
to Indra's Thunderbolts, sharp are their point and straight is their egress, similar to enraged snakes, 
and these arrows of mine will be speeded up to fall on that vicious Vali... [4-5-26b, 27, 28a]

shloka: तम् अद्य वालिनम् पश्य तीक्ष्णैः आशी विष उपमैः
translation:
"You will see now itself the falling of Vali like a splintered mountain onto ground, when completely 
ruined by these cruel arrows that are similar to venomous snakes..." Thus Rama inculcated confidence 
in Sugreeva. [4-5-28b, 29a]

shloka:
स तु तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राघवस्य आत्मनोहितम् |
सुग्रीवः परम प्रीतः परमम् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
On hearing Raghava's words that are appeasing for his self, Sugreeva is very completely satisfied and 
said this fine sentence. [4-5-29b, c]

shloka:
तव प्रसादेन नृसिंह वीर
प्रियाम् च राज्यम् च समाप्नुयाम् अहम् |
तथा कुरु त्वम् नर देव वैरिणम्
यथा न हिंस्यत् स पुनर् मम अग्रजम्
translation:
"By your grace, oh, lion among men, let me regain my wife and kingdom too... oh, god of humans, as to 
how he does not suffer me again, thus you may please make happen... let not my elder brother turned 
as an enemy of mine suffer me again...

shloka:
सीत कपीन्द्र क्षणदा चराणाम्
राजीव हेम ज्वलनोपमानानि |
सुग्रीव राम प्रणय पसङ्गे
वामानि नेत्राणि 
समम् स्फुरन्ति
translation:
During the friendly conversation of Rama and Sugreeva, the left eyes of Seetha, Vali and Ravana that 
bear similitude with lotuses, golden orbs, and fireballs respectively have fluttered equally.

shloka:
पुनरेव अब्रवीत् प्रीतः राघवम् रघुनन्दनम् |
अयम् आख्याति ते राम सेवकः मन्त्रि सत्तमः
translation:
Then Sugreeva who is gladdened again spoke to Rama of Raghu's dynasty, "My best
minister and this servant of yours Hanuma informed me of the reason for which you have come to
uninhabited forests along with your brother Lakshmana, and that while living in the forest, and
when you and this courageous Lakshmana are not her alongside a demon stole your wife Maithili, the
daughter of Janaka, wailing as she was.

shloka:
अन्तरम् प्रेप्सुना तेन हत्वा गृध्रम् जटायुषम् |
भार्या वियोगजम् दुःखम् प्रापितः तेन रक्ष्सा
translation:
"And he also said about that arch demon's killing an eagle named Jatayu on waiting
for an opportunity, and his causing an agony in you by way of separating your wife.

shloka:
भर्या वियोगजम् दुःखम् न चिरात् त्वम् विमोक्ष्यसे |
अहम् ताम् आनयिष्यामि नष्टाम् वेदश्रुतीम् इव
translation:
"Before long you will get rid off your agony caused by the separation of wife, for I
will fetch her very soon, like the retrieval Vedic Scriptures.

shloka:
रसातले वा वर्तन्तीम् वर्तन्तीम् वा नभः तले |
अहम् आनीय दास्यामि तव भार्याम् अरिन्दम
translation:
"Oh! Enemy destroyer, Rama, I will fetch your wife to give her to you whether she is
in netherworlds or even in empyrean worlds.

shloka:
इदम् तथ्यम् मम वचः त्वम् अवेहि च राघव |
न शक्या सा जरयितुम् अपि सः इन्द्रैः सुर असुरैः
translation:
"You may know that this word of mine is definite oh, Raghava. Your wife is as good
as an indigestible foodstuff made with poison, indigestive even to Indra, put together with all
gods and demons. [4-6-7, 8a]

shloka:
त्यज शोकम् महाबाहो ताम् कान्ताम् आनयामि ते | ४-६-८
अनुमानात् तु जानामि मैथिली सा न संशयः |
ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रक्षसा रौउद्र कर्मणा
translation:
"Give-up your lamentation, oh, great-shouldered one, for I will bring back that lady
for you. And by inference I know her... undoubtedly I have seen Maithilee while that demon with
cruel deeds was abducting her... then she was crying piteously calling 'Rama, Rama...' and also
calling 'Lakshmana...' and she was writhing in the flanks of Ravana like the wife of serpent's
lord... [4-6-8b, 9, 10]

shloka:
आत्मना पञ्चमम् माम् हि दृष्ट्वा शैल तले स्थितम् |
उत्तरीयम् तया त्यक्तम् शुभानि आभरणानि च
translation:
"Myself being the fifth one on the cliff of the mountain, on seeing me she dropped
the upper cloth of her sari along with auspicious jewellery.

shloka:
तानि अस्माभिः गृहीतानि निहितानि च राघव |
आनयिष्यामि अहम् तानि प्रत्यभिज्ञातुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"We took those jewellery items and stored them, Raaghava... I will get them and it
will be apt of you to identify them..." thus said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
तम् अब्रवीत् ततः रामः सुग्रीवम् प्रिय वादिनम् |
आनयस्व सखे शीघ्रम् किम् अर्थम् प्रविलम्बसे
translation:
Then Rama said to that pleasant talker Sugreeva, "Get them quickly, my friend, what
for you are delaying."

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सुग्रीवः शैलस्य गहनाम् गुहाम् |
प्रविवेश ततः शीघ्रम् राघव प्रिय काम्यया
translation:
Thus said Sugreeva then entered the cavernous cave of that mountain quickly, to
fulfil the yearning of Raghava.

shloka:
उत्तरीयम् गृहीत्वा तु स तानि आभरणानि च |
इदम् पश्य इति रामाय दर्शयामास वानरः
translation:
On taking and bringing the parcel of that upper cloth with the auspicious jewellery,
"This, you see..." saying thus that monkey started to show them to Rama.

shloka:
ततो गृहीत्वा वासः तु शुभानि आभरणानि च |
अभवत् बाष्प सम्रुद्धः नीहारेण इव चन्द्रमाः
translation:
Then on taking that cloth and also the auspicious jewellery, Rama became like mist
filled moon with overfilling tears.

shloka:
सीता स्नेह प्रवृत्तेन स तु बाष्पेण दूषितः |
हा प्रिये इति रुदन् धैर्यम् उत्सृज्य न्यपतत् क्षितौ
translation:
But he who is blemished by tears that outpoured in all his friendship with Seetha,
leaving off his courage fell on the ground wailing, 'oh, dear... oh, dear...'

shloka:
हृदि कृत्वा स बहुशः तम् अलंकारम् उत्तमम् |
निशश्वास भृशम् सर्पः बिलस्थ इव रोषितः
translation:
The more he hugged those best decorative ornaments close to his heart, the more he
hissed like a wrathful serpent in a snake pit.

shloka:
अविच्छिन्न अश्रु वेगः तु सौमित्रिम् प्रेक्ष्य पार्श्वतः |
परिदेवयितुम् दीनम् रामः सम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
With the unending rush of tears he saw Lakshmana at his side and started to wail
piteously.

shloka:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्या संत्यक्तम् ह्रियमाणया |
उत्तरीयम् इदम् भूमौ शरीराद् भूषणानि च
translation:
"Lakshmana, see this upper cloth and these ornaments too of Vaidehi, shed from her
body and dropped onto the ground while she is being abducted.

shloka:
शाद्वलिन्याम् ध्रुवम् भूम्याम् सीतया ह्रियमाणया |
उत्सृष्टम् भूषणाम् इदम् तथा रूपम् हि दृश्यते
translation:
"Seetha must have definitely dropped these ornaments onto pastureland, for they
appear to be in their original shape, indeed." So said Rama to Lakshmana.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तसः तु रामेण लक्ष्मणो वाक्यम् इदम् अब्रवीत् |
न अहम् जानामि केयूरे न अहम् जानामि कुण्डले
translation:
When Rama thus said Lakshmana said this, "I know not the bracelets and I know not
the earrings But because I always salute her feet I know these anklets well...

shloka: ततः तु राघवो वाक्यम् सुग्रीवम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
" Then Rama sadly asked to Sugreeva, "tell me Sugreeva, towards which country that
ferocious looking demon abducted my dear one dearest than my lives, as spotted by you...

shloka:
क्व वा वसति तत् रक्षज़ः महत् व्यसनदम् मम |
यन् निमित्तम् अहम् सर्वान् नाशयिष्यामि राक्षसान्
translation:
"For the sake of which demon I wish to eliminate whole of the demons, that
troublemaker of mine, where does he live, either...

shloka:
हरता मैथिलीम् येन माम् च रोषयता ध्रुवम् |
आत्मनो जीवित अन्ताय मृत्यु द्वारम् अपावृतम्
translation:
"By whom Maithili is abducted and thus caused indignation in me, he has opened up
the doors of his death suicidally.

shloka:
मम दयित तमा हृता वनात् रजनिचरेण विमथ्य येन सा |
कथय मम रिपुम् तम् अद्य वै प्लवगपते यम सन्निधिम् नयामि
translation:
" Oh, king of the fly-jumpers, tell me which demon forcibly stole her, my dearest
one than all, by molesting her in the forest, tell me about that enemy of mine, for sure I will
lead him to the fore of Death today itself...

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सुग्रीवः रामेण आर्तेन वानरः |
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिः वाक्यम् सबाष्पम् बाष्प गद्गदः
translation:
Thus said by Rama in agony that monkey Sugreeva with his palms adjoined, and with
tears rolling in eyes and also voice trembling with tears said this to Rama.

shloka:
न जाने निलयम् तस्य सर्वथा पाप रक्षसः |
सामर्थ्यम् विक्रमम् वा अपि दौष्कुलेयस्य वा कुलम्
translation:
"Unfamiliar is the residence, or capability, or valour, or lineage of that sinning
demon from a sinister dynasty, in any wise...

shloka:
सत्यम् तु प्रतिजानामि त्यज शोकम् अरिन्दम |
करिष्यामि तथा यत्नम् यथा प्राप्स्यसि मैथिलीम्
translation:
"Truthfully I am promising you, oh, enemy destroyer, as to how you will get back
Maithili therefor I strive to make effort, let anguish be discarded...

shloka:
रावणम् सगणम् हत्वा परितोष्य आत्म पौरुषम् |
तथा अस्मि कर्ता नचिराद् यथा प्रीतो भविष्यसि
translation:
"As to how you will satisfy yourself on killing Ravana along with his henchmen, and
as to how to you pride yourself thereby, I will make it happen in that way in no longer a time...

shloka:
अलम् वैक्लव्यम् आलम्ब्य धैर्यम् आत्मगतम् स्मर |
त्वत् विधानाम् न सदृशम् ईदृशम् बुद्धि लाघवम्
translation:
"Enough is this clinging on to despair, recollect your inherent courage, and it is
unseemly for persons of your sort to have this kind of mental ineptness...

shloka:
मया अपि व्यसनम् प्राप्तम् भार्या विरहजम् महत् |
न अहम् एवम् हि शोचामि धैर्यम् न च परित्यजे
translation:
"Upon me too this yearning caused by the separation of wife has chanced, but I did
not despair this way, nor I have forsaken my courage...

shloka:
न अहम् ताम् अनुशोचामि प्राकृतो वानरो अपि सन् |
महात्मा च विनीतः च किम् पुनर् धृतिमान् महान्
translation:
"Though I am a primitive monkey I am not totally disheartened for the distancing of
wife, why tell about a great soul like you who are well read and courageous...

shloka:
बाष्पम् आपतितम् धैर्यात् निग्रहीतुम् त्वम् अर्हसि |
मर्यादाम् सत्त्व युक्तानाम् धृतिम् न उत्स्रष्टुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"It is apt of you to control trickling tears with courage, and equally it is inapt
of you to discard the courage and propriety of self-controlled people...

shloka:
व्यसने वा अर्थ कृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे |
विमृशन् वै स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान् न अवसीदति
translation:
"Either in a riddle, or in financial loss, or at the end of life, or in fear, a
courageous one does not sink down, but indeed introspects in his own mind...

shloka:
बालिशस् तु नरो नित्यम् वैक्लब्यम् योऽनुवर्तते |
स मज्जति अवशः शोके भार आक्रान्ता इव नौः जले
translation:
"Stupid is that man who always follows self-piteous sadness unable to control
himself, and he drowns down in that melancholy like a overweighing ship in waters...

shloka:
एषो अन्जलिः मया बद्धः प्रणयात् त्वाम् प्रसादये |
पौरुषम् श्रय शोकस्य न अन्तरम् दातुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"Adjoined are my palms in this way beseeching you in friendship, kindly bear up your
self-esteem and you should not give any leeway to sadness...

shloka:
ये शोकम् अनुवर्तन्ते न तेषाम् विद्यते सुखम् |
तेजः च क्षीयते तेषाम् न त्वम् शोचितुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"Those that delve deep into moroseness, to them there is no happiness, and their
brilliance too dwindles, thus saddening is inapt on your part...

shloka:
शोकेन अभिप्रपन्नस्य जीविते च अपि संशयः |
स शोकम् त्यज राजेन्द्र धैर्यम् आश्रय केवलम्
translation:
"One well-engulfed in sadness doubts even his life, oh, king of kings, leave off
that sadness and just hold on to courage...

shloka:
हितम् वयस्य भावेन ब्रूमि न उपदिशामि ते |
वयस्यताम् पूजयन् मे न त्वम् शोचितुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"I am telling a benefiting and friendly thought, but not instructing you, should you
regard my friendship then your saddening is inapt..." [Thus said Sugreeva to Rama.]

shloka:
मधुरम् सान्त्वितः तेन सुग्रीवेण स राघवः |
मुखम् अश्रु परि क्लिन्नम् वस्त्र अन्तेन प्रमार्जयत्
translation:
Sweetly solaced thus by that Sugreeva Rama dabbed his face with the edge of cloth,
which is covered fully with tears.

shloka:
प्रकृतिः स्थः तु काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीव वचनात् प्रभुः |
संपरिष्वज्य सुग्रीवम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Lord Rama steadied himself in his own nature by the words of Sugreeva, and on
embracing him Rama said this sentence to him.

shloka:
कर्तव्यम् यत् वयस्येन स्निग्धेन च हितेन च |
अनुरूपम् च युक्तम् च कृतम् सुग्रीव तत् त्वया
translation:
"Sugreeva, a friendly obligation that which is to be done, a benefiting, befitting
and a timely one too, is what you have performed with your friendly advise...

shloka:
एष च प्रकृतिः स्थः अहम् अनुनीतः त्वया सखे |
दुर्लभो हि ईदृशो बन्धुः अस्मिन् काले विशेषतः
translation:
"Oh, friend, I steadied myself in my own nature when implored by you... it is
impossible to get this kind of friend, especially at these times...

shloka:
किम् तु यत्नः त्वया कार्यो मैथिल्याः परिमार्गणे |
राक्षसस्य च रौद्रस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
translation:
"But, trying to search for Maithili and that furious, evil-minded demon Ravana, is
your endeavour...

shloka:
मया च यद् अनुष्ठेयम् विस्रब्धेन तत् उच्यताम् |
वर्षासु इव च सुक्षेत्रे सर्वम् संपद्यते तव
translation:
"What is to done by me that be said in all believability, and all your endeavour
will reap like the crops planted during rainy season in good lands...

shloka:
मया च यदिदम् वाक्यम् अभिमानात् समीरितम् |
तत् त्वया हरिशार्दूल तत् त्वम् इति उपधार्यताम्
translation:
"What that is spoken by me is in my self-confidence but not in any self-conceit, oh,
tigerly-monkey, deem them as doubtless facts...

shloka:
अनृतम् न उक्त पूर्वम् मे न च वक्ष्ये कदाचन |
एतत् ते प्रतिजानामि सत्येन एव शपामि अहम्
translation:
"Untruth is not uttered by me earlier nor will be at anytime from now, and all this
I am promising you taking oath on that truthfulness alone..

shloka:
ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवः वानरैः सचिवैः सह |
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रतिज्ञातम् विशेषतः
translation:
Then on hearing the words of Rama Sugreeva along with his monkey ministers is
gladdened, especially of Rama promise.

shloka:
एवम् एकान्त संपृक्तौ ततः तौ नर वानरौ |
उभौ अन्योन्य सदृशम् सुख दुःखम् अभाष्ताम्
translation:
Then those two, the man and the monkey, met in privacy and both discussed in a
mutually befitting manner about their pleasures and pains.

shloka:
महानुभावस्य वचो निशम्य
हरिर् नृपाणाम् अधिपस्य तस्य |
कृतम् स मेने हरिवीर मुख्यः
तदा च कार्यम् हृदयेन विद्वान्
translation:
On hearing the word of that intellectual, highly capable one and the best king among
kings, namely Rama, he that Sugreeva, the chief among the monkey heroes, thought at heart that his
manoeuvre to surpass his dominant brother Vali is accomplished.

shloka:
परितुष्टः तु सुग्रीवः तेन वाक्येन हर्षितः |
लक्ष्मणस्य अग्रजम् शूरम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Sugreeva is gladdened and satisfied too by that sentence, and said this sentence to
Lakshmana's elder brother, Rama the valiant one.

shloka:
सर्वथा अहम् अनुग्राह्यो देवतानाम् न संशयः |
उपपन्नः गुण उपेतः सखा यस्य भवान् मम
translation:
"When you wth all kinds of endowment and good virtues are my friend, doubtlessly I
am worthy to be blessed by all gods in everyway.

shloka:
शक्यम् खलु भवेत् राम सहायेन त्वया अनघ |
सुर राज्यम् अपि प्राप्तुम् स्व राज्यम् किमुत प्रभो
translation:
"Oh, merited one, with your help it will be possible to achieve kingdom of gods, oh,
lord, then why tell about one's own kingdom...

shloka:
सोऽहम् सभाज्यो बन्धूनाम् सुहृदाम् चैव राघव |
यस्य अग्नि साक्षिकम् मित्रम् लब्धम् राघव वंशजम्
translation:
"He who has gained the one born in Raghava-s dynasty as friend, to which sacred fire
bore the witness, such a being like me is estimable among his relative, more so among his
kind-hearted friends...

shloka:
अहम् अपि अनुरूपः ते वयस्यो ज्ञास्यसे शनैः |
न तु वक्तुम् समर्थोऽहम् त्वयि आत्मगतान् गुणान्
translation:
"Even though I am a matching friend to you, that you will know soon, it will be
inexpedient of myself to talk about my inherent capabilities.

shloka:
महात्मनाम् तु भूयिष्ठम् त्वत् विधानाम् कृत आत्मनाम् |
निश्चला भवति प्रीतिः धैर्यम् आत्मवताम् वर
translation:
"Great souls of your kind, whose hearts are purified like yours, oh, amiable Rama,
their friendship and courage will generally be stable.

shloka:
रजतम् वा सुवर्णम् वा शुभानि आभरणानि च |
अविभक्तानि साधूनाम् अवगच्छन्ति साधवः
translation:
"Gentle souls will be knowing that silver or gold, or even prosperous ornaments are
not to be apportioned among themselves as this is mine and that is yours.

shloka:
आढ्यो वा अपि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा |
निर्दोषः च सदोषः च वयस्यः परमा गतिः
translation:
"May he be rich or poor, saddened or gladdened, flawless or flawed, a friend is the
ultimate recourse to any.

shloka:
धन त्यागः सुख त्यागो देश त्यागोऽपि वा अनघः |
वयस्यार्थे प्रवर्तन्ते स्नेहम् दृष्ट्वा तथा विधम्
translation:
"On observing the course of friendship and knowing which is true friendship, the
true friends do not hesitate to extend wealth, pleasure or even their own country for the sake of
friendship." Sugreeva thus extolled Rama and his friendship.

shloka:
तत् तथा इति अब्रवीत् रामः सुग्रीवम् प्रिय दर्शनम् |
लक्ष्मणस्य अग्रतः लक्ष्म्या वासवस्य इव धीमतः
translation:
"That is thus only," said Rama before Lakshmana, which Lakshmana is sagacious,
resplendent and who vies with Indra, about what is said by Sugreeva, which Sugreeva is by now
soft-natured in his looks, doffing off his jittery look.

shloka:
ततो रामम् स्थितम् दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणम् च महाबलम् |
सुग्रीवः सर्वतः चक्षुः वने लोलम् अपातयत्
translation:
Then on seeing Rama standing there with greatly mighty Lakshmana, Sugreeva cast his
sight with his bolting eyes around that forest.

shloka:
स ददर्श ततः सालम् अविदूरे हरीश्वरः |
सुपुष्पम् ईषत् पत्र आढ्यम् भ्रमरैः उपशोभितम्
translation:
He that lord of monkeys Sugreeva has then seen a well flowered sala tree not far off
from there, covered with some leaves and bedecked with honeybees.

shloka:
तस्य एकाम् पर्ण बहुलाम् शाखाम् भंक्त्वा सुशोभिताम् |
रामस्य आस्तीर्य सुग्रीवो निषसाद स राघवः
translation:
And Sugreeva broke off one branch of that sala tree that is with many leaves and a
well charming one, and spreading it out for Rama, he sat on it with Raghava.

shloka:
तौ आसीनौ ततः दृष्ट्वा हनूमान् अपि लक्ष्मणम् |
साल शाखाम् समुत्पाट्य विनीतम् उपवेशयत्
translation:
On seeing those two sitting on a branch then Hanuma also broke a branch of sala tree
for the modest Lakshmana and seated Lakshmana on it.

shloka:
सुख उपविष्टम् रामम् तु प्रसन्नम् उदधिम् यथा |
साल पुष्पाव संकीर्णे तस्मिन् गिरिवर उत्तमे
translation:
Then to him, who by now is comfortably sitting on a flowery mat laid by the bestrewn
flowers of sala trees on that best mountain like a quiet ocean, to such Rama who by his very
presence delights hearts, that gladsome Sugreeva said this in friendship with his gentle and
gracious words that fluttered with happiness while he spoke. [4-8-15, 16]

shloka:
अहम् विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा चरामि एष भयार्दितः |
ऋष्यमूकम् गिरि वरम् हृत भार्यः सुदुःखितः
translation:
"My brother calumniated me and stole my wife, with his fear and my anguish haunting
me I am moving about this best mountain Rishyamuka.

shloka:
सोऽहम् त्रस्तः भये मग्नः वने संब्रान्त चेतनः |
वालिना निकृतः भ्रात्रा कृत वैरः च राघव
translation:
"Affronted by my brother, oh, Raghava, I am made as his enemy, such as I am, I am
living on with a scared and dazed vitality far flung in fear.

shloka:
वालिनः मे भय आर्तस्य सर्वलोक अभयंकर |
मम अपि त्वम् अनाथस्य प्रसादम् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"I am agonized by the fear from Vali, oh, protector of all the worlds, you protect
me too for I am unprotected, and able are you to accord protection." Thus Sugreeva appealed to
Rama.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्म वत्सलः |
प्रत्युवाच स काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीवम् प्रहसन् इव
translation:
Thus said by Sugreeva, the resplendent and virtuous Rama, the patron of
righteousness replied Sugreeva as though laughing off the task.

shloka:
उपकार फलम् मित्रम् अपकारो अरि लक्षणम् |
अद्य एव तम् वधिष्यामि तव भार्या अपहारिणम्
translation:
"Helping is the fruit of friendship while harming is enemy's trait, hence I wish to
kill him today only, that abductor of your wife..." Rama continued thus.

shloka:
इमे हि मे महाभाग पत्रिणः तिग्म तेजसः |
कार्तिकेय वन उद्भूताः शरा हेम विभूषिताः
translation:
"These are my arrows winged from pinion of the hern, oh, highly fortunate Sugreeva,
these that are decorated in gold sparkle sharply like the Thunderbolts of Indra, and they are
begotten from the reed forest of Kartikeya, ends tied with eagles feathers for fins, smooth are
their nodes, sharp are their tips that pierce sharply, and these will be like enraged snakes.
[4-8-22, 23]

shloka:
वालि सज्ञम् अमित्रम् ते भ्रातरम् कृत किल्बिषम् |
शरैः विनिहतम् पश्य विकीर्णम् इव पर्वतम्
translation:
"You may see your malicious and intimidating brother, someone denotative by name
Vali, eradicated with these very arrows and splintered down like a mountain." Rama said so to
Sugreeva.

shloka:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनी पतिः |
प्रहर्षम् अतुलम् लेभे साधु साध्विति च अब्रवीत्
translation:
On hearing Raghava's words, the lord of monkey-force Sugreeva attained much
happiness and said, 'good, good...'

shloka:
राम शोक अभिभूतो अहम् शोक आर्तानाम् भवान् गतिः |
वयस्य इति कृत्वा हि त्वयि अहम् परिदेवये
translation:
"Rama, I am confounded in sadness, and for those lamenting sadly you are the only
recourse, and because you have befriended me I am opening up my woes before you.

shloka:
त्वम् हि पाणि प्रदानेन वयस्यो मे अग्नि साक्षिकम् |
कृतः प्राणैः बहुमतः सत्येन च शपामि अहम्
translation:
"By extending a helping hand and befriending me while sacred fire bore witness, you
have indeed become my dearest friend on par with my life, and hence I take promise on truth to
broach.

shloka:
वयस्य इति कृत्वा च विस्रब्धः प्रवदामि अहम् |
दुःखम् अन्तर्गतम् तन् मे मनो हरति नित्यशः
translation:
"By befriending you I am able to say clearly about my internal sorrow without any
hitches and hold-ups, which is always rending my heart..." So said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
एतावत् उक्त्वा वचनम् बाष्प दूषित लोचनः |
बाष्प दूषितया वाचा न उच्चैः श्क्नोति भाषितुम्
translation:
Sugreeva said this much sentence with tears abusing his eyes and his voice is unable
talk aloud since it is equally abused by tears.

shloka:
बाष्प वेगम् तु सहसा नदी वेगम् इव आगतम् |
धारयामास धैर्येण सुग्रीवः राम संनिधौ
translation:
Sugreeva courageously controlled the sudden haste of tears that came up hastily and
suddenly like a river in the presence of Rama.

shloka:
स निगृह्य तु तम् बाष्पम् प्रमृज्य नयने शुभे |
विनिःश्वस्य च तेजस्वी राघवम् पुनरूचिवान्
translation:
He that bright Sugreeva controlled those tears, and on wiping his fortunate eyes,
but sighing heavily he again started to speak this sentence to Raghava.

shloka:
पुरा अहम् वलिना राम राज्यात् स्वात् अवरोपितः |
परुषाणि च संश्राव्य निर्धूतो अस्मि बलीयसा
translation:
"Earlier he that forceful Vali deposed me from my kingdom, oh Rama, and speaking
harsh words he even banished me.

shloka:
हृता भार्या च मे तेन प्राणेभ्यो अपि गरीयसी |
सुहृदः च मदीया ये संयता बन्धनेषु ते
translation:
"My wife who is loftier than my lives is stolen by him, and those that are my
sympathisers they are also captivated and imprisoned by him.

shloka:
यत्नवान् च स दुष्टात्मा मद् विनाशाय राघव |
बहुशः तत् प्रयुक्ताः च वानरा निहता मया
translation:
"He that very evil minded one tried many times to annihilate me, and Raghava, I
killed those combatants monkeys that are deployed by Vali to kill me.

shloka:
शंकया एतया अहम् च दृष्ट्वा त्वाम् अपि राघव |
न उपसर्पामि अहम् भीतो भये सर्वे हि बिभ्यति
translation:
"With the same doubt I did not even near you when I saw you... in fear everything
will be fearsome, isn't it...

shloka:
केवलम् हि सहाया मे हनुमत् प्रमुखास्त्विमे |
अतः अहम् धारयामि अद्य प्राणान् कृच्छ्र गतः अपि सन्
translation:
"Though I am engulfed in tribulations I still bear my lives even today due to these
important monkeys like Hanuma and others, who are the only helping hands of mine.

shloka:
एते हि कपयः स्निग्धा माम् रक्षन्ति समन्ततः |
सह गच्छन्ति गन्तव्ये नित्यम् तिष्ठन्ति च स्थिते
translation:
"These are the friendly monkeys guarding me all over, while I go they go along with
me, and if I were to stay they too will stay.

shloka:
संक्षेपः ते एष मे राम किम् उक्त्वा विस्तरम् हि ते |
स मे ज्येष्ठो रिपुः भ्राता वाली विश्रुत पौरुषः
translation:
"Rama, this is briefly my sad-story and why tell this very broadly to you as it
would be too tedious... my elder brother Vali is a renowned one for his intrepidity, and he that
Vali alone is my enemy.

shloka:
तद् विनाशे अपि मे दुःखम् प्रमृष्टम् स्यात् अनन्तरम् |
सुखम् मे जीवितम् चैव तद् विनाश निबन्धनम्
translation:
"His end ends my distress and my later life and quietude are subjected to his
destruction.

shloka:
एष मे राम शोकान्तः शोक आर्तेन निवेदितः |
दुःखितः सुखितः वा अपि सख्युः नित्यम् सखा गतिः
translation:
"Grief stricken such as I am, I have submitted as to how my misery ends, whether one
is gladdened or saddened he has recourse only to his friend." So said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
श्रुत्वा एतत् च वचः रामः सुग्रीवम् इदम् अब्रवीत् |
किम् निमित्तम् अभूत् वैरम् श्रोतुम् इच्छामि तत्त्वतः
translation:
Hearing all that is spoken by Sugreeva, Rama asked, "What for chanced the enmity? I
am interested to listen, in its reality...

shloka:
सुखम् हि कारणम् श्रुत्वा वैरस्य तव वानर |
आनन्तर्यद् विधास्यामि संप्रधार्य बलाबलम्
translation:
"On knowing the cause of your enmity, oh, monkey, and after a proper thought, and
deciding upon the strength and weakness of the cause of enmity, or of the enmity itself, I will do
the needful very easily.

shloka:
बलवान् हि मम अमर्षः श्रुत्वा त्वाम् अवमानितम् |
वर्धते हृदय उत्कम्पी प्रावृड् वेग इव अंभसः
translation:
"On hearing that you are insulted my intense anger that can flutter my heartbeat is
intensifying like the intensifying speed of waters in rainy reason.

shloka:
हृष्टः कथय विस्रब्धो यावत् आरोप्यते धनुः |
सृष्टः च हि मया बाणो निरस्तः च रिपुः तव
translation:
"Be glad to say in belief, Sugreeva, before I take aim with my bow, and even before
I release the arrow, and even before silencing your enemy." Rama assured Sugreeva in this way.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सुग्रीवः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना |
प्रहर्षम् अतुलम् लेभे चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः
translation:
Thus said by the great souled Rama, Sugreeva is very much rejoiced along with four
of vanara-s available in his attendance.

shloka:
ततः प्रहृ^इष्ट वदनः सुग्रीवः लक्ष्मणाग्रजे |
वैरस्य कारणम् तत्त्वम् आख्यातुम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
Then with a pleased countenance Sugreeva started to tell Rama about the cause of the
enmity, it all it truthfulness.

shloka:
वाली नाम मम भ्राता ज्येष्ठः शत्रु निषूदनः |
पितुः बहुमतः नित्यम् मम च अपि तथा पुरा
translation:
"Oh, great enemy destroyer Rama, my elder brother Vali is a very dear one to our
father, and even for me too he was so, earlier.

shloka:
पितरि उपरते तस्मिन् ज्येष्ठो अयम् इति मंत्रिभिः |
कपीनाम् ईश्वरो राज्ये कृतः परम सम्मतः
translation:
After the demise of our father all the ministers have glorified him immensely and
made him the king of all the monkeys as he is the elder.

shloka:
राज्यम् प्रशासतः तस्य पितृ पैतामहम् महत् |
अहम् सर्वेषु कालेषु प्रणतः प्रेष्यवत् स्थितः
translation:
While he was ruling the great kingdom of my father and forefathers, I have always
bowed down to him like a servant and stood by him.

shloka:
मायावी नाम तेजस्वी पूर्वजो दुन्दुभेः सुतः |
तेन तस्य महद् वैरम् वालिनः स्त्री कृतम् पुरा
translation:
There was a fierce demon named Maayaavi, the elder brother of Dundubhi and the son
of one demon named Maya. There was a great enmity between this Maayaavi and Vali owing to some
female.

shloka:
स तु सुप्ते जने रात्रौ किष्किन्धा द्वारम् आगतः |
नर्दति स्म सुसम्रब्धो वालिनम् च आह्वयत् रणे
translation:
He that Maayaavi arrived at the doors of Kishkindha in a night when the people are
sleeping, and blared very much inviting Vali for a fight.

shloka:
प्रसुप्तः तु मम भ्राता नर्दितो भैरव स्वनम् |
श्रुत्वा न ममृषे वाली निष्पपात जवात् तदा
translation:
Then my brother who was also sleeping well, on hearing that bellowing in a
clamouring voice, did not tolerate and came out speedily.

shloka:
स तु वै निःसृतः क्रोधात् तम् हन्तुम् असुरोत्तमम् |
वार्यमाणः ततः स्त्रीभिः मया च प्रणत आत्मना
translation:
Though the females and myself bowed reverently to prevent Vali, he came out of
palace in all his anger to kill that great demon.

shloka:
स तु निर्धूय सर्वान् नो निर्जगाम महाबलः |
ततः अहम् अपि सौहार्दान् निःसृतः वालिना सह
translation:
But Vali spurned all of us away and forged ahead, and then I also have started to go
along with Vali in all my predisposition.

shloka:
स तु मे भ्रातरम् दृष्ट्वा माम् च दूरात् अवस्थितम् |
असुरो जात संत्रासः प्रदुद्राव तदा भृशम्
translation:
A great fear was induced in that demon on seeing my brother and me too coming from a
distance, and then he quickly ran away.

shloka:
तस्मिन् द्रवति संत्रस्ते हि आवाम् द्रुततरम् गतौ |
प्रकाशः अपि कृतः मार्गः चन्द्रेण उद्गच्छता तदा
translation:
While he is running away in fear we quickly followed him on a path that is barely
lit by moonlight of the moon who is just coming up.

shloka:
स तृणैः आवृतम् दुर्गम् धरण्या विवरम् महत् |
प्रविवेश असुरः वेगात् आवाम् आसाद्य विष्ठितौ
translation:
That demon speedily entered an un-enterable cavity under the ground, covered with
grass, and we too having reached there speedily stood at the aperture of that cavity for a while.

shloka:
तम् प्रविष्टम् रिपुम् दृष्ट्वा बिलम् रोष वशम् गतः |
माम् उवाच ततो वाली वचनम् क्षुभित इन्द्रियः
translation:
Then Vali has gone into the enfoldment of fury on observing the entry of that demon
into the hole, whereby his senses felt outraged, and he said this sentence to me.

shloka:
इह तिष्ठ अद्य सुग्रीव बिल द्वारि समाहितः |
यावत् अत्र प्रविश्य अहम् निहन्मि समरे रिपुम्
translation:
Then Vali said to me, "Now you stay here on the alert, Sugreeva, at the entrance of
this hole till I return on destroying the enemy in a fight on my entering this hole..."

shloka:
मया तु एतत् वचः श्रुत्वा याचितः स परंतपः |
शापयित्वा च माम् पद्भ्याम् प्रविवेश बिलम् ततः
translation:
On hearing those words I requested him to allow me too to come in to the hole, but
he being the great tormentor of his enemies disallowed it, and he made me to swear on his feet and
entered that hole.

shloka:
तस्य प्रविष्टस्य बिलम् साग्रः संवत्सरः गतः |
स्थितस्य च बिल द्वारि सः कालः व्यत्यवर्तत
translation:
Well over a year is over after his entering into that cleavage, and to me too who
stayed at the entrance of the cleavage that much time had passed away.

shloka:
अहम् तु नष्टम् तम् ज्ञात्वा स्नेहात् आगत संभ्रमः |
भ्रातरम् न प्रपश्यामि पाप शङ्कि च मे मनः
translation:
I thought I lost him for my brother is unseen, and in all fondness towards him my
mind started to doubt about some harm might have befallen on him.

shloka:
अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य बिलात् तस्मात् विनिःसृतम् |
सः फेनम् रुधिरम् दृष्ट्वा ततो अहम् भृशदुःखितः
translation:
After a long time blood with foam gushed out that hole, and on seeing it I was
deeply saddened.

shloka:
नर्दताम् असुराणाम् च ध्वनिः मे श्रोत्रम् आगतः |
न रस्तस्य च संग्रामे क्रोशतो अपि स्वनो गुरोः
translation:
Sounds of screaming demon came to my ear, but the screeches of my brother who is
involved in fight are unheard, in the least.

shloka:
अहम् तु अवगतः बुद्ध्या चिह्नैः तैः भ्रातरम् हतम् |
पिधाय च बिल द्वारम् शिलया गिरि मात्रया
translation:
Oh, friend, Rama... I have surmised and concluded in mind by the indications that my
brother is finished, and covered the cavity's opening with a mountain similar boulder, and
performed water oblations to my deceased brother with saddening pain, and then returned to
Kishkindha. But the ministers have persuaded and heard from me the actual happening though I was
concealing it. [4-9-19, 20]

shloka:
ततः अहम् तैः समागम्य समेतैः अभिषेचितः |
राज्यम् प्रशासतः तस्य न्यायतो मम राघव
translation:
Then duly summoned by all of those ministers I was crowned, and while I was ruling
the kingdom judiciously, oh, Raghava, that semi-human Vali returned on killing that demoniac enemy.
[4-9-21, 22a]

shloka: अभिषिक्तम् तु माम् दृष्ट्वा कोपात् संरक्त लोचनः
translation:
But on seeing me crowned his eyes were reddened in anger, and he arrested all my
ministers as he spoke rudely. [4-9-22b, 23a]

shloka: निग्रहे च समर्थस्य तम् पापम् प्रति राघव
translation:
And oh, Raghava, though I was capable enough to counter him, my reason was
controlled by my esteem to brotherhood, and I was indisposed to commit that sin of defying
brotherhood. [4-9-23b, 24a]

shloka: हत्वा शत्रुम् सः मे भ्राता प्रविवेश पुरम् तदा
translation:
He that brother of mine entered the capital thus on destroying the enemy, and I
hailed him as usual while respecting that audacious soul, but his inner self is unsatisfied and I
remained unblest. [4-9-24b, 25]

shloka:
नत्वा पादौ अहम् तस्य मुकुटेन अस्पृशम् प्रभो |
अपि वाली मम क्रोधात् न प्रसादम् चकार सः
translation:
Oh, lord Rama, though I bowed with the crown touching his feet, he that rancorous
Vali showed no quarter towards me." So said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
ततः क्रोध समाविष्टम् सम्रब्धम् तम् उपागतम् |
अहम् प्रसादयान् चक्रे भ्रातरम् हित काम्यया
translation:
"Then desiring both of our well-being I have begged of my brother who is enveloped
in anger and behaving capriciously.

shloka:
दिष्ट्या असि कुशली प्राप्तो निहतः च त्वया रिपुः |
अनाथस्य हि मे नाथः त्वम् एको अनाथ नन्दनः
translation:
"Oh, orphan's, delight Rama, I addressed him like this, "Luckily you have eliminated
the enemy and returned safely, and to an orphaned one like me you alone are the protector.

shloka:
इदम् बहु शलाकम् ते पूर्ण चन्द्रम् इव उदितम् |
छत्रम् स वाल व्यजनम् प्रतीच्छस्व मया धृतम्
translation:
Let this regal umbrella unfolded like a full moon, with its many of its spikes, and
with accompanying fur-fans may please be accepted while I hold it for you.

shloka:
आर्तस्य अथ बिला द्वारि स्थितः संवत्सरम् नृप |
दृष्ट्वा च शोणितम् द्वारि बिलात् च अपि समुत्थितम्
translation:
"Saddened I was after staying at the entrance of the cave for one year, oh, king,
and on seeing the blood that started to flow from out the cave in the entrance my heart is engulfed
in sadness and my senses perturbed very much, and then covering that cave's entrance with a
hilltop, and departing from that country, I re-entered Kishkindha. [4-10-4, 5, 6a]

shloka: विषादात् इह माम् दृष्ट्वा पौरैः मंत्रिभिर् एव च
translation:
"On seeing me returning with grief, the citizens and ministers alike crowned me, but
that is not at my desire, therefore it is apt of you pardon me. [4-10-6b, 7a]

shloka: त्वम् एव राजा मानार्हः सदा च अहम् यथा पुरा
translation:
"As an estimable one you alone are the king, and I will be as I was, and
establishing me in kingship is owing to your unavailability, but the capital with citizens and
ministers is kept up without thorniness. [4-10-7b, 8]

shloka:
न्यास भूतम् इदम् राज्यम् तव निर्यातयामि अहम् |
मा च रोषम् कृथाः सौम्य मम शत्रु निषूदन
translation:
"Oh, gentle one, I am now returning this custodial kingdom to you, oh, enemy
eliminator, you need not be hostile towards me.

shloka:
याचे त्वाम् शिरसा राजन् मया बद्धो अयम् अंजलिः |
बलात् अस्मिन् समागम्य मंत्रिभिः पुर वासिभिः
translation:
"I beg you with my bowed head and with my prayerful palm-fold, the ministers and the
city dwellers have collectively and forcibly nominated me to the kingship, only to keep the
kingless kingdom under control. [4-10-10, 11a]

shloka: स्निग्धम् एवम् ब्रुवाणम् माम् स विनिर्भर्त्स्य वानरः
translation:
"While I was speaking that politely he threatened me and indeed used many expletives
starting from 'fie, fie, upon you.' and the like. [4-10-11b, 12a]

shloka: प्रकृतीः च समानीय मंत्रिणः चैव सम्मतान्
translation:
"And summoning people and venerable ministers he hurled very abusive words at me
among friends. [4-10-12b, 13a]

shloka: विदितम् वो मया रात्रौ मायावी स महाअसुरः
translation:
"You all are aware that earlier the gigantic and rancorous demon Maayaavi invited me
desiring a duel in that night. [4-10-13b, 14a]

shloka: तस्य तद् भाषितम् श्रुत्वा निःसृतः अहम् नृपाअलयात्
translation:
"On hearing his call for a duel I went out of the royal palace, and this very
hazardous brother of mine quickly followed me. [4-10-14b, 15a]

shloka: स तु दृष्ट्वा एव माम् रात्रौ स द्वितीयम् महाबलः
translation:
"And that formidable demon Maayaavi ran away as he was fraught with fear on seeing
me with a second one at my side, and he speedily entered a great cavity of earth on seeing us two
nearly reaching him. [4-10-15b, 16]

shloka:
तम् प्रविष्टम् विदित्वा तु सुघोरम् सुमहद् बिलम् |
अयम् उक्तो अथ मे भ्राता मया तु क्रूर दर्शनः
translation:
"On knowing the demon's entry into that great precarious cavity, I said to this one,
this cruel looking brother of mine.

shloka:
अहत्वा न अस्ति मे शक्तिः प्रति गन्तुम् इतः पुरीम् |
बिल द्वारि प्रतीक्ष त्वम् यावत् एनम् निहन्मि अहम्
translation:
"My power will not let me return from here to the capital without killing that
demon, hence you wait at this cavity's entrance, till I kill that demon and come out of the cavity.

shloka:
स्थितोऽयम् इति मत्वा अहम् प्रविष्टः तु दुरासदम् |
तम् मे मार्गयतः तत्र गतः संवत्सरः तदा
translation:
"Believing that he stayed at the entrance of the cavity I entered that impenetrable
cavity, and then in searching for that demon there one year elapsed.

shloka:
स तु दृष्टो मया शत्रुः अनिर्वेदात् भयाअवहः |
निहतः च मया सद्यः सः सर्वैः सह बन्धुभिः
translation:
"I have seen that terrified enemy of mine effortlessly, and I killed him immediately
along with all of his relatives.

shloka:
तस्य आस्यात् तु प्रवृत्तेन रुधिरौघेण तद् बिलम् |
पूर्णम् आसीत् दुराक्रामम् स्वनतः तस्य भूतले
translation:
"That cavity has become impassable, since it is fully filled with the gushes of
blood emanating from the mouth of that demon who fell yelling onto ground.

shloka:
सूदयित्वा तु तम् शत्रुम् विक्रान्तम् तम् अहम् सुखम् |
निष्क्रामम् न एव पश्यामि बिलस्य पिहितम् मुखम्
translation:
"On my killing that invading enemy easily, I could not see any exit from that cavity
as its mouth was closed.

shloka:
विक्रोशमानस्य तु मे सुग्रीव इति पुनः पुनः |
यतः प्रतिवचो नास्ति ततः अहम् भृश दुःखितः
translation:
"Wherefore I did not get a reply though I repeatedly shouted, 'Sugreeva, oh,
Sugreeva.' thereby I was very saddened.

shloka:
पाद प्रहारैः तु मया बहुभिः परिपातितम् |
ततः अहम् तेन निष्क्रम्य पथा पुरम् उपागतः
translation:
"With my foot I pounded and smashed that lidded hilltop, and from there I exited
that way and arrived here.

shloka:
तत्र अनेन अस्मि सम्रुद्धः राज्यम् मृगयत आत्मनः |
सुग्रीवेण नृशंसेन विस्मृत्य भ्रातृ सौहृदम्
translation:
"As such this cruel fantasist of kingdom trammelled me in there forgetting the
clannishness." So said Vali to all the courtiers.

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु माम् तत्र वस्त्रेण एकेन वानरः |
तदा निर्वासयामास वाली विगत साध्वसः
translation:
"On saying thus that monkey ruthlessly banished me, then and there in the court
itself, who am with a single clothing on my body.

shloka:
तेन अहम् अपविद्धः च हृत दारः च राघव |
तत् भयात् च महीम् सर्वान् क्रान्तवान् स वन अर्णवाम्
translation:
"Thus he threw me away and even stole my wife, oh, Rama, and owing to his fear alone
I roamed all over the earth with its forests and oceans.

shloka:
ऋश्यमूकम् गिरि वरम् भार्या हरण दुःखितः |
प्रविष्टो अस्मि दुराधर्षम् वालिनः कारणान्तरे
translation:
"I who am saddened by stealing my wife have entered this safest mountain Rishyamuka,
which is impenetrable for Vali by another reason.

shloka:
एतत् ते सर्वम् आख्यातम् वैर अनुकथनम् महत् |
अनागसा मया प्राप्तम् व्यसनम् पश्य राघव
translation:
"All this notable account of enmity is reported to you, oh, Raghava, and you may
examine the dire straits befallen on me at no fault of mine.

shloka:
वालिनः च भयात् तस्य सर्वलोक भयापह |
कर्तुम् अर्हसि मे वीर प्रसादम् तस्य निग्रहात्
translation:
"Oh, Rama, the fear-remover of all the worlds, it is apt of you to bestow me
invulnerability from the fear of Vali, and oh, valiant one, as well as to rein him in." Sugreeva
requested Rama thus.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः स तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्म संहितम् |
वचनम् वक्तुम् आरेभे सुग्रीवम् प्रहसन् इव
translation:
When he is requested thus by Sugreeva, that virtuous and resplendent Rama started to
tell Sugreeva, the words that abide by virtue, as though trivializing the task on hand.

shloka:
अमोघाः सूर्य संकाशा निशिता मे शरा इमे |
तस्मिन् वालिनि दुर्वृत्ते पतिष्यन्ति रुष अन्विताः
translation:
"Admirable and sun-like burners are these arrows of mine that are now mingled with
my wrath, and they are bound fall on that evil minded Vali.

shloka:
यावत् तम् न हि पश्येयम् तव भार्य अपहारिणम् |
तावत् स जीवेत् पापात्मा वाली चारित्र दूषकः
translation:
"He that stealer of your wife, that evil-minded abuser of history lives as long as I
descry.

shloka:
आत्म अनुमानात् पश्यामि मग्नः त्वाम् शोक सागरे |
त्वाम् अहम् तारयिष्यामि बाढम् प्राप्स्यसि पुष्कलम्
translation:
"By my experience I see how you are deluged in a sea of sadness, but I will make you
to get over that sea, and you will definitely regain abundantly whatever you lost." Rama assured
Sugreeva thus.

shloka:
तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा हर्ष पौरुष वर्धनम् |
सुग्रीवः परम प्रीतः सु महत् वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Hearing that sentence of Rama, which is enhancing happiness and self-esteem,
Sugreeva is very gladdened and further said this great sentence.

shloka:
रामस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा हर्ष पौरुष वर्धनम् |
सुग्रीवः पूजयाम् चक्रे राघवम् प्रशशंस च
translation:
Sugreeva started to adore and extol Raghava on hearing the words of Rama that are
inculcating happiness and pride.

shloka:
असंशयम् प्रज्वलितैः तीक्ष्णैर् मर्म अतिगैः शरैः |
त्वम् दहेः कुपितो लोकान् युगान्त इव भास्करः
translation:
"It is doubtless that you will burn down everything when you are angry, like the
blazing sun at the end of era, with these arrows of yours that are highly blazing, incisive and
invaders on stealthy places." Thus Sugreeva started extolling Rama.

shloka:
वालिनः पौरुषम् यत् तद् यत् च वीर्यम् धृतिः च या |
तन् मम एक मनाः श्रुत्वा विधत्स्व यद् अनन्तरम्
translation:
"That which is impetuousness of Vali, that which is his bravery and courageousness
are there, they may be listened from me single-mindedly, and later you impose that which need be
imposed.

shloka:
समुद्रात् पश्चिमात् पूर्वम् दक्षिणाद् अपि च उत्तरम् |
क्रामति अनुदिते सूर्ये वाली व्यपगत क्लमः
translation:
"Before the dawn of sun Vali unweariedly strides from western ocean to eastern, and
even from southern to northern for offering water oblations to the rising sun.

shloka:
अग्राणि आरुह्य शैलानाम् शिखराणि महान्ति अपि |
ऊर्ध्वम् उत्पात्य तरसा प्रति गृह्णाति वीर्यवान्
translation:
"Ascending the heights of mountains and even rending their greatest peaks, that
mighty one volleys them upwards and in turn catches them, as though they are play balls.

shloka:
बहवः सारवन्तः च वनेषु विविधा द्रुमाः |
वालिना तरसा भग्ना बलम् प्रथयता आत्मनः
translation:
"As a show his strength Vali used to personally fell many sturdy trees of diverse
origin by his might.

shloka:
महिषो दुन्दुभिर् नाम कैलास शिखर प्रभः |
बलम् नाग सहस्रस्य धारयामास वीर्यवान्
translation:
"One named Dundubhi was there in the form of a buffalo, whose size shone forth like
Mt. Kailash and who bears the strength of a thousand elephants." Thus Sugreeva started telling
Dundubhi's episode to Rama.

shloka:
स वीर्य उत्सेक दुष्टात्मा वर दानेन च मोहितः |
जगाम स महाकायः समुद्रम् सरिताम् पतिम्
translation:
"He that evil-minded and colossal bodied Dundubhi was bemused by the vanity of his
own vigour, and by the boon bestowed oo him, and once he went to the lord of rivers, namely the
Ocean.

shloka:
ऊर्मिमंतम् अतिक्रम्य सागरम् रत्न संचयम् |
मम युद्धम् प्रयच्छ इति तम् उवाच महार्णवम्
translation:
"Deriding the garner of weaves and gems he said to that vastly ocean "give me a
fight"

shloka:
ततः समुद्रो धर्मात्मा समुत्थाय महाबलः |
अब्रवीद् वचनम् राजन् असुरम् काल चोदितम्
translation:
"Then, oh, Rama, that virtue-minded and very powerful ocean rose up from his tabular
position to heights, and spoke these words to that demon Dundubhi who is driven to doom by his own
time.

shloka:
समर्थो न अस्मि ते दातुम् युद्धम् युद्ध विशारद |
श्रूयताम् त्वम् अभिधास्यामि यत् ते युद्धम् प्रदास्यति
translation:
"I am not capable to give you a fight, oh, war-expert, but I will name him who can
give you a fight, listen." So said ocean to the demon.

shloka:
शैल राजो महारण्ये तपस्वि शरणम् परम् |
शंकर श्वशुरो नाम्ना हिमवान् इति विश्रुतः
translation:
"A sublime shelter for sages and the father-in-law of Shankara is there in great
forests, well-know by the name Himavan, the king of mountains, and he embodies great cascades,
cataracts, and caves, and he alone is capable to accord a matchless happiness to you in the form of
a fight." So said ocean to Dundubhi. [4-11-12, 13]

shloka:
तम् भीतम् इति विज्ञाय समुद्रम् असुरोत्तमः |
हिमवद् वनम् आगम्य शरः चापाद् इव च्युतः
translation:
"Fathoming that ocean to be scared of him that noted demon Dundubhi arrived at the
forests of Himavan like an arrow darted from bow, and that Dundubhi started to blare discordantly
and toss the rock-faces of that mountain that are like white elephants in their figuration,
severally. [4-11-14, 15]

shloka:
ततः श्वेत अम्बुद आकारः सौम्यः प्रीति कर आकृतिः |
हिमवान् अब्रवीद् वाक्यम् स्व एव शिखरे स्थितः
translation:
"Then he who is like a silver cloud in his figuration, a gentle and delightful one
in his appearance, that Himavan spoke these words to the demon staying on his own cliff.

shloka:
क्लेष्टुम् अर्हसि माम् न त्वम् दुन्दुभे धर्म वत्सल |
रण कर्मसु अकुशलः तपस्वि शरणो हि अहम्
translation:
"It is inapt of you to annoy me, oh, virtuous Dundubhi, I am just a shelterer of
sages, and an unskilled one in fights." So said Himavan to Dundubhi.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा गिरि राजस्य धीमतः |
उवाच दुन्दुभिर् वाक्यम् क्रोधात् संरक्त लोचनः
translation:
"On hearing the words of that modest king of mountains Dundubhi's uyes are bloodshot
and he said this sentence.

shloka:
यदि युद्धे असमर्थः त्वम् मद् भयाद् वा निरुद्यमः |
तम् आचक्ष्व प्रदद्यात् मे यो हि युद्धम् युयुत्सतः
translation:
"Whether you are incapable to fight with me, or not venturing me as you are scared
of me is not my concern, but tell me who can really give me a very combative fight,.

shloka:
हिमवान् अब्रवीद् वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा वाक्य विशारदः |
अनुक्त पूर्वम् धर्मात्मा क्रोधात् तम् असुरोत्तमम्
translation:
On hearing Dundubhi's arrogant words that honest Himavan being an expert in
sentence-making, had to say angry words to that fierce demon that were never uttered by him
earlier.

shloka:
वाली नाम महा प्राज्ञः शक्र पुत्र प्रतापवान् |
अध्यास्ते वानरः श्रीमान् किष्किन्धाम् अतुल प्रभाम्
translation:
"Oh, war-expert Dundubhi, Indra's son is there, a brave and glorious one by name
Vali, and he is now presiding over the matchlessly pompous city Kishkindha.

shloka:
स समर्थो महा प्राज्ञः तव युद्ध विशारदः |
द्वन्द्व युद्धम् स दातुम् ते नमुचिः इव वासवः
translation:
"He is a highly intelligent one and a war-expert too, and he is the capable one to
give you a duel, like Indra to Namuchi.

shloka:
तम् शीघ्रम् अभिगच्छ त्वम् यदि युद्धम् इह इच्छसि |
स हि दुर्मर्षणो नित्यम् शूरः समर कर्मणि
translation:
"Approach him promptly if you desire a fight now, and he is an intrepid one who will
always be in the manoeuvres of war, and indeed none can assail him." Thus said Himavan to that
demon Dundubhi.

shloka:
श्रुत्वा हिमवतो वाक्यम् कोप आविष्टः स दुन्दुभिः |
जगाम ताम् पुरीम् तस्य किष्किन्धाम् वालिनः तदा
translation:
"Then on hearing Himavan's words he that Dundubhi is convulsed in anger and
proceeded to Vali's city Kishkindha..

shloka:
धारयन् माहिषम् रूपम् तीक्ष्ण शृङ्गो भयावहः |
प्रावृषि इव महा मेघः तोय पूर्णो नभस्तले
translation:
"That great mighty demon Dundubhi wearing the look of a buffalo with sharp horns was
awe-inspiring, and like the arrival of a massive dark cloud in rainy season full with water on the
edge of firmament, he arrived at the gateway of Kishkindha and bellowed clamorously like a war-drum
as though to quake the earth. [4-11-25, 26]

shloka:
समीपजान् द्रुमान् भंजन् वसुधाम् दारयन् खुरैः |
विषाणेन उल्लिखन् दर्पात् तद् द्वारम् द्विरदो यथा
translation:
"He bellowed uprooting trees that are rooted nearby, scooping the earth with hooves,
and insolently goring the gateway with horns like a goring elephant.

shloka:
अन्तःपुर गतो वाली श्रुत्वा शब्दम् अमर्षणः |
निष्पपात सह स्त्रीभिः ताराभिः इव चंद्रमाः
translation:
"Vali who by then went into his palace chambers became intolerant to hear that noise
and fell out from there along with ladies, like the moon with stars.

shloka:
मितम् व्यक्त अक्षर पदम् तम् उवाच स दुन्दुभिम् |
हरीणाम् ईश्वरो वाली सर्वेषाम् वन चारिणाम्
translation:
"Vali being the lord of monkeys, and of all the other forest-dwellers as well, spoke
a clearly worded brief sentence to Dundubhi.

shloka:
किम् अर्थम् नगर द्वारम् इदम् रुद् ध्वा विनर्दसे |
दुन्दुभे विदितो मेऽसि रक्ष प्राणान् महाबल
translation:
"Oh, Dundubhi, impeding the gateway of this city what for you are bellowing, I know
you, oh, might one, save your lives." Vali cautioned that demon that way.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्य धीमतः |
उवाच दुन्दुभिर् वाक्यम् क्रोधात् संरक्त लोचनः
translation:
"On hearing that sentence of Vali, the tactful lord of monkeys, Dundubhi said this
sentence with his eyes bloodshot in anger." Thus Sugreeva continued his narration to Rama.

shloka:
न त्वम् स्त्री सन्निधौ वीर वचनम् वक्तुम् अर्हसि |
मम युद्धम् प्रयच्छ अद्य ततो ज्ञास्यामि ते बलम्
translation:
"It is inapt of you to speak words in the vicinity of ladies, oh, valiant Vali, give
me a duel now and then I can appreciate your might."

shloka:
अथवा धारयिष्यामि क्रोधम् अद्य निशाम् इमाम् |
गृह्यताम् उदयः स्वैरम् काम भोगेषु वानर
translation:
"Otherwise I bear up my rage for this night, oh, monkey, you may unrestrainedly
delight yourself till morning in your voluptuous gratifications, for you are now surrounded by your
ladies."

shloka:
दीयताम् संप्रदानम् च परिष्वज्य च वानरान् |
सर्व शखा मृगेन्द्रत्वम् संसादय सुहृज्जनम्
translation:
"Also embrace all the monkeys and bequeath endowments to them, and you may bid adieu
to all the good-hearted people of yours for you are the king of all the tree-branch animals, as you
may not see them later.

shloka:
सु दृष्टाम् कुरु किष्किन्धाम् कुरुष्व आत्म समम् पुरे |
क्रीडयस्व च समम् स्त्रीभिः अहम् ते दर्प शासनः
translation:
"Let Kishkindha city be seen clearly by you as last sight, and keep someone
equalling you as in charge of city, and also rejoice with the females till sunrise as there is no
tomorrow to you.

shloka:
यो हि मत्तम् प्रमत्तम् वा भग्नम् वा रहितम् कृशम् |
हन्यात् स भ्रूणहा लोके त्वद् विधम् मद मोहितम्
translation:
"He who kills a drunken one, unvigilant one, defeated one, or one without weapons,
or an atrophied one, he get the sin of foeticide in the world, and your present state is suchlike."
Dundubhi incited Vali in this way.

shloka:
स प्रहस्य अब्रवीत् मन्दम् क्रोधात् तम् असुरेश्वरम् |
विसृज्य ताः स्त्रियः सर्वाः तारा प्रभृतिकाः तदा
translation:
