"Then Vali laughed that demon off, discharged all the females namely Tara and
others, and then he spoke to that stupid lord of demons in anger.

shloka:
मत्तो अयम् इति मा मंस्था यदि अभीतो असि संयुगे |
मदो अयम् संप्रहारे अस्मिन् वीर पानम् समर्थ्यताम्
translation:
"Don't surmise that I am drunk, and should you be unafraid of a fight, regard this
drunkenness of mine as the toast of a gallant fighter in this deadly fight." Vali said so to
Dundubhi.

shloka:
तम् एवम् उक्त्वा संक्रुद्धो मालाम् उत्क्षिप्य कांचनीम् |
पित्रा दत्ताम् महेन्द्रेण युद्धाय व्यवतिष्ठत
translation:
"Saying that way to that Dundubhi that highly enraged Vali heaved up the golden
chest-pendant around his neck on to his chest, which was given by his father Mahendra, and stood
firm for fight.

shloka:
विषाणयो गृहीत्वा तम् दुन्दुभिम् गिरि संनिभम् |
आविध्यत तथा वाली विनदन् कपि कुंजरः
translation:
"Then that elephantine monkey Vali took that mountain-similar Dundubhi by horns, and
booming highly he whirled and bumped him onto ground.

shloka:
वाली व्यापादयाम् चक्रे ननर्द च महास्वनम् |
श्रोत्राभ्याम् अथ रक्तम् तु तस्य सुस्राव पात्यतः
translation:
"Vali while blaring highly with great sound repeatedly whirled him and thrown onto
ground, and while Dundubhi was hurled and thrown to ground, blood gushed out of his two ears.

shloka:
तयोः तु क्रोध संरम्भात् परस्पर जयैषिणोः |
युद्धम् समभवत् घोरम् दुन्दुभेर् वालिनः तथा
translation:
"There occurred a gruesome fight among those two, Dundubhi and Vali, who by their
fury are impetuous and who aspired victory over the other.

shloka:
अयुध्यत तदा वाली शक्र तुल्य पराक्रमः |
मुष्टिभिर् जानुभिः पद्भिः शिलाभिः पादपैः तथा
translation:
"Then Vali who is similar to Indra in his fortitude fought with him with his fists,
knees and feet, and like that with boulders and trees.

shloka:
परस्परम् घ्नतोः तत्र वानर असुरयोः तदा |
आसीत् हीनो असुरो युद्धे शक्र सूनुः व्यवर्धत
translation:
"While each is assaulting the other in that fight between that monkey and demon,
that demon is impaired and Indra's son Vali toughened.

shloka:
तम् तु दुन्दुभिम् उद्यम्य धरण्याम् अभ्यपातयत् |
युद्धे प्राणहरे तस्मिन् निष्पिष्टो दुन्दुभिः तदा
translation:
"In that life-taking fight when Dundubhi is lifted up and flung to ground, he is
completely pounded out.

shloka:
स्रोत्रेभ्यो बहु रक्तम् तु तस्य सुस्राव पात्यतः |
पपात च महाबाहुः क्षितौ पंचत्वम् आगतः
translation:
"While he is felled down much blood is flown out from the vent-holes of his body,
nine of them, ears, nose, eyes etc., and on his falling that mighty one Dundubhi attained the
fifth-state.

shloka:
तम् तोलयित्वा बाहुभ्याम् गत सत्त्वम् अचेतनम् |
चिक्षेप वेगवान् वाली वेगेन एकेन योजनम्
translation:
"Then the hastiest Vali swayed that dead and inanimate demon with both of his hands
and hurled him a yojana distance in a single flick.

shloka:
तस्य वेग प्रविद्धस्य वक्त्रात् क्षतज बिन्दवः |
प्रपेतुः मारुत उत्क्षिप्ता मतंगस्य आश्रमम् प्रति
translation:
"And while he is thrown that hastily blood drops oozed from his mouth, and flung by
air they fell in the hermitage of sage Matanga.

shloka:
तान् दृष्ट्वा पतिताम् तत्र मुनिः शोणित विप्रुषः |
क्रुद्धः तस्य महाभाग चिन्तयामास कोन्वम्
translation:
"On seeing the blood drops fallen there, oh Rama, that sage is enraged and thought,
'who is he indeed, who dropped the blood...' Thus Sugreeva narrated to Rama.

shloka:
येन अहम् सहसा स्पृष्टः शोणितेन दुरात्मना |
कोऽयम् दुरात्मा दुर् बुद्धिः अकृतात्मा च बालिशः
translation:
" 'By which evil-spirited one I am abruptly touched with blood? Who is that
evil-minded one? Who is that malevolent, disobedient and a reckless one?' Thus the sage Matanga
pondered.

shloka:
इति उक्त्वा स विनिष्क्रम्य ददृशे मुनिसत्तम |
महिषम् पर्वत आकारम् गत असुम् पतितम् भुवि
translation:
"Thinking thus and coming out of hermitage that celebrated sage has seen the
mountainous buffalo fallen on ground lifelessly.

shloka:
स तु विज्ञाय तपसा वानरेण कृतम् हि तत् |
उत्ससर्ज महा शापम् क्षेप्तारम् वानरम् प्रति
translation:
"On knowing by his ascetic power that this deed is done by the monkey, he released a
great curse on him who tossed the cadaver of buffalo.

shloka:
इह तेन अप्रवेष्टव्यम् प्रविष्टस्य वधो भवेत् |
वनम् मत् संश्रयम् येन दूषितम् रुधिर स्रवैः
translation:
"Untreadable is this sheltering wood of mine to him who has stained it with squirts
of blood, and if he enters this place peradventure, fatality occurs on him.

shloka:
क्षिपता पादपाः च इमे संभग्नाः च असुरीम् तनुम् |
समन्तात् आश्रमम् पूर्णम् योजनम् मामकम् यदि
translation:
"By his hurling the demon's body these trees are also completely destroyed, hence he
ought not set his foot in a distance of one full yojana around this hermitage, and if that
evil-minded one places his foot then he evidently does not exist. [4-11-54, 55a]

shloka: ये च अस्य सचिवाः केचित् संश्रिता मामकम् वनम्
translation:
"And some of his friends that are dependent on my woods shall not live here and they
may depart on hearing my words and solace themselves with my words. [4-11-55b, 56a]

shloka: ते अपि वा यदि तिष्टन्ति शपिष्ये तान् अपि ध्रुवम्
translation:
"This forest of mine is always protected like my own son, and if the monkeys of Vali
wish to stay behind in this forest alone for further destruction of leaves or sprouts, or even for
the non-existence of fruits and tubers of this forest, defiantly they too will be cursed.

shloka:
दिवसः च अद्य मर्यादा यम् द्रष्टा श्वः अस्मि वानरम् |
बहु वर्ष सहस्राणि स वै शैलः भविष्यति
translation:
"And today is the day of limit and the monkey whom I will see tomorrow, he will be
petrified for many thousand years to come.

shloka:
ततः ते वानराः श्रुत्वा गिरम् मुनि समीरिताम् |
निश्चक्रमुः वनात् तस्मात् तान् दृष्ट्वा वालिर् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"Then those monkeys on hearing the clear wording of the sage started out from that
forest, and on their coming to Kishkindha, Vali saw them and spoke this way to them.

shloka:
किम् भवन्तः समस्ताः च मतंग वन वासिनः |
मत् समीपम् अनुप्राप्ता अपि स्वस्ति वनौकसाम्
translation:
" 'Why all of you dwellers of Matanga forest arrived in my presence, even so, are
you the dwellers of that forest safe?' Thus Vali asked all.

shloka:
ततः ते कारणम् सर्वम् तथा शापम् च वालिनः |
शशंसुर् वानराः सर्वे वलिने हेममालिने
translation:
"Then all of those monkeys have reported to Vali, the one with a golden
chest-pendant, all the reasons for their exit, likewise the curse to Vali.

shloka:
एतत् श्रुत्वा तदा वाली वचनम् वनर ईरितम् |
स महर्षिम् समासाद्य याचते स्म कृत अंजलिः
translation:
"Then on hearing all those words narrated by monkeys Vali approached that great sage
and begged of him on becoming humble with palm-fold.

shloka:
महर्षिः तम् अनादृत्य प्रविवेश आश्रमम् प्रति |
शाप धारण भीतः तु वाली विह्वलताम् गतः
translation:
"The sage inconsiderate of Vali's request withdrew into hermitage, and fearing to
bear the brunt of the curse Vali was distraught and withdrew from that place.

shloka:
ततः शाप भयात् भीत ऋश्यमूकम् महागिरिम् |
प्रवेष्टुम् न इच्छति हरिः द्रष्टुम् वा अपि नरेश्वर
translation:
"Then, dreaded by the fear of curse that monkey Vali does not aspire to enter the
great mountain Rishyamuka, oh, people's lord, Rama, or he does not even wish to look at it." Thus
Sugreeva continued his narration.

shloka:
तस्य अप्रवेशम् ज्ञात्वा अहम् इदम् राम महावनम् |
विचरामि सह अमात्यो विषादेन विवर्जितः
translation:
"Knowing the inaccessibility of this forest to him I got rid of my agony, Rama, and
I move here about in this great forest along with my ministers.

shloka:
एषो अस्थिनिचयः तस्य दुन्दुभेः संप्रकाशते |
वीर्य उत्सेकात् निरस्तस्य गिरि कूट निभो महान्
translation:
"This huge heap of bones that is shining forth like a mountaintop is that of
Dundubhi, which Vali once hurled by the vanity of his valour.

shloka:
इमे च विपुलाः सालाः सप्त शाखा अवलंबिनः |
यत्र एकम् घटते वाली निष् पत्रयितुम् ओजसा
translation:
"Also these are the seven enormous sala trees full with their branches, and Vali is
capable to make each of them leafless by his vigour, of course, one at a time.

shloka:
एतत् अस्य असमम् वीर्यम् मया राम प्रकाशितम् |
कथम् तम् वालिनम् हन्तुम् समरे शक्ष्यसे नृप
translation:
"Oh, Rama, I am apprising all this to tell about the unequalled vitality of Vali,
and oh, king, then how is it possible for you to eliminate Vali in war." Thus Sugreeva enquired
with Rama.

shloka:
तथा बृउवाणम् सुग्रीवम् प्रहसन् लक्ष्मणो अब्रवीत् |
कस्मिन् कर्मणि निर्वृत्ते श्रद्दध्या वालिनः वधम्
translation:
When Sugreeva spoke that way Lakshmana a little smiled and asked him, "On performing
which act do you confide in the possibility of Vali's elimination?"

shloka:
तम् उवाचथ सुग्रीवः सप्त सालन् इमान् पुरा |
एवम् एकैकशो वाली विव्याथ अथ स असकृत्
translation:
Then Sugreeva said to Lakshmana, "earlier Vali used to agitate each of the trees,
one after the other, on many occasions."

shloka:
रामो निर्दारयेद् एषाम् बाणेन एकेन च द्रुमम् |
वालिनम् निहतम् मन्ये दृष्ट्वा रामस्य विक्रमम्
translation:
"If Rama can rend one tree out of the seven with only one arrow, then on seeing
Rama's valour I can construe that Vali is utterly dead at his hand.

shloka:
हतस्य महिषस्य अस्थि पादेन एकेन लक्ष्मण |
उद्यम्य प्रक्षिपेत् च अपि तरसा द्वे धनुः शते
translation:
"Lakshmana, if he lifts and kicks the skeleton of this dead buffalo by the might of
his foot, and makes it fall at a distance of two hundred bow-lengths, I can confide." So said
Sugreeva to Lakshmana.

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवो रामम् रक्तान्त लोचनम् |
ध्यत्वा मुहूर्तम् काकुत्स्थम् पुनरेव वचो अब्रवीत्
translation:
Sugreeva paused for a while on saying thus to Rama, for Rama's eye-corners are
reddened with anger towards Vali, and then Sugreeva again spoke to Rama.

shloka:
शूरः च शूरमानी च प्रख्यात बल पौरुषः |
बलवान् वानरः वाली संयुगेषु अपराजितः
translation:
"Vali is a mighty monkey, an intrepid one, who esteems his own intrepidity, and one
who is well renowned by his might and tenacity, and in combats he is an undefeated one.

shloka:
दृश्यन्ते च अस्य कर्माणि दुष्कराणि सुरैः अपि |
यानि संचिन्त्य भीतः अहम् ऋष्यमूकम् उपाश्रितः
translation:
"His deeds that are impracticable even for gods are obvious, and scared for
recollecting them I took shelter of Mt. Rishyamuka.

shloka:
तम् अजय्यम् अधृष्यम् च वानरेन्द्रम् अमर्षणम् |
विचिन्तयन् न मुंचामि ॠष्यमूकम् अमुम् तु अहम्
translation:
"Concluding that the lord of monkeys Vali to be an unconquerable, unattackable,
unsympathetic one I am not leaving this Mt. Rishyamuka.

shloka:
उद्विग्नः शंकितः च अहम् विचरामि महावने |
अनुरक्तैः सह अमात्यैः हनुमत् प्रमुखैः वीरैः
translation:
"I am moving about these forests along with earnest ministers like Hanuma and other
significant ones, only because I am disconcerted and sceptical of him.

shloka:
उपलब्धम् च मे श्लाघ्यम् सन् मित्रम् मित्र वत्सल |
त्वाम् अहम् पुरुषव्याघ्र हिमवन्तम् इव आश्रितः
translation:
"I chanced upon a laudable and true friend in you, oh, Rama, the patron of friends,
hence I take shelter in you, oh, tigerly man, for you are the final resort for those seeking
salvation, like Mt. Himavan.

shloka:
किम् तु तस्य बलज्ञः अहम् दुर्भ्रातुः बलशालिनः |
अप्रत्यक्षम् तु मे वीर्यम् समरे तव राघव
translation:
"I know the might of that mighty brother-the-malice of mine, and oh, Raghava, but
your valour in combat is imprecise to me."

shloka:
न खलु अहम् त्वाम् तुलये न अवमन्ये न भीषये |
कर्मभिः तस्य भीमैः च कातर्यम् जनितम् मम
translation:
"Definitely I am neither examining, nor demeaning, nor intimidating you, but his
macabre exploits caused cowardice in me.

shloka:
कामम् राघव ते वाणी प्रमाणम् धैर्यम् आकृतिः |
सूचयन्ति परम् तेजो भस्म च्छन्नम् इव अनलम्
translation:
"It is definite, oh, Raghava, your word, courage, and physique denote some sublime
radiance in you, as with ash covered fire." So said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य महत्मनः |
स्मित पूर्वम् अथः रामः प्रति उवाच हरिम् प्रति
translation:
On hearing that word of great-souled Sugreeva, Rama smilingly replied that monkey in
his turn.

shloka:
यदि न प्रत्ययो अस्मासु विक्रमे तव वानर |
प्रत्ययम् समरे श्लाघ्यम् अहम् उत्पादयामि ते
translation:
"If you are unable to confide in the intrepidity of ours, oh, monkey, I shall
ingrain commendable confidence in you with respect to our action." Thus Rama said to Sugreeva.

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवम् सान्त्वयन् लक्ष्मणाग्रजः |
राघवो दुन्दुभेः कायम् पाद अंगुष्ठेन लीलया
translation:
Saying so to Sugreeva in a comforting manner, he that dextrous, vigorous Rama, the
elder brother of Lakshmana sportively flipped the skeleton of Dundubhi with his big toe, and
flicked that withered body of the demon with his big toe itself to a ten yojana distance without
lifting his foot. [4-11-84, 85]

shloka:
क्षिप्तम् दृष्ट्वा ततः कायम् सुग्रीवः पुनर् अब्रवीत् |
लक्ष्मणस्य अग्रतो रामम् तपन्तम् इव भास्करम्
हरीणाम् अग्रतो वीरम् इदम् वचनम् अर्थवत्
translation:
Then on seeing at the hurled body, and at valiant Rama who by now is like the
blazing sun, again Sugreeva said this meaningful word to Rama in the presence of Lakshmana and
other monkeys.

shloka:
आर्द्रः स मांसः प्रत्यग्रः क्षिप्तः कायः पुरा सखे |
परिश्रान्तेन मत्तेन भ्राता मे वालिना तदा
translation:
"Oh, friend, at that time when my tired and tipsy brother Vali tossed this body it
was unspoilt, wet with blood and full with flesh.

shloka:
लघुः संप्रति निर्मांसः तृण भूतः च राघव |
क्षिप्ता एवम् प्रहर्षेण भवता रघुनंदन
translation:
"Raghava, now this body is sleazy, without flesh, also rendered into a strawy
condition, and oh, Raghu's delight, you too flipped it because you are now energetic.

shloka:
न अत्र शक्यम् बलम् ज्ञातुम् तव वा तस्य वा अधिकम् |
आर्द्रम् शुष्कम् इति हि एतत् सुमहद् राघव अन्तरम्
translation:
"If it be said something is wet or dried up there chances a lot of difference, oh,
Raghava, thereby it may not be possible to assess whether you might is greater or his, as the
gravity of the case depends much on that wetness or dryness alone, isn't it."

shloka:
स एव संशयः तात तव तस्य च यद् बलम् |
सालम् एकम् विनिर् भिद्या भवेत् व्यक्तिः बलाबले
translation:
"That alone is the uncertainty in that matter, sire, whether your strength is
superior or his, and if a single sala tree is ripped in an outright manner the ability or otherwise
will be evident.

shloka:
कृत्वा एतत् कार्मुकम् सज्यम् हस्ति हतम् इव अपरम् |
आकर्ण पूर्णम् आयम्य विसृजस्व महाशरम्
translation:
"String the bowstring to this bow of yours, an alternate of elephant's trunk, and
stretch it out up to your ear, and release a great arrow.

shloka:
इमम् हि सालम् प्रहितः त्वया शरो
न संशयो अत्र अस्ति विदारयिष्यति |
अलम् विमर्शेन मम प्रियम् ध्रुवम्
कुरुष्व राजन् प्रति शापितो मया
translation:
"Darted by you your arrow will rip off this sala tree, oh, king, there is no doubt
in that matter, enough is this thinking of yours and you will definitely do me this favour, I pray
and swear upon me."

shloka:
यथा हि तेजस्सु वरः सदा रविः
यथा हि शैलो हिमवान् महा अद्रिषु |
यथा चतुष्पात्सु च केसरी वरः
तथा नराणाम् असि विक्रमे वरः
translation:
"As to how the sun is unsurpassed among all brilliances, as to how Himavan is
unmatched among all mountains, as to how the lion is unequalled among all quadrupeds, so you are
among all men for your unique valour." So said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
एतच् च वचनम् श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य सुभाषितम् |
प्रत्ययार्थम् महातेजा रामो जग्राह कार्मुकम्
translation:
On hearing the well-spoken words of Sugreeva that expressed doubt about Rama's
valour, that great resplendent Rama took-up bow to inculcate credence in Sugreeva.

shloka:
स गृहीत्वा धनुर् घोरम् शरम् एकम् च मानदः |
सालम् उद्दिश्य चिक्षेप पूरयन् स रवैः दिशः
translation:
Rama, the bestower of dignity to the sufferers, took up his dreadful bow, aimed at a
sala tree, and darted single arrow, by which all the directions reverberated with the twang of his
bowstring.

shloka:
स विसृष्टो बलवता बाणः स्वर्ण परिष्कृतः |
भित्त्वा सालान् गिरि प्रस्थम् सप्त भूमिम् विवेश ह
translation:
The golden arrow released by the mighty Rama perforated all the seven sala trees,
and even the levelled areas of mountain, and then entered the earth.

shloka:
सायकः तु मुहूर्तेन सालान् भित्त्वा महाजवः |
निष्पत्य च पुनः तूर्णम् तम् एव प्रविवेश ह
translation:
Thus that arrow which briskly drilled all the sala trees, came up in a moment from
under the earth, and again swiftly re-entered the quiver of Rama.

shloka:
तान् दृष्ट्वा सप्त निर्भिन्नान् सालान् वानरपुंगवः |
रामस्य शर वेगेन विस्मयम् परमम् गतः
translation:
On seeing them the seven sala trees that are profoundly fissured, that best monkey
Sugreeva went into a stunning astonishment at the rapidity of Rama's arrow.

shloka:
स मूर्ध्ना न्यपतत् भूमौ प्रलंबीकृत भूषणः |
सुग्रीवः परम प्रीतो राघवाय कृतांजलिः
translation:
Highly gladdened Sugreeva made palm-fold in that astonishment, kneeled while his
ornaments dangled, and prostrated before Raghava with his head touching the ground.

shloka:
इदम् च उवाच धर्मज्ञम् कर्मणा तेन हर्षितः |
रामम् सर्व अस्त्र विदुषाम् श्रेष्ठम् शूरम् अवस्थितम्
translation:
Overjoyed with that deed Sugreeva said this to that virtue-knower, the one who is
proficient among all experts of missiles, namely the valorous Rama, who is just in his presence
him.

shloka:
स इन्द्रान् अपि सुरान् सर्वाम् त्वम् बाणैः पुरुषर्षभ |
समर्थः समरे हन्तुम् किम् पुनर् वालिनम् प्रभो
translation:
"You with your arrows, oh, best one among men, are capable of eliminating all the
gods including Indra, oh, lord, then why to speak of Vali.

shloka:
येन सप्त महा साला गिरिर् भूमिः च दारिताः |
बाणेन एकेन काकुत्स्थ स्थाता ते को रण अग्रतः
translation:
"By whom seven great sala trees, a mountain and also the earth is ripped off with
only one arrow, oh Kakutstha, who then can stand up to you in the vanguard of war.

shloka:
अद्य मे विगतः शोकः प्रीतिर् अद्य परा मम |
सुहृदम् त्वाम् समासाद्य महेन्द्र वरुणोपमम्
translation:
"Today on gaining a kind-hearted friend like you, who is similar to Indra and
Rain-god who accord favour on their own, my distress is gone and my joy is heightened.

shloka:
तम् अद्य एव प्रियार्थम् मे वैरिणम् भ्रातृ रूपिणम् |
वालिनम् जहि काकुत्स्थ मया बद्धो अयम् अंजलिः
translation:
"Oh, Rama, today itself you eliminate that enemy of mine in a brother's semblance
for my happiness, for which I adjoin my palms in supplication." Thus Sugreeva requested Rama.

shloka:
ततो रामः परिष्वज्य सुग्रीवम् प्रिय दर्शनम् |
प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणानुगतम् वचः

अस्माद् गच्छाम किष्किन्धाम् क्षिप्रम् गच्छ त्वम् अग्रतः |
गत्वा च आह्वय सुग्रीव वालिनम् भ्रातृ गन्धिनम्
translation:
""Let us quickly go from here to Kishkindha, oh, Sugreeva, you move in advance, and
on going there you invite that Vali, one redolent of your brotherhood." So said Rama to Sugreeva.

shloka:
सर्वे ते त्वरितम् गत्वा किष्किन्धाम् वालिनः पुरीम् |
वृक्षैः आत्मानम् आवृत्य हि अतिष्ठन् गहने वने
translation:
They all on quickly going to Kishkindha, the city of Vali, hedged themselves in the
thickets of forest trees and waited.

shloka:
सुग्रीवो अपि व्यनदद् घोरम् वालिनो ह्वान कारणात् |
गाढम् परिहितो वेगान् नादैः भिन्दन् इव अंबरम्
translation:
Sugreeva firmly tightened his girdle-cloth for the duel and shouted boisterously for
the purpose of inviting Vali for a duel, and his rapidity in shouting appeared as though to crack
the sky.

shloka:
तम् श्रुत्वा निनदम् भ्रातुः क्रुद्धो वाली महाबलः |
निष्पपात सुसंरब्धो भास्करो अस्त तटात् इव
translation:
On hearing his brother's shouting that great mighty Vali is infuriated and
impetuously rushed out of his palace chambers, like the sun falling back onto sky from his dusking
brink.

shloka:
ततः सुतुमुलम् युद्धम् वालि सुग्रीवयोः अभूत् |
गगने ग्रहयोः घोरम् बुध अंगारकयोः इव
translation:
Then a very tumultuous and awful fight occurred between Vali and Sugreeva, which is
like the awful fight between the planets Mercury and Mars in skies.

shloka:
तलैः अशनि कल्पैः च वज्र कल्पैः च मुष्टिभिः |
जघ्नतुः समरे अन्योन्यम् भ्रातरौ क्रोध मूर्च्छितौ
translation:
Those two brothers who are convulsed in frenzy battered each other in that fight
with their thunderbolt-like palms, and lightning-like fists.

shloka:
ततो रामो धनुष् पाणिः तौ उभौ समुदैक्षत |
अन्योन्य सदृशौ वीरौ उभौ देवौ इव अश्विनौ
translation:
Then Rama wielding bow in his hand watched those valiant ones that are alike in
their appearance, like the Ashwin twins among gods.

shloka:
यत् न अवगच्छत् सुग्रीवम् वालिनम् वा अपि राघवः |
ततो न कृतवान् बुद्धिम् मोक्तुम् अन्तकरम् शरम्
translation:
For which reason Raghava could not differentiate between Sugreeva or Vali, for the
same reason did not make up his mind to release his arrow, otherwise it would have been a deadening
arrow, as confusion is the only reason for Rama.

shloka:
एतस्मिन् अन्तरे भग्नः सुग्रीवः तेन वालिना |
अपश्यन् राघवम् नाथम् ऋश्यमूकम् प्रदुद्रुवे
translation:
Meanwhile Sugreeva is unable to spot out his benefactor Raghava as Vali whacked him
down, and thereby he immediately fled to Mt. Rishyamuka.

shloka:
क्लान्तो रुधिर सिक्त अंगो प्रहारैः जर्जरी कृतः |
वालिना अभिद्रुतः क्रोधात् प्रविवेश महावनम्
translation:
Sugreeva is debilitated and enervated by Vali's thwacking till his limbs soaked in
blood, and he entered the great forest of Rishyamuka as Vali chased him.

shloka:
तम् प्रविष्टम् वनम् दृष्ट्वा वाली शाप भयात् ततः |
मुक्तो हि असि त्वम् इति उक्त्वा स निवृत्तो महाबलः
translation:
On seeing Sugreeva's entry into the forest of Rishyamuka, Vali said to him "you are
let off for now..." and saying so he returned to Kishkindha from there in view of fear from curse
of Sage Matanga.

shloka:
राघवो अपि सह भ्रात्रा सह चैव हनूमता |
तदेव वनम् आगच्छत् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः
translation:
Raghava also came to that forest, along with his brother Lakshmana and along with
Hanuma, where that monkey Sugreeva fled.

shloka:
तम् समीक्ष्य आगतम् रामम् सुग्रीवः सह लक्ष्मणम् |
ह्रीमान् दीनम् उवाच इदम् वसुधाम् अवलोकयन्
translation:
Seeing the arrival of Rama with Lakshmana, Sugreeva ashamedly turned his eyes down
to earth and piteously spoke this without eyeing Rama

shloka:
आह्वयस्व इति माम् उक्त्वा दर्शयित्वा च विक्रमम् |
वैरिणा घातयित्वा च किम् इदानीम् त्वया कृतम्
translation:
"Showing your dexterity you encouraged me to invite Vali for fight, but you got me
battered by my enemy, what is this done by you."

shloka:
ताम् एव वेलाम् वक्तव्यम् त्वया राघव तत्त्वतः |
वालिनम् न निहन्मि इति ततो न अहम् इतो व्रजे
translation:
"You should have truly made it known at that time only, oh, Raghava, that you will
not kill Vali, then I would not have come here, to Kishkindha.

shloka:
तस्य च एवम् ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
करुणम् दीनया वाचा राघवः पुनर् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Rama replied that great-souled Sugreeva who is speaking woefully with pathetic words
in this way.

shloka:
सुग्रीव श्रूयताम् तात क्रोधः च व्यपनीयताम् |
कारणम् येन बाणो अयम् स मया न विसर्जितः
translation:
"Sugreeva, by which reason I have not let-off an arrow such as that of mine, that
reason may be heard and let the anger be discarded.

shloka:
अलंकारेण वेषेण प्रमाणेन गतेन च |
त्वम् च सुग्रीव वाली च सदृशौ स्थः परस्परम्
translation: "By ornamentation, attire, physicality and movements, you and Vali look-alike.

shloka:
स्वरेण वर्चसा च एव प्रेक्षितेन च वानर |
विक्रमेण च वाक्यैः च व्यक्तिम् वाम् न उपलक्षये
translation:
"By your voice, bodily glow also thus in your looking, also in bravery and in
speech, oh monkey, I could not mark any difference.

shloka:
ततो अहम् रूप सादृश्यात् मोहितो वानरोत्तम |
न उत्सृजामि महावेगम् शरम् शत्रु निबर्हणम्
translation:
"Thereby, oh, great monkey, I have not released this great speeded and enemy
annihilating arrow of mine as I was confused in the similarity of your personalities.

shloka:
जीवित अन्तकरम् घोरम् सादृश्यात् तु विशंकितः |
मूलघातो न नौ स्याद्धि द्वयोः इति कृतो मया
translation:
"I was ambiguous by your similarities, as such I have not released this ghastly and
life-taking arrow, otherwise the basic object of ours will be ruined, isn't it.

shloka:
त्वयि वीर विपन्ने हि अज्ञान् लाघवान् मया |
मौढ्यम् च मम बाल्यम् च ख्यापितम् स्यात् कपीस्वर
translation:
"When my unawareness and fallacy hazardously afflicts none but you in the form of my
own arrow, oh, brave lord of monkeys, then I will be establishing my own imbecility and naivety,
isn't it.

shloka:
दत्त अभय वधो नाम पातकम् महत् अद्भुतम् |
अहम् च लक्ष्मणः च एव सीत च वरवर्णिनी
translation:
"Eliminating one who is protected means a terrifying sin of highest order, even so,
myself and Lakshmana and also thus Seetha with her exquisite glow are all dependent on you, and you
are our shelterer in this forest. [4-12-35, 36a]

shloka: तस्मात् युध्यस्व भूयस्त्वम् मा शंकी च वानर
translation:
"Therefore, oh, monkey, again you fight with him without doubting me, and I will
render him ineffective at this moment only with a single arrow of mine, and you can see Vali
squirming on the ground. [4-12-36, 37],

shloka:
अभिज्ञानम् कुरुष्व त्वम् आत्मनो वानरेश्वर |
येन त्वाम् अभिजानीयाम् द्वन्द्व युद्धम् उपागतम्
translation:
"You have an identification for yourself, oh lord of monkeys, by which you can be
identified when you are engaged in duel.

shloka:
गज पुष्पीम् इमाम् फुल्लाम् उत्पाट्य शुभ लक्षणाम् |
कुरु लक्ष्मण कण्ठे अस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
translation:
"Lakshmana, pick up this gaja creeper that is beautiful in its appearance and let
this noble souled Sugreeva be garlanded with that." So said Rama to Lakshmana.

shloka:
ततो गिरि तटे जाताम् उत्पाट्य कुसुमायुताम् |
लक्ष्मणो गज पुष्पीम् ताम् तस्य कण्ठे व्यसर्जयत्
translation:
Then Lakshmana plucked that gaja creeper with flowers growing at the foot of the
mountain, and slung it like a garland around the neck of that Sugreeva.  n

shloka:
स तथा शुशुभे श्रीमान् लतया कण्ठ सक्तया |
मालया इव बलाकानाम् ससंध्य इव तोयदः
translation:
He that prosperous Sugreeva with that flowery-creeper adorning his neck then shone
forth like a black rain cloud against a backdrop of rich ochry colour of sunset, and with a train
of herons adorning that cloud like a garland.

shloka:
विभ्राजमानो वपुषा राम वाक्य समाहितः |
जगाम सह रामेण किष्किंधाम् पुनराप सः
translation:
He that Sugreeva whose physique became effulgent by that creeper-garland is again
emboldened by Rama's words, and he again advanced to Kishkindha with Rama, and reached it again.

shloka:
ऋश्यमूकात् स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धाम् लक्ष्मण अग्रजः |
जगाम सह सुग्रीवो वालि विक्रम पालिताम्
translation:
That righteous Rama readying his great bow decorated with gold, and on taking blazing sun similar arrows 
that are victory-oriented in wars, proceeded from Rishyamuka along with Sugreeva to the city ruled by 
the valour of Vali, namely Kishkindha. [4-13-1, 2]

shloka:
अग्रतः तु ययौ तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः |
सुग्रीवः संहत ग्रीवो लक्ष्मणः च महाबलः
translation: Stern-necked Sugreeva and the great mighty Lakshmana strode ahead of that great soul Rama.

shloka:
पृष्ठतो हनुमान् वीरो नलो नीलः च वीर्यवान् |
तारः चैव महातेजा हरि यूथप यूथपाः
translation:
The brave Hanuma, dauntless Nala and Neela, and the captain of monkey's captains Tara of great energy 
followed them rearward.

shloka:
ते वीक्षमाणा वृक्षाम् च पुष्प भार अवलम्बिनः |
प्रसन्न अंबुवहाः चैव सरितः सागरम् गमाः
translation:
They moved on looking at the trees that are drooping with the weight of their flowers, and at he rivers 
that are carrying pleasant water while themselves are coursing towards ocean.

shloka:
कन्दराणि च शैलाम् च निर्दराणि गुहाः तथा |
शिखराणि च मुख्यानि दरीः च प्रिय दर्शनाः
translation:
They on seeing house-like caverns, crags, ravines and caves, and monumental peaks, cavities that are 
pleasant for sight have moved on.

shloka:
वैदूर्य विमलैः तोयैः पद्मैः च आकोश कुड्मलैः |
शोभितान् सजलान् मार्गे तटाकान् च अवलोकयन्
translation:
On their way they observed lakes that are glistening forth with gem-like waters without slime, and with 
lotus buds in budding stage.

shloka:
कारण्डैस्सारसैर्हंसैर्वञ्जुलैर्जलकुक्कुटैः |
चक्रवाकैस्थाचान्यैश्शकुनैर्प्रतिनादितान्
translation:
Those lakes are reverberant with Karandava-s, Saarasa-s, Swans, Vanjula-s and other waterfowls, also 
like that with Chakravaaka-s and other birds.

shloka:
मृदुशष्पाङ्कुराअहारान्निर्भयान्वनगोचरान् |
चरतांसर्वतोपश्यन्स्थलीषु हरिणान्स्थितान्
translation:
They have seen fearless deer feeding on soft grass blades everywhere, somewhere moving here and there 
in the forest, and else where standing.

shloka:
तटाक वैरिणः च अपि शुक्ल दन्त विभूषितान् |
घोरान् एकचरान् वन्यान् द्विरदान् कूल घातिनः
translation:
They have also seen the forest elephants that have white tusks for their ornaments and that are moving 
in herds, and which are the dangerous enemies of lakes as they destroy lakebeds.

shloka:
मत्तन् गिरि तट उद्घुष्टान् पर्वतान् इव जंगमान् |
वानरान् द्विरद प्रख्यान् मही रेणु समुक्षितान्
translation:
Also seen are the vigorous and elephantine monkeys that are like mobile mountains, begrimed with dust, 
and bellowing on mountain ridges.

shloka:
वने वन चराम् च अन्यान् खेचराम् च विहंगमान् |
पश्यन्तः त्वरिता जग्मुः सुग्रीव वश वर्तिनः
translation:
On seeing other forest beings in that forest and birds moving aloft in sky, those followers of Sugreeva 
quickly moved on.

shloka:
तेषाम् तु गच्छताम् तत्र त्वरितम् रघुनंदनः |
द्रुम षण्ड वनम् दृष्ट्वा रामः सुग्रीवम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
While they are quickly going, Rama, the delight of Raghu's dynasty, saw there a clump of forest trees 
and he asked Sugreeva like this.

shloka:
एष मेघ इव आकाशे वृक्ष षण्डः प्रकाशते |
मेघ संघात विपुलः पर्यन्त कदली वृतः
translation:
"This cluster of trees surrounded with plantain trees is like an accumulation of thick clouds, and this 
is shining forth like a cloudscape in sky.

shloka:
किम् एतत् ज्ञातुम् इच्छामि सखे कौतूहलम् मम |
कौतूहल अपनयनम् कर्तुम् इच्छामि अहम् त्वया
translation: "What is this? I wish to know and oh, friend, I wish you to clear this inquisitiveness of mine.

shloka:
तस्य तद् वचनम् श्रुत्वा राघवस्य महात्मनः |
गच्छन्न् एव आचचक्षे अथ सुग्रीवः तत् महद् वनम्
translation:
On hearing that sentence of that great soul Raghava, then Sugreeva described about the significance 
of that forest while proceeding on the way.

shloka:
एतद् राघव विस्तीर्णम् आश्रमम् श्रम नाशनम् |
उद्यान वन संपन्नम् स्वादु मूल फल उदकम्
translation:
"Raghava, this spacious hermitage with abundant gardens and dainty tubers, fruits and water is a weary 
remover." Thus Sugreeva started telling Rama.

shloka:
अत्र सप्तजना नाम मुनयः संशित व्रताः |
सप्त एव आसन् अधः शीर्षा नियतम् जल शायिनः
translation:
"There were hermits namedsapta jana, Seven Persons, who were dourly vowed 
with their heads pendulous downward and legs up, as inshiirSa aasana, 
the upside-down yogic body posture, and who always reclined in water.

shloka:
सप्त रात्रे कृत आहारा वायुना अचल वासिनः |
दिवम् वर्ष शतैः याताः सप्तभिः सकलेवराः
translation:
"They were making diet on air alone that too once in seven days, and living unwaveringly in that way 
they practised their asceticism for seven hundred years and went to heavens with their bodies.

shloka:
तेषाम् एतत् प्रभावेण द्रुम प्राकार संवृतम् |
आश्रमम् सुदुराधर्षम् अपि स इन्द्रैः सुर असुरैः
translation:
"This hermitage that has encircling trees for its compound wall has become highly unassailable even 
for Indra together with all gods and demons.

shloka:
पक्षिणो वर्जयन्ति एतत् तथा अन्ये वनचारिणः |
विशन्ति मोहाद् ये अपि अत्र न निवर्तन्ते ते पुनः
translation:
"Birds and other forest moving animals forbear this hermitage and those that unknowingly enter in there 
they do not return.

shloka:
विभूषण रवाअः च अत्र श्रूयंते सकलाक्षराः |
तूर्य गीत स्वनाअः च अपि गन्धो दिव्यः च राघव
translation:
"From there artistically worded lyrical and instrumental tunes, and even the sounds of ornaments are 
audible, and oh, Raghava, one can sense a divine fragrance too.

shloka:
त्रेताग्नयो अपि दीप्यन्ते धूमो हि एष प्रदृश्यते |
वेष्टयन् इव वृक्ष अग्रान् कपोत अंग अरुणो घनः
translation:
"Even the triadic ritual-fires glow there, and their thick and ochry coloured smoke like that of a reddish-brown 
pigeon is apparent muffling the treetops.

shloka:
एते वृक्षाः प्रकाशन्ते धूम संसक्त मस्तकाः |
मेघ जाल प्रतिच्छन्ना वैदूर्य गिरयो यथा
translation:
"When that smoke is mantling their tops these trees are beaming forth like mountains of gems overlaid 
with clusters of clouds.

shloka:
कुरु प्रणामम् धर्मात्मन् तेषाम् उद्दिश्य राघवः |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा प्रयतः संयत अंजलिः
translation:
"Offer salutations determinedly and adjoining palms addressing the sages called Seven Persons, oh Raghava, 
along with brother Lakshmana

shloka:
प्रणमन्ति हि ये तेषाम् ऋषीणाम् भावित आत्मनाम् |
न तेषाम् अशुभम् किंचित् शरीरे राम दृश्यते
translation:
"Those that offer salutations to those sages with contemplated souls will evince no bodily trauma in 
the least." Thus said Sugreeva to Rama.

shloka:
ततो रामः सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन कृतांजलिः |
समुद्दिश्य महात्मानः तान् ऋषीन् अभ्यवादयत्
translation:
Then Rama along with brother Lakshmana adjoined palms, addressed himself to the great-souled sages known 
as Seven Persons, and offered salutations to them.

shloka:
अभिवाद्य च धर्मात्मा रामो भ्राता च लक्ष्मणः |
सुग्रीवो वानराअः चैव जग्मुः संहृष्ट मानसाः | ४-१३-२८
translation:
That righteous Rama along with brother Lakshmana, Sugreeva and other monkeys having worshipped those 
sages proceeded to Kishkindha well-pleased at heart.

shloka:
ते गत्वा दूरम् अध्वानम् तस्मात् सप्त जन आश्रमात् |
ददृशुः ताम् दुराधर्षाम् किष्किन्धाम् वालि पालिताम्
translation:
Having gone a long way from that hermitage of Seven Persons they have seen that unassailable and Vali 
ruled city namely Kishkindha.

shloka:
ततस्तु रामानुज राम वानराः
प्रगृह्य शस्त्राणि उदित उग्र तेजसा |
पुरीम् सुरेश आत्मज वीर्य पालिताम्
वधाय शत्रोः पुनर् आगताः इह
translation:
Then Rama's bother Lakshmana, Rama, and other monkeys wielding their weapons and flaring with their 
upsurged fiery again came to eliminate that enemy Vali to the city that is ruled by the brawn of the 
same Vali, the son of Indra.

shloka:
सर्वे ते त्वरितम् गत्वा किष्किन्धाम् वालिनः पालिताम् |
वृक्षैर् आत्मानम् आवृत्य व्यतिष्ठन् गहने वने
translation:
They all on quickly going to Kishkindha, the city of Vali, hedged themselves in the
thickets of forest trees and waited.

shloka:
विसार्य सर्वतो दृष्टिम् कानने कानन प्रियः |
सुग्रीवो विपुल ग्रीवः क्रोधम् आहारयद् भृशम्
translation:
That forest lover with tumultuous voice Sugreeva cast his eye everywhere and assumed
tremendous fury.

shloka:
ततः तु निनदम् घोरम् कृत्वा युद्धाय च आह्वयत् |
परिवारैः परिवृतो नादैर् भिन्दन् इव अंबरम्
translation:
Then Sugreeva encompassed by his followers war-whooped ghastlily, like a great cloud
that emerged accelerated by gusty wind and that is thundering as though to rip the sky, inviting
Vali for fight.

shloka: अथ बालार्क सदृशो दृप्त सिम्ह गतिः ततः
translation:
Then Sugreeva who is like the rising sun and whose stride is like that of a proud
lion saw the adroit Rama and then said this sentence. [4-14-4b, 5a]

shloka: हरि वागुरया व्याप्तम् तप्त कांचन तोरणाम्
translation:
" She whose arch-way is decorated in gold, who is spread out with snares of monkeys,
and who is impregnated with flags and machinery, we arrived at such city of Vali, Kishkindha.
[4-14-5b, 6a]

shloka: प्रतिज्ञा या कृता वीर त्वया वालि वधे पुरा
translation:
"Oh Brave one, you make happen the promise you earlier made regarding the
elimination of Vali on time, like the time of sprouting that enables a creeper-plant to bear a
sprout on time. [4-14-6b, 7a]

shloka: एवम् उक्तः तु धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवेण स राघवः
translation:
When thus said by Sugreeva that enemy-destroyer and righteous Raghava said this word
Sugreeva. [4-14-7b, 8a]

shloka: कृत अभिज्ञान चिह्नः त्वम् अनया गज साह्वया
translation:
"By which creeper-garland that Lakshmana plucked out and garlanded you, by this
creeper-garland of gaja-flowers alone your identification is marked. [4-14-8b, 9a]

shloka: सोभासे अपि अधिकम् वीर लतया कण्ठसक्तया
translation:
"Oh brave-one, you are shining forth with this creeper-garland laced at your neck
like the night time sun with a garland of stars. [4-14-9b, 10a]

shloka: अद्य वालि समुत्थम् ते भयम् वैरम् च वानर
translation:
"Oh Vanara, today itself I will set you free from the fear and enmity whipped up by
Vali by releasing a single arrow in fight. [4-14-10b, 11a]

shloka: मम दर्शय सुग्रीव वैरिणम् भ्रातृ रूपिणम्
translation:
"You show me your enemy in a brother's mien, oh, monkey, by then he will be rolling
in the dust of this forest eliminated by me. [4-14-11b, 12a]

shloka: यदि दृष्टि पथम् प्राप्तो जीवन् स विनिवर्तते
translation:
"If he returns to live even after my espying him then immediately you can find fault
with me, you can even deride me. [4-14-12b, 13a]

shloka: प्रत्यक्षम् सप्त ते साला मया बाणेन दारिताः
translation:
"Seven saala trees are rived with a single of arrow of mine in your presence,
thereby be sure that Vali will be dispatched now, by my might. [4-14-13b, 14a]

shloka: अनृतम् न उक्त पूर्वम् मे चिरम् कृच्छ्रे अपि तिष्ठता
translation:
"Just bound by the anxiousness to implement righteousness untruth is unsaid by me
earlier though I am involved in distresses for a long time, and hereafter it will not be said in
anywise. [4-14-14b, 15a]

shloka: सफलाम् च करिष्यामि प्रतिज्ञाम् जहि संभ्रमम्
translation:
"As Indra fructifies the sprouted paddy field I will make happen my promise, hence
leave off your perplexity." [4-14-15b, 16a]

shloka: तद् आह्वान निमित्तम् च वालिनो हेममालिनः
translation:
"Thereby to invite that Vali with golden pendant, oh, Sugreeva, you make such a
war-cry by which that monkey Vali comes out. [4-14-16b, 17a]

shloka: जितकाशी जयश्लाघी त्वया च अधर्षितः पुरात्
translation:
"Vali is a willing fighter who shines forth by his victories and one who is given
ovation for his triumphs, and undefeated by you as yet, such as he is he may be incited with
war-whoop so that he comes out without any hindrance. [4-14-17b, 18a]

shloka: रिपूणाम् धर्षितम् श्रुत्वा मर्षयन्ति न संयुगे
translation:
"One who is assertive of his own valour will not tolerate to hear enemy's daring in
a brawl, that too in the presence of ladies." So said Rama to Sugreeva. [4-14-18b, 19a]

shloka: स तु राम वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो हेमपिंगलः
translation:
On hearing the words of Rama he that Sugreeva with golden yellow complexion blared a
gruesome blare as though to completely rend the sky. [4-14-19b, 20a]

shloka: तत्र शब्देन वित्रस्ता गावो यान्ति हतप्रभाः
translation:
By that sound of Sugreeva the splendour of cows is marred and they are running
helter-skelter like the well-born ladies who are mishandled by invaders due to the misrule of their
own king. [4-14-20b, 21a]

shloka:
द्रवन्ति च मृगाः शीघ्रम् भग्ना;इव रणे हयाः |
पतन्ति च खगा भूमौ क्षीण पुण्या इव ग्रहाः
translation:
And deer are hurriedly fleeing like war worsted horses, and the sky-flying birds are
falling to ground like planets or stars when their merit diminishes. [4-14-21b, c]

shloka:
ततः स जीमूत कृत प्रणादो
नादम् हि अमुंचत् त्वरया प्रतीतः |
सूर्यात्मजः शौर्य विवृद्ध तेजाः
सरित् पतिर्वा अनिल चंचल ऊर्मिः
translation:
Sugreeva, the son of Sun, who is well-known for cloud like thundering, and whose
vigour is now reinforced by his bravery, then promptly released an oceanic roar like an ocean with
splashing waves drifted by gales.

shloka:
अथ तस्य निनादम् तम् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
शुश्राव अन्तःपुर गतो वाली भ्रातुर् अमर्षणः
translation:
Then the illiberal Vali has clearly heard that outcry of his plain-spoken brother
Sugreeva from his palace chambers.

shloka:
श्रुत्वा तु तस्य निनदम् सर्वभूत प्रकंपनम् |
मदः च एकपदे नष्टः क्रोधः च आपादितो महान्
translation:
On hearing Sugreeva's outcry that is shuddering all beings Vali's insolence is
diminished as high furore superimposed on it.

shloka:
ततो रोष परीत अंगो वाली स कनक प्रभः |
उपरक्त इव आदित्यः सद्यो निष्प्रभताम् गतः
translation:
Then, embitterment overspreading on all his limbs Vali with golden-hue is
immediately rendered non-luminous like the eclipsed sun.

shloka:
वाली दंष्ट्रा करालः तु क्रोधाद् दीप्त अग्नि लोचनः |
भाति उत्पतित पद्माभः समृणाल इव ह्रदः
translation:
With asymmetrical teeth and with burning fireball like eyes Vali is reflective of a
lake whose red-lotuses are uprooted leaving stalks afloat.

shloka:
शब्दम् दुर्मर्षणम् श्रुत्वा निष्पपात ततो हरिः |
वेगेन च पद न्यासैर् दारयन् इव मेदिनीम्
translation:
That monkey Vali then on hearing that intolerable noise bolted out of palace
chambers thumping his feet as though to shatter the earth.

shloka:
तम् तु तारा परिष्वज्य स्नेहाद् दर्शित सौहृदा |
उवाच त्रस्त संभ्रांता हित उदर्कम् इदम् वचः
translation:
His wife Tara stepped in and showing goodwill and amity hugged him, for she is in
fear and bewilderment, and said this word that is beneficial in its futurity if Vali heeds it.

shloka:
साधु क्रोधम् इमम् वीर नदी वेगम् इव आगतम् |
शयनाद् उत्थितः काल्यम् त्यज भुक्ताम् इव स्रजम्
translation:
"Oh brave one, you better gently leave off this anger that is coming on like a
gushing river as is done with an enjoyed chaplet on getting up from bed in early hours.

shloka:
काल्यम् एतेन संग्रामम् करिष्यसि च वानर |
वीर ते शत्रु बाहुल्यम् फल्गुता वा न विद्यते
translation:
"Oh, monkey, you can fight with him in early hours of tomorrow, oh, brave one,
evidently you neither have divers enemies nor your valour is trivialised."

shloka:
सहसा तव निष्क्रामो मम तावत् न रोचते |
श्रूयताम् अभिधास्यामि यन् निमित्तम् निवार्यते
translation:
"Your quick exiting is disagreeable for me, and what for you are dissuaded that may
be listened as I tell.

shloka:
पूर्वम् आपतितः क्रोधात् स त्वाम् आह्वयते युधि |
निष्पत्य च निरस्तः ते हन्यमानो दिशो गतः
translation:
"Earlier Sugreeva came assaulting and inviting you for a combat, and you also have
gone out and rendered him as a nonentity, and being battered by you he fled in all directions.

shloka:
त्वया तस्य निरस्तस्य पीडितस्य विशेषतः |
इह एत्य पुनर् आह्वानम् शंकाम् जनयति इव मे
translation:
"He who is undone earlier by you, particularly after torturing by you, his coming
here again and inviting you for a duel is causing a doubt in me.

shloka:
दर्पः च व्यवसायः च यादृशः तस्य नर्दतः |
निनादस्य च संरंभो न एतत् अल्पम् हि कारणम्
translation:
"The arrogance and endeavour of the shouter, and even the rampage of his furore, all
these will not have a trivial reason, isn't it.

shloka:
न असहायम् अहम् मन्ये सुग्रीवम् तम् इह आगतम् |
अवष्टब्ध सहायः च यम् आश्रित्य एष गर्जति
translation:
"I do not think that Sugreeva has come here unaccompanied, and on whom he is
dependant must be an unflinching support foregathered by Sugreeva.

shloka:
प्रकृत्या निपुणः चैव बुद्धिमान् चैव वानरः |
न अपरीक्षित वीर्येण सुग्रीवः सख्यम् एष्यति
translation:
"By his nature Sugreeva is an expert and even so a clever one, and he does not enter
into friendship with anyone without examining his mettle.

shloka:
पूर्वम् एव मया वीर श्रुतम् कथयतो वचः |
अंगदस्य कुमारस्य वक्ष्यामि अद्य हितम् वचः
translation:
"I am already briefed by our son Angada's information, and what I have heard I will
now relate that helpful word to you.

shloka:
अंगदः तु कुमरो अयम् वनांतम् उपनिर्गतः |
प्रवृत्तिः तेन कथिता चारैः असीत् निवेदिता
translation:
"Son Angada said this account when he returned from forests, and to him spies are
said to have reported this.

shloka:
अयोध्य अधिपतेः पुत्रौ शूरौ समर दुर्जयौ |
इक्ष्वाकूणाम् कुले जातौ प्रथितौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
"Those that are born in Ikshvaku dynasty, sons of the king of Ayodhya, valiant and
unconquerable ones in war, called Rama and Lakshmana are there in this country. These two
unassailable ones have chanced there at Sugreeva's place to fulfil the longing desire of Sugreeva.
[4-15-17, 18a]

shloka: स ते भ्रातुर् हि विख्यातः सहायो रण कर्मणि
translation:
"He is an acclaimed one for his warfare, and like the fire flaring up at the end of
era he shatters the strength of enemies, and he is Rama your brother's helpmate, they say so.
[4-15-18b, 19a]

shloka:
निवास वृक्षः साधूनाम् आपन्नानाम् परा गतिः | ४-१५-१९
आर्तानाम् संश्रयः चैव यशसः च एक भाजनम् |
translation:
"And he is said to the habitable tree for the polite, the ultimate course for the
woebegone, a hospice for the agonised, and for grace Rama is the only abode. [4-15-19b, 20a]

shloka: ज्ञान विज्ञान संपन्नो निदेशो निरतः पितुः
translation:
"He is endowed with the knowledge of mundane and ultra-mundane things, he always
abides in the directives of his father, and as with Mt. Himalayas for all natural elements he is
the greatest mine of merits. [4-15-20b, 21a]

shloka: तत् क्षमो न विरोधः ते सह तेन महात्मना
translation:
"By that reason, with that unconquerable on in conflicts, an imponderable one and a
great-soul Rama, your enmity is inapposite. [4-15-21b, 22a]

shloka: शूर वक्ष्यामि ते किंचिन् न च इच्छामि अभ्यसूयितुम्
translation:
"Oh dauntless one, I tell you this much that you shall not become overcritical of
him, and what I say is beneficial to you that may now be listened and even implemented. [4-15-22b,
23a]

shloka: यौवराज्येन सुग्रीवम् तूर्णम् साधु अभिषेचय
translation:
"Oh, king, let Sugreeva be decorously and quickly anointed as prince regent, and oh,
resolute one, let there be no hostility to your own younger brother. [4-15-23b, 24a]

shloka: अहम् हि ते क्षमम् मन्ये तेन रामेण सौहृदम्
translation:
"Achieving unanimity with Sugreeva and solidarity with Rama by discarding enmity, in
effect is appropriate for you, thus I deem. [4-15-24b, 25a]

shloka: लालनीयो हि ते भ्राता यवीयान् एष वानरः
translation:
"This Sugreeva is your younger brother and you should be keen about him, isn't it...
and whether he is here or there in Rishyamuka he is just your brother. [4-15-25b, 26a]

shloka: नहि तेन समम् बन्धुम् भुवि पश्यामि किंचन
translation:
"Indeed, I do not see anyone on earth a coequal to him in kindred spirit, hence
leave off this enmity and honour him with bestowals and felicitations as an insider, and retain him
at your side. [4-15-26b, 27]

shloka:
सुग्रीवो विपुल ग्रीवो महाबन्धुः मतः तव |
भ्रातृ सौहृदम् आलंब्य न अन्या गति इह अस्ति ते
translation:
"That boisterously voiced Sugreeva is indisputably an excellent kinsman of yours,
and hence brace yourself with the fondness of brotherhood, as there is no other way out to you.

shloka:
यदि ते मत् प्रियम् कार्यम् यदि च अवैषि माम् हिताम् |
याच्यमानः प्रियत्वेन साधु वाक्यम् कुरुष्व मे
translation:
"If you look upon to do my favoured deed, and if you look upon me as an expedient
one, I beg of you in our loving attachment that my gentle word of advise be done.

shloka:
प्रसीद पथ्यम् श्रुणु जल्पितम् हि मे
न रोषम् एव अनुविधातुम् अर्हसि |
क्षमो हि ते कोशल राज सूनुना
न विग्रहः शक्र सम तेजसा
translation:
"Be graceful and it behove you to listen to my small but expedient talk, and
following up rancour alone is unbecoming of you, thereby your confrontation with the Prince of
Kosala will be unpardonable for his dynamism equals that of Indra." Thus Tara spoke to her husband
Vali.

shloka:
तदा हि तारा हितम् एव वाक्यम्
तम् वालिनम् पथ्यम् इदम् बभाषे |
न रोचते तद् वचनम् हि तस्य
काल अभिपन्नस्य विनाश काले
translation:
Then, though Tara spoke beneficial and advisable words they are unimpressive to Vali
for he is impounded by fatality and driven by time to his doom.

shloka:
ताम् एवम् ब्रुवतीम् ताराम् ताराधिप निभ आननाम् |
वाली निर्भर्त्सयामास वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
While Tara with a face that shines like the lord of stars is speaking thus, Vali dauntingly spoke to 
her with these words.

shloka:
गर्जतो अस्य च सुसंरब्धम् भ्रातुः शत्रोर् विशेषतः |
मर्षयिष्यामि केन कारणेन वरानने
translation:
"He is an younger brother and an adversary in particular, oh, pretty-faced Tara, can I by any reason 
tolerate him when he kept raving on frenetically, tell me.

shloka:
अधर्षितानाम् शूराणाम् समरेषु अनिवर्तिनाम् |
धर्षणाम् अर्षणम् भीरु मरणात् अतिरिच्यते
translation:
"To those valiant ones who neither give ground nor get assailed in wars, oh, shyly, endurance of a overweening 
war-whoop is more than death.

shloka:
सोढुम् न च समर्थो अहम् युद्ध कामस्य संयुगे |
सुग्रीवस्य च संरंभम् हीन ग्रीवस्य गर्जतम्
translation: "I am incapable of withstanding that dumbly Sugreeva's bawling commotion desiring a brawling duel.

shloka:
न च कार्यो विषादः ते राघवम् प्रति मत् कृते |
धर्मज्ञः च कृतज्ञः च कथम् पापम् करिष्यति
translation:
"Also, you need not bother about Raghava's doing some harm to me, as I wonder how a diligent man and 
knower of virtue can commit sin.

shloka:
निवर्तस्व सह स्त्रीभिः कथम् भूयो अनुगच्छसि |
सौहृदम् दर्शितम् तावत् मयि भक्तिः त्वया कृता
translation:
"How do you follow me again, you return with all these females, truly you have expressed your friendliness 
owing to your devotion to me.

shloka:
प्रति योत्स्यामि अहम् गत्वा सुग्रीवम् जहि संभ्रमम् |
दर्पम् च अस्य विनेष्यामि न च प्राणैर् वियोक्ष्यते
translation:
"You may do away with your perplexity as I will retaliate Sugreeva on my going there only to drive him 
and his arrogance out, but without letting his lives loose.

shloka:
अहम् हि अजि स्थितस्य अस्य करिष्यामि यत् ईप्सितम् |
वृक्षैः मुष्टि प्रहारैः च पीडितः प्रति यास्यति
translation:
"As he is firmed up for a combat, I will indeed have to effectuate what his desire is, by caning with 
trees and fistfights, by which roughed up he returns.

shloka:
न मे गर्वितम् आयस्तम् सहिष्यति दुरात्मवान् |
कृतम् तारे सहायत्वम् दर्शितम् सौहृदम् मयि
translation:
"My nerve and pace of combat will be insufferable to that malign minded Sugreeva, oh, Tara, you have 
offered your helping suggestion and you have shown all your friendliness to me, it is enough.

shloka:
शापिता असि मम प्राणैः निवर्तस्व जनेन च |
अलम् जित्वा निवर्तिष्ये तम् अहम् भ्रातरम् रणे
translation:
"I adjured you on my lives, return with your followers, and I shall return to you on easily defeating 
and returning that 'brother of mine." Said Vali to Tara.

shloka:
तम् तु तारा परिष्वज्य वालिनम् प्रिय वादिनी |
चकार रुदती मन्दम् दक्षिणा सा प्रदक्षिणम्
translation:
She that pleasant articulator and talented Tara then hugged and circumabulated Vali, suppressing her 
moaning, as an honour to the braver.

shloka:
ततः स्वस्त्ययनम् कृत्वा मंत्रवित् विजय एषिणी |
अंतःपुरम् सह स्त्रीभिः प्रविष्टा शोक मोहिता
translation:
Then she who is a hymnodist that Tara has performed a hymnal bon voyage wishing triumph to Vali, and 
entered palace chambers along with other females, disoriented by her own sadness.

shloka:
प्रविष्टायाम् तु तारायाम् सह स्त्रीभिः स्वम् आलयम् |
नगर्या निर्ययौ क्रुद्धो महा सर्प इव श्वसन्
translation:
On Tara entering her own palace chambers along with other females, Vali emerged out of the city hissing 
like an infuriated great snake.

shloka:
स निःश्वस्य महारोषो वाली परम वेगवान् |
सर्वतः चारयन् दृष्टिम् शत्रु दर्शन कांक्षया
translation:
He that highly rancorous Vali suspired with high audacity and spread his sight everywhere intending 
to sight his enemy.

shloka:
स ददर्श ततः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवम् हेम पिङ्गलम् |
सुसंवीतम् अवष्टब्धम् दीप्यमानम् इव अनलम्
translation:
Then that celebrated Vali saw Sugreeva who is in golden-ochre hue, whose girdle cloth is tightened for 
a fight, and who is with an air of self-confidence, blazing like fiery-fire.

shloka:
तम् स दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुः सुग्रीवम् पर्यवस्थितम् |
गाढम् परिदधे वासो वाली परम कोपिनः
translation:
That strong armed Vali who is highly provoked has also tightened his girdle cloth on seeing proximately 
available Sugreeva.

shloka:
स वाली गाढ संवीतो मुष्टिम् उद्यम्य वीर्यवान् |
सुग्रीवम् एव अभिमुखो ययौ योद्धुम् कृत क्षणः
translation:
He that formidable Vali strongly tightening his girdle-cloth too, and proceeded towards Sugreeva in 
a well timed manner uplifting fists to fight him off.

shloka:
श्लिष्टम् मुष्टिम् समुद्यम्य संरब्धतरम् आगतः |
सुग्रीवो अपि समुद्दिश्य वालिनम् हेम मालिनम्
translation:
Even Sugreeva has come at that imprudent Vali with golden pendant, on tightening his fists, lifting 
them up at the ready, and aiming them well at Vali.

shloka:
तम् वाली क्रोध ताम्राक्षः सुग्रीवम् रण कोविदम् |
आपतंतम् महा वेगम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Vali spoke this word to that Sugreeva who is swooping down on him, whose eyes are reddened in fury, 
and who is an expert and expeditious in fighting.

shloka:
एष मुष्टिर् महान् बद्धो गाढः सुनियत अंगुलिः |
मया वेग विमुक्तः ते प्राणान् आदाय यास्यति
translation:
"Properly clenching fingers this great fist of mine is firmly clenched, and it will unclench only on 
taking your lives when I pitch this on you at full speed." So said Vali threateningly to Sugreeva.

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सुग्रीवः क्रुद्धो वालिनम् अब्रवीत् |
तव च एष हरन् प्राणान् मुष्टिः पततु मूर्धनि
translation:
Thus said, Sugreeva with high dudgeon said, "this fist of mine shall fall on your forehead plundering 
your lives."

shloka:
ताडितः तेन तम् क्रुद्धः समभिक्रम्य वेगतः |
अभवत् शोणित उद्गारी सापीड इव पर्वतः
translation:
Coming near instantaneously Vali hit him, whereby Sugreeva is enraged and became like a mountain streaming 
blood in its torrents.

shloka:
सुग्रीवेण तु निःशंकम् सालम् उत्पाट्य तेजसा |
गात्रेषु अभिहतो वाली वज्रेण इव महा गिरिः
translation:
But Sugreeva unhesitatingly uprooted a saala tree with his force and thrashed the limbs of Vali as with 
the thunderbolt thrashing a great mountain.

shloka:
स तु वृक्षेण निर्भग्नः साल ताडन विह्वलः |
गुरु भार भर आक्रान्ता नौः ससार्था इव सागरे
translation:
But Vali when thwacked with saala tree had staggered and looked like a tossing ship in an ocean filled 
with heavy weight of merchandise and brimming with merchants, but on the brink of wrecking.

shloka:
तौ भीम बल विक्रान्तौ सुपर्ण सम वेगिनौ |
प्रयुद्धौ घोर वपुषौ चन्द्र सूर्यौ इव अंबरे
translation:
Those two, Vali and Sugreeva, with their sensational energy, triumphing zeal, frightful physiques, swiftness 
as good as the Divine Eagle Garuda, vigilance in exploring perilous body parts of one another, ravagement 
of their own enemies fought frighteningly, like the sun and moon in the sky, which is inconceivable. 
[4-16-25, 26a]

shloka: ततो अवर्धत वाली तु बल वीर्य समन्वितः
translation:
But Vali being the possessor of might and vigour progressed and though greatly mighty is son of sun, 
Sugreeva, regressed. [4-16-26b, 27a]

shloka: वालिना भग्न दर्पः तु सुग्रीवो मन्द विक्रमः
translation:
Sugreeva became retardant in aggression when Vali routed his pride and then he exasperatedly started 
searching for Raghava to counteract Vali.

shloka: वृक्षैः स शाखैः शिखरैः वज्र कोटि निभैः नखैः
translation:
Among those two there happened a deadly fight time and again using trees with branches, peaks of mountains, 
their own nails that are similar to the razor-sharp edges of thunderbolts, and with fists, knees, feet, 
and arms, like the fight that once chanced between demon Vritra and Indra. [4-16-28b, 29]

shloka:
तौ शोणितात्कौ युध्येताम् वानारौ वन् चारिणौ |
मेघौ इव महा शब्दैः तर्जमानौ परस्परम्
translation:
Those forest moving vanara-s that are soaked in blood have gone on clashing, threatening each other, 
like two clouds clashing uproariously.

shloka:
हीयमानम् अथ अपश्यत् सुग्रीवम् वानरेश्वरम् |
प्रेक्षमाणम् दिशः च एव राघवः स मुहुर् मुहुर्
translation:
Raghava has then seen the lord of monkeys Sugreeva who is repeatedly eyeing all sides for help and who 
is even deteriorating in his enterprise.

shloka:
ततो रामो महातेजा आर्तम् दृष्ट्वा हरीश्वरम् |
स शरम् वीक्षते वीरो वालिनो वध कांक्षया
translation:
On seeing the lord of monkeys Sugreeva in a forlornness, then the refulgent and fearless Rama scanned 
for an arrow aiming to eliminate Vali.

shloka:
ततो धनुषि संधाय शरम् आशी विष उपमम् |
पूरयामास तत् चापम् काल चक्रम् इव अन्तकः
translation:
Then on tautening a venomous serpent like arrow in the bow, Rama started to draw out bowstring, whereby 
that bow attained a similitude with the Time-disc of the Terminator.

shloka:
तस्य ज्यातल घोषेण त्रस्ताः पत्ररथेश्वराः |
प्रदुद्रुवुर् मृगाः च एव युगांत इव मोहिताः
translation:
At the blast of bowstring the lordly birds and animals are panicked, like those that will be startled 
by the approach of ear ending, and they all fled.

shloka:
मुक्तस्तु वज्र निर्घोषः प्रदीप्त अशनि संनिभः |
राघवेण महा बाणो वालि वक्षसि पातितः
translation:
The arrow released by Raghava that has the boom of thunderbolt's thunderclap and the flashes of a lightning 
fell on the chest of Vali.

shloka:
ततः तेन महातेजा वीर्य युक्तः कपीश्वरः |
वेगेन अभिहतो वाली निपपात मही तले
translation:
Hit by the fleetness of that arrow then that highly magnificent and intrepid lord of monkeys Vali fell 
onto the plane of earth.

shloka:
इन्द्र ध्वज इव उद्धूत पौर्ण मास्याम् महीतले |
अश्वयुक् समये मासि गत सत्त्वो विचेतनः |
बाष्प संरुद्ध 
कण्ठस्तु वाली च आर्त स्वरः शनैः
translation:
Like the flag that will be raised in honour of Indra during the month of ashvin on a full-moon day, 
but thrown onto earth along with its flagstaff after the festival, Vali with depleted energy and dissipated 
vitality slowly fell onto ground, and with tears blocking throat he moaned piteously.

shloka:
नरोत्तमः काल युगांतकोपमम् शरोत्तमम् कांचन रूप्यभूषितम् |
ससर्ज दीप्तम् तम् अमित्र मर्दनम् स धूममग्निम् 
मुखतो यथा हरः
translation:
That best one among men Rama released a blazing and enemy subjugating arrow which in simile is like 
an Epoch-ender at the end of era, and that best arrow decorated in gold and silver looked like the glance 
from the Third-Eye of Rudra, emitting fire with smoke.

shloka:
अथ उक्षितः शोणित तोय विस्रवैः
सुपुष्पित अशोक इव अचलोद्गतः |
विचेतनो वासव सूनुर् आहवे
प्रभ्रञ्शित 
इन्द्र ध्वजवत् क्षितिम् गतः
translation:
That Indra's son Vali, dampened with blood and sweat, then looked like just felled Ashoka tree which 
has stemmed up and so far standing high on a mountain with fully bloomed clusters of its blood-red flowers, 
and when his anima is undone he even looked like the flagstaff on which a flag is raised in honour of 
Indra, but which is altogether dislodged and abandoned on the ground.

shloka:
ततः शरेण अभिहतो रामेण रण कर्कशः |
पपात सहसा वाली निकृत्तैव पादपः
translation: When Rama's arrow hit him then Vali, the scourger in war, suddenly fell down like a hewed down tree.

shloka:
स भूमौ न्यस्त सर्वांगः तप्त कांचन भूषणः |
अपतत् देव राजस्य मुक्त रश्मिर् इव ध्वजः
translation:
He who glittered with pure golden ornaments, that Vali fell down on earth while all of his limbs sank 
to dust, like the flag of Indra when released from its ropes.

shloka:
अस्मिन् निपतिते भूमौ हरि ऋषाणाम् गणेश्वरे |
नष्ट चन्द्रम् इव व्योम न व्यराजत मेदिनी
translation:
On the fall of that lord of hosts of monkeys and bears onto earth, unilluminated is the earth like the 
welkin that has forsooth lost its moon.

shloka:
भूमौ निपतितस्य अपि तस्य देहम् महात्मनः |
न श्रीर् जहाति न प्राणा न तेजो न पराक्रमः
translation:
Though that great souled Vali fell onto earth, neither his brilliance, nor lives, nor resplendence, 
nor his bravery are unfettering from his body.

shloka:
शक्र दत्ता वरा माला कान्चनी रत्न भूषिता |
दधार हरि मुख्यस्य प्राणान् तेजः श्रियम् च सा
translation:
That superb and gem-studded golden pendent given by Indra sustained that monkey chief's lives, resplendence 
and brilliance.

shloka:
स तया मालया वीरो हैमया हरियूथपः |
संध्यानुगत पर्यन्तः पयोधर इव अभवत्
translation:
By still wearing that golden chest-pendant around his neck, that brave general of monkeys Vali appeared 
like a black-cloud smeared with the colour of golden sunset all around its edges.

shloka:
तस्य माला च देहः च मर्मघाती च यः शरः |
त्रिधा इव रचिता लक्ष्मीः पतितस्य अपि शोभते
translation:
Even though Vali has fallen on ground his splendour is as though refulgent devising itself into three 
aspects, namely by his body, chest-pendant, and the arrow of Rama, which arrow is given to strike the 
crucial body parts alone, and which is still stuck in Vali's chest.

shloka:
तत् अस्त्रम् तस्य वीरस्य स्वर्ग मार्ग प्रभावनम् |
राम बाणासन क्षिप्तम् आवहत् परमाम् गतिम्
translation:
That arrow which effectuates the pathway to heaven, now discharged from the bow of Rama has brought 
forth that redemption to brave Vali .

shloka:
तम् तथा पतितम् संख्ये गत अर्चिषम् इव अनलम् |
ययातिम् इव पुण्यान्ते देव लोकात् परिच्युतम्
translation:
Then on seeing him who has fallen in war, the one with golden pendant, enormously chested, mightily 
armed, face golden, eye greenish, but who is like a fire extinct of its flame; who is like Indra in 
unassailability and like Upendra in indomitability; and who like Yayaati who has fallen from heaven, 
as well like the sun who falls onto earth from solar orbit when Time-ender flings him at the end of 
era; such as he is, on seeing that son of Indra, who forsooth has fallen, Rama neared him followed by 
Lakshmana. [4-17-9, 10, 11, 12a]

shloka: तम् तथा पतितम् वीरम् गत अर्चिष्मतम् इव अनलम्
translation:
On seeing the brave Vali fallen like that, who by now is like fire with extinguished tongues of flames, 
and who is seeing droopily, those two valiant brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, neared him with due honour. 
[4-17-12b, 13]

shloka:
तम् दृष्ट्वा राघवम् वाली लक्ष्मणम् च महाबलम् |
अब्रवीत् परुषम् वाक्यम् प्रश्रितम् धर्म संहितम्
translation:
On seeing Rama and the great mighty Lakshmana as well, he who fell to ground flatly hurt by arrow, and 
whose energy and lives are trifling and vigour trivialised thereby, that Vali spoke these sarcastic 
words in his proper pride to Rama, who is taking pride in this conflict as a victor, which words at 
the same time have meaning, politeness, and self-righteousness. [4-17-14, 15]

shloka:
त्वम् नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रथितः प्रिय दर्शनः |
पराङ्मुख वधम् कृत्वा को अत्र प्राप्तः त्वया गुणः |
यदहम् युद्ध सम्रब्धः त्वत् कृते निधनम् गतः
translation:
"You are a renowned prince with pleasing looks.. but, which kind of death I am getting now, that too 
when I was in the commotion of conflict with another, alas, that ignoble death is owing to you, and 
what merit is achieved by you in this undertaking of yours to kill someone who is facing away from you...

shloka:
कुलीनः सत्त्व संपन्नः तेजस्वी चरितव्रतः |
रामः करुणवेदी च प्रजानाम् च हितेरतः
translation:
"Rama is high-born, they say, gifted with mightiness, resplendent, pursuer of vows, mindful of mercy, 
delighter in people's welfare, sympathetic, greatly enthusiastic and assertively committed in doing 
good deeds, knower of time-and-action, all these living-beings on earth are thus relating your renown, 
aren't they. [4-17-17, 18]

shloka:
दमः शमः क्षमा धर्मो धृति सत्यम् पराक्रमः |
पर्थिवानाम् गुणा राजन् दण्डः च अपकारिषु
translation:
"To be able to control senses and will, forgiveness, conscientiousness, resoluteness, truthfulness, 
and adventurousness, oh, king, are the aptitudes of a king, and even punishing the wrongdoers, too.

shloka:
तान् गुणान् संप्रधार्य अहम् अग्र्यम् च अभिजनम् तव |
तारया प्रतिषिद्धो अपि सुग्रीवेण समागतः
translation:
"Concluding that those kingly characteristics will be obtainable in you, and even judging by the noble 
dynasty of yours, I have confronted Sugreeva though Tara dissuaded me.

shloka:
न माम् अन्येन संरब्धम् प्रमत्तम् वेद्धुम् अर्हसि |
इति मे बुद्धिर् उत्पन्ना बभूव अदर्शने तव
translation:
"When you have not appeared before me when I confronted Sugreeva my concept was, 'it will be inapt of 
Rama to hurt me while I am combating with another combatant, besides, when I will be unvigilant in that 
fight...'

shloka:
न त्वाम् विनिहत आत्मानम् धर्म ध्वजम् अधार्मिकम् |
जाने पाप समाचारम् तृणैः कूपम् इव आवृतम्
translation:
"Not known that your soul is put to death, not known that you are the unrighteous flag bearer of righteousness, 
to me not known that you are insidious like straw covered well.

shloka:
सताम् वेष धरम् पापम् प्रच्छन्नम् इव पावकम् |
न अहम् त्वाम् अभिजानामि धर्म छद्माभि संवृतम्
translation:
"I have no knowledge that you are a sinner, one in the garb of a benign soul, and explicitly mantled 
under the garb of probity like ash covered fire.

shloka:
विषये वा पुरे वा ते यदा पापम् करोमि अहम् |
न च त्वाम् अवजाने अहं कस्मात् त्वम् हंसि अकिल्बिषम्
translation:
"I am non-guilty as I have not committed any misdeed either in your country or in your city, nor I have 
taunted you; I am a vanara subsisting on fruits and tubers and always moving in forests alone; such 
as I am, what made you to torture me when I was not combating with you en face, furthermore, when I 
was involved with another? [4-17-24, 25]

shloka:
त्वम् नराधिपतेः पुत्रः प्रतीतः प्रियदर्शनः |
लिन्गम् अपि अस्ति ते राजन् दृश्यते धर्म सम्हितम्
translation:
"You are renowned to be a prince with charming looks, oh, king, and indications agreeable to rectitude 
are also appearing on your body.

shloka:
कः क्षत्रिय कुलेजातः श्रुतवान् नष्टसंशयः |
धर्म लिंग प्रतिच्छन्नः क्रूरम् कर्म समाचरेत्
translation:
"Will anybody born in Kshatriya's family, a learned one in Veda-s, thereby who is rid of ambiguities 
with respect to right and wrong, and who is cloaked in an air of probity, execute such a ruthless deed 
like this?

shloka:
राम राघव कुले जातो धर्मवान् इति विश्रुतः |
अभव्यो भव्य रूपेण किम् अर्थम् परिधावसे
translation:
"Though born in Raghava's dynasty and renowned as a moralist you are actually amoral, and for what purpose 
you run around with this moral aspect?

shloka:
साम दानम् क्षमा धर्मः सत्यम् धृति पराक्रमौ |
पार्थिवानाम् गुणा राजन् दण्डः च अपि अपकारिषु
translation:
"Influencing, largesse, forbearance, probity, candour, and conquering are the attributes of the kings, 
oh, king, and even punishing the wrongdoers.

shloka:
वयम् वनचरा राम मृगा मूल फल अशनाः |
एषा प्रकृतिर् अस्माकम् पुरुषः त्वम् नरेश्वरः
translation:
"We as animals live in forests while you are city dwellers, we live by eating fruits and tubers while 
you enjoy feasts and banquets, our nature is such to kill and get killed, thus you and me have no correlation. 
And you, even if you are a man and a prince for humans, you resorted to this animalistic way of killing 
me lying in the wait, thus your action is worse than that of an animal, if not subhuman or un-princely.

shloka:
भूमिर् हिरण्यम् रूपम् च निग्रहे कारणानि च |
तत्र कः ते वने लोभो मदीयेषु फलेषु वा
translation:
"Territory, gold, and silver will be the causes while counteracting somebody, in that case, by what 
you are decoyed into these forests of mine or in the fruits of mine.

shloka:
नयः च विनयः च उभौ निग्रह अनुग्रहौ अपि |
राज वृत्तिर् असंकीर्णा न नृपाः काम वृत्तयः
translation:
"In the pairs of propriety and compliance, punishment and pardoning, no admixture is exercised in kingcraft, 
for the kings do not conduct themselves volitionally.

shloka:
त्वम् तु काम प्रधानः च कोपनः च अनवस्थितः |
राज वृत्तेषु संकीर्णः शरासन परायणः
translation:
"But, to you your self-interests are primary, and you are a wrathful, capricious, contriver of kingcraft, 
and an impetuous shooting-happy archer.

shloka:
न ते अस्ति अपचितिः धर्मे न अर्थे बुद्धिर् अवस्थिता |
इन्द्रियैः काम वृत्तः सन् कृष्यसे मनुजेश्वर
translation:
"Oh, king, you have no devotion to probity, nor your mind is firm about material gains, but as a free-willed 
one you are distracted by senses.

shloka:
हत्वा बाणेन काकुत्स्थ माम् इह अनपराधिनम् |
किम् वक्ष्यसि सताम् मध्ये कर्म कृत्वा जुगुप्सितम्
translation:
"How you are answerable to gentlemen, Rama, when you have done this detestable deed of killing an unoffending 
one like me with your arrow?

shloka:
राजहा ब्रह्महा गोघ्नः चोरः प्राणिवधे रतः |
नास्तिकः परिवेत्ता च सर्वे निरय गामिनः
translation:
"A regicide, a Brahman-cide, a cow-slayer, a thief, an inveterate killer, an atheist, and an younger 
brother who marries before his elder, all of them will go to hell.

shloka:
सूचकः च कदर्यः च मित्र्घ्नो गुरुतल्पगः |
लोकं पापात्मानम् एते गच्छन्ते न अत्र संशयः
translation:
"A slander-monger, skinflint, friend-killer and one who makes love with his teacher's wife, they all 
go to the worlds of evil-souls, no doubt about it.

shloka:
अधार्यम् चर्म मे सद्भी रोमाणि अस्थि च वर्जितम् |
अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि त्वत् विधैः धर्मचारिभिः
translation:
"My skin is unwearable, holy people forbid my hair and bones, and uneatable is my meat for your kind 
of reputable people.

shloka:
पंच पंच नखा भक्ष्या ब्रह्म क्षत्रेण राघव |
शल्यकः श्वाविधो गोधा शशः कूर्मः च पंचमः
translation:
"Raghava, five kinds of five-nailed animals, viz., a kind of wild rodent, a kind of wild-boar, a kind 
of lizard, a hare and fifthly the turtle are edible for Brahmans and Kshatriya-s.

shloka:
चर्म च अस्थि च मे राजन् न स्पृशन्ति मनीषिणः |
अभक्ष्याणि च मांसानि सो अहम् पंच नखो हतः
translation:
"Sensible people will not touch my skin and bones, oh, king, nor meats from my body are to be eaten, 
such as I am, a five-nailed animal, I am killed.

shloka:
तारया वाक्यम् उक्तो अहम् सत्यम् सर्वज्ञया हितम् |
तद् अतिक्रम्य मोहेन कालस्य वशम् आगतः
translation:
"Though Tara appraised me with truthful and favourable words, I just disregarded her advise owing to 
my own delusion, and gone into the control of Time.

shloka:
त्वया नाथेन काकुत्स्थ न सनाथा वसुंधरा |
प्रमदा शील संपूर्णा पति एव च विधर्मिणा
translation:
"With you as her espouser the Earth is not with a correct spouse, as with any lady who is with full-fledged 
chastity, but with a husband who is without rectitude.

shloka:
शठो नैकृतिकः क्षुद्रो मिथ्या प्रश्रित मानसः |
कथम् दशरथेन त्वम् जातः पापो महात्मना
translation:
"How are you borne to that great-souled Dasharatha when you are artful, felonious, knavish, disposed 
to a false modesty subconsciously, and an evildoer?

shloka:
छिन्न चारित्र्य कक्ष्येण सताम् धर्म अतिवर्तिना |
त्यक्त धर्म अंकुशेन अहम् निहतो राम हस्तिना
translation:
"I am killed by an elephant called Rama that snapped off its girdle-cord called tradition, that infringed 
the conventions of righteous people, and that discarded the goad called virtue.

shloka:
अशुभम् च अपि अयुक्तम् च सताम् च एव विगर्हितम् |
वक्ष्यसे च ईदृशम् कृत्वा सद्भिः सह समागतः
translation:
"On accomplishing this sort of unpropitious, unjustified killing, which is condemned by the righteous 
people, what can you say when you meet the godly men?

shloka:
उदासीनेषु यो अस्मासु विक्रमो अयम् प्रकाशितः |
अपकारिषु ते राम न एवम् पश्यामि विक्रमम्
translation:
"The valour that which is displayed on the unprejudiced few like us, oh, Rama, I do not see that sort 
of valour is shown by you in respect of your enemies.

shloka:
दृश्यमानः तु युध्येथा मया युधि नृपात्मज |
अद्य वैवस्वतम् देवम् पश्येः त्वम् निहतो मया
translation:
"Had you been in combat with me en face oh, prince, you would have been killed by me and by now you 
would have seen the death-god Yama.

shloka:
त्वया अदृश्येन तु रणे निहतो अहम् दुरासदः |
प्रसुप्तः पन्नगेन इव नरः पाप वशम् गतः
translation:
"An unassailable one, such as I am, I am killed by you while you remained invisible on the field of 
fight, as with a sinner bitten by a snake while he is asleep.

shloka:
सुग्रीव प्रिय कामेन यद् अहम् निहतः त्वया |
माम् एव यदि पूर्वम् त्वम् एतद् अर्थम् अचोदयः |
मैथिलिम् 
अहम् एक आह्ना तव च आनीतवान् भवेः
translation:
"For which purpose I am killed, intending to do good to Sugreeva is incidental to it, you should have 
assigned me for that purpose in the first instance itself, and I would have brought that evil-minded 
demon Ravana, the abductor of your wife in one day, that too without killing him in any fight, but by 
fastening him by neck, and I would have presented Maithili to you. [3-17-49, 50]

shloka:
न्यस्ताम् सागर तोये वा पाताले वा अपि मैथिलीम् |
आनयेयम् तव आदेशात् श्वेताम् अश्वतरीम् इव
translation:
"I would have brought Maithili at your order even if she is lodged in oceanic waters or in nether worlds, 
as with the White Horse of Vedic lore.

shloka:
युक्तम् यत् प्रप्नुयात् राज्यम् सुग्रीवः स्वर् गते मयि |
अयुक्तम् यद् अधर्मेण त्वया अहम् निहतो रणे
translation:
"The fact of Sugreeva's getting the kingdom after my going to heaven is proper, but the fact of your 
killing me in war, unrighteously, is improper.

shloka:
कामम् एवम् विधम् लोकः कालेन विनियुज्यते |
क्षमम् चेत् भवता प्राप्तम् उत्तरम् साधु चिंत्यताम्
translation:
"Admittedly the world is this way, and if possible a relevant reply may gently be thought ofabout your 
propriety in killing me..." So said Vali to Rama.

shloka:
इति एवम् उक्त्वा परिशुष्क वक्त्रः
शर अभिघातात् व्यथितो महात्मा |
समीक्ष्य रामम् रवि संनिकाशम्
तूष्णीम् बभौ वानर राज सूनुः
translation:
That great-souled son of a vanara king Vali, whom the arrow impaled and agonised, on keenly seeing Rama 
whose resplendence equals the brightness of the sun, said that much and remained silent when his mouth 
has dried up.

shloka:
इति उक्तः प्रश्रितम् वाक्यम् धर्म अर्थ सहितम् हितम् |
परुषम् वालिना रामो निहतेन विचेतसा
translation:
Thus, Vali who is hit down by arrow and who is collapsing humbly spoke exacting words that contained 
probity, meaningfulness, and expedience, to Rama.

shloka:
तम् निष्प्रभम् इव आदित्यम् मुक्त तोयम् इव अंबुदम् |
उक्त वाक्यम् हरि श्रेष्ठम् उपशांतम् इव अनलम्
translation:
Then to him who is rendered like a lusterless sun, fizzling out like a cloud that released its water, 
and who became like a quenched fire, to such a best monkey and an unexcelled lord of monkeys who has 
just now imputed Rama with words that are abounding with righteousness and meaningfulness, Rama spoke 
subsequently. [4-18-3, 4]

shloka:
धर्मम् अर्थम् च कामम् च समयम् च अपि लौकिकम् |
अविज्ञाय कथम् बाल्यात् माम् इह अद्य विगर्हसे
translation:
"Uncaring for probity, prosperity, pleasure deriving, and even for the social conventions, now how do 
you rebuke me childishly in this matter?

shloka:
अपृष्ट्वा बुद्धि संपन्नान् वृद्धान् आचार्य संमतान् |
सौम्य वानर चापल्यात् त्वम् माम् वक्तुम् इह इच्छसि
translation:
"Unconsulted are the doyens of your race that are intellectually well off and agreeable to your mentors 
about rights and wrongs about your deeds, oh, gentle one, how do you wish to debate with me in this 
matter with your primate's caprice.

shloka:
इक्ष्वाकूणाम् इयम् भूमिः स शैल वन कानना |
मृग पक्षि मनुष्याणाम् निग्रह अनुग्रहेषु अपि
translation:
"This earth with its mountains, woods, and forests, even along with the authority to condone or condemn 
the animals, birds, and humans on it belongs to Ikshvaku-s.

shloka:
ताम् पालयति धर्मात्मा भरतः सत्यवान् ऋजुः |
धर्म काम अर्थ तत्त्वज्ञो निग्रह अनुग्रहे रतः
translation:
"He who is virtue-souled, truth-abiding, plain-speaking, and the knower of the import of probity, pleasures, 
and prosperity, and the one who is concerned in controlling or condoning his subjects, that Bharata 
is the ruler of earth.

shloka:
नयः च विनयः च उभौ यस्मिन् सत्यम् च सुस्थितम् |
विक्रमः च यथा दृष्टः स राजा देश कालवित्
translation:
"In whom both scrupulousness and benignancy are there, truthfulness is firmed up, and valour as evinced 
by scriptures is evident, and he who is the knower of time and place is the king, namely Bharata.

shloka:
तस्य धर्म कृत आदेशा वयम् अन्ये च पार्थिवः |
चरामो वसुधाम् कृत्स्नाम् धर्म संतानम् इच्छवः
translation:
"Holding his virtuous decree desiring to keep up the continuum of righteousness, we and some other kings 
are wayfaring this earth in its entirety.

shloka:
तस्मिन् नृपति शार्दूल भरते धर्म वत्सले |
पालयति अखिलाम् पृथ्वीम् कः चरेत् धर्म विप्रियम्
translation:
"While that Bharata, the kingly-tiger and a patron of virtue, is ruling the earth in its entirety, who 
is there to conduct himself in an unacceptable way to morality on it?

shloka:
ते वयम् मार्ग विभ्रष्टम् स्वधर्मे परमे स्थिताः |
भरत आज्ञाम् पुरस्कृत्य निगृह्णीमो यथा विधि
translation:
"Abiding in our own pre-eminent righteousness, and even abiding by the order of Bharata we punish him 
who deviated from the path of morality, according to custom.

shloka:
त्वम् तु संक्लिष्ट धर्मः च कर्मणा च विगर्हितः |
काम तंत्र प्रधानः च न स्थितो राज वर्त्मनि
translation:
"As for you, you brought virtue to a state of decadence, rendered yourself reprovable by your own decadent 
behaviour, for carnality alone has become your primary doctrine, and thus you have not abided by the 
conduct meetly to a king.

shloka:
ज्येष्ठो भ्राता पिता चैव यः च विद्याम् प्रयच्छति |
त्रयः ते पितरो ज्ञेया धर्मे च पथि वर्तिनः
translation:
"It is to be known by him who treads the way of righteousness that he has three fatherly personages, 
namely his own father, his elder brother, and the one who accords education to him.

shloka:
यवीयान् आत्मनः पुत्रः शिष्यः च अपि गुणोदितः |
पुत्रवत् ते त्रयः चिंत्या धर्मः चैव अत्र कारणम्
translation:
"An younger brother, a son, and a disciple with good characteristics, these three are to be deemed as 
one's own sons, for such matters take base on rectitude alone.

shloka:
सूक्ष्मः परम दुर्ज्ञेयः सताम् धर्मः प्लवंगम |
हृदिस्थः सर्व भूतानाम् आत्मा वेद शुभाशुभम्
translation:
"The probity practised by principled people is very subtle and highly imponderable, and the soul that 
abides in the hearts of all beings alone can differentiate between just and unjust.

shloka:
चपलः चपलैः सार्धम् वानरैः अकृत आत्मभिः |
जात्यंध इव जात्यन्धैः मंत्रयन् द्रक्ष्यसे नु किम्
translation:
"Like a blind by birth counselling with similarly blind, you being a vacillant, on your counselling 
only with frantic minded vacillant monkeys, what can you really fathom about right and wrong?

shloka:
अहम् तु व्यक्तताम् अस्य वचनस्य ब्रवीमि ते |
न हि माम् केवलम् रोषात् त्वम् विगर्हितुम् अर्हसि
translation:
"I will clarify about the words I have said, but I tell you that it is indeed inapt of you to disdain 
me just out of your outrage.

shloka:
तत् एतत् कारणम् पश्य यत् अर्थम् त्वम् मया हतः |
भ्रातुर् वर्तसि भार्यायाम् त्यक्त्वा धर्मम् सनातनम्
translation:
"Realise this reason by which I have eliminated you... you misbehaved with your brother's wife, forsaking 
the perpetual tradition.

shloka:
अस्य त्वम् धरमाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
रुमायाम् वर्तसे कामात् स्नुषायाम् पाप कर्मकृत्
translation:
"While the great-souled Sugreeva is still alive, you with your habit of sinful acts have lustily misbehaved 
with Sugreeva's wife Ruma, who should be counted as your daughter-in-law.

shloka:
तद् व्यतीतस्य ते धर्मात् काम वृत्तस्य वानर |
भ्रातृ भार्या अभिमर्शे अस्मिन् दण्डो अयम् प्रतिपादितः
translation:
"Thereby, oh, vanara, this punishment is imposed on you, for your dissolute sinning in abusing your 
brother's wife, thereby for your transgression of tradition and virtue.

shloka:
न हि लोक विरुद्धस्य लोक वृत्तात् अपेयुषः |
दण्डात् अन्यत्र पश्यामि निग्रहम् हरि यूथप
translation:
"I foresee no other kind of control other than punishment to him who conducts himself contrary to the 
society and who is deviant of conventions.

shloka:
न च ते मर्षये पापम् क्ष्त्रियो अहम् कुलोद्गतः |
औरसीम् भगिनीम् वा अपि भार्याम् वा अपि अनुजस्य यः
translation:
"As a Kshatriya emerged from a best dynasty I do not tolerate your wrongdoing, and the punishment to 
the one who lustfully indulges with his daughter, or with his sister, or with the wife of his younger 
brother is his elimination, as recalled from scriptures. [4-18-22, 23a]

shloka: भरतः तु महीपालो वयम् तु आदेश वर्तिनः
translation:
While Bharata is the lord of land and we are his proxies adhering to his orders, and while you too have 
overstepped the bounds of rightness, then how is it possible to be lenient? [4-18-23b, 24a]

shloka: गुरु धर्म व्यतिक्रान्तम् प्राज्ञो धर्मेण पालयन्
translation:
"While ruling righteously sensible Bharata punishes him who oversteps the momentous virtue, and he is 
poised to put down lustful ones. [4-18-24b, 25a]

shloka:
वयम् तु भरत आदेशम् विधिम् कृत्वा हरीश्वर |
त्वत् विधान् भिन्न मर्यादान् निग्रहीतुम् व्यवस्थिताः
translation:
"As for us, oh, monkey's lord, we effectuate our brother's orders and our duty, and we stand for curbing 
your kind of shatterers of ethics. [4-18-25b, c]

shloka:
सुग्रीवेण च मे सख्यम् लक्ष्मणेन यथा तथा |
दार राज्य निमित्तम् च निःश्रेयसकरः स मे
translation:
"My association with Sugreeva is as good as that with Lakshmana, nevertheless it betided with an understanding 
to regain Sugreeva's wife and kingdom, and he will give succour to me.

shloka:
प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता तदा वानर संनिधौ |
प्रतिज्ञा च कथम् शक्या मत् विधेन अनवेक्षितुम्
translation:
"I gave a promise to Sugreeva at the time of befriending him in the presence of vanara-s, and how is 
it possible for my kind to dishonour a given promise?

shloka:
तत् एभिः कारणैः सर्वैर् महद्भिः धर्म संहितैः |
शासनम् तव यत् युक्तम् तत् भवान् अनुमन्यताम्
translation:
"Thereby you have to infer that a befitting punishment is given to you, owing to all these great reasons 
that abound with virtue and with supreme value.

shloka:
सर्वथा धर्म इति एव द्रष्टव्यः तव निग्रहः |
वयस्यस्य उपकर्तव्यम् धर्मम् एव अनुपश्यता
translation:
"Anywise, you have to regard the punishment given to you is legitimate, and he whom rectitude guides
