Then that monkey who is the son of Air-god and a selfsame of Air-god shinned up that
towering mountain Mahendra, as he is an enemy-subjugator about to subjugate the arch rival Ravana,
where that mountain is hedged in with diverse flowers, its pastures are the sweethearts of deer, it
is constrictive with diverse flowers of ever flowering, ever fruiting trees and with the flowers of
climbers as well, and where lions and tigers are freely moving and ruttish elephants love it, and
where the flights of birds are uproarious, and pent-up rapids are clangourous. [4-67-39, 40,
41]

shloka:
महद्भिः उच्छ्रितम् शृन्गैः महेन्द्रम् स महाबलः |
विचचार हरिश्रेष्ठो महेन्द्र साम विक्रमः
translation:
He who is equal in valour to the Paradisiacal Mahendra, that highly energetic and
grand monkey Hanuma ambled on loftiest and towery crags of such a mountain.

shloka:
बाहुभ्याम् पीडितः तेन महाशैलो महात्मना |
ररास सिंह अभिहतो महान् मत्त इव द्विपः
translation:
When squeezed by both the arms and hands of that high souled Hanuma, that lofty
mountain trumpeted, as if it is a lion-paw-hit brutish-elephantine-elephant.

shloka:
मुमोच सलिल उत्पीडान् विप्रकीर्ण शिलौच्चयः |
वित्रस्त मृग मातंगः प्रकंपित महा द्रुमः
translation:
Virtually and widely bestrewn are the heaps of boulders, essentially scared are all
the animals and elephants, and actually rocked are the gigantic trees, and its rapids and
waterfalls have spouted out of that mountain by the impact of foot-stepping of Hanuma.

shloka:
नानागंधर्वमिथुनैर्पानसंसर्गकर्कशैः |
उत्पतद्भिर्विहंगैश्चविद्याधरगणैरपि - यद्वा -
नाना गन्धर्व मिथुनैः पान संसर्ग कर्कशैः |
उत् पतद्भिः विहंगैः च विद्याधर गणैः अपि
translation:
Then, the numerous gandharva couples and the hoards of vidhyaadhara-s even, that are
indulged in drinking and inebriated on that mountain are forsaking those lofty cliffs of that
mountain, and even the birds are put to flight, spanking snakes are completely slouching, and
rising up and falling down are the stones of that mountaintops to each step of Hanuma, and thus
that colossal mountain is desolated. [4-67-45, 46]

shloka:
निःश्वसद्भिस्तदातैतुभुजगैरर्धनिःसृतैः |
सपताकैवाभातिसतदाधरणीधरः
translation:
With snakes popping up halfway through their snake-pits with their hoods swaying and
tongues hissing that earth-borne mountain Mahendra appeared to be a gleaming mountain with flying
flags.

shloka:
ऋषिभित्राससंभ्रान्तैस्त्यज्यमानश्शिलोच्चयः - यद्वा -
ऋषिभिः त्रास संभ्रांतैः त्यज्यमानः शिला उच्चयः |
सीदन् महति कांतारे सार्थ हीन इव अध्व गः
translation:
While the sages are forsaking that towering mountain as their own scare bewildering
them, that mountain appeared to be one who is desolated by his associates in the vast of a thick of
forest, as a wilting wayfarer.

shloka:
स वेगवान् वेग समाहित आत्मा
हरि प्रवीरः पर वीर हन्ता |
मनः समाधाय महाअनुभावो
जगाम लंकाम् मनसा मनस्वी
translation:
And he who is an importantly brave monkey among all the monkeys, an eliminator of
enemy stalwarts, that highly proficient, expeditious, and conscientious Hanuma, on stabilising his
impulses and making soul is quite staid in speediness, he made head away to Lanka, instinctually.

shloka:
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध
काण्डे सप्त षष्टितमः सर्गः
translation:
Thus, this is the 66th, and conclusive chapter
of Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

shloka:
ततो रावणनीतायाः सीतायाः शत्रुकर्शनः |
इयेष पदमन्वेष्टुं चारणाचरिते पथि
translation:
After that, Hanuma, the destroyer of foes, desired to travel in the sky where
celestials like chaaranas tread, to search for Seetha, who was taken away by Ravana.

shloka:
दुष्करं निष्प्रतिद्वन्द्वं चिकीर्षन् कर्म वानरः |
समुदग्रशिरोग्रीवो गवांपतिरिवाबभौ
translation:
Hanuma who desired to perform a deed done by no one else, shone like a bull without
any obstacles, with his stretched neck and raised head.

shloka:
अथ वैडूर्यवर्णेषु शाद्वलेषु महाबलः |
धीरः सलिलकल्पेषु विच्चार यथासुखम्
translation:
After that, the mighty and courageous Hanuma roamed at ease on the lawns with the
hue of an emerald, which looked like still water from a distance.

shloka:
द्विजान् वित्रासयन् धीमानुरसा पादपान् हरन् |
मृगांश्च सुबाहुन्निघ्नन् प्रवृद्ध इव केसरी
translation:
The thoughtful Hanuma tread like a rampant lion, making birds fear, uprooting trees
by his breast and also killing many animals.

shloka:
नीललोहितमाञ्जिष्ठपत्रवर्णैः सितासितैः |
स्वभावविहितैश्चित्रैर्धातुभिः समलंकृतम्
translation:
That great monkey Hanuma shone like an elephant in a lake, standing on the foot of
that great mountain by the name of Mahendra, where many elephants of good breed resided, which was
beautifully decorated with many naturally formed mineral rocks of varied hue like black, white,
red, blue, yellow and green and which was surrounded by godly serpents and Yakshas, Kinnaras,
Gandharvas who were capable of assuming desired form, together with their families.

shloka:
स सूर्याय महेन्द्राय पवनाय स्वयंभुवे |
भूतेभ्यश्चाञ्जलिं कृत्वा चकार गमने मतिम्
translation:
He saluted with joined palms to the Sun-God, Lord Indra, God of Wind, Lord Brahma
and Bhutas and decided to leave.

shloka:
अञ्जलिं प्राङ्मुखः कृत्वा पवनायात्मयोओनयो |
ततो हि ववृधे गन्तुं दक्षिणो दक्षिणां दिश्म्
translation:
Hanuma turned towards east, saluted his father, the Lord of Wind and increased his
body to go towards southern direction.

shloka:
प्लवङ्गप्रवरैर्दृष्टः प्लवने कृतनिश्चयः |
ववृधे रामवृद्ध्यर्थम् समुद्र इव पर्वसु
translation:
With all the Vaanaras seeing, Hanuma decided to fly and like an ocean swelling on
full moon days, grew for Rama's success.

shloka:
निष्प्रमाणशरीरः सन् लिलङ्घयिषुरर्णवम् |
बाहुभ्यां पीडयामास चरणाभ्यां च पर्वतम्
translation:
With a desire to cross the ocean, Hanuma grew his body immeasurably and pressed the
mountain with his feet and hands.

shloka:
स चचालाचलश्चापि मुहूर्तं कपिपीडितः |
तरूणां पुष्पिताग्राणां सर्वं पुष्पमशातयत्
translation:
Thus tormented by Hanuma, that mountain shook for an instant and showered all
flowers of trees on it.

shloka:
तेन पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पौघेन सुगन्धिना |
सर्वतः संवृतः शैलो बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा
translation:
Covered all through by those fragrant flowers which fell down from the trees, that
mountain shone like a mountain made of flowers.

shloka:
तेन चोत्तमवीर्येण पीड्यमानः स पर्वतः |
सलिलं संप्रसुस्राव मदं मत्त इव द्विपः
translation:
That mountain shed water like an elephant in rut emitting rut juice, after being
pressed by the mighty Hanuma.

shloka:
पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः |
रीतीर्निर्वर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः
translation:
Pressed by that mighty Hanuma, streaks of gold silver and antimony color appeared on
the Mahendra mountain.

shloka:
मुमोच च शिलाः शैलो विशालाः समनःशिलाः |
मध्यमेनार्चिषा जुष्टो धूमराजीरिवानलः
translation:
Huge Rocks of Sulfur were also shot forth from that mountain, just as a fire burning
with a medium flame would emit columns of smoke.

shloka:
गिरिणा पीड्यमानेन पीड्यमानानि सर्वशः |
गुहाविष्टानि भूतानि विनेदुर्विकृतैः स्वरैः
translation:
Being pressed on all sides by the mountain which itself was being pressed by Hanuma,
creatures living in the caves of that mountain shrieked in horrifying tones.

shloka:
स महासत्त्वसंनादः शैलपीडानिमित्तजः |
पृथिवीं पूरयामास दिशश्चोपवनानि च
translation:
That loud noise from creatures which emanated because of stress caused to the
mountain, filled the earth and all four directions and forests near that mountain.

shloka:
शिरोभिः पृथुभिः सर्पा व्यक्तस्वस्तिकलक्षणैः |
वमन्तः पावकं घोरं ददंशुर्दशनैः शिलाः
translation:
Great snakes with clear swastika signs on their hoods, spewed out frightening flames
with their great heads and bit the rocks with their teeth.

shloka:
तास्तदा सविषैर्दष्टाः कुपितैस्तैर्महाशिलाः|
जज्ज्वलुः पावकोद्दीप्ता बिभिदुश्च सहस्रधा
translation:
Then those great rocks bit by those snakes with anger and venom, burned due to the
flame and split into thousand pieces.

shloka:
यानि चौषधजालानि तस्मिन् जातानि पर्वते |
विषघ्नान्यपि नागानां न शेकुः शमितुं विषम्
translation:
Medicinal herbs from that mountain, although capable of destroying ordinary poisons,
could not neutralize the poison from those snakes.

shloka:
भिद्यतेऽयं गिरिर्भूतैरिति मत्त्वा तपस्विनः |
त्रस्ता विद्याधरास्तस्मादुत्पेतुः स्त्रीगणैः सह
translation:
Ascetics residing on that mountain flew away from there thinking that some demons
were destroying it. Vidhyadharas who lived there, became afraid and flew away with their women
folk, leaving behind them golden jugs of wine in the liquor house, gold vases, a varieties of
sauces that can be licked, eatables, various meats, skins of oxen and swords with golden hilts.

shloka:
कृतक्ण्ठगुणाः क्षीबा र्क्तमाल्यानुलेपनाः |
र्क्तक्षाः पुष्कराक्षाश्च गगनं प्रतिपेदिरे
translation:
The intoxicated Vidyadharas with garlands around their neck decked with red flower
garlands and smeared with sandal paste, with reddened eyes, and with lotus shaped eyes, obtained
the sky.

shloka:
हारनूपुरकेयूरपारिहार्यधराः स्त्रियः |
विस्मिताः सस्मितास्तस्थुराकाशे रमणैः सह
translation:
Vidyadhara women wearing necklaces, anklets, armlets and bangles stood in the sky
with surprise and with smiles along with their loved ones.

shloka:
दर्शयन्तो महाविद्यां विद्याधरमहर्षयः |
सहितास्तस्थुराकाशे वीक्षाञ्चक्रुश्च पर्वतम्
translation:
Vidyadharas and great sages stood in the sky in a group, showing their great prowess
and viewed the mountain.

shloka:
शुश्रुवुश्चतदा शब्दमृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्|
चारणानां च सिद्धानां स्थितानांविमलेऽम्बरे
translation:
Then they heard words of Charanas, Siddhas and pure hearted Rishis who were located
in that clear sky.

shloka:
एष पर्वतसंकाशो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः |
तितीर्षति महावेगः समुद्रं मकरालयम्
translation:
"This Hanuma, who is equal to a mountain, who is the son of Vayu, and who has great
speed, wants to cross the ocean which is abode to crocodiles."

shloka:
रामार्थं वानरार्थं च चिकीर्षन् कर्मदुष्करम् |
समुद्रस्य परं पारं दुष्प्रापं प्राप्तुमिच्छति
translation:
"Hanuma has decided to perform an impossible task for the sake of Rama and Vanaras
and wants to obtain the other side of ocean which is hard to obtain."

shloka:
इति विद्याधराः श्रुत्वा वचस्तेषां महात्मनाम् |
तमप्रमेयं ददृशुः पर्वते वानरर्षभम्
translation:
Vidyadharas thus listened to the words of those great people and looked at the
incomparable Hanuma, best among Vanaras, standing on the mountain.

shloka:
दुधुवे च स रोमाणि चकम्पे चाचलोपमः |
ननाद सुमहानादं सुमहानिव तोयदः
translation:
He, who is equal to a mountain, shook his hair, quivered his body and let out a
great roar like from a vast cloud.

shloka:
आनुपूर्व्येण वृत्तं च लाङ्गूलं लोमभिश्चितम् |
उत्पतिष्यन् विचिक्षेप पक्षिराज इवोरगम्
translation:
About to fly, Hanuma jolted his tail, which was rolled into a circle from top to
bottom, and which was covered with hair, just as Garuda, the king of birds would jolt a snake.

shloka:
तस्य लाङ्गूलमाविद्धमात्तवेगस्य पृष्ठतः |
ददृशे गरुडेनेव ह्रियमाणो महोरगः
translation:
Receiving his vigor, the tail curled at his back was seen like a great serpent being
stolen by Garuda.

shloka:
बाहू संस्तंभयामास महापरिघसंनिभौ |
ससाद च कपिः क्ट्यां चरणौ संचुकोच च
translation:
Hanuma firmly supported his arms (on the mountain surface) which resembled huge iron
clubs, crouched the waist and contracted his feet.

shloka:
संहृत्य च भुजौ श्रीमांस्तथैव च शिरोधराम् |
तेजः स्त्त्वं तथा वीर्यमाविवेश स वीर्यवान्
translation:
Bending shoulders and neck, that mighty and glorious Hanuma, increased his energy,
strength and courage.

shloka:
मार्गमालोकयन्दूरादूर्ध्वं प्रणिहितेक्षणः |
रुरोध हृदये प्राणानाकाशमवलोकयन्
translation:
With his eyes raised up, seeing the way from a distance, viewing the sky, he held
his breath in his heart.

shloka:
पद्भ्यां दृढमवस्थानं कृत्वा स कपिकुञ्जरः |
निकुञ्च्य कर्णौ हनुमानुत्पतिष्यन् महाबलः |
वानरान् वानरश्रेष्ठ इदं वचनमब्रवीत्
translation:
That mighty Hanuma, equal to an elephant among monkeys and the best among Vaanaraas,
stood firmly with his legs, bent his ears and before flying spoke these words to the Vaanaraas.

shloka:
यथा राघवनिर्मुक्तः शरः श्वसनविक्रमः |
गच्चेत्तद्वद्गमिष्यामि लङ्कां रावणपालिताम्
translation:
"I will go to the city of Lanka, ruled by Ravana just like an arrow released by Rama
will go, with wind-like speed. If I do not see the daughter of Janaka there, I will go with the
same speed to the abode of gods. If I do not see Seetha there in heaven, I will get Ravana the king
of raakshasaas tied up in chains without any effort. I will, in all events, return successfully
along with Seetha or I will get Lanka along with Ravana after uprooting it."

shloka: एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमान्वानरान्वानरोत्तमः
translation:
The best among Vaanaraas, Hanuma, spoke in this way to Vaanaraas and then without
thinking about anything else, flew up with lot of vigor. That great monkey also thought himself
equal to Garuda, the king of birds.

shloka:
समुत्पतति तस्मिंस्तु वेगात्ते नगरोहिणः |
संहृत्य विटपान् सर्वान् समुत्पेतुः समन्ततः
translation:
While he was flying up, due to that force, all trees on that mountain flew away in
all directions, drawing together all their branches.

shloka:
स मत्तकोयष्टिभकान् पादपान् पुष्पशालिनः |
उद्वहन्नूरुवेगेन जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे
translation:
While flying in the sky, he took along with him, because of the force of his thighs,
trees shining with flowers and with fattened lapwing birds.

shloka:
ऊरुवेगोत्थिता वृक्षा मुहूर्तं कपिमन्वयुः |
प्रस्थितं दीर्घमध्वानं स्वबन्धमिव बान्धवाः
translation:
The trees thus being held aloft by the speed of Hanuma's thighs, followed him for a
while just as relatives would follow their loved ones embarking on a long journey.

shloka:
तमूरुवेगोन्मथिताःसालाश्चन्ये नगोत्तमाः|
अनुजग्मुर्हनूमन्तं सैन्या इव महीपतिम्
translation:
Uprooted by the force of Hanuma's thighs, Sal and other excellent trees followed
Hanuma like soldiers following their king.

shloka:
सुपुष्पिताग्रैर्बहुभिः पादपैरन्वितः कपिः |
हनुमान् पर्वताकारो बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः
translation:
Hanuma the great monkey presented a wonderful sight, with his mountain-like
appearance together with the well flowered trees.

shloka:
सारवन्तोऽथ ये वृक्षा न्यमज्जन् लवणाम्भसि |
भयादिव महेन्द्रस्य पर्वता वरुणालये
translation:
After that, powerful trees sank into the salt ocean like mountains sinking into
ocean due to fear of Mahendra.

shloka:
स नानाकुसुमैः कीर्णः कपिः साङ्कुरकोरकैः |
शुशुभे मेघसंकाशः खद्योतैरिव पर्वतः
translation:
That Hanuma who was equal to a cloud, covered with flowers of various kinds, shoots
and buds, shone like a mountain with fireflies.

shloka:
विमुक्तास्तस्य वेगेन मुक्त्वा पुष्पाणि ते द्रुमाः |
अवशीर्यन्त सलिले निवृत्ताः सुहृदो यथा
translation:
Those trees which were released by Hanuma's speed, dropped flowers and fell down in
the water like friends going back after bidding farewell to their dear one.

shloka:
लघुत्वेनोपपन्नं तद्विचित्रं सागरेऽपतत् |
द्रुमाणां विविधं पुष्पं कपिवायुसमीरितम्
translation:
Set in motion by the wind from the movement of Hanuma, that variety of blossom, with
various hues, from the trees fell down into the sea. That great ocean shone like the sky filled
with stars.

shloka:
पुष्पौघेनानुबद्धेन नानावर्णेन वानरः |
बभौ मेघ इवाकाशे विद्युद्गणविभूषितः
translation:
Hanuma shone like a cloud in the sky decorated by lightening, with flowers of
various hues sticking to his body.

shloka: तस्य वेगसमाधूतैः पुष्पैस्तोयमदृश्यत
translation:
That sea water looked like the sky with delightful stars rising up, with flowers
flown up by Hanuma's speed.

shloka: तस्याम्बरगतौ बाहू ददृशाते प्रसारितौ
translation:
That sky-borne Hanuma's arms which were spread out, were seen like five-headed
serpents coming out of a mountain's peak.

shloka: पिबन्निव बभौ चापि सोओर्मिमालं महार्णवम्
translation:
That great monkey shone like one who is drinking the great sea together with its
waves. He also seemed like one who desires to drink the whole of sky.

shloka: तस्य विद्युत्प्रभाकारे वायुमार्गानुसारिणः
translation:
The eyes of that Hanuma, who was following the path of sky, which had a brilliance
equal to that of lightening, were shining like two fires on a mountain.

shloka: पिङ्गे पिङ्गाक्षमुख्यस्य बृहती परिमण्डले
translation:
The round, wide, reddish brown eyes of Hanuma, the best among the monkeys shone like
fully risen sun and moon.

shloka: मुखं नासिकया तस्य ताम्रया ताम्रमाबभौ
translation:
The ruddy face of Hanuma, with His reddish face shone like the Sun touched by
twilight.

shloka: लाङ्गूलं च समाविद्धं प्लवमानस्य शोभते
translation:
The tail of Hanuma, the son of Vayu floating in the sky, being risen up looked like
the pillar erected in honour of Indra.

shloka: लाङ्गूलचक्रेण महान् शुक्लदंष्ट्रोऽनिलात्मजः
translation:
The great intellectual Hanuma, with his great body, and with white teeth, shone like
the Sun, being surrounded by his circular tail.

shloka: स्फिग्देशेनाभिताम्रेण रराज स महाकपिः
translation:
That great monkey Hanuma, with his red colored buttocks, shone like a mountain with
a large deposit of red Gairika herb broken into pieces.

shloka: तस्य वानरसिंहस्य प्लवमानस्य सागरम्
translation:
Air passing through the lion among monkeys Hanuma's arm pits sounded like a
thundering cloud.

shloka: खे यथा निपतन्त्युल्का ह्युत्तरान्ताद्विनिःसृता
translation:
The best among monkeys Hanuma flying thus in the sky, looked like a meteor darting
away with great speed in the sky from northern direction.

shloka: पतत्पतङ्गसंकाशो व्यायतः शुशुभे कपिः
translation:
With a fast pace equaling that of Sun god, the tall Hanuma shone like an elephant
which increases its size when being festered by a rope.

shloka:
उपरिष्टाच्छरीरेण छायया चावगाढया |
सागरे मारुताविष्टा नौरिवासीत्तदा कपिः
translation:
Then Hanuma who was flying above the ocean with his body above the ocean and his
shadow being immersed in the sea below, looked like a boat being driven by wind.

shloka:
यं यं देशं समुद्रस्य जगाम स महाकपिः |
स स तस्योरुवेगेन सोन्माद इव लक्ष्यते | ५-१-६८
translation:
Whatever place Hanuma went towards on the ocean, that place became agitated due to
the force of thighs.

shloka:
सागरस्योओर्मिजालानामुरसा शैलवर्ष्मणाम् |
अभिघ्नंस्तु महावेगः पुप्लुवे स महाकपिः |५-१-६९
translation:
That great monkey with great speed flew in the sky striking with his chest series of
waves which had a great body like that of mountains.

shloka:
कपिवातश्च बलवान् मेघवातश्च निःसृतः |
सागरं भीमनिर्घोषं कम्पयामासतुर्भृशम्
translation:
Wind from the mighty Hanuma and the wind released from the clouds caused the ocean
with a fearful sound to shake a lot.

shloka:
विकर्षन्नूर्मिजालानि बृहन्ति लवणाम्भसि |
पुप्लुवे कपिशार्दूलो विकिरन्निव रोदसी
translation:
Hanuma flew in the sky dragging along with him big waves from the ocean as though he
were sprinkling them in the sky.

shloka:
मेरुमन्दरसंकाशानुद्धतान् स महार्णवे |
अत्यक्रामन्महावेगस्तरङ्गान् गणयन्निव
translation:
Hanuma with great speed crossed waves which were equal to Mount Meru and Mount
Mandara, that had risen up in the sea, as if counting them.

shloka:
तस्य वेगसमुद्धूतं जलं सजलदं तदा |
अम्बर्स्थं विबभ्राज शारदाभ्रमिवाततम्
translation:
Then the water together with clouds which was driven up by the force of Hanuma,
shone like a stretched autumnal cloud in the sky.

shloka:
तिमिनक्रझषाः कूर्मा दृश्यन्ते विवृतास्तदा |
वस्त्रापकर्षणेनेव शरीराणि शरीरिणाम्
translation:
Then various whales, fishes, turtles and crocodiles were being seen clearly in the
sea just as bodies of humans would be seen when clothes are removed.

shloka:
प्लवमानं समीक्ष्यथ भुजङ्गाः सागरालयाः |
व्योम्नि तं कपिशार्दूलं सुपर्ण इति मेनिरे
translation:
Serpents living in the sea saw Hanuma flying in the sky and thought that it was
Garuda, the king of birds.

shloka:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा त्रिंशद्योजनमायता |
छाया वानरसिंहस्य जले चारुतराभवत्
translation:
Hanuma's shadow which was ten yojanas wide and thirty yojanas long appeared very
beautiful on water.

shloka:
श्वेताभ्रघनराजीव वायुपुत्रानुगामिनी |
तस्य सा शुशुभे छाया वितता लवणाम्भसि
translation:
That shadow which was following Hanuma and spread on the ocean, shone like a series
of dense white clouds.

shloka:
शुशुभे स महातेजा महाकायो महाकपिः |
वायुमार्गे निरालम्बे पक्षवानिव पर्वतः
translation:
That great monkey Hanuma, the great resplendent one with a huge body, shone like a
mountain with wings flying in the sky without any support underneath.

shloka:
येनासौ याति बलवान् वेगेन कपिकुञ्जरः |
तेन मार्गेण सहसा द्रोणीकृत इवार्णवः
translation:
In whatever path Hanuma the mighty one went, in that path, there immediately
appeared a trough in the ocean below.

shloka:
आपाते पक्षिसंघानां पक्षिराज इव व्रजन् |
हनुमान् मेघजालानि प्रकर्षन् मारुतो यथा
translation:
Hanuma while coursing through the path of birds like the king of birds Garuda,
dragged with him series of clouds like the god of wind.

shloka:
पाण्डुरारुणवर्णानि नीलमाञ्जिष्ठकानि च |
कपिनाकृष्यमाणानि महाभ्राणि चकाशिरे
translation:
Great clouds with white, red, blue and madder colors shone on being dragged by
Hanuma.

shloka:
प्रविशन्नभ्रजालानिनिष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः |
प्रच्चन्नश्च प्रकाशश्च चन्द्रमा इव लक्ष्यते
translation:
Hanuma who is repeatedly entering and leaving series of clouds as He flies in the
sky, is being seen like the moon who shines and is hidden alternately.

shloka:
प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा प्लवङ्गं त्वरितं तदा |
ववर्षुः पुष्पवर्षणि देवगन्धर्वदानवाः
translation:
Then, on seeing Hanuma flying quickly in the sky, Devas, Gandharvas and Danavas
showered flowers on him.

shloka:
तताप न हि तं सूर्यः प्लवन्तं वानरोत्तमम् |
सिषेवे च तदा वायू रामकार्याद्थसिद्धये
translation:
Then, the Sun did not scorch Hanuma, the best among Vanaras, who was flying for
Rama's welfare. The wind god Vayu also served him with a delightful breeze.

shloka:
ऋषयस्तुष्टुवुश्चैव प्लवमानं विहायसा |
जगुश्च देवगन्धर्वाः प्रशंसन्तो महौजसम्
translation:
Sages praised the great resplendent Hanuma flying in the sky. Devas and Gandharvas
also sang in His praise.

shloka: नागाश्च तुष्टुवुर्यक्षा रक्षांसि विबुधाः खगाः
translation:
Immediately on seeing the best among monkeys, Hanuma, flying without any effort,
Nagas, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Devas and birds all praised Him.

shloka: तस्मिन् प्लवगशार्दूले प्लवमाने हनूमति
translation:
While that best among vanaras, Hanuma, was flying, the god of ocean thought thus for
the respect of Ikshvaaku dynasty:

shloka: साहाय्यं वानरेन्द्रस्य यदि नाहं हनूमतः
translation:
"If I do not help this best among vanaras Hanuma, I shall become prone to all kinds
of ill-talk by those who want to speak against me."

shloka: अहमिक्ष्वाकुनाथेन सगरेण विवर्धतः
translation:
"I was developed by Sagara of Ikshvaaku dynasty. This Hanuma who is helping a
descendant of that dynasty should not become tired."

shloka: तथा मया विधातव्यं विश्रमेत यथा कपिः
translation:
"I have to behave in such a way that Hanuma would take rest. After resting in me for
a while, He can cross the remaining distance with comfort."

shloka: इति कृत्वा मतिं साध्वीं समुद्रश्चन्नमम्भसि
translation:
Samudra thus making a good thought, spoke to Mainaka, the best among mountains with
gold in the middle hidden in water.

shloka: त्वमिहासुरसंघानां पाताळतलवासिनां
translation:
"O best among mountains Mainaka! You have been positioned here by Devendra as an
obstacle to the groups of asuras living in paataala."

shloka: त्वमेषां जातवीर्याणां पुनरेवोत्पतिष्यताम्
translation:
"You are standing at the entrance of paataala which is difficult to measure, fully
covering it, when asuras courageous by birth are trying to rise up again."

shloka: तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव शक्तिस्ते शैल वर्धितुम्
translation:
"O mountain, you have capability to grow wide, up or down. O best among mountains,
for that reason I am encouraging you. Raise up."

shloka: न एष कपिशार्दूलस्त्वमुपर्येति वीर्यवान्
translation:
"Hanuma, the best among monkeys, the courageous one, who has taken up a fearful task
for the benefit of Rama, that such Hanuma while flying in the sky is coming over you."

shloka: अस्य साह्यं मया कार्यमिक्ष्वाकुकुलवर्तिनः
translation:
"To this Hanuma, who is a follower of the Ikshvaaku dynasty, help should be done by
me now. Descendants of Ikshvaaku are repectable to me. They are even more respectable to you."

shloka: कुरु साचिव्यमस्माकं न नः कार्यमतिक्रमेत्
translation:
"Do help to us. Our task may not be miscarried. A task which needs to be performed
and not done, will increase the anger of good people."

shloka: सलिलादूर्ध्वमुत्तिष्ठ तिष्ठत्वेष कपिस्त्वयि
translation:
"Raise up above from the water. This Hanuma is the best among fliers and is a guest
to be worshipped for us. Let him stand on you."

shloka: चामीकरमहानाभ देवगन्धर्व सेवित
translation:
"O mountain with golden hued middle area and one who is served by Devas and
Gandharvas! Hanuma can take rest on you and then traverse rest of the distance."

shloka: काकुत्थ्सस्यानृशंस्यं च मैथिल्याश्च विवासनम्
translation:
"You are fit to raise up after seeing the gentleness of Sri Rama, and the exile of
Seetha, and the effort of Hanuma."

shloka: हिरण्य नाभो मैनाको निशम्य लवणाम्भसः
translation:
The mountain with gold in the middle, Mainaka, listening to the words of the salty
ocean, got up quickly from the water, together with great trees and creepers.

shloka: स सागरजलं भित्त्वा बभूवाभ्युत्थितस्तदा
translation:
Then that Mainaka became in the risen state, passing through the ocean water, just
like the Sun piercing through a cloud with His shining rays.

shloka: स महात्मा मुहूर्तेन सर्वतः सलिलावृतः
translation:
That great Mainaka who was covered by water in all directions, who had peaks with
Kinnaras and great serpents, which were equal to a sun rise, which were touching the sky, and which
had a golden hue, being ordered by the ocean, showed his peaks in an instant.

shloka: तप्तजाम्बूनदैः शृङिगाः पर्वतस्य समुत्थितैः
translation:
The sky which had a bluish tinge like that of a sword, shone with a golden hue
because of the peaks of the mountain which rose up and which was like molten gold.

shloka: जातरूपमयैः शृङ्गैर्भ्राजमानैः स्वयंप्रभैः
translation:
That best among mountains became equal to a hundred suns with its peaks which had a
golden hue and which were shining with a self generated shine.

shloka: तमुत्थितमसंगेन हनुमानग्रतः स्थितम्
translation:
Hanuma on seeing the mountain which stood before Him, rising up from the middle of
the salty ocean suddenly, decided that it as an obstacle.

shloka: स तमुच्छ्रित मत्यर्थं महावेगो महाकपिः
translation:
That great monkey Hanuma with a great speed, brought that great tall mountain with
His chest just as the God of wind would a cloud.

shloka: स तथा पातितस्तेन कपिना पर्वतोत्तमः
translation:
That best among mountains Mainaka, thus being fell down by that Hanuma, recognized
Hanuma's speed and lauded him with pleasure.

shloka: तमाकाशगतं वीरमाकाशे समुपस्थितः
translation:
Mount Mainaka with love and with gladdened heart obtained a human form and standing
on its own peak, spoke these words approaching that courageous Hanuma in the sky.

shloka:
दुष्करं कृतावन्कर्म त्वमिदं वानरोत्तम |
निपत्य मम शृङ्गेषु विश्रमस्व यथासुखम्
translation:
"O the great Vanara! You have performed this impossible task of flying over the
ocean. Do come down on to my peaks and rest for a while to your comfort."

shloka:
राघवस्य कुले जातैरुदधिः परिवर्धितः |
स त्वां रामहिते युक्तं प्रत्यर्चयति सागरः
translation:
"The ocean was developed by people born in Sri Rama's dynasty. That such ocean is
worshipping in lieu of Sri Rama, you who is desirous of Sri Rama's welfare."

shloka:
कृते च प्रतिकर्तव्यमेष धर्मः सनातनः |
सोऽयं तत्प्रतिकारार्थी त्वत्तः संमानमर्हति
translation:
"When a service is done, a return service needs to be rendered. This is an ancient
tradition. Such this ocean who wants to do a return service to the Raghu dynasty, is suitable for
respect by you."

shloka:
त्वन्निमित्तमनेनाहं बहुमानात्प्रचोदितः |
योजनानां शतं चापि कपिरेष समाप्लुतः
translation:
""After flying a hundred yojanas, let this Hanuma rest on your peak and then travel
the rest of distance." - Thus I have been encouraged by this ocean for your sake due to His great
respect for you. O best among vanaras! Stop for a while and then go after resting on me."

shloka:
तदिदं गन्धवत्स्वादु कन्दमूलफलं बहु |
तदास्वाद्य हरिश्रेष्ठ विश्रान्तोऽनु गमिष्यसि
translation:
"O best among vanaras! For that reason, here is lots of roots, fruits and other
eatables which are fragrant and sweet. May you leave after eating that and resting here for a
while."

shloka:
अस्माकमपि सम्बन्धः कपिमुख्य त्वयास्ति वै |
प्रख्यातस्त्रिषु लोकेषु महागुणपरिग्रहः
translation:
"O chief among vanaras! Besides this, there also exists a relationship which is
famous in all the three worlds, which is based on great virtues, for us with you."

shloka:
वेगवन्तः प्लवन्तो ये प्लवगा मारुतात्मज |
तेषां मुख्यतमं मन्ये त्वामहं कपिकुञ्जर
translation:
"O son of Vayu, the god of wind! O best among vanaras! I am thinking you as being
very important among those vanaras who are fast and who are capable of flying."

shloka:
अतिथिः किलपूजार्हः प्राकृतोऽपि विजानता |
धर्मं जिज्ञासमानेन किं पुनस्त्वादृशो महान्
translation:
"By a person who wants to know dharma or by one who knows dharma, a guest even
though ordinary is to be respected. What else can I say in the case of a great guest like you."

shloka:
त्वं हि देववरिष्ठस्य मारुतस्य महात्मनः |
पुत्रस्तस्यैव वेगेन सदृशः कपिकुञ्जर
translation:
"O best among vanaras! You are the son of the great Vayu - the God of wind, who is
best in speed among the Devas. In speed you are equal to him alone."

shloka:
पूजिते त्वयि धर्मज्ञ पूजां प्राप्नोति मारुतः |
तस्मात्त्वं पूजनीयो मे शृणु चाप्यत्र कारणम्
translation:
"O knower of Dharma! If you are worshipped, Vayu also gets worship. For that reason
you are to be worshipped by me. Also listen to another reason in this matter."

shloka:
पूर्वं कृतयुगे तात पर्वताः पक्षिणोऽभवन् |
ते हि जग्मुर्दिशः सर्वा गरुडानिलवेगिनः
translation:
"O son! Earlier in the Krita yuga, mountains had wings. With speed equal to that of
Garuda and Vayu, they went in all directions."

shloka:
ततस्तेषु प्रयातेषु देवसंघः सहर्षिभिः |
भूतानि च भयं जग्मुस्तेषां पतनशङ्कया
translation:
"After that when those mountains were thus flying freely, Devas and living creatures
together with sages obtained fear in the doubt that those mountains might fall down."

shloka:
ततः क्रुद्धः सहस्राअक्षः पर्वतानां शतक्रतुः |
पक्षान् चिच्छेद वज्रेण तत्र तत्र सहस्रशः
translation:
"Then the angry Devendra who performed a hundred Asvamedha rituals, cut off the
wings of thousands of mountains by his weapon vajra then and there."

shloka:
स मामुपागतः क्रुद्धो वज्रमुद्यम्य देवराट् |
ततोऽहं सहसा क्षिप्तः स्वसनेन महात्मना
translation:
"That Devendra angrily reached me with raised vajra. Then I was thrown away
immediately by the great Vayu."

shloka:
अस्मिन्लवणतोये च प्रक्षिप्तः प्लवगोत्तम |
गुप्तपक्षसमग्रश्च तव पित्राभिरक्षितः
translation:
"O best among vanaras! With saved full wings, being thrown down into this salt
ocean, I have been protected by your father."

shloka:
ततोऽहं मानयामि त्वां मान्यो हि मम मारुतः |
त्वया मे ह्येष संबन्धः कपिमुख्य महागुणः
translation:
"O chief among vanaras! Vayu is thus indeed respectable to me. For that reason I am
respecting you. My this relationship with you has great virtues."

shloka:
अस्मिन्नेवंगते कार्ये सागरस्य ममैव च |
प्रीतिं प्रीतमनाः कर्तुं त्वमर्हसि महाकपे
translation:
"O great Vanara! Because this matter is like this, you are suitable to make myself
and Sagara happy, with a gladdened heart."

shloka:
श्रमं मोक्षय पूजां च गृहाण कपिसत्तम |
प्रीतिं च बहुमन्यस्व प्रीतोऽस्मि तव दर्शनात्
translation:
"O best among Vanaras! Reduce your fatigue. Accept our worship also. Respect our
love. I am happy by your manifestation."

shloka:
एवमुक्तः कपिश्रेष्ठस्तं नगोत्तममब्रवीत् |
प्रीतोऽस्मि कृतमातिथ्यं मन्युरेषोऽपनीयताम्
translation:
Hanuma listening to the best mountain's words, spoke thus : "I am happy. Hospitality
has been done. Let this ill feeling be removed."

shloka:
त्वरते कार्यकालो मे अहश्चाप्यतिवर्तते |
प्रतिज्ञा च मया दत्ता न स्थातव्यमिहान्त्तरे
translation:
"The time to perform my duty is hastening me. The day too is passing. A promise has
also been given by me. I should not stand here in the middle neglecting my duty."

shloka:
इत्युक्त्वा पाणिना शैलमालभ्य हरिपुङ्गवः |
जगामाकाशमाविश्य वीर्यवान् प्रहसन्निव
translation:
The courageous Hanuma saying thus, touched the mountain with His hand, entered the
sky and flew on with a smile.

shloka:
स पर्वतसमुद्राभ्यां बहुमानादवेक्षितः |
पूजितश्चोपपन्नाभिराशीर्भिरनिलात्मजः
translation:
That Hanuma was thus seen with great respect by the ocean and the mountain, and also
worshipped with suitable blessings.

shloka:
अथोर्ध्वं दूरमुत्प्लुत्य हित्वा शैलमहार्णवौ |
पितुः पन्थानमास्थाय जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे
translation:
After that leaving the mountain and the great ocean, and flying up far into the
clear sky, Hanuma followed the path of his father.

shloka:
भूयश्चोर्ध्वं गतिं प्राप्य गिरिं तमवलोकयन् |
वायुसूनुर्निरालम्बे जगाम विमलेऽम्बरे
translation:
The son of Vayu obtained the speed to fly still higher into the sky and seeing that
mountain below, went in the clear sky which had no support.

shloka:
तद्द्वितीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम् |
प्रश्शंसुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
translation:
Seeing Hanuma perform that very difficult second task (first one being the flight
over ocean), all Devas, Siddhas and great sages praised Him.

shloka:
देवताश्चाभवन् हृष्टास्तत्रस्थास्तस्य कर्मणा |
काञ्चनस्य सुनाभस्य सहस्राक्षश्च वासवः
translation:
Devas and the thousand eyed Devendra who were there, became happy by the task of
that golden hued Mainaka.

shloka:
उवाच वचनं धीमान् परितोषात्सगद्गदम् |
सुनाभं पर्वतश्रेष्ठं स्वयमेव शचीपतिः
translation:
The wise Devendra himself spoke these words through faltering tones due to extreme
happiness, to Mainaka, the best among mountains.

shloka:
हिरण्यनाभ शैलेन्द्र परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते भृशम् |
अभयं ते प्रयच्छामि तिष्ठ सौम्य यथासुखम्
translation:
"O Mainaka, the king of mountains! I am very happy with you. O gentle one! I am
giving protection to you. Proceed according to your comfort."

shloka:
साह्यं ते सुमहद्विक्रान्तस्य हनूमतः |
क्रमतो योजनशतं निर्भयस्य भये सति
translation:
To the dauntless Hanuma crossing hundred yojanas, who is fearless even when there is
reason to be afraid, a great help has been done by you.

shloka:
रामस्यैष हितायैव याति दाशरथेर्हरिः |
सत्क्रियां कुर्वता तस्य तोषितोऽस्मि दृढं त्वया
translation:
This Vanara Hanuma is going for the benefit of Sri Rama, the son of Dasaratha. I am
very happy with you who is doing respect to Him.

shloka:
ततः प्रहर्षमगमद्विपुलं पर्वतोत्तमः |
देवतानां पतिं दृष्ट्वा परितुष्टं शतक्रतुम्
translation:
Thereafter, the best among mountains obtained great happiness on seeing Devendra,
the lord of Devas being happy.

shloka:
स वै दत्तवरः शैलो बभूवावस्थितस्तदा |
हनुमांश्च मुहूर्तेन व्यतिचक्राम सागरम्
translation:
Then that mountain with a given boon from Devendra stood still there. Hanuma also
leaped over that part of the ocean in an instant.

shloka:
ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः |
अब्रूवन् सूर्यसंकाशां सुरसां नागमातरम्
translation:
Thereafter, Devas together with Gandharvas, Siddhas and great sages spoke thus to
Surasa, the mother of Nagas, equal to the Sun in brilliance.

shloka:
अयं वातात्मजः श्रीमान्प्लवते सागरोपरि |
हनुमान्नाम तस्य त्वं मुहूर्तं विघ्नमाचर
translation:
"This glorious son of Vayu, going by the name of Hanuma is flying over the ocean.
You obtain a horrible mountain like demonic appearance and make a face with fearful tusks,
red-brown eyes and as vast as the sky, and create an obstacle to Him for an instant."

shloka:
बलमिच्छामहे ज्ञातुं भूयश्चास्य पराक्रमम् |
त्वां विजेष्यत्युपायेन विषादं वा गमिष्यति
translation:
"We are desiring to find out if by His strength and also courage and intelligence He
can win over you or obtain sorrow."

shloka:
एवमुक्ता तु सा देवी दैवतैरभिसत्कृता |
समुद्रमध्ये सुरसा बिभ्रती राक्षसं वपुः
translation:
That Goddess Surasa, thus spoken to by Devas and also being respected by them,
wearing a horrible disfigured appearance of a demon in the middle of the ocean which caused fear to
all, and stopping Hanuma who was flying, spoke these words.

shloka:
मम भक्षः प्रदिष्टस्त्वमीश्वरैर्वानरर्षभ |
अहं त्वा भक्षयिष्यामि प्रविशेदं ममाननम्
translation:
"O best among Vanaras! You have been given by Devas as my food. I will eat you.
Enter inside my mouth."

shloka:
एवमुक्तः सुरसया प्राञ्जलिर्वानरर्षभः |
प्रहृष्टवदनः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
translation:
Thus spoken to by Surasa, the glorious Hanuma, with a happy face and with folded
hands, spoke these words to Surasa.

shloka:
रामो दाशरथिर्नाम प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम् |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या चापि भार्यया
translation:
"The son of Dasaratha, with the name of Rama entered the forest of Dandaka together
with His brother Lakshmana and wife Seetha."

shloka:
अन्यकार्यविषक्तस्य बद्धवैरस्य राक्षसैः |
तस्य सीत हृता भार्या रावणेन यशस्विनी
translation:
"When that Sri Rama, with a bitter enmity towards Rakshasas, was diverted in another
task, His famed wife Seetha had been taken away by Ravana."

shloka:
तस्याः सकाशं दूतोऽहं गमिष्ये रामकारणात् |
कर्तुमर्हसि रामस्य साह्यं विषयवासिनि
translation:
"I am going for Rama's sake as a messenger to find Her presence. O subject of Sri
Rama! You are suited to help Rama."

shloka:
अथवा मैथिलीं दृष्ट्वा रामं चाक्लिष्टकारिणम् |
आगमिष्यामि ते वक्त्रं सत्यं प्रतिशृणोमि ते
translation:
"Otherwise after seeing Seetha and informing that to Sri Rama who makes Seetha
without troubles, I will obtain your mouth. I am promising truthfully to you."

shloka:
एवमुक्ता हनुमता सुरसा कामरूपिणी |
अब्रवीन्नातिवर्तेत कश्चिदेष वरो मम
translation:
Thus being spoken to by Hanuma, Surasa with power to take desired form, spoke thus:
"No one can overcome me. This is my boon."

shloka:
तं प्रयान्तं समुद्वीक्ष्य सुरसा वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
बलं जिज्ञासमाना वै नागमाता हनूमतः
translation:
Mother of Nagas, Surasa, desiring to know the strength of Hanuma, spoke these words
on seeing Him going away.

shloka:
प्रविश्य वदनं मेऽद्य गन्तव्यं वानरोत्तम |
वर एष पुरा दत्तो मम धात्रेति सत्वरा
translation:
"O best among Vanaras! You are bound to go only after entering my mouth. This boon
had been given to me long ago by Brahma." - speaking thus, with quickness she opened her wide mouth
and stood before Hanuma.

shloka: एवमुक्तः सुरसया क्रुद्धो वानरपुञ्गवः
translation:
Then Hanuma speaking thus to Surasa, became angry and became ten yojanas long and
ten yojanas wide.

shloka:
प्रविश्य वदनं मेऽद्य ग्न्तव्यं वानरोत्तम |
वर एष पुरा दत्तो ममम् ध्रात्रेति सत्वरा
translation:
Seeing Hanuma, who looked like a cloud, being ten yojanas long, Surasa also made her
mouth twenty yojanas long.

shloka: तं दृष्ट्वा मेघसंकाशं दशयोजनमायतम्
translation:
Thereafter, Hanuma got angry and became thirty yojanas long. Surasa made her mouth
forty yojanas high. The courageous Hanuma then became fifty yojanas high.

shloka: हनुमांस्तु ततः क्रुद्धस्त्रिंशद्योजनमायतः
translation:
Thereafter, Hanuma got angry and became thirty yojanas long. Surasa made her mouth
forty yojanas high. The courageous Hanuma then became fifty yojanas high.

shloka:
चकार सुरसा वक्त्रं षष्टियोजनमायतम् |
तथैव हनुमान्वीरः सप्ततीयोजिनोच्छ्रितः
translation:
Surasa then made her mouth sixty yojanas long. The mighty Hanuma in the same
fashion, became seventy yojanas high.

shloka:
चकार सुरसा व्क्त्रंशीतीयोजनोच्छ्रितम् |
हनुमानचलप्रख्यो नवतीयोजनोच्छ्रितः
translation:
Surasa made her mouth eighty yojanas high. The mountain-like Hanuma then became
ninety yojanas high.

shloka:
तद्दृष्ट्वा व्यादितं त्वास्यं वायुपुत्रः सुबुद्धिमान् |
दीर्घजिह्वं सुरसया सुघोरं नरकोपमम्
translation:
The great wise Hanuma seeing that mouth with a long tongue which was horrible and
equal to hell being opened by Surasa, greatly reduced His own body and became the size of a
thumb.

shloka:
सोऽभिपत्याशु तद्वक्त्रं निष्पत्य च महाजवः |
अन्तरिक्षे स्थितः श्रीमानिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
translation:
The glorious Hanuma with great speed, quickly entered Surasa's mouth and came out of
it and standing in the sky spoke these words to Surasa.

shloka:
प्रविष्टोऽस्मि हि ते वक्त्रं दाक्षायणि नमोऽस्तु ते |
गमिष्ये यत्र वैदेही सत्यं चासीद्वरस्तव
translation:
"O daughter of Daksha! I indeed entered your mouth. My regards to you. I will now go
where Seetha is. Your boon also came true."

shloka:
तं दृष्ट्वा वदनान्मुक्तं चन्द्रं राहुमुखादिव |
अब्रवीत्सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण वानरम्
translation:
Seeing that Vanara being released from her mouth like the moon from the mouth of
Rahu, goddess Surasa spoke these words assuming her normal form.

shloka:
अर्थसिद्ध्यै हरिश्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथासुखम् |
समानयस्व वैदेहीं राघवेण महात्मना
translation:
"O gentle Hanuma! Go according to your comfort to achieve the desired task. Bring
Seetha together with the great Sri Rama."

shloka:
तत्तृतीयं हनुमतो दृष्ट्वा कर्म सुदुष्करम् |
साधु साध्विति भूतानि प्रश्शंसुस्तदा हरिम्
translation:
Seeing that third very difficult task of Hanuma, all the creatures then praised
Hanuma saying "Good! Good!".

shloka:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमभ्येत्य वरुणालयम् |
जगामाकाशमाविश्य वेगेन गरुडोपमः
translation:
That Hanuma, equal to Garuda in speed, neared the ocean which is the abode of
Varuna, entered the sky and went in His original path.

shloka: चरिते कैशिकाचार्यैरैरावतनिषेविते
translation:
Hanuma went, like Garuda, in the sky served by clouds (or streams of water), served
also by birds, tread by masters of music Tumbura and other Gandharvas, served by Airavata, borne by
lions, elephants, tigers, birds and serpents, decorated by clear Vimanas moving with great speed,
shone by fires with thunderous jolt equal to that of Vajra - the weapon of Devendra, decorated by
people with good deeds, people with great luck who conquered the heavens, served by the God of fire
carrying great quantities of oblations, shone by planets, stars, moon, sun and starlets, occupied
by groups of great sages, Gandharvas, Nagas, Yakshas but unpopulated by humans, clear and all
pervasive, served by the gandharva king Vishvaavasu, roamed by elephants of Devendra, the path of
the moon and the sun, the auspicious one, a wide canopy of the earth constructed by Brahma, served
in various ways by excellent courageous groups of Vidyadharas.

shloka:
प्रदृश्यमानः सर्वत्र हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः |
भेजेऽम्बरं निरालम्बं लम्बपक्ष इवाद्रिराट्
translation:
Hanuma, the son of Vayu, visible everywhere, obtained the sky without support, like
the king of birds with long wings.

shloka:
प्लवमानं तु तं दृष्ट्वा सिंहिका नाम राक्षसी |
मनसा चिन्तयामास प्रवृद्धा कामरूपिणी
translation:
A demoness by the name of Simhika with the power to assume desired form, saw Hanuma
flying, increased in size and thought thus in her mind.

shloka:
अद्य दीर्ग़्हस्य कालस्य भविष्याम्यहामाशिता |
इदं हि मे महत्सत्त्वं चिरस्य वशमागतम्
translation:
"After a long time, this great animal came into my grasp. After long time, today I
will enjoy my meal."

shloka:
इति संचिन्त्य मनसा छायामस्य समाक्षिपत् |
छायायां गृह्यमाणायां चिन्तयामास वानरः
translation:
Thinking thus in her mind, Simhika attracted His shadow. While the shadow was thus
being grasped, Hanuma thought thus.

shloka:
समाक्षिप्तोऽस्मि तरसा पञूकृतपराक्रमः |
प्रतिलोमेन वातेन महानौरिव सागरे
translation:
"Like a great boat in the ocean with opposing winds, I am being pulled back
forcefully, with disabled power."

shloka:
तिर्यगूर्ध्वमधश्चैव वीक्षिमाणस्ततः कपिः |
ददर्श स महत्सत्त्वमुत्थितं लवणाम्भसि
translation:
After that, Hanuma looking sideways, upwards and downwards, saw a big animal raised
up in the salty ocean.

shloka:
छाय्तद्धृष्ट्वा चिन्तयामास मारुतिर्विकृताननम् |
कपिराजेन कथितं सत्त्वमद्भुतदर्शनम्
translation:
Hanuma saw that animal with a horrible face and thought: "This animal with a strange
appearance, with great strength attracting shadow, is indeed the animal that had been told by
Sugriva. There is no doubt in that."

shloka:
आग्राहि महावीर्यं तदिदं नात्र संशयः |
स तां बुद्ध्वार्थतत्त्वेन सिंहिकां मतिमान्कपिः |
व्यवर्धत महाकायः प्रवृषीव वलाहकः
translation:
That wise Hanuma recognizing that animal correctly as Simhika, increased His body
greatly, like a cloud in rainy season.

shloka: तस्य सा कायमुद्वीक्ष्य वर्धमानं महाकपेः
translation:
That Simhika seeing the growing body of the great monkey Hanuma, spread her mouth to
be equal to the middle of Patala.

shloka: घनराजीव गर्जन्ती वानरं सम्भिद्रवत्
translation:
Roaring like a dense cloud, she ran towards the Vanara. Then the wise Hanuma saw her
opened very big mouth equal to His own body and also her internal organs.

shloka:
स तस्या विवृते वक्त्रे वज्रसंहननः कपिः |
संक्षिप्य मुहुरात्मानं निष्पपात महाबलः
translation:
That Hanuma with great strength and with a body equal to a diamond, repeatedly
contracted His body and fell into her opened mouth.

shloka:
आस्ये तस्या निमज्जन्तं ददृशुः सिद्धचारणाः |
ग्रस्यमानं यथा चन्द्रं पूर्णं पर्वणि राहुणा
translation:
Siddhas and Charanas saw Hanuma sinking in her mouth, like the full moon on a full
moon day being swallowed by Rahu.

shloka:
ततस्तस्या नखैस्तीक्णैर्मर्माण्युत्कृत्य वानरः |
उत्पपाताथ वेगेन मनः संपातविक्रमः
translation:
Then Hanuma rend her internal organs with His sharp nails and after that flew up
with a speed equal to that of thought.

shloka:
तां तु दृष्ट्वा च धऋत्या च दाक्षिण्येन निपात्य च |
स कपिप्रवरो वेगाद्ववृधे पुनरात्मवान्
translation:
That wise Hanuma felling Simhika down with His vision, courage and ability,
developed again by speed.

shloka:
हृतहृत्सा हनुमता पपात विधुराम्भसि |
तां हतां वानरेणाशु पतितां वीक्ष्य सिंहिकाम्
translation:
That Simhika with heart rend by Hanuma fell in water with sorrow. Seeing Simhika
killed by Hanuma, creatures roaming in the sky spoke thus to that best among Vanaras.

shloka: भीममद्य कृतं कर्म महत्सत्त्वं त्वया हतम्
translation:
"O best among Vanaras! A huge animal has been killed by you. A great task has been
done. Perform the task dear to you auspiciously."

shloka:
यस्य त्वेतानि चत्वारि वानरेन्द्र यथा तव || ५-१९८
धृतिर्दृष्टिर्मतिर्दाक्ष्यं स कर्मसु न सीदति |
translation:
"O best among Vanaras! Whoever has the four qualities of courage, vision, intellect
and skill, all these four virtues like you, such a person will not fail in any task."

shloka: स तैः संभावितः पूज्यः प्रतिपन्नप्रयोजनः
translation:
That Hanuma the respectable one, thus respected by them, entered the sky and went
like the Garuda with a determined goal.

shloka: प्राप्तभूयिष्ठपारस्तु सर्वतः प्रतिलोकयन्
translation:
Hanuma after almost reaching the other shore, looked in all directions and saw a
series of trees at the end of his journey of hundred yojanas.

shloka: ददर्श च पतन्नेव विविधद्रुमभूषितम्
translation:
The best among Vanaras, Hanuma, immediately after getting down also saw an island
decorated by a variety of trees and also the forests in the region of Malaya.

shloka: सागरं सागरानूपं सागरानूपजान् द्रुमान्
translation:
That Hanuma with controlled senses and with good thoughts looked at the ocean, the
bay and the trees born in the bay, and also the faces of the wives of the ocean (rivers are
considered wives of ocean), observed Himself to be equal in size to a great cloud as though
stopping the sky, and thought thus.

shloka: कायवृद्धिं प्रवेगं च मम दृष्ट्वव राक्षसाः
translation:
"After seeing my huge body and the speed, Rakshasas will become curious." - thus
thought the great Hanuma.

shloka: ततः शरीरं संक्षिप्य तन्महीधरसन्निभम्
translation:
For that reason, Hanuma reduced His mountain-like body and obtained the nature of
one who reached self-realization, free from infatuations.

shloka: तद्रूपमतिसंक्षिप्य हनुमान् प्रकृतौ स्थितः
translation:
Hanuma greatly reducing His size became normal in nature regaining His original
form, like Vishnu who mitigated the strength of Bali by taking three strides.

shloka:
स चारुनानाविधरूपधारी |
परं समासाद्य समुद्रतीरम् |
परैरशक्यः प्रतिपन्नरूपः |
समीक्षितात्मा समवेक्षितार्थः
translation:
Hanuma capable of assuming many different beautiful forms, who cannot be defeated by
enemies, obtained the other side of ocean and being cognizant of Himself restored His own form and
became with a decided mission.

shloka:
ततः स लम्बस्य गिरेः समृद्धे |
विचित्रकूटे निपपात कूटे |
सकेतकोद्दालकनाळिकेरे |
महाभ्रकूटप्रतिमो महात्मा
translation:
After that great one who looked like a huge mass of clouds, alighted on the mountain
peak of Lamba with wonderful lower peaks, abundant with various things and filled with Ketaka,
Uddalaka and coconut trees.

shloka:
ततस्तु संप्राप्य समुद्रतीरं |
समीक्ष्य लङ्कां गिरिवर्यमूर्ध्नि |
कपिस्तु तस्मिन्निपपात पर्वते |
विधूय रूपं व्यथयन्म्ऱृगद्विजान्
translation:
After that Hanuma for His part obtained the ocean shore, observed the city of Lanka
from the top of the mountain, leaving His original form, tormenting animals and birds, alighted on
that mountain.

shloka:
स सागरं दानवपन्नगायुतं |
बलेन विक्रम्य महोर्मिमालिनम् |
निपत्य तीरे च महोदधेस्तदा |
ददर्श लङ्काममरावतीमिव
translation:
Having tranersed, by the dint of his strength over the ocean which was infested with
demons and reptiles and endowed with series of huge waves, and alighting on the shore of the great
sea, Hanuma then saw the City of Lanka having a resemblance of Amaravati, the capital City of
Indra.

shloka:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः |
त्रिकूटशिखरे लङ्कां स्थितां स्वस्थो ददर्श ह
translation:
That Hanuma with great strength crossed the insurmountable ocean without becoming tired and viewed the city of 
Lanka located on the peak of Mount Trikuta.

shloka:
ततः पादपमुक्तेन पुष्पवर्षेण वीर्यवान् |
अभिवृष्टः स्थितस्तत्र बभौ पुष्पमयो यथा
translation:
After that, the powerful Hanuma standing there shone like one made of flowers being showered by a rain of flowers 
released by trees.

shloka:
योजनानां शतं श्रीमांस्तीर्त्वाप्युत्तमविक्रमः |
अनिःस्वसन् कपिस्तत्र न ग्लानिमधिगच्छति
translation:
The glorious Hanuma with the best courage, even though crossing a hundred yojanas, was without a sigh and did 
not obtain any tiredness.

shloka:
शतान्यहं योजनानां क्रमेयं सुबहुन्यपि |
किं पुनः सागरस्यान्तं संख्यातं शतयोजनम्
translation:
"I can cross many hundreds of yojanas. What to say about the end of the ocean which had been counted to be hundred 
yojanas long?"

shloka:
स तु वीर्यवतां श्रेष्ठः प्लवतामपि चोत्तमः |
जगाम वेगवान् लङ्कां लङ्घयित्वा महोदधिम्
translation:
That Hanuma, the best among powerful ones and the foremost also among those who can fly, reached the city of Lanka 
by crossing the great ocean with good speed.

shloka:
शाद्वलानि च नीलानि गन्धवन्ति वनानि च |
गण्डवन्ति च मध्येन जगाम नगवन्ति च
translation: He passed through forests with dark green hued fragrant lawns and also consisting of great rocks and hills.

shloka:
शैलांश्च तरुसंचन्नान् वनराजीश्च पुष्पिताः |
अभिचक्राम तेजस्वी हनुमान् प्लवगर्षभः
translation:
Hanuma, the best among Vanaras and the radiant one, tread on mountains covered with trees and on series of trees 
full of flowers.

shloka:
स तस्मिन्नचले तिष्ठन्वनान्युपवनानि च |
स नगाग्रे च तां लङ्कां ददर्श पवनात्मजः
translation:
That son of God Vayu stood on a mountain and saw forests and gardens and also the city of Lanka situated on the 
top of a mountain.

shloka:
सरळान् कर्णिकारांश्च खर्जूरांश्च सुपुष्पितान् |
प्रियाळान्मुचुळिन्दांश्च कुटजान् केतकानपि
translation:
Standing on that mountain, the elephant among monkeys, Hanuma, saw pine trees, Karnikaras, date-palms in full 
blossom, Priyalas, lemon trees, wild jasmine trees, mogra trees, long pepper trees filled with sweet fragrance, 
Kadamba trees and seven leaved banana trees, Asana trees, Kovidaras, Karaviras in full blossom, trees that were 
tied by the weight of their flowers and flower buds, that were distressed by birds, with their crests moved by 
wind, wells and various glorious pleasure-groves filled by various trees that give fruits and flowers in all seasons 
and beautiful gardens also, surrounded by various ponds consisting of swans and ducks.

shloka:
समासाद्य च लक्ष्मीवन् लङ्कां रावणपालिताम् |
परिखाभिः सपद्माभिः सोत्पलाभिरलंकृताम्
translation:
The glorious Hanuma neared the city of Lanka ruled by Ravana, and saw the city which looked like the city of Gods 
in heaven, decorated by moats filled with lotuses and water-lilies, which was well protected, since the time of 
Seetha's abduction, by Ravana and by Rakshasas with horrifying voices roaming around, which was surrounded by 
a golden boundary wall, that beautiful great city consisted of houses equal in height to mountains and which looked 
like autumnal clouds, with white and elevated main streets, decorated with flags and pennons, with excellent golden 
hued archways adorned with sculpted rows of vines.

shloka:
गिरिमूर्ध्नि स्थितां लङ्कां पाण्डुरैर्भवनैः शुभैः |
ददर्श स कपिश्रेष्ठः पुरमाकाशगं यथा
translation:
That best among monkeys Hanuma saw the city of Lanka with beautiful white buildings situated on the top of a mountain 
like a city located in the sky.

shloka:
पालितां राक्षसेन्द्रेण निर्मितां विश्वकर्मणा |
प्लवमानामिवाकाशे ददर्श हनुमान् पुरीम्
translation:
Hanuma saw that city of Lanka ruled by Ravana the king of Rakshasas, constructed by Visvakarma (architect of Gods), 
and which looked as though it were floating in the sky.

shloka:
पप्रप्राकारजघनां विपुलाम्बुनवाम्बराम् |
शतघ्नीशूलकेशान्तामट्टालकवतंसकाम्
translation:
Hanuma saw the city of Lanka with buttress and enclosure wall as her hip and loins, the vast body pf water in 
the moat as her raiment, Satagnis and Sulas as her locks, the mansions as her earrings, constructed by thought. 
He reached the northern gate and thought thus.

shloka:
कैलासशिखरप्रख्यामालिख्स्न्तीमिवाम्बरम् |
डीयमानामिवाकाशमुच्छ्रितैर्भवनोत्तमैः
translation:
Hanuma saw the city of Lanka equal to peak of Kailasa as though touching the sky, as though flying to reach the 
sky, with its best mansions, filled with horrible rakshasas and serpants like the city of Bhogavati (capital of 
Patala), one which was unfathomable, a well arranged and a clear city governed by Kubera in earlier times, protected 
by courageous, horrible serpents and Rakshasas with mouths with sharp teeth like a cave, with spikes and Pattisas 
(spears) in their hands. Hanuma saw that Lanka's great protection and the ocean and Ravana the horrible enemy 
and thought thus.

shloka:
आगत्यापीह हरयो भविष्यन्ति निररथकाः |
न हि युद्धेन व लङ्का शक्या जेतुं सुरैरपि
translation:
"Even if Vanaras were to come here they would not meet with success. It is not possible even for Devas to be victorious 
against Lanka in war".

shloka:
इमां तु विषमां दुर्गां लङ्कां रावणपालिताम् |
प्राप्यापि स महाबाहुः किम् करिष्यति राघवः
translation:
"Even if He reaches this very difficult and impenetrable Lanka ruled by Ravana, what can that Sri Rama with mighty 
arms do"?

shloka:
अवकाशो न सान्त्वस्य रक्षसेष्वभिगम्यते |
न दानस्य न भेदस्य नैव युद्धस्य दृश्यते
translation:
"In the matter of overcoming rakshasas, there seems to be no opportunity for persuasion, gifts, dissension or 
even war".

shloka:
चतुर्णामेव हि गतिर्वानराणां महात्मनाम् |
वालिपुत्रस्य नीलस्य मम राज्ञश्च धीमतः
translation: "Only four great Vanaras can come here - the son of Vali (Angada), Nila, myself and the wise king Sugriva".

shloka:
यावज्जानामि वैदेहीं यदि जीवति वा न वा |
तत्रैव चिन्तयिष्यामि दृष्ट्वा तां जनकात्मजाम्
translation: "I will first find out if Seetha is alive or not. I will think all this later, after seeing that daughter of Janaka".

shloka:
ततः स चिन्तयामास मुहूर्तं कपिकुञ्जरः |
गिरिशृङ्गे स्थितस्तस्मिन् रामस्याभ्युदये रतः
translation:
After that, that elephant among monkeys Hanuma who was interested in the welfare of Sri Rama, stood on that mountain 
peak and thought for an instant.

shloka:
अनेन रूपेण मया न शक्या रक्षसां पुरी |
प्रवेष्टुं राक्षसैर्गुप्ता क्रूरैर्बलसमन्वितैः
translation: "It is not possible for me to enter the city of ogres protected by cruel and strong rakshasas, with this appearance".

shloka:
उग्रौजसो महावीर्या बलवन्तश्च राक्षसाः |
वञ्चनीया मया सर्वे जानकीं परिमार्गता
translation:
"All these mighty ogres with extraordinary energy and great prowess are to be cheated by me while engaged in the 
search of Seetha".

shloka:
लक्ष्यालक्ष्येण रूपेण रात्रौ लङ्का पुरी मया |
प्रवेष्टुं प्राप्तकालं मे कृत्यं साधयितुं महत्
translation:
"To achieve this great deed successfully, entering the city of Lanka in a small form at night is a timely thing 
to do" .

shloka:
तां पुरीं तादृशीं दृष्ट्वा दुराधर्शां सुरासुरैः |
हनुमान् चिन्तयामास विनिश्चित्य मुहुर्मुहुः
translation:
Hanuma saw such that city of Lanka, which was difficult to overcome even for Devas or asuras, and thought thus 
repeatedly.

shloka:
केनोपायेन पशेयं मैथिलीं जनकात्मजाम् |
अदृष्टो राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना
translation: "By what idea can I see Seetha the daughter of Janaka, unseen by the wicked Ravana, the king of the ogres.

shloka:
न विनश्येत्कथं कार्यं रामस्य विदितात्मनः |
एकामेकश्च पश्येयं रहिते जनकात्मजाम्
translation:
"How can the task of Sri Rama, one who knows self, not be destroyed? How can I alone see Seetha alone in a place 
devoid of people?."

shloka:
भूताश्चार्था विपद्यन्ते देशकालविरोधिताः |
विक्लबं दूतमासाद्य तमः सूर्योदये यथा
translation:
"With a mediator who has an unsteady and gloomy mind working against time and place, tasks that are otherwise 
ready to succeed get harmed, like the darkness that gets destroyed at dawn".

shloka:
अर्थानर्थान्तरे बुद्धिर्निश्चितापि न शोभते |
घातयन्ति हि कार्याणि दूताः पण्डितमानिनः
translation:
"Even a decided mind will not shine when thinking about gain and loss. Mediators who are respected by scholarly 
people will also harm tasks due to their arrogance."

shloka:
न विनश्येत्कथं कार्यं वैक्लब्यम् न कथं भवेत् |
लङ्घनं च समुद्रस्य कथं नु न वृथा भवेत्
translation:
"How will the task at hand be not harmed? How will my mind not get gloominess? How will not the crossing of ocean 
go waste?."

shloka:
मयि दृष्टे तु रक्षोभी रामस्य विदितात्मनः |
भवेद्व्यर्थमिदं कार्यं रावणानर्थमिच्छतः
translation:
"If I were to be seen by rakshasas, this task of Sri Rama, with a famed mind, who desires the slaying of Ravana 
will become wasteful."

shloka:
न हि शक्यं क्वचित् स्थातुमविज्ञातेन राक्षसैः |
अपि राक्षसरूपेण किमुतान्येन केनचित्
translation:
"It is not possible to be in Lanka even in the form of a rakshasa. What to say about being there in any other 
form?"

shloka:
वायुरप्यत्र नाज्ञातश्चरेदिति मतिर्मम |
न ह्यस्त्यविदितं किंचिद्राक्षसानां बलीयसाम्
translation:
"My thought goes thus: Even wind cannot pass here without being known. There is nothing not known to the might 
rakshasas."

shloka:
इहाहं यदि तिष्ठामि स्वेन रूपेण संवृतः |
विनाशमुपयास्यामि भर्तुरर्थश्च हीयते
translation: "If I stay here with my usual form, I can be destroyed. The task of the Lord will also be harmed."

shloka:
तदहं स्वेन रूपेण रजन्यां ह्रस्वतां गतः |
लङ्कामभिपतिष्यामि राघवस्यार्थसिद्धये
translation:
"For that reason, I will become small in my appearance and will enter Lanka at night for the success of the task 
of Sri Rama."

shloka:
रावणस्य पुरीं रात्रौ प्रविश्य सुदुरासदाम् |
विचिन्वन् भवनं स्र्वं द्रक्ष्यामि जनकात्मजाम्
translation: "Entering the unapproachable city of Lanka at night and searching all the mansion of Ravana, I can see Seetha."

shloka:
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमान् सूर्यस्यास्तमयं कपिः |
आचकांक्षे ततो वीरो वैदेह्या द्रशनोतुसकः
translation: The courageous Hanuma thus thinking and being interested in discovering Seetha, then desired the sun to set.

shloka:
सूर्ये चास्तं गते रात्रौ देहं संक्षिप्य मारुतिः |
वृषदंशकमात्रः सन् बभूवाद्भुतदर्शनः
translation:
After the sun had set, Hanuma reduced His body at night with a size equal to that of a cat and became a wonderful 
sight to behold.

shloka:
प्रदोषकाले हनुमांस्तूर्णमुत्प्लुत्य वीर्यवान् |
प्रविवेश पुरीं रम्यां सुविभक्तमहापथाम्
translation: The courageous Hanuma quickly flew during evening time and entered the beautiful city with well divided main pathways.

shloka:
प्रासादमालाविततां स्तम्भैः काञ्चनराजतैः |
शातकुम्भमयैर्जालैर्गन्धर्वनगरोपमाम्
translation:
Hanuma saw that great city filled with series of mansions, golden hued pillars and window lattices, which was 
equal to the city of Gandharvas, consisting of seven and eight storied buildings with their top portions studded 
with crystals and pearls and decorated with gold.

shloka:
वैडूर्यमणिचित्रैश्च मुक्ताजालविभूषितैः |
तलैः शुशुभिरे तानि भवनान्यत्र रक्षसाम्
translation:
There in that city of Lanka, the houses of rakshasas shone with top portions painted by cats-eyes and emeralds 
and decorated by groups of pearls.

shloka:
काञ्चनानि च चित्राणि तोरणानि च रक्षसाम् |
लङ्कामुद्द्योतयामासुः सर्वतः समलंकृताम्
translation: Golden archways with strange hues illuminated the well decorated city of Lanka in all directions.

shloka:
अचिन्त्यामद्भुताकारां दृष्ट्वा लङ्कां महाकपिः |
आसीद्विष्ण्डो हृष्टश्च वैदेह्या दर्शनोत्सुकः
translation:
Hanuma on seeing the unimaginable city of Lanka with a wonderful appearance became sad thinking about the prospect 
of capturing Lanka and also happy being eager to see Seetha.

shloka:
स पाण्डुराविद्धविमानमालिनीं |
महार्हजाम्बूनदजालतोरणाम् |
यशस्विनीं रावणबाहुपालितां |
क्षपाचरैर्भिमबलैः 
समावृताम्
translation:
Hanuma saw that city of Lanka of great fame, with white, closely built buildings having golden windows and doorways 
of great value, consisting of ogres of great strength and ruled by the hands of Ravana.

shloka:
चन्द्रोऽपि साचिव्यमिवास्य कुर्वं |
स्तारागणैर्मध्यगतो विराजन् |
ज्योत्स्नावितानेन वितत्य लोक |
मुत्तिष्ठते 
नैकसहस्ररश्मिः
translation:
The shining moon too rose up with its many thousands of rays, as though performing help to Hanuma, being at the 
middle of its retinue of stars and covering the earth with a canopy of light. That Hanuma saw the moon rising 
up with a glow of a conch shell, shining with a milky white hue of a lotus-fiber, like a swan swimming in a lake.

shloka:
शङ्खप्रभं क्षीरमृणालवर्ण |
मुद्गच्छमानं व्यवभासमानम् |
ददर्श चन्द्रं स हरिप्रवीरः |
प्लोप्लूयमानं सरसीव 
हंसम्
translation:
That Hanuma saw the moon, who was rising up in the sky with the splendour of a couch-shell, shining in white colour 
as milk or lotus-fibre, and looking like a swan swimming in a lake.

shloka:
स लम्ब शिखरे लम्बे लम्ब तोयद सम्निभे |
सत्त्वम् आस्थाय मेधावी हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
translation:
That Hanuma, best among monkeys, the intellectual son of Vayu, one with great might, stood on the 
moutain called Lamba with its high peaks equalling a high cloud, gathered courage and entered at night the city 
of Lanka ruled by Ravana and filled with beautiful forests and places of water such as lakes.

shloka:
शारद अम्बु धर प्रख्यैः भवनैः उपशोभिताम् |
सागर उपम निर्घोषाम् सागर अनिल सेविताम्
translation:
The city of Lanka was shone by buildings equalling autumnal clouds. With a sound resembling that 
of an ocean, it was served by ocean breeze. It was filled with well fed and mighty armies like Vitapati, the capital 
of Kubera. It had elephants positioned at archways and had white gates and archways.

shloka:
भुजग आचरिताम् गुप्ताम् शुभाम् भोगवतीम् इव |
ताम् सविद्युत् घन आकीर्णाम् ज्योतिः मार्ग निषेविताम्
translation:
Quickly approaching that city of Lanka which was protected by Rakshasas, like the the auspicious 
city of Bhogavati being protected by serpents moving about, spread with cloud illumined by flashes of lightening, 
served by pathways of stars, witha light breeze like the Indra's city of Amaravati, surrounded by a wall with 
a golden hue, decorated by flags with sounds from groups of small bells. He became happy and leapt up the wall.

shloka:
विस्मय आविष्ट हृदयः पुरीम् आलोक्य सर्वतः |
जाम्बूनदमयैः द्वारैः वैदूर्य कृत वेदिकैः
translation:
Seeing the city everywhere Hanuma became surprised at heart. Thereafter Hanuma the monkey, became 
happy seeing the doors which were of golden color, with platforms of cat's eye gems, inlaid with diamonds, crystals 
and pearls, embellished with floors of gems, graced with elephants made of refined gold, crowned with spotless 
white silver, stairs studded with cat's eye gems, with inside walls made of crystal free from dust, provided with 
lovely assembly halls, with sounds of Krauncha birds and peacocks, served by royal swans, looking as though flying 
toward the sky, with auspicious houses resounding everywhere with the sounds of clarionets and ornaments, equalling 
the city of Vasvaukasaara, as though flying towards the sky.

shloka:
ताम् समीक्ष्य पुरीम् लन्काम् राक्षस अधिपतेः शुभाम् |
अनुत्तमाम् ऋद्धि युताम् चिन्तयाम् 
आस वीर्यवान्
translation:
Seeing that city of Ravana, which was best among cities, a wealthy city, a beautiful and auspicious 
city, that powerful Hanuma thought thus.

shloka:
न इयम् अन्येन नगरी शक्या धर्षयितुम् बलात् |
रक्षिता रावण बलैः उद्यत आयुध धारिभिः
translation:
"It is not possible for anyone else to oppose this city, by strength alone, which is being guarded 
by armies of Ravana with raised weapons."

shloka:
कुमुद अन्गदयोः वा अपि सुषेणस्य महा कपेः |
प्रसिद्धा इयम् भवेत् भूमिः मैन्द द्विविदयोः अपि
translation: This land may be conquerable by Kumuda or Angada, to the great monkey Sushena or to Mainda or Dvivida.

shloka:
विवस्वतः तनूजस्य हरेः च कुश पर्वणः |
ऋक्षस्य केतु मालस्य मम चैव गतिः भवेत्
translation:
There may be access to this land to the son of Sun God Sugreeva, to the monkey Kusaparvana, to 
the chief among monkeys Riksha and to me.

shloka:
समीक्ष्य तु महा बाहः राघवस्य पराक्रमम् |
लक्ष्मणस्य च विक्रान्तम् अभवत् प्रीतिमान् कपिः
translation: Considering the long armed Sri Rama's strength and Lakshmana's valour, Hanuma became happy.

shloka:
ताम् रत्न वसन उपेताम् कोष्ठ आगार अवतंसकाम् |
यन्त्र अगार स्तनीम् ऋद्धाम् प्रमदाम् इव भूषिताम्
translation:
That great monkey saw that city of king of rakshasas like a wealthy woman decorated with diamonds 
for her clothes, with various storage houses as earrings, with amouries for her breasts. Due to the lamps that 
illuminated the radiant great houses, all darkness was lost.

shloka:
अथ सा हरिशार्दूलम् प्रविशन्तिम् महाबलम् |
नगरी स्वेन रूपेण ददर्श पवनात्मजम्
translation:
Thereafter, the guardian of that city, in her own form, saw Hanuma, the best among monkeys and 
the mighty one, entering.

shloka:
सा तम् हरिवरम् दृष्ट्वा लङ्का रावणपालिता |
स्वयमेवोत्थिता तत्र विकृताननदर्शना
translation:
Seeing that best among monkeys Hanuma there, that Lanka ruled by Ravana, rose up herself with a 
horrific appearance of face an eyes.

shloka:
पुरस्तत्क पिवर्यस्य वायुसूनोरतिष्ठत |
मुञ्चमाना महानादमब्रवीत्पवनात्मजम्
translation:
She stood in front of the best among Vanaras Hanuma. She made a great sound and spoke to Hanuma 
thus.

shloka:
कस्त्वम् केन च कार्येण इह प्राप्तो वनालय |
कथय स्वेह यत्तत्त्वम् यावत्प्राणा धरन्ति ते
translation:
"O one who lives in gardens! Who are you? For what reason did you come here? As long as your lives 
are sustained, tell me the truth here before that."

shloka:
न शक्यम् खल्वियम् लङ्का प्रवेष्टुम् वानर त्वया |
रक्षिता रावणबलैरभिगुप्ता समन्ततः
translation:
"O Vanara! It is indeed not possible for you to enter this city of Lanka which is protected by 
Ravana's forces and strongly guarded all around."

shloka:
अथ तामब्रवीद्वीरो हनुमानग्रतः स्थिताम् |
कथयिष्यामि ते तत्त्वम् यन्मम् त्वम् परिपृच्छसि
translation:
Therafter the mighty Hanuma spoke to Lanka standing in front of Him as follows : "Whatever matter 
you are asking me, I will tell you that truthfully."

shloka:
का त्वम् विरूपनयना पुरद्वारेऽवतिष्ठसि |
किमर्थम् चापि माम् रुद्ध्वा निर्भर्त्सयसि दारुणा
translation:
"You are standing at the entrance to the city. O one with ugly eyes! Who are you? O horrible one! 
Stopping me, for what reason are you threatening me?"

shloka:
हनुमद्वचनम् श्रुत्वा लङ्का सा कामरूपिणी |
उवाच वचनम् क्रुद्धा परुषं पवनात्मजम्
translation:
Listening to Hanuma's words, that Lanka, with ability to achieve desired form, became angry and 
spoke these strong words to Hanuma.

shloka:
अहम् राक्षसराजस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः |
आज्ञाप्रतीक्षा दुर्धर्षा रक्षामि नगरीमिमाम्
translation:
"I protect this city, being invincible. I wait for the orders of the king of demons Ravana, the 
great one."

shloka:
न शक्या मामवज्ञाय प्रवेष्टुम् नगरी त्वया |
अद्य प्राणैः परित्यक्तः स्वप्स्यसे निहतो मया
translation:
"After humilliating me it is not possible for you to enter the city. Being beaten by me, you will 
leave life and have a permanent sleep."

shloka:
अहम् हि नगरी लङ्का स्वयमेव प्लवङ्गम |
सर्वतः परिरक्षामि ह्येतत्ते कथितम् मया
translation:
"O Vanara! I am protecting this city of Lanka in all directions. This matter has been already told 
to you by me."

shloka:
लङ्काया वचनम् श्रुत्वा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः |
यत्नवान्स हरिश्रेष्ठः स्थितश्शैल इवापरः
translation:
The son of Vayu and best among Vanaras heard Lanka's words and stood up like a second mountain, 
with a purpose.

shloka:
स ताम् स्त्रीरूपविकृताम् दृष्ट्वा वानरपुङ्गवः |
आबभाषेऽथ मेधावि सत्त्वान् प्लवगर्षभः
translation:
Thereafter that Hanuma the wise one, with great strength, best among those who can fly and best 
among Vanaras, saw that city of Lanka in the form of an ugly woman and spoke thus.

shloka:
द्रक्ष्यामि नगरीम् लङ्काम् साट्टप्राकारतोरणाम् |
इत्यर्थमिह सम्प्राप्तः परम् कौतूहलम् हि 
मे
translation:
"I should like to see the city of Lanka with its palaces, defensive walls and archways. I came 
here for that reason. I am very curious to see them."

shloka:
वनान्युपवनानीह लङ्कायाः काननानि च |
सर्वतो गृहमुख्यानि द्रष्टुमागमनम् हि मे
translation: "My arrival here is indeed to see Lanka's gardens, parks, forests and important houses all over."

shloka:
तस्य तद्वचनम् श्रुत्वा लङ्का सा कामरूपिणी |
भूय एव पुनर्वाक्यम् बभाषे परुषाक्षरम्
translation:
Listening to Hanuma's words, Lanka with the ability to assume desired form, spoke harsh words stronger 
than before.

shloka:
मामनिर्जत्य दुर्बद्धे राक्षसेश्वरपालिता |
न शक्यमद्य ते द्रष्टुम् पुरीयम् वनराधम
translation:
"O lowly Vanara with an evil mind! It is not possile for you to see this city ruled by king of 
rakshasas, without first defeating me."

shloka:
ततः स कपिशार्दूलस्तामुवाच निशाचरीम् |
दृष्वा पुरीमिमाम् भद्रे पुनर्यास्ये यथागतम्
translation:
Then that tiger among Vanaras Hanuma spoke to that demon : "O auspicious one! After seeing this 
city I will return back again to where I came from."

shloka:
ततः कृत्वा महानादम् सा वै लङ्का भयावहम् |
तलेन वानरश्रेष्ठम् ताडयामास वेगिता
translation:
Thereafter that Lanka made a great sound causing terror and hit Hanuma, the best among Vanaras, 
with her palm quickly.

shloka:
ततः स कपिशार्दुलो लङ्काया ताडितो भृशम् |
ननाद सुमहानादम् वीर्यवान् पवनात्मजः
translation:
Then that tiger among Vanaras, the powerful son of Vayu, being hit powerfully by Lanka made a great 
sound.

shloka:
ततः सम्वर्तयामास वामहस्तस्य सोऽङ्गुळीः |
मुष्टिनाभिजघूनैनाम् हनुमान् क्रोधमूर्चितः
translation:
Thereafter that Hanuma became dizzy with anger and folded his fingers of left hand. He then hit 
her with His fist. "She is a woman" - thinking thus He did not show much anger by Himself.

shloka: सा तु तेन प्रहारेण विह्वलाङ्गी नीशाचरी
translation:
That demon fell on land immediately by that hit with a distressed body and appeared with a horrific 
face.

shloka: ततस्तु हनुमान् प्राज्ञस्ताम् दृष्ट्वा विनिपातिताम्
translation:
Thereafter the intellectual and glorious Hanuma saw her fallen down and thinking her to be woman, 
showed kindness.

shloka: ततो वै भृशसम्विग्ना लङ्का गद्गदाक्षरम्
translation:
Thereafter that Lanka being very gloomy spoke with a falterting tone without pride these words 
to Hanuma the Vanara.

shloka: प्रसीद सुमहाबाहो त्रायस्व हरिसत्तम
translation:
"O long armed one! O best among Vanaras! Get propitiated and protect me. O gentle one! Those with 
great strength and courage always stand firm on tradition."

shloka: अहं तु नगरी लङ्का स्वयमेव प्लवङ्गम
translation:
"O Vanara! I am myself the city of Lanka. O strong one! O courageous one! I am defeated by your 
strength."

shloka: इदम् तु तथ्यम् शृणु वै ब्रुवन्त्य मे हरीश्वर
translation:
"O lord of Vanaras! In earlier times I had been given a boon by Lord Brahma. Hear from me about 
this matter."

shloka: यदा त्वाम् वानरः कश्चिद्विक्रमाद्वशमानयेत्
translation:
"Let this be known by you - whenever a Vanara conquers you with his might, then a fear will come 
for Rakshasas."

shloka: स हि म् समयः सौम्य प्राप्तोऽय तव द्र्शनात्
translation:
"O gentle one! With your appearance now, that time has come for me. Ordinance of Brahma is the 
truth and is immutable."

shloka: सीतानिमित्तंम् राज्ञस्तु रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
translation: "The destruction has come for Ravana the evil minded king and to all Rakshasas due to Seetha."

shloka: तत्प्रविश्य हरिश्रेष्ठम् पुरीम् रावणपालिताम्
translation:
"O best aming Vanaras! For that reason, enter the city of Lanka ruled by Ravana and do here whatever 
tasks you want to."

shloka:
प्रविश्य शापोपहताम् हरीश्वर |
शुभाम् पुरीम् राक्षसराजपालिताम् |
यदृच्छया त्वम् जनकात्मजाम् 
सतीम् |
विमार्ग सर्वत्र गतो यथासुखम्
translation:
"O lord of Vanaras! Enter the auspicious city of Lanka stuck by the curse, ruled by the king of 
Rakshasas, roam everywhere and search for the chaste wife Seetha according to your comfort."

shloka:
स निर्जत्य पुरीम् लण्का श्रेष्ठाम् ताम् कामरूपिणीम् |
विक्रमेण महातेजा हनुमान् कपिसत्तमः
translation:
That Hanuma the best among Vanaras, the great radiant one, the long armed one,
conquered with His might the best Lanka who is capable of assuming desired form. He then leapt over
the city wall at a place that was not a gate.

shloka: प्रविश्य नगरीम् लङ्काम् कपिराजहितम्करः
translation:
Desiring the benefit of the king of Vanaras Sugreeva, that Hanuma entered the city
of Lanka and thus actually placed His left foot on the enemies' heads.

shloka: प्रविष्टः सत्त्वसंपन्नो विशायाम् मारुतात्मजः
translation:
That son of Vayu endowed with great strength, entered the city at night and took the
grand road shone by flowers and pearls. After that Hanuma went towards that beautiful city of
Lanka.

shloka:
हसित उद्घुष्ट निनदैः तूर्य घोष पुरः सरैः |
वज्र अन्कुश निकाशैः च वज्र जाल विभूषितैः
translation:
The beautiful city shone like the sky together with clouds, with its cloud like
houses filled with sounds of laughter and with sounds of musical instruments at the interior, equal
in strength to diamonds and clubs and with windows decorated with diamonds.

shloka: प्रजज्वाल तदा लन्का रक्षः गण गृहैः शुभैः
translation:
Then that city of Lanka shone brilliantly being well decorated by the houses of
Rakshasas. These were modern houses which equalled white clouds, which were surprising with the
shape of lotus and swastika and which were auspicious.

shloka:
ताम् चित्र माल्य आभरणाम् कपि राज हितम् करः |
राघव अर्थम् चरन् श्रीमान् ददर्श च ननन्द च
translation:
That glorious Hanuma, performer of beneficial deeds for Sugreeva the king of
monkeys, moved around the city of Lanka which had wonderful garlands and jewellery, for the sake of
Sri Rama. He saw the city and became happy too.

shloka:
भवनाद्भवनं गच्छ्न् ददर्श पवनात्मजः |
विविधाकृतिरूपाणि भवनानि ततस्ततः
translation:
Going from one building to another, Hanuma saw buildings in various shapes and forms
on every side.

shloka:
शुश्राव मधुरम् गीतम् त्रि स्थान स्वर भूषितम् |
स्त्रीणाम् मद समृद्धानाम् दिवि च अप्सरसाम् इव
translation:
Hanuma heard a sweet song which was decorated by sound from the three svaras -
Mandra, Madhya and Tara of love lorne women like Apsara women in heaven.

shloka:
शुश्राव कान्ची निनदम् नूपुराणाम् च निह्स्वनम् |
सोपान निनदामः चैव भवनेषु महात्मनम्
translation:
Hanuma also heard there and there sound from the tinkling of ornaments worn around
the waist in the houses of wealthy people, sounds of footfall over stair, sound from clapping of
arms by warriors and roar of ogres.

shloka:
आस्फोटित निनादामः च क्ष्वेडितामः च ततः ततः |
शुश्राव जपताम् तत्र मन्त्रन् रक्षोगृहेषु वै
translation:
Hanuma also heard there and there sound from the tinkling of ornaments worn around
the waist in the houses of wealthy people, sounds of footfall over stair, sound from clapping of
arms by warriors and roar of ogres.

shloka:
स्वाध्याय निरतामः चैव यातु धानान् ददर्श सः |
रावण स्तव सम्युक्तान् गर्जतः राक्षसान् अपि
translation:
There Hanuma heard ritual chantings muttered by rakshasas in their houses. He saw
ogres engaged in study of Vedas. He also saw roaring rakshasas who came together to praise
Ravana.

shloka:
राज मार्गम् समावृत्य स्थितम् रक्षः बलम् महत् |
ददर्श मध्यमे गुल्मे राक्षसस्य चरान् बहून्
translation:
He saw many spies of Ravana and a big army of ogres which stood surrounding the
royal highway in the central zone of city.

shloka:
दीक्षितान् जटिलान् मुण्डान् गः अजिन अम्बर वाससः |
दर्भ मुष्टि प्रहरणान् अग्नि कुण्ड आयुधामः तथा
translation:
Hanuma saw those who were initiated into various Vedic practices, those who wore
matted locks on their head, those who had shaven heads, those who wore cow hides and other
clothing, those who were carrying Kusa grass as weapons and also those who had fire vessels as
weapons, those who carried hammers and clubs in their hands and also those who had worn staffs as
weapons, hose who were one-eyed, those who had one ear, hose who were pot-bellied and with hanging
breast, those who had horrible appearances, those with twisted mouths, those who were horrific and
also short people, those who carried bows and arrows those who carried swords, those who carried
pestles and clubs as weapons, those who carried excellent Parighas in their hands, those who shone
with strange armour, those who were not very fat, those who were not too thin, those who were
neither tall nor short, those who were not very fair, those who were not very dark, those who were
not very hunchbacked, those who were not very short, those who had great brilliance, those who
carried banners, those who carried flags and those who carried different weapons.

shloka:
ध्वजीन् पताकिनश्चैव ददर्श विविधायुधान् |
शक्ति वृक्ष आयुधामः चैव पट्टिश अशनि धारिणः
translation:
Hanuma saw many people, who had great might, who carried javelins and trees as
weapons, those who carried Pattisas and thunderbolts, those who carried in their hands sling and
nooses, those who carried flowered garlands, wearing sandal paste and decorated with best
jewellery, those who had various kinds of appearances roaming freely at will, those who carried
sharp spikes and thunderbolts.

shloka:
शत साहस्रम् अव्यग्रम् आरक्षम् मध्यमम् कपिः |
रक्षोधिपतिनिर्दिष्टम् ददर्शान्तःपुराग्रतः || | ५-४-२३
translation:
Hanuma saw at the front of inner city, a hundred thousand central protective force
which was attentive and was positioned there at the command of Ravana.

shloka:
स तदा तद्गृहम् दृष्ट्वा महाहाटकतोरणम् |
राक्षसेन्द्रस्य विख्यातमद्रिमूर्ध्नि प्रतिष्ठितम्
translation:
That Hanuma saw Ravana's house with a golden doorway. That famed house was on the
top of a mountain. Motes filled with white lotuses surrounded it. It was also surrounded by a
compound wall. He watched the house again and again.

shloka:
त्रिविष्टप निभम् दिव्यम् दिव्य नाद विनादितम् |
वाजि हेषित सम्घुष्टम् नादितम् भूषणैः तथा
translation:
The great Hanuma entered secretly Ravana's inner city which was equal to paradise,
rendered noisy by neighing of horses and tinkling of ornaments, by chariots, vehicles and
aerial-cars and decorated by auspicious elephants and horses and great elephants with four tusks
and by birds and animals in heat. It had beautiful entrances and was protected by thousands of
rakshasas with great strength.

shloka:
सहेमजाम्बूनदचक्रवाळम् |
महार्ह मुक्तामणिभूषितान्तम् |
परार्थ्यकालागुरुचन्दनाक्तं |
स रावणान्तःपुरमाविवेश
translation:
Hanuma entered the inner city of Ravana which was filled with gold, which had a
golden court-yard , with a central area decorated by pearls and diamonds of great value and
sprinkled daily with water containing superb algallocum and sandal-wood.

shloka: || इति रामायने सुन्दरकाण्डे चतुर्थः सर्गः ||
translation:
Thus, this is the 4th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic
poem of India.

shloka:
ततः स मध्यंगतमंशुमन्तं |
ज्योत्स्नावितानम् महदुद्वमन्तम् |
ददर्श धीमान् दिवि भानुमन्तम् |
गोष्ठे वृषं मत्तमिव भ्रामन्तम्
translation:
Thereafter that intellectual Hanuma saw the moon in the sky shining with rays,
obtaining the middle portion of sky. Spreading a great quantity of moon shine, moon looked like a
bull in heat among cows.

shloka:
लोकस्य पापानि विनाशयन्तम् |
महोदधिं चापि समेधयन्तम् |
भूतानि सर्वाणि विराजयन्तम् |
ददर्श शीतांशुमथाभियान्तम्
translation:
