After that Hanuma saw the moon coming up destroying the sins of the world, causing
the great ocean to grow and causing all living beings to shine.

shloka:
या भाति लक्ष्मीर्भुवि मन्दरस्था |
तथा प्रदोषेषु च सागरस्था |
तथैव तोयेषु च पुष्करस्था |
रराज सा चारुनिशाकरस्था
translation:
What ever splendour shines over Mount Mandara on earth, on the ocean during
evenings, over the lotuses in the waters, the same splendour shone on the beautiful moon.

shloka:
हंसो यथा राजतपञ्जरसथः |
सिम्हो यथा मन्दरकन्दरस्थः |
वीरो यथा गर्वितकुञ्जरस्थ |
श्चन्द्रो विबभ्राज तथामभरस्थः
translation:
Like a swan in a silver cage, like a lion in the cave of Mount Mandara, like a
warrior on a proud elephant, in the same way the moon shone in the sky.

shloka:
स्थितह् ककुद्मानिव तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो |
महाचलः श्वेत इवोच्चशृङ्गः |
हस्तीव जाम्बूनदबद्धश्^इङ्गो |
रराज चन्द्रह् परिपूर्णशृङ्गः
translation:
The full moon with its horn like spot shone like a sharp horned standing ox with a
high hump, like a great white mountain with tall summits, like an elephant with golden tusks.

shloka:
विनष्टशीताम्बुतुषारपङ्को |
महाग्रहग्राहविनष्टपङ्कः |
प्रकाशलक्ष्म्याश्रयनिर्मलाङ्को |
रराज चन्द्रो भगवान् शशाङ्कः
translation:
The Divine moon who lost the stain of cold water and frost, with lost stain due to
eclipse by the great planet sun, one who has a calm spot which is an abode of brilliant splendour,
with a symbol of hare, shone brilliantly.

shloka:
शीलातलम् प्राप्य यथा मृगेन्द्रो |
महारणम् प्राप्य यथा गजेन्द्रह् |
राज्यम् समासाद्य यथा नरेन्द्र |
स्तथाप्रकाशो विरराज चन्द्रः
translation:
In whatever way a lion obtaining a level surfaced rock (shines), in whatever way
best elephant obtaining a great battle(shines), in whatever way a king obtaining kingdom(shines),
in the same way the clear moon shone.

shloka:
प्रकाशचन्द्रोदयनष्टदोषः |
प्रवृत्तरक्षः पिशिताशदोषः |
रामाभिरामेरितचित्तदोषः |
स्वर्गप्रकाशो भगवान् प्रदोषः
translation:
The Divine evening with lost stain due to rise of shining moon, with the stain due
to meal of flesh eating rakshasas, and in which the bitterness of mind of young women and their
lovers is wiped away, became with a heavenly glow.

shloka:
तन्त्रीस्वनाह् कर्णसुखाः प्रवृत्ताः |
स्वपन्ति नार्यः पतिभिः सुवृत्ताः |
नक्तंचराश्चापि तथा प्रवृत्ता |
विहर्तुमत्यद्भुतरौद्रवृत्ताः
translation:
Musical notes from stringed instruments which were comforting to ears started. Women
with good character were sleeping with husbands and also rakshasas with extremely strange character
started to roam.

shloka:
मत्तप्रमत्तानि समाकुलानि |
तथाश्वभद्रासनसम्कुलानि |
वीरः श्रिया चापि समाकुलानि |
ददर्श धीमान् स कपिः कुलानि
translation:
That Hanuma the courageous one, the intellectual one, saw houses with people in
heat, houses filled with people, full chariots, horses, elephants and best furniture and also full
of wealth.

shloka:
परस्परं चाधिकमाक्षिपन्ति |
भुआंश्च पीनानधिनिक्षिपन्ति |
मत्तप्रलापानधिकम् क्षिपन्ति |
मत्तानि चान्योन्यमधिक्षिपन्ति
translation:
Hanuma saw rakshasas railing a lot at one another moving their heavy shoulders,
throwing wild and incoherent words a lot, insulting one another being intoxicated.

shloka:
रक्षांसि वक्षांसि च विक्षिपन्ति |
गात्राणि कान्तासु च विक्षिपन्ति |
रूपाअणि चित्राणि च विक्षिपन्ति |
दृढानि चापानि च विक्षिपन्ति
translation:
(Hanuma saw) rakshasas who smote breast, those who threw limbs on women, those who
were spreading their strange forms sporting their strong bows.

shloka:
ददर्श कान्ताश्च समालभन्त्य |
स्तथा परास्तत्र पुनः स्वपन्त्यः |
सुरूपवक्त्राश्च तथा हसन्त्यः |
क्रुद्धाः पराश्चपि विनिःश्वसन्त्यः
translation:
Hanuma saw some women applying sandal paste on their bodies and also some other
women sleeping there, in the same way some women with good appearance were smiling, and some other
women were sighing in anger.

shloka:
महागजैश्चापि तथा नदद्भिः |
सुपूजितैश्चापि तथा सुसद्भिः |
रराज वीरैश्च विनिःश्वसद्भि |
र्ह्रदो भुजङ्गैरिव निःश्वसद्भिः
translation:
Hanuma saw (the city of Lanka that) shone with great elephants making sound and also
with gentlemen well respected, shone with warriors in a wresting bout, with long sighs, like
serpents in a lake hissing.

shloka:
बुद्धिप्रधानान् रुचिराभिधानान् |
संश्रद्दधानान् जगतः प्रधानान् |
नानाविधानान् रुचिराभिधानान् |
ददर्श तस्याम् पुरि यातुधानान्
translation:
Hanuma saw Yatudhanaas who were intellectuals, who were good talkers, who had good
devotion, important people to the world, who had various ways, and people who had beautiful names
in that city.

shloka:
ननन्द दृष्ट्वा स च तान् सुरूपा |
न्नानागुणानात्मगुणानुरूपान् |
विद्योतमानान्स तदानुरूपान् |
ददर्श कांश्चिच्च पुनर्विरूपान्
translation:
That Hanuma seeing people with good appearance, who had various good virtues, those
who were according to their character, those who were radiant, all those - became happy. Then that
Hanuma saw those who had horrific appearance, those who were according to their appearance - some
of those too.

shloka:
ततो वरार्हः सुविशुद्धभावा |
स्तेषाम् स्त्रियस्तत्र महानुभावाह् |
प्रियेषु पानेषु च सक्तभावा |
ददर्श ताराइव सुप्रभावाः
translation:
Hanuma saw thereafter there, their women - those who were eligible for distinction,
those who were of great skill with an interested heart in lovers and in drinks and those who were
like stars with good effect.

shloka:
श्रिया ज्वलन्तीस्त्रपयोगूढा |
निशीथकाले रमणोपगूढाः |
ददर्श काश्चित्प्रमदोपगूढा |
यथा विहङ्गाः कुसुमोपगूढाः
translation:
Hanuma saw some women who were brilliant with radiance, adorned a lot with
bashfulness, those who were hugged by lovers in the middle of night, those who were hugged with
great pleasure, those who were hugged by flowers like birds.

shloka:
अन्याः पुनर्हर्म्यतलोपविष्टा |
स्तत्र प्रियाङ्केषु सुखोपविष्टाः |
भर्तुः प्रिया धर्मपरा निविष्टा |
ददर्श धीमान् मदनाभिविष्टाः
translation:
The intellectual Hanuma saw some other women there comfortably sitting on the laps
of their lovers, at the top of their buildings, dear to their husbands and (some other women)
interested in virtuous deeds, and some possessed by the lord of love.

shloka:
अप्रावृताः काञ्चनराजिवर्णाः |
काश्चित्परार्थ्यास्तपनीयवर्णाः |
पुनश्च काश्चिच्छशलक्ष्मवर्णाः |
कान्तप्रहीणारुचिराङ्गवर्णाः
translation:
Hanuma saw women with golden complexion lacking clothes, women with a complexion of
refined gold suitable for mating and some other women also with the colour of moon and some other
women with beautiful bodies lacking a lover.

shloka:
ततह् प्रियान् प्राप्य मनोभिरामान् |
सुप्रीतियुक्ताः सुमनोभिरामाः |
गृहेषु हृष्टाः परमाभिरामाः |
हरिप्रवीरः स ददर्श रामाः
translation:
Thereafter that Vanara warrior saw those with great happiness, those who obtained
lovers who entertained, those who attracted like flowers, those with great beauty and women in
their houses filled with happiness.

shloka:
चन्द्रप्रकाशाश्च हि वक्त्रमाला |
वक्राक्षिपक्ष्माश्च सुनेत्रमालाः |
विभूषाणानाम् च ददर्श मालाः |
शतह्रदानामिव चारुमालाः
translation:
Hanuma saw rows of faces shining like the moon, beautiful rows of eyes with curved
eyebrows and rows of ornaments like beautiful rows of lighting.

shloka:
न त्वेव सीताम् परमाभिजाताम् |
पथि स्थिते राजकुले प्रजाताम् |
लताम् प्रपुल्लामिव साधु जाताम् |
ददर्श तन्वीम् मनसाभिजाताम्
translation:
Hanuma did not see Seetha, one with great beauty born in a royal family following a
virtuous path, well brought up, like a creeper in full blossom, one who was thin, and one who was
born from the mind (of creator).

shloka:
सनातने वर्त्मानि सम्निविष्टाम् |
रामेक्षणां तां मदनाभिविष्टाम् |
भर्तुर्मनः श्रीमदनुप्रविष्टाम् |
स्त्रीभ्यो वराभ्यश्च सदा विशिष्टाम्
translation:
Hanuma did not see that Seetha who stood in the path of ancient righteousness with
Her sight on Sri Rama, who was possessed by the love for Sri Rama, who entered the glorious mind of
husband and always the best among women who were the best.

shloka:
उष्णार्दिताम् सानुसृतास्रकण्ठीम् |
पुरा वरार्होत्तमनिष्ककण्ठीम् |
सुजातपक्ष्मामभिरक्तकण्ठीम् |
वनेऽप्रनृत्तामिव नीलकण्ठीम्
translation:
Hanuma did not see Seetha, tortured by separation from Sri Rama, with unabounding
tears in her throat, in earlier times who had invaluable and best jewellery on her neck, born with
beautiful eyebrows, with a sweet voice, like a she- hen who did not dance in a forest because of
Her current sorrow.

shloka:
अव्यक्तरेखामिव चन्द्ररेखां |
पांसुप्रदिग्धामिव हेमरेखाम् |
क्षतप्ररूढामिव बाणरेखां |
वायुप्रभिन्नामिव मेघरेक्षाम्
translation:
Hanuma did not see Seetha who was like a crescent with a blurred outline, like a
streek of gold coated by dust, like an arrow in an injury, like a series of clouds scattered by
wind.

shloka:
सीतामपश्यन् मनुजेश्वरस्य |
रामस्य पत्नीम् वदताम् वरस्य |
बभूव दुःखाभिहतश्चिरस्य |
प्लवङ्गमो मन्द इवाचिरस्य
translation:
Hanuma became a numb minded one for sometime, stricken with grief not seeing for a
moment Seetha, wife of Sri Rama the best among those who talk, and the lord of all humans.

shloka: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये सुन्दर काण्डे पञ्चमः सर्गः
translation:
Thus, this is the 5th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic
poem of India.

shloka:
स निकामम् विमानेषु विषण्णः काम रूपधृत् |
विचचार पुनर्लङ्काम् लाघवेन समन्वितः
translation:
That Hanuma who could assume any desire form, searching among houses had a lot of
grief. Endowed with great speed, He roamed again the city of Lanka.

shloka:
आससाद अथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षस इन्द्र निवेशनम् |
प्राकारेण अर्क वर्णेन भास्वरेण अभिसम्व्ऱ्तम्
translation:
After that, the glorious Hanuma neared the house of Ravana shining with the golden
hue of Sun, surrounded by a compound wall.

shloka:
रक्षितम् राक्षसैर् भीमैः सिम्हैर् इव महद् वनम् |
समीक्षमाणो भवनम् चकाशे कपि कुन्जरः
translation:
Hanuma shined purveying the building protected by horrible rakshasas, like a forest
by lions.

shloka:
रूप्य कोप हितैः चित्रैः तोरणैर् हेम भूषितैः |
विचित्राभिः च कक्ष्याभिर् द्वारैः च रुचिरैर् व्ऱ्तम्
translation:
Ravana's house consisted of surprising archways decorated with sliver and gold,
strange entrances and beautiful doors.

shloka:
गज आस्थितैर् महा मात्रैः शूरैः च विगत श्रमैः |
उपस्थितम् असम्हार्यैर् हयैः स्यन्दन यायिभिः
translation:
Ravana's house waited upon by men on elephants, warriors, people with removed
tiredness, drivers of elephants, by undefeatable horses, and by charioteers.

shloka:
सिम्ह व्याघ्र तनु त्राणैर् दान्त कान्चन राजतैः |
घोषवद्भिर् विचित्रैः च सदा विचरितम् रथैः
translation:
Hanuma saw Ravana's house with protective shields made of lion and tiger skins,
decorated with ivory, gold and silver, being roamed always by strange chariots with great
sound.

shloka:
बहु रत्न समाकीर्णम् पर अर्ध्य आसन भाजनम् |
महा रथ समावासम् महा रथ महा आसनम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Ravana's house filled with a lot of diamonds, having valuable seats and
utensils, abode of great warriors, with great chariots and great utensils.

shloka:
दृश्यैः च परम उदारैः तैः तैः च मृग पक्षिभिः |
विविधैर् बहु साहस्रैः परिपूर्णम् समन्ततः
translation:
Filled all around with those and those various kinds of animals and birds in
thousands, lovely to watch - very beautiful ones.

shloka:
विनीतैर् अन्त पालैः च रक्षोभिः च सुरक्षितम् |
मुख्याभिः च वर स्त्रीभिः परिपूर्णम् समन्ततः
translation:
Well protected by well trained rakshasas, protecting the inner area, filled all over
by best women who were important.

shloka:
मुदित प्रमदा रत्नम् राक्षस इन्द्र निवेशनम् |
वर आभरण निर्ह्रादैः समुद्र स्वन निह्स्वनम्
translation:
Having happy women, the abode of Ravana with the tinkling of best jewellery had a
sound like that of an ocean.

shloka:
तद् राज गुण सम्पन्नम् मुख्यैः च वर चन्दनैः |
भेरी म्ऱ्दन्ग अभिरुतम् शन्ख घोष विनादितम्
translation:
Together with royal insignia, with best scents and sandal wood, spread with great
number of people like a great forest with lions.

shloka:
भेरीमृदङ्गाभिरुतम् शङ्खघोषनिनादितम् |
नित्य अर्चितम् पर्व हुतम् पूजितम् राक्षसैः सदा
translation:
Resounded by bheris and mridagas, resounded by the sound of conch-shells, prayed
upon daily by Rakshsas, with rituals on festivals, always worshipped by rakshasas.

shloka:
समुद्रम् इव गम्भीरम् समुद्रम् इव निह्स्वनम् |
महात्मानो महद् वेश्म महा रत्न परिच्चदम्
translation:
The great Hanuma saw the wealthy Ravana's huge house, inscrutable like an ocean,
like a noiseless ocean, with a roof embedded with great diamondsand filled with great diamonds.

shloka: विराजमानम् वपुषा गज अश्व रथ सम्कुलम्
translation:
That great Hanuma thought the house, which was shining with its form filled with
elephants, horses, chariots, to be the jewel of Lanka. Hanuma walked about there in the near-hood
of Ravana.

shloka:
गृहाद् गृहम् राक्षसानाम् उद्यानानि च वानरः |
वीक्षमाणो हि असम्त्रस्तः प्रासादामः च चचार सः
translation:
That Hanuma moved about from one house to another of Rakshasas and also parks and
observing in all directions without fear and also courtyards.

shloka:
अवप्लुत्य महा वेगः प्रहस्तस्य निवेशनम् |
ततो अन्यत् पुप्लुवे वेश्म महा पार्श्वस्य वीर्यवान्
translation:
Hanuma with great prowess, and one with great speed, jumped for the house of
Prahasta and from there leapt for another house that of Mahaparshva.

shloka:
अथ मेघ प्रतीकाशम् कुम्भ कर्ण निवेशनम् |
विभीषणस्य च तथा पुप्लुवे स महा कपिः
translation:
Thereafter the great Hanuma leapt for the house of Kumbhakarna which resembled a
cloud and in the same way for the house of Vibhishana.

shloka:
महा उदरस्य च तथा विरूप अक्षस्य चैव हि |
विद्युज् जिह्वस्य भवनम् विद्युन् मालेः तथैव च
translation:
That great Hanuma in the same way leapt for the house of Mahodara and also that of
Virupaaksha, that of Viddutjihva.

shloka:
शुकस्य च महा वेगः सारणस्य च धीमतः |
तथा च इन्द्रजितो वेश्म जगाम हरि यूथपः
translation:
Hanuma the commander of Vanara army with great radiance went for the intellectual
Suka's house, for Sarana's house, and in the same way for the house of Indrajit.

shloka: जम्बु मालेः सुमालेः च जगाम हरि यूथपः
translation:
The best among Vanaras Hanuma went for the house of Jambumali and for the house of
Sumali. The great Hanuma jumped for the house Rasmiketu and in the same way for the house of
Suryaketu and in that way for the building of Vajrakaaya.

shloka:
धूम्र अक्षस्य च सम्पातेर् भवनम् मारुत आत्मजः |
विद्युद् रूपस्य भीमस्य घनस्य विघनस्य च
translation:
Hanuma jumped for Dhumrah's house, for Sampati's house, for Vidhudrupa's, Bhiima's
house, for Ghana's house and Vighana's house, for Sukhana's house, for Vakra's, for Satha's house
and also for Vikata's house, for Brahmakarna's house, for Damshra's house, for Roma's house, for
Raksha's house, for Ydhonmata's and Indrajihva's house, in the same way for Hastimukas house, for
Karala's house, for Pisacha's house, and also for the building of Shonita.

shloka: क्रममाणः क्रमेण एव हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
translation:
The son of Vayu, one with great fame, great one among Vanaras , moving about in a
sequence in those and those best buildings, saw the wealth of those rakshasas, who were rich.

shloka:
सर्वेषाम् समतिक्रम्य भवनानि समन्ततः |
आससाद अथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षस इन्द्र निवेशनम्
translation:
The glorious Hanuma passing everyone's houses all round, there-after neared the
house of Ravana.

shloka:
रावणस्य उपशायिन्यो ददर्श हरि सत्तमः |
विचरन् हरि शार्दूलो राक्षसीर् विकृत ईक्षणाः
translation:
Hanuma best among Vanaras, tiger among Vanaras, moving about saw Rakshas women,
those who were sleeping near to Ravana, those who had horrific eyes, those who had Sulaas, Mudgaras
in their hands, those who had Shaktis and Tomaras.

shloka:
ददर्श विविधान् गुल्मामः तस्य रक्षः पतेर् गृहे |
राक्षसांश्च महाकायान्नानाप्रहरणोद्यतान्
translation:
Hanuma saw in that house of Ravana a variety of army divisions and also Rakshasas
those who had huge bodies having different weapons raise up.

shloka: रक्तान् श्वेतान् सितामः चैव हरीमः चैव महा जवान्
translation:
That Hanuma in that house saw horses in red colour and in white colour, slightly
whitish, capable of great speed, elephants born in a good breed having good appearance capable of
harassing enemy's elephants, skilled in good elephant training, equalling Iraavata, capable of
killing enemies armies in war, rutting like raining clouds, like mountains with water falls that
are pouring down, with trumpeting resembling thundering of clouds, unassailable by enemies in a
battle.

shloka: सहस्रम् वाहिनीः तत्र जाम्बूनद परिष्कृताः
translation:
There Hanuma saw in the house of Ravana, the king of rakshasas, army divisions in
thousands decorated with gold, covered with heaps of gold, equalling the Sun who has fully come
up.

shloka:
शिबिका विविध आकाराः स कपिर् मारुत आत्मजः |
लता गृहाणि चित्राणि चित्र शाला गृहाणि च
translation:
That Hanuma the son of Vayu saw in the house of Ravana the king of rakshasas,
palanquins of various shapes, wonderful bowers, art galleries and other pleasure houses which were
constructed with wooden mountains, house for sexual delight and a beautiful diurnal house.

shloka: स मन्दर तल प्रख्यम् मयूर स्थान सम्कुलम्
translation:
That Hanuma saw the best among buildings equalling mount Mandara filled with pens
for peacocks, spread by flag staffs managed by courageous ones like the house of Kubera filled with
many diamonds and also heaps of riches.

shloka: अर्चिर्भिः च अपि रत्नानाम् तेजसा रावणस्य च
translation:
That building shone by the rays of diamonds, by the splendour of Ravana like the Sun
by rays.

shloka: जाम्बू नदमयानि एव शयनानि आसनानि च
translation:
Hanuma leader of Vanaras saw couches and seats and chief vessels all made with
gold.

shloka: मध्व् आसव कृत क्लेदम् मणि भाजन सम्कुलम्
translation:
Hanuma entered the big house moistened by liquor made of honey, filled with vessels
made of gems delightful one, un-congested one like the building of Kubera resounded by the sound of
tinkles by the sound of waist ornaments, by the sound of percussion on Mrudangas with deep sound,
which consisted of many mansions filled with hundreds of best women, encircled by many spacious
enclosures.

shloka: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये सुन्दर काण्डे षष्ठः सर्गः
translation:
Thus, this is the 6th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic
poem of India.

shloka:
स वेश्म जालम् बलवान् ददर्श |
व्यासक्त वैदूर्य सुवर्ण जालम् |
यथा महत् प्राव्ऱ्षि मेघ जालम् |
विद्युत् पिनद्धम् सविहम्ग जालम्
translation:
That Hanuma, the strong one, saw a group of houses with windows in golden hue,
embedded with cat's-eye gems, like a great group of clouds in rainy season with lighting, together
with a group of birds.

shloka:
निवेशनानाम् विविधाः च शालाः |
प्रधान शन्ख आयुध चाप शालाः |
मनो हराः च अपि पुनर् विशाला |
ददर्श वेश्म अद्रिषु चन्द्र शालाः
translation:
Hanuma saw various halls of the houses, important buildings storing conches, bows,
and other weapons, and also heartening spacious attics at the top of mountain- like houses.

shloka:
गृहाणि नाना वसु राजितानि |
देव असुरैः च अपि सुपूजितानि |
सर्वैः च दोषैः परिवर्जितानि |
कपिर् ददर्श स्व बल अर्जितानि
translation:
Hanuma saw houses glittered by various riches, well worshipped by Devas and Asuras,
devoid of all flaws and obtained by the self-might of rakshasas.

shloka:
तानि प्रयत्न अभिसमाहितानि |
मयेन साक्षाद् इव निर्मितानि |
मही तले सर्व गुण उत्तराणि |
ददर्श लन्का अधिपतेर् ग्ऱ्हाणि
translation:
Hanuma saw those houses of the ruler of Lanka, constructed by great effort as though
constructed by Mayaa himself on earth with all best qualities.

shloka:
ततो ददर्श उच्च्रित मेघ रूपम् |
मनो हरम् कान्चन चारु रूपम् |
रक्षो अधिपस्य आत्म बल अनुरूपम् |
गृह उत्तमम् हि अप्रतिरूप रूपम्
translation:
Thereafter Hanuma saw the best house of the lord of rakshasas, having the appearance
of a cloud, soul-captivating one having a beautiful form made of gold which has no comparison,
suitable of Ravana's might

shloka:
मही तले स्वर्गम् इव प्रकीर्णम् |
श्रिया ज्वलन्तम् बहु रत्न कीर्णम् |
नाना तरूणाम् कुसुम अवकीर्णम् |
गिरेर् इव अग्रम् रजसा अवकीर्णम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Ravana's house like heaven thrown upon earth, effulgent with glory,
embedded with variety of diamonds covered by flowers of various trees, like the summit of a
mountain covered by pollen.

shloka:
नारी प्रवेकैर् इव दीप्यमानम् |
तडिद्भिर् अम्भोदवद् अर्च्यमानम् |
हंस प्रवेकैर् इव वाह्यमानम् |
श्रिया युतम् खे सुक्ऱ्ताम् विमानम्
translation:
Being shone by the best among women like a cloud by lightening, being worshipped,
like being carried by the best swans, like an aerial car full of splendor, of good people in
sky.

shloka:
यथा नग अग्रम् बहु धातु चित्रम् |
यथा नभः च ग्रह चन्द्र चित्रम् |
ददर्श युक्ती कृत मेघ चित्रम् |
विमान रत्नम् बहु रत्न चित्रम्
translation:
Hanuma saw the best house like a beautiful cloud endowed with many hues, like the
sky illumined by planets including the moon, decked with numerous precious stones like a mountain
peak, looking picturesque with numerous minerals.

shloka:
मही कृता पर्वत राजि पूर्णा |
शैलाः कृता वृक्ष वितान पूर्णाः |
वृक्षाः क्ऱ्ताः पुष्प वितान पूर्णाः |
पुष्पम् क्ऱ्तम् केसर पत्र पूर्णम्
translation:
The earth was made to be full of mountain ranges. The mountains were made to be
abounded of trees. The trees were made to be full of flowers. The flower was made to be full of
filaments and petals.

shloka:
कृतानि वेश्मानि च पाण्डुराणि |
तथा सुपुष्पा अपि पुष्करिण्यः |
पुनः च पद्मानि सकेसराणि |
धन्यानि चित्राणि तथा वनानि
translation:
White mansions were also built in the same way. Lakes also with beautiful flowers
and also lotuses together with filaments and forest that were the best and wonderful.

shloka:
पुष्प आह्वयम् नाम विराजमानम् |
रत्न प्रभाभिः च विवर्धमानम् |
वेश्म उत्तमानाम् अपि च उच्च मानम् |
महा कपिः तत्र महा विमानम्
translation:
There the great Hanuma saw a great aerial car, the best among best of aerial cars,
shining with the name of Pushpaka with the rays of precious stones, and capable of traveling long
distances.

shloka:
कृताः च वैदूर्यमया विहम्गा |
रूप्य प्रवालैः च तथा विहम्गाः |
चित्राः च नाना वसुभिर् भुजम्गा |
जात्या अनुरूपाः तुरगाः शुभ अन्गाः
translation:
Artificial birds made of cat's-eye gems, as well as birds made of silver and coral,
wonderful serpants made of various jewels, horses of beautiful limbs suitable by their noble breed
were arranged.

shloka:
प्रवाल जाम्बूनद पुष्प पक्षाः |
सलीलम् आवर्जित जिह्म पक्षाः |
कामस्य साक्षाद् इव भान्ति पक्षाः |
कृता विहम्गाः सुमुखाः सुपक्षाः
translation:
Birds were made with corals on their wings and ogether with golden flowers, with
good wings, with curved and bent wings in a playful way, shining like helpers of the god of love
himself

shloka:
नियुज्यमानाः च गजाः सुहस्ताः |
सकेसराः च उत्पल पत्र हस्ताः |
बभूव देवी च कृता सुहस्ता |
लक्ष्मीः तथा पद्मिनि पद्म हस्ता
translation:
Images of elephants in a lotus-pool with filaments of lotus on body, with lotus
petals held in their trunks, were devoted to the worship of an image of Goddess Lakshmi. And also
an image of Goddess Lakshmi with four graceful hands and holding lotus in Her hand was made to
exist in Pushpaka.

shloka:
इति इव तद् ग्ऱ्हम् अभिगम्य शोभनम् |
सविस्मयो नगम् इव चारु शोभनम् |
पुनः च तत् परम सुगन्धि सुन्दरम् |
हिम अत्यये नगम् इव चारु कन्दरम्
translation:
In this fashion, nearing that house which was shining like a mountain with a
beautiful glow that house with great sweet fragrance like a beautiful mountain during spring, with
beautiful cave became surprised and saw (again).

shloka:
ततः स ताम् कपिर् अभिपत्य पूजिताम् |
चरन् पुरीम् दश मुख बाहु पालिताम् |
अदृश्य ताम् जनक सुताम् सुपूजिताम् |
सुदुह्खिताम् पति गुण वेग निर्जिताम्
translation:
Thereafter that Hanuma nearing that city of Lanka worshipped by Rakshasas, ruled by
arms of ten-headed Ravana, moving thereabout became very gloomy on not seeing that Seetha well
worshipped by all and greatly conquered by the virtues of Her husband Sri Rama

shloka:
ततः तदा बहु विध भावित आत्मनः |
कृत आत्मनो जनक सुताम् सुवर्त्मनः |
अपश्यतो अभवद् अतिदुह्खितम् मनः |
सुचक्षुषः प्रविचरतो महात्मनः
translation:
Thereafter then the heart of the great souled Hanuma who contemplated supreme spirit
in many ways with a disciplined mind following righteous path, with good observant eyes, moving
about in the city of Lanka became greatly sorrowful on not seeing Seetha.

shloka: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये सुन्दर काण्डे सप्तमः सर्गः
translation:
Thus, this is the 7th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic
poem of India.

shloka:
स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य संस्थितम् |
महद्विमानम् मणिवज्रचित्रितम् |
प्रतप्तजाम्बूनदजालकृत्रिमम् |
ददर्श वीरः पवनात्मजः कपिः
translation:
That Hanuma the courageous one, the son of Lord Vayu, saw the great aerial plane
standing in the middle of that building with a surprising hue, due to diamonds, and gems decorated
by series of refined gold.

shloka:
तदप्रमेयाप्रतिकारकृत्रिमम् |
कृतम् स्वयम् साध्विति विश्वकर्मणाः |
दिवम् गतम् वायुपथप्रतिष्ठितम् |
व्यराजतादित्यपथस्य लक्ष्मिवत्
translation:
That plane shone like symbol for solar path standing in the aerial path obtaining
the sky. Manufactured by Vishvakarma himself and praised by him as one without comparison in
beauty.

shloka:
न तत्र किंचिन्न कृतम् प्रयत्नतो |
न तत्र किंचिन्न महर्हरत्नवत् |
न ते विशेषा नियताः सुरेष्वपि |
न तत्र किंचिन्न महाविशेषवत्
translation:
In that plane there is not even a small thing that is not made with great effort, in
that there is nothing without the best diamonds, those characteristics definitely are not in Devas
also, in that there is nothing that is not of great significance.

shloka:
तपह्समाधानपराक्रमार्जितम् |
मनःसमाधानविचारचारिणम् |
अनेकसंस्थानविषेषनिर्मितम् |
ततस्ततस्तुल्यविशेषदर्शनम्
translation:
One that has been obtained by austerities and by prowess, one that moves about by
thoughts of concentrated mind, made from various significant parts with an appearance of parts of
equal significance, collected from here and there from all over the world.

shloka:
विशेषमालम्ब्य विशेषसंस्थितम् |
विचित्रकूटम् बहुकूटमण्डितम् |
मनोऽभिरामम् शरद्न्दुनिर्मलम् |
विचित्रकूटम् शिखरम् गिरेर्यथा
translation:
Obtaining a special construction as a special object, like a mountain with wonderful
peaks adorned by many peaks, attractive to soul, calm like an autumnal moon, like the peak of a
mountain with other wonderful small peaks.

shloka:
वहन्ति यम् कुण्डशोभितानना |
महाशना व्योमचरा निशाचराः |
विवृत्तविध्वस्तविशाललोचना |
महाजवा भूतगणाः सहस्रशः
translation:
Hanuma saw that aerial plane which rakshasas who were great eaters, with a face
beautified by earnings, who roamed around in the sky and thousands of genii with round eyes,
crooked eyes and wide eyes capable of great speed carrying it.

shloka:
वसन्तपुष्पोत्करचारुदर्शनम् |
वसन्तमासदपि कान्तदर्शनम् |
स पुष्पकम् तत्र विमानमुत्तमम् |
ददर्श तद्वानरवीरसत्तमः
translation:
That Hanuma the best among Vanara warriors saw there a best plane with the name of
Pushpaka with a more beautiful appearance than a group of flowers during spring, a more attractive
appearance than even the spring season.

shloka: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये सुन्दर काण्डे अष्टमः सर्गः
translation:
Thus, this is the 8th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic
poem of India.

shloka:
तस्य आलय वरिष्ठस्य मध्ये विपुलम् आयतम् |
ददर्श भवन श्रेष्ठम् हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
translation:
Hanuma, the son of Vayu, saw a best tall building and a wide one in the middle of
that best group of houses.

shloka:
अर्ध योजन विस्तीर्णम् आयतम् योजनम् हि तत् |
भवनम् राक्षस इन्द्रस्य बहु प्रासाद सम्कुलम्
translation:
That building of Ravana filled with many edifices was half a Yojana long and one
Yojana tall.

shloka:
मार्गमाणः तु वैदेहीम् सीताम् आयत लोचनाम् |
सर्वतः परिचक्राम हनूमान् अरि सूदनः
translation:
Hanuma, the destructor of enemies, moved around in all directions searching for
Seetha the wide eyed daughter of King of Videha

shloka:
उत्तमम् राक्षसावासम् हनुमानवलोकयन् |
आससादाथ लक्ष्मीवान् राक्षसेन्द्रनिवेशनम्
translation:
Thereafter, Hanuma the glorious one neared and observed the best residence of
Rakshasas and the house of Ravana, containing elephants with four tusks and also those with three
tusks, those with two tusks and still not crowded. It was protected by soldiers bearing raised
weapons.

shloka:
राक्षसीभिः च पत्नीभी रावणस्य निवेशनम् |
आह्ऱ्ताभिः च विक्रम्य राज कन्याभिर् आव्ऱ्तम्
translation:
That building surrounded by the wives of Ravana, by demonesses, and princesses
brought by strength, was like an ocean filled with crocodiles, big fishes, sharks and other fishes,
moved by the speed of wind, and together with serpants.

shloka:
या हि वैश्वरणे लक्ष्मीर् या च इन्द्रे हरि वाहने |
सा रावण ग्ऱ्हे सर्वा नित्यम् एव अनपायिनी
translation:
Whatever wealth is at Kubera, whatever riches at Indra with green horses, all that
affluence was at Ravana's house. That wealth was always without reduction.

shloka:
या च राज्ञः कुबेरस्य यमस्य वरुणस्य च |
ताद्ऱ्शी तद् विशिष्टा वा ऱ्द्धी रक्षो ग्ऱ्हेष्व् इह
translation:
Whatever was the fortune of Kubera the King of Yakshas, of Yama and of Varuna, the
same fortune or even greater treasure was at this house of Ravana.

shloka:
तस्य हर्म्यस्य मध्यस्थम् वेश्म च अन्यत् सुनिर्मितम् |
बहुनिर्यूह सम्कीर्णम् ददर्श पवन आत्मजः
translation:
Hanuma saw another house in the middle of that house, a well built one consisting of
many elephants in rut.

shloka:
ब्रह्मणो अर्थे क्ऱ्तम् दिव्यम् दिवि यद् विश्व कर्मणा |
विमानम् पुष्पकम् नाम सर्व रत्न विभूषितम्
translation:
Whatever wonderful aeroplane by the name of Pushpaka, decorated with all kinds of
precious stones, made by Visvakarma in heaven for lord Brahma, whatever plane Kubera obtained by
great austerity from Lord Brahma, Ravana obtained that plane by prowess defeating Kubera.

shloka:
ईहा म्ऱ्ग समायुक्तैः कार्य स्वर हिरण्मयैः |
सुक्ऱ्तैर् आचितम् स्तम्भैः प्रदीप्तम् इव च श्रिया
translation:
Supported by pillars decorated with images of wolves, with silver and golden hue and
which were well made, radiant with splendour, decorated all around with rooms equalling Mount Meru
and Mount Mandara, as though touching the sky with an auspicious shape.

shloka:
ज्वलन अर्क प्रतीकाशम् सुक्ऱ्तम् विश्व कर्मणा |
हेम सोपान सम्युक्तम् चारु प्रवर वेदिकम्
translation:
Well made by Visvakarma and resembling Fire and Sun in splendour, with stairways
made of gold and with beautiful and best platforms;

shloka:
जाल वात अयनैर् युक्तम् कान्चनैः स्थाटिकैर् अपि |
इन्द्र नील महा नील मणि प्रवरवेदिकम्
translation:
With windows and ventilation holes made of gold and also made of crystal, with
platforms made of sapphires and emeralds;

shloka:
विद्रुमेण विचित्रेण मणिभिश्च महाधनैः |
विस्तुलाभिश्च मुक्ताभिस्तलेनाभिविराजितम्
translation:
Shone by floors embellished with corals of strange hue and with precious stones of
great value, with pearls without comparison;

shloka:
चन्दनेन च रक्तेन तपनीयनिभेन च |
सुपुण्यगन्धिना युक्तमादित्यतरुणोपमम्
translation:
Reddish and resembling gold, together with sandal wood having a good smell and
brilliant like the Sun at noon;

shloka:
कूटागारैर्वराकारैर्विविधैः समलम्कृतम् |
विमानम् पुष्पकम् दिव्यम् आरुरोह महा कपिः
translation:
The great Hanuma alighted the best aeroplane called Pushpaka with an excellent form
decorated by rows of upper floors.

shloka:
तत्रस्थः स तदा गन्धम् पान भक्ष्य अन्न सम्भवम् |
दिव्यम् सम्मूर्चितम् जिघ्रन् रूपवन्तम् इव अनिलम्
translation:
That Hanuma then being there, smelled a wonderful sweet fragrance like wind with an
appearance, created from drinks and foods, including cooked rice diffused on all sides.

shloka:
स गन्धः तम् महा सत्त्वम् बन्धुर् बन्धुम् इव उत्तमम् |
इत एहि इति उवाच इव तत्र यत्र स रावणः
translation:
That sweet smell was as though saying thus to that Hanuma : "Come here!", like a
relative to a best relative pointing to there wherever that Ravana was.

shloka:
ततः ताम् प्रस्थितः शालाम् ददर्श महतीम् शुभाम् |
रावणस्य मनः कान्ताम् कान्ताम् इव वर स्त्रियम्
translation:
Hanuma started thereafter there (in that direction) and saw an auspicious great
hall, close to heart of Ravana, like a delightful best woman.

shloka:
मणि सोपान विक्ऱ्ताम् हेम जाल विराजिताम् |
स्फाटिकैर् आव्ऱ्त तलाम् दन्त अन्तरित रूपिकाम्
translation:
That hall was made of stairways embedded with diamonds, decorated with golden
windows, with a floor embellished with crystal, with shapes made from ivory in the middle.

shloka:
मुक्ताभिः च प्रवालैः च रूप्य चामी करैर् अपि |
विभूषिताम् मणि स्तम्भैः सुबहु स्तम्भ भूषिताम्
translation:
Well decorated with pearls, corals and also with silver and gold and with diamond
studded pillars and also decorated with many pillars.

shloka:
नम्रैरृजुभिरत्युच्चैः समन्तात्सुविभूषितैः |
स्तम्भैः पक्षैर् इव अत्युच्चैर् दिवम् सम्प्रस्थिताम् इव
translation:
By pillars slightly bent with no distortion, which were very tall and well decorated
all over, that hall was as though starting for sky with very high wings.

shloka:
महत्या कुथय आस्त्रीणम् प्ऱ्थिवी लक्षण अन्कया |
पृथिवीम् इव विस्तीर्णाम् सराष्ट्र ग्ऱ्ह मालिनीम्
translation:
Covered by a wonderful large carpet with all earth's characteristics like rivers,
mountains, oceans, forests, painted over, that hall was like the vast earth together with states
and rows of houses.

shloka:
नादिताम् मत्त विहगैर् दिव्य गन्ध अधिवासिताम् |
पर अर्ध्य आस्तरण उपेताम् रक्षो अधिप निषेविताम्
translation:
It was resounded by birds in heat, made fragrant by excellent perfumes, hung with
best tapestries and inhabited by the king of rakshasas

shloka:
धूम्राम् अगरु धूपेन विमलाम् हंस पाण्डुराम् |
चित्राम् पुष्प उपहारेण कल्माषीम् इव सुप्रभाम्
translation:
It was made smokey by the fumes of agallocum. It was a pure one white like a swan,
wonderful by the decoration of flowers, like divine cow with a great radiance.

shloka:
मनः सम्ह्लाद जननीम् वर्णस्य अपि प्रसादिनीम् |
ताम् शोक नाशिनीम् दिव्याम् श्रियः सम्जननीम् इव
translation:
That excellent hall was causing happiness to heart, causing a fair complexion,
destroying sorrow and was as though producing prosperity.

shloka:
इन्द्रियाणि इन्द्रिय अर्थैः तु पन्च पन्चभिर् उत्तमैः |
तर्पयाम् आस माता इव तदा रावण पालिता
translation:
Like a mother, then that hall governed by Ravana caused satisfaction to all five
sensory organs with all the excellent five objects of the senses.

shloka:
स्वर्गो अयम् देव लोको अयम् इन्द्रस्य इयम् पुरी भवेत् |
सिद्धिर् वा इयम् परा हि स्याद् इति अमन्यत मारुतिः
translation:
Hanuma thought thus : "This is heaven! This is indeed the abode of Devas! This is a
city of Indra. This might be the result of a great austerity."

shloka:
प्रध्यायत इव अपश्यत् प्रदीपामः तत्र कान्चनान् (ःइअतुस्!)|
धूर्तान् इव महा धूर्तैर् देवनेन पराजितान्
translation:
Like gamblers defeated by greater gamblers in gambling, Hanuma saw golden hued lamps
being still, as though in thought.

shloka:
दीपानाम् च प्रकाशेन तेजसा रावणस्य च |
अर्चिर्भिर् भूषणानाम् च प्रदीप्ता इति अभ्यमन्यत
translation:
Hanuma thought thus : "This building shines by the light of lamps and the brilliance
of Ravana and also due to the radiance of jewellery."

shloka:
ततो अपश्यत् कुथा आसीनम् नाना वर्ण अम्बर स्रजम् |
सहस्रम् वर नारीणाम् नाना वेष विभूषितम्
translation:
Thereafter Hanuma saw a thousand of best women sitting on the rug with clothing of
various colours and decorated in a variety of ways.

shloka:
परिव्ऱ्त्ते अर्ध रात्रे तु पान निद्रा वशम् गतम् |
क्रीडित्वा उपरतम् रात्रौ सुष्वाप बलवत् तदा
translation:
Then at the turn of midnight, those women slept deeply resting after playing during
night, with a deep sleep caused by liquor.

shloka:
तत् प्रसुप्तम् विरुरुचे निह्शब्द अन्तर भूषणम् |
निह्शब्द हंस भ्रमरम् यथा पद्म वनम् महत्
translation:
That sleeping group of women, adorned with jewels which were not making sound, shone
like a great park of lotuses with calm swans and bees.

shloka:
तासाम् सम्व्ऱ्त दन्तानि मीलित अक्षाणि मारुतिः |
अपश्यत् पद्म गन्धीनि वदनानि सुयोषिताम्
translation:
Hanuma saw faces of those best women, with teeth covered by lips with closed eyes
and with lotus fragrance.

shloka:
प्रबुद्धानि इव पद्मानि तासाम् भूत्वा क्षपा क्षये |
पुनः सम्व्ऱ्त पत्राणि रात्राव् इव बभुः तदा
translation:
At that time, those faces shone which became like lotuses in blossom during day time
and again were like lotuses with closed petals at night.

shloka:
इमानि मुख पद्मानि नियतम् मत्त षट्पदाः |
अम्बुजानि इव फुल्लानि प्रार्थयन्ति पुनः पुनः
translation:
Hanuma thought that drunk bees definitely are desiring again and again these lotus
faces like lotuses in blossom.

shloka:
इति वा अमन्यत श्रीमान् उपपत्त्या महा कपिः |
मेने हि गुणतः तानि समानि सलिल उद्भवैः
translation:
The glorious great Hanuma thought as above by recourse to reason. He also thought
thus "Those faces equal lotuses by their qualities such as beauty, fragrance, and others".

shloka:
सा तस्य शुशुभे शाला ताभिः स्त्रीभिर् विराजिता |
शारदी इव प्रसन्ना द्यौः ताराभिर् अभिशोभिता
translation:
That hall of Ravana's being shone by those women, glittered like a calm cloudless
sky in autumn shone by stars.

shloka:
स च ताभिः परिव्ऱ्तः शुशुभे राक्षस अधिपः |
यथा हि उडु पतिः श्रीमामः ताराभिर् अभिसम्व्ऱ्तः
translation:
That lord of Rakshasas surrounded by those women shone like the radiant moon
surrounded by stars.

shloka:
याः च्यवन्ते अम्बरात् ताराः पुण्य शेष समाव्ऱ्ताः |
इमाः ताः सम्गताः क्ऱ्त्स्ना इति मेने हरिः तदा
translation:
Then Hanuma thought thus : "Whatever meteors together with residue of piety fall
down from the sky, all those meteors had been together as these women".

shloka:
ताराणाम् इव सुव्यक्तम् महतीनाम् शुभ अर्चिषाम् |
प्रभा वर्ण प्रसादाः च विरेजुः तत्र योषिताम्
translation:
There the luster, complexion and grace of those women clearly resembled great stars
which emitted an auspicious radience.

shloka:
व्याव्ऱ्त्त गुरु पीन स्रक् प्रकीर्ण वर भूषणाः |
पान व्यायाम कालेषु निद्रा अपह्ऱ्त चेतसः
translation:
Those women with dishevelled large thick garlands and scattered excellent jewels
during the time of drinking, dancing etc., were with consciousness stolen by sleep.

shloka:
व्याव्ऱ्त्त तिलकाः काश्चित् काश्चिद् उद्भ्रान्त नूपुराः |
पार्श्वे गलित हाराः च काश्चित् परम योषितः
translation:
Best women with disturbed sacred marks (tilaka) on forehead became with displaced
anklets, became with necklaces fallen off to side.

shloka:
मुखा हार व्ऱ्ताः च अन्याः काश्चित् प्रस्रस्त वाससः |
व्याविद्ध रशना दामाः किशोर्य इव वाहिताः
translation:
Some other women became tied with pearl necklaces, some others became with tied-up
waist ornaments (and) resembled young female horses who had walked long.

shloka:
सुकुण्डल धराः च अन्या विच्चिन्न म्ऱ्दित स्रजः |
गज इन्द्र म्ऱ्दिताः फुल्ला लता इव महा वने
translation:
Some others wearing nice earrings with flower garlands that were torn and disturbed,
resembled creepers, tread upon by an elephant in a big forest.

shloka:
चन्द्र अंशु किरण आभाः च हाराः कासांचिद् उत्कटाः |
हंसा इव बभुः सुप्ताः स्तन मध्येषु योषिताम्
translation:
Big pearl necklaces with the radiance of moon-rays in the middle of breasts of some
other women shone like sleeping swans.

shloka:
अपरासाम् च वैदूर्याः कादम्बा इव पक्षिणः |
हेम सूत्राणि च अन्यासाम् चक्र वाका इव अभवन्
translation:
And of some other women, necklaces made with cat's eye gems resembled birds called
Kadambas and for some others golden chains were like Chakravaka birds.

shloka:
हंस कारण्डव आकीर्णाः चक्र वाक उपशोभिताः |
आपगा इव ता रेजुर् जघनैः पुलिनैर् इव
translation:
Those women with buttocks resembling sand dunes, shone like rivers filled with swans
and birds called Karandas and decorated by Chakravaka birds.

shloka:
किन्किणी जाल सम्काशाः ता हेम विपुल अम्बुजाः |
भाव ग्राहा यशः तीराः सुप्ता नद्य इव आबभुः
translation:
Those sleeping women shone like rivers with their smiles as flower buds, with golden
jewellery as big lotuses, with their behaviours as crocodiles, with fame as banks.

shloka:
मृदुष्व् अन्गेषु कासांचित् कुच अग्रेषु च संस्थिताः |
बभूवुर् भूषणानि इव शुभा भूषण राजयः
translation:
Auspicious lines of decoration which were on smooth parts of some other women and on
nipples, were like jewellery.

shloka:
अंशु कान्ताः च कासांचिन् मुख मारुत कम्पिताः |
उपरि उपरि वक्त्राणाम् व्याधूयन्ते पुनः पुनः
translation:
Edges of clothing (worn by them) disturbed by air from breathing of some other
women, were being fluttered again and again on their faces.

shloka:
ताः पाताका इव उद्धूताः पत्नीनाम् रुचिर प्रभाः |
नाना वर्ण सुवर्णानाम् वक्त्र मूलेषु रेजिरे
translation:
Those edges of clothes with various beautiful colours, shone at the base of Ravana's
wives' throats like hoisted flags of beautiful shine.

shloka:
ववल्गुः च अत्र कासांचित् कुण्डलानि शुभ अर्चिषाम् |
मुख मारुत संसर्गान् मन्दम् मन्दम् सुयोषिताम्
translation:
Here ear-rings of some beautiful women with a good glory, also moved lightly due to
the air from breathing of those women.

shloka:
शर्कर आसव गन्धः स प्रक्ऱ्त्या सुरभिः सुखः |
तासाम् वदन निह्श्वासः सिषेवे रावणम् तदा
translation:
Then comforting breath from the faces of those women, by nature fragrant with the
smell of liquor made of Sarkara, served Ravana.

shloka:
रावण आनन शन्काः च काश्चिद् रावण योषितः |
मुखानि स्म सपत्नीनाम् उपाजिघ्रन् पुनः पुनः
translation:
Some women of Ravana smelled co-wives' faces again and again imagining them to be
face of Ravana.

shloka:
अत्यर्थम् सक्त मनसो रावणे ता वर स्त्रियः |
अस्वतन्त्राः सपत्नीनाम् प्रियम् एव आचरमः तदा
translation:
Those best women with greatly devoted mind in Ravana, then not being on own will,
brought delight only to their co-wives.

shloka:
बाहून् उपनिधाय अन्याः पारिहार्य विभूषिताः |
अंशुकानि च रम्याणि प्रमदाः तत्र शिश्यिरे
translation:
Some other women slept there, making as pillows their arms decorated with bracelets
and beautiful clothes.

shloka:
अन्या वक्षसि च अन्यस्याः तस्याः काचित् पुनर् भुजम् |
अपरा त्व् अन्कम् अन्यस्याः तस्याः च अपि अपरा भुजौ
translation:
Another woman slept on another's bosom, again another woman slept on her shoulder,
another woman slept on another woman's thigh and another slept on her breasts.

shloka:
ऊरु पार्श्व कटी प्ऱ्ष्ठम् अन्योन्यस्य समाश्रिताः |
परस्पर निविष्ट अन्ग्यो मद स्नेह वश अनुगाः
translation:
Overcome with heat and friendship, they resorted to thighs, sides, waist and back of
one another, with mutual limbs placed on one another.

shloka:
अन्योन्यस्य अन्ग संस्पर्शात् प्रीयमाणाः सुमध्यमाः |
एकी क्ऱ्त भुजाः सर्वाः सुषुपुः तत्र योषितः
अन्योन्य भुज सूत्रेण स्त्री माला ग्रथिता हि सा |
माला इव ग्रथिता सूत्रे शुशुभे मत्त षट्पदा
translation:
That garland of women tied with the rope of each other's shoulders shone like a
flower garland with dragon flies on it tied in thread.

shloka:
लतानाम् माधवे मासि फुल्लानाम् वायु सेवनात् |
अन्योन्य माला ग्रथितम् संसक्त कुसुम उच्चयम्
translation:
That group of women of Ravana, tied by each other as garland with mixed group of
flowers, with beautiful shoulders entwined promiscuously, hair like an exalted garden with a flower
garland tied together of creepers in bloom due to the caress of the lord of wind in the vernal in
the month of Vaisakha, with entwined beautiful trees.

shloka:
उचितेष्व् अपि सुव्यक्तम् न तासाम् योषिताम् तदा |
विवेकः शक्य आधातुम् भूषण अन्ग अम्बर स्रजाम्
translation:
Then it was not possible to make clear the knowledge of jewellery, body parts and
clothes of those women even for those used to them.

shloka:
रावणे सुख सम्विष्टे ताः स्त्रियो विविध प्रभाः |
ज्वलन्तः कान्चना दीपाः प्रेक्षन्त अनिमिषा इव
translation:
While Ravana slept comfortably, golden lamps shining brilliant, were as though
seeing without closing eyes, those women of various glows.

shloka:
राज ऱ्षि पित्ऱ् दैत्यानाम् गन्धर्वाणाम् च योषितः |
रक्षसाम् च अभवन् कन्याः तस्य काम वशम् गताः
translation:
Women of royal sages, brahmanas and demons and of Gandharvas, of Rakshasas - all
those unmarried girls surrendered from lust to Ravana.

shloka:
युद्धकामेन ताः सर्वा रावणेन हृताः स्त्रियः |
समदा मदनेनैव मोहिताः काश्चिदागताः
translation:
All those women had been stolen by Ravana with a desire for war, some together with
heat of youth obtained Ravana being desired by god of love.

shloka:
न तत्र काचित् प्रमदा प्रसह्य |
वीर्य उपपन्नेन गुणेन लब्धा |
न च अन्य कामा अपि न च अन्य पूर्वा |
विना वर अर्हाम् जनक आत्मजाम् तु
translation:
There, even one woman had not been obtained forcefully by the strong Ravana, except
for that daughter of Janaka, Seetha. Every other woman had been obtained by her character alone and
there was no woman who had desire in another man, and there also was none with another lover.

shloka:
न च अकुलीना न च हीन रूपा |
न अदक्षिणा न अनुपचार युक्ता |
भार्या अभवत् तस्य न हीन सत्त्वा |
न च अपि कान्तस्य न कामनीया
translation:
And there was no wife of his without a good lineage, there was no one with less
beauty, no one without skill, no one without service, none with low intellect, no one without
causing desire to lover.

shloka:
बभूव बुद्धिः तु हरि ईश्वरस्य |
यदि ईद्ऱ्शी राघव धर्म पत्नी |
इमा यथा राक्षस राज भार्याः |
सुजातम् अस्य इति हि साधु बुद्धेः
translation:
Following thought occurred to Hanuma with a pious mind : "It would have been good
for this Ravana if the virtuous wife of Rama had been left happy with her husband in the same such
manner as these wives of the king of rakshasas."

shloka:
पुनः च सो अचिन्तयद् आर्त रूपो |
ध्रुवम् विशिष्टा गुणतो हि सीता |
अथ अयम् अस्याम् क्ऱ्तवान् महात्मा |
लन्का ईश्वरः कष्टम् अनार्य कर्म
इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये सुन्दर काण्डे नवमः सर्गः
translation:
Thus, this is the 9th chapter in Sundara Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic
poem of India.

shloka:
तत्र दिव्य उपमम् मुख्यम् स्फाटिकम् रत्न भूषितम् |
अवेक्षमाणो हनुमान् ददर्श शयन आसनम्
translation:
In that house, while observing, Hanuma saw a portion of house with beds and couches, consisting 
of best couches equaling those in heaven, made of crystal decorated with diamonds, with wonderful parts made of 
ivory and gold, covered with best beds made of cat's eye gems of great value.

shloka:
तस्य च एकतमे देशे सो अग्र्य माल्य विभूषितम् |
ददर्श पाण्डुरम् चत्रम् तारा अधिपति सम्निभम्
translation:
Hanuma saw in a part of that room, an umbrella white in colour decorated with best flower garlands 
and resembling moon - the lord of stars.

shloka:
जातरूपपरिक्षिप्तम् चित्रभानुसमप्रभम् |
अशोकमालाविततम् ददर्श परमासनम्
translation:
Hanuma saw an excellent couch made of gold with radiance equaling that of fire, spread by garlands 
of Ashoka flowers.

shloka:
वाल व्यजन हस्ताभिर् वीज्यमानम् समन्ततः |
गन्धैः च विविधैर् जुष्टम् वर धूपेन धूपितम्
translation:
Fanned by women with fans in their hands in all the four directions and obtained by various fragrances 
fumigated by the best incense.

shloka:
परम आस्तरण आस्तीर्णम् आविक अजिन सम्व्र्तम् |
दामभिर् वर माल्यानाम् समन्ताद् उपशोभितम्
translation: Covered by an excellent bed, spread by sheep skin everywhere and shone by rows of excellent garlands.

shloka:
तस्मिन् जीमूत सम्काशम् प्रदीप्त उत्तम कुण्डलम् |
लोहित अक्षम् महा बाहुम् महा रजत वाससम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Ravana in that house, equaling a cloud, wearing earrings with a brilliant shine with 
red eyes and with long arms wearing gold clothes.

shloka:
लोहितेन अनुलिप्त अन्गम् चन्दनेन सुगन्धिना |
संध्या रक्तम् इव आकाशे तोयदम् सतडिद् गुणम्
translation:
With his body smeared with red sandal-wood with good fragrance like a cloud in the red sky at sunset, 
together with groups of lightening.

shloka:
वृतम् आभरणैर् दिव्यैः सुरूपम् काम रूपिणम् |
सव्र्क्ष वन गुल्म आढ्यम् प्रसुप्तम् इव मन्दरम्
translation:
Ravana was filled with excellent jewellery, with a good appearance, with an ability to assume desired 
form, resembling mount Mandara in sleep, together with groups of trees and bushes.

shloka:
क्रीडित्वा उपरतम् रात्रौ वर आभरण भूषितम् |
प्रियम् राक्षस कन्यानाम् राक्षसानाम् सुख आवहम्
translation:
Resting after having pleasure at night, bedecked with the best ornaments, he was a lover to the 
rakshasa girls and causing comfort to rakshasas.

shloka:
पीत्वा अपि उपरतम् च अपि ददर्श स महा कपिः |
भास्करे शयने वीरम् प्रसुप्तम् राक्षस अधिपम्
translation: That great Hanuma saw the gallant king of rakshasas in sleep on a shining couch resting after drinking.

shloka:
निह्श्वसन्तम् यथा नागम् रावणम् वानर उत्तमः |
आसाद्य परम उद्विग्नः सो अपासर्पत् सुभीतवत्
translation:
That Hanuma, best among Vanaras neared Ravana, became very gloomy and moved away with great dread, 
as though from a hissing serpent.

shloka:
अथ आरोहणम् आसाद्य वेदिका अन्तरम् आश्रितः |
सुप्तम् राक्षस शार्दूलम् प्रेक्षते स्म महा कपिः
translation: Thereafter the great Hanuma neared staircase, sought another dais and observed closely Ravana.

shloka:
शुशुभे राक्षस इन्द्रस्य स्वपतः शयन उत्तमम् |
गन्ध हस्तिनि सम्विष्टे यथा प्रस्रवणम् महत्
translation:
The excellent couch of the sleeping Ravana shone like a great lake when a scented elephant resides 
in it.

shloka:
कान्चन अन्गद नद्धौ च ददर्श स महात्मनः |
विक्षिप्तौ राक्षस इन्द्रस्य भुजाव् इन्द्र ध्वज 
उपमौ
translation:
That Hanuma also saw the wealthy Ravana's arms tied with golden armlets thrown apart, resembling 
flag staffs raised in honor of Indra.

shloka:
ऐरावत विषाण अग्रैर् आपीडित क्र्त व्रणौ |
वज्र उल्लिखित पीन अंसौ विष्णु चक्र परिक्षितौ
translation:
Those arms had wounds made by stabbing from the pointed edges of tusks of Iraavata and fleshy shoulders 
smeared with diamond and hit by Vishnu chakra.

shloka:
पीनौ समसुजात अंसौ सम्गतौ बल सम्युतौ |
सुलक्षण नख अन्गुष्ठौ स्वन्गुली तल लक्षितौ
translation:
These arms of Ravana were corpulent with well grown and equal strong shoulders proportionate to 
body, with knees and thumbs of good characteristics, with good fingers and palms.

shloka:
सम्हतौ परिघ आकारौ व्र्त्तौ करि कर उपमौ |
विक्षिप्तौ शयने शुभ्रे पन्च शीर्षाव् इव उरगौ
translation:
With strong joints in the shape of club, round in shape resembling the trunks of an elephant, like 
five headed snakes thrown on clean couch.

shloka:
शश क्षतज कल्पेन सुशीतेन सुगन्धिना |
चन्दनेन पर अर्ध्येन स्वनुलिप्तौ स्वलम्क्र्तौ
translation:
Shoulders well smeared by best sandal with good smell and very cool resembling in color to a hare's 
blood, well decorated, massaged by the best women, served by the best sandal and which made yakshas, nagas, gandharvas, 
devas and daanavaas scream.

shloka:
ददर्श स कपिः तस्य बाहू शयन संस्थितौ |
मन्दरस्य अन्तरे सुप्तौ महा अर्ही रुषिताव् इव
translation:
That Hanuma saw there arms on the couch like great serpents in anger sleeping in the middle of 
mount Mandara.

shloka:
ताभ्याम् स परिपूर्णाभ्याम् भुजाभ्याम् राक्षस अधिपः |
शुशुभे अचल सम्काशः श्र्न्गाभ्याम् 
इव मन्दरः
translation:
That king of Rakshasas equaling a mountain with those shoulders, which were well built and shone 
like Mount Mandara with twin peaks.

shloka:
चूत पुम्नाग सुरभिर् बकुल उत्तम सम्युतः |
मृष्ट अन्न रस सम्युक्तः पान गन्ध पुरः सरः
translation:
From the great face of that king of Rakshasas who was sleeping, came out breath with fragrance 
like that of flowers of chuuta and punnaaga, consisting of the best fragrance of Vakula flowers, together with 
the flavor of best cooked rice, with the smell of liquor as though filling that house.

shloka:
मुक्ता मणि विचित्रेण कान्चनेन विराजता |
मुकुटेन अपव्र्त्तेन कुण्डल उज्ज्वलित आननम्
translation:
That Hanuma saw in the house of that king of Rakshasa's, wives at the feet, Ravana being a gigantic 
one with loving wives, shone with crown tilted to the side, having strange hue with pearls and diamonds and of 
golden colour, with a face made brilliant by earrings, shone with the chest region smeared with red sandal, shining 
with a necklace wide, high and corpulent with a silk cloth of white colour falling on him, with eyes reddish like 
blood, well tied by a best cloth of yellow colour and of very best quality, resembling a heap of black beans, 
snoring like a hiss of a snake, like an elephant sleeping in the middle of water belonging to the great river 
Ganga with all the four directions shone by the four lamps of golden colour, resembling a cloud with all the parts 
being shone by groups of lighting.

shloka:
शशि प्रकाश वदना वर कुण्डल भूषिताः |
अम्बाल माल्य आभरणा ददर्श हरि यूथपः
translation:
The leader of Vanaras saw those wives of Ravana with faces with radiance of moon, adorned with 
beautiful earrings, wearing jewellery and flower garlands which were not worn out.

shloka:
नृत्त वादित्र कुशला राक्षस इन्द्र भुज अन्कगाः |
वर आभरण धारिण्यो निषन्ना दद्र्शे कपिः
translation:
Hanuma saw wives of Ravana with skill in dance and musical instruments, who obtained the shoulders 
of Ravana wearing the best jewellery and being in sleep.

shloka:
वज्र वैदूर्य गर्भाणि श्रवण अन्तेषु योषिताम् |
ददर्श तापनीयानि कुण्डलानि अन्गदानि च
translation:
He saw earrings of those women at the end of ears with embedded diamonds and cats eye gems and 
having golden colour.

shloka:
तासाम् चन्द्र उपमैर् वक्त्रैः शुभैर् ललित कुण्डलैः |
विरराज विमानम् तन् नभः तारा गणैर् 
इव
translation:
With the faces of those women with delicate earrings which were equal to moon and auspicious that 
house shone like the sky with clusters of stars.

shloka:
मद व्यायाम खिन्नाः ताः राक्षस इन्द्रस्य योषितः |
तेषु तेष्व् अवकाशेषु प्रसुप्ताः तनु मध्यमाः
translation:
Women of that Ravana being tired from lustful passion and exertion and having lean waists slept 
at first opportunity.

shloka:
अङ्गहारैस्तथैवान्या कोवलैर्नृत्तशालिनी |
विन्यस्तशुभसर्वाङ्गी प्रसुप्ता वरवर्णिनी
translation:
Another woman with skill in dancing consisting of delicate body postures slept in the same way 
with all her body parts making the same dance postures.

shloka:
काचिद् वीणाम् परिष्वज्य प्रसुप्ता सम्प्रकाशते |
महा नदी प्रकीर्णा इव नलिनी पोतम् आश्रिता
translation:
One woman hugging veena and sleeping was shining like a lotus plant thrown away by the flow of 
a great river and resorting a boat.

shloka:
अन्या कक्ष गतेन एव मड्डुकेन असित ईक्षणा |
प्रसुप्ता भामिनी भाति बाल पुत्रा इव वत्सला
translation:
Another woman with black eyes sleeping with an instrument called madduka under arm pit shone like 
a woman carrying an infant boy with love.

shloka:
पटहम् चारु सर्व अन्गी पीड्य शेते शुभ स्तनी |
चिरस्य रमणम् लब्ध्वा परिष्वज्य इव कामिनी
translation:
A woman with beautiful body features and with beautiful breasts slept tightly and hugged instrument 
called pataha as though hugging a lover, getting him after a long time.

shloka:
काचिद् अंशम् परिष्वज्य सुप्ता कमल लोचना |
रहः प्रियतमम् गृह्य सकामेव च कामिनी
translation:
Another woman with lotus like eyes hugging a flute slept like a woman with lust holding her lover 
in secret.

shloka:
विपञ्चैइम् परिगृह्यान्या नियता नृत्तशालिनी |
निद्रा वशम् अनुप्राप्ता सह कान्ता इव भामिनी
translation:
Another woman skilled in dance obtained sleep getting an instrument like veena and being in tune 
with it like a woman together with her lover.

shloka:
अन्या कनक सम्काशैर् म्र्दु पीनैर् मनो रमैः |
मृदन्गम् परिपीड्य अन्गैः प्रसुप्ता मत्त लोचना
translation:
Another woman with lusty eyes slept hugging a percussion instrument called mridanga with her body 
parts which were pleasant which resembled gold and which were smooth and fleshy.

shloka:
भुज पार्श्व अन्तरस्थेन कक्षगेन क्र्श उदरी |
पणवेन सह अनिन्द्या सुप्ता मद क्र्त श्रमा
translation:
Another woman with thin stomach, who was not to be blamed, slept due to tiresomeness from lust 
together with an instrument called Padama between her shoulders and reaching arm pits.

shloka:
डिण्डिमम् परिग्र्ह्य अन्या तथैव आसक्त डिण्डिमा |
प्रसुप्ता तरुणम् वत्सम् उपगूह्य इव भामिनी
translation:
Another woman with an instrument called Dindima near her slept in the same way as a woman hugging 
her husband and also her child.

shloka:
काचिद् आडम्बरम् नारी भुज सम्भोग पीडितम् |
कृत्वा कमल पत्र अक्षी प्रसुप्ता मद मोहिता
translation:
Another woman with eyes like lotus petals slept making the instrument called adambara pressing 
it by her shoulders being desired by lust.

shloka:
कलशीम् अपविद्ध्य अन्या प्रसुप्ता भाति भामिनी |
वसन्ते पुष्प शबला माला इव परिमार्जिता
translation:
Another woman sleeping, felling down a small pot, shone like a flower garland with the flowers 
of strange hue made auspicious in spring.

shloka:
पाणिभ्याम् च कुचौ काचित् सुवर्ण कलश उपमौ |
उपगूह्य अबला सुप्ता निद्रा बल पराजिता
translation: Another woman slept hugging her breasts resembling golden pots by her hands, overcome with sleep.

shloka:
अन्या कमल पत्र अक्षी पूर्ण इन्दु सद्र्श आनना |
अन्याम् आलिन्ग्य सुश्रोणी प्रसुप्ता मद विह्वला
translation:
Another woman with eyes like lotus petals, with her face resembling full moon, overcome with lust 
slept hugging another woman with a beautiful hip region.

shloka:
आतोद्यानि विचित्राणि परिष्वज्य वर स्त्रियः |
निपीड्य च कुचैः सुप्ताः कामिन्यः कामुकान् 
इव
translation:
Some excellent women slept hugging strange instruments and pressing them with breasts as though 
lustful woman with lusty men.

shloka:
तासाम् एक अन्त विन्यस्ते शयानाम् शयने शुभे |
ददर्श रूप सम्पन्नाम् अपराम् स कपिः स्त्रियम्
translation:
That Hanuma saw among those women a very beautiful woman sleeping on an auspicious couch arranged 
alone at a side.

shloka:
मुक्ता मणि समायुक्तैर् भूषणैः सुविभूषिताम् |
विभूषयन्तीम् इव च स्व श्रिया भवन उत्तमम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Mandodari with a beautiful form together with diamonds and pearls, well decorated by 
jewellery and with her self radiance as though decorating that great building with a fair complexion and with 
a radiance like golden colour, who was dear to her husband the lady of women in that gynaeceum sleeping there.

shloka:
स ताम् दृष्ट्वा महा बाहुर् भूषिताम् मारुत आत्मजः |
तर्कयाम् आस सीता इति रूप यौवन सम्पदा
translation:
That Hanuma with great arms seeing the woman well decorated, out of logic thought thus: "This is 
Seetha by the wealth of her appearance and her youth". That warrior of Vanaras was delighted together with great 
pleasure.

shloka:
आश्पोटयाम् आस चुचुम्ब पुच्चम् |
ननन्द चिक्रीड जगौ जगाम|
स्तम्भान् अरोहन् निपपात भूमौ 
|
निदर्शयन् स्वाम् प्रक्र्तिम् कपीनाम्
translation:
He clasped his arms, kissed his tail he was delighted, he was playful, sang, paced showing his 
simian nature, climbed pillars and fell down on land.

shloka:
अवधूय च ताम् बुद्धिम् बभूव अवस्थितः तदा |
जगाम च अपराम् चिन्ताम् सीताम् प्रति महा कपिः
translation:
The great Hanuma then removing that thought became with the right mind and had another thought 
about Seetha.

shloka:
न रामेण वियुक्ता सा स्वप्तुम् अर्हति भामिनी |
न भोक्तुम् न अपि अलम्कर्तुम् न पानम् उपसेवितुम्
translation:
That Seetha is not suitable to sleep separated from Rama, will not eat, will not decorate also, 
not suited to drink a beverage, to reach another man even though if he were Indra because there is indeed no one 
equaling Rama even among gods. This is another woman - thus deciding that Hanuma paced in that banqueting hall.

shloka: क्रीडितेन अपराः क्लान्ता गीतेन च तथा पराः
translation:
Some women were tired from erotic dalliance and then some other women were tired from singing; 
some others were weary from dance and were unconscious from consumption of liquor.

shloka: मुरजेषु म्ऱ्दन्गेषु पीठिकासु च संस्थिताः
translation: Some women were stationed on tabors, on Mrudangas, on seats, some other women rested on chief carpets.

shloka: अङ्गनानाम् सहस्रेण भूषितेन विभूषणैः
translation:
The warrior among Vanaras saw a thousand of women decorated by jewellery with a nature of talking 
about beauty, conversing about the correct meaning of songs being sung, behaving according to time and place, 
wont to speak appropriate words, indulged in sleep after sexual dalliance.

shloka: तासाम् मध्ये महा बाहुः शुशुभे राक्षस ईश्वरः
translation:
In the middle of that group of women, Ravana with great arms shone like a bull in the middle of 
cows in a big cow-pen.

shloka: स राक्षस इन्द्रः शुशुभे ताभिः परिवृतः स्वयम्
translation:
That Ravana himself surrounded by those women, shone like a great elephant surrounded by she elephants 
in a great forest.

shloka: सर्व कामैर् उपेताम् च पान भूमिम् महात्मनः
translation: The best among Vanaras saw in that wealthy Ravana's house a bar also, consisting of all desirables.

shloka: मृगाणाम् महिषाणाम् च वराहाणाम् च भागशः
translation: Hanuma saw there in that bar, meat of dear and of buffalo, of wild boar kept separately.

shloka: रौक्मेषु च विशलेषु भाजनेष्व् अर्ध भक्षितान्
translation: The best among Vanaras saw half eaten peacocks and chicken in wide vessels of golden colour.

shloka: वराह वार्ध्राणसकान् दधि सौवर्चल आयुतान्
translation:
Hanuma observed meat of pigs and goats, porcupines, deer and peacocks preserved in curds and sochal 
salt.

shloka: कृकरान् विविधान् सिद्धामः चकोरान् अर्ध भक्षितान्
translation:
Hanuma saw birds called Krakara cooked ready to be eaten in variety of ways, birds called Chakoras 
half eaten, wild buffalos, fishes called ekashleya, goats, food to be licked of various kinds, beverages and various 
foods.

shloka:
तथा अम्ल लवण उत्तंसैर् विविधै राग षाडवैः |
हार नूपुर केयूरैर् अपविद्धैर् महा धनैः
translation:
In the same way that floor was obtaining glory greatly with Ragas and Shadabas seasoned with sour 
and salty sauces, with necklaces, anklets and armlets of great value thrown around, with various fruits left in 
drinking vessels, with flowers sprinkled.

shloka:
तत्र तत्र च विन्यस्तैः सुश्लिष्टैः शयन आसनैः |
पान भूमिर् विना वह्निम् प्रदीप्ता इव उपलक्ष्यते
translation:
That bar was seen as though radiant without fire, with couches and chairs well arranged and placed 
there and there.

shloka:
बहु प्रकारैर् विविधैर् वर संस्कार संस्कृतैः |
मांसैः कुशल सम्युक्तैः पान भूमि गतैः पृथक्
translation:
Many meats of different kinds cultured with various best seasonings, well arranged separately obtained 
that bar.

shloka:
दिव्याः प्रसन्ना विविधाः सुराः कृत सुरा अपि |
शर्कर आसव माध्वीकाः पुष्प आसव फल आसवाः
translation:
Excellent and clear various liquors, a liquor called Sura, liquor made of sugar, liquor made of 
honey, liquor made of flowers and liquors made of fruits also, artificially made liquors - those and those were 
cultured separately with various fragrant powders.

shloka: सम्तता शुशुभे भूमिर् माल्यैः च बहु संस्थितैः
translation:
The floor shone filled by flower garlands in a variety of forms, with various vessels of golden 
hue and also made of crystal, filled with other small vessels of golden colour.

shloka:
राजतेषु च कुम्भेषु जाम्बूनदमयेषु च |
पान श्रेष्ठम् तदा भूरि कपिः तत्र ददर्श ह
translation: Hanuma saw indeed then lot of best quality liquor in pots of silver and of golden colour.

shloka:
सो अपश्यत् शात कुम्भानि शीधोर् मणिमयानि च |
राजतानि च पूर्णानि भाजनानि महा कपिः
translation:
That great Hanuma saw vessels full of liquor of golden colour, embedded with gem stones and also 
of silver hue.

shloka:
क्वचिद् अर्ध अवशेषाणि क्वचित् पीतानि सर्वशः |
क्वचिन् न एव प्रपीतानि पानानि स ददर्श ह
translation:
That Hanuma saw indeed at some places drinks half filled and at some places completely drunk and 
some places not at all drunk.

shloka:
क्वचिद् भक्ष्यामः च विविधान् क्वचित् पानानि भागशः |
क्वचिद् अन्न अवशेषाणि पश्यन् वै विचचार 
ह
translation:
Hanuma paced about seeing at some places various eatables and at some places drinks separately, 
and at some places remnants of cooked rice.

shloka:
क्वचित् प्रभिन्नैः करकैः क्वचिद् आलोडितैर् घटैः |
क्वचित् सम्पृक्त माल्यानि जलानि च फलानि 
च
translation:
Hanuma saw some places with vessels broken, some places with pots in shambles, some places with 
water together with flower garlands and fruits.

shloka:
शयनानि अत्र नारीणाम् शून्यानि बहुधा पुनः |
परस्परम् समाश्लिष्य काश्चित् सुप्ता वर अन्गनाः
translation: Here couches again of women were varied and clean, some best women slept there hugging one another.

shloka:
काचिच् च वस्त्रम् अन्यस्या अपह्ऱ्त्य उपगुह्य च |
उपगम्य अबला सुप्ता निद्रा बल पराजिता
translation:
Some women conquered by the power of sleep pulled other sleeping women's clothing and slept covering 
themselves.

shloka:
तासाम् उच्च्वास वातेन वस्त्रम् माल्यम् च गात्रजम् |
न अत्यर्थम् स्पन्दते चित्रम् प्राप्य 
मन्दम् इव अनिलम्
translation:
Clothing and garland on the throats of those women was moving slightly and wonderfully as though 
obtaining air from the air of breath.

shloka:
चन्दनस्य च शीतस्य शीधोर् मधु रसस्य च |
विविधस्य च माल्यस्य पुष्पस्य विविधस्य च
translation:
There wind blew carrying in a lot of directions, a variety of fragrances of cool sandal-paste and 
of sweet liquor, of various flower garlands and of various kinds of agallocum fumes.

shloka:
स्नानानाम् चन्दनानाम् च धूपानाम् चैव मूर्चितः |
प्रववौ सुरभिर् गन्धो विमाने पुष्पके तदा
translation:
Then the blossoming fragrance from the baths and sandal paste and from agallocum fumes blew spreading 
all around in that Pushpaka plane.

shloka: श्याम अवदाताः तत्र अन्याः काश्चित् कृष्णा वर अन्गनाः
translation:
There in that Ravana's house, some women had fair and white complexion some best women were black, 
some women had a body of golden complexion.

shloka: तासाम् निद्रा वशत्वाच् च मदनेन विमूर्चितम्
translation:
Appearance of those sleeping women, tired from being possessed by sleep and from lust, was like 
lotuses sleeping.

shloka: एवम् सर्वम् अशेषेण रावण अन्तः पुरम् कपिः
translation: Hanuma with great radiance thus saw entire Ravana's house completely but did not see Seetha.

shloka: निरीक्षमाणः च ततः ताः स्त्रियः स महा कपिः
translation:
Then that Hanuma seeing those women obtained great anguish being in doubt because of fear in the 
matter of dharma.

shloka: पर दार अवरोधस्य प्रसुप्तस्य निरीक्षणम्
translation: "My seeing sleeping house of other people's wives will do a great deficit to dharma."

shloka: न हि मे पर दाराणाम् दृष्टिर् विषय वर्तिनी
translation:
"My sight is indeed not in the matter of other wives here. These other's wives have been seen by 
me."

shloka: तस्य प्रादुर् अभूच् चिन्ता पुनर् अन्या मनस्विनः
translation:
To that Hanuma with an excellent mind, with a fixed and concentrated mind, was born another thought 
again, showing a fixed resolve in the task at hand.

shloka: कामम् दृष्ट्वा मया सर्वा विश्वस्ता रावण स्त्रियः
translation:
"All Ravana's women who were in faith could have been seen by me; to my mind there indeed was not 
even a little disturbance".

shloka: मनो हि हेतुः सर्वेषाम् इन्द्रियाणाम् प्रवर्तते
translation:
"Among auspicious or inauspicious states in the behavior of all senses mind is the reason. My that 
mind is very steady."

shloka: न अन्यत्र हि मया शक्या वैदेही परिमार्गितुम्
translation:
"By me it is not possible to search Seetha at another place. Always during search women will be 
seen among other women."

shloka: यस्य सत्त्वस्य या योनिः तस्याम् तत् परिमार्ग्यते
translation:
"To an animal of whatever race that animal is searched in that race; a woman missing is not possible 
to be searched among female deer."

shloka: तद् इदम् मार्गितम् तावत् शुद्धेन मनसा मया
translation:
"For that reason all this Ravana's house has been search by me with a pure mind Seetha alone cannot 
be seen."

shloka: देव गन्धर्व कन्याः च नाग कन्याः च वीर्यवान्
translation: The strong Hanuma observing girls from devas, gandharvas and girls from nagas did not see Janaki.

shloka: ताम् अपश्यन् कपिः तत्र पश्यमः च अन्या वर स्त्रियः
translation:
The powerful Hanuma not seeing Her there and seeing other best women then started to think deeply 
going far from there.

shloka: स भूयस्तु परम् श्रीमान् मारुतिर्यत्नमास्थितः
translation:
That Hanuma the glorious one adopting a great task again left that bar and began to search that 
house.

shloka:
स तस्य मध्ये भवनस्य वानरो |
लता ग्ऱ्हामः चित्र गृहान् निशा गृहान् |
जगाम सीताम् प्रति 
दर्शन उत्सुको |
न च एव ताम् पश्यति चारु दर्शनाम्
translation:
That Hanuma interested in sight of Seetha, in the middle of that building, went towards houses 
made of plant creepers, art houses, and nocturnal houses but did not see Her with a beautiful appearance.

shloka:
स चिन्तयाम् आस ततो महा कपिः |
प्रियाम् अपश्यन् रघु नन्दनस्य ताम् |
ध्रुवम् नु सीता म्रियते 
यथा न मे |
विचिन्वतो दर्शनम् एति मैथिली
translation:
That great Hanuma then later not seeing that Seetha dear to Rama thought thus: "to me searching 
Seetha in whatever way appearance not being obtained, from that Seetha definitely has died."

shloka:
सा राक्षसानाम् प्रवरेण बाला |
स्व शील सम्रक्षण तत् परा सती |
अनेन नूनम् प्रतिदुष्ट कर्मणा 
|
हता भवेद् आर्य पथे परे स्थिता
translation:
"That Seetha standing in the best traditional path being chaste interested, in preserving her character 
must have been killed by the king of these Rakshasas who performed evil deeds - this is certain."

shloka:
विरूप रूपा विकृता विवर्चसो |
महा आनना दीर्घ विरूप दर्शनाः |
समीक्ष्य सा राक्षस राज योषितो 
|
भयाद् विनष्टा जनक ईश्वर आत्मजा
translation:
"That daughter of King Janaka died of fear seeing the wives of Ravana with crooked appearances 
- horrible ones without radiance with great faces with long and crooked eyes."

shloka:
सीताम् अद्ऱ्ष्ट्वा हि अनवाप्य पौरुषम् |
विह्ऱ्त्य कालम् सह वानरैः चिरम् |
न मे अस्ति 
सुग्रीव समीपगा गतिः |
सुतीक्ष्ण दण्डो बलवामः च वानरः
translation:
"Without seeing Seetha, not obtaining destiny and wandering for a long time together with Vanaras, 
to me there is not a path to go near Sugreeva. Sugreeva has a sharp punishment and also is strong."

shloka:
दृष्टम् अन्तः पुरम् सर्वम् दृष्ट्वा रावण योषितः |
न सीता दृश्यते साध्वी वृथा जातो मम श्रमः
translation:
"All inner city has been seen. Women of Ravana have been seen. The chaste Seetha has not been seen. 
My effort became wastefull."

shloka:
किम् नु माम् वानराः सर्वे गतम् वक्ष्यन्ति सम्गताः |
गत्वा तत्र त्वया वीर किम् कृतम् तद् 
वदस्व नः
translation:
"To me who has gone back all Vanaras after meeting what they would say? O strong one! Going there, 
what has been done by you? Tell that to us."

shloka:
अदृष्ट्वा किम् प्रवक्ष्यामि ताम् अहम् जनक आत्मजाम् |
ध्रुवम् प्रायम् उपेष्यन्ति कालस्य 
व्यतिवर्तने
translation:
"Without seeing that Seetha what can I say? Due to passing of time, definitely they will obtain 
fire."

shloka:
किम् वा वक्ष्यति व्ऱ्द्धः च जाम्बवान् अन्गदः च सः |
गतम् पारम् समुद्रस्य वानराः च समागताः
translation:
"To me who had gone for the other shore of the ocean what will the old Jambavan say? What would 
that Angada and vanaras who meet say?"

shloka:
अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलम् अनिर्वेदः परम् सुखम् |
अनिर्वेदो हि सततम् सर्व अर्थेषु प्रवर्तकः
translation:
"Non-depression is root of development. Absence of despondency is the greatest comfort. Self reliance 
always is indeed the promoter in all matters."

shloka:
करोति सफलम् जन्तोः कर्म यच् च करोति सः |
तस्माद् अनिर्वेद क्ऱ्तम् यत्नम् चेष्टे अहम् उत्तमम्
translation:
"Whatever action a human does that action of man is made to be successful by non-depression. For 
that reason I will perform a best effort together with non-depression. I will search all those regions ruled by 
Ravana not yet seen."

shloka: आपान शाला विचिताः तथा पुष्प गृहाणि च
translation:
"Bars have been searched; in the same way flower houses, art houses have been searched; again pleasure 
houses, pathways in the middle of gardens, buildings in all directions have been searched."

shloka:
इति संचिन्त्य भूयो अपि विचेतुम् उपचक्रमे |
भूमी गृहामः चैत्य गृहान् गृह अतिगृहकान् अपि
translation:
Thus thinking Hanuma began to search again undergrounds, houses at the beginning of street intersections 
and also small houses faraway from the main houses.

shloka:
उत्पतन् निपतमः च अपि तिष्ठन् गच्चन् पुनः क्वचित् |
अपावृण्वमः च द्वाराणि कपाटानि अवघट्टयन्
translation:
The great Hanuma flying again and again and jumping down, standing up, walking, opening doors, 
pushing doors and entering inside, coming out, climbing down, climbing up wandered all opportunity.

shloka:
चतुर् अन्गुल मात्रो अपि न अवकाशः स विद्यते |
रावण अन्तः पुरे तस्मिन् यम् कपिर् न जगाम सः
translation:
That Hanuma in that city of Ravana - whatever region he did not go that region was not there even 
for four angulas.

shloka:
प्राकर अन्तर रथ्याः च वेदिकः चैत्य संश्रयाः |
श्वभ्राः च पुष्करिण्यः च सर्वम् तेन अवलोकितम्
translation:
Streets between fort walls, platforms together with the intersection of four streets, wells, lakes 
all these had been seen by him.

shloka:
राक्षस्यो विविध आकारा विरूपा विकृताः तथा |
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु सा जनक आत्मजा
translation:
Rakshasa women of various forms, with crooked forms and horrific forms had been seen there by Hanuma 
but not that Seetha.

shloka:
रूपेण अप्रतिमा लोके वरा विद्या धर स्त्रियः |
दृटा हनूमता तत्र न तु राघव नन्दिनी
translation:
The best Vidhyadhara women incomparable by beauty in the world had been seen there by Hanuma, but 
not Seetha.

shloka:
नाग कन्या वर आरोहाः पूर्ण चन्द्र निभ आननाः |
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न तु सीता सुमध्यमा
translation:
Naaga women with beautiful buttocks, with faces equaling full moon had been seen by Hanuma there, 
but not Seetha with a beautiful waist.

shloka:
प्रमथ्य राक्षस इन्द्रेण नाग कन्या बलाद्द् हृताः |
दृष्टा हनूमता तत्र न सा जनक नन्दिनी
translation:
Naaga women who had been stolen forcefully, being defeated by Ravana had been seen there by Hanuma, 
not that Seetha

shloka:
सो अपश्यमः ताम् महा बाहुः पश्यमः च अन्या वर स्त्रियः |
विषसाद महा बाहुर् हनूमान् मारुत 
आत्मजः
translation:
That Hanuma with great arms, the wise one, the son of Vayu not seeing that Seetha and seeing other 
women became depressed again and again.

shloka:
उद्योगम् वानर इन्द्राणम् प्लवनम् सागरस्य च |
व्यर्थम् वीक्ष्य अनिल सुतः चिन्ताम् पुनर् 
उपागमत्
translation:
Seeing the effort of the best Vanaras and the crossing of ocean as being wasted, Hanuma got depression 
again.

shloka:
अवतीर्य विमानाच् च हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः |
चिन्ताम् उपजगाम अथ शोक उपहत चेतनः
translation:
Thereafter the son of Vayu Hanuma got down from Pushpaka, obtained thought with a mind overcome 
with grief.

shloka:
विमानात् तु सुसम्क्रम्य प्राकारम् हरि यूथपः |
हनूमान् वेगवान् आसीद् यथा विद्युद् घन अन्तरे
translation:
Hanuma the leader of Vanaras crossed from pushpaka toward the fort wall and became with speed like 
lighting in the middle of a cloud.

shloka:
सम्परिक्रम्य हनुमान् रावणस्य निवेशनान् |
अदृष्ट्वा जानकीम् सीताम् अब्रवीद् वचनम् कपिः
translation:
The simian Hanuma went far from the house of Ravana and not seeing Seetha, the daughter of King 
Janaka, said these words:

shloka:
भूयिष्ठम् लोडिता लन्का रामस्य चरता प्रियम् |
न हि पश्यामि वैदेहीम् सीताम् सर्व अन्ग शोभनाम्
translation:
"The city of Lanka has been mostly explored by me attempting for the pleasure of Rama. But I am 
unable to see Seetha, beautiful in all limbs, and the daughter of Videha."

shloka:
पल्वलानि तटाकानि सरांसि सरितः तथा |
नद्यो अनूपवन अन्ताः च दुर्गाः च धरणी धराः
translation:
"All earth consisting of pools, ponds, lakes and streams, rivers and forest areas filled with water, 
mountains difficult of access have been explored but I did not see Seetha."

shloka: इह सम्पातिना सीता रावणस्य निवेशने
translation:
"It has been said by the eagle King Sampati that Seetha is here in the house of Ravana. I am unable 
to see her."

shloka: किम् नु सीता अथ वैदेही मैथिली जनक आत्मजा
translation:
"Otherwise Seetha belonging to Videha born in Mithila and daughter of king Janaka - Can she be 
helplessly together with the evil minded Ravana."

shloka: क्षिप्रम् उत्पततो मन्ये सीताम् आदाय रक्षसः
translation:
"I think while Ravana fearing Rama's arrows flew quickly carrying Seetha, she might have fallen 
down in the middle of the journey."

shloka: अथवा ह्रियमाणायाः पथि सिद्ध निषेविते
translation:
"Or I think the heart of the noble Seetha being stolen in the path served by Siddhas must have 
sunk at the site of the ocean."

shloka: रावणस्य ऊरु वेगेन भुजाभ्याम् पीडितेन च
translation:
"I think due to great speed of Ravana and due to the torture of Ravana's shoulders the life has 
been given up by that noble one with wide eyes."

shloka: उपरि उपरि वा नूनम् सागरम् क्रमतः तदा
translation:
"Then while being flown upon the surface of the ocean, Seetha definitely fell down in the ocean 
while wriggling."

shloka: आहो क्षुद्रेण च अनेन रक्षन्ती शीलम् आत्मनः
translation:
"Or has the austere Seetha been eaten by this Ravana, the evil minded one while she was protecting 
her chastity without any relatives near her."

shloka: अथवा राक्षस इन्द्रस्य पत्नीभिर् असित ईक्षणा
translation:
"Otherwise not being evil with black eyes, She may have been eaten by the wives of Ravana with 
evil thoughts."

shloka: सम्पूर्ण चन्द्र प्रतिमम् पद्म पत्र निभ ईक्षणम्
translation:
"The pitiable Seetha equaling full moon, with eyes equaling lotus petals must have obtained death 
while meditating upon Rama's face."

shloka: हा राम लक्ष्मण इति एव हा अयोध्येति च मैथिली
translation:
"The daughter of Videha, Seetha. �O Rama!' �O Lakshmana!' �O Ayodhya!', thus weeping greatly may 
have given up her body."

shloka: अथवा निहिता मन्ये रावणस्य निवेशने
translation: "I think otherwise being put in the house of Ravana Seetha is definitely crying like a caged myna."

shloka: जनकस्य कुले जाता राम पत्नी सुमध्यमा
translation:
"How can the daughter of King Janaka, Rama's wife Seetha with a beautiful waist, with eyes like 
black lotus petals obtain Ravana's capture."

shloka: विनष्टा वा प्रनष्टा वा मृता वा जनक आत्मजा
translation:
"It is not fair to let know Rama who has a dear wife if Seetha is lost or is not to be seen or 
has died."

shloka: निवेद्यमाने दोषः स्याद् दोषः स्याद् अनिवेदने
translation:
"To be let known becomes an error; not to let know becomes an error how to perform the duty? To 
me this seems dire situation."

shloka: अस्मिन्न् एवम् गते कर्ये प्राप्त कालम् क्षमम् च किम्
translation:
"This task while it goes this way the time is approaching. What becomes appropriate" thus Hanuma 
thought again this view point.

shloka: यदि सीताम् अदृष्ट्वा अहम् वानर इन्द्र पुरीम् इतः
translation:
"If I go towards Sugreeva's city from here without seeing Seetha from that to what avail will this 
effort be?"

shloka: मम इदम् लन्घनम् व्यर्थम् सागरस्य भविष्यति
translation:
"My crossing of the ocean entering the city of Lanka the site of rakshasas - all this will become 
waste."

shloka: किम् वा वक्ष्यति सुग्रीवो हरयो व समागताः
translation:
"To me reaching Kishkindha what would Sugreeva say or Vanaras there or those sons of Dasharatha 
what would they say?"

shloka: गत्वा तु यदि काकुत्स्थम् वक्ष्यामि परम् अप्रियम्
translation:
"Going there by me for Rama, �Seetha has not been seen' - thus if I say a very unpleasant word 
thereafter Rama will give up life."

shloka: परुषम् दारुणम् क्रूरम् तीक्ष्णम् इन्द्रिय तापनम्
translation:
"Hearing bad word belonging to Seetha that is harsh, horrible, cruel, sharp, sense agonizing, He 
will not exist."

shloka: तम् तु कृच्च्र गतम् दृष्ट्वा पन्चत्व गत मानसम्
translation:
"Seeing that Rama being with troubles, being with a heart towards death, Lakshmana, one with great 
love and an intellectual will not exist."

shloka: विनष्टौ भ्रातरौ श्रुत्वा भरतो अपि मरिष्यति
translation:
"Hearing brothers to be dead, Bharata also will die. Seeing the dead Bharata, Shatrughana also 
will not exist."

shloka: पुत्रान् मृतान् समीक्ष्य अथ न भविष्यन्ति मातरः
translation:
"Thereafter seeing sons to be dead the mothers Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi will not exist - there 
is no doubt."

shloka: कृतज्ञः सत्य संधः च सुग्रीवः प्लवग अधिपः
translation:
"Grateful, true to pledge Sugreeva, the leader of Vanaras, seeing Rama the leader of Vanaras seeing 
Rama die in that way will give up life thereafter."

shloka: दुर्मना व्यथिता दीना निरानन्दा तपस्विनी
translation:
"Being tortured by the sorrow of husband, made sad by a gloomy heart, disconsolate without happiness, 
to be pitied, Ruma will give up life."

shloka: वालिजेन तु दुह्खेन पीडिता शोक कर्शिता
translation:
"Being distressed from the sorrow of Vali, being emaciated from grief, Tara also will not exist 
while the king Sugreeva is obtaining death."

shloka: माता पित्रोर् विनाशेन सुग्रीव व्यसनेन च
translation:
"The young Angada also from the death of mother and father, from the grief of Sugreeva - why will 
he retain life?"

shloka: भर्तृजेन तु शोकेन अभिभूता वन ओकसः
translation:
"Vanaras being rejected by the sorrow due to their lord will strike their heads with palms and 
fists."

shloka: सान्त्वेन अनुप्रदानेन मानेन च यशस्विना
translation:
"Vanaras loved by the famous king Sugreeva through good words, through small gifts, through respect 
will give up lives."

shloka: न वनेषु न शैलेषु न निरोधेषु वा पुनः
translation:
"Best among Vanaras will not enjoy together sport in forest, not on mountains, not again in covered 
places."

shloka: सपुत्र दाराः सामात्या भर्तृ व्यसन पीडिताः
translation:
"Together with wife and children and together with ministers being tortured by grief of their lord, 
they will fall down from top of mountains on to flat lands and on to rugged lands."
