shloka: विषम् उद्बन्धनम् वा अपि प्रवेशम् ज्वलनस्य वा
translation:
"Vanaras will perform death by taking poison or getting hanged or entering fire or fasting or a 
weapon."

shloka: घोरम् आरोदनम् मन्ये गते मयि भविष्यति
translation:
"While I am going I think about the destruction of Ikshvaaku dynasty and destruction of Vanaras 
and there will be a terrible wail."

shloka: सो अहम् न एव गमिष्यामि किष्किन्धाम् नगरीम् इतः
translation: "I will not go from here to the Kishkindha city. I am not capable to see Sugreeva without Seetha."

shloka: मयि अगच्चति च इहस्थे धर्म आत्मानौ महा रथौ
translation:
"I while not going, being here those virtuous ones, those great warriors those two Rama and Lakshmana 
will live by hope. Vanaras also who are agile will live."

shloka: हस्त आदानो मुख आदानो नियतो वृक्ष मूलिकः
translation:
"Without seeing Seetha subsisting on whatever falls on hand, whatever comes to mouth, being self 
restrained I will become a hermit living on trees and herbs at a region near ocean which has many roots, fruits 
and much water."

shloka:
चिताम् कृत्वा प्रवेक्ष्यामि समिद्धम् अरणी सुतम् |
उपविष्टस्य वा सम्यग् लिन्गिनम् साधयिष्यतः
translation:
"Or I will enter fire which is glowing after making a funeral pile or while sitting performing 
fasting onto death my body will be eaten by crows and by beasts of prey."

shloka: इदम् अपि ऋषिभिर् दृष्टम् निर्याणम् इति मे मतिः
translation:
"This way to giving up body has been seen by sages. This is my opinion if I do not see Seetha, 
I will enter lot of water."

shloka: सुजात मूला सुभगा कीर्ति माला यशस्विनी
translation:
"Not seeing Seetha, my garland of glory of long time with a strong foundation, beautiful one together 
with fame has been destroyed."

shloka: तापसो वा भविष्यामि नियतो वृक्ष मूलिकः
translation:
"I will become a hermit who is self restrained resorting to trees and herbs, I will not go from 
here not seeing Seetha with black eyes."

shloka: यदि इतः प्रतिगच्चामि सीताम् अनधिगम्य ताम्
translation:
"If I go back from here without knowing that Seetha, there will not be Angada together with all 
those Vanaras."

shloka: विनाशे बहवो दोषा जीवन् प्राप्नोति भद्रकम्
translation:
"There are lots of blemishes in dying; one who is alive sees auspicious things. For that reason 
I will keep my life. It is definite for the meeting of people who are alive."

shloka: एवम् बहु विधम् दुह्खम् मनसा धारयन् मुहुः
translation:
Hanuma carrying in mind sorrow of various kinds again and again did not get then the crossing of 
sorrow.

shloka: रावणम् वा वधिष्यामि दशग्रीवम् महा बलम्
translation:
"Otherwise I will kill Ravana with ten heads, with great prowess. Whatever happened to the stolen 
Seetha, this will be revenge to that."

shloka: अथवा एनम् समुत्क्षिप्य उपरि उपरि सागरम्
translation:
"Otherwise carrying this Ravana over the surface of ocean I will take him to Rama like an animal 
to the lord of animals."

shloka: इति चिन्ता समापन्नः सीताम् अनधिगम्य ताम्
translation:
Hanuma not seeing that Seetha thus begetting sorrow, thought with a mind cluttered with thoughts 
and sorrow.

shloka: यावत् सीताम् न पश्यामि राम पत्नीम् यशस्विनीम्
translation:
"To wherever I see Seetha, the wife of Sri Rama and one with fame, till there I will search the 
city of Lanka again and again."

shloka: सम्पाति वचनाच् च अपि रामम् यदि आनयामि अहम्
translation: "Based on words of Sampati if I bring Sri Rama then Sri Rama not seeing wife will burn all Vanaras."

shloka: इह एव नियत आहारो वत्स्यामि नियत इन्द्रियः
translation:
"With limited food and with restrained senses, I live here itself. By my deed those men and vanaras 
- let they not be destroyed."

shloka: अशोक वनिका च अपि महती इयम् महा द्रुमा
translation:
"Whatever this Ashoka garden with great trees is being seen this I will obtain. This has not been 
searched by me."

shloka: वसून् रुद्रामः तथा आदित्यान् अश्विनौ मरुतो अपि च
translation:
"Saluting the eight Vasus, Rudras and Adityas, the two Aswinis, seven Maruts, I will go to increase 
the grief of Rakshasas."

shloka: जित्वा तु राक्षसान् देवीम् इक्ष्वाकु कुल नन्दिनीम्
translation:
"Defeating all rakshasas, I will give Seetha, who gives happiness to Ikshvaaku dynasty to Sri Rama 
as the fruit of austerity to an ascetic."

shloka: स मुहूर्तम् इव ध्यात्वा चिन्ता विग्रथित इन्द्रियः
translation: The gloried son of Vayu that Hanuma got up with his senses tied by grief.

shloka:
नमो अस्तु रामाय सलक्ष्मणाय |
देव्यै च तस्यै जनक आत्मजायै |
नमो अस्तु रुद्र इन्द्र यम 
अनिलेभ्यो |
नमो अस्तु चन्द्र अर्क मरुद् गणेभ्यः
translation:
"Let there be salutations to Sri Rama together with Lakshmana, also to that, who is divine let 
there be salutations. To Rudra, Indra, Yama and Vaayu let there be salutations."

shloka:
स तेभ्यः तु नमः कृत्वा सुग्रीवाय च मारुतिः |
दिशः सर्वाः समालोक्य अशोक वनिकाम् प्रति
translation:
That Hanuma saluting to all those and also to Sugreeva, observing all directions went towards Ashoka 
garden.

shloka:
स गत्वा मनसा पूर्वम् अशोक वनिकाम् शुभाम् |
उत्तरम् चिन्तयाम् आस वानरो मारुत आत्मजः
translation:
The son of Vayu, that Vanara went by mind before itself toward that Ashoka garden. The auspicious 
one pondered the task to be done later.

shloka:
ध्रुवम् तु रक्षो बहुला भविष्यति वन आकुला |
अशोक वनिका चिन्त्या सर्व संस्कार संस्कृता
translation:
"The Ashoka garden definitely will be with many rakshasas, filled with trees, adorned with various 
cultures and sacred."

shloka:
रक्षिणः च अत्र विहिता नूनम् रक्षन्ति पादपान् |
भगवान् अपि सर्व आत्मा न अतिक्षोभम् प्रवायति
translation:
"There definitely guards will be protecting assigned, trees, omnipresent Lord Vayu also will be 
blowing by without force, and by me this body has been made small for the sake of Sri Rama and to avoid Ravana."

shloka: सिद्धिम् मे सम्विधास्यन्ति देवाः सर्षि गणाः त्व् इह
translation:
"Devas together with ascetics will make success to me here, self born Brahma the divine one and 
devas and Agni and Vaayu, Devendra wearing the weapon of Vajra and Varuna with Pasha in hand and also the Sun 
and the moon and the aswinis. The great ones Maruts and Eshwara may give my success. Whoever is the lord of all 
living creatures among all living beings others who being unseen exist in the path may give success to me."

shloka:
तद् उन्नसम् पाण्डुर दन्तम् अव्रणम् |
शुचि स्मितम् पद्म पलाश लोचनम् |
द्रक्ष्ये तद् आर्या 
वदनम् कदा न्व् अहम् |
प्रसन्न तारा अधिप तुल्य दर्शनम्
translation:
"When will I see that noble face with a high nose, with white teeth without any injuries with a 
bright smile, with eyes resembling lotus petals with sight equaling the splendor of clear full moon?"

shloka:
क्षुद्रेण पापेन नृशंस कर्मणा |
सुदारुण अलाम्कृत वेष धारिणा|
बल अभिभूता अबला तपस्विनी 
|
कथम् नु मे दृष्ट पथे अद्य सा भवेत्
translation:
"How that powerless Seetha, a helpless one, forcefully taken away by the mean vile Ravana with 
a cruel action, with a horribly decorated form will fall in the range of my sight today."

shloka:
स मुहूर्तम् इव ध्यत्वा मनसा च अधिगम्य ताम् |
अवप्लुतो महा तेजाः प्राकारम् तस्य वेश्मनः
translation:
That Hanuma with great resplendence thought for a moment, obtained that Ashoka garden by mind and 
jumped from the compound wall of that house.

shloka:
स तु सम्हृष्ट सर्व अन्गः प्राकारस्थो महा कपिः |
पुष्पित अग्रान् वसन्त आदौ ददर्श विविधान् 
द्रुमान्
translation:
That great Hanuma with joyful limbs, being on enclosure wall saw various trees such as Sal, beautiful 
Ashoka, Champaka full of flowers, Uddalaka, Naga, mango trees with their fruit in the colour of the snout of a 
monkey, in full blossom at the start of the spring.

shloka:
अथ आम्र वण संचन्नाम् लता शत समावृताम् |
ज्या मुक्त इव नाराचः पुप्लुवे वृक्ष वाटिकाम्
translation:
Thereafter Hanuma flew like a Naracha arrow released from bow string, toward the garden covered 
by mango trees and surrounded by hundreds of creepers.

shloka:
स प्रविष्य विचित्राम् ताम् विहगैर् अभिनादिताम् |
राजतैः कान्चनैः चैव पादपैः सर्वतो वृताम्
translation:
That Hanuma the simian, saw on entering that garden filled with happy humans, animals and birds 
with varied hues during spring, resounded by birds, with trees made of silver, made of gold, surrounded everywhere 
by birds and groups of animals; wonderful with wonderful trees equaling the Sun at sunrise together with trees 
of various kinds which obtained flowers and fruits, served daily by Cuckoos and by dragon flies, resounded by 
peacocks in heat and with groups of birds of various kinds.

shloka:
मार्गमाणो वर आरोहाम् राज पुत्रीम् अनिन्दिताम् |
सुख प्रसुप्तान् विहगान् बोधयाम् आस वानरः
translation:
Hanuma searching the royal daughter Seetha with excellent limbs and without blame, woke up birds 
in comfortable sleep.

shloka:
उत्पतद्भिर् द्विज गणैः पक्षैः सालाः समाहताः |
अनेक वर्णा विविधा मुमुचुः पुष्प वृष्टयः
translation:
Trees hit by wings of groups of birds in flight shed showers of flowers of various colours and 
of various kinds.

shloka:
पुष्प अवकीर्णः शुशुभे हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः |
अशोक वनिका मध्ये यथा पुष्पमयो गिरिः
translation:
The son of Lord Vayu, Hanuma sprinkled with flowers shone like a mountain of flowers in the middle 
of Ashoka garden.

shloka:
दिशः सर्व अभिदावन्तम् वृक्ष षण्ड गतम् कपिम् |
द्ऱ्ष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि वसन्त इति मेनिरे
translation:
Seeing Hanuma running in all directions and being in the middle of trees, all living creatures 
thought Him to be Vasanta, the lord of spring.

shloka:
वृक्षेभ्यः पतितैः पुष्पैर् अवकीर्णा पृथग् विधैः |
रराज वसुधा तत्र प्रमदा इव विभूषिता
translation:
There the Earth sprinkled by flowers of various kinds which fell down from trees shone like a well 
decorated woman.

shloka:
तरस्विना ते तरवः तरसा अभिप्रकम्पिताः |
कुसुमानि विचित्राणि सस्ऱ्जुः कपिना तदा
translation: Then those trees, shaken by the might of Hanuma the mighty one, showered wonderful flowers.

shloka:
निर्धूत पत्र शिखराः शीर्ण पुष्प फल द्रुमाः |
निक्षिप्त वस्त्र आभरणा धूर्ता इव पराजिताः
translation:
The trees with their branches, removed leaves with fallen down fruits and flowers were like defeated 
gamblers with their clothes and jewellery kept down.

shloka:
हनूमता वेगवता कम्पिताः ते नग उत्तमाः |
पुष्प पर्ण फलानि आशु मुमुचुः पुष्प शालिनः
translation: The excellent trees shining with best flowers fell down instantly flowers, leaves and fruits.

shloka:
विहम्ग सम्घैर् हीनाः ते स्कन्ध मात्र आश्रया द्रुमाः |
बभूवुर् अगमाः सर्वे मारुतेन इव निर्धुताः
translation:
All those trees losing groups of birds became being a resort to branches only like trees shook 
by wind.

shloka:
विधूत केशी युवतिर् यथा मृदित वर्णिका |
निष्पीत शुभ दन्त ओष्ठी नखैर् दन्तैः च विक्षता
translation:
Hit by Hanuma's tail, hands and feet, Ashoka garden with broken best trees became like a young 
woman with disturbed hair, with effaced sandal paste, with her auspicious teeth and lips drunk from and wounded 
by nails and by teeth.

shloka:
महा लतानाम् दामानि व्यधमत् तरसा कपिः |
यथा प्रावृषि विन्ध्यस्य मेघ जालानि मारुतः
translation:
Hanuma broke circles of great creepers by His might like the wind during rainy season, breaking 
the groups of clouds of mountain Vindhya.

shloka:
स तत्र मणि भूमीः च राजतीः च मनो रमाः |
तथा कान्चन भूमीः च विचरन् ददृशे कपिः
translation:
That Hanuma pacing there saw diamond studded floors, silver inlaid floors, and beautiful gold inlaid 
floors.

shloka:
वापीः च विविध आकाराः पूर्णाः परम वारिणा |
महा अर्हैर् मणि सोपानैर् उपपन्नाः ततः ततः
translation:
Hanuma saw ponds filled with the best waters, together there and there with stairs embedded with 
diamonds of great value, with pearls and corals as sand, with bottoms made of crystal and precious stones, shone 
by trees of golden hue and of wonderful hue at banks containing beds of lotuses in full blossom and lilies, resounded 
by chakravaka birds nearby, sounded by water fowls, resounded by swans and cranes, together with tall trees, with 
nectar like waters, with hundreds of auspicious creepers, covered by the flowers of santaana trees, surrounded 
by various shrubs with middle regions of karaveera and also wells and in various shapes.

shloka:
ततो अम्बु धर सम्काशम् प्रव्ऱ्द्ध शिखरम् गिरिम् |
विचित्र कूटम् कूटैः च सर्वतः परिवारितम्
translation:
Thereafter the monkey warrior Hanuma saw a mountain which was a beautiful mountain in the world, 
equaling cloud with high peaks, with wonderful peaks surrounded in all directions by peaks, spread by caves and 
covered by different trees.

shloka:
ददर्श च नगात् तस्मान् नदीम् निपतिताम् कपिः |
अन्काद् इव समुत्पत्य प्रियस्य पतिताम् प्रियाम्
translation:
Hanuma saw river which fell down from the mountain like a beloved (young wife) who fell down after 
jumping from the lap of a loved one shone by trees whose ends fell down in water or like a woman in anger being 
detained by her near and dear. That great Hanuma again saw that river with water, turning back like a beloved 
woman reaching her beloved again, being reconciled to her beloved one.

shloka:
तस्य अदूरात् स पद्मिन्यो नाना द्विज गण आयुताः |
ददर्श कपि शार्दूलो हनुमान् मारुत आत्मजः
translation:
The best among vanaras and the son of Vayu, that Hanuma saw near to that mountain, lotus ponds 
together with many groups of birds.

shloka:
कृत्रिमाम् दीर्घिकाम् च अपि पूर्णाम् शीतेन वारिणा |
मणि प्रवर सोपानाम् मुख्ता सिकत शोभिताम्
translation:
He also saw an artificial pond filled with cold water, with steps embedded with best diamonds, 
shone by the sand of pearls, wonderful forest with very big buildings made by Vishwakarma, with groups of artificial 
trees decorated in all directions.

shloka: ये केचित् पादपाः तत्र पुष्प उपग फल उपगाः
translation:
There whatever trees were there with flowers and fruits, all those were together with umbrellas, 
together with big platforms and with smaller golden platforms.

shloka: लता प्रतानैः बहुभिः पर्णैः च बहुभिर् व्ऱ्ताम्
translation:
The monkey warrior Hanuma saw one shimshupaa tree golden in colour covered with many groups of 
creepers and with many leaves surrounded everywhere with platforms made of gold.

shloka:
सो अपश्यद् भूमि भागामः च गर्त प्रस्रवणानि च |
सुवर्ण वृक्षान् अपरान् ददर्श शिखि सम्निभान्
translation: Hanuma saw lands, mountain springs, and some other golden trees equal to fire.

shloka:
तेषाम् द्रुमाणाम् प्रभया मेरोर् इव महा कपिः |
अमन्यत तदा वीरः कान्चनो अस्मि इति वानरः
translation:
Then the courageous Hanuma thought thus: "Like the sun by the radiance of Mount Meru, by the radiance 
of those trees, I am of golden colour."

shloka:
ताम् कान्चनैः तरु गणैर् मारुतेन च वीजिताम् |
किन्किणी शत निर्घोषाम् दृष्ट्वा विस्मयम् आगमत्
translation:
Seeing that shimshupaa tree with groups of trees of golden colour blown by the wind, with the sound 
of hundreds of tinkle bells, Hanuma got surprised.

shloka:
स पुष्पित अग्राम् रुचिराम् तरुण अन्कुर पल्लवाम् |
ताम् आरुह्य महा वेगः शिंशपाम् पर्ण सम्व्ऱ्ताम्
translation:
Hanuma with great arms climbing up that shimshupaa tree with well flowered ends, beautiful tree, 
mature with young shoots and leaves and covered by leaves (thought thus).

shloka:
इतो द्रक्ष्यामि वैदेहीम् राम दर्शन लालसाम् |
इतः च इतः च दुह्ख आर्ताम् सम्पतन्तीम् यद्ऱ्च्चया
translation:
"I will see by God's grace, Seetha who is interested in the sight of Sri Rama while she is moving 
here and there with grief."

shloka:
अशोक वनिका च इयम् दृढम् रम्या दुरात्मनः |
चम्पकैः चन्दनैः च अपि बकुलैः च विभूषिता
translation:
This Ashoka garden of evil-souled Ravana is definitely beautiful; it is well decorated by Champaka 
trees, by sandal trees and by Vakula trees.

shloka:
इयम् च नलिनी रम्या द्विज सम्घ निषेविता |
इमाम् सा राम महिषी नूनम् एष्यति जानकी
translation:
"This pond also served by groups of birds is beautiful; that wife of Sri Rama definitely will come 
for this pond."

shloka:
सा राम राम महिषी राघवस्य प्रिया सदा |
वन संचार कुशला नूनम् एष्यति जानकी
translation:
"The wife of Sri Rama dear to Sri Rama, a chaste wife, soul captivating one, expert at moving in 
forest, that Janaki will definitely come."

shloka:
अथवा मृग शाव अक्षी वनस्य अस्य विचक्षणा |
वनम् एष्यति सा च इह राम चिन्ता अनुकर्शिता
translation:
"Otherwise one with the eyes of a deer, emaciated by the thought of Sri Rama, that noble one will 
come for this garden."

shloka:
राम शोक अभिसम्तप्ता सा देवी वाम लोचना |
वन वास रता नित्यम् एष्यते वन चारिणी
translation:
"Tortured by grief for Sri Rama, with beautiful eyes, interested always living in the garden, that 
Devi moving about in the garden will come."

shloka:
वने चराणाम् सततम् नूनम् स्पृहयते पुरा |
रामस्य दयिता भार्या जनकस्य सुता सती
translation:
"The beloved wife of Sri Rama, the daughter of king Janaka, the chaste wife, earlier always was 
interested the denizens of the garden. This is true."

shloka:
संध्या काल मनाः श्यामा ध्रुवम् एष्यति जानकी |
नदीम् च इमाम् शिव जलाम् संध्या अर्थे वर वर्णिनी
translation:
"The ever youthful one with the best complexion, Seetha interested in the rites of Sandhya time 
will definitely come to this river with the auspicious water for Sandhya rite."

shloka:
तस्याः च अपि अनुरूपेयम् अशोक वनिका शुभा |
शुभा या पार्थिव इन्द्रस्य पत्नी रामस्य सम्मिता
translation:
"Whoever Seetha, the auspicious wife, a dear one of Sri Rama, the king of kings, to that Seetha 
this Ashoka garden, an auspicious one, is well suited also."

shloka:
यदि जिवति सा देवी तारा अधिप निभ आनना |
आगमिष्यति सा अवश्यम् इमाम् शिव जलाम् नदीम्
translation:
"That Devi with the face like that of the moon, if alive, she definitely will come for this river 
with auspicious water."

shloka:
एवम् तु मत्वा हनुमान् महात्मा |
प्रतीक्षमाणो मनुज इन्द्र पत्नीम्
translation:
The great-souled Hanuma thus thinking being concealed in the mass of well flowered leaves saw everything 
observing everywhere.

shloka:
स वीक्षमाणः तत्रस्थो मार्गमाणः च मैथिलीम् |
अवेक्षमाणः च महीम् सर्वाम् ताम् अन्ववैक्षत
translation:
That Hanuma being there, seeing and searching for Seetha, observing all that land, explored 
	the garden.

shloka:
सन्तान कलताभिः च पादपैर् उपशोभिताम् |
दिव्य गन्ध रस उपेताम् सर्वतः समलम्कृताम्
translation:
That Hanuma being there observed closely that Ashoka garden shone by Santanaka creepers, Santana 
	trees with heavenly aroma and juice, well decorated in all directions equalling the garden of Nandana, surrounded 
	by animals and birds, congested with mansions and palaces, resounded with the notes of cuckoos, decorated 
	with wells having golden water lilies, lotuses and with many chairs and carpets; with many sub-terrain houses, 
	beautiful trees, with trees with flowers of all seasons and with fruit, with the radiance of raising sun, 
	by the glory of ashoka trees in bloom, as though radiant as though being made to be with branches without 
	leaves, by hundreds of birds perching again and again, Ashoka trees with wonderful flowers as head decoration, 
	with flowers spread till the roots destroying leaves, with weight of groups of flowers as touching the earth 
	with karnolaara trees; in blossom with Kimkusa trees in full blossom.

shloka:
स देशः प्रभया तेषाम् प्रदीप्त इव सर्वतः |
पुम्नागाः सप्त पर्णाः च चम्पक उद्दालकाः तथा
translation:
By the radiance of those trees that region was as though lit in all directions. Punnaaga trees 
	with flatted roots and in full blossom, Saptaparna trees Campaka and Uddalaka trees were shining.

shloka: शात कुम्भ निभाः केचित् केचिद् अग्नि शिख उपमाः
translation:
There in that garden of Ashoka there were thousands of Ashoka trees some equalling gold, some 
	equalling fire, some equalling the precious stone Niila and Anjana.

shloka: नन्दनम् विविध उद्यानम् चित्रम् चैत्ररथम् यथा
translation:
Like the garden of Nandana, a celestial garden, wonderful like Caitraratham, a garden of Kubera, 
	surpassing all, unfathomable, an excellent one, a beautiful one consisting of glory together with flowers 
	like clusters of stars, like a second sky wonderful with flowers, like hundreds of diamonds, like a second 
	ocean with flowers of all seasons, spread with trees having the smell of honey, beautiful with groups of animals 
	of various sounds, diffused with many smells with an auspicious soul pleasing smell.

shloka:
शैल इन्द्रम् इव गन्ध आढ्यम् द्वितीयम् गन्ध मादनम् |
अशोक वनिकायाम् तु तस्याम् वानर 
	पुम्गवः
translation:
That monkey warrior Hanuma saw not far away in that Ashoka garden, in the middle, a lofty temple 
	filled with fragrance like a second Gandhamadana Mountain, standing by a thousand pillars, white like Mount 
	Kailaasa with stairs made of corals with platforms made of refined gold as though radiant with glory, clear 
	and because of being tall as though scraping the sky.

shloka: ततो मलिन सम्वीताम् राक्षसीभिः समावृताम्
translation:
Thereafter Hanuma saw Seetha wearing a soiled garment, surrounded by rakshasa women, emaciated 
	due to fasting, looking miserable, sighing again and again, like the pure crescent moon at the beginning of 
	a bright fortnight.

shloka:
मन्द प्रख्यायमानेन रूपेण रुचिर प्रभाम् |
पिनद्धाम् धूम जालेन शिखाम् इव विभावसोः
translation: With a form that slowly came out like a tongue of fire, of beautiful radiance covered by smoke.

shloka:
पीतेन एकेन सम्वीताम् क्लिष्टेन उत्तम वाससा |
सपन्काम् अनलम्काराम् विपद्माम् इव पद्मिनीम्
translation:
Covered by a single best cloth of yellow colour, which was wrinkled, without any decorations 
	like a lotus plant without lotuses, together with mud.

shloka:
व्रीडिताम् दुह्ख सम्तप्ताम् परिम्लानाम् तपस्विनीम् |
ग्रहेण अन्गारकेण एव पीडिताम् इव 
	रोहिणीम्
translation:
Bashful, tortured by sorrow worn out in a pitiable condition like the constellation Rohini, 
	pressed by the planet mars.

shloka:
अश्रु पूर्ण मुखीम् दीनाम् कृशाम् अननशेन च |
शोक ध्यान पराम् दीनाम् नित्यम् दुह्ख परायणाम्
translation:
With a face full of tears in a pitiable condition, emaciated due to not taking food, immersed 
	in thought with gloom, always in a pitiable state, surrendering to sorrow.

shloka:
प्रियम् जनम् अपश्यन्तीम् पश्यन्तीम् राक्षसी गणम् |
स्व गणेन मृगीम् हीनाम् श्व गण अभिवृताम् 
	इव
translation:
Not seeing dear people, seeing groups of demonesses, like a female deer loosing her own herd 
	surrounded by group of hounds.

shloka:
नील नाग आभया वेण्या जघनम् गतया एकया |
नीलया नीरदापाये वनराज्या महीमिव
translation:
With a braid with the radiance of a single black serpent reaching hinder part, like the earth 
	with dark green groups of trees during the end of rainy season, deserving of comforts, tormented by grief, 
	not accustomed to calamities.

shloka: ताम् समीक्ष्य विशाल अक्षीम् अधिकम् मलिनाम् कृशाम्
translation:
Observing that woman with wide eyes, very untidy, emaciated, Hanuma thought that this is indeed 
	Seetha on logical grounds.

shloka: ह्रियमाणा तदा तेन रक्षसा काम रूपिणा
translation:
Then, while being abducted by that rakshasa with the ability to assume desired form in whatever 
	way, She was seen, this woman has the same form.

shloka: पूर्ण चन्द्र आननाम् सुभ्रूम् चारु वृत्त पयो धराम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Seetha with a face like full moon, with beautiful eyebrows, with graceful rounded 
	breasts, by the radiance making all directions without darkness, goddess like with black hair, with lips like 
	bimba fruit, with a good waist, very firm, with eyes like lotus petals, like Rati the consort of god of love.

shloka: इष्टाम् सर्वस्य जगतः पूर्ण चन्द्र प्रभाम् इव
translation:
As the light of full moon, dear to all world, like an ascetic woman leading austere life sitting 
	on bare ground with a good body.

shloka: निःश्वास बहुलाम् भीरुम् भुजग इन्द्र वधूम् इव
translation:
Sighing a lot like the consort of lord of serpents in fright, not radiant by sorrow which was 
	great and extensive.

shloka: संसक्ताम् धूम जालेन शिखाम् इव विभावसोः
translation:
Hanuma saw Her like a tongue of fire mixed with column of smoke, like an intellect together 
	with doubts, like a cast away treasure.

shloka: विहताम् इव च श्रद्धाम् आशाम् प्रतिहताम् इव
translation:
Like shattered faith, like frustrated hope, like success together with obstacles, like an impure 
	mind.

shloka: अभूतेन अपवादेन कीर्तिम् निपतिताम् इव
translation:
Like fame that has fallen down by a false scandal, tortured by the obstruction caused to Rama, 
	emaciated due to the abduction by Ravana.

shloka: अबलाम् मृग शाव अक्षीम् वीक्षमाणाम् ततः ततः
translation:
With eyes like those of a young doe full of tears, with black and oblique eye-brows, with a 
	cheerless countenance, seeing there and there, being helpless, sighing again and again.

shloka:
मल पन्क धराम् दीनाम् मण्डन अर्हाम् अमण्डिताम् |
प्रभाम् नक्षत्र राजस्य काल मेघैः इव 
	आवृताम्
translation:
Wearing a coat of dust, pitiable one, although suited for decorations undecorated, like the 
	radiance of the moon, the lord of stars, covered by black clouds.

shloka:
तस्य संदिदिहे बुद्धिः मुहुः सीताम् निरीक्ष्य तु |
आम्नायानाम् अयोगेन विद्याम् प्रशिथिलाम् 
	इव
translation:
Seeing Seetha like knowledge in ruin for want of repeated study, that Hanuma's mind got repeatedly 
	doubtful.

shloka:
दुह्खेन बुबुधे सीताम् हनुमान् अनलम्कृताम् |
संस्कारेण यथा हीनाम् वाचम् अर्थ अन्तरम् 
	गताम्
translation:
Hanuma recognized with great sorrow Seetha not decorated, like a sentence which got a different 
	meaning being devoid of culture.

shloka:
ताम् समीक्ष्य विशाल अक्षीम् राज पुत्रीम् अनिन्दिताम् |
तर्कयाम् आस सीता इति कारणैः 
	उपपादयन्
translation:
Seeing that princess, the wide eyed one, blameless one, Hanuma reasoned her to be Seetha for 
	the following reasons.

shloka:
वैदेह्या यानि च अन्गेषु तदा रामो अन्वकीर्तयत् |
तानि आभरण जालानि गात्र शोभीनि अलक्षयत्
translation:
Then Hanuma saw whatever groups of jewellery of Seetha on various parts Rama spoke, those charming 
	Her limbs, well made earrings, well fitting Svadamstras and ornaments wonderful with diamonds on the limbs 
	of Her hands, belonging to body for long time, blackened and making marks on body.

shloka: तानि एव एतानि मन्ये अहम् यानि रामो अन्वकीर्तयत्
translation:
"I think all these to be same about which Rama spoke; among them whatever have been worn out 
	those I will not see; whatever jewels of Her are not worn out these are they - no doubt."

shloka:
पीतम् कनक पट्ट आभम् स्रस्तम् तद् वसनम् शुभम् |
उत्तरीयम् नग आसक्तम् तदा दृष्टम् प्लवम् 
	गमैः
translation:
That upper garment yellow with a shine like a golden plate, auspicious one, being dropped had 
	been seen caught in a tree then by vanaras.

shloka:
भूषणानि च मुख्यानि दृष्टानि धरणी तले |
अनया एव अपविद्धानि स्वनवन्ति महान्ति च
translation:
"Dropped on the earth by Her, ornaments also great and important, those making sound have been 
	seen."

shloka:
इदम् चिर गृहीतत्वाद् वसनम् क्लिष्टवत्तरम् |
तथा हि नूनम् तद् वर्णम् तथा श्रीमद् यथा 
	इतरत्
translation:
"This cloth being worn for a long time has worn out a lot, even then definitely it is of the 
	same colour, like the other upper garment; in the same way this is glorious."

shloka:
इयम् कनक वर्ण अन्गी रामस्य महिषी प्रिया |
प्रनष्टा अपि सती यस्य मनसो न प्रणश्यति
translation:
"This She of golden colour is indeed Rama's dear wife; who ever Seetha the chaste one, even 
	though not seen, is not gone from Rama's heart."

shloka:
इयम् सा यत् कृते रामः चतुर्भिः परितप्यते |
कारुण्येन आनृशंस्येन शोकेन मदनेन च
translation:
"This is She for whose sake Rama tormented in four ways from compassion from pity from grief 
	from love; (thinking that) a woman has disappeared from compassion, depending on him from pity, wife has been 
	lost from grief, a dear one from love."

shloka:
अस्या देव्या यथा रूपम् अन्ग प्रत्यन्ग सौष्ठवम् |
रामस्य च यथा रूपम् तस्य इयम् असित 
	ईक्षणा
translation:
"In whatever way is this lady's appearance, elegance of major and minor limbs, in the same 
	way is Rama's. In whatever way His appearance, in the same way is this black-eyed one's appearance."

shloka:
अस्या देव्या मनः तस्मिमः तस्य च अस्याम् प्रतिष्ठितम् |
तेन इयम् स च धर्म आत्मा मुहूर्तम् 
	अपि जीवति
translation:
"This lady's heart is in Rama, His heart is firmly in Her, for that reason She and that noble 
	Rama are able to live even for a moment."

shloka:
दुष्करम् कुरुते रामो इमाम् मत्त काशिनीम् |
सीताम् विना महा बाहुः मुहूर्तम् अपि जीवति
translation:
"Lord Rama losing Her has done an impossible task in that He still preserved His body, in that 
	He did not die from grief."

shloka:
एवम् सीताम् तदा दृष्ट्वा हृष्टः पवन सम्भवः |
जगाम मनसा रामम् प्रशशंस च तम् प्रभुम्
translation:
Hanuma, then seeing Seetha became happy thus and went by mind to Rama and also praised that 
	Lord.

shloka:
प्रशस्य तु प्रशस्तव्याम् सीताम् ताम् हरि पुम्गवः |
गुण अभिरामम् रामम् च पुनः चिन्ता परो 
अभवत्
translation:
The best among vanaras praising that Seetha who is fit to be praised, and also praising Sri Rama 
pleasing with His virtues, became immersed in thought again.

shloka:
स मुहूर्तम् इव ध्यात्वा बाष्प पर्याकुलेक्षणः |
सीताम् आश्रित्य तेजस्वी हनुमान् विललाप ह
translation:
That Hanuma the radiant one thinking for a moment, cried about Seetha and became with eyes tormented 
with tears.

shloka:
मान्या गुरु विनीतस्य लक्ष्मणस्य गुरु प्रिया |
यदि सीता अपि दुह्ख आर्ता कालो हि दुरतिक्रमः
translation:
"Respectable to Lakshmana, instructed by teachers, Seetha is also dear to teachers; if She is stricken 
with grief, destiny is indeed difficult to withstand."

shloka:
रामस्य व्यवसायज्ञा लक्ष्मणस्य च धीमतः |
न अत्यर्थम् क्षुभ्यते देवी गन्गा इव जलद आगमे
translation:
"Knowing the effort of Sri Rama and of sagacious Lakshmana, Seetha is not worried a lot, like Ganga 
in the rainy season."

shloka:
तुल्य शील वयो वृत्ताम् तुल्य अभिजन लक्षणाम् |
राघवो अर्हति वैदेहीम् तम् च इयम् असित ईक्षणा
translation:
"Sri Rama is suited to Seetha with Her well matched character, age and conduct; with well matched 
pedigree and characteristics this black-eyed Seetha is also suited to Him."

shloka:
ताम् दृष्ट्वा नव हेम आभाम् लोक कान्ताम् इव श्रियम् |
जगाम मनसा रामम् वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Seeing that Seetha with the radiance of new gold, like the goddess Laksmi, delightful to the world, 
Hanuma went by heart to Sri Rama spoke these words also.

shloka:
अस्या हेतोर् विशाल अक्ष्या हतो वाली महा बलः |
रावण प्रतिमो वीर्ये कबन्धः च निपातितः
translation:
"For the sake of this Seetha, the wide eyed one, Vali of great strength has been killed, Kabanda 
also equalling Ravana in strength has been felled."

shloka:
विराधः च हतः सम्ख्ये राक्षसो भीम विक्रमः |
वने रामेण विक्रम्य महा इन्द्रेण इव शम्बरः
translation:
"In the forest during war Virada of horrible prowess has been killed by Rama by valour, like Sambara 
by Mahendra."

shloka:
चतुर् दश सहस्राणि रक्षसाम् भीम कर्मणाम् |
निहतानि जन स्थाने शरैर् अग्नि शिख उपमैः
translation:
"At Janastaana fourteen thousands of rakshasas of terrible deed have been killed by arrows equalling 
tongues of fires."

shloka:
करः च निहतः सम्ख्ये त्रिशिराः च निपातितः |
दूषणः च महा तेजा रामेण विदित आत्मना
translation:
"By Rama with a famed mind, Khara has been killed, Trisira also has been fell down, Duushana with 
great glory also has been killed in war."

shloka:
ऐश्वर्यम् वानराणाम् च दुर्लभम् वालि पालितम् |
अस्या निमित्ते सुग्रीवः प्राप्तवान् लोक सत्कृतम्
translation:
"For Her sake Sugreeva obtained wealth of vanaras ruled by Vali difficult to be obtained and worshiped 
by the world."

shloka:
सागरः च मया क्रान्तः श्रीमान् नद नदी पतिः |
अस्या हेतोर् विशाल अक्ष्याः पुरी च इयम् निरीक्षिता
translation:
"For the sake of Her, with wide eyes, the ocean, lord of rivers and streams, has been crossed by 
me; this city also has been explored."

shloka:
यदि रामः समुद्रान्ताम् मेदिनीम् परिवर्तयेत् |
अस्याः कृते जगत् च अपि युक्तम् इति एव मे 
मतिः
translation:
"If Sri Rama for Her sake turns upside down the earth with the ocean at the end, and the entire 
universe it is fair, this is my opinion."

shloka:
राज्यम् वा त्रिषु लोकेषु सीता वा जनक आत्मजा |
त्रैलोक्य राज्यम् सकलम् सीताया न आप्नुयात् 
कलाम्
translation:
"Among three worlds, if it is a choice between kingdom or Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, all the 
kingdom of three worlds will not approach a sixteenth part of Seetha."

shloka:
इयम् सा धर्म शीलस्य जनकस्य महात्मनः |
सुता मैथिलराजस्य सीता भर्तृदृढ व्रता
translation:
"This She is that Seetha, the daughter of king Janaka of Mithila, the great soul, and noble one 
with a firm resolution towards husband."

shloka:
उत्थिता मेदिनीम् भित्त्वा क्षेत्रे हल मुख क्षते |
पद्म रेणु निभैः कीर्णा शुभैः केदार पांसुभिः
translation:
"While a field was being ploughed She rose up splitting the earth covered by auspicious dust of 
field equalling pollen."

shloka:
विक्रान्तस्य आर्य शीलस्य सम्युगेषु अनिवर्तिनः |
स्नुषा दशरथस्य एषा ज्येष्ठा राज्ञो यशस्विनी
translation:
"She is the famed eldest daughter-in-law of king Dasaratha the valorous one, not turning back in 
the battle."

shloka:
धर्मज्ञस्य कृतज्ञस्य रामस्य विदित आत्मनः |
इयम् सा दयिता भार्या राक्षसी वशम् आगता
translation:
"This She the dear wife of Rama the righteous one, grateful one, knower of Self has obtained capture 
of demonesses."

shloka:
सर्वान् भोगान् परित्यज्य भर्तृ स्नेह बलात् कृता |
अचिन्तयित्वा दुह्खानि प्रविष्टा निर्जनम् 
वनम्
translation:
"Whoever Seetha abandoning all comforts, forced by the love towards husband not thinking about 
sorrows, entering forest unpopulated with humans, being happy with fruits and roots, devoted to the service of 
Her husband, even in forest is getting great happiness like in a palace, the one with golden limbs, always with 
a smiling talk, not suited to misfortunes - that this Seetha is bearing all this suffering."

shloka:
इमाम् तु शील सम्पन्नाम् द्रष्टुम् इच्चति राघवः |
रावणेन प्रमथिताम् प्रपाम् इव पिपासितः
translation:
"Sri Rama likes to see this Seetha who is endowed with excellent character and tormented by Ravana, 
like a thirsty one for a place where water is available freely."

shloka:
अस्या नूनम् पुनर् लाभाद् राघवः प्रीतिम् एष्यति |
राजा राज्य परिभ्रष्टः पुनः प्राप्य इव 
मेदिनीम्
translation:
"By Her gain again Sri Rama definitely will get happiness like a king who lost kingdom getting 
back the land."

shloka:
काम भोगैः परित्यक्ता हीना बन्धु जनेन च |
धारयति आत्मनो देहम् तत् समागम कान्क्षिणी
translation:
"Left by coveted enjoyments, lacking relatives also Seetha is keeping body desirous of meeting 
with Sri Rama."

shloka:
न एषा पश्यति राक्षस्यो न इमान् पुष्प फल द्रुमान् |
एकस्थ हृदया नूनम् रामम् एव अनुपश्यति
translation:
"She is not seeing demonesses, not flowers, fruits or trees and with a single heart is meditating 
only on Sri Rama - this is sure."

shloka:
भर्ता नाम परम् नार्या भूषणम् भूषणाद् अपि |
एषा हि रहिता तेन शोभन अर्हा न शोभते
translation:
"Husband is indeed the greatest adornment for a woman greater than jewellery; this Seetha though 
deserving of decoration, is not looking charming without Sri Rama."

shloka:
दुष्करम् कुरुते रामो हीनो यद् अनया प्रभुः |
धारयति आत्मनो देहम् न दुह्खेन अवसीदति
translation:
"Sri Rama although bereft of Her that Lord Rama is doing an impossible task by retaining His body 
and not being depressed by sorrow."

shloka:
इमाम् असित केश अन्ताम् शत पत्र निभ ईक्षणाम् |
सुख अर्हाम् दुःखिताम् ज्~आत्वा मम अपि व्यथितम् 
मनः
translation:
"Knowing Her with black ended hairs, with lotus like eyes, deserving of comforts, and in sorrow, 
my mind also is gloomy."

shloka:
क्षिति क्षमा पुष्कर सम्निभ अक्षी |
या रक्षिता राघव लक्ष्मणाभ्याम् |
सा राक्षसीभिर् विकृत 
ईक्षणाभिः |
सम्रक्ष्यते सम्प्रति वृक्ष मूले
translation:
"Whoever Seetha with earth-like patience, with eyes resembling lotuses, was protected by Sri Rama 
and Lakshmana, that Seetha now is being guarded by ogresses with crooked eyes at the base of a tree."

shloka:
हिम हत नलिनी इव नष्ट शोभा |
व्यसन परम्परया निपीड्यमाना |
सह चर रहिता इव चक्र वाकी |
जनक सुता कृपणाम् दशाम् प्रपन्ना
translation:
"With lost glory like a lotus plant hit by snow, being tormented by a series of calamities, Seetha 
obtained a pitiable condition like a chakravaka bird without a companion."

shloka:
अस्या हि पुष्प अवनत अग्र शाखाः |
शोकम् दृढम् वै जनयति अशोकाः |
हिम व्यपायेन च शीतरश्मिः 
|
रभ्युत्थितो न एक सहस्र रश्मिः
translation:
"Ashoka trees with bent branches due to flowers are giving rise to gloom a lot to Her; Due to melting 
of snow the risen up moon also with thousands of rays is causing grief."

shloka:
इति एवम् अर्थम् कपिर् अन्ववेक्ष्य |
सीता इयम् इति एव निविष्ट बुद्धिः |
संश्रित्य तस्मिन् 
निषसाद वृक्षे |
बली हरीणाम् ऋषभः तरस्वी
translation:
The mighty one, the best among vanaras, quick one, Hanuma thus observed the subject: "This is Seetha!" 
- thus with a firm mind sat at that tree, leaning against it.

shloka:
ततः कुमुदषण्डाभो निर्मलम् निर्मलोदयः |
प्रजगाम नभश्चन्द्रो हंसो नीलमिवोदकम् || ५-१७- १
translation:
Thereafter the moon with a peaceful rise, with radiance equaling that of a group of lotuses, obtained 
the clear sky like a swan obtaining blue water.

shloka:
साचिव्यमिव कुर्वन् स प्रभया निर्मलप्रभः |
चन्द्रमा रश्मभिः शीतैः सिषेवे पवनात्मजम्
translation: That moon with a peaceful glow served Hanuma with cool rays as though performing help with radiance.

shloka:
स ददर्श ततः सीताम् पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननाम् |
शोकभारैरिव न्यस्तां भारैर्नावमिवाम्भसि
translation:
Thereafter Hanuma saw Seetha with a face like a full moon, put down by the weight of grief, like 
a ship sinking down in water due to weight.

shloka:
दिदृक्षमाणो वैदेहीम् हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः |
स ददर्शाविदूरस्था राक्षसीर्घोरदर्शनाः
translation:
Hanuma wanting to see Seetha saw nearby ogresses with horrible appearance - one with one eye; one 
with a single ear and also one with ears as covering; one with conch shell like ears; one with fattened nose up 
to head; one with lean and long neck; one with disheveled hair and also one without hair; one with blanket like 
hair; one with hanging stomach and breasts; one with hanging face; one with lips at chin; one with hanging face; 
one with hanging knees; one who is short; one who is tall and also hunch backed one; one who is distorted; a dwarf 
one and also one with high teeth and one with crooked mouth, one with green eyes and one with a horrible face.

shloka:
विकृताः पिङ्गलाः कालीः क्रोधनाः कलहप्रियाः |
कालायसमहाशूलकूटमुद्गधारिणीः
translation:
Hanuma saw horrible ogresses, dark complexioned ones, angry ones, those who like quarrels, ones 
wearing big darts, mallets and clubs of iron, with faces like those of pigs, deer, tigers, buffaloes, goats, she-foxes, 
with feet like those of elephants, camels, horses, with heads sunk into bodies, with single hand and single foot, 
those ears like that of donkeys and horses, those with cow ears, those with elephant ears, those with monkey ears, 
and some others without nose, those with horizontal nose, those with crooked nose, those with elephant-like nose, 
toes with nose fixed in forehead, with feet like those of elephant, those with big feet, those with cow like feet, 
those with hair on their feet, those with big heads and necks, those with big nipples and big stomach, those with 
big eyes and mouths, with long tongues and nails, and also the a face like that of a she-goat, those with elephant 
like face, those with face like that of a cow, those with face of a she-pig, those with faces like those of horses, 
camels, donkeys, those with horrible appearance, ogresses carrying pikes and clubs in their hand, angry ones, 
those who like quarrels, those with high teeth, with hair color like that of smoke, with horrible faces, always 
drinking liquor, always desiring meat and liquor, with body smeared by meat and blood, with meat and blood as 
food, whose appearance made hair to stand up, sitting around a great tree with huge trunk.

shloka: तस्याधस्ताच्च ताम् देवीम् राजपुत्रीमनिन्दिताम्
translation:
Hanuma the glorious one saw that Seetha, the princess, daughter of Janaka, unblemished one below 
that tree.

shloka: निष्प्रभाम् षोकसन्तप्ताम् मलसम्कुलमूर्धजाम्
translation:
She was lack luster being tormented by grief, with hair covered by dirt, with merits exhausted, 
like star fallen from heavens onto ground.

shloka: चारित्रव्यपदेशाड्यां भर्तृदर्शनदुर्गताम्
translation:
She was rich with fame of lofty character, poor due to not seeing husband, lacking excellent ornaments, 
with husband's love as ornament.

shloka: राक्षसाधिपसम्रुद्धाम् बन्धुभिश्च विना कृताम्
translation:
Being held captive by Ravana, without any relatives, She was like a she-elephant without herd, 
being detained by a lion.

shloka: चन्द्ररेखाम् पयोदान्ते शारदाब्रैरिवावृताम्
translation:
She was like moon being covered by clouds at the end of rainy season with an appearance lacking 
lustre due to lack of contact with husband, was like an unplucked Veena.

shloka: स ताम् भर्तवशे युक्तामयुक्ताम् राक्षसीवशे
translation:
Hanuma saw Seetha being suited to be with her husband, in the custody of ogresses, in the middle 
of Ashoka garden being immersed in an ocean of grief

shloka: ताभिः परिवृताम् तत्र सग्रहामिव रोहिणीम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Seetha there surrounded by those ogresses, like Rohini with planets, like a creeper 
without flowers.

shloka: सा मलेन च दिग्धाङ्गीवपुषा चाप्यलंकृता
translation:
With body smeared with dirt, being graced by Her body, that Seetha shone and also did not shine, 
like a lotus-fibre covered with dirt.

shloka: मलिनेन तु वस्त्रेण परिक्लिष्टेन भामिनीम्
translation:
The monkey Hanuma saw that Seetha with great beauty with black eyes, covered by a cloth which was 
creased and dirty, with eyes of a deer, with a pitiful face, not depressed due to the brilliance of her husband, 
protected by her own character.

shloka:
ताम् दृष्ट्वा हनुमान् सीताम् मृगशाबनिभेक्षणाम् |
मृगकन्यामिव त्रस्ताम् वीक्षमाणाम् समन्ततः
translation:
Hanuma became happy on seeing Seetha with eyes of a fawn, fearful like a she-deer, seeing trees 
with young shoots, as though being burnt by sighs, like a bundle of grief, with a wave of sorrow risen up.

shloka:
ताम् क्षमां सुविभक्ताङ्गीं विनाभरणशोभिनीम् |
प्रहर्षमतुलम् लेभे मारुतिः प्रेक्ष्य मैथिलीम्
translation:
Hanuma the son of wind god on seeing Seetha that Seetha like the goddess earth, with well divided 
body parts shining eve without ornaments, obtained great joy.

shloka:
हर्षजानि च सोऽश्रूणि ताम् दृष्ट्वा मदिरेक्षणाम् |
मुमुचे हनुमांस्तत्र नमश्चक्रे च राघवम्
translation:
Hanuma on seeing Seetha there with intoxicating eyes shed tears of joy and also paid obeisance 
to Sri Rama.

shloka:
नमस्कृत्वा रामाय लक्ष्मणाय च वीर्यवान् |
सीतादर्शनसम्हृष्टो हनुमान् सम्वृतोऽभवत्
translation:
Being joyful on seeing Seetha, Hanuma the mighty one paid obeisance to Sri Rama and to Lakshmana 
and became covered with leaves.

shloka:
तथा विप्रेक्षमाणस्य वनम् पुष्पितपादपम् |
विचिन्वतश्च वैदेहीम् किंचिच्चेषा निशाभवत्
translation:
A little of the night was left while Hanuma was searching like that for Seetha in the garden with 
flowers in blossom.

shloka:
षडङ्गवेदविदुषाम् क्रतुप्रवरयाजिनाम् |
शुश्राव ब्रह्मघोषान् स विरात्रे ब्रह्मरक्षसाम्
translation:
That Hanuma heard Vedic sounds early in the morning of Brahma Rakshasas well versed in six parts 
of Vedas and those who performed excellent sacrifices.

shloka:
अथ मङ्गलवादित्रशब्दैः श्रुतिमनोहरैः |
प्रबुध्यत महाबाहुर्दशग्रीवो महाबलः
translation:
Thereafter Ravana with great arms and great prowess was woken by the sounds of various auspicious 
musical instruments pleasing to the ear.

shloka:
विबुध्य तु यथाकालम् राक्षसेन्द्रः प्रतापवान् |
स्रस्तमाल्याम्बरधरो वैदेहीमन्वचिन्तयात्
translation:
The king of rakshasas with great might woke up at the appropriate hour wearing slippery flower 
garlands remembered about Seetha.

shloka:
भृशं नियुक्तस्तस्याम् च मदनेन मदोत्कटः |
न स तं राक्षसः कामं शशाकात्मनि गूहितुम्
translation:
In that Seetha's matter, directed a lot by the god of love and excited by passion, that Rakshasa 
was not capable to suppress in self that desire.

shloka:
स सर्वाभरणैर्युक्तो बिभच्छ्रियमनुत्तमाम् |
तां नगैर्बहुभिर्जुष्टाम् सर्वपुष्पफलोपगैः
translation:
Together with all ornaments wearing great glory that Ravana entered that Ashoka garden having a 
lot of trees with all fruits and flowers.

shloka:
वृतां पुष्करिणीभिश्च नानापुष्पोपशोभिताम् |
सदामदैश्च विहगैर्विचित्राम् परमाद्भुताम्
translation:
Ravana entered that great wonderful Ashoka garden together with lakes, shone by various flowers, 
brilliant with birds always in rut.

shloka:
ईहामृगैश्च विविधैर्जुष्टां डृष्टिमनोहरैः |
वीथीः संप्रेक्षमाणश्च मणिकाञ्चनतोरणाः
translation:
Ravana entered Ashoka garden seeing archways of gold and gems crowded by artificial deer of various 
kinds ravishing eyes and mind, filled with animals of various kinds, together with fallen fruits and full of trees.

shloka:
अङ्गनाशतमात्रं तु तं व्रजन्तमनुव्रजत् |
महेन्द्रमिव पौलस्त्यम्ं देवगन्धर्वयोषितः
translation:
While He was going only a hundred of women followed that Ravana like Deva and Gandharva women following 
Indra.

shloka:
दीपिकाः काञ्चनीः काश्चिज्जगृहुस्तत्र योषितः |
वालव्यजनहस्ताश्च तालवृन्तानि चापराः
translation:
There some women bore lamps of gold; some others carried chowries; some others had fans of Palmyra 
leaves in their hands.

shloka:
काञ्चनैरपि भृङ्गारैर्जह्रुः सलिलमग्रतः |
मण्डलागान् ब्रुसींश्चापि गृह्यान्याः पृष्ठतो ययुः
translation:
Some women carried water in small vessels of gold; some others followed in the back taking pillows 
with circular ends.

shloka:
काचिद्रत्नमयीं स्थालीं पूर्णां पानस्य ब्राजतम् |
दक्षिणा दक्षिणेनैव तदा जग्राह पाणिना
translation:
One woman to the right of Ravana held with her right hand a vessel with gem stones filled with 
liqour.

shloka:
राजहंसप्रतीकाशं चत्रं पूर्णशशिप्रभम् |
सौवर्णदण्डमपरा गृहीत्वा पृष्ठतो ययौ
translation:
Another woman went at back taking an umbrella equalling a royal swan with the radiance of full 
moon with a golden handle.

shloka:
निद्रामदपरीताक्ष्यो रावनस्योत्तमाः स्त्रियः |
अनुजग्मुः पतिं वीरम् घनम् विद्युल्लता इव
translation: With sleepy eyes best women of Ravana followed mighty husband like lightning following a cloud.

shloka:
व्याविद्धहारकेयूराः समामृदितवर्णकाः |
समागळितकेशान्ताः सस्वेदवदनास्तथा
translation:
With displaced necklaces and armlets, with effaced cover of sandal-paste, with dishevelled hair, 
and also with sweaty faces, staggering due to surviving trace of liquor and due to sleepiness, with shrivelled 
flowers on perspiring bodies, with dishevelled hair along with good garlands, with intoxicating eyes, women who 
were dear wives followed that king of Rakshasas who was going due to respect and due to love.

shloka:
स च कामपराधीनः पतिस्तासां महाबलः |
सीतासक्तमना मन्दो मन्दाञ्चितगतिर्बभौ
translation:
Husband of those women, of great might, who was surrendered to lust, that Ravana also who was dull 
witted, with his mind interested in Seetha shone with a slow and beautiful gait.

shloka:
ततः काञ्चीनिनादं च नूपुराणाम् च निस्वनम् |
शुश्राव परमस्त्रीणां स कपिर्मारुतात्मजः
translation:
Thereafter that Hanuma, the son of wind-god heard the sound of waist-bands and the sound of anklets 
of those excellent women.

shloka:
तं चाप्रतिमकर्माणमचिन्त्यबलपौरुषम् |
द्वारदेशमनुप्राप्तं ददर्श हनुमान् कपिः
translation:
Hanuma the monkey saw that Ravana also, performer of deeds without an equal, with unfathomable 
might and virility, reaching the entrance region.

shloka:
दीपिकाभिरनेकाभिः समन्तादवभासितम् |
गन्धतैलावसिक्ताभिर्द्रियमाणाभिरग्रतः
translation:
Wettened by fragrant oil, being carried in front of Ravana, Hanuma saw Ravana being shone in all 
directions by many lamps.

shloka:
कामदर्पमदैर्युक्तं जिह्मताम्रायतेक्षणम् |
समक्षमिव कन्दर्पमपविद्धशरासनम्
translation:
Hanuma saw Ravana together with lust, vanity and intoxication, with wide red eyes which were slanted, 
like the god of love in person with bow kept at a distance.

shloka:
मथितामृतफेनाभमरजोवस्त्रमुत्तमम् |
सलीलमनुकर्षन्तं विमुक्तं सक्तमङ्गदे
translation:
Hanuma saw Ravana playfully readjusting his excellent upper garment with the luster of churned 
nectar froth, without stain,slipping being entangled in armlet.

shloka:
तं पत्रविटपे लीनः अत्रपुष्पघनावृतह् |
समीपमिव संक्रान्तं निध्यातुमुपचक्रमे
translation:
Hanuma blended in a branch full of leaves covered by groups of leaves and flowers started to see 
that Ravana as though coming near Him.

shloka:
अवेक्षमाणस्तु ततो ददर्श कपिकुञ्जरः |
रूपयौवनसंपन्ना रावणस्य वरस्तियः
translation:
Thereafter Hanuma, the best among Vanaras looking in all directions saw best women of Ravana full 
of beauty and youth.

shloka:
ताभिः परिवृतो राजा सुरूपाभिर्महायशाः |
तस्मृगद्विजसम्घष्टं प्रविष्टः प्रमदावनम्
translation:
King of great fame, Ravana, together with those women with good appearance entered that garden 
resounded by animals and birds.

shloka:
क्षीबो विचित्राभरणः शङ्कुकर्णो महाबलः |
तेन विश्रवसः पुत्रः स दृष्टो राक्षसाधिपः
translation:
That king of Rakshasas who was intoxicated with wonderful ornaments, with pointed ears, son of 
Visravasa was like the moon together with stars, together with best women was seen by Hanuma. That great Vanara 
with great brilliance saw that Ravana with glory.

shloka:
रावणोऽयम् महाबाहुरिति संचिन्त्य वानरः |
अवप्लुतो महातेजा हनुमान्मारुतात्मजः
translation:
The son of god of wind Vanara Hanuma of great brilliance thinking thus "This long armed one is 
Ravana", jumped down.

shloka:
स तथाप्युग्रतेजाः सन्निर्धूतस्तस्य तेजसा |
पत्रगुह्यान्तरे सक्तो हनुमान् संवृतोऽभवत्
translation:
Thus Hanuma although of terrible energy was overshadowed by Ravana's brilliance and became rooted 
behind a group of leaves and was concealed.

shloka:
स तामसितकेशान्तां सुश्रोणीं संहतस्तनीम् |
दिदृक्षुरसितापाङ्गमुपावर्तत रावणः
translation:
That Ravana neared Seetha with black hair, with charming limbs with well knit breasts, with black 
corners of eyes, wishing to see Her.

shloka:
तस्मिन्नेव ततः काले राजपुत्री त्वनिन्दिता |
रूपयौवनसम्पन्नं भूषणोत्तमभूषितम्
translation:
Thereafter at that time Seetha a princess without any blame of excellent limbs shook like a plantain 
tree in wind on seeing Ravana the king of rakshasas endowed with beauty and youth adorned with excellent ornaments.

shloka:
आच्छाद्योदरमूरुभ्यां बाहुभ्यां च पयोधरौ |
उपविष्टा विशालाक्षी रुदन्ती वरवर्णिनी
translation:
The wide eyed Seetha with excellent color covering stomach with thighs and breasts with hands sat 
down crying.

shloka:
दशग्रीवस्तु वैदेहीम् रक्षितां राक्षसीगणैः |
ददर्श दीनाम् दुःखार्तां नावं सन्नामिवार्णवे
translation:
Ravana saw Seetha protected by batches of ogres looking miserable being struck with grief like 
a ship in danger in the sea.

shloka:
असंवृतायामासीनाम् धरण्याम् संशितव्रताम् |
चिनां प्रपतितां भूमौ शाखामिव वनस्पतेः
translation:
Hanuma saw Seetha sitting down on uncovered land, with a firm resolve, like a branch of a tree 
fallen down on earth being torn from the tree.

shloka:
मलमण्डनचित्राङ्गीम् मण्डनार्हाममण्डिताम् |
मृणाली पङ्कदिग्धेव विभाति न विभाति च
translation:
Hanuma saw Seetha with a stange body with dirt as ornament, who although suited to decorate with 
ornaments was without ornaments. Although She was shining like a lotus stem covered with mud, She was not shining 
also.

shloka:
समीपम् राजसिम्हस्य रामस्य विदितात्मनः |
सङ्कल्पहयसम्युक्तैर्यान्तीमिव मनोरथैः
translation:
Seetha was as though going near to Rama a lion among kings with a famous personality with desires 
as chariot tied with thoughts as horses.

shloka:
शुष्यन्तीम् रुदतीमेकां ध्यानशोकपरायणाम् |
दुःखस्यान्तमपश्यन्तीं रामां राममनुव्रताम्
translation:
Seetha a pleasant one, was emaciated, was crying, being alone having surrendered to Her thoughts 
and sorrow not seeing the end of grief, following the will of Rama.

shloka:
चेष्टमानां तथाविष्टां पन्नगेन्द्रवधूमिव |
धूप्यमानाम् ग्रहेणेव रोहिणीं धूमकेतुना
translation:
And also Seetha was like a great she-serpant writhing under the spell of an incantation. She was 
like Rohini being fumigated by a smoke colored planet called Ketu.

shloka:
वृत्तशीलकुले जातामाचारवति धार्मिके |
पुनः संस्कारमापन्नां जातामिव च दुष्कुले
translation:
Being born in a virtuous traditional family with good conduct and character and getting married, 
Seetha appeared as if She was born in a bad family.

shloka:
अभूतेनापवादेन कीर्तीम् निपतितामिव |
अम्नायानामयोगेन विद्यां प्रशिथिलामिव
translation:
Seetha was like fame fallen down due to false blame. She was like education ruined due to lack 
of learning by heart.

shloka:
सन्नामिव महाकीर्तिं श्रद्धामिव विमानिताम् |
प्रज्ञामिव परिक्षीणामाशां प्रतिहतामिव
translation:
Seetha was like deteriorated great fame,like insulted faith,like an understanding grown feeble, 
like dulled hope.

shloka:
आयतीमिव विध्वस्तामाज्ञां प्रतिहतामिव |
दीप्तामिव दिशं काले पूजामपहृतामिव
translation:
Seetha was like an expectation destroyed, like an order flouted; like a blazing quarter during 
a period of destruction, like a worship stolen.

shloka:
पद्मिनीमिव विध्वस्तां हतशूरां चमूमिव |
प्रभामिव तमोध्वस्तामुपक्षीणामिवापगाम्
translation:
Seetha was like a lotus destroyed, like an army with killed warriors, like light destroyed by darkness, 
like vanished river.

shloka:
वेदीमिव परामृष्टां शान्तामग्निशिखामिव |
पौर्णमासीमिव निशां राहुग्रस्तेन्दुमण्डलाम्
translation:
Seetha was like an altar desecrated, like a tongue of fire gone out, like a full moon night with 
moon devoured by Rahu.

shloka:
उत्कृष्टपर्णकमलां वित्रासितविहङ्गमाम् |
हस्तिहस्तपरामृष्टमाकुलां पद्मिनीमिव
translation:
Seetha was like a lotus pond agitated with torned out leaves and lotuses, being roughly traeated 
by the trunk of an elephant.

shloka:
पतिशोकातुरां शुष्कां नदीं विस्रावितामिव |
परया मृजया हीनाम् कृष्णपक्षनिशामिव
translation:
Grieved for husband, Seetha was like a river which has dried uo with water caused to flow out lacking 
best washing, was like a new moon night.

shloka:
सुकुमारीम् सुजाताङ्गीं रत्न गर्भगृहोचिताम् |
तप्यमानामिवोष्णेन मृणालीमचिरोद्धृताम्
translation:
Seetha was a delicate one with well built limbs, accustomed to houses full of diamonds, being tormented 
by heat, like a lotus fibre uprooted short time back.

shloka:
गृहीतामाळितां स्तम्भे यूथपेन विनाकृताम् |
निःश्वसन्तीं सुदुःखार्तां गजराजवधूमिव
translation:
Seetha was like a she-elephant captured and tied to a pillar, made to be without the leader of 
herd, sighing, very much tormented by grief.

shloka:
एकया दीर्घया वेण्या शोभमानामयत्नतः |
नीलया नीरदापाये वनराज्या महीमिव
translation:
With a long single plait, shining without effort, Seetha was like the earth with dark groups of 
trees at the end of rainy season.

shloka:
उपवासेन शोकेन ध्यानेन च भयेन च |
परिक्षीणां कृशां दीनामल्पाहारां तपोधनाम्
translation:
Wasted, emaciated due to fasting, due to sorrow, due to thought and due to fear, Seetha was with 
limited food and with austerity as wealth.

shloka:
आयाचमानाम् दुःखार्तां प्राञ्जलिं देवतामिव |
भावेन रघुमुख्यस्य दशग्रीवपराभवम्
translation:
Seetha was like a celestial being, tormented by grief and by thought with joined palms, desiring 
the defeat of Ravana at the hands of Sri Rama

shloka:
समीक्षमाणां रुदतीमनिन्दितां |
सुपक्ष्मताम्रायतशुक्ललोचनाम् |
अनुव्रतां राममतीव मैथिलीं 
|
प्रलोभयामास वधाय रावणः
translation:
Ravana was trying to allure and threatening death to Seetha who was looking at every direction, 
crying, without blame, with good eye lids and reddish and white eyes, with an excessive vow to follow Sri Rama.

shloka:
स ताम् परिवृतां दीनां निरानन्दां तपस्विनीम् |
साकारैर्मधुरैर्वाक्यैर्न्यदर्शयत रावणः
translation:
Ravana conveyed in significant words to that Seetha who was surrounded by ogresses, wretched, without 
happiness and pitiable.

shloka:
मां दृष्ट्वा नागनासोरु गूहमाना स्तनोदरम् |
अदर्शनमिवात्मानं भयान्नेतुं त्वमिच्चसि
translation:
"You are with thighs like the trunk of an elephant. Seeing me covering your breasts and belly, 
you desire obtaining disappearance of self due to fear.

shloka:
कामये त्वाम् विशालाक्षि बहुमन्यस्व मां प्रिये |
सर्वाङ्गगुणसम्पन्ने सर्वलोकमनोहरे
translation:
"O wide eyed one! You are endowed with bodily excellencies, pleasing to all people. I desire you. 
O lovable one! respect me."

shloka:
नेह केचिन्मनुष्या वा राक्षसाः कामरूपिणः |
व्यपसर्पतु ते सीते भयम् मत्तः समुत्थितम्
translation:
"O Seetha! Here there are no humans or ogres with ability to change form. Let your fear caused 
due to me be removed."

shloka:
स्वधर्मो रक्षसां भीरु सर्वथैव न संशयः |
गमनं वा परस्त्रीणाम् हरणम् सम्प्रमथ्य वा
translation:
"O one with fear! Obtaining women belonging to others or abducting by force is the righteous deed 
for ogres by all means. There is no doubt in this."

shloka:
एवं चैतदकामां तु न त्वां स्प्रक्ष्यामि मैथिलि |
कामम् कामः शरीरे मे यथाकामं प्रार्तताम्
translation:
"O Seetha! It is like this. desire very much may behave in whatever way it likes in my body. But 
I will not touch you without lust."

shloka:
देवि नेह भयम् कार्यम् मयि विश्वसिहि प्रिये |
प्रणयस्व च तत्वएन मैवम् भूः शिकलालसा
translation:
"O queen of my heart! In this matter fear is not to be made. O love! Believe in me. Truly become 
with love. Do not become absorbed in sorrow like this."

shloka:
एकवेणी धराशय्या ध्यानं मलिनमम्बरम् |
अस्थानेऽप्युपवासश्च नैतान्यौपयिकानि ते
translation:
"Single plait, the bed of ground,mediation,dirty cloth,fasting at an inappropriate time - all these 
are not useful to you."

shloka:
विचित्राणि च माल्यानि चन्दनान्यगरूणि च |
विविधानि च वासांसि द्व्यान्याभरणानि च
translation:
"O Seetha! After getting me gain wonderful garlands, sandals, Agallochums, a variety of cloths 
and best ornaments, the best drinks, beds and seats, song and dance and musical instrument."

shloka:
स्त्रीरत्नमसि मैवम् भूः कुरु गात्रेषु भूषणम् |
मां प्राप्य हि कथम् नु स्यास्त्वमनर्हा सुविग्रहे
translation:
"You are a gem among women. Do not be like this. Make decoration on your limbs. O one with a good 
body! Getting me how will you become unsuited for luxuries?"

shloka:
इदम् ते चारु सम्जातम् यौवनम् व्यतिवर्तते |
यदतीतं पुनर्नैति स्रोतः शीघ्रमपामिव
translation:
"This your youth born beautifully is passing away, whichever youth is quickly passing away will 
not come back again like the flow of water."

shloka:
त्वां कृत्वोपरतो मन्ये रूपकर्ता स विश्वसृक् |
न हि रूपोपमा त्वन्या तवास्ति शुभदर्शने
translation:
"O one with auspicious appearance! The creator of form, that creator of the world, Lord Brahma 
has made you and stopped - I think thus. There is not another who is equal to your appearance."

shloka:
त्वाम् समाअसाद्य वैदेहि रूपयौवनशालिनीम् |
कः पुमानतिवर्तेत साक्षादपि पितामहः
translation:
"O Seetha! Obtaining you endowed with beauty and youth, which man even if he is Lord Brahma himself 
will disregard (leave) you."

shloka:
यद्यत्पश्यामि ते गात्रम् शीतांशुसदृशानने |
तस्मिंस्तस्मिन् पृधुश्रोणि चक्षुर्मम निबध्यते
translation:
"O one with face like that of moon! O one with broad hips! Your whichever limb I see, my eye is 
getting tied in that that limb."

shloka:
भव मैथिलि भाया मे मोहमेनम् विसर्जय |
बह्वीनामुत्तमस्त्रीणामाहृतानामितस्ततः
translation:
"O Seetha! Become my wife. Leave this ignorance. In all my many best women brought from here and 
there, become foremost consort. Let there be auspicious to you."

shloka: लोकेभो यानि रत्नानि सम्प्रमथ्याहृतानि वै
translation:
"O timid one! Whatever gems that have been brought by force, all those, my this kingdom and also 
myself belong to you."

shloka: विजित्य पृथिवीं सर्वां नानानगरमालिनीम्
translation:
"O charmful lady! Conquering the entire earth together with chain of various cities for your sake, 
I can give to king Janaka.

shloka: नेह पश्यामि लोकेऽन्यम् यो मे प्रतिबलो भवेत्
translation: "In this world I do not see another one who is equally matched to me. See my very great power."

shloka: असकृत्सम्युगे भग्ना मया विमृदितध्वजाः
translation:
"Suras and Asuras defeated with broken flags by me in war many times are powerless to stand in 
an army against me."

shloka: इच्छ मां क्रियतामद्य प्रतिकर्म तवोत्तमम्
translation:
"Desire me! Now let your best decoration be made. On your body let ornaments also with great brilliance 
be fit. I will see well your form together with decoration."

shloka:
प्रतिकर्माभिसम्युक्ता दाक्षिण्येन वरानने |
भुम्क्ष्व भोगान्यथाकामं पिब भीरु रमस्व च
translation:
"O one with best face! O timid one! With consideration enjoy luxuries according to your desire 
together with decoration. Drink. Rejoice."

shloka:
यथेच्छम् च प्रयच्छ त्वं पृथिवीम् वा धनानि च |
ललस्व मयि विस्रब्धा धृष्टमाज्ञापयस्व च
translation:
"You donate land and wealth according to your wish. With confidence behave freely in my matter. 
Fearlessly order also."

shloka:
मत्र्पसादाल्ललन्त्याश्च ललन्तां बान्धवास्तव |
बुद्धिं ममानुपश्य त्वम् श्रियम् भद्रे यशश्च 
मे
translation:
" By my grace with your sporting, tour relatives will also sport. O auspicious one! You see my 
wealth and my fame."

shloka:
किं करिष्यसि रामेण सुभगे चीरवाससा |
निक्षिप्तविजयो रामो गतश्रीर्वनगोचरः
translation:
"O beautiful one! What can you do with Rama clad in tatters, with lost hope of victory, with gone 
fortune. Roaming in forests, observing austerities and also sleeping on floor, I doubt if Rama is alive or not."

shloka: न हि वैदेहि रांस्त्वां द्रष्टुं वा प्युपलस्स्यते
translation:
"O Seetha, Rama indeed does not get opportunity even to see you like moonlight covered by dark 
clous with cranes at the front."

shloka: न चापि मम हस्तात्त्वां प्राप्तुमर्हति राघवः
translation: "Like Keerthi got by Hiranyakasipu from Indra's hand, Rama is not suited to get you from my hands."

shloka: चारुस्मिते चारुदति चारुनेत्रे विलासिनि
translation:
"O one with a beautiful smile! O one with beautiful teeth!O one with beautiful eyes! O charmful 
one! O timid one! You are stealing my heart like a serpent stolen by Garuda.

shloka: क्लिष्टकौशेयवसनाम् तन्वीमप्यनलम्कृताम्
translation:
"You are Wearing a silk cloth in a bad condition. You are emaciated. Even though you have not decorated, 
seeing you I am not getting happiness in my wives."

shloka: अन्तः पुरविनासिन्यः स्त्रियः सर्वगुणान्विताः
translation:
"O Seetha! whoever women living in gynaeceum endowed with all virtues, have sovereignty on all 
of them."

shloka: मम ह्यसितकेशान्ते त्रैलोक्यप्रवराः स्त्रियः
translation:
"O one with black hair! My those women and apsarasas who are the best among the three worlds will 
serve you like the goddess of wealth."

shloka: यानि वैश्रवणे सुभ्रु रत्नानि च धनानि च
translation:
"O one with beautiful hips! O one with beuatiful eyebrows! Enjoy according to your comfort whatever 
gems and wealth belonging to Kubera, all those three worlds and me."

shloka: न रामस्तपसा देवि न बलेन विक्रमैः
translation:
"O Seetha! Rama is not equal to me by austerity, not equal by might; not equal by strength, not 
equal by wealth, by brilliance and by fame."

shloka:
पिब विहर रमस्व भुंक्ष्व भोगान् |
धननिचौअम् प्रदिशामि मेदिनीम् च |
मयि लल ललने यथासुखम् 
त्वम् |
त्वयि च समेत्य ललन्तु बान्धव्वस्ते
translation:
"O playful one! I will give hordes of wealth and land. You drink. Roam freely and play. Enjoy luxuries. 
Sport according to comfort in me. Your relatives may sport together in you."

shloka:
कनकविमलहारभूषिताङ्गी |
विहर मया सह भीरु काननानि
translation:
"O timid one! With body decorated with gold colored, pure garlands, roam with me in forests born 
at sea shore filled with groups of flowered trees and with humble bees."

shloka:
तस्य तद्वचनम् श्रुत्वा सीता रौद्रस्य रक्षसः |
आर्ता दीनस्वरा दीनम् प्रत्युवाच ततः शनैः
translation:
Seetha listening to that horrible ogre's word, being tormented spoke in reply with a pitiable voice, 
pitifully and slowly.

shloka:
दुःखार्ता रुदती सीता वेपमाना तपस्विनी |
चिन्तयन्ती वरारोह पतिमेव पतिव्रता
translation:
Being tormented by grief, in a pitiful state, with excellent limbs, devoted to husband, thinking 
about husband alone, with pleasant smiles Seetha was sobbing, shivering and placing a straw in between herself 
and Ravana spoke thus in reply.

shloka: निवर्तय मनो मत्तः स्वजने क्रियतां मनः
translation:
"Turn your mind back from me. Let your mind be made on your own wives. Like best emancipation for 
a sinner, it is not appropriate to pray me."

shloka: अकार्यम् न मया कार्यमेकपत्न्या विगर्हितम्
translation:
"I was born in a great family. Getting such family, having one husband, a bad deed which is blameable 
is not to be made by me."

shloka: एवमुक्त्वा तु वैदेही रावणम् तम् यशस्विनी
translation: Seetha with renown thus speaking to that Ravana, turned back and spoke words again.

shloka: वाहमौपयिकी भार्या परभार्या सती तव
translation:
"I who am wife of another and devoted to husband am not suitable wife to you. Observe righteousness 
well. Follow well course of conduct of virtuous."

shloka: यथा तव तथान्येषां दारा रक्ष्या विशाचर
translation:
"O Ogre! How your wives are to be protected, in the same way others' wives are to be protected. 
Making yourself as an example enjoy your own wives."

shloka: अतुष्टं स्वेषु दारेषु चपलम् चलितेन्द्रियम्
translation:
"One who is not satisfied in own wives, a fickle-minded one with disturbed senses, mean minded 
one, to such a man, others' wives will lead to humilation."

shloka: इह सन्तो न वा सन्ति सतो वा नानुवर्तसे
translation:
"Here are there not good people? Or are you not following those who are good? It must be like that 
because your mind, devoid of traditions is perverse."

shloka: वचो मिथ्याप्रणीतात्मा पथ्यमुक्तं विचक्षणैः
translation:
"You who is being led by mind towards unreal is not taking wholesome words being said by righteous 
onesfor the destruction of ogres."

shloka: आकृतात्मानमासाद्य राजानमनये रतम्
translation:
"After getting a king who has uncontrolled mind, interested in a bad path, wealthy states and cities 
also will be destroyed. After getting you like that this Lanka filled with best things in a short while will be 
destroyed due to your one sin."

shloka: स्वकृतैर्हन्यमानस्य आवणादीर्घदर्शिनः
translation:
"O Ravana! When there is destruction of a short sighted one being hit by his own deeds, a sinner, 
living beings will be happy."

shloka: एवं त्वां पापकर्माणम् वक्ष्यन्ति निकृता जनाः
translation:
"About you who is a sinner thus being destroyed, people who have been humiliated by you being happy 
will speak thus: 'The cruel Ravana by God's grace has got this danger' ".

shloka: शक्या लोभयितुं नाहमैश्वर्येण धनेन वा
translation:
"I am not capable to be tempted by wealth or by money. I am not separate with Raghava like the 
sun-shine with the sun."

shloka: उपधाय भुजम् तस्य लोकनाथस्य सत्कृतम्
translation:
"After making as a pillow that worshipped shoulder of that lord of the world, of that Rama, how 
can I make as pillow some other one's shoulder?"

shloka: अहमौपयीकी भार्या तस्यैव वसुधापतेः
translation:
"Like the education of a brahmin with a famous mind, initiated in religious vow, I am suitable 
wife to that Rama alone the lord of earth."

shloka: साधु रावण रामेण मां समानय दुःखिताम्
translation: "O Ravana! Let me meet together with Rama like a female elephant with a male elephant in a forest."

shloka: मित्रमौपयिकम् कर्तुम् रामः स्थानम् परीप्सता
translation:
"It is suited that this Rama, best among men, is made to be a friend by you who is desiring continued 
existence and not desiring a horrible slaying."

shloka: विदितः स हि धर्मज्ञः शरणागतवत्सलः
translation:
"Rama the righteous one is indeed known as one who loves those who seek protection. If you desire 
to live. let there be friendship between you and Rama."

shloka: प्रसादयस्व त्वं चनं शरणागतवत्सलम्
translation:
"You seek graciousness of this Rama who loves those who seek protection. Becoming piously disposed, 
you are suited to return me to this Rama."

shloka: एवम् हि ते भवेत्स्वस्ति सम्प्रदाय रघूत्तमे
translation:
"In this way giving me to Rama will become fortunate to you. O Ravana! If you do in a different 
way, you will get slayed."

shloka: वर्जयेद्वज्रमुत्सृष्टं वर्जयेदन्तकश्चिरम्
translation:
"Drawn out Vajrayudha, the weapon of Indra may spare some one like you. Lord of death may spare 
you for a long time. That Rama the lord of worlds greatly enraged will not spare you."

shloka: रामस्य धनुषः शब्दं श्रोष्यसि त्वं महास्वनम्
translation:
"Like the great sound of Vajrayudha hurled by Indra, you will hear a loud sound which is sonorous 
of Rama's bow."

shloka: इह शीग्रं सुपर्वाणो ज्वलितास्य इवोरगाः
translation:
"Arrows with good nodes, with blazing tips, like snakes, with characteristic signs of Rama and 
Lakshmana will fall down soon here in Lanka."

shloka: रक्षांसि परिनिघ्नस्तः पुर्यामस्यां समन्ततः
translation:
"Arrows tied with the plumes of an eagle will hit ogres everywhere in this city and will cover 
the city without space."

shloka: राक्षसेन्द्रमहासर्पान् स रामगरुडो महान्
translation:
"That Garuda called Rama speedily will pluck the great serpants called ogres like Vainateya plucking 
the serpants."

shloka: अपनेष्यति मां भर्ता त्वत्तः शीघ्रमरिन्दमः
translation:
"My husband who is a destroyer of foes will take me away from you like Lord Vishnu with three steps 
taking away the brilliant prosperity from Asuras."

shloka: जनस्थाने हतस्थाने निहते रक्षसां बले
translation:
"O ogre! While the army of ogres was being killed at Janasthana which became the land of dead, 
this bad deed has been done by you being powerless."

shloka: अश्रमम् तु तयोः शून्यं प्रविश्य नरसिम्हयोः
translation:
"O lowest one! When those brothers were gone out, entering hermitage without them, I have been 
abducted by you."

shloka: न हि गन्धमुपाघ्राय रामलक्ष्मणयोस्त्वया
translation:
"Like tiger by dog, smelling the scent of Rama and Lakshmana it is indeed not possible by you to 
stand in their view."

shloka: तस्य ते विग्रहे ताभ्यां युगग्रहणमस्थिरम्
translation:
"To you like that, enmity with those two is like the enmity of one hand of Vruttasura with two 
hands of Indra and it is not persevering for you to be an opponent with them."

shloka: क्षिप्रं तव स नाथो मे रामः सौमित्रिणा सह
translation:
"My husband that Rama together with Lakshmana will take away with His arrows your life quickly 
like the sun drying up shallow water."

shloka:
गिरिं कुबेरस्य गतोऽथवालयम् |
सभां गतो वा वरुणस्य राज्ञः |
असंशयं दाशरथेर्न मोक्ष्यसे 
|
महाद्रुमः कालहतोऽशनेरिव
translation:
"Killed by time even if you go to the mountain of Kubera or to his house or if you go to the assembly 
of King Varuna, without doubt you will not be relased from Rama like a great tree from thunderbolt."

shloka:
सीताय वचनं श्रुत्वा परुषं राक्षसेश्वरः |
प्रत्युवाच ततः सीतां विप्रियं प्रियदर्शनम्
translation:
Ravana listening to Seetha's words which were harsh thereafter replied to Seetha unpleasant words 
which are seen to be pleasant.

shloka:
यथा यथा सान्त्वयिता वश्यः स्त्रीणां तथा तथा |
यथा यथा प्रियम् वक्ता परिBहूतस्तथा तहा
translation:
"In whatever way gentle language is used to women in that way they will be under control. In whatever 
way men speak dear words, in that way they will be rejected."

shloka:
संनियच्चति मे क्रोधं त्वयि कामः समुत्थितः |
द्रवतोऽमार्गमासाद्य हयानिव सुसारथिः
translation:
"In your matter desire which has risen up is subdueing my anger like horses running obtaining a 
bad path being subdued by a good charioteer."

shloka:
वामः कामो मनुष्याणाम् यस्मिन् किल निबध्यते |
जने तस्मिंस्त्वनुक्रोशः स्नेहश्च किल जायते
translation:
"Desire of men is unfavourable. In which man desire is tied up, in that man there is compassion 
and fondness."

shloka:
एतस्मात्कारणान्न त्वां घातयामि वरानने |
वधार्हमवमानार्हां मिथ्याप्रव्रजिते रताम्
translation:
"O one with a beautiful face! For this reason although you are suitable to be killed and suitable 
to be humilaited, interested in Rama who is in sham exile, I am not killing you."

shloka:
परुषाणीह वाक्यानि यानि यानि ब्रवीषि माम् |
तेषु तेषु वधो युक्तस्तव मैथिलि दारुणः
translation:
"O Seetha! Here whatever harsh words you are speaking about me, because of those words, you are 
suitable to be horribly slayed."

shloka:
एकमुक्त्वा तु विअदेशीं रावणो राक्षसाधिपः |
क्रोधसंरम्भसम्युक्तः सीतामुत्तरमब्रवीत्
translation:
The king of ogres Ravana speaking thus to Seetha, full of anger and fury spoke subsequent word 
to Seetha.

shloka:
द्वौ मासौ रक्षितव्यौ मे योऽवधिस्ते मया कृतः |
ततः शयनमारोह मम त्वं वरवर्णिनि
translation:
"O Seetha with best complexion! Whatever limit has been made by me to you, those two months are 
protectable to me. Thereafter ascend my bed."

shloka:
ऊर्ध्वं द्वाभ्यां तु मासाभ्यां भर्तारम् मामनिच्चतीम् |
मम त्वां प्रातराशार्थमालभन्ते महानसे
translation: "Above two months you not desiring me as husband will be killed in my kitched for my breakfast."

shloka:
तां तर्ज्यमानां सम्प्रेक्ष्य राक्षसेन्द्रेण जानकीम् |
देवगन्धर्वकन्यास्ता विषेदुर्विकृतेक्षणाः
translation:
Seeing Seetha being frightened by Ravana those Deva and Gandharva maidens grieved with troubled 
eyes.

shloka:
औष्ठप्रकारैरपरा वक्त्रनेत्रैस्तथापराः |
सीतामाश्वासयामासुस्तर्जितां तेन रक्षसा
translation:
Some in the way of lips and in like manner some others with faces and eyes consoled that Seetha 
frightened by that ogre.

shloka:
ताभिराश्वासिता सीता रावणम् राक्षसाधिपम् |
उवाचात्महितं वाक्यं वृत्तशौण्डीर्यगर्वितम्
translation:
Consoled by them Seetha proud of virtuous conduct spoke words beneficial to self to the king of 
ogres Ravana.

shloka:
नूनम् न ते जनः कश्चिदस्ति निःश्रेयसे स्थितः |
निवारयति यो न त्वां कर्मणोऽस्माद्विगर्हितात्
translation:
"Whoever prevents you from these actions which are blameable, such a person interested in your 
welfare there is none. This is definite."

shloka:
मां हि धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं शचीमिव शचीपतेः |
त्वदन्यस्त्रिषु लोकेषु प्रार्थयेन्मनसापि कः
translation:
"In all the three worlds except you who even by heart will desire me who am the wife of virtuous 
Rama like Sachi the wife of Indra."

shloka:
राक्षसाधम रामस्य भार्याममिततेजसः |
उक्तवानसि यत्पापं क्व गतस्तस्य मोक्ष्यसे
translation:
"O vile ogre! Whatever sinful word you spoke to me who is the wife of the great resplendent Rama, 
from that word where will you go to be released?"

shloka:
यथा दृप्तश्च मातङ्गः शशश्च सहितौ वने |
तथा द्विरदवद्रामस्त्वं नीच शशवत् स्मृतः
translation:
"Like an elephant in rut and a hare at war in the forest, in the same way O vile one! Rama is like 
an elephant and you are said to be like a hare."

shloka:
स त्वमिक्ष्वाकुनाथम् वै क्षिपन्निह न लज्जसे |
चक्षुषोर्विषयम् तस्य न तावदुपगच्छसि
translation:
"Such you are not shameful abusing the lord of Ikshvaku dynasty Rama. You are not getting Rama's 
matter so much."

shloka:
इवे ते नयने क्रूते विरूपे कृष्णपिङ्गले |
क्षितौ न पतिते कस्मान्मामनार्य निरीक्षतः
translation:
"O ignoble one! your these eyes which are cruel, crooked, which are black and reddish brown, which 
are seeing me, for what reason are they not falling down."

shloka:
तस्य धर्मात्मनः पत्नीं स्नुषां दशरथस्य च |
कथं व्याहरतो मां ते न जिह्वा व्यवशीर्यते
translation:
"Thus speaking about me who am the wife of virtuous Rama and the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha how 
your tongue did not fall off."

shloka:
असंदेशात्तु रामस्य तपसश्चामपालनात् |
न त्वां कुर्मि दशग्रीव भस्म भर्मार्ह तेजसा
translation:
"O Ravana! Although you are suited to be burnt into ashes, not having the mandate of Rama and preserving 
austerity, I am not reducing you into ashes with my glory."

shloka:
नापहर्तुमहं शक्या त्वया रामस्य धीमतः |
विधिस्तव वधार्थाय विहितो नात्र संशयः
translation:
"Wise Rama's I am not capable of being abducted by you. This act has been made for your slaying. 
In this there is no doubt."

shloka:
शूरेण धनदभ्रात्रा बलैः समुदितेन च |
अपिह्य रामं कस्माद्धि दारचौर्यं त्वया कृतम्
translation:
"By you who is strong, brother of Kubera possessed of army, removing Rama for what reason abduction 
of wife has been done."

shloka:
सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा रावणो राक्षसाधिपः |
विनृत्य नयने क्रूरे जानकीमन्ववैक्षत
translation: King of rakshasas Ravana listening to Seetha's words turned around his cruel eyes and saw Seetha.

shloka:
नीलजीमूतसम्काशो महाभुजशिरोधरः |
सिंहसत्त्वगतिः श्रीमान् दीप्त जिह्वग्रलोचनः
translation:
Ravana was qual to a black cloud, with big shoulders and neck with the strength and gait of a lion, 
glorious with radiant tip of tongue and eyes.

shloka:
चलाग्रमकुटप्रांशुश्चित्रमाल्यानुलेपनः |
रक्तमाल्याम्बरधरस्तप्ताङ्गदविभूषणः
translation:
He was tall with moving front portion of crown, with excellent garlands and anointments, wearing 
red garlands and clothes, with ornaments made of refined gold.

shloka:
श्रोणिसूत्रेण महता मेचकेन सुसम्वृतः |
अमृतोत्पादनद्धेन भुजगेनेव मन्दरः
translation: Like Mount Mandara tied by Vasuki for producing nectar, Ravana was well tied by a black big thread.

shloka:
ताभ्यां स परिपूर्णाभ्यां भुजाभ्यां राक्षसेश्वरः |
शुशुभेऽचलसंकाशः शृङ्गाभ्यामिव मन्दरः
translation:
Equalling a mountain the king of ogres shone with those perfect shoulders like Mount Mandara with 
its peaks.

shloka:
तरुणादित्यवर्णाभ्यां कुण्डलाभ्यां विभूषितः |
रक्तपल्लवपुष्पाभ्यामशोकाभ्यामिवाचलः
translation:
With the color of just risen sun, decorated by earrings, he was like a mountain with Ashoka trees 
with red flowers and shoots.

shloka:
स कल्पवृक्षप्रतिमो वसन्त इव मूर्तिमान् |
श्मशानचैत्यप्रतिमो भूषितोऽपि भयम्करः
translation:
Equalling a Kalpavriksha he was like the embodiment of spring season. Like a funeral mound in a 
grave-yard was horrible even though decorated.

shloka:
अवेक्षमाणो वैदेहीं कोपसम्रक्तलोचनः |
उवाच रावणः सीतां भुजङ्ग इव निःश्वसन्
translation: With red eyes due to anger Ravana was looking at Seetha sighing like a serpant and spoke to Seetha.

shloka:
अनयेनाभिसम्पन्नमर्थहीनमनुव्रते |
नाशयाम्यहमद्य त्वां सूर्यः सन्ध्यामिवौजसा
translation:
O foloower of Rama posessing bad conduct, without wealth! Now I will destroy you like sun destroying 
morning twilight with light.

shloka:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीम् राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः |
संदिदेश ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्गोरदर्शनाः
translation:
The king Ravana who causes enemies to cry thus speaking to Seetha, thereafter ordered all ogre 
women with horrible appearances.

shloka:
एकाक्षीमेककर्णां च कर्णप्रावरणां तथा |
गोकर्णीं हस्तिकर्णीम् च लम्बकर्णीमकर्णिकाम्
translation:
Ravana ordered one with a single eye, one with a single ear and one with ears as covering, one 
with cow's wars, one with ears of an elephant, one with dangling ears, one without ears and one with the feet 
of an elephant and one with the feet of a horse, one with feet of a cow,one with hair over feet, one with a single 
eye and one with a single foot, one with big feet, one without feet, one with a big head and neck,one with big 
breasts and stomach, and one with big mouth and eyes, one with a long tongue, one without tongue, one without 
nose, one with the face of a lion, one with the face of a cow,one with the face of a pig.

shloka: यथा मद्वशगा सीता क्ष्प्रं भवति जानकी
translation:
"O ogres! How the daughter of Janaka, Seetha becomes under my control quickly, thus all of you 
together do that task."

shloka: प्रतिलोमानुलोमैश्च सामदानादिभेदनैः
translation:
"With hostile and favourable tasks, with kind words, with gifts and dividing words and exertion 
of punishment, bring Seetha under my possession."

shloka: इति प्रतिसमादिश्य राक्षसेन्द्रः पुनः पुनः
translation: Ravana thus ordered again and again with a mind full of lust and anger frightened Seetha.

shloka: उपगम्य ततः शीघ्रं राक्षसी धान्यमालिनी
translation: Thereafter an ogre named Dhanyamalini quickly neared Ravana, embraced him and spoke these words.

shloka: मया क्रीड महाराज सीतया किं तवानया
translation:
"O king! Sport with me. O lord of ogres! Of what use to you is this Seetha who is colorless and 
a wreched human."

shloka: नूनमस्या महाराज न दिव्यान् भोगसत्तमान्
translation:
"O king! Lord Barhma did not assign to Her wonderful best luxuries earned by the might of your 
arms. This is definite."

shloka: अकामां कामयानस्य शरीरमुपतप्यते
translation:
"The body of one who desires a woman without desire suffers pain. Good happiness will occur to 
one who loves a woman who desires him."

shloka: एवमुक्तस्तु राक्षस्या समुत्क्षिप्तस्ततो बली
translation:
Thus spoken to by that ogre that Ravana who was strong equalling a cloud, thereafter being taken 
away turned back laughing."

shloka: प्रस्थितः स दशग्रीवः कम्पयन्निव मेदिनीम्
translation:
That Ravana departing was as though shaking the earth and entered his house with the lustre of 
blazing sun shine.

shloka: देवगन्धर्वकन्याश्च नागकन्याश्च सर्वतः
translation:
Deva and Gandharva maidens and Naga maidens surrounding Ravana in all directions entered that best 
among houses.

shloka:
स मैथिलीं ध्रम परामवस्थितां |
प्रवेपमानां परिभर्स्य रावणः |
विहाय सीतां मदनेन मोहितः 
|
स्वमेव वेश्म प्रविवेश भास्वरम्
translation:
That Ravana frightening Seetha who was steadfastly intent on virtue and who was shaking, leaving
