Seetha, infatuated by love, entered his own house which was shining.

shloka:
इत्युक्त्वा मैथिलीं राजा रावणः शत्रुरावणः |
संदिश्य च ततः सर्वा राक्षसीर्निर्जगाम ह
translation:
The king Ravana who makes enemies to cry thus speaking to Seetha thereafter also ordering all ogre 
women went away.

shloka:
निष्क्रन्ते राक्षसेन्द्र तु पुनरन्तःपुरं गते |
राक्षस्यो भीमरूपास्ताः सीतां समभिदुद्रुवुः
translation:
After Ravana left and obtained gynaeceum, those ogres with horrible appearances went running to 
Seetha.

shloka:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्चिताः |
परं पुरुषया वाचा वैदेहीमिदमब्रवन्
translation:
Thereafter reaching Seetha ogre women swooned with anger and with a very harsh speech spoke these 
words to Seetha.

shloka:
पौलस्त्यस्य वरिष्ठस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः |
दशग्रीवस्य भार्यात्वं सीते न बहुमन्यसे
translation:
"O Seetha! You are not respscting becoming wife of Ravana born in the family of Paulastya, best 
among men, a great soul with ten heads."

shloka:
ततस्वएकजटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
अमन्त्य्र क्रोधताम्राक्षी सीतां करतलोदरीम्
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Ekajata with red eyes sue to anger calling Seetha with stomach that 
can be held by palm of the hand, spoke these words.

shloka:
प्रजापतीनाम् षण्णं तु चतुर्थो यः प्रजापतिः |
मानसो ब्रह्मणः पुत्रः पुलस्त्य इति विश्रुतः
translation:
"Among th six Prajapatis, whichever son, the fourth Prajapati, born by the thought of Lord Brahma 
,he is famous as Paulastya."

shloka:
पुलस्त्यस्य तु तेजस्वी महार्षिर्मानसः सुतः |
नाम्ना स विश्रवा नाम प्रजापतिसमप्रभः
translation:
By the name, famous as Visrava, with a radiance equalling that of Lord Brahmathat glorious sage 
is the son born from the thought of Pulastya.

shloka:
तस्य पुत्रो विशालाक्षि रावणः शत्रुरावणः |
तस्य त्वं राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हसि
translation:
"O wide eyed one! Ravana who makes enemies to cry, is Visrava's son. You are suited to become Ravana's 
wife. O one with all beautiful limbs! Why will you not agree words spoken by me."

shloka: ततो हरिजटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Harijata with eyes like those of a cat turned around eyes due to 
anger and spoke these words.

shloka: येन देवास्त्रायस्त्रिंशद्देवराजश्च निर्जताः
translation:
"By whom thirty three Devas and the king of Devas have been conquered, you are suited to become 
the wife of that lord of ogres.

shloka: ततस्तु प्रघसा नाम राक्षसी क्रोधमूर्छिता
translation:
Thereafter an ogre named Praghasa swooning with anger and then frightening Seetha, spoke this horrible 
word.

shloka: वीर्योत्सिक्तस्य शूरस्य सम्ग्रामे न निवर्तिनः
translation:
"Why will you not get wifehood of Ravana who is proud of his might, valiant, who will not turn 
back in wars, who is strong together with valour."

shloka: प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां त्यक्त्वा राजा महाबलः
translation:
"The mighty Ravana can leave dear respectable wife who among all wives is most fortunate and can 
obtain you."

shloka: समृद्धम् स्त्रीसहस्रेण नानारत्नोपशोभितम्
translation:
"Ravana leaving gynaeceum filled with thousand women and shone by various best things can obtain 
you.

shloka: अन्या तु विकटा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत्
translation:
Another ogre woman named Vikata spoke these words: "By whom a number of times in war Devas, in 
war Nagas, Gandharvas and Danavas have been conquered that Ravana has come to your side."

shloka:
तस्य सर्वसमृद्धस्य रावणस्य महात्मनः |
किमद्य राक्षसेन्द्रस्य भार्यात्वं नेच्छऽधमे
translation:
"O vile one! Why are you not desiring wifehood of such Ravana, fulfilled in all respects, who is 
a great soul and lord of ogres.

shloka:
ततस्तु दुर्मुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
यस्य सूर्यो न तपति भीतो यस्य च मारुतः
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Durmukhi spoke these words: " O one with long eyes! Fearing whom 
the sun will not comsume by heat, fearing whom the win will not blow, to that one why are you not favourable."

shloka: पुष्टवृष्टं च तरवो मुमुचुर्यस्य वै भयात्
translation:
"O one with good eyebrows! O Seetha! By the fear of whom trees shed a shower of flowers, whenever 
Ravana desired mountains and clouds will shed water, why you are not making mind to be the wife of such Ravana, 
who is the king of ogres and king of kings."

shloka: साधु ते तत्त्वतो देवि कथितं साधु भामिनि
translation: "O Seetha with a good smile! O princess! Understand kind words spoken to you well and truly."

shloka:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो विकृताननाः |
परुषं परुषा नार्य ऊचुस्तां वाक्यमप्रियम्
translation:
Thereafter ogre women with a cruel nature, with crooked faces neared that Seetha and spoke unpleasant 
words harshly.

shloka:
किं त्वमन्तःपुरे सीते सर्वभूतमनोहरे |
महार्हशयनोपेते न वासमनुमन्यसे
translation:
"O Seetha! Why are you not agreeing to stay in the gynaeceum pleasing to all beings together with 
very best beds."

shloka:
मानुषी मानुषस्यैव भार्यात्वं बहुमन्यसे |
प्रत्याहर मनो रामान्न त्वं जातु भविष्यसि
translation:
"You who are a human are thinking highly about the wifehood of a human being. Withdraw your mind 
from Rama. Otherwise you will not exist at all."

shloka:
त्रैलोक्यवसुभोक्तारं रावणं राक्षसेश्वरम् |
भर्तारमुपसंगम्य विहरस्व यथासुखम्
translation:
"Sport according to your comfort coming together with the king of ogres Ravana enjoying luxuries 
of the three worlds and taking him as husband.

shloka:
मानुषी मानुषं तं तु राममिच्छसि शोभने |
राज्याद्भ्राष्टमसिद्धार्थं विक्लबं त्वमनिन्दिते
translation:
"O beautiful one! O irrreproachable one! But being a human you are desiring that Rama who is a 
human, banished from kingdom, unsuccessful and gloomy."

shloka:
राक्षसीनां वचः श्रुत्वा सीता पद्मनिभेक्षणा |
नेत्राभ्यामश्रुपूर्णाभ्यामिदं वचनमब्रवीत्
translation:
Seetha with eyes like lotuses hearing the words of ogre women spoke these words with eyes filled 
with tears.

shloka:
यदिदम् लोकविद्विष्टमुदाहरथ संगताः |
नैतन्मनसि वाक्यं मे किल्बिषं प्रतिभाति वः
translation:
"All of you coming together whatever words which are hated in the world you spoke in my matter, 
this does it not seem sinful in your mind?"

shloka:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति |
कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
translation:
"Human woman is not waited to become wife of an ogre. All of you freely eat me. I will not honour 
your words."

shloka:
दीनो वा राज्यहीनो वा यो मे भर्ता स मे गुरुः |
तं नित्यमनुरक्तास्मि यथा सूर्यं सुवर्चला
translation:
"Although wretched or without kingdom, whoever is my husband, He alone is my master. Like Suvarchala 
with the Sun God, I am fond of Him always."

shloka:
यथा शची महाभागा शक्रं समुपतिष्ठति |
अरुन्धती वसिष्ठं च रोहिणी शशिनं यथा
translation:
"Like the highly fortunate Sachi who waits upon Indra, like Arundhati on Vasishta, like Rohini 
on the Moon God, like Lopamudra on Agastya, like Sukanya on Chyavana, like Savitri on Satyavanta, like Srimati 
on Kapila, like Madayanti on Saudasa, like Kesini on Sagara, like Damayanti the daughter of Bhima, devoted to 
husband Nala, in the same way I am devoted to my husband Rama, the best in Ikshvaku dynasty."

shloka: सीताया वचनं श्रुत्वा राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्चिताः
translation:
Ogre women incited by Ravana listening to the words of Seetha, swooned with anger and frightened 
Her with harsh words.

shloka: अवलीनः स निर्वाक्यो हनुमान् शिंशुपाद्रुमे
translation:
That monkey Hanuma not talking and hiding in the Simsupa tree listened to those ogre women frightening 
Seetha.

shloka: तामभिक्रम्य संक्रुद्दा वेपमानां समन्ततः
translation:
Nearing that Seetha shaking with fear in all directions, those ogres being angry licked a lot shining 
and hanging lips.

shloka: ऊचुश्च परमक्रुद्धाः प्रगृह्याशु परश्वधान्
translation:
Being angry a lot and grasping axes quickly spoke as follows: "This woman is not suited to have 
the king of ogres Ravana as husband."

shloka: सा भर्तस्यमाना भीमाभी राक्षसीभिर्वरानना
translation:
Being frightened by ogre women who were horrible that Seetha with best face with tears in eyes 
and moving from there reached that Simsupa tree.

shloka: ततस्तां शिंशुपां सीता राक्षसीभिः समावृता
translation:
Thereafter the wide eyed Seetha nearing that Simsupa tree being surrounded by ogre women was situated 
there with gloom.

shloka: तां कृशां दीनवदनां मलिनाम्बरधारिणीम्
translation:
Those ogres frightened from all directions that Seetha who was emaciated with a pitiful face and 
wearing dirty garments.

shloka: ततस्तां विनता नाम राक्षसी भीमदर्शना
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Vinata with a horrible appearance with an angry form, crooked, having 
a prominent belly spoke to Her.

shloka: सीते पर्याप्तमेतावद्भर्तुः स्नेहो निदर्शितः
translation:
"O Seetha! You have showed love of husband. This much is enough. O auspicious one! At all times 
doing something excessively serves as vice."

shloka: परितुष्टास्मि भद्रं ते मानुषस्ते कृतो विधिः
translation:
"O Seetha! I am happy. Human duty has been done by you. Let there be fortune to you. Do also according 
to my wholesome words being told."

shloka: रावणं भ्ज भर्तारं भर्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्
translation:
"Obtain as husband Ravana who is the lord of al l ogres, bold and handsome, like Indra the lord 
of Devas, able one and liberal with a pleasing appearance to all."

shloka:
मानुषं कृपणं रामं त्यक्त्वा रावणमाश्रय |
दिव्याङ्गरागा वैदेहि दिव्याभरणभूषिता
translation:
"Leaving Rama who is a human and miserable, seek refuge in Ravana. O Seetha! With best unguents 
to the body and decorated with best ornaments, become mistress of all the worlds from today."

shloka: अग्नेः स्वाहा यथा देवी शिची वेन्द्रस्य शोभने
translation:
"O auspicious one! Like Svaha the wife of the Fire God, like Sachi the wife of Indra become mistress 
of all worlds. O Seetha! What is the use with Rama who is miserable and with gone vigour."

shloka: एतदुक्तं च मे वाक्यं यदि त्वं न करिष्यपि
translation: If you do not do my this spoken word, all of us in this moment will eat you.

shloka: अन्या तु विकटा नाम लबमानपयोधरा
translation: Another ogre named Vikata with hanging breasts raising fist and roaring with anger spoke to Seetha.

shloka: बहून्य्प्रियरूपाणि वचनानि सुदुर्मते
translation:
"O Seetha with an evil mind! Your many words which are unpleasant have been tolerated due to pity 
and due to softness."

shloka: न च नः कुरुषे वाक्यं हितं कालपुरुस्कृतम्
translation:
"O Seetha! You are not doing according to our word which is respected by time and wholesome. You 
have been brought to this bank of the ocean not obtainable by others. You have entered the terrible gynaeceum 
of Ravana."

shloka:
रावणस्य गृहे रुद्धामस्माभिस्तु सुरक्षिताम् |
न त्वां शक्तः परित्रातुमपि साक्षात्पुरन्दरः
translation:
"Withheld in the house of Ravana well protected by us, even Devendra himself is not capable to 
protect you."

shloka:
कुरुष्व हितवादिन्या वचनं मम मैथिलि |
अलमश्रुप्रपातेन त्यज शोकमन्र्थकम्
translation:
"O Seetha! Do according to my word, which is beneficial. Discharge of tears is enough. Leave worthless 
gloom."

shloka:
भज प्रीतिं च हर्षं च त्यजैतां नित्यदैन्यताम् |
सीते राक्षसराजेन सह क्रीड यथासुखम्
translation:
"O Seetha! Have love and happiness. Leave this daily gloom. Sport according to comfort with the 
king of ogres."

shloka:
जानासि हि यथा भीरु स्त्रीणां यौवनमध्रुवम् |
यावन्न ते व्यतिक्रामेत्तावत्सुखमवाप्नुहि
translation:
"O timid one! You know how youth of women is not lasting. As long as your youth will not pass away, 
so long get comfort."

shloka:
उद्यानानि च रम्याणि पर्वतोपवनानि च |
सह राक्षसराजेन चर त्वं मदिरेक्षणे
translation:
"O one with intoxicating eyes! You along with king of ogres roam beautiful groves, mountains and 
nearby forests.

shloka:
स्त्रीसहस्राणि ते सप्त वशे स्थास्यन्ति सुन्दरि |
रावणं भज भर्तारं भ्र्तारं सर्वरक्षसाम्
translation:
"O beautiful one! seven thousand women will be in your control. Have as husband Ravana the lord 
of all ogres."

shloka:
उत्पाट्य वा ते हृदयं भक्षयिष्यामि मैथिलि |
यदि मे व्याहृतं वाक्यं न यथावत्करिष्यसि
translation:
"O Seetha! If you do not do according to my spoken word as is, I will eat your heart indeed by 
plucking it out."

shloka:
ततश्चण्डोदरी नाम राक्षसी क्रोधमूर्छिता |
भ्रामयन्ती महच्चूलमिदं वचनम्ब्रवीत्
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Chandodari swooning with anger, turning around a big spike spoke 
this word.

shloka:
इमां हरिणलोलाक्षीं त्रासोत्कम्पिपयोधरां |
रावणेन हृतां दृष्ट्वा दौहृदो मे महानभूत्
translation:
"Seeing this woman with eyes like that of a deer, with moving breasts due to fear, abducted by 
Ravana, there occured to me a great desire."

shloka:
यकृत्ल्पीहमथोत्पीडं हृदयं च सबन्धनम् |
अन्त्राण्यपि तथा शीर्षं खादेयमिति मे मतिः
translation:
"It is my mind to eat the liver, the spleen, flesh above heart and heart together with muscle and 
entrails and the head."

shloka:
ततस्तु प्रघसा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
कण्ठमस्या नृशंसायाः पीडयाम किमास्यते
translation:
An ogre woman named Pragasa spoke these words : "Squeeze the neck of this cruel woman. Why do we 
delay?"

shloka:
निवेद्यतां ततो राज्ञे मानुषी सा मृतेति ह |
नात्र कश्चन संदेहः खादतेति स वक्ष्यति
translation:
"Thereafter let it be known to the king that that human woman has died. He will say thus : "Eat.". 
There is no doubt in this matter."

shloka:
ततस्त्वजामुखी नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
विशस्येमां ततः सर्वाः समान् कुरुत पीलुकान्
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Ajamukhi spoke these words : "All of you killing this woman thereafter 
do equal pieces."

shloka:
विभजाम ततः सर्वा विवादो मे न रोचते |
पेयमानीयतां क्षिप्रं लेह्यमुच्चावचं बहु
translation:
"Thereafter all of us will divide. Quarrel is not desirable to me. Liquor, many kinds and a lot 
of lickables be brought quickly."

shloka:
ततः शूर्पणखा नाम राक्षसी वाक्यमब्रवीत् |
अजामुख्या यदुक्तं हि तदेव मम रोचते
translation:
Thereafter an ogre woman named Surpanakha spoke these words: "That which was spoken by Ajamukhi, 
is desirable to me."

shloka:
सुरा चानीयतां क्षिप्रं सर्वशोकविनाशिनी |
मानुषं मां समास्वाद्य नृत्यामोथ निकुम्भिलाम्
translation:
"Liquor which is the destroyer of all sorrow be brought quickly. Eating human flesh afterwards, 
we will dance for propitiating Nikumbila."

shloka:
एवं संभर्त्स्यमाना सा सीता सुरसुतोपमा |
राक्षसीभिः सुघोराभिर्धैर्यमुत्सृज्य रोदिति
translation:
Thus being frightened by horrible ogres, that Seetha equalling a daughter of gods, abandoning fortitude, 
was crying.

shloka:
अथ तासां वदन्तीनां परुषं दारुणं बहु |
राक्षसीनामसौम्यानां रुरोद जनकात्मजा
translation: As those ogre woman with a cruel nature were speaking a lot harshly and horribly, Seetha cried.

shloka:
एवमुक्ता तु वैदेही राक्षसीभिर्मनस्विनी |
उवाच परमत्रस्ताबाष्पगद्गदया गिरा
translation:
Thus being spoken to by ogre women, Seetha with a good mind being frightened a lot spoke as follows 
with a voice indistinct due to tears.

shloka:
न मानुषी राक्षसस्य भार्या भवितुमर्हति |
कामं खादत मां सर्वा न करिष्यामि वो वचः
translation:
"A human woman is not suited to become a wife of an ogre. All of you eat me according to your desire. 
I will not do according to your words."

shloka:
सा राक्षसीमध्यगता सीता सुरसुतोपमा |
न शर्म लेभे दुःखार्ता रावणेन च तर्जिता
translation:
Being in the middle of ogre women, being frightened by Ravana also, like a daughter of gods, that 
Seetha did not get comfort being tormented by grief.

shloka:
वेपते स्माधिकं सीता विशन्ती वाङ्गमात्मनः |
वने यथा परिभ्रष्टा मृगी कोकैरिवार्दिता
translation:
Like a fawn in a forest lost from its herd and tormented by wolves, Seetha was as though sinking 
into own body and shook a lot.

shloka:
सा त्वशोकस्य विपुलां शाखामालम्ब्य पुष्पिताम् |
चिन्तयामास शोकेन भर्तारं भग्नमानसा
translation:
That Seetha with a broken heart due to grief, held a wide flowering branch of Ashoka tree and thought 
about Her husband.

shloka:
सा स्नापयन्ती विपुलौ स्तनौ नेत्रजलस्रवैः |
चिन्तयन्ती न शोकस्य तदान्तमधिगच्छति
translation:
Then that Seetha washing Her wide breasts with a flow of tears from eyes and thinking, did not 
get end of sorrow.

shloka:
सा वेपमाना पतिता प्रवाते कदळी यथा |
राक्षसीनां भयत्रस्ता विवर्णवदनाभवत्
translation:
That Seetha was shaking like a plantain tree fallen down in an exceedingly windy place, trembling 
with fear of the ogre women, and became with a pale face.

shloka:
तस्याः सा दीर्घविपुला वेपन्त्या सीतया तदा |
ददृशे कम्पिनी वेणी व्याळीव परिसर्पती
translation:
That moving plait, which was wide and long, of that best woman was seen to be like a serpant in 
motion.

shloka:
सा निःश्वसन्ती दुःखार्ता शोकोपहतचेतना |
आर्ता व्यसृजदश्रूणि मैथिली विललाप च
translation:
That Seetha tormented by grief, with a mind hit by sorrow, struck by calamity was sighing and let 
down tears and also cried.

shloka:
हा रामेति च दुःखार्ता हा पुनर्लक्ष्मणेति च |
हा श्वश्रु मम कौसल्ये हा सुमित्रेति भामिनी
translation:
Seetha being tormented by grief said : "Oh! Rama!" and again "Oh! Lakshmana!","Oh! Kausalya!, my 
mother-in-law" "Oh! Sumitra!"

shloka:
लोकप्रवादः सत्योऽयं पण्डितैः समुदाहृतः |
अकाले दुर्लभो मृत्युः स्त्रिया वा पुरुषस्य वा
translation:
"I thus being tormented by cruel ogre women here lacking Rama, being tormented by grief, when I 
am living even for a moment,' death at wrong time to woman or to a man is hard' - thus being said this popular 
saying in the world is true."

shloka:
एषाल्पपुण्या कृपणा विनशिष्याम्यनाथवत् |
समुद्रमथ्ये नौः पूर्णा वायुवेगैरिवाहता
translation:
"This me with small merit,wreched, like an orphan, will perish like a ship in the middle of the 
ocean being hit by the speed of wind."

shloka:
भर्तारं तमपश्यन्ती राक्षसीवशमागता |
सीदामि खलु शोकेन कूलं तोयहतं यथा
translation:
"Not seeing my husband that Rama and obtaining control of ogre women like a bank hit by water I 
am verily perishing with sorrow."

shloka:
तं पद्मदळपत्राक्षं सिंहविक्रान्तगामिनम् |
धन्याः पश्यन्ति मे नाथं कृतज्ञं प्रियवादिनम्
translation:
"Only fortunate see that my husband with eyes like petals of an expanded lotus, walking with the 
gait of a lion, correct in conduct and a pleasant talker."

shloka:
सर्वथा तेन हीनाया रामेण विदितात्मना |
तीक्ष्णंविषमिवास्वाद्यदुर्लभं मम जीवितम्
translation:
"To me lacking that Rama with a famous soul, like after eating a pungent poison life in all ways 
is hard."

shloka:
कीदृशं तु महापापं मया जन्मान्तरे कृतम् |
येनेदं प्राप्यते दुःखं मया घोरं सुदारुणं
translation:
"By what this horrible and very dreadful grief is obtained by me, what kind of great sin had been 
done by me in another life."

shloka:
जीवितं त्यक्तुंइच्छामि शोकेन महता वृता |
राक्षसीभिश्च रक्ष्यन्त्या रामो नासाद्यते मया
translation:
"Together with great grief, I desire to give away my life. This desire is not obtainable by me. 
I am well protected by ogre women."

shloka:
धिगस्तु खलु मानुष्यं धिगस्तु परवश्यताम् |
न शक्यं यत्परित्यक्तुमात्मच्छन्देन जीवितम्
translation:
"Fie upon human condition! Fie upon being in the control of others. By what reason it is not possible 
according to own desire to give up life."

shloka:
प्रसक्ताश्रुमुखी त्वेवं ब्रुवती जनकात्मजा |
अधोगतमुखी बाला विलप्तुमुपचक्रमे
translation:
With a face continually shedding tears, Seetha an young woman, thus speaking with a downward face, 
started to weep.

shloka:
उन्मत्तेव प्रमत्तेव भ्रान्तचित्तेव शोचती |
उपावृत्ता किशोरीव विवेष्टन्ती महीतले
translation:
Seetha was crying like a mad one, like an intoxicated one, with a deluded mind. Like a female horse 
rolling on ground, Seetha rolled on the ground.

shloka:
राघवस्य प्रमत्तस्य रक्षसा कामरूपिणा |
रावणेन प्रमथ्याहमानीता क्रोशती बलात्
translation:
"While Rama was heedless (taken away by Mareecha), I who have been crying was forcibly brought 
overpowered by the ogre Ravana who can wear desired form."

shloka:
राक्षसीवशमापन्ना भर्त्स्यमाना सुदारुणम् |
चिन्तयन्ती सुदुःखार्ता नाहं जीवितुमुत्सहे
translation:
"Being under the control of ogresses, being frightened very horribly, thinking and being tormented 
by grief, I do not desire to live."

shloka:
न हि मे जीविते नार्थो नै वार्थैर्न च भूषणैः |
वसन्त्या राक्षसीमध्ये विना रामं महारथम्
translation:
"Without Rama, a great car-warrior, living in the midst of ogresses, there is no use with life 
to me; not with wealth, not with ornaments."

shloka:
अश्मसारमिदं नूनथवाप्यजरामरम् |
हृदयं मम येनेदं न दुःखेनावशीर्यते
translation:
"Or my this heart truly is made of iron. It is undecaying and without death. By what reason is 
it not destroying with sorrow?"

shloka:
धिङ्मामनार्यामसतीं याहं तेन विना कृता |
मुहूर्तमपि रक्षामि जीवितं पापजीविता
translation:
"Whoever I with a sinful life made to be without Rama, protecting life even for a moment, to such 
me who am ignoble, who am bad wife, shame on me."

shloka:
का च मे जीविते श्रद्धा सुखे वा तं प्रियं विना |
भर्तारं सागरान्ताया वसुधायाः प्रियंवदम्
translation:
"Without husband Rama who is the lord of the earth with ocean at the end, a pleasant talker, what 
is the interest to me in life or in comfort."

shloka:
भिद्यतां भक्ष्यतां वापि शरीरं विसृजाम्यहम् |
न चाप्यहं चिरं कुःखं सहेयं प्रियवर्जिता
translation:
"I will leave the body. Let it be split into pieces or let it be eaten. I without husband will 
not tolerate sorrow for a long time."

shloka:
चरणेनापि सव्येन न स्पृशेयं निशाचरम् |
रावणं किं पुनरहं कावयेयं विगर्हतम्
translation:
"I will not touch even with my left foot Ravana an ogre of reprehensible conduct. What to say of 
desiring him."

shloka:
प्रत्याख्यातं न जानाति नात्मानं नात्मनः कुलम् |
यो नृशंसस्वभावेन मां प्रार्थयितुमिच्छति
translation:
"Whoever Ravana with a cruel nature is desiring to solicit me, that Ravana does not know him to 
be refused; he does not know his race."

shloka:
चिन्ना भिन्ना विभक्ता वा दीप्तेवाग्नौ प्रदीपिता |
रावणं नोपतिष्ठेयं किं प्रलापेन वश्चिरम्
translation:
"Even if cut or if divided into parts in blazing fire, I will not reach Ravana. What is the use 
with your prattling for a long time?"

shloka:
ख्यातः प्राज्ञः कृतज्ञ्शश्च राघवः |
सद्वृत्तो निरनुक्रोशः शङ्के मद्भाग्यसंक्षयात्
translation:
"Rama is famous, is a wise man, is compassionate with a good conduct. Due to the deterioration 
of my fortune, I doubt He became hard hearted."

shloka:
राक्षसानां सहस्राणि जनस्थाने चतुर्दश |
येनैकेन निरस्तानि स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
translation: "By whom alone fourteen thousand of ogres have been destroyed, why is that Rama not saving me."

shloka:
निरुद्धा रावणेनाहमल्पवीर्येण रक्षसा |
समर्थः खलु मे भर्ता रावणं हन्तुमाहवे
translation:
"I am withheld by the ogre Ravana with little strength. My husband is indeed capable of killing 
Ravana in a war."

shloka:
विराधो दण्डकारण्ये येन राक्षसपुङ्गवः |
रणे रामेण निहतः स मां किं नाभिपद्यते
translation:
"By which Rama Viradha, best among ogres, has been killed in Dandaka forest in a war, why is that 
He not saving me?"

shloka:
कामं मध्ये समुद्रस्य लङ्केयं दुष्प्रधर्षणा |
न तु राघवबाणानां गतिरोधो भविष्यति
translation:
"This city of Lanka being in the middle of ocean is difficult to be attacked. But there will not 
be an obstacle to flying of Rama's arrows."

shloka:
किं नु तत्कारणं येन रामो दृढपराक्रमः |
रक्षसापहृतां भार्यामिष्टां नाभ्यवपद्यते
translation:
"What now is that reason by which Rama with a firm courage is not protecting His dear wife stolen 
by an ogre."

shloka:
इहस्थां मां न जानीते शङ्के लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः |
जानन्नपि स तेजस्वी धर्षणं मर्षयिष्यति
translation:
"I doubt that Rama elder to Laksmana does not know me to be here. After knowing will that glorious 
Rama tolerate this outrage?"

shloka:
हृतेति योऽधिगत्वा मां राघवाय निवेदयेत् |
गृध्रारजोऽपि स रणे रावणेन निपातितः
translation:
"Whoever Jatayu nearing Rama will have let known to Rama that Seetha was stolen, that king of vultures 
has been killed by Ravana in war."

shloka:
कृतं कर्म महत्तेन मां तथाभ्यवपद्यता |
तिष्ठता रावणद्वन्द्वे वृद्धेनापि जटायुषा
translation:
"A great deed has been done by that Jatayu, thus protecting me, although of old age, standing in 
a dual combat with Ravana."

shloka:
यदि मामिह जानीयाद्वर्तमानां स राघवः |
अद्य बाणैरभिक्रुद्धः कुर्याल्लोकमराक्षसम्
translation:
"If that Rama knows me to be living here, with anger He will make the world to be without ogres 
with His arrows now."

shloka:
विधमेच्च पुरीं लङ्कां शोषयेच्च महोदधिम् |
रावणस्य च नीचस्य कीर्तिं नाम च नाशयेत्
translation:
"Rama will blow away the city of Lanka, will dry up the great ocean, will destroy the name and 
fame of Ravana."

shloka:
ततो निहतनाथानां राक्षसीनां गृहे गृहे |
यथाहमेवं रुदती तथा भुयो न संशयः
translation:
"Thereafter how I am crying in this way, in the same way, in very house, ogresses with killed husbands 
will cry again and again. There is no doubt in this."

shloka:
अन्विष्य रक्षसां लङ्कां कुर्याद्रामः सलक्ष्मणः |
न हि ताभ्यां रिपुर्दृष्टो मुहूर्तमपि जीवति
translation:
"Rama together will Lakshmana will search the city of Lanka belonging to ogres. An enemy seen by 
those two will indeed not live even for a moment."

shloka:
चिताधुमाकुलपथा गृध्रमण्डलसंकुला |
अचिरेण तु लङ्केयं श्मशानसदृशी भवेत्
translation:
"This Lanka shortly will become like a graveyard, with paths agitated with smoke of funeral pyres, 
crowded with a group of vultures."

shloka:
अचिरेणैव कालेन प्राप्स्याम्येव मनोरथम् |
दुष्प्रस्थानोऽयमाख्याति सर्वेषाम् वो विपर्ययम्
translation:
"In a short time only I will attain my desire. This evil course is telling of destruction of you 
all."

shloka:
यादृशानीह दृशन्ते लङ्कायामशुभानि वै |
अचिरेणैव कालेन भविष्यति हतप्रभा
translation:
"Here in Lanka whatever inauspicious things are being seen, from those, in a short while Lanka 
will become deprived of glory."

shloka:
नूनं लङ्का हते पापे रावणे राक्षसाधमे |
शोषं यास्यति दुर्धर्षा प्रमदा विधव यथा
translation:
"While the sinful, vile ogre Ravana is being killed, Lanka which is unconquerable till now, definitely 
will get drying up like a woman who lost husband."

shloka:
पुण्योत्सव समृद्धा च नष्टभर्र्ती सराक्षसी |
भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का नष्टभर्त्री यथाङ्गना
translation:
"Now abounding in pious festivities, the city of Lanka with lost lord together with ogresses will 
become like a woman with lost husband."

shloka:
नूनं राक्षसकन्यानां रुदन्तीनां गृहे गृहे |
श्रोष्यामि नचिरादेव दुःखार्तानामिह ध्वनिम्
translation:
"In a short while here in every house I can definitely hear the sound of ogresses crying being 
tormented by grief."

shloka:
सान्धकारा हतद्योता हतराक्षसपुङ्गवा |
भविष्यति पुरी लङ्का निर्दग्धा रामसायकैः
translation:
"The city of Lanka will become burnt by Rama's arrows together with darkness, with destroyed luster 
with killed best ogres."

shloka:
यदि नाम स शूरो मां रामो रक्तान्तालोचनः |
जानीयद्वर्तमानां हि रावणस्य निवेशने
translation: "Will that Rama who is a strong man with red eye corners know me to be in the house of Ravana."

shloka:
अनेन तु नृशंसेन रावणेनाधमेन मे |
समयो यस्तु निर्दिष्टस्तस्य कालोऽयमागतः
translation:
"Whatever time has been ordered by this cruel and vilest of men Ravana, this time has come to me. 
That death decreed to me does not hold good to this evil one (Ravana)."

shloka: अकार्यं ये न जानन्ति नैरृताः पापकारिणः
translation:
"Whoever sinful ogres who do not know what should not be done, due to their unrighteousness now 
there will be a great calamity. These meat eating ogres do not know virtue."

shloka:
ध्रुवं मां प्रातराशार्थे राक्षसः कल्पयिस्यति |
साहं कथं करिष्यामि तं विना प्रियदर्शनम्
translation:
"An ogre will definitely eat me for breakfast. What should such I do without Rama with pleasing 
appearance? I am grieving a lot not seeing Rama with red eye corners."

shloka: यदि कश्चित् प्रदाता मे विषस्याद्य भवेदिह
translation:
"Now if there exists any one who is a giver of poison here, I without husband quickly will see 
the god Yama."

shloka: नाजानाज्जिवतीं रामः स मां लक्ष्मणपूर्वजः
translation:
"That Rama elder to Lakshmana may not know me to be alive. If those two know me to be alive, then 
it cannot be said that they will not do my search on earth."

shloka: नूनं ममैव शोकेन स नीरो लक्ष्मणाग्रजः
translation:
"That valiant Rama who is the elder brother of Lakshmana due to grief of me, leaving the body on 
earth has gone to celestial world. This is certain."

shloka: धन्या देवाह् सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः
translation:
"Whoever is seeing my husband Rama with eyes resembling a lotus flower such Devas, Siddhas together 
with Gandharvas and great sages are fortunate."

shloka: अथवा न हि तस्यार्थो द्कर्मकामस्य धीमतः
translation:
"Or to that Rama with a desire in virtuousness, who is intelligent, a sage-king, the supreme spirit, 
there is no use with me, his wife."

shloka: दृश्यमाने भवेत्प्रीतिः सौहृदं नास्त्यपश्यतः
translation:
"Friendly disposition will occur in what is being seen. There is no friendship to one who does 
not see. Ungrateful ones destroy frindship. But Rama will not destroy friendship."

shloka: किं नु मे न गुणाः केचित्किं वा भाग्यक्षयो मम
translation:
"I who is a woman who is perishing without the chief Rama to such me are there no good qualities 
or has my fortune diminished."

shloka: श्र्यो हि हीवितान्मर्तुं विहीनाया महात्मनः
translation:
"To me who is deprived of Rama with untroubled reputation, a warrior, annihilator of enemies, a 
great soul, more than living, death is good."

shloka: अथवा न्यस्तशस्त्रौ तौ वने मूलफलाशिनौ
translation:
"Or those two brothers who are best among men giving up weapons in the forest may have become dwellers 
of forest eating roots and fruits."

shloka: अथवा राक्षसेन्द्रेण रावणेन दुरात्मना
translation:
"Or Rama and Lakshmana the warrior brothers may have been killed by the evil soul king of ogres 
Ravana by deceit."

shloka: साहमेवंगते काले मर्तुमिच्छामि सर्वथा
translation:
"Under such circumstances and time, such I in all ways am desiring to die. Even in this grief, 
death is not bestowed on me."

shloka: धन्याः खलु महात्मानो मुनयस्त्यक्तकिल्बिषाः
translation:
"Great souled ones with abandoned sins, with a conquered mind, those with great fortune, sages 
are indeed fortunate to whom there is no pleasure and displeasure."

shloka: प्रियान्न संभवेद्दुःखमप्रियादधिकं भयम्
translation:
"From pleasure sorrow and from displeasure great fear do not occur to great souls. Whoever are 
separated from pleasure and displeasure, my obeisance to such great souls."

shloka: साहंत्युक्ता प्रियेणैव रामेन विदितात्मना
translation:
"Left by dear Rama with a well known mind coming under the control of sinful Ravana, such I will 
leave breath of life."

shloka:
इत्युक्ताह् सीतया घोरं राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः |
काश्चिज्जग्मुस्तदाख्यातुं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः
translation:
Thus spoken to by Seetha, ogresses swooned with anger terribly. Some went to tell that to Ravana 
the evil minded one.

shloka:
ततः सीतामुपागम्य राक्षस्यो घोरदर्शनाः |
पुनः पुरुषमेकार्थमनर्थार्थमथाब्रुवन्
translation:
Therafter ogresses with a terrible appearance neared Seetha and ten agin spoke words of evil purpose, 
with a single meaning and which were harsh.

shloka:
अद्येदानीं तवानार्ये सीते पापविनिश्चये |
राक्षस्यो भक्षयिष्यन्ति मांसमेतद्यथासुखम्
translation:
"O ignoble one! O one with a sinful resolve! O Seetha! Today at this moment ogreeses will eat this 
your flesh according to comfort."

shloka:
सीतां ताभिरनार्याभिर्दृष्ट्वा संतर्जितां तदा |
राक्षसी त्रिजटा वृद्धा शयाना वाक्यमब्रवीत्
translation:
Then, seeing Seetha frightened by those evil ones, an ogress named Trijata, sleeping till then, 
spoke these words.

shloka:
आत्मानं खादतानार्या न सीतां भक्षयिष्यथ |
जनकस्य सुतामिष्टां सुन्नषां दशरथस्य च
translation:
"O evil ones! Eat your selves. You will not eat Seetha who is the dear daughter of king Janaka 
and daughter-in-law of king Dasaratha."

shloka:
स्वप्नो ह्यद्य मया दृष्टो दारुनो रोमहर्षणः |
राक्षसानामभावाय भर्तुरस्या भवाय च
translation:
"Now a dream which is terrible, causing the hairs to stand erect for the destruction of ogres and 
for the welfare of Her husband, has been seen by me."

shloka:
एवमुक्टास्त्रिजटया राक्षस्यः क्रोधमूर्छिताः |
सर्वा एवाब्रुवन्भीतास्त्रिजटां तामिदं वचः
translation: Thus spoken to by Trijata all ogresses were frightened and spoke to that Trijata these words.

shloka:
कथयस्व त्वया दृष्टः स्वप्नोऽयं कीदृशो निशि |
तासां श्रुत्वा तु वचनं राक्षसीनां मुखाच्य्चुतम्
translation:
"Of what kind is this dream seen by you. Tell us". Listening to this utterance that came forth 
from the mouths of those ogresses, Trijata spoke at that time this word relating to the dream.

shloka: गजदन्तमयीं दिव्यां शिबिकामन्तरिक्षगाम्
translation:
"Rama wearing white garlands and clothes passing through the sky, Himself ascending a palanquin 
made of ivory tied with a thousand swans, arrived along with Lakshmana."

shloka:
स्वप्ने चाद्य मया दृष्टा सीता शुक्लाम्बरावृता |
सागरेण परिक्षिप्तं स्वेतं पर्वतमास्थिता
translation:
"Now it has been seen by me in the dream that Seetha also wearing white clothes was sitting on 
a white mountain surrounded by the ocean."

shloka:
रामेण संगता सीता भास्करेण प्रभा यथा |
राघवश्च मया दृष्टश्च तुर्दंष्ट्रं महागजम्
translation:
"Seetha came together with Rama like the light with the Sun. Rama also was seen by me to be mounted 
on a great elephant with four tusks and equalling a mountain and Rama wandered together with Lakshmana."

shloka: ततस्तौ नरशार्दूलौ दीप्यमानौ स्वतेजसा
translation:
"Thereafter shining with their own radiance, wearing white garlands and clothes, those two best 
among men Rama and Laksmana neared Seetha."

shloka: ततस्तस्य नगस्याग्रे ह्याकाशस्थस्य दन्तिनः
translation:
"Thereafter Seetha rested on the upper part of back of elephant in the sky; taken by Her husband 
Rama to the front of that mountain."

shloka: भर्तुरङ्कात्समुत्पत्य ततः कमललोचना
translation:
"Thereafter it has been seen by me that Seetha with eyes like lotuses has risen up from the lap 
of Her husband and gently touched the Moon and the Sun with Her hand."

shloka: ततस्ताभ्यां कुमाराभ्यामास्थितः स गजोत्तमः
translation:
"Thereafter that best elephant ascended by those princes Rama and Lakshmana and by Seetha with 
wide eyes stood on the top of Lanka."

shloka: पाण्डुरर्षभयुक्तेन रथेनाष्टयुजा स्वयम्
translation: "Rama together with wife Seetha, Himself came here in a chariot tied with eight white bulls."

shloka: लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया सह वीर्यवान्
translation:
"The valorous best among men Rama together with brother Lakshmana and with Seetha ascended wonderful 
Pushpaka aeroplane equalling the Sun, went in the northern direction."

shloka:
एवं स्वप्ने मया दृष्टो रामो विष्णुपराक्रमः |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया सह राघवः
translation:
"Rama with strength equalling that of Lord Vishnu, born in Raghu's dynasty together with brother 
Lakshmana and with Seetha has been seen by me thus in the dream."

shloka:
न हि रामो महातेजाः शोक्यो जेतुं सुरासुरैः |
राक्षसैर्वापि चान्यैर्वा स्वर्गः पापजनैरिव
translation:
"Rama with great glory is not possible to be defeated by Suras or by ogres or by others like heaven 
not being conquerable by sinners."

shloka:
रावणश्च मया दृष्टः क्षितौ तैलसमुक्षितः |
रक्तवासाह् पिबन् मत्तः करवीरकृतस्रजः
translation:
"Ravana also was seen by me on earth sprinkled with oil, with red clothes, with garlands tied with 
Oleander flowers, drinking oil and intoxicated."

shloka:
विमानात्पुष्पकादद्य रावणः पतितो भुवि |
कृष्यमाणः स्त्रिया दृष्टो मुण्डः कृष्णाम्बरः पुनः
translation:
"Now Ravana fallen down on to earth from Pushpaka aeroplane having the head shaved, wearing black 
clothes again was seen to be pulled by a woman."

shloka:
रथेन खरयुक्तेन रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनः |
पिबंस्तैलं हसन्नृतन् भ्रान्तचित्ताकुलेन्द्रियः
translation:
"Wearing red garlands and unguents, drinking oil, laughing, dancing, with a confused mind, with 
agitated senses, Ravana went by a chariot tied by donkeys."

shloka:
गर्दभेन ययौ शीग्रं दक्षिणां दिशमास्थितः |
पुनरेव मया दृष्टो रावणो राक्षसेश्वरः
translation:
"Undertaking southern direction, Ravana went quickly by a donkey.Again it was seen by me that the 
king of ogres Ravana stupefied with fear, fell down from the donkey with head down."

shloka: सहसोत्थाय संभ्रान्तो भयार्तो मदविह्वलः
translation:
"That Ravana rising up quickly, together with perplexity, distressed with fear, excited by passion, 
being naked, like a mad man, prattling many bad words, entering dirt with a bad smell, which was intolerable, 
horrible, dark, like the hell and quickly sank in that."

shloka: कण्ठे बद्ध्वा दशग्रीवं प्रमदा रक्तवासिनी
translation:
"A woman with red clothes, who was black, with body smeared with dirt, tying Ravana by the throat, 
was pulling hiim in southern direction."

shloka: एवं तत्र मया दृष्टह् कुम्भकर्णो निशाचरः
translation:
"In that dream the ogre Kumbhakarna has been seen thus by me. All Ravana's sons have been seen 
to be sprinkled with oil."

shloka: वराहेण दशग्रीवः शिंशुमारेण चेन्द्रजित्
translation: "Ravana by a pig, Indrajit by a porpoise, Kumbhakarna by a camel set out in southern direction."

shloka: एकस्तत्र मया दृष्टः श्वेतच्छत्रो विभीसणः
translation:
"Among those Vibhishana is the only one who has been seen by me to be having a white umbrella, 
wearing white garlands and clothes and anointing body with white unguents."

shloka: शङ्खदुन्दुभिनिर्घोषैर्नृत्तगीतैरलङ्कृतः
translation:
"Vibhishana is there adorned with the sound of conch shells and kettledrums, with dances and songs, 
ascended a best elephant equalling a mountain with the sound of a thundering cloud, with four tusks. He approached 
the sky together with four ministers"

shloka: समाजश्च मया दृष्टो गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनः
translation:
"An assembly also of ogres drinking oil and wearing red garlands, with red clothes, with the sound 
of songs and musical instruments has been seen by me."

shloka: लङ्का चेयं पुरी रम्या सवाजिरथकुञ्जरा
translation:
"This beautiful city of Lanka has also been seen together with horses and elephants with broken 
gates and arches fallen down in the ocean."

shloka: लङ्का दृष्टा मया स्वप्ने रावणेनाभिरक्षिता
translation:
"Lanka protected by Ravana has been seen by me in the dream to be burnt by a quick Vanara who is 
a messenger of Rama."

shloka: सीत्वा तैलं प्रनृत्ताश्च प्रहसन्त्यो महास्वनाः
translation:
"In Lanka horrible with ash, all ogresses were drinking oil, laughing heartily with a great noise 
and also dancing a lot."

shloka: कुम्भकर्णादयश्चेमे सर्वे राक्षसपुङ्गवाः
translation:
"All these best among ogres such as Kumbhakarna and others taking a red cloth entered a hole filled 
with cow dung."

shloka: अपगच्छत नश्यध्वं सीतामाप्नोति राघवः
translation:
"Go away! Be destroyed! Rama will get Seetha. With a great anger He will get you killed together 
with other ogres."

shloka: प्रियां बहुमतां भार्यां वनवासमनुव्रताम्
translation:
"Rama will not approve frightening ot threatening His dear wife who is highly valued by Him, who 
followed Him to live in the forest."

shloka: तदलं क्रूरवाक्यैश्च सान्त्वमेवाभिधीयताम्
translation:
"For that reason, enough of cruel words. Gentle words indeed be said. Let us request Seetha. This 
is agreeable to me."

shloka: यस्यामेवंविधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायां प्रदृश्यते
translation:
"Which woman while being sorrowful, such type of dream has been seen, that woman being released 
from various sorrows, will get unsurpassed pleasure."

shloka: भर्त्सितामपि याचध्वं राक्सस्यः किं विवक्षया
translation:
"O ogresses! Entreat Seetha who has been frightened. What is the use with a desire to speak. From 
Rama a horrible fear has come to ogres."

shloka: प्रणिपातप्रसन्ना हि मैथिली जनकात्मजा
चायावैगुण्यमात्रं तु शङ्के दुःखमुपस्थितम्
translation:
"I see an imperfection in complexion alone. I doubt that this princess who came near an aeroplane 
in my dream, who is not suited to sorrows received sorrow."

shloka: अर्थसिद्धिं तु वैदेह्याः पश्याम्यहमुपस्थिताम्
translation:
"I am seeing Seetha coming near accomplishment of motive. I also see the destruction of Ravana 
also and victory of Rama coming near."

shloka: निमित्तभूतमेतत्तु श्रोतुमस्या महत्प्रियम्
translation:
"Being a cause to listen to a great pleasure of Her, this throbbing eye long like a lotus petal 
is being seen my me."

shloka: ईषच्च हृषितो वास्या दक्षिणाया ह्यदक्षिणः
translation: "One left arm of this strightforward Seetha suddenly has become erect and is slightly trembling."

shloka: करेणुहस्तप्रतिमः सव्यश्चोरुरनुत्तमः
translation:
"Seetha's best left thigh equal to an elephant's trunk is trembling indicating Rama's standing 
in front of Her."

shloka:
पक्षी च शाखानिलयं प्रविष्टः |
पुनः पुनश्चोत्तमसान्त्ववादी |
सुस्वागतं वाचमुदीरयानः |
पुनः पुनश्चोदयतीव हृष्टः
translation:
"A bird also entering its dwelling place on a branch again and again speaking best consolating 
words, is telling heartily welcoming words being delighted again and again, as though impelling Seetha."

shloka:
सा राक्षसेन्द्रस्य वचो निशम्य |
तद्रावणस्याप्रियमप्रियार्ता |
सीता वितत्रास यथा वनान्ते 
|
सिंहाभिपन्ना गजराजकन्या
translation:
That Seetha, hearing those unpleasant words of Ravana, tormented by grief, was frightened like 
a tiny female-elephant overpowered by a lion in the middle of a forest.

shloka:
सा राक्षसीमध्यगता च भीरु |
र्वाग्भिर्भृशं रावणतर्जिता च |
कान्तारमध्ये विजने विसृष्टा 
|
बालेव कन्या विललाप सीता
translation:
That fearful Seetha, who was situated in the middle of female-demons and also threatened by Ravana 
with his words galore, lamented (as follows) like a young virgin who was left lonely in the midst of a forest.

shloka:
सत्यं बतेदं प्रवदन्ति लोके |
नाकालमृत्युर्भवतीति सन्तः |
यत्राहमेवं परिभर्त्स्यमाना 
|
जीवामि दीना क्षणमप्यपुण्या
translation:
"Truly the saints affirm that untimely death does not come in the world, as I being impure am surviving 
even for an instant, though being threatened in this way."

shloka:
सुखाद्विहीनं बहुदुःखपूर्ण |
मिदं तु नूनं हृदयं स्थिरं मे |
विशीर्यते यन्न सहस्रधाद्य 
|
वज्राहतं शृङ्गमिवाचलस्य
translation:
"Though devoid of happiness and frequently full of sorrow, my heart must be hard indeed, in that 
it does not break into a thousand pieces today like a mountain-top struck by lightning."

shloka:
वैवास्ति दोषो मम नूनमत्र |
वध्याहमस्याप्रियदर्शनस्य |
भावं न चास्याहमनुप्रदातु |
मलं द्विजो मन्त्रमिवाद्विजाय
translation:
"There is no fault of mine in this matter. I have become killable at the hands of this demon of 
disagreeable perception. I am not able to give him my affection any more than a member of the twice-born classes 
would offer a mystical verse to one not belonging to the twice-born classes."

shloka:
नूनं ममाङ्गान्यचिरादनार्यः |
शस्त्रैः शितै श्छेत्स्यति राक्षसेन्द्रः |
तस्मिन्ननागच्छति 
लोकनाथे |
गर्भस्थजन्तोरिव शल्यकृन्तः
translation:
"If Rama the Ruler of the world does not come here, the evil Ravana, the king of Demons will cut 
off my limbs with his sharpened weapons, even as a surgeon would cut the limbs of a lifeless feotus."

shloka:
दुःखं बतेदं मम दुःखिताया |
मासौ चिरायाधिगमिष्यतो द्वौ |
बद्धस्य वध्यस्य तथा निशान्ते 
|
राजापराधादिव तस्करस्य
translation:
"To me lamenting, two months will go up to a long time, as at the end of a night a thief imprisoned 
and to be capitally punished under the detention orders of a king. Alas! This is painful."

shloka:
हा राम हा लक्ष्मण हा सुमित्रे |
हा राममातः सह मे जनन्या |
एषा विपद्याम्यहमल्पभाग्या 
|
महार्णवे नौरिव मूढवाता
translation:
"O Rama, O Lakshmana, O Sumitra, O Kausalya! O mother! I, of a scanty fortune, am going to be destroyed, 
like a ship driven out of its course by a strong wind in a mighty ocean."

shloka:
तरस्विनौ धारयता मृगस्य |
सत्त्वेन रूपं मनुजेन्द्रपुत्रौ |
नूनं विशस्तौ मम कारणात्तौ 
|
सिंहर्षभौ द्वाविव वैद्युतेन
translation:
"In the disguise of a deer, those two energetic sons of Dasaratha were surely killed for my sake, 
as two excellent lions killed by a flashing thunderbolt."

shloka:
नूनं स कालो मृगरूपधारी |
मामल्पभाग्यां लुलुभे तदानीम् |
यत्रार्यपुत्रं विससर्ज मूढा 
|
रामानुजं लक्ष्मणपूर्वजं च
translation:
"Certainly that Time-spirit, assuming the guise of a deer, allured me, a woman of poor fortune 
at that time and to whom I, a stupid woman, sent forth (far away) Lakshmana and the noble prince Rama the elder 
brother of Lakshmana."

shloka:
हा राम सत्यव्रत दीर्घबाहो |
हा पूर्णचन्द्रप्रतिमानवक्त्र |
हा जीवलोकस्य हितः प्रियश्च 
|
वध्यां न मां वेत्सि हि राक्षसानाम्
translation:
"O Rama, the strictly truthful man and the long-armed, O the man whose face resembles the full-moon! 
You, who are well-disposed of the world of living beings, do not indeed know me to have been sentenced to death 
by the demons."

shloka:
अनन्यदैवत्वमियं क्षमा च |
भूमौ च शय्या नियमश्च धर्मे |
पतिव्रतात्वं विफलं ममेदम् |
कृतं कृतघ्नेष्विव मानुषाणाम्
translation:
"My not having a deity (other than my husband), this patience, my reposing on the floor, my restriction 
in righteousness, my devotion to the husband - all this has become a waste, like a good act done by men to ungrateful 
men becoming waste".

shloka:
मोघो हि धर्मश्चरितो मयायं |
तथैकपत्नीत्वमिदं निरर्थम् |
या त्वां न पश्यामि कृशा विवर्णा 
|
हीना त्वया संगमने निराशा
translation:
"For me who is not seeing you, who is bereft of you, who is not hopeful of coming into contact 
with you, who is emaciated and pale in complexion this righteous act performed by me has indeed become a waste. 
Likewise, this state of my being only one wife to you has become useless.."

shloka:
पितुर्निदेशं नियमेन कृत्वा वनान्निवृत्तश्चरितव्रतश्च |
स्त्रीभिस्तु मन्ये विपुलेक्षणाभिस्त्वं 
रंस्यसे वीतभयः कृतार्थः
translation:
"Having fulfilled your father's command as per the order of his words and observed your vow, you 
return from the forest fearlessly and having accomplished your purpose, I think you will enjoy carnally with large-eyed 
women."

shloka:
अहं तु राम त्वयि जातकामा चिरं विनाशाय निबद्धभावा |
मोघं चरित्वाथ तपो व्रतञ्च त्यक्ष्यामि 
धिग्जीवितमल्पभाग्याम्
translation:
"O Rama! Having performed austerity and vow in vain, I for myself who has fallen in love with you 
and in whose was confined an affection for you for a long time, for my own destruction, I can lose my life. Woe 
to me of my little fortune!"

shloka:
सा जीवितं क्षिप्रमहं त्यजेयं |
विषेण शस्त्रेण शितेन वापि |
विषस्य दाता न हि मेऽस्ति 
कश्चि |
च्छस्त्रस्य वा वेश्मनि राक्षसस्य
translation:
"I as such will abandon quickly my life by poison or by a sharp weapon. To me, none is there, who 
is a giver either of a poison or of a sharp weapon in the house of Ravana."

shloka:
इतीव देवी बहुधा विलप्य |
सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती |
प्रवेपमाना परिशुष्कवक्त्रा |
नगोत्तमं पुष्पितमाससाद
translation:
Thus lamenting in several ways, Seetha was recollecting Rama in all spirits and trembling with 
and emaciated face, approached that excellent tree in bloom.

shloka:
सा शोकतप्ता बहुधा विचिन्त्य |
सीताथ वेण्युद्ग्रथनं गृहीत्वा |
उद्भुध्य वेण्युद्ग्रथनेन 
श्रीघ्र |
महं गमिष्यामि यमस्य मूलम्
translation:
Seetha, who was tormented with grief, thus thinking in various ways and thereafter holding her 
braid of hair looking like a hanging rope (now thought within herself) "I shall go to the presence of Yama the 
God of Death by tying my neck quickly with my braid of hair looking like a hanging rope"

shloka:
उपस्थिता सा मृदुसर्वगात्री |
शाखां गृहीत्वाथ नगस्य तस्य |
तस्यास्तु रामं प्रविचिन्तयन्त्या 
|
रामानुजं स्वं च कुलं शुभाङ्ग्याः
translation:
Thereafter Seetha with all her soft limbs stood seizing a branch of that tree. To her having handsome 
limbs, who was thinking of Rama, Lakshmana and her own race, then appeared many omens, which were not having adequate 
occasion for grief, which procured courage in the world, which were excellent and which were seen earlier also 
as thoroughly efficacious.

shloka:
तथा गताम् ताम् व्यथिताम् अनिन्दिताम् |
व्यपेत हर्षाम् परिदीन मानसाम् |
शुभाम् निमित्तानि 
शुभानि भेजिरे |
नरम् श्रिया जुष्टम् इव उपजीविनः
translation:
To her who was in such circumstances, who was in distress, who was irraproachable, devoid of joy 
and dejected but virtuous, was bestowed with auspicious omens, as a prosperous man is bestowed with dependent 
servants.

shloka:
तस्याः शुभम् वामम् अराल पक्ष्म |
राजी वृतम् कृष्ण विशाल शुक्लम् |
प्रास्पन्दत एकम् नयनम् 
सुकेश्या |
मीन आहतम् पद्मम् इव अभिताम्रम्
translation:
The beautifully haired Seetha's left eye, which was auspicious, whose surrounding row of eye-lashes 
were curved, which was black, wide and bright-looking; was predominantly quivering, like a red lotus quivered 
by the blow of a fish.

shloka:
भुजः च चार्व् अन्चित पीन वृत्तः |
पर अर्ध्य काल अगुरु चन्दन अर्हः |
अनुत्तमेन अध्युषितः 
प्रियेण |
चिरेण वामः समवेपत आशु
translation:
Her left shoulder, which was pretty, distinguished beefy and round, which deserved to be applied 
with excellent black aloe and sandalwood paste, which had been used

shloka:
गज इन्द्र हस्त प्रतिमः च पीनः |
तयोः द्वयोः सम्हतयोः सुजातः |
प्रस्पन्दमानः पुनः ऊरुः 
अस्या |
रामम् पुरस्तात् स्थितम् आचचक्षे
translation:
Of her two thighs kept together, the left tigh which was beefy and well born, which resembled the 
trunk of a princely elephant was predominantly quivering, spoke indistinctly of existenc of Rama in front.

shloka:
शुभम् पुनः हेम समान वर्णम् |
ईषत् रजो ध्वस्तम् इव अमल अक्ष्याः |
वासः स्थितायाः शिखर 
अग्र दन्त्याः |
किंचित् परिस्रंसत चारु गात्र्याः
translation:
Again, the clothing of Seetha standing there, of spotless eyes and charming limbs, having teeth 
resembling the buds of jasmine, which was of golden shade and was slightly soiled as it were with dust, glited 
down, which appeared auspicious (for her).

shloka:
एतैः निमित्तैः अपरैः च सुभ्रूः |
सम्बोधिता प्राग् अपि साधु सिद्धैः |
वात आतप क्लान्तम् 
इव प्रनष्टम् |
वर्षेण बीजम् प्रतिसम्जहर्ष
translation:
Bolstered by these and some other omens which straight explained that they were fruitful on the 
earlier occasion also, Seetha of beautiful eyebrows disclosed a great joy, even as a seed vanished and withered 
by the wind and the sun, got sprouted by rain.

shloka:
तस्याः पुनः बिम्ब फल उपम ओष्ठम् |
स्वक्षि भ्रु केश अन्तम् अराल पक्ष्म |
वक्त्रम् बभासे 
सित शुक्ल दम्ष्ट्रम् |
राहोः मुखाच् चन्द्र इव प्रमुक्तः
translation:
Moreover, having the lips resembling Bimba fruit, having beautiful eyes and eyebrows, whose eye 
lids are curved, having charming white teeth, her face shone like the moon liberated from the mouth of the demon 
Rahu.

shloka:
सा वीत शोका व्यपनीत तन्द्री |
शान्त ज्वरा हर्ष विबुद्ध सत्त्वा |
अशोभत आर्या वदनेन शुक्ले 
|
शीत अन्शुना रात्रिः इव उदितेन
translation:
Free from sorrow, her weariness removed, her mental affliction alleviated and her consciousness 
awakened with exaltation, that esteemed lady (Seetha) looked handsome with her countenance, as a night with the 
moon appears during the bright fortnight.

shloka:
हनुमान् अपि विक्रान्तः सर्वम् शुश्राव तत्त्वतः |
सीतायाः त्रिजटायाः च राक्षसीनाम् च तर्जनम्
translation:
The valiant Hanuma also heard truly all those words of Seetha, Trijata and the threatening words 
of the female demons.

shloka:
अवेक्षमाणः ताम् देवीम् देवताम् इव नन्दने |
ततो बहु विधाम् चिन्ताम् चिन्तयामास वानरः
translation:
Thereafter, seeing that Seetha as a divine lady in the garden of Nandana, Hanuma echoed his thought 
in various ways.

shloka:
याम् कपीनाम् सहस्राणि सुबहूनि अयुतानि च |
दिक्षु सर्वासु मार्गन्ते सा इयम् आसादिता मया
translation:
"Which Seetha is being searched in all directions by many thousands and myriads of monkeys, the 
same Seetha has been found by me."

shloka:
चारेण तु सुयुक्तेन शत्रोः शक्तिम् अवेक्षिता |
गूढेन चरता तावत् अवेक्षितम् इदम् मया
translation:
"By me, employed thoughtfully (by my Master) as a secret agent and gone about secretly with a view 
to ascertain the enemy's strength, this has been perceived.

shloka:
राक्षसानाम् विशेषः च पुरी च इयम् अवेक्षिता |
राक्षस अधिपतेः अस्य प्रभावो रावणस्य च
translation:
"The characteristics of demons, this town and the power of the king of demons, Ravana, have been 
perceived by me."

shloka:
युक्तम् तस्य अप्रमेयस्य सर्व सत्त्व दयावतः |
समाश्वासयितुम् भार्याम् पतिदर्शन कान्क्षिणीम्
translation:
"It is proper for me to console the wife of Rama, desirous of seeing her husband who is compassionate 
towards all beings and who is of immeasurable might."

shloka:
अहम् आश्वासयामि एनाम् पूर्ण चन्द्र निभ आननाम् |
अदृष्ट दुह्खाम् दुह्खस्य न हि अन्तम् अधिगच्छतीम्
translation:
"I shall console this woman, whose face resembles a full moon, who is having an unforeseen affliction, 
who is tormented by grief and who is not attaining the end to her affliction."

shloka:
यदि हि अहम् इमाम् देवीम् शोक उपहत चेतनाम् |
अनाश्वास्य गमिष्यामि दोषवत् गमनम् भवेत्
translation:
"If I return without consoling this Seetha, the wife of Rama, even though her mind is tormented 
by grief, my departure becomes blemished."

shloka:
गते हि मयि तत्र इयम् राज पुत्री यशस्विनी |
परित्राणम् अविन्दन्ती जानकी जीवितम् त्यजेत्
translation:
"Not finding a rescue when I return to Kishkindha, the illustrious princess Seetha may give up 
her life."

shloka:
मया च स महाबाहुः पूर्ण चन्द्र निभ आननः |
समाश्वासयितुम् न्याय्यः सीता दर्शन लालसः
translation:
"That long-armed Rama having the countenance of a full moon, eagerly longing to see Seetha, is 
fit to be consoled by me."

shloka:
निशा चरीणाम् प्रत्यक्षम् अक्षमम् च अभिभाषणम् |
कथम् नु खलु कर्तव्यम् इदम् कृच्छ्र गतो हि 
अहम्
translation:
"It is not proper to speak with her within the sight of these female-demons. How indeed is this 
to be done? I am indeed perplexed."

shloka:
अनेन रात्रि शेषेण यदि न आश्वास्यते मया |
सर्वथा न अस्ति संदेहः परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्
translation:
"If she is not consoled by me during the rest of this night, she will forsake her life by all means. 
There is no doubt about it."

shloka:
रामः च यदि पृच्छेन् माम् किम् माम् सीता अब्रवीत् वचः |
किम् अहम् तम् प्रतिब्रूयाम् असम्भाष्य 
सुमध्यमाम्
translation:
"If Rama enquires of me as to what words did Seetha speak about him, what can I say to Rama without 
speaking now to this Seetha, the slender-waisted lady?"

shloka:
सीता संदेश रहितम् माम् इतः त्वरया गतम् |
निर्दहेत् अपि काकुत्स्थः क्रुद्धः तीव्रेण चक्षुषा
translation:
"To me returning in haste from here without carrying Seetha's message Rama may get irritated and 
burn me up with his pungent eyes."

shloka:
यदि चेत् योजयिष्यामि भर्तारम् राम कारणात् |
व्यर्थम् आगमनम् तस्य ससैन्यस्य भविष्यति
translation:
"Even if I instigate my master Sugreeva to do his best in the cause of Rama, his arrival here with 
an army will be futile."

shloka:
अन्तरम् तु अहम् आसाद्य राक्षसीनाम् इह स्थितः |
शनैः आश्वासयिष्यामि सम्ताप बहुलाम् इमाम्
translation:
"Staying here itself and getting hold of an opportunity even in the midst of the female-demons 
(when they are in attentive), I shall slowly console Seetha who is very much in distress."

shloka:
अहम् हि अतितनुः चैव वनरः च विशेषतः |
वाचम् च उदाहरिष्यामि मानुषीम् इह संस्कृताम्
translation:
"However, I am very small in stature, particularly as a monkey and can speak now Sanskrit, the 
human language too."

shloka:
यदि वाचम् प्रदास्यामि द्विजातिः इव संस्कृताम् |
रावणम् मन्यमाना माम् सीता भीता भविष्यति
translation:
"If I use Sanskrit language like a brahmin, Seetha will get frightened, thinking me as Ravana. 
Especially, how can a monkey speak it?"

shloka: अवश्यम् एव वक्तव्यम् मानुषम् वाक्यम् अर्थवत्
translation:
"Certainly, meaningful words of a human being are to be spoken by me. Otherwise, the virtuous Seetha 
cannot be consoled."

shloka: सा इयम् आलोक्य मे रूपम् जानकी भाषितम् तथा
translation:
"Looking at my figure and the language, Seetha who was already frightened previously by the demons, 
will get frightened again."

shloka: ततो जात परित्रासा शब्दम् कुर्यान् मनस्विनी
translation:
"Thereafter, this large-eyed Seetha who is full of mind, thinking me as Ravana who can assume any 
form at will, may shout loudly, engendered by fear."

shloka: सीतया च कृते शब्दे सहसा राक्षसी गणः
translation:
"As soon as Seetha shouts loudly, a troop of female-demons, wielding various kinds of weapons and 
appearing dreadful as Yama the Lord of Death, may assemble here."

shloka: ततो माम् सम्परिक्षिप्य सर्वतो विकृत आननाः
translation:
"Then those ugly faced female-demons may encircle me from all sides and try to catch and kill me 
with all their might."

shloka: गृह्य शाखाः प्रशाखाश्च स्कन्धांश्चोत्तमशाखिनाम्
translation:
"Then, seeing me running hither and thither, seizing big branches, twigs and trunks of excellent 
trees, they may get alarmed with fear."

shloka: मम रूपम् च सम्प्रेक्ष्य वनम् विचरतो महत्
translation:
"The ugly faced female-demons will be frightened with fear, after seeing my huge figure wandering 
in the grove."

shloka: ततः कुर्युः समाह्वानम् राक्षस्यो रक्षसाम् अपि
translation: "Then those female-demons may call the other demons too retained by Ravana in his house."

shloka: ते शूल शर निस्त्रिंश विविध आयुध पाणयः
translation:
"Those female-demons with an element of turbulence and rapidity may rush into a battle with various 
kinds of weapons like spears lances and swords."

shloka: सम्क्रुद्धः तैः तु परितो विधमन् रक्षसाम् बलम्
translation:
"Surrounded on all sides by them, I may not be able to reach the other shore of the great ocean, 
while destroying the army of demons."

shloka: माम् वा गृह्णीयुः आप्लुत्य बहवः शीघ्र कारिणः
translation:
"Or having jumped up (over me) many demons operating speedily may capture me. Then, Seetha may 
not be able to know the occurrence of my arrival. Even I may get captured too."

shloka: हिंसा अभिरुचयो हिंस्युः इमाम् वा जनक आत्मजाम्
translation:
"Or the violent minded demons may kill this Seetha. Consequently this work of Rama and Sugreeva 
will be ruined."

shloka: उद्देशे नष्ट मार्गे अस्मिन् राक्षसैः परिवारिते
translation:
"Seetha is residing in this secret place, with a concealed access, surrounded by demons and encircled 
by an ocean."

shloka: विशस्ते वा गृहीते वा रक्षोभिः मयि सम्युगे
translation:
"If I am killed in the battle or got captured by the demons, I do not see any other companion for 
Rama who can fulfill this work (of searching for Seetha)."

shloka: विमृशन् च न पश्यामि यो हते मयि वानरः
translation:
"Even after due reflection, I do not see any monkey who can transgress the ocean with a breadth 
of one hundred Yojanas, in case I am killed."

shloka: कामम् हन्तुम् समर्थो अस्मि सहस्राणि अपि रक्षसाम्
translation:
"I am competent to kill even thousands of demons. I am quite sure. But, after doing such a large 
battle, I may not be capable of reaching the other shore of the ocean."

shloka: असत्यानि च युद्धानि संशयो मे न रोचते
translation:
'Conflicts are unreal too and to me, there is no desire for uncertainty. which intellectual will 
do an assured act with an apprehension?"

shloka: एष दोषो महान् हि स्यान् मम सीता अभिभाषणे
translation: "If I do not talk, there will be Seetha's death. If I talk to Seetha, this great lapse will occur."

shloka: भूताः च अर्था विनश्यन्ति देश काल विरोधिताः
translation:
"Actions which are going to be accomplished shortly, get spoiled at the hands of a accomplished 
shortly, get spoiled at the hands of a confused messenger, when the actions are set in opposition to time and 
space, even as darkness disappears at sun rise."

shloka: अर्थ अनर्थ अन्तरे बुद्धिः निश्चिता अपि न शोभते
translation:
"Even if a decision is taken, regarding what is worthy and what is worthless, it does not yield 
good results. Messengers boasting themselves to be learned, thus indeed ruin those actions."

shloka: न विनश्येत् कथम् कार्यम् वैक्लव्यम् न कथम् भवेत्
translation:
"How does not my work get spoiled? How should I avoid my feebleness? Also how does not my leaping 
across the sea become vain?"

shloka: कथम् नु खलु वाक्यम् मे शृणुयान् न उद्विजेत च
translation:
"How can Seetha hear my words without fear?" Thinking in this way, the wise Hanuma made up his 
mind (as follows):

shloka: रामम् अक्लिष्ट कर्माणम् स्व बन्धुम् अनुकीर्तयन्
translation:
"If I eulogize Rama, who is unwearied in action and a good relation, I shall not frighten her, 
whose mind is directed towards that relation."

shloka: इक्ष्वाकूणाम् वरिष्ठस्य रामस्य विदित आत्मनः
translation:
"Offering auspicious and righteous words about Rama the most excellent prince Ikshvaku dynasty 
who possesses a learned soul and myself speaking in a sweet voice, I shall make everything intelligible so that 
Seetha rightly believes everything."

shloka:
इति स बहु विधम् महाअनुभावो |
जगति पतेः प्रमदाम् अवेक्षमाणः |
मधुरम् अवितथम् जगाद वाक्यम् 
|
द्रुम विटप अन्तरम् आस्थितो
translation:
The noble-minded Hanuman, abiding in the midst of the twigs of the trees and seeing Seetha, spoke 
the following words of many kinds which were not futile.

shloka:
एवम् बहु विधाम् चिन्ताम् चिन्तयित्व महाकपिः |
संश्रवे मधुरम् वाक्यम् वैदेह्या व्याजहार 
ह
translation:
Thus reflecting on many kinds of thought, Hanuma spoke the following sweet words within the hearing 
range of Seetha.

shloka:
राजा दशरथो नाम रथ कुन्जर वाजिनाम् |
पुण्य शीलो महाकीर्तिः ऋजुः आसीन् महायशाः
translation:
"There was a king named Dasaratha who was very glorious among the kings of Ikshvaku dynasty and 
had a virtuous disposition. He owned chariots, elephants and horses, becoming very famous.

shloka:
राजर्षीणां गुणश्रेष्ठस्तपसा चर्षिभिः समः |
चक्र वर्ति कुले जातः पुरम् दर समो बले
translation:
"He was excellent in virtues among royal sages. He was equal to the seven sages in austerity. He 
was born in the lineage of emperors and was equivalent to Indra in prowess."

shloka:
अहिंसा रतिः अक्षुद्रो घृणी सत्य पराक्रमः |
मुख्यः च इक्ष्वाकु वंशस्य लक्ष्मीवाम्ल् लक्ष्मि 
वर्धनः
translation:
"He was keen on harmlessness. He was not vulgar. He was compassionate. He was truly mighty. He 
was an eminent king in Ikshvaku race. He was endowed with prosperity and was causing to increase prosperity."

shloka:
पार्थिव व्यञ्जनैः युक्तः पृथु श्रीः पार्थिव ऋषभः |
पृथिव्याम् चतुः अन्तयाम् विश्रुतः सुखदः 
सुखी
translation:
"The king Dasaratha was endowed with royal characteristics, highly prosperous, excellent among 
kings and highly prosperous, excellent among kings and famous on earth with its four borders. He was happy man 
and gave happiness to others."

shloka:
तस्य पुत्रः प्रियो ज्येष्ठः तारा अधिप निभ आननः |
रामो नाम विशेषज्ञः श्रेष्ठः सर्व धनुष्मताम्
translation:
"There was an eldest son named Rama to that Dasaratha. Rama was beloved having a moon-like face. 
He, knows the distinctions among humans and others. He was excellent among all the wielders of the bow."

shloka:
रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य स्व जनस्य अपि रक्षिता |
रक्षिता जीव लोकस्य धर्मस्य च परम् तपः
translation:
"That Rama who annihilates enemies, is a protector of his own mode of life, a protector of his 
own people, a protector of every living being and a protector of righteousness."

shloka:
तस्य सत्य अभिसंधस्य वृद्धस्य वचनात् पितुः |
सभार्यः सह च भ्रात्रा वीरः प्रव्रजितो वनम्
translation:
"By the command of that Dasaratha, his old father and true-speaking man, that Rama a brave man 
went on exile to a forest along with his wife and brother."

shloka:
तेन तत्र महाअरण्ये मृगयाम् परिधावता |
राक्षसा निहताः शूरा बहवः कामरूपिणः
translation:
"While hunting in that forest, that Rama killed many demons who were valiant and who could assume 
any form at will."

shloka:
जन स्थान वधम् श्रुत्वा हतौ च खर दूषणौ |
ततः तु अमर्ष अपहृता जानकी रावणेन तु
translation:
"Thereafter, hearing about the killing of demons in Janasthana, a part of Dandaka forest, in addition 
to killing of Khara and Dushana the demons, the enraged Ravana took away, Seetha, by deceiving Rama in creating 
an illusive image of deer in the forest."

shloka: स मार्गमाणस्ताम् देवीम् रामः सीतामन्न्दिताम्
translation:
"Searching for Seetha the irreproachable lady, that Rama met a monkey called Sugreeva as his friend 
in the forest."

shloka: ततः स वालिनम् ह्त्वा रामः परपुरम्जयः
translation:
"Thereafter, Rama the conqueror of enemy's cities and very strong man, killed Vali and gave away 
that kingdom of monkeys to Sugreeva."

shloka: सुग्रीवेणापि संदिष्टा हरयः कामरूपिणः
translation:
"As commanded and sent by Sugreeva, thousands of monkeys capable of assuming form at their will, 
are searching for that lady Seetha in all quarters of the earth."

shloka: अहम् सम्पातिवचनाच्छतयोजनमायतम्
translation:
"By the words of Sampati, I a swift monkey crossed the ocean having a length of one hundred yojanas 
for the sake of this broad eyed Seetha."

shloka: यथा रूपाम् यथा वर्णाम् यथा लक्ष्मीम् विनिश्चिताम्
translation:
"This Seetha has been found by me according to the same comeliness, complexion and the bodily marks 
as I had heard from Rama."

shloka: विरराम एवम् उक्त्वा असौ वाचम् वानर पुम्गवः
translation: Having spoken these words, Hanuma kept quiet. Hearing those words, Seetha too got a great surprise.

shloka: ततः सा वक्र केश अन्ता सुकेशी केश सम्वृतम्
translation:
Thereafter, that Seetha whose consciousness was enshrouded by affliction, whose hair-ends were 
curved and who was of a fearful nature, lifted her face and looked towards Shimshupa tree.

shloka:
निशम्य सीता वचनम् कपेश्च |
दिशश्च सर्वाः प्रदिशश्च वीक्ष्य |
स्वयम् प्रहर्षं परमं जगाम 
|
सर्वात्मना राममनुस्मरन्ती
translation:
Hearing Hanuma's words and looking at all quarters and sub-quarters, Seetha was recollecting Rama 
in all ways and obtained a great joy.

shloka:
सा तिर्यग् ऊर्ध्वम् च तथा अपि अधस्तान् |
निरीक्षमाणा तम् अचिन्त्य बुद्धिम् |
ददर्श पिन्ग 
अधिपतेः अमात्यम् |
वात आत्मजम् सूर्यम् इव उदयस्थम्
translation:
Looking at sides, up and down, that Seetha saw that Hanuman, the sun of wind-god, having an unimaginable 
intelligence, the minister of Sugreeva and looking like the sun behind an eastern mountain.

shloka:
ततः शाखा अन्तरे लीनम् दृष्ट्वा चलित मानसा |
वेष्टितार्जुनवस्त्रम् तं विद्युत्सम्घातपिङ्गलम्
translation:
Then, seeing Hanuma, who was tawny coloured like a series of flashing thunderbolts wrapped up in 
a white cloth and hiding behind the branches of a tree, Seetha had her mind shaken.

shloka:
सा ददर्श कपिम् तत्र प्रश्रितम् प्रिय वादिनम् |
पुल्लाशोकोत्कराभासम् तप्तचामिकरेक्षणम्
translation:
Seetha beheld there a monkey, beaming like a cluster of Ashoka flowers wide opened, with his eyes 
resembling regined gold, humble and speaking agreeable words.

shloka:
मैथिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नो अयम् इति भामिनी |
अहो भीममिदं रूपं वानरस्य दुरासदम्
translation:
Seetha got a great surprise and thought (as follows): "Alas! This monkey is hard to be approached, 
fearful and difficult to be looked at." Thus thinking, she was bewildered again.

shloka: विललाप भृशं सीता करुणम् भयमोहिता
translation:
The splendid woman Seetha, bewildered by fear and afflicted with grief, lamented most piteously 
saying "O, Rama! O, Rama! and "O Lakshmana!". Seetha wept faintly in a low voice in many ways.

shloka:
सा तम् दृष्ट्वा हरिश्रेष्ठं विनीतवदुपस्थितम् |
मैथिली चिन्तयामास स्वप्नोऽयमिति भामिनी
translation: Seeing that excellent monkey appraching humbly, that splendid woman Seetha thought it as a dream.

shloka:
सा वीक्षमाणा पृथुभुग्नवक्त्रं शाखामृगेन्द्रस्य यथोक्तकारम् |
ददर्श पिङ्गप्रवरं महार्हं 
वातात्मजं बुद्धिमतां वरिष्ठम्
translation:
Seetha, looking hither and thither, saw Hanuman, who was having a wide and curved mouth, doing 
acts as told by sugreeva the king of monkeys, the foremost of monkeys, greatly adored and the best among the inelligent.

shloka:
सा तम् समीक्ष्य एव भृशम् विसम्ज्ञा गत असु कल्पा इव बभूव सीता |
चिरेण सम्ज्ञाम् प्रतिलभ्य 
चैव चैव विचिन्तयामास विशाल नेत्रा
translation:
As soon as seeing Hanuma Seetha lost her consciousness very much and became seemingly lifeless. 
Regaining her consciousness after a long time the wide eyed Seetha moreover thought (as follows)

shloka:
स्वप्नो मया अयम् विकृतो अद्य दृष्टः शाखा मृगः शास्त्र गणैः निषिद्धः |
स्वस्ति अस्तु रामाय 
सलक्ष्मणाय तथा पितुः मे जनकस्य राज्ञः
translation:
"Today, I saw an ugly monkey in my dream, which is forbidden according to a body of scriptures. 
May it be well with Rama together with Lakshmana and with my father, King Janaka.

shloka:
स्वप्नो अपि न अयम् न हि मे अस्ति निद्रा |
शोकेन दुह्खेन च पीडितायाः |
सुखम् हि मे न 
अस्ति यतो अस्मि हीना |
तेन इन्दु पूर्ण प्रतिम आननेन
translation:
"This is not a dream. To me, tormented by sorrow and grief, there is indeed no sleep. To me, separated 
from Rama whose countenance resembles a full moon, there is no happiness indeed!"

shloka:
रामेति रामेति सदैव बुद्ध्या विचिन्त्या वाचा ब्रुवती तमेव |
तस्यानुरूपं च कथां तदर्था मेवं 
प्रपश्यामि तथा शृणोमि
translation:
"Since I am pondering with my mind about that Rama only, and always saying 'Rama! Rama!' thus, 
confomably I am seeing and hearing a story thus corresponding to he same thought."

shloka:
अहम् हि तस्य अद्य मनो भवेन सम्पीडिता तत् गत सर्व भावा |
विचिन्तयन्ती सततम् तम् एव तथैव 
पश्यामि तथा शृणोमि
translation:
"Tormented as I am today by manmatha god of love longing for Rama, my whole feelings directed towards 
him and constantly thinking of him alone, in the like manner I am seeing him and in the like manner i am hearing 
of him alone."

shloka:
मनो रथः स्यात् इति चिन्तयामि |
तथा अपि बुद्ध्या च वितर्कयामि |
किम् कारणम् तस्य हि न 
अस्ति रूपम् |
सुव्यक्त रूपः च वदति अयम् माम्
translation:
"I am imagining that my wish will be fulfilled. Likewise, I am reasoning my wish by my intellect 
also. There is no concrete form indeed for my wish. He, with a well manifested form is speaking to me. for what 
reason?"

shloka:
नमो अस्तु वाचः पतये सवज्रिणे स्वयम्भुवे चैव हुत अशनाय |
अनेन च उक्तम् यत् इदम् मम अग्रतो 
वन ओकसा तच् च तथा अस्तु न अन्यथा
translation:
"My salutation to Brihaspati the Lord of eloquence, together with Indra the wielder of a thunderbolt, 
to Brahma the self-existent Lord and to the Lord of Fire eating the oblations! Let whatever words spoken by this 
monkey be true! Let them not be untrue!"

shloka:
सोऽवतीर्य द्रुमात्तस्माद्विद्रुमप्रतिमाननः |
विनीतवेषः कृपणः प्रणिपत्योपसृत्य च
translation:
That Hanuma, with coral-coloured face, very bright, the son of wind-god, wearing a humble and feeble 
look, approached Seetha by stepping down from the tree and offered her his salutation by keeping his joined palms 
on his head and spoke the following sweet words:

shloka:
का नु पद्म पलाश अक्षी क्लिष्ट कौशेय वासिनी |
द्रुमस्य शाखाम् आलम्ब्य तिष्ठसि त्वम् अनिन्दिता
translation:
"O Lady with your eyes resembling lotus leaves, wearing a worn out silken cloth! O, the irreproachable 
one! You have stood, holding by the hand a branch of the tree who are you?"

shloka:
किम् अर्थम् तव नेत्राभ्याम् वारि स्रवति शोकजम् |
पुण्डरीक पलाशाभ्याम् विप्रकीर्णम् इव उदकम्
translation:
"Tears of sorrow are gushing down from your eyes, as water is scattered down from two lotus-petals. 
Why?"

shloka:
सुराणाम् असुराणाम् च नाग गन्धर्व रक्षसाम् |
यक्षाणाम् किम्नराणाम् च का त्वम् भवसि शोभने
translation:
"O auspicious lady! In whom are you born-whether in celestials or in ogres or in serpent-demons 
or in celestial musicians or in demons or in semi-divine beings or in mythical beings?"

shloka:
का त्वम् भवसि रुद्राणाम् मरुताम् वा वर आनने |
वसूनाम् वा वर आरोहे देवता प्रतिभासि मे
translation:
"O lovely-faced woman! Who are you among eleven Rudras who bestow strength, or among Maruts the 
storm-gods or among eight Vasus the beneficent gods? O Handsome lady with fine hips! You appear to me as a deity."

shloka:
किम् नु चन्द्रमसा हीना पतिता विबुध आलयात् |
रोहिणी ज्योतिषाम् श्रेष्ठा श्रेष्ठा सर्व गुण 
अन्विता
translation:
"Are you Rohini, endowed with all the best qualities, fallen from heaven, left behind by moon and 
excellent among stars."

shloka: कोपात् वा यदि वा मोहात् भर्तारम् असित ईक्षणा
translation:
"O dark-eyed lady! Are you not the auspicious Arundhati, who irritated her husband, Vasishta the 
sage either by anger or by error?"

shloka: को नु पुत्रः पिता भ्रात भर्ता वा ते सुमध्यमे
translation:
"O the slender waisted lady! You seem to be lamenting over someone who died is he your son, or 
father or brother or husband."

shloka: रोदनादतिनिःश्वासाद्भूमिसंस्पर्शनादपि
translation:
"You are lamenting. You are sighing a lot. You are touching the earth. You have royal insignia 
in you. According to these things, I do not consider you as a divine woman."

shloka: व्यञ्जनानि हि ते यानि लक्षणानि च लक्षये
translation:
"Based on the marks on your person and your bodily characteristics, I believe you to be a queen 
of an emperor and the daughter of a king."

shloka: रावणेन जन स्थानात् बलात् अपहृता यदि
translation:
"If you are Seetha stolen per force by Ravana from Janasthana, tell it to me who is asking if you 
please!"

shloka: यथा हि तव वैदैन्यम् रूपम् चाप्यतिमानुषम्
translation:
"According to your miserable state, the super-human beautiful figure and your costume endowed with 
austerity, surely you are Rama's wife."

shloka: सा तस्य वचनम् श्रुत्वा राम कीर्तन हर्षिता
translation:
Hearing his words, Seetha was delighted of Rama's mention and spoke the following words to Hanuma, 
who was dwelling on a tree.

shloka: पृथिव्यां राजसिंहानां मुख्यस्य विदितात्मनः
translation:
"I am the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha, eminent among the excellent kings on earth, who understands 
the nature of the spirit and who torments the army of the adversary."

shloka: दुहिता जनकस्य अहम् वैदेहस्य महात्मनः
translation: "I am the daughter of the noble-natured Janaka, the king of Videha kingdom. I am know.

shloka: समा द्वादश तत्र अहम् राघवस्य निवेशने
translation:
"I stayed in Rama's house there for twelve years, enjoying the worldly pleasures belonging to human 
kind and fulfilling all my desires."

shloka: ततः त्रयोदशे वर्षे राज्येन इक्ष्वाकु नन्दनम्
translation:
"Thereafter, in the thirteenth year, King Dasaratha along with his preceptors started to perform 
anointment of the kingdom to Rama, a celebrity of Ikshvaku dynasty."

shloka: तस्मिन् सम्भ्रियमाणे तु राघवस्य अभिषेचने
translation:
"While that anointment of Rama was being arranged, a queen called Kaikeyi spoke the following words 
to Dasaratha, her husband.

shloka: न पिबेयम् न खादेयम् प्रत्यहम् मम भोजनम्
translation:
"If Rama gets anointed for the kingdom, from now onwards, I shall neither drink water nor take 
my food daily. This is the end to my life."

shloka: यत् तत् उक्तम् त्वया वाक्यम् प्रीत्या नृपति सत्तम
translation:
"O the excellent king! If that word of pledge was uttered affectionately by you and if it is not 
going to be a waste, let Rama go to the forest."

shloka: स राजा सत्य वाग् देव्या वर दानम् अनुस्मरन्
translation:
"Hearing the cruel and the disagreeable words of Kaikeyi and recollecting the boon given to the 
queen, King Dasaratha who was true to his word, fell unconscious.

shloka: ततः तु स्थविरो राजा सत्य धर्मे व्यवस्थितः
translation:
"Then, the aged king, who was firmly established in truth and righteousness, regretfully asked 
his illustrious eldest son to give back the kingdom, which he bestowed him earlier."

shloka: स पितुः वचनम् श्रीमान् अभिषेकात् परम् प्रियम्
translation:
"That glorious Rama first admitted his father's words in mind, considering them more dearer than 
his anointment to the kingdom and accepted them with his word."

shloka: दद्यान् न प्रतिगृह्णीयान् न ब्रूयत् किंचित् अप्रियम्
translation:
"The truly courageous Rama always gives anything to others and does not take anything from others. 
He does not speak just a little of a disagreeable word even for the cause of his life."

shloka: स विहाय उत्तरीयाणि महाअर्हाणि महायशाः
translation:
"Leaving behind his greatly valuable outer garments and wearing garments made of bark, that highly 
illustrious Rama gave up his kingdom willingly and assigned me to his mother."

shloka: सा अहम् तस्य अग्रतः तूर्णम् प्रस्थिता वन चारिणी
translation:
"To me bereft of him, residing even in heaven does not indeed give pleasure. I, as such, decided 
to proceed to the forest and soon was ready to start even ahead of Rama."

shloka: प्राग् एव तु महाभागः सौमित्रिः मित्र नन्दनः
translation:
"Adorned with clothes of bark, the illustrious Lakshmana, the rejoice of his friends, got ready 
to follow his elder brother even before (me)."

shloka: ते वयम् भर्तुः आदेशम् बहु मान्य दृढ व्रताः
translation:
"Obeying respectfully the command of Lord Dasaratha, we as such with a firm resolution, entered 
the forest, which we have never seen before and which was deep and profound in appearance."

shloka: वसतो दण्डक अरण्ये तस्य अहम् अमित ओजसः
translation:
While Rama of great vigour was dwelling in the forest of Dandaka, the evil-minded demon, Ravana 
took me, Rama's wife, away."

shloka: द्वौ मासौ तेन मे कालो जीवित अनुग्रहः कृतः
translation:
"A period of two months of survival-benefit has been given to me by him. For that reason, after 
the said two months, I shall give up my life."

shloka:
तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा हनूमान् हरि यूथपः |
दुह्खात् दुह्ख अभिभूतायाः सान्तम् उत्तरम् 
अब्रवीत्
translation:
Hearing those words of Seetha who was overthrown from one grief to another, Hanuma the best of 
monkeys gave the following reply in a kindly and affectionate manner.

shloka:
अहम् रामस्य संदेशात् देवि दूतः तव आगतः |
वैदेहि कुशली रामः त्वाम् च कौशलम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"O Seetha the daughter of the king of Videha Kingdom! I have come here as your messenger on Rama's 
directions. The virtuous Rama enquired about your welfare too."

shloka:
यो ब्राह्मम् अस्त्रम् वेदान् च वेद वेदविदाम् वरः |
स त्वाम् दाशरथी रामो देवि कौशलम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"O Divine Lady! Rama the son of Dasaratha, who is excellent among the knowers of Veda and who knows 
Brahma's missile (a mythical weapon which deals infallible destruction) and Vedas the sacred knowledge, enquired 
about your welfare."

shloka:
लक्ष्मणः च महातेजा भर्तुः ते अनुचरः प्रियः |
कृतवान् शोक सम्तप्तः शिरसा ते अभिवादनम्
translation:
"Also the greatly splendourous Lakshmana, the favourite brother and the follower of your husband, 
himself tormented with grief, performed salutation to you by bowing his head."

shloka:
सा तयोः कुशलम् देवी निशम्य नर सिम्हयोः |
प्रीति सम्हृष्ट सर्व अन्गी हनूमान्तम् अथ अब्रवीत्
translation:
Hearing that news of welfare of Rama and Lakshmana the excellent of men, the divine lady, with 
all her limbs thrilled with joy, spoke to Hanuma (as follows):

shloka:
कल्याणी बत गथा इयम् लौकिकी प्रतिभाति मे |
एहि जीवन्तम् आनदो नरम् वर्ष शतात् अपि
translation:
" 'Joy rushes to surviving man even though (it be) as the end of a hundred years' - this popular 
adage appears true and and auspicious for me."

shloka:
तयोः समागमे तस्मिन् प्रीतिः उत्पादिता अद्भुता |
परस्परेण च आलापम् विश्वस्तौ तौ प्रचक्रतुः
translation:
Seetha showed wonderful friendly disposition towards Hanuma who approached her. Both of them also 
conversed with each other in full confidence.

shloka:
तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा हनूमान् हरि यूथपः |
सीतायाः शोक दीनायाः समीपम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
Hearing that reply of Seetha who was afflicted with grief, Hanuma the army-chief of monkeys endeavoured 
to draw nearer to her.

shloka:
यथा यथा समीपम् स हनूमान् उपसर्पति |
तथा तथा रावणम् सा तम् सीता परिशन्कते
translation: In as much as that Hanuma drew nearer to her, in the same way, that Seetha suspected him as Ravana.

shloka:
अहो धिग् धिग् कृतम् इदम् कथितम् हि यत् अस्य मे |
रूप अन्तरम् उपागम्य स एव अयम् हि रावणः
translation:
"O shame! It was my guilt to tell him all this to him. He is indeed that Ravana, who obtained another 
guise."

shloka:
ताम् अशोकस्य शाखाम् सा विमुक्त्वा शोक कर्शिता |
तस्याम् एव अनवद्य अन्गी धरण्याम् समुपाविशत्
translation:
That Seetha, having faultless limbs, leaving that branch of Ashoka tree and as emaciated with grief, 
sat down on that ground itself.

shloka:
हनुमानपि दुःखार्तां तां दृष्ट्वा भयमोहिताम् |
अवन्दत महाबाहुः ततः ताम् जनक आत्मजाम्
translation:
Seeing Seetha afflicted with grief and deluded with fear, the great armed Hanuma also then simply 
saluted her. She too, trembling with fear, did not look towards him again.

shloka: तम् दृष्ट्वा वन्दमानम् तु सीता शशि निभ आनना
translation:
Seetha, with her countenance resembling the moon, seeing Hanuma saluting her, had a deep sigh and 
spoke to Hanuma in a sweet-sounding voice (as follows)

shloka: मायाम् प्रविष्टो मायावी यदि त्वम् रावणः स्वयम्
translation:
"If you are Ravana, who made use of an illusive guise and yourself a conjurer, you are causing 
me a further agony. It is no good."

shloka: स्वम् परित्यज्य रूपम् यः परिव्राजक रूपधृत्
translation:
'You are indeed the same Ravana, who, abandoning your real form, appeared to me in the guise of 
a vagrant religious mendicant in Janasthana."

shloka: उपवास कृशाम् दीनाम् काम रूप निशा चर
translation:
"O demon who can assume any form at your will! It is no good that again you are causing agony to 
me, emaciated because of fasting and feeling very miserable."

shloka: अथवा नैतदेवं हि यन्मया परिशङ्कितम्
translation:
