"Otherwise, whatever is suspected by me is not indeed true because in my mind, a pleasurable sensation 
indeed occurred by reason of your audience."

shloka: यदि रामस्य दूतः त्वम् आगतो भद्रम् अस्तु ते
translation:
"If you have come as Rama's messenger, may you be blessed! O the best of monkeys! Rama's anecdote 
is very pleasurable for me. Hence, I am requesting you to narrate it."

shloka: गुणान् रामस्य कथय प्रियस्य मम वानर
translation:
"O monkey! Narrate the qualities of my beloved Rama. O gentle one! You are eroding my mind as a 
rapid course of stream erodes a river bank."

shloka: अहो स्वप्नस्य सुखता या अहम् एवम् चिर आहृता
translation:
"I, who was taken away long ago, is seeing a monkey sent by Rama in this way. Alas! How delightful 
this dream is!'

shloka: स्वप्नेऽपि यद्यहम् वीरं राघवम् सहलक्ष्मणम्
translation:
"If I have seen the eminent Rama together with Lakshmana, I would not have disheartened. In my 
case, even my dream is wicked!"

shloka: न अहम् स्वप्नम् इमम् मन्ये स्वप्ने दृष्ट्वा हि वानरम्
translation:
"I do not deem it as a dream. Seeing a monkey in a dream does not bring about prosperity But prosperity 
has come to me!"

shloka: किम् नु स्याच् चित्त मोहो अयम् भवेत् वात गतिः तु इयम्
translation:
"How possibly is it a delusion of my mind? Is it an impending course of flatulence or changing 
mental condition of madness? Is it a looming mirage?"

shloka: अथवा न अयम् उन्मादो मोहो अपि उन्माद लक्ष्मणः
translation:
"Otherwise, it is neither madness nor even a delusion, which is a symptom of madness. Because I 
am knowing about myself as also about this monkey."

shloka: इति एवम् बहुधा सीता सम्प्रधार्य बल अबलम्
translation:
Thus deliberating upon the strengths and weaknesses in several ways, Seetha finally imagined him 
to be Ravana, as demons can change their forms at will.

shloka: एताम् बुद्धिम् तदा कृत्वा सीता सा तनु मध्यमा
translation:
Then, that slender waisted Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, thus having made up her mind, did not 
reply in return anything further to Hanuman.

shloka: सीतायाः चिन्तितम् बुद्ध्वा हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः
translation:
Understanding the contemplation of Seetha, Hanuma the son of wind-god then brought about a great 
joy in her with his words most favourable to her ears (as follows):

shloka: आदित्य इव तेजस्वी लोक कान्तः शशी यथा
translation:
"Rama has a great splendour like that of the sun. He is pleasing to all like the moon. As Kubera 
the Lord of wealth, he is a lord to the entire world. Like Vishnu, he is greatly renowned and endowed with valour."

shloka:
सत्य वादी मधुर वाग् देवो वाचस्पतिः यथा |
रूपवान् सुभगः श्रीमान् कन्दर्प इव मूर्तिमान्
translation:
"Rama is a speaker of truth. Like Lord Brihaspati, he has a sweet voice. He is a handsome man, 
possessing good fortune and a royal dignity. He is a personified Manmadha, the lord of love."

shloka:
स्थान क्रोध प्रहर्ता च श्रेष्ठो लोके महारथः |
बाहुच् चायाम् अवष्टब्धो यस्य लोको महात्मनः
translation:
"Rama gets anger only at right time. He strikes a befitting person at a right time. He is an excellent 
chariot-warrior. The world is resting under the shelter of arms of this high souled man."

shloka:
अपकृश्ष्य आश्रम पदान् मृग रूपेण राघवम् |
शून्ये येन अपनीता असि तस्य द्रक्ष्यसि यत् फलम्
translation:
"Showing an illusory antelope, Ravana detracted Rama and took you away from a deserted hermitage. 
You will see later, the consequence Ravana will get for this act."

shloka:
नचिरात् रावणम् सम्ख्ये यो वधिष्यति वीर्यवान् |
रोष प्रमुक्तैः इषुभिः ज्वलद्भिः इव पावकैः
translation:
"Which valiant Rama with arrows strongly shining like sparkles released with anger, by the same 
Rama I was sent here as a messenger and I arrived at your presence. That Rama, agonised by your separation wishes 
to enquire of your welfare."

shloka:
लक्ष्मणः च महातेजाः सुमित्र आनन्द वर्धनः |
अभिवाद्य महाबाहुः सो अपि कौशलम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"That long-armed Lakshmana too, having a great splendour and who augments the happiness of Sumitra 
his mother, saluted you and enquired about your welfare."

shloka:
रामस्य च सखा देवि सुग्रीवो नाम वानरः |
राजा वानर मुख्यानाम् स त्वाम् कौशलम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"O princess! That monkey called Sugreeva, a companion of Rama and the king of the excellent monkeys, 
asked about your welfare."

shloka:
नित्यम् स्मरति रामः त्वाम् ससुग्रीवः सलक्ष्मणः |
दिष्ट्या जीवसि वैदेहि राक्षसी वशम् आगता
translation:
"Rama, together with Sugreeva and Lakshmana, is always recollecting you. O Seetha! Eventhough coming 
into the control female-demons, you are somehow surviving by your good luck!"

shloka:
नचिरात् द्रक्ष्यसे रामम् लक्ष्मणम् च महारथम् |
मध्ये वानर कोटीनाम् सुग्रीवम् च अमित ओजसम्
translation:
"Within a few days, you will see Rama, the mighty Lakshmana and the highly splendorous Sugreeva, 
in the presence of crores of monkeys."

shloka:
अहम् सुग्रीव सचिवो हनूमान् नाम वानरः |
प्रविष्टो नगरीम् लन्काम् लन्घयित्वा महाउदधिम्
translation:
"I am a monkey, the minister of Sugreeva, called Hanuma. I entered the city of Lanka, by traversing 
the great ocean."

shloka:
कृत्वा मूर्ध्नि पद न्यासम् रावणस्य दुरात्मनः |
त्वाम् द्रष्टुम् उपयातो अहम् समाश्रित्य 
पराक्रमम्
translation:
"Asserting my strength and putting down my feet on the head of the evil minded Ravana, I have come 
to see you."

shloka:
न अहम् अस्मि तथा देवि यथा माम् अवगच्छसि |
विशन्का त्यज्यताम् एषा श्रद्धत्स्व वदतो मम
translation:
"O Princess! I am not so, as you comprehend me (as Ravana). Let your suspicion be given up. Believe 
me as I say it."

shloka:
ताम् तु राम कथाम् श्रुत्वा वैदेही वानर ऋषभात् |
उवाच वचनम् सान्त्वम् इदम् मधुरया गिरा
translation:
Hearing that narration about Rama from Hanuma the excellent of monkeys, Seetha in a sweet voice 
spoke the following gentle words:

shloka:
क्व ते रामेण संसर्गः कथम् जानासि लक्ष्मणम् |
वानराणाम् नराणाम् च कथम् आसीत् समागमः
translation:
"Where was your contact with Rama? How do you know Lakshmana? How did the union between monkeys 
and men arise?"

shloka:
यानि रामस्य लिन्गानि लक्ष्मणस्य च वानर |
तानि भूयः समाचक्ष्व न माम् शोकः समाविशेत्
translation:
"O Hanuma! What are the characteristics of Rama and Lakshmana? Narrate them to me, so that sorrow 
will not take possession of me again."

shloka:
कीदृशम् तस्य संस्थानम् रूपम् रामस्य कीदृशम् |
कथम् ऊरू कथम् बाहू लक्ष्मणस्य च शंस मे
translation:
"Of what kind was the appearance of that Rama and of Lakshmana? Of what kind was their form? How 
were the thighs? How were the arms? Tell me."

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु वैदेह्या हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः |
ततो रामम् यथा तत्त्वम् आख्यातुम् उपचक्रमे
translation:
Hearing the words of Seetha, Hanuma, the son of wind-god, then started to describe Rama according 
to his actual state (as follows):

shloka:
जानन्ती बत दिष्ट्या माम् वैदेहि परिपृच्छसि |
भर्तुः कमल पत्र अक्षि सम्ख्यानम् लक्ष्मणस्य 
च
translation:
"O Seetha having eyes resembling lotus leaves! By my fortune, you are enquiring about the appearance 
of Rama your husband and Lakshmana, eventhough you know about them. Alas! what a pleasure!"

shloka:
यानि रामस्य चिह्नानि लक्ष्मणस्य च यानि वै |
लक्षितानि विशाल अक्षि वदतः शृणु तानि मे
translation:
"O the large eyed Seetha! I tell the characteristics of Rama and Lakshmana as I recognized them; 
hear them from me."

shloka:
रामः कमल पत्र अक्षः सर्व भूत मनो हरः |
रूप दाक्षिण्य सम्पन्नः प्रसूतो जनक आत्मजे
translation:
"O Seetha the daughter of Janaka! Rama has his eyes resembling the petals of a lotus. He has a 
handsomeness, attracting the hearts of all living beings. He is endowed with grace and dexterity, by birth."

shloka:
तेजसा आदित्य सम्काशः क्षमया पृथिवी समः |
बृहस्पति समो बुद्ध्या यशसा वासव उपमः
translation:
"He is equal to the sun in splendour, earth in endurance, Brihaspati in intelligence and Indra 
in fame."

shloka:
रक्षिता जीव लोकस्य स्व जनस्य च रक्षिता |
रक्षिता स्वस्य वृत्तस्य धर्मस्य च परम् तपः
translation:
"Rama the tormentator of his adversaries, is a protector of the world of beings, further protecting 
his own people. He is the protector of his own behaviour and righteousness.

shloka:
रामो भामिनि लोकस्य चातुर्वर्ण्यस्य रक्षिता |
मर्यादानाम् च लोकस्य कर्ता कारयिता च सः
translation:
"O Seetha! Rama is the protector of the four castes of the world. He is the doer and also the agent 
for the people's propriety of conduct."

shloka:
अर्चिष्मान् अर्चितो अत्यर्थम् ब्रह्म चर्य व्रते स्थितः |
साधूनाम् उपकारज्ञः प्रचारज्ञः 
च कर्मणाम्
translation:
"Rama is a resplendent man. He is respected exceedingly. He is established in a vow of chastity. 
He knows how to do good to virtuous people. He knows the application and advantage of his actions."

shloka:
राज विद्या विनीतः च ब्राह्मणानाम् उपासिता |
श्रुतवान् शील सम्पन्नो विनीतः च परम् तपः
translation:
"He is well trained in statesmanship. He honours brahmins, the priestly class. He possesses sacred 
knowledge. He is endowed with good conduct. He is a modest man. He torments his adversaries."

shloka:
यजुः वेद विनीतः च वेदविद्भिः सुपूजितः |
धनुः वेदे च वेदे च वेद अन्गेषु च निष्ठितः
translation:
"He got trained in Yajurveda, the sacrificial Veda. He is highly honoured by those well-versed 
in Vedas. He is skilled in Dhanurveda, the science of archery, other Vedas and the six limbs* of Vedangas."

shloka:
विपुल अंसो महाबाहुः कम्बु ग्रीवः शुभ आननः |
गूढ जत्रुः सुताम्र अक्षो रामो देवि जनैः श्रुतः
translation:
"O princess! Rama is a broad shouldered and a long-armed man. He has a shell-like neck. He has 
a handsome countenance. He has a hidden collar-bone. He has beautiful red eyes. His fame is heard about by people."

shloka:
दुन्दुभि स्वन निर्घोषः स्निग्ध वर्णः प्रतापवान् |
समः सम विभक्त अन्गो वर्णम् श्यामम् समाश्रितः
translation:
"He has a voice like the sound of a kettle-drum. He has a shining skin. He is full of splendour. 
He is square-built. His limbs are built symmetrically. He is endowed with a dark-brown complexion."

shloka:
त्रिस्थिरः त्रिप्रलम्बः च त्रिसमः त्रिषु च उन्नतः |
त्रिवलीवान् त्र्यवनतः चतुः व्यन्गः 
त्रिशीर्षवान्
translation:
"He is ever firm in three limbs (viz. the breast, waist and fist), long in three (viz. the breast, 
waist and fist), long in three (viz. the eyebrows, arms and soles), uniform in three (viz. his locks, testical 
and knees, elevated in three (viz. his breast, rim of his navel and lower abdomen), coppery in three of the navel 
and the lower abdomen), coppery in three (viz. the rims of his eyes, nails, palms and soles), soft in three (viz. 
the lines on his soles, hair and the end of the membrane virile) and always deep in three (viz. the voice, gait 
and the navel)."

shloka:
त्रिवलीवांस्त्र्यवनतश्चतुर्व्यङ्गस्त्रिशीर्षवान् |
चतुष्कलश्चतुर्लेखश्चतुष्किष्कुश्चतुःसमः
translation:
"He has three folds in the skin of his neck and belly. He is depressed at three places (viz. the 
middle of his soles, the lines on his soles and the nipples). He is undersized at four places (viz. the neck, 
membran virile, the back and the shanks). He is endowed with three spirals in the hair of his head. He has four 
lines at the root of his thumb (denoting his proficiency in the four Vedas). He has four lines on his forehead 
(indicating longevity). He is four cubits high (96 inches). He has four pairs of limbs (viz. the cheeks, arms, 
shanks and knees) equally matched."

shloka:
चतुष् कलः चतुः लेखः चतुष् किष्कुः चतुः समः |
चतुर्दश सम द्वन्द्वः चतुः दष्टः चतुः गतिः
translation:
"He has fourteen other pairs of limbs (viz. the eye brows, nostrils, eyes, ears, lips, nipples, 
elbows, wrists, knees testicles, lions, hands, feet and thighs) equally matched. The four large teeth at both 
the ends of his upper and lower jaws are very sharp. He walks in four gaits (resembling the walks of a lion, a 
tiger, an elephant and a bull). He is endowed with excellent lips, chin and nose. He has five glossy limbs (viz. 
the hair, eyes, teeth, skin and soles). He has eight long limbs (viz. the arms, fingers and toes, eyes and ears, 
thighs and shanks).

shloka:
दश पद्मो दश बृहत् त्रिभिः व्याप्तो द्वि शुक्लवान् |
षड् उन्नतो नव तनुः त्रिभिः व्याप्नोति 
राघवः
translation:
"Rama has ten lotus-like limbs (viz. the countenance, the mouth, the eyes, the tongue, lips, palate, 
breasts, nails, the hands and the feet). He has ten ample limbs (viz. the chest, the head, the forehead, the neck, 
the arms, the heart, the mouth the feet, the back and the ears). He is spread through by reason of three (viz. 
splendour, renown and glory). He is doubly pure (on father's and mother's side). He is elevated in six limbs (viz. 
the flanks, the abdomen, the breast, the nose, the shoulders and the forehead). He is small, thin, fine or sharp 
in nine (viz. the hair, the moustaches and the beard, nails the hair on the body, the skin, the finger-joints, 
the membrum virile, acumen and perception). He pursues religious merit, worldly riches and the sensuous delight 
in three periods (viz. the forenoon, midday and afternoon).

shloka:
सत्य धर्म परः श्रीमान् सम्ग्रह अनुग्रहे रतः |
देश काल विभागज्ञः सर्व लोक प्रियम् वदः
translation:
"Rama is engrossed in truth and righteousness. He is a prosperous man. He is interested in reception 
and facilitation. He knows how to apportion place and time. He speaks affectionately with all."

shloka:
भ्राता च तस्य द्वैमात्रः सौमित्रिः अपराजितः |
अनुरागेन रूपेण गुणैः चैव तथा विधः
translation:
"The invincible Lakshmana, the son of Rama's step-mother and Rama's brother, is resembling Rama 
in appearance, affection and in qualities."

shloka:
तावुभौ नरशार्डूलौ त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकौ |
विचिन्वनौ महीम् कृत्स्नामस्माभिरभिसम्गातौ
translation:
"Rama and Lakshmana, the two tigers among men, very anxiously desirous of seeing you and searching 
all over the earth, came in contact with us."

shloka:
त्वाम् एव मार्गमाणो तौ विचरन्तौ वसुम् धराम् |
ददर्शतुः मृग पतिम् पूर्वजेन अवरोपितम्
translation:
"Those two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, wandering only in search of you all over the earth, saw 
Sugreeva the Lord of monkeys, sitting on the top of Rishyamuka mountain, filled with several trees, having been 
dethroned by his elder brother, oppressed with fear, but who was pleasant to the sight."

shloka:
वयम् तु हरि राजम् तम् सुग्रीवम् सत्य सम्गरम् |
परिचर्यामहे राज्यात् पूर्वजेन अवरोपितम्
translation:
"We for one are serving that Sugreeva, the Lord of monkeys, who was true to his promise, but was 
dethroned from the kingdom from his elder brother."

shloka:
ततः तौ चीर वसनौ धनुः प्रवर पाणिनौ |
ऋश्यमूकस्य शैलस्य रम्यम् देशम् उपागतौ
translation:
"In the meanwhile, those two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, wearing clothes made of bark and arming 
the best bows, came to the charming place of Rishyamuka mountain."

shloka:
स तौ दृष्ट्वा नर व्याघ्रौ धन्विनौ वानर ऋषभः |
अभिप्लुतो गिरेः तस्य शिखरम् भय मोहितः
translation:
"Seeing Rama and Lakshmana, the excellent of men, coming with bows in hand, that Sugreeva the best 
of monkeys was deluded with fear and jumped over to the hill-top of that mountain."

shloka:
ततः स शिखरे तस्मिन् वानर इन्द्रो व्यवस्थितः |
तयोः समीपम् माम् एव प्रेषयामास सत्वरः
translation:
"Thereafter, stationed on that hill-top, that Sugreeva the lord of monkeys, very soon sent me only, 
to approach those two brothers."

shloka:
ताव् अहम् पुरुष व्याघ्रौ सुग्रीव वचनात् प्रभू |
रूप लक्षण सम्पन्नौ कृत अञ्जलिः उपस्थितः
translation:
"On that command of Sugreeva, I reached saluting those two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana the excellent 
and capable men, endowed with good form and characteristics."

shloka:
तौ परिज्ञात तत्त्व अर्थौ मया प्रीति समन्वितौ |
पृष्ठम् आरोप्य तम् देशम् प्रापितौ पुरुष 
ऋषभौ
translation:
"Those two brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, the excellent among men, were fully endowed with kindness, 
after knowing the exact position about Sugreeva. Then, I made Rama and Lakshmana to ascend on my back and took 
them to Sugreeva's place."

shloka:
निवेदितौ च तत्त्वेन सुग्रीवाय महात्मने |
तयोः अन्योन्य सम्भाषात् भृशम् प्रीतिः अजायत
translation:
"I informed the high-souled Sugreeva about the true position of Rama and Lakshmana. After a mutual 
conversation between those two brothers and Sugreeva, a great friendship developed among them."

shloka:
ततस्तौ प्रीतिसंपन्नौ हरि ईश्वर नर ईश्वरौ |
परस्पर कृत आश्वासौ कथया पूर्व वृत्तया
translation:
"Thus endowed with friendship, Sugreeva the lord of monkeys and Rama the best of men, by talking 
together of their earlier occurrences, developed mutual confidence."

shloka:
तम् ततः सान्त्वयामास सुग्रीवम् लक्ष्मण आग्रजः |
स्त्री हेतोः वालिना भ्रात्रा निरस्तम् उरु 
तेजसा
translation:
"Thereafter, that Rama the elder brother of Lakshmana, through the extremely effulgent Vali the 
brother of Sugreeva, consoled Sugreeva who was earlier expelled from the kingdom; (by Vali), for the sake of Ruma 
a woman."

shloka:
ततः त्वन् नाशजम् शोकम् रामस्य अक्लिष्ट कर्मणः |
लक्ष्मणो वानर इन्द्राय सुग्रीवाय न्यवेदयत्
translation:
"Then, Lakshmana informed Sugreeva the king of monkeys about the sadness of Rama, (who is unwearied 
in action), born out of your disappearance."

shloka:
स श्रुत्वा वानर इन्द्रः तु लक्ष्मणेन ईरितम् वचः |
तदा आसीन् निष्प्रभो अत्यर्थम् ग्रह ग्रस्त 
इव अंशुमान्
translation:
"Hearing the words of Lakshmana, Sugreeva then became highly dim-witted, as the sun becomes dim 
when overpowered by an eclipse."

shloka:
ततः त्वत् गात्र शोभीनि रक्षसा ह्रियमाणया |
यानि आभरण जालानि पातितानि मही तले
translation:
"Thereafter, all those multitude of ornaments which adorned your body, which were being tried to 
be be snatched away by Ravana and which were dropped on to the earth, were brought by monkey-leaders joyfully 
and shown to Rama. But the monkey-leaders did not know the further course of your movement."

shloka:
तानि रामाय दत्तानि मया एव उपहृतानि च |
स्वनवन्ति अवकीर्णन्ति तस्मिन् विहत चेतसि
translation:
"I indeed brought those ornaments near to Rama and gave them to him. Then, soon after receiving 
them, Rama lost his consciousness and the resounding ornaments were scattered all over."

shloka:
तानि अन्के दर्शनीयानि कृत्वा बहु विधम् ततः |
तेन देव प्रकाशेन देवेन परिदेवितम्
translation:
"That Lord Rama looking like god, kept those beautiful ornaments of yours in his flank and lamented 
in many ways."

shloka:
पश्यतः तस्या रुदतः ताम्यतः च पुनः पुनः |
प्रादीपयन् दाशरथेः तानि शोक हुत अशनम्
translation:
"While seeing those ornaments, Rama was lamenting and getting suffocated again and again. Thus, 
those ornaments ignited the fire of Rama's grief."

shloka:
शयितम् च चिरम् तेन दुह्ख आर्तेन महात्मना |
मया अपि विविधैः वाक्यैः कृच्छ्रात् उत्थापितः 
पुनः
translation:
"That grief-stricken mighty man was thus lying on the floor for a long time. Then, with great difficulty, 
I made him to get up by telling several consoling words."

shloka:
तानि दृष्ट्वा महाअर्हाणि दर्शयित्वा मुहुः मुहुः |
राघवः सह सौमित्रिः सुग्रीवे स न्यवेदयत्
translation:
"That long-armed Rama, along with Lakshmana, after seeing those ornaments, examined them, again 
and again. He later gave them to Sugreeva."

shloka:
स तव अदर्शनात् आर्ये राघवः परितप्यते |
महता ज्वलता नित्यम् अग्निना इव अग्नि पर्वतः
translation:
"O the kind mistress! As you were being unseen, Rama was tormented forever with a great flaming 
fire of grief, like a volcano."

shloka:
त्वत् कृते तम् अनिद्रा च शोकः चिन्ता च राघवम् |
तापयन्ति महात्मानम् अग्नि अगारम् इव अग्नयः
translation:
"For your sake, insomnia, grief and worry were tormenting that great souled Rama, as flames torment 
a burning house."

shloka:
तव अदर्शन शोकेन राघवः प्रविचाल्यते |
महता भूमि कम्पेन महान् इव शिला उच्चयः
translation:
"By the grief caused by your not being seen, Rama is trembled with grief, as a high mountain is 
trembled by a great earthquake."

shloka:
कानानानि सुरम्याणि नदी प्रस्रवणानि च |
चरन् न रतिम् आप्नोति त्वम् अपश्यन् नृप आत्मजे
translation:
"O princess! In not seeing you, Rama is not obtaining delight, even while moving in quite charming 
forests, encompassing rivers and water-falls."

shloka:
स त्वाम् मनुज शार्दूलः क्षिप्रम् प्राप्स्यति राघवः |
समित्र बान्धवम् हत्वा रावणम् जनक आत्मजे
translation:
"O Seetha the daughter of Janaka! That Rama the excellent of men will receive you, soon after, 
killing Ravana along with Ravana's friends and relatives."

shloka:
सहितौ राम सुग्रीवाव् उभाव् अकुरुताम् तदा |
समयम् वालिनम् हन्तुम् तव च अन्वेषणम् तथा
translation:
"That day when Rama and Sugreeva were together, both of them made an agreement that Rama would 
annihilate Vali and Sugreeva would arrange for a search of you."

shloka:
ततस्ताभ्याम् कुमाराभ्याम् वीराभ्याम् स हरीश्वरः |
किष्किन्धाम् समूपागम्य वाली युद्धे निपातितः
translation:
"Thereafter, Rama and Lakshmana the two valiant princes reached Kishkindha. Rama killed Vali the 
king of monkeys there in a combat."

shloka:
ततो निहत्य तरसा रामो वालिनम् आहवे |
सर्व ऋष्क हरि सम्घानाम् सुग्रीवम् अकरोत् पतिम्
translation:
"After killing Vali in combat by means of his strength, Rama made Sugreeva the king for the entire 
multitude of bears and monkeys."

shloka:
राम सुग्रीवयोः ऐक्यम् देवि एवम् समजायत |
हनूमन्तम् च माम् विद्धि तयोः दूतम् इह आगतम्
translation:
"O princess! A friendship was held well in such a manner between Rama and Sugreeva. Know me as 
Hanuma, who came here as a messenger on behalf of both of them."

shloka:
स्व राज्यम् प्राप्य सुग्रीवः समनीय महाहरीन् |
त्वत् अर्थम् प्रेषयामास दिशो दश महाबलान्
translation:
"Having got his own kingdom, Sugreeva summoned for mighty as well as capable monkeys and sent them 
to ten different directions in search of you."

shloka:
आदिष्टा वानर इन्द्रेण सुग्रीवेण महाओजसः |
अद्रि राज प्रतीकाशाः सर्वतः प्रस्थिता महीम्
translation:
"As commanded by Sugreeva of a great splendour and the king of monkeys, those monkeys resembling 
Himalayan mountains, started out on all directions of the earth."

shloka:
ततस्ते मार्गमाणा वै सुग्रीववचनातुराः |
चरन्ति वसुधाम् कृत्स्नाम् वयमन्ये च वानराः
translation:
"Then, we along with other monkeys too who are eager to fulfill the command of Sugreeva, are wandering 
the entire earth in search of you."

shloka:
अन्गदो नाम लक्ष्मीवान् वालि सूनुः महाबलः |
प्रस्थितः कपि शार्दूलः त्रिभाग बल सम्वृतः
translation:
"An excellent monkey named Angada, possessed of fortune, son of Vali and having great strength, 
taking one third of army along with him, set out in search of you."

shloka:
तेषाम् नो विप्रनष्टानाम् विन्ध्ये पर्वत सत्तमे |
भृशम् शोक परीतनाम् अहो रात्र गणा गताः
translation:
"A number of days and nights passed, filled as we were with grief, having got lost our way intensely 
in a mountain-range called Vindhya."

shloka:
ते वयम् कार्य नैराश्यात् कालस्य अतिक्रमेण च |
भयाच् च कपि राजस्य प्राणान् त्यक्तुम् व्यवस्थिताः
translation:
"We were determined to forsake our lives because of despair in our non-fulfillment of work, in 
our overstepping of time-limit given by Sugreeva and in fear of the King Sugreeva."

shloka:
विचित्य वन दुर्गाणि गिरि प्रस्रवणानि च |
अनासाद्य पदम् देव्याः प्राणान् त्यक्तुम् व्यवस्थिताः
translation:
"Having searched in places difficult of access in forests, at mountains and at cascades and not 
obtaining any indication of you the princess, we were ready to give up our lives."

shloka:
दृष्ट्वा प्रायोपविष्टांश्च सर्वान्वानरपुङ्गवान् |
भृशम् शोक अर्णवे मग्नः पर्यदेवयत् अन्गदः
translation:
"O Seetha! Seeing all the excellent monkeys sitting down and calmly awaiting for the approach of 
death, Angada was very much immerssed in the ocean of sorrow and lamented about your loss, the killing of Vali, 
the death of Jatayu and our practice of calmly awaiting for the approach of death in simply sitting down."

shloka:
तेषाम् नः स्वामि संदेशान् निराशानाम् मुमूर्षताम् |
कार्य हेतोः इव आयातः शकुनिः वीर्यवान् 
महान्
translation:
"For us who lost all our hopes on our lives and willing to give up our lives as per the command 
of Sugreeva, as though for the sake of our need alone, a great valiant bird came there."

shloka:
गृध्र राजस्य सोदर्यः सम्पातिः नाम गृध्र राट् |
श्रुत्वा भ्रातृ वधम् कोपात् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"Hearing about the killing of his brother, the vulture-king Sampati the brother of slain Jatayu 
the King of vultures spoke (the following) words in anger:

shloka:
यवीयान् केन मे भ्राता हतः क्व च विनाशितः |
एतत् आख्यातुम् इच्छामि भवद्भिः वानर उत्तमाः
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! Tell me who, where and how my younger brother Jabali was killed and made 
to fall."

shloka:
अन्गदो अकथयत् तस्य जन स्थाने महत् वधम् |
रक्षसा भीम रूपेण त्वाम् उद्दिश्य यथा तथम्
translation:
"Then, Angada told Sampati a detailed account of events which led tot he killing of that great 
bird at Janasthana, by a demon of terrific form, for your sake."

shloka:
जटायोः तु वधम् श्रुत्वा दुह्हितः सो अरुण आत्मजः |
त्वाम् आह स वर आरोहे वसन्तीम् रावण आलये
translation:
"O Seetha with an excellent waist! Hearing about the slaughter of Jatayu, that Sampati the son 
of Aruna was very much pained and said that you were staying in Ravana's house."

shloka:
तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा सम्पातेः प्रीति वर्धनम् |
अन्गद प्रमुखाः सर्वे ततः सम्प्रस्थिता 
वयम्
translation: "Hearing those delightful words of Sampati, we with our Chief Angada started soon from there."

shloka:
विन्ध्यादुत्थाय सम्प्राप्ताः सागरस्यान्तमुत्तरम् |
त्वत् दर्शन कृत उत्साहा हृष्टाः तुष्टाः 
प्लवम्गमाः
translation:
"The monkeys were very much delighted and satisfied. They were making up their energy to see you, 
rose up from Vindhya mountain and reached the northern shore of the ocean."

shloka:
अङ्गदप्रमुखाः सर्वे वेलोपान्तमुपस्थिताः |
चिन्ताम् जग्मुः पुनर्भीतास्त्वद्दर्शनसमुत्सुकाः
translation:
"All the monkeys with their Chief Angada, in their anxiety to see you, reached the ocean. They 
were frightened after seeing the ocean there and they were again worried."

shloka:
अथ अहम् हरि सैन्यस्य सागरम् दृश्य सीदतः |
व्यवधूय भयम् तीव्रम् योजनानाम् शतम् प्लुतः
translation:
"Thereafter, seeing the ocean, I removed the serious fears of the army of monkeys who were worrying 
and crossed hundred Yojanas across the sea."

shloka:
लन्का च अपि मया रात्रौ प्रविष्टा राक्षस आकुला |
रावणः च मया दृष्टः त्वम् च शोक निपीडिता
translation:
"Entering even Lanka, filled with demons in the night, I saw Ravana and you too who were immersed 
in grief."

shloka:
एतत् ते सर्वम् आख्यातम् यथा वृत्तम् अनिन्दिते |
अभिभाषस्व माम् देवि दूतो दाशरथेः अहम्
translation:
"O the faultless princess! I told you all this as actually occurred. I am the messenger of Rama. 
Talk to me."

shloka:
त्वम् माम् राम कृत उद्योगम् त्वन् निमित्तम् इह आगतम् |
सुग्रीव सचिवम् देवि बुध्यस्व पवन 
आत्मजम्
translation:
"O princess! I made an effort on Rama's behalf and came here for your sake. I am Sugreeva's minister. 
I am the son of wind-god. Know me, as such."

shloka:
कुशली तव काकुत्स्थः सर्व शस्त्रभृताम् वरः |
गुरोः आराधने युक्तो लक्ष्मणः च सुलक्षणः
translation:
"You Rama, the excellent man among all the wielders of bow, is safe. Lakshmana, who is engaged 
in the service of his elder brother and possessing good characteristics, is also safe."

shloka:
तस्य वीर्यवतो देवि भर्तुः तव हिते रतः |
अहम् एकः तु सम्प्राप्तः सुग्रीव वचनात् इह
translation:
"O princess! I, who am interested in the welfare of the valiant Rama, your husband, came here alone 
on the command of Sugreeva."

shloka:
मया इयम् असहायेन चरता काम रूपिणा |
दक्षिणा दिग् अनुक्रान्ता त्वन् मार्ग विचय एषिणा
translation:
"I, who can change my form at will, desirous of finding out your access, wandering alone without 
any helper, came to this southern direction."

shloka:
दिष्ट्या अहम् हरि सैन्यानाम् त्वन् नाशम् अनुशोचताम् |
अपनेष्यामि सम्तापम् तव अभिगम शंसनात्
translation:
"I shall remove the anguish of the army of monkeys who are lamenting because of your disappearance 
by informing them about my coming close to you because of my good fortune!"

shloka:
दिष्ट्या हि न मम व्यर्थम् देवि सागर लन्घनम् |
प्राप्स्यामि अहम् इदम् दिष्ट्या त्वत् दर्शन 
कृतम् यशः
translation:
"O princess! By my fortune, my crossing of ocean has not gone in vain. I can get this fame of having 
seen you because of my good luck."

shloka:
राघवः च महावीर्यः क्षिप्रम् त्वाम् अभिपत्स्यते |
समित्र बान्धवम् हत्वा रावणम् राक्षस अधिपम्
translation:
"The highly valiant Rama, by killing Ravana the Lord of demons along with his friends and relatives, 
will obtain you soon."

shloka:
कौरजो नाम वैदेहि गिरीणाम् उत्तमो गिरिः |
ततो गच्छति गो कर्णम् पर्वतम् केसरी हरिः
translation:
"O Seetha! There is a mountain called Malyavan, which is the best among mountains. From there, 
a monkeys called Kesari went to another mountain called Gokarna."

shloka:
स च देव ऋषिभिः दृष्टः पिता मम महाकपिः |
तीर्थे नदी पतेः पुण्ये शम्ब सादनम् उद्धरत्
translation:
"As prayed by gods and seers, that great monkey called Kesari, my father killed a demon named Shambasadana 
at a sacred shrine near the sea-shore."

shloka:
तस्य अहम् हरिणः क्षेत्रे जातो वातेन मैथिलि |
हनूमान् इति विख्यातो लोके स्वेन एव कर्मणा
translation:
"O Seetha! I am born in the womb of the wife of that Kesari the monkey, by the grace of the wind-god. 
By my activity alone, I am renowned as Hanuma in this world."

shloka:
विश्वासार्थम् तु वैदेहि भर्तुरुक्ता मया गुणाः |
विश्वास अर्थम् तु वैदेहि भर्तुः उक्ता मया 
गुणाः
translation:
"O Seetha! I described the qualities of Rama, your husband, to cause trust in you. O the faultless 
princess! Rama will take you from here within a short time."

shloka:
एवम् विश्वासिता सीता हेतुभिः शोक कर्शिता |
उपपन्नैः अभिज्ञानैः दूतम् तम् अवगच्छति
translation:
Thus inspired by confidence because of the above reasons, Seetha emaciated with grief, by adequate 
clues served as proof.

shloka:
अतुलम् च गता हर्षम् प्रहर्षेण तु जानकी |
नेत्राभ्याम् वक्र पक्ष्माभ्याम् मुमोच आनन्दजम् 
जलम्
translation:
Seetha obtained unequal delight. She released tears of joy from her eyes having curved eye-lashes, 
with a thrill of delight.

shloka:
चारु तच् च आननम् तस्याः ताम्र शुक्ल आयत ईक्षणम् |
अशोभत विशाल अक्ष्या राहु मुक्त इव उडु 
राट्
translation:
The countenance of that large-eyed Seetha, who is beautiful, whose eyes are red white and long 
is shining like a moon, the king of stars liberated from Rahu the demon.

shloka:
हनूमन्तम् कपिम् व्यक्तम् मन्यते न अन्यथा इति सा |
अथ उवाच हनूमान् ताम् उत्तरम् प्रिय दर्शनाम्
translation:
Seetha considered Hanuma clearly as a monkey and not otherwise. Thereafter Hanuma replied to her 
who is pleasant to the sight (as follows)

shloka:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातम् समाश्वसिहि मैथिलि |
किम् करोमि कथम् वा ते रोचते प्रतियाम्यहम्
translation:
"O Seetha! I told you indeed all this please be consoled. Tell me what I can do for you and also 
what is agreeable to you. I am going back now."

shloka:
हते असुरे सम्यति शम्ब सादने |
कपि प्रवीरेण महर्षि चोदनात् |
ततो अस्मि वायु प्रभवो हि 
मैथिलि |
प्रभावतः तत् प्रतिमः च वानरः
translation:
"O Seetha! As provoked by the sages, Kesari, the valiant monkey killed a demon called Shambasadana 
in battle. I am a monkey born through wind-god and through his influence I am equal to the wind-god in strength."

shloka:
भूय एव महातेजा हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः |
अब्रवीत् प्रश्रितम् वाक्यम् सीता प्रत्यय कारणात्
translation:
Hanuma, the highly energetic son of wind-god, with an inducement to obtain confidence 
from Seetha, again modestly spoke the following words:

shloka:
वानरो अहम् महाभागे दूतो रामस्य धीमतः |
राम नाम अन्कितम् च इदम् पश्य देवि अन्गुलीयकम्
translation:
"O illustrious lady! I am a monkey and a messenger of the wise Rama. O princess! Look 
at this ring too, marked with Rama's name."

shloka:
प्रत्ययार्थम् तवानीतम् तेन दत्तम् महात्मना |
समाश्वसिहि भद्रम् ते क्षीण दुह्ख फला हि असि
translation:
"I brought this ring given by the high souled Rama, for the purpose of gaining your confidence. 
Get consoled indeed. Happiness to you! You are now free from the object of your grief."

shloka:
गृहीत्वा प्रेक्षमाणा सा भर्तुः कर विभूषणम् |
भर्तारम् इव सम्प्राप्ता जानकी मुदिता अभवत्
translation:
"I brought this ring given by the high souled Rama, for the purpose of gaining your confidence. 
Get consoled indeed. Happiness to you! You are now free from the object of your grief."

shloka:
चारु तत् वदनम् तस्याः ताम्र शुक्ल आयत ईक्षणम् |
अशोभत विशालाक्ष्या राहु मुक्त इव उडु राट्
translation:
The countenance of that large-eyed Seetha, which appeared charming with red and white 
eyes shone like a moon the king of stars liberated by Rahu the demon. Then, that young Seetha, gladdened 
by the message of her husband, became shy and message of her husband, became shy and well-pleased. Uttering 
delightful words, she praised Hanuma the great monkey (as follows):

shloka:
विक्रान्तः त्वम् समर्थः त्वम् प्राज्ञः त्वम् वानर उत्तम |
येन इदम् राक्षस पदम् त्वया एकेन प्रधर्षितम्
translation:
"O Hanuma the best of monkeys! You have singly overpowered this place infested by demons. 
You are valiant. You are competent. You are intelligent."

shloka:
शत योजन विस्तीर्णः सागरो मकर आलयः |
विक्रम श्लाघनीयेन क्रमता गोष्पदी कृतः
translation:
"You, with an acclaimable gallantry, crossed the ocean having a width of one hundred 
Yojanas and an asylum of crocodiles, making it as a small puddle."

shloka:
न हि त्वाम् प्राकृतम् मन्ये वनरम् वनर ऋषभ |
यस्य ते न अस्ति सम्त्रासो रावणान् न अपि सम्भ्रमः
translation:
"O excellent of monkeys! For you there is no fear nor even bewilderment from Ravana. 
Hence, I do not consider you as an ordinary monkey."

shloka:
अर्हसे च कपि श्रेष्ठ मया समभिभाषितुम् |
यदि असि प्रेषितः तेन रामेण विदित आत्मना
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! If you are sent by that Rama, who knows the nature of his self, 
you are worthy of talking to me well."

shloka:
प्रेषयिष्यति दुर्धर्षो रामो न हि अपरीक्षितम् |
पराक्रमम् अविज्ञाय मत् सकाशम् विशेषतः
translation:
"The indomitable Rama must not have sent you indeed, especially to me, without knowing 
your enterprise and without testing you in advance."

shloka:
दिष्ट्या च कुशली रामो धर्म आत्मा धर्म वत्सलः |
लक्ष्मणः च महातेजाः सुमित्र आनन्द वर्धनः
translation:
"Rama the righteous man who is true to his promise and Lakshmana of great splendour who 
enriches the joy of Sumitra are fortunately safe."

shloka:
कुशली यदि काकुत्स्थः किम् नु सागर मेखलाम् |
महीम् दहति कोपेन युग अन्त अग्निः इव उत्थितः
translation:
"If Rama is safe, with his anger why is he not scorching the earth with ocean as its 
belt, like rising fire at the end of the world?"

shloka:
अथवा शक्तिमन्तौ तौ सुराणाम् अपि निग्रहे |
मम एव तु न दुह्खानाम् अस्ति मन्ये विपर्ययः
translation:
"Otherwise, Rama and Lakshmana are capable of holding down even the celestials. But I 
think there is no end indeed to my troubles."

shloka:
कच्चिच् च व्यथते रामः कच्चिन् न परिपत्यते |
उत्तराणि च कार्याणि कुरुते पुरुष उत्तमः
translation:
"Is not Rama getting perturbed? Is he not tormented with grief? Is Rama the best of men 
now doing the right acts to annihilate the enemies?"

shloka:
कच्चिन् न दीनः सम्भ्रान्तः कार्येषु च न मुह्यति |
कच्चिन् पुरुष कार्याणि कुरुते नृपतेः सुतः
translation:
"Is Rama the prince miserable and confused? Is he even mistaken in his actions? I hope 
he is doing all acts which require human effort."

shloka:
द्विविधम् त्रिविध उपायम् उपायम् अपि सेवते |
विजिगीषुः सुहृत् कच्चिन् मित्रेषु च परम् तपः
translation:
"Is Rama the annihilator of enemies as per necessity resorting to the two strategies 
viz., conciliatory and partaking approaches and even the three strategies viz., partaking, sowing dissension 
and open assault? Is he kind-hearted towards friends, with a wish to conquer the enemies?"

shloka:
कच्चिन् मित्राणि लभते मित्रैः च अपि अभिगम्यते |
कच्चित् कल्याण मित्रः च मित्रैः च अपि पुरः कृतः
translation:
"Is he getting friends? Has he been approached for friendship by others? I hope he is 
having good friends and even so honoured by them."

shloka:
कच्चित् आशास्ति देवानाम् प्रसादम् पार्थिव आत्मजः |
कच्चित् पुरुष कारम् च दैवम् च प्रतिपद्यते
translation:
"Is Rama the prince wishing the grace of the gods? Is he equally aware of the role of 
human endeavour and the role of fate?"

shloka:
कच्चिन् न विगत स्नेहो विवासान् मयि राघवः |
कच्चिन् माम् व्यसनात् अस्मान् मोक्षयिष्यति वानरः
translation:
"O Hanuma! Is Rama not losing affection in me because of my staying away from home? Will 
he release me from this evil predicament?"

shloka:
सुखानाम् उचितो नित्यम् असुखानाम् अनूचितः |
दुह्खम् उत्तरम् आसाद्य कच्चित् रामो न सीदति
translation:
"Is Rama, who is habituated always to pleasures and not habituated to pains, not sinking 
into despondency by now getting this great pain?"

shloka:
कौसल्यायाः तथा कच्चित् सुमित्रायाः तथैव च |
अभीक्ष्णम् श्रूयते कच्चित् कुशलम् भरतस्य च
translation: "Are you constantly hearing the news of safety of Kausalya, Sumitra and Bharata?"

shloka:
मन् निमित्तेन मान अर्हः कच्चित् शोकेन राघवः |
कच्चिन् न अन्य मना रामः कच्चिन् माम् तारयिष्यति
translation:
"Is Rama worthy of honour, suffering from pain just because of me? Will he liberate me 
from my sorrow, without fixing his mind on something else?"

shloka:
कच्चित् अक्षाउहिणीम् भीमाम् भरतो भ्रातृ वत्सलः |
ध्वजिनीम् मन्त्रिभिः गुप्ताम् प्रेषयिष्यति मत् कृते
translation:
"I hope Bharata, having a brotherly affection, will send for my sake, an army furnished 
with banners, guarded by the ministers, consisting of ten anikinis (21870 elephants, 21870 chariots, 
65610 horses and 109350 foot soldiers) which were terrific in appearance."

shloka:
वानर अधिपतिः श्रीमान् सुग्रीवः कच्चित् एष्यति |
मत् कृते हरिभिः वीरैः वृतो दन्त नख आयुधैः
translation:
"The glorious Sugreeva the lord of monkeys will indeed come for my sake along with his 
valiant monkeys, who have their tusks and nails as their weapons."

shloka:
कच्चिच् च लक्ष्मणः शूरः सुमित्रा आनन्द वर्धनः |
अस्त्रवित् शर जालेन राक्षसान् विधमिष्यति
translation:
"Lakshmana, the strong man, who augments the joy of Sumitra and who is an expert in weaponry, 
will indeed destroy the demons by the multitude of his arrows."

shloka:
रौद्रेण कच्चित् अस्त्रेण रामेण निहतम् रणे |
द्रक्ष्यामि अल्पेन कालेन रावणम् ससुहृज् जनम्
translation:
"Within a short time, I hope see Ravana killed along with his companions in the battle-field 
by terrific weapons burning brightly."

shloka:
कच्चिन् न तद्त् हेम समान वर्णम् |
तस्य आननम् पद्म समान गन्धि |
मया विना शुष्यति शोक दीनम् |
जल क्षये पद्मम् इव आतपेन
translation:
"That face of Rama with its golden and with the fragrance of a lotus may be looking miserable 
as bereft of me and getting dehydrated too. I hope it is not parched by the sun, like a louts."

shloka:
धर्म अपदेशात् त्यजतः च राज्याम् |
माम् च अपि अरण्यम् नयतः पदातिम् |
न आसीत् व्यथा यस्य न भीः न शोकः |
कच्चित् स धैर्यम् हृदये करोति
translation:
"Which Rama left the kingdom as an indication of his righteousness and to whom there 
was neither disturbance nor fear nor sorrow even while taking me to the forest by foot, I hope that 
the same Rama is maintaining boldness in his heart."

shloka:
न च अस्य माता न पिता न च अन्यः न |
स्नेहात् विशिष्टो अस्ति मया समो वा |
तावद्त् हि अहम् दूत जिजीविषेयम् |
यावत् प्रवृत्तिम् शृणुयाम् प्रियस्य
translation:
"To Rama, in the matter of affection, neither his mother nor his father nor any body 
else is equal to or more than me. O Hanuma the messenger! I wish to survive only as long as I hear the 
activity of my beloved."

shloka:
इति इव देवी वचनम् महाअर्थम् |
तम् वानर इन्द्रम् मधुर अर्थम् उक्त्वा |
श्रोतुम् पुनः तस्य वचो अभिरामम् |
राम अर्थ युक्तम् विरराम रामा
translation:
Uttering thus those greatly meaningful and sweetly worthwhile words, Seetha the princess 
further abstained from talking so as to hear Hanuma's delightful words describing the matters pertaining 
to Rama.

shloka:
सीताया वचनम् श्रुत्वा मारुतिः भीम विक्रमः |
शिरसि अञ्जलिम् आधाय वाक्यम् उत्तरम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
Hearing Seetha's words, Hanuma of terrific prowess, keeping his joined palms on his head, 
spoke the following words in reply.

shloka:
न त्वाम् इहस्थाम् जानीते रामः कमल लोचनः |
तेन त्वामिहस्थाम् जानीते रामः कमललोचने
translation:
"O Seetha having lotus eyes! Rama does not know that you are here. For that reason, he 
did not take you back soon, as Indra the destroyer of strong holds did not take back Sachi, his wife."

shloka:
श्रुत्वा एव तु वचो मह्यम् क्षिप्रम् एष्यति राघवः |
चमूम् प्रकर्षन् महतीम् हरि ऋष्क गण सम्कुलाम्
translation:
"Soon after hearing my words, Rama will come soon, drawing forth a large army, consisting 
of a multitude of monkeys and bears."

shloka:
विष्टम्भयित्वा बाण ओघैः अक्षोभ्यम् वरुण आलयम् |
करिष्यति पुरीम् लन्काम् काकुत्स्थः शान्त राक्षसाम्
translation:
"Rama will paralyze the imperturbable ocean with his flood of arrows and make the City 
of Lanka extinguished of demons."

shloka:
तत्र यदि अन्तरा मृत्युः यदि देवाः सह असुराः |
स्थास्यन्ति पथि रामस्य स तान् अपि वधिष्यति
translation:
"If the goddess of Death along with demons or celestials stand firmly in the way of Rama 
at that time, he will kill them also."

shloka:
तव अदर्शनजेन आर्ये शोकेन स परिप्लुतः |
न शर्म लभते रामः सिम्ह अर्दित इव द्विपः
translation:
"O noble lady! Being full of grief caused by your non-appearance, that Rama is not obtaining 
happiness, like an elephant tornmented by a lion."

shloka:
दर्दरेण च ते देवि शपे मूल फलेन च |
मलयेन च विन्ध्येन मेरुणा मन्दरेण च
translation:
"O Seetha the princess! I swear and tell you by the mountains Malaya, Vindhya, Meru and 
Dardura as well as by our staple food of roots and fruits, that you will soon see Rama's face, having 
good eyes, handsome, having lips with the colour of a bright-red gourd (fruit of Momordica monodelpha) 
and with its charming look like a rising full moon."

shloka:
क्षिप्रं द्रक्ष्यसि वैदेहि रामं प्रस्रवणे गिरौ |
शतक्रतुमिवासीनं नाकपृष्ठस्य मूर्धनि
translation:
"O Seetha! You will see soon Rama on the Prasravana mountain, like Indra the Lord of 
celestials seated on the back of Airavata, the chief of elephants."

shloka:
न मांसं राघवो भुङ्क्ते न चापि मधुसेवते |
वन्यं सुविहितं नित्यं भक्तमश्नाति पञ्चमम्
translation:
"Rama is not eating meat, nor indulging even in spirituous liquor. Everyday, in the evening, 
he is eating the food existing in the forest, well arranged for him."

shloka:
न एव दंशान् न मशकान् न कीटान् न सरी सृपान् |
राघवो अपनयेत् गत्रात् त्वत् गतेन अन्तः आत्मना
translation:
"With his mind wholly devoted to you, Rama is not even driving away forest-flies from 
his body, nor mosquitoes nor insects nor reptiles from his body."

shloka:
नित्यम् ध्यान परो रामो नित्यम् शोक परायणः |
न अन्यच् चिन्तयते किंचित् स तु काम वशम् गतः
translation:
"Rama always cogitates on something or the other. He is forever engaged in sorrow. He 
is enamoured with the god of love and thinks of nothing else."

shloka:
अनिद्रः सततम् रामः सुप्तो अपि च नर उत्तमः |
सीतेति मधुराम् वाणीम् व्याहरन् प्रतिबुध्यते
translation:
"Rama mostly does not have sleep. Even if that best of men sleeps, he keeps awake uttering 
sweet words like "lo! Behold! Seetha!"

shloka:
दृष्ट्वा फलम् वा पुष्पम् वा यच् च अन्यत् स्त्री मनो हरम् |
बहुशो हा प्रियेति एवम् श्वसन् त्वाम् अभिभाषते
translation:
"When he happens to see a fruit or a flower or any other beautiful object, he recollects 
of you and says 'O beloved!' many times and breathes a sigh."

shloka:
स देवि नित्यम् परितप्यमानः |
त्वाम् एव सीतेति अभिभाषमाणः |
धृत व्रतो राज सुतो महात्मा |
तव एव लाभाय कृत प्रयत्नः
translation:
"O Seetha the princess! Rama the magnanimous prince is always lamenting, speaking just 
about you, recollecting "Seetha, Seetha!". Being firm in his vow, he makes effort to find you only."

shloka:
सा राम सम्कीर्तन वीत शोका |
रामस्य शोकेन समान शोका |
शरन् मुखेन अम्बुद शेष |
निशा इव वैदेह सुता बभूव
translation:
"That Seetha, who has the same amount of grief as that of Rama, became worn out of her 
grief upon hearing the adoration of Rama, like a night with the moon obscured by the remnant clouds 
at the commencement of autumn."

shloka:
सा सीता तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा पूर्ण चन्द्र निभ आनना |
हनूमन्तम् उवाच इदम् धर्म अर्थ सहितम् वचः
translation:
Hearing Hanuma's words, Seetha whose face resembled the full moon, spoke the following 
words braced with justice and utility, to Hanuma.

shloka:
अमृतम् विष संसृष्टम् त्वया वानर भाषितम् |
यच् च न अन्य मना रामो यच् च शोक परायणः
translation:
"O Hanuma! The words spoken by you viz. that Rama is not having any other thoughts (than 
on me) and is fully overwhelmed by sorrow are like ambrosia mixed with poisons."

shloka:
ऐश्वर्ये वा सुविस्तीर्णे व्यसने वा सुदारुणे |
रज्ज्वा इव पुरुषम् बद्ध्वा कृत अन्तः परिकर्षति
translation:
"Destiny drags out a man into a very extensive fortune or into a very dreadful adversity, 
as if being dragged, tied with ropes."

shloka:
विधिः नूनम् असम्हार्यः प्राणिनाम् प्लवग उत्तम |
सौमित्रिम् माम् च रामम् च व्यसनैः पश्य मोहितान्
translation:
"O Hanuma the best of monkeys! For living beings, destiny is surely irresistible. See 
how Lakshmana, myself and Rama are baffled by misfortunes."

shloka:
शोकस्य अस्य कदा पारम् राघवो अधिगमिष्यति |
प्लवमानः परिश्रान्तो हत नौः सागरे यथा
translation:
"When will Rama reach the end of this grief any more than a thoroughly fatigued man, 
having suffered a ship wreck is swimming in the middle of the sea?"

shloka:
राक्षसानाम् क्षयम् कृत्वा सूदयित्वा च रावणम् |
लन्काम् उन्मूलिताम् कृत्वा कदा द्रक्ष्यति माम् पतिः
translation:
"When will my husband see me, after annihilation of the demons, killing of Ravana and 
making the City of Lanka debacled?."

shloka:
स वाच्यः सम्त्वरस्व इति यावत् एव न पूर्यते |
अयम् सम्वत्सरः कालः तावद्त् हि मम जीवितम्
translation:
"Till the current period of one year is not completed, that Rama is to be told to make 
haste to save me; since my life will be lasting till such time only."

shloka:
वर्तते दशमो मासो द्वौ तु शेषौ प्लवम्गम |
रावणेन नृशंसेन समयो यः कृतो मम
translation:
"O Hanuma! Out of the time-limit given to me by the cruel Ravana for my survival, the 
tenth month is now running. Only two months are left out."

shloka:
विभीषणेन च भ्रात्रा मम निर्यातनम् प्रति |
अनुनीतः प्रयत्नेन न च तत् कुरुते मतिम्
translation:
"Even when humbly entreated with continued exertion by Vibhishana his brother about my 
restoration (to Rama), Ravana is not making up his mind to do so."

shloka:
मम प्रतिप्रदानम् हि रावणस्य न रोचते |
रावणम् मार्गते सम्ख्ये मृत्युः काल वशम् गतम्
translation:
"My restoration is not agreeable to Ravana. In the battle, death lies in wait for Ravana, 
who has become subject to the power of Time."

shloka:
ज्येष्ठा कन्या अनला नम विभीषण सुता कपे |
तया मम एतत् आख्यातम् मात्रा प्रहितया स्वयम्
translation:
"O Hanuma! Nala, the eldest maiden daughter of Vibhishana, when she was sent personally 
to me by her mother, told me about this."

shloka:
आशंस इति हरि श्रेष्ठ क्षिप्रम् माम् प्राप्स्यते पतिः |
अन्तः आत्मा हि मे शुद्धः तस्मिन् च बहवो गुणाः
translation:
"O Hanuma the excellent of monkeys! Rama, my husband, will soon regain me without any 
doubt. Because my heart is pure and in Rama also, there are many good qualities existing."

shloka:
उत्साहः पौरुषम् सत्त्वम् आनृशंस्यम् कृतज्ञता |
विक्रमः च प्रभावः च सन्ति वानर राघवे
translation:
"O Hanuma! In Rama are figured, pesseverence, manliness, courage, non-mischievousness, 
gratitude, prowess and energy."

shloka:
चतुर्दश सहस्राणि राक्षसानाम् जघान यः |
जन स्थाने विना भ्रात्रा शत्रुः कः तस्य न उद्विजेत्
translation:
"Which Rama, who without the help of Lakshmana his brother, killed fourteen thousand 
demos in Janasthana (part of the forest), what adversary will not have fear of such a man?"

shloka:
न स शक्यः तुलयितुम् व्यसनैः पुरुष ऋषभः |
अहम् तस्य अनुभावज्ञा शक्रस्य इव पुलोमजा
translation:
"Rama, the excellent among men, is not compelled to be moved by troubles. I now well 
the energy of Rama, as Shachi the wife of Indra knows the energy of Indra the Lord of celestials."

shloka:
शर जाल अंशुमान् शूरः कपे राम दिवा करः |
शत्रु रक्षोमयम् तोयम् उपशोषम् नयिष्यति
translation:
"O Hanuma! The powerful Rama like the sun, with his multitude of ray-like arrows, will 
dry up the water in the form of hostile adversaries."

shloka:
इति सम्जल्पमानाम् ताम् राम अर्थे शोक कर्शिताम् |
अश्रु सम्पूर्ण वदनाम् उवाच हनुमान् कपिः
translation:
Hanuma spoke the following words to Seetha, who was thus talking with grief for Rama 
and with her eyes full of tears."

shloka:
श्रुत्वा एव तु वचो मह्यम् क्षिप्रम् एष्यति राघवः |
चमूम् प्रकर्षन् महतीम् हरि ऋक्ष गण सम्कुलाम्
translation:
"Soon after hearing my words, Rama will soon come, engaging a great army comprising of 
a multitude of monkeys and bears with him."

shloka:
अथवा मोचयिष्यामि ताम् अद्य एव हि राक्षसात् |
अस्मात् दुह्खात् उपारोह मम पृष्ठम् अनिन्दिते
translation:
"O Seetha with a charming face! Or rather, I shall relieve you from this grief now itself. 
O irreproachable lady! Ascend my back. I shall take you to Rama."

shloka:
त्वम् हि पृष्ठ गताम् कृत्वा सम्तरिष्यामि सागरम् |
शक्तिः अस्ति हि मे वोढुम् लन्काम् अपि सरावणाम्
translation:
"I shall cause you sit on my back and cross the ocean. I have indeed capacity to carry 
even Lanka together with Ravana."

shloka:
अहम् प्रस्रवणस्थाय राघवाय अद्य मैथिलि |
प्रापयिष्यामि शक्राय हव्यम् हुतम् इव अनलः
translation:
"O Seetha! Now itself, I shall cause you to reach Rama who is staying at Prasravana Mountain, 
even as fire-god hands over the oblations offered in the sacrifices to Indra the Lord of celestials."

shloka:
द्रक्ष्यसि अद्य एव वैदेहि राघवम् सह लक्ष्मणम् |
व्यवसाय समायुक्तम् विष्णुम् दैत्य वधे यथा
translation:
"O Seetha! Now itself, you can see Rama together with Lakshmana, getting ready for a 
strenuous effort to annihilate the demons, as Vishnu the Lord of Preservation getting ready for killing 
of demons."

shloka:
त्वत् दर्शन कृत उत्साहम् आश्रमस्थम् महाबलम् |
पुरंदरम् इव आसीनम् नाग राजस्य मूर्धनि
translation:
"The mighty Rama, with a gusto to see you, is staying in a hermitage, even as Indra the 
destroyer of strong-holds sitting on the back of Airavata the elephant."

shloka:
पृष्ठम् आरोह मे देवि मा विकान्क्षस्व शोभने |
योगम् अन्विच्छ रामेण शश अन्केन इव रोहिणी
translation:
"O Seetha the auspicious princess! Mount on my back. Do not have any hesitation. Be inclined 
of joining Rama even as Rohini, moon's favourite wife, joined the moon."

shloka:
कथयन्ति इव चन्द्रेण सूर्येण इव सुवर्चला |
मत् पृष्ठम् अधिरुह्य त्वम् तर आकाश महाअर्णवम्
translation:
"You ascend my back and cross the ocean by journeying through the sky, as though speaking 
to the greatly resplendent sun and to the moon."

shloka:
न हि मे सम्प्रयातस्य त्वाम् इतो नयतो अन्गने |
अनुगन्तुम् गतिम् शक्ताः सर्वे लन्का निवासिनः
translation:
"O Seetha! While I am taking you from here, no body staying in Lanka is competent to 
come along with me."

shloka:
यथा एव अहम् इह प्राप्तः तथैव अहम् असंशयम् |
यास्यामि पश्य वैदेहि त्वाम् उद्यम्य विहायसम्
translation:
"O Seetha! In what manner I reached here, in the same manner, I shall move through the 
sky, taking you along with me. See, there is no doubt."

shloka:
मैथिली तु हरि श्रेष्ठात् श्रुत्वा वचनम् अद्भुतम् |
हर्ष विस्मित सर्व अन्गी हनूमन्तम् अथ अब्रवीत्
translation:
Hearing those astonishing words from Hanuma, Seetha with her entire limbs flowered with 
joy, thereafter spoke to Hanuma (as follows):

shloka:
हनूमन् दूरम् अध्वनम् कथम् माम् वोढुम् इच्छसि |
तत् एव खलु ते मन्ये कपित्वम् हरि यूथप
translation:
"O Hanuma! How are you wishing to carry me for such a long distance? O chief of monkeys! 
I consider this indeed as your apishness!"

shloka:
कथम् वा अल्प शरीरः त्वम् माम् इतो नेतुम् इच्छसि |
सकाशम् मानव इन्द्रस्य भर्तुः मे प्लवग ऋषभ
translation:
"O Hanuma the best of monkeys! With such a small seized body, how do you wish to take 
me from here to the presence of my husband, Rama the Lord of human beings?"

shloka:
सीताया वचनम् श्रुत्वा हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः |
चिन्तयामास लक्ष्मीवान् नवम् परिभवम् कृतम्
translation:
Hearing the words of Seetha, the illustrious Hanuma, the son of wind-god thought it to 
be the first insult was caused to him.

shloka:
न मे जानाति सत्त्वम् वा प्रभावम् वा असित ईक्षणा |
तस्मात् पश्यतु वैदेही यत् रूपम् मम कामतः
translation:
(Hanuma said to himself); "The black-eyed Seetha is not aware of my strength or power. 
That is why, let her see the form I can assume at will."

shloka:
इति संचिन्त्य हनुमान् तदा प्लवग सत्तमः |
दर्शयामास वैदेह्याः स्वरूपम् अरि मर्दनः
translation:
Hanuma, the best of monkeys and the annihilator of enemies, thinking in this way, then 
showed his peculiarity to Seetha.

shloka:
स तस्मात् पादपात् धीमान् आप्लुत्य प्लवग ऋषभः |
ततो वर्धितुम् आरेभे सीता प्रत्यय कारणात्
translation:
Hanuma, the intelligent and the excellent of monkeys, leaped down from that tree and 
then, to create confidence in Seetha, started to increase his body-form.

shloka:
मेरु मन्दार सम्काशो बभौ दीप्त अनल प्रभः |
अग्रतो व्यवतस्थे च सीताया वानर ऋषभः
translation:
Hanuma, the foremost of monkeys, flashed like Meru and Mandara mountains, shining brightly 
like a blazing fire. He thus stood too in front of Seetha.

shloka:
हरिः पर्वत सम्काशः ताम्र वक्त्रो महाबलः |
वज्र दम्ष्ट्र नखो भीमो वैदेहीम् इदम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
The mighty Hanuma, resembling a mountain, having a red face, having teeth and nails as 
hard as adamant and terrific in appearance, spoke the following words to Seetha.

shloka:
सपर्वत वन उद्देशाम् साट्ट प्राकार तोरणाम् |
लन्काम् इमाम् सनथाम् वा नयितुम् शक्तिः अस्ति मे
translation:
"To me, there is capability to carry this Lanka along with its hills, forest-areas, market-places, 
defensive walls and arches together with its Lord Ravana himself."

shloka:
तत् अवस्थाप्य ताम् बुद्धिः अलम् देवि विकान्क्षया |
विशोकम् कुरु वैदेहि राघवम् सह लक्ष्मणम्
translation:
"O princess! For this reason, leave your suspicion and keep you mind steady. Come along 
with me and make Rama and Lakshmana bereft of grief."

shloka:
तम् दृष्ट्वा अचल सम्काशम् उवाच जनक आत्मजा |
पद्म पत्र विशाल अक्षी मारुतस्य औरसम् सुतम्
translation:
Seetha, with her large eyes resembling lotus-petals, spoke to that terrific Hanuma, the 
son of wind-god (as follows)

shloka:
तव सत्त्वम् बलम् चैव विजानामि महाकपे |
वायोः इव गतिम् च अपि तेजः च अग्निः इव अद्भुतम्
translation:
"O great monkey! I know fully well your courage, strength, your power of movement like 
that of the wind and your wonderful brilliance like that of the fire."

shloka:
प्राकृतो अन्यः कथम् च इमाम् भूमिम् आगन्तुम् अर्हति |
उदधेः अप्रमेयस्य पारम् वानर पुम्गव
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! How can any other common person cross this unfathomable ocean 
and reach this place?"

shloka:
जानामि गमने शक्तिम् नयने च अपि ते मम |
अवश्यम् साम्प्रधार्य आशु कार्य सिद्धिः इह आत्मनः
translation:
"I know your capacity of carrying and taking me from here. However, we have to determine 
soon whether the accomplishment of work by the high souled Rama would not thus get spoiled."

shloka:
अयुक्तम् तु कपि श्रेष्ठ मया गन्तुम् त्वया सह |
वायु वेग सवेगस्य वेगो माम् मोहयेत् तव
translation:
"O the faultless one! O the excellent of monkeys! It is not befitting of me to go with 
you. For, your speed resembling the winds speed, may bewilder my mind."

shloka:
अहम् आकाशम् आसक्ता उपरि उपरि सागरम् |
प्रपतेयम् हि ते पृष्ठात् भयात् वेगेन गच्छतः
translation:
"Reaching the sky high above the sea, I will fall down out of fear from your back even 
as you sweep with speed."

shloka:
पतिता सागरे च अहम् तिमि नक्र झष आकुले |
भयेयम् आशु विवशा यादसाम् अन्नम् उत्तमम्
translation:
"Having fallen insensible into the sea, which is filled with sharks, crocodiles and giant 
fish, I may become the best food soon for the aquatic creatures."

shloka:
न च शक्ष्ये त्वया सार्धम् गन्तुम् शत्रु विनाशन |
कलत्रवति संदेहः त्वयि अपि स्यात् असंशयम्
translation:
"O Hanuma the annihilator of enemies! It is not possible for me to go with you. There 
will also be a risk for you, having me a lady additionally to protect. There is no doubt."

shloka:
ह्रियमाणाम् तु माम् दृष्ट्वा राक्षसा भीम विक्रमाः |
अनुगच्छेयुः आदिष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना
translation:
"Seeing me being taken away by you, the demons of terrific prowess, incited by the evil-minded 
Ravana, will follow you."

shloka:
तैः त्वम् परिवृतः शूरैः शूलम् उद्गर पाणिभिः |
भवेः त्वम् संशयम् प्राप्तो मया वीर कलत्रवान्
translation:
"O brave monkey! Those valiant demons wielding darts and clubs in their hands will surround 
you. Accompanied by a lady in me, you will be at a risk."

shloka:
सायुधा बहवो व्योम्नि राक्षसाः त्वम् निरायुधः |
कथम् शक्ष्यसि सम्यातुम् माम् चैव परिरक्षितुम्
translation:
"Many demons will come with their weapons, in the sky. You will be alone without any 
weapon. How can you continue your travel, while protecting me?"

shloka:
युध्यमानस्य रक्षोभिः ततः तैः क्रूर कर्मभिः |
प्रपतेयम् हि ते पृष्ठत् भय आर्ता कपि सत्तम
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! While you will be resorting to battle with those demons, who 
perform cruel acts, I, stricken with fear, may fall down from your back."

shloka:
अथ रक्षांसि भीमानि महान्ति बलवन्ति च |
कथंचित् साम्पराये त्वाम् जयेयुः कपि सत्तम
translation:
"O excellent of monkeys! Then the powerful and terrific demons with their giant bodies 
will conquer you in battle, somehow or other."

shloka:
अथवा युध्यमानस्य पतेयम् विमुखस्य ते |
पतिताम् च गृहीत्वा माम् नयेयुः पाप राक्षसाः
translation:
"Otherwise, if you are indifferent of me and resort to battle, I may eventually fall 
down. Then, the wicked demons, catching hold of me fallen, may take me again to Lanka."

shloka:
माम् वा हरेयुः त्वद्त् हस्तात् विशसेयुः अथ अपि वा |
अव्यवस्थौ हि दृश्येते युद्धे जय पराजयौ
translation:
"Or they may take me away from your hand, or may even kill me. In battle, victory and 
defeat are perceived as uncertain."

shloka:
अहम् वा अपि विपद्येयम् रक्षोभिः अभितर्जिता |
त्वत् प्रयत्नो हरि श्रेष्ठ भवेन् निष्फल एव तु
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! Or while I am frightened by the demons, I may get into a mishap. 
Thus, your effort may become futile indeed!"

shloka:
कामम् त्वम् अपि पर्याप्तो निहन्तुम् सर्व राक्षसान् |
राघवस्य यशो हीयेत् त्वया शस्तैः तु राक्षसैः
translation:
"You may be surely able to kill all the demons. But if you alone kill all the demons, 
Rama's celebrity will be lowered."

shloka:
अथवा आदाय रक्षांसि न्यस्येयुः सम्वृते हि माम् |
यत्र ते न अभिजानीयुः हरयो न अपि राघवः
translation:
"Otherwise, the demons may take me away and hide me in any secret place that will not 
be known by those monkeys or even Rama and Lakshmana."

shloka:
आरम्भः तु मत् अर्थो अयम् ततः तव निरर्थकः |
त्वया हि सह रामस्य महान् आगमने गुणः
translation:
"Then your effort taken for my sake will become futile. That is why there is a great 
merit in Rama's coming here along with you."

shloka:
मयि जीवितम् आयत्तम् राघवस्य महात्मनः |
भ्रातृऋणाम् च महाबाहो तव राज कुलस्य च
translation:
"O Hanuma the long-armed! The survival of the high souled Rama, his brothers, of yourself 
and of your royal family (of Sugreeva) is dependent on me."

shloka:
तौ निराशौ मत् अर्थे तु शोक सम्ताप कर्शितौ |
सह सर्व ऋक्ष हरिभिः त्यक्ष्यतः प्राण सम्ग्रहम्
translation:
"Those two men Rama and Lakshmana who are emaciated by grief and anguish along with all 
bears and monkeys, losing their hope, will abandon their lives."

shloka:
भर्तुः भक्तिम् पुरः कृत्य रामात् अन्यस्य वानर |
न अहम् स्प्रष्टुम् पदा गात्रम् इच्छेयम् वानर उत्तम
translation:
"O Hanuma, the best of monkeys! Honouring the devotion to my husband, I cannot touch 
the body of any man other that of Rama."

shloka:
यत् अहम् गात्र संस्पर्शम् रावणस्य गता बलात् |
अनीशा किम् करिष्यामि विनाथा विवशा सती
translation:
"That I got, by force, the touch of Ravana's body, was because being helpless, having 
lost control of myself and without a protector, I could not do anything."

shloka:
यदि रामो दशग्रीवम् इह हत्वा सराक्षसम् |
माम् इतो गृह्य गच्छेत तत् तस्य सदृशम् भवेत्
translation:
"If Rama kills Ravana here along with his relatives and departs taking me from here, 
it would be proper for him"

shloka:
श्रुता हि दृष्टाः च मया पराक्रमा |
महात्मनः तस्य रण अवमर्दिनः |
न देव गन्धर्व भुजम्ग राक्षसा |
भवन्ति रामेण समा हि सम्युगे
translation:
"I have not only heard but seen myself about the strength of the high souled Rama destroying 
enemies in battle. Neither the celestials nor the divine musicians nor the serpent-gods nor the demons 
are equal to Rama in combat."

shloka:
समीक्ष्य तम् सम्यति चित्र कार्मुकम् |
महाबलम् वासव तुल्य विक्रमम् |
सलक्ष्मणम् को विषहेत राघवम् |
हुत अशनम् दीप्तम् इव अनिल ईरितम्
translation:
"Who can withstand seeing in battle that mighty Rama, dazzling like fire fanned by wind, 
wielding his conspicuous bow and having prowess equal to that of Indra the Lord of celestials, together 
with Lakshmana?"

shloka:
सलक्ष्मणम् राघवम् आजि मर्दनम् |
दिशा गजम् मत्तम् इव व्यवस्थितम् |
सहेत को वानर मुख्य सम्युगे |
युग अन्त सूर्य प्रतिमम् शर अर्चिषम्
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! In battle, who can endure Rama resembling the sun at noon-time, 
with his arrows resembling its rays, the destroyer in battle, stationed like a mythical elephant in 
rut, along with Lakshmana?

shloka:
स मे हरि श्रेष्ठ सलक्ष्मणम् पतिम् |
सयूथपम् क्षिप्रम् इह उपपादय |
चिराय रामम् प्रति शोक कर्शिताम् |
कुरुष्व माम् वानर मुख्य हर्षिताम्
translation:
"O the excellent of monkeys! You, as such, soon bring my husband here along with Lakshmana, 
and the chiefs of army. O the best of monkeys! I am emaciated with grief about Rama since long. Make 
me now joyful."

shloka:
ततः स कपि शार्दूलः तेन वाक्येन हर्षितः |
सीताम् उवाच तत् श्रुत्वा वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारदः
translation:
Hearing those words of Seetha, the eloquent Hanuma was very much pleased and spoke to 
Seetha (as follows):

shloka:
युक्त रूपम् त्वया देवि भाषितम् शुभ दर्शने |
सदृशम् स्त्री स्वभावस्य साध्वीनाम् विनयस्य च
translation:
"O Seetha, the beautiful princess! Whatever you spoke is befitting. It is in keeping 
with woman's nature and humility of a chaste women."

shloka:
स्त्रीत्वम् न तु समर्थम् हि सागरम् व्यतिवर्तितुम् |
माम् अधिष्ठाय विस्तीर्णम् शत योजनम् आयतम्
translation:
"It is indeed not fit for a woman to mount on my back and traverse an extensive ocean, 
which is having a width of one hundred yojanas."

shloka:
द्वितीयम् कारणम् यच् च ब्रवीषि विनय अन्विते |
रामात् अन्यस्य न अर्हामि संस्पर्शम् इति जानकि
translation:
"O Seetha endowed with modesty! The second reason you mentioned that you would not be 
touching any one else other then Rama is befitting of you, the wife of that high soled Rama. O princess! 
which other lady except you can speak of such sweet words?"

shloka:
श्रोष्यते चैव काकुत्स्थः सर्वम् निरवशेषतः |
चेष्टितम् यत् त्वया देवि भाषितम् मम च अग्रतः
translation:
"O princess! I can completely inform Rama of all that you have done and of all that you 
have spoken before me."

shloka:
कारणैः बहुभिः देवि राम प्रिय चिकीर्षया |
स्नेह प्रस्कन्न मनसा मया एतत् समुदीरितम्
translation:
"O princess! All this was told by me because of several reasons, being desirous of doing 
good to Rama ad with my mind moistened with affection towards him."

shloka:
लन्काया दुष्प्रवेशत्वात् दुस्तरत्वान् महाउदधेः |
सामर्थ्यात् आत्मनः चैव मया एतत् समुदाहृतम्
translation:
"I spoke this because of the unassailability of Lanka, its great ocean so difficult to 
be crossed and also my capacity of taking you."

shloka:
इच्छामि त्वाम् समानेतुम् अद्य एव रघु बन्धुना |
गुरु स्नेहेन भक्त्या च न अन्यथा तत् उदाहृतम्
translation:
"Because of my great affection and devotion towards you, I wish to carry you well now 
itself to Rama your hushand. These words were not spoken by me with any other motive."

shloka:
यदि न उत्सहसे यातुम् मया सार्धम् अनिन्दिते |
अभिज्ञानम् प्रयच्छ त्वम् जानीयात् राघवो हि यत्
translation:
"O faultless Seetha! If you are not willing to go with me, give me a token of remembrance 
which Rama can recognise."

shloka:
एवम् उक्ता हनुमता सीता सुर सुत उपमा |
उवाच वचनम् मन्दम् बाष्प प्रग्रथित अक्षरम्
translation:
Hearing Hanuma's words, Seetha like the daughter of a god, slowly spoke the following 
words, strung together with alphabets of tears: "You tell this (following) excellent thing as a token 
of remembrance to my beloved husband."

shloka: शैलस्य चित्र कूटस्य पादे पूर्व उत्तरे तदा
translation:
"There is a place inhabited by sages at a hillock in the north-eastern It was bountiful 
with roots fruits and water. In that place, while we were residing in a hermitage of sages, on a day 
long ago, we were strolling in water in parts of groves with various kinds of flowers of perfume in 
that hillock. Your thereupon became wet and sat at my proximity."

shloka:
ततो मांस समायुक्तो वायसः पर्यतुण्डयत् |
तम् अहम् लोष्टम् उद्यम्य वारयामि स्म वायसम्
translation:
"Then, a crow, yearning for meat, began to peck me. Picking up a clod of earth, I prevented 
the crow from its act."

shloka:
दारयन् स च माम् काकः तत्र एव परिलीयते |
न च अपि उपरमन् मांसात् भक्ष अर्थी बलि भोजनः
translation:
"Pecking me again and again, the crow was hiding there only. That crow, yearning for 
food, did not resig from meat."

shloka:
उत्कर्षन्त्याम् च रशनाम् क्रुद्धायाम् मयि पक्षिणे |
स्रंसमाने च वसने ततो दृष्टा त्वया हि अहम्
translation:
"While I was angry with that bird, my skirt was slipping and I was pulling its string 
(so as to tighten it). I was seen by you then."

shloka:
त्वया विहसिता च अहम् क्रुद्धा सम्लज्जिता तदा |
भक्ष्य गृद्धेन कालेन दारिता त्वाम् उपागता
translation:
"Moved by anger, I felt abashed for being laughed at by you. Torn down by the crow, which 
was yearning for food, I sought shelter with you."

shloka:
आसीनस्य च ते श्रान्ता पुनः उत्सन्गम् आविशम् |
क्रुध्यन्ती च प्रहृष्टेन त्वया अहम् परिसान्त्विता
translation:
"Feeling tired, I again settled on your lap. As though angry, I was consoled by you and 
I was fully delighted."

shloka:
बाष्प पूर्ण मुखी मन्दम् चक्षुषी परिमार्जती |
लक्षिता अहम् त्वया नाथ वायसेन प्रकोपिता
translation:
"Slowly wiping my eyes, my face filled with tears, I was seen by you, O Lord, as having 
been annoyed by the crow."

shloka:
परिश्रमात्प्रसुप्ता च राघवाङ्के ऽप्य्हम् चिरम् |
पर्याय़ेण प्रसुप्तश्च ममाङ्के भरताग्रजः ५-३८-२१
translation:
"I even slept for a long time on Rama's lap because of my fatigue. In his turn, Rama 
the elder brother of Bharata, slept in my arms."

shloka:
स तत्र पुनरे वाथ वायसः समुपागमत् |
ततः सुप्तप्रबुद्धाम् माम् रामस्याङ्कात्समुत्थिताम्
translation:
"Meanwhile, the same crow appeared there. Descending all of a sudden, the crow clawed 
me at the space between the breasts, even as I awoke from my sleep and rose from the lap of Rama. Flying 
up again, it tore me up a lot."

shloka:
ततः समुक्षितो रामो मुक्तैः शोणितबिन्दुभिः |
वयसेन ततस्तेन बलवत्क्लिश्यमानया
translation:
"Then, Rama got wet by the discharged drops of blood. Thereafter, that splendorous Rama, 
the annihilator of enemies, who was in a pleasant slumber, was woken up by that crow and by me who was 
grievously tormented by the crow."

shloka: स माम् दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुर्वितुन्नाम् स्तनयोस्तदा
translation:
"That long-armed Rama, seeing me pierced violently on the breasts, then spoke the following 
words, hissing like an angry serpant.

shloka: केन ते नाग नास ऊरु विक्षतम् वै स्तन अन्तरम्
translation:
"O Seetha the round-thighed woman! Who has wounded the space between your breasts? who 
is playing with a fire-faced serpent filled with fury?"

shloka: वीक्षमाणः ततः तम् वै वायसम् समवैक्षथाः
translation:
'Then, throwing a glance around, Rama saw that crow with its sharp claws moistened iwth 
blood and sitting in front of me alone."

shloka: पुत्रः किल स शक्रस्य वायसः पतताम् वरः
translation:
"That crow, the best among birds, seems to be the son of Indra the Lord of celestials, 
staying in mountains and moving with a peed equal to the wind."

shloka: ततः तस्मिन् महाबाहुः कोप सम्वर्तित ईक्षणः
translation:
"Then, the long-armed Rama, the best among wise men, swirling his eyes in anger, made 
a resolve in the matter of that ferocious crow."

shloka: स दर्भ संस्तरात् गृह्य ब्रह्मणो अस्त्रेण योजयः
translation:
"Taking a blade of Kusa grass from his bed ( made of Kusa grass), Rama employed it to 
work with Brahma's missile (a mythical weapon which deals with infallible destruction). That blazing 
shoot of grass, resembling a fire destroying the world, flared up in front of that bird."

shloka: स तम् प्रदीप्तम् चिक्षेप दर्भम् तम् वायसम् प्रति
translation:
"As Rama threw that blazing blade of Kusa grass towards that crow, that blade of grass 
went chasing that crow in the sky."

shloka: अनुसृष्टः तदा कालो जगाम विविधाम् गतिम्
translation:
"Then, while that blade of grass came chasing, that crow went flying in many a way. Seeking 
protection, it roamed all over the world."

shloka: स पित्रा च परित्यक्तः सुरैः सर्वैः महर्षिभिः
translation:
"Roaming the three worlds in search of a saviour, that crow was abandoned by Indra; its 
father, the celestials and the sages. Finally, it sought refuge in the same Rama."

shloka: स तम् निपतितम् भूमौ शरण्यः शरणा गतम्
translation:
"That Rama, who affords protection, was compassionate and protected that crow, which 
fell on the ground (in salutation to Rama) and sought for protection, eventhough it was apt to be killed."

shloka: परिद्यूनम् विषण्णम् च स त्वम् आयान्तम् उक्तवान्
translation:
"Seeing that crow, coming exhausted and dejected, Rama said to it: 'It is not possible 
to make Brahma missile a waste. For this reason, tell me what to do now."

shloka: हिनस्तु दक्षिणाक्षित्वच्छर इत्यथ सोऽब्रवीत्
translation:
Thereafter, that crow said "Let your arrow shoot my right eye." Then that blade of Kusa 
grass shooted the right eye of that crow. By giving away its right eye in that way, the crow saved its 
life."

shloka:
स रामाय नमस्कृत्वा राज्ञे दशरथाय च |
विसृष्टस्तेन वीरेण प्रतिपेदे स्वमालयम्
translation:
"After offering salutations to Rama and King Dasaratha and being discharged by that valiant 
Rama, the crow returned to its own abode."

shloka:
मत् कृते काक मात्रे अपि ब्रह्म अस्त्रम् समुदीरितम् |
कस्मात् यो माम् हरत् त्वत्तः क्षमसे तम् मही पते
translation:
"O lord of the earth! For my sake you hurled a Brahma's missile even at a crow. Why are 
you forgiving the one who has taken me away from you?"

shloka:
स कुरुष्व महाउत्साहम् कृपाम् मयि नर ऋषभ |
त्वया नाथवती नाथ ह्यनाथा इव दृश्यते
translation:
"O Rama the best among men! You, with great strength, annihilate the enemy and bestow 
your mercy on me. O Lord! She who has a protector in you, actually looks like one without any protector."

shloka:
आनृशंस्यम् परो धर्मः त्वत्त एव मया श्रुतः |
जानामि त्वाम् महावीर्यम् महाउत्साहम् महाबलम्
translation:
"You yourself told me that kindness is the best righteousness. I know you, having a great 
prowess, a great energy, and a great strength. I know your non-acquiescence, imperturbability, profoundness 
like an ocean, as Lord of the earth including the oceans and as equal to Indra the Lord of celestials."

shloka:
एवम् अस्त्रविदाम् श्रेष्ठः सत्त्ववान् बलवान् अपि |
किम् अर्थम् अस्त्रम् रक्षह्सु न योजयसि राघव
translation:
"O Rama! Eventhough you are strong, excellently skilled in archery and a truthful man, 
why are you not utilizing your arrow on demons?"

shloka:
न नागा न अपि गन्धर्वा न असुरा न मरुत् गणाः |
रामस्य समरे वेगम् शक्ताः प्रति समाधितुम्
translation:
"Neither the serpent-demons, nor the divine musicians nor the demons nor the storm-gods 
are able to resist the onrush of Rama in battle."

shloka:
तस्या वीर्यवतः कश्चित् यदि अस्ति मयि सम्भ्रमः |
किम् अर्थम् न शरैः तीक्ष्णैः क्षयम् नयति राक्षसान्
translation:
"If the valiant Rama has any haste in my case, why does he not destroy the demons with 
his sharp arrows?!

shloka:
भ्रातुः आदेशम् आदाय लक्ष्मणो वा परम् तपः |
कस्य हेतोः न माम् वीरः परित्राति महाबलः
translation:
"For what reason, even Lakshmana the tormentator of enemies, the mighty man and the valiant 
man does not protect me, by taking the command of his elder brother?'

shloka:
यदि तौ पुरुष व्याघ्रौ वाय्व् इन्द्र सम तेजसौ |
सुराणाम् अपि दुर्धर्षो किम् अर्थम् माम् उपेक्षतः
translation:
Those two tigers among men, Rama and Lakshmana, with a sharpness equal to that of wind 
and fire, even if they are unconquerable by demons too, why are they neglecting me?"

shloka:
मम एव दुष्कृतम् किंचिन् महत् अस्ति न संशयः |
समर्थाव् अपि तौ यन् माम् न अवेक्षेते परम् तपौ
translation:
"There is not doubt that I would have committed a great sin, for which reason those two 
brothers Rama and Lakshmana the tormentators of enemies, even when capable , are neglecting me."

shloka:
वैदेह्या वचनम् श्रुत्वा करुणम् साशुभाषितम् |
अथाब्रवीन्महातेजा हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः
translation:
Hearing the pitiable appeal Seetha with tears, Hanuma of great splendour and the son 
of wind-god spoke (as follows)

shloka:
त्वच्छोकविमुखो रामो देवि सत्येन ते शपे |
रामे दुःखाभिपन्ने च लक्ष्मणः परितप्यते
translation:
"O Seetha! Rama has grown averse to everything else, caused by grief towards you. I swear 
it to you by truth. When Rama is overpowered by grief; Lakshmana too gets tormented by grief."

shloka:
कथम् चिद्भवती दृष्टा न कालः परिदेवितुम् |
इमम् मुहूर्तम् दुःखानाम् द्रक्ष्यस्यन्तमनिन्दिते
translation:
"O faultless Seetha! Somehow or other, you have been discovered by me. This is not the 
time to lament. Your will see the end of your sorrow within a short time."

shloka:
तावुभौ पुरुषव्याघ्रौ राजपुत्रौ महाबलौ |
त्वद्दर्शनकृतोत्साहौ लङ्काम् भस्मीकरिष्यतः
translation:
"Those two mighty princes, the excellent among men, are eager to see you and they will 
reduce Lanka to ashes."

shloka:
हत्वा च समरे क्रूतम् रावणम् सहबान्धवम् |
राघवस्त्वाम् विशालाक्षि नेष्यति स्वाम् पुरीम् प्रति
translation:
"O large-eyed Seetha! Killing the cruel Ravana along with his relatives in battle, Rama 
will take you back to his own city."

shloka:
ब्रूहि यद्राघवो वाच्यो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः |
सुग्रीवो वापि तेजस्वी हरयोऽपि समागताः
translation:
"Tell me what to be expressed to Rama or to the mighty Lakshmana or to the splendourous 
Sugreeva or even to the other monkeys assembled there."

shloka:
इत्युक्तवति तस्मिंस्तु सीता सुरसुतोपमा |
उवाच शोकसंतप्ता हनुमन्तं प्लवंगमम्
translation:
Hearing the words of Hanuma, Seetha, like the daughter of a sage, tormented with grief, 
spoke to Hanuma the monkey (as follows):

shloka:
कौसल्या लोक भर्तारम् सुषुवे यम् मनस्विनी |
तम् मम अर्थे सुखम् पृच्छ शिरसा च अभिवादय
translation:
"On my behalf, salute by bowing your head and ask about the welfare of Rama, the Lord 
of the worlds, whom the magnanimous Kausalya gave birth."

shloka:
स्रजः च सर्व रत्नानि प्रिया याः च वर अन्गनाः |
ऐश्वर्यम् च विशालायाम् पृथिव्याम् अपि दुर्लभम्
translation:
(On my behalf, ask about the welfare of ) Lakshmana, that good child of Sumitra who, 
having renounced the wreaths of flowers, all the riches, pleasant and beautiful girls and even the prosperity 
difficult to be obtained in this extensive world, offered his profound respects to and pacified his 
father and mother, followed Rama to exile."

shloka:
आनुकूल्येन धर्म आत्मा त्यक्त्वा सुखम् अनुत्तमम् |
अनुगच्छति काकुत्स्थम् भ्रातरम् पालयन् वने
translation:
"Renouncing a great comfort, the righteous Lakshmana, acting in an affectionate manner 
towards Rama, followed him, watching over him in the forest."

shloka:
सिम्ह स्कन्धो महाबाहुः मनस्वी प्रिय दर्शनः |
पितृवत् वर्तते रामे मातृवन् माम् समाचरन्
translation:
"Lakshmana, who has broad shoulders like that ofa lion, mighty-armed, steady-minded and 
having pleasant looks, behaves towards Rama as towards his father and looks to me as his own mother."

shloka:
प्रियमाणाम् तदा वीरो न तु माम् वेद लक्ष्मणः |
वृद्ध उपसेवी लक्ष्मीवान् शक्तो न बहु भाषिता
translation:
"The valiant Lakshmana, on that day of occurrence, did not know that I was being taken 
away by Ravana. He serves elders. He possesses a splendour. Though capable, he does not talk much. To 
Dasaratha, my father-in-law, he is his replica a beloved and the best prince."

shloka: मत्तः प्रियतरो नित्यम् भ्राता रामस्य लक्ष्मणः
translation:
"Lakshmana, the younger brother of Rama is the one who is dearer to me always. That energetic 
Lakshmana carries out well, whatever load of work is entrusted to him"

shloka: यम् दृष्ट्वा राघवो न एव वृद्धम् आर्यम् अनुस्मरत्
translation:
"Seeing whom, Rama ceases to recollect his deceased father, that Lakshmana is to be asked 
about his well-being, as my word and on my behalf."

shloka: मृदुः नित्यम् शुचिः दक्षः प्रियो रामस्य लक्ष्मणः
translation:
"O Hanuma, the excellent of monkeys and the best of monkeys! you are the model for fulfilling 
this act of addressing him in such a way that Lakshmana, the mild, every-pure and clever darling of 
Rama may bring my sorrows to an end."

shloka:
राघवस्त्वत्समारम्भान्मयि यत्नपरो भवेत् |
इदम् ब्रूयाः च मे नाथम् शूरम् रामम् पुनः पुनः
translation:
"Depending on your effort, Rama will be more active with his effort the following words 
again and again to Rama, my Lord and the hero:"

shloka:
जीवितम् धारयिष्यामि मासम् दशरथ आत्मज |
ऊर्ध्वम् मासान् न जीवेयम् सत्येन अहम् ब्रवीमि ते
translation:
"O Rama! I shall hold my life for a month. I cannot survive after a month I am telling 
you the truth."

shloka:
रावणेन उपरुद्धाम् माम् निकृत्या पाप कर्मणा |
त्रातुम् अर्हसि वीर त्वम् पातालात् इव कौशिकीम्
translation:
"O valiant man! You are required to rescue me, detained (as I am) by Ravana the criminal 
and subjected to humiliation, as you (as Lord Vishnu) earlier protected Indra the Lord of celestials 
and Lakshmi the goddess of prosperity from the abode of servants and demons."

shloka:
ततो वस्त्र गतम् मुक्त्वा दिव्यम् चूडा मणिम् शुभम् |
प्रदेयो राघवाय इति सीता हनुमते ददौ
translation:
Then, untying the bright devine jewel for her head tied in her garment, Seetha gave it 
to Hanuma, saying that it might be handed over to Rama.

shloka:
प्रतिगृह्य ततो वीरो मणि रत्नम् अनुत्तमम् |
अन्गुल्या योजयामास न हि अस्या प्राभवत् भुजः
translation:
Taking the excellent jewel, the valiant Hanuma thereupon fitted it to his finger, since 
his arm (eventhough he had assumed his former tiny form), was not fitting to it properly.

shloka:
मणि रत्नम् कपि वरः प्रतिगृह्य अभिवाद्य च |
सीताम् प्रदक्षिणम् कृत्वा प्रणतः पार्श्वतः स्थितः
translation:
Receiving that jewel, Hanuma the best among the monkeys, offered his salutation to seetha, 
by engaging himself in circumambulation and stood aside with humbleness.

shloka:
हर्षेण महता युक्तः सीता दर्शनजेन सः |
हृदयेन गतो रामम् शरीरेण तु विष्ठितः
translation:
Filled with a great delight, born out of Seetha's discovery by him, that Hanuma mentally 
sought (the presence) of Rama but stood there with just his physical body.

shloka:
मणि वरम् उपगृह्य तम् महाअर्हम् |
जनक नृप आत्मजया धृतम् प्रभावात् |
गिरि वर पवन अवधूत मुक्तः |
सुखित मनाः प्रतिसम्क्रमम् प्रपेदे
translation:
Taking that excellent and highly venerable jewel, worn by Seetha and by its influence 
resembling one who was shaken by a blast coming from the top of a huge mountain, Hanuma was mentally 
pleased and set out for crossing the ocean in his return journey.

shloka:
मणिम् दत्त्वा ततः सीता हनूमन्तम् अथ अब्रवीत् |
अभिज्ञानम् अभिज्ञातम् एतत् रामस्य तत्त्वतः
translation:
Then, after giving the jewel for head, Seetha spoke to Hanuma as follows: "This token 
of remembrance is actually known to Rama."

shloka:
मणिम् तु दृष्ट्वा रामो वै त्रयाणाम् संस्मरिष्यति |
वीरो जनन्या मम च राज्ञो दशरथस्य च
translation:
"By seeing this jewel, the heroic Rama can recollect three of us, viz. my mother, myself 
and the king Dasaratha."

shloka:
स भूयः त्वम् समुत्साहे चोदितो हरि सत्तम |
अस्मिन् कार्य समारम्भे प्रचिन्तय यत् उत्तरम्
translation:
"O Hanuma the excellent among monkeys! Driven by your enthusiasm again, think what remains 
to be done in undertaking this task."

shloka:
त्वम् अस्मिन् कार्य निर्योगे प्रमाणम् हरि सत्तम |
हनुमन् यत्नमास्थाय दुःखक्षयकरो भव
translation:
"O Hanuma the best among monkeys! You are capable of fulfilling this task. O Hanuma! 
Become the one who can remove my misfortunes, by employing your effort. If you think of it carefully, 
your effort will become the one which can remove my misfortunes."

shloka: स तथा इति प्रतिज्ञाय मारुतिः भीम विक्रमः
translation:
That Hanuma of terrific prowess, having promised 'so be it', offered salutation to Seetha 
by bowing his head to her and was set off to go.

shloka: ज्ञात्वा सम्प्रस्थितम् देवी वानरम् मारुत आत्मजम्
translation:
Getting to know Hanuma ready to set out, Seetha the princess spoke the following words 
with her voice choked by tears.

shloka: कुशलम् हनुमन् ब्रूयाः सहितौ राम लक्ष्मणौ
translation:
"O Hanuma, the excellent among monkeys! Ask about the welfare of both Rama and Lakshmana 
together. You also ask, according to our usage, about the welfare of Sugreeva together with his ministers
