with their hoods and necks severely pressed lay coiled.

shloka: किन्नर उरग गन्धर्व यक्ष विद्या धराः तथा
translation:
Then, leaving that tormented mountain of excellence; Kinnaras, Nagas, Gadharvas, Yakshas 
and Vidyadharas ascended to the sky.

shloka: स च भूमि धरः श्रीमान् बलिना तेन पीडितः
translation:
Pressed down by that strong Hanuma, that beautiful mountain having its elevated summits 
crowned with trees, entered the bowels of the earth.

shloka: दश योजन विस्तारः त्रिंशत् योजनम् उच्छ्रितः
translation:
That mountain, with a width of ten yojanas (or eighty miles) and a height of thirty yojanas 
(or two hundred and forty miles) got level with the earth.

shloka: स लिलङ्घुयिर्भीमम् सलीलम् लवणार्णवम्
translation:
With a desire to cross easily the terrific ocean, whose shores were being lashed by its 
waves, which Hanuma jumped up into the air.

shloka:
सचन्द्र कुमुदम् रम्यम् सार्क कारण्डवम् शुभम् |
तिष्य श्रवण कदम्बम् अभ्र शैवल शाद्वलम्
translation:
Hanuma, with a rush equal to that of wind, withaut a fatigue, leapt across the baundless 
	sea looking analogaus to sky, like a large ship crossing the ocean. In that pleasant and auspiciaus 
	sky-like sea, shone the moon as a white water-like sea, shone having the constellations known by 
	the names of Pushya and Shravana as swans, the clauds as its duck-weeds; the twin constellations 
	the Punarvasus as its large fish, the planet Mars as its large alligator, a large island as Airavata 
	(Indra's elephant), graced with a swan in the form of the constellation, Shwati, having gales as 
	its waves, the moon bea.ns as its cool water and with the Nagas, yakshas and Gandharvas as its full 
	blown lotuses and water-lilies.

shloka:
ग्रासमान इव आकाशम् तारा अधिपम् इव आलिखन् |
हरन्न् इव सनक्षत्रम् गगनम् सार्क मण्डलम्
translation:
While moving in the sky, the illustrious Hanuma, the son of wind-god and the great 
	monkey, appeared as if swallowing the sky, scratching the moon and carrying off the sky with its 
	stars and the disc of the sun and was going as though dragging asunder, a mass of clouds.

shloka:
पाण्डुर अरुण वर्णानि नील मान्जिष्ठकानि च |
हरित अरुण वर्णानि महाअभ्राणि चकाशिरे
translation:
Dense clauds, with white and red colaurs, blue and yellow colaurs as also green and 
	reddish brown colaurs shone brightly in the sky.

shloka:
प्रविशन्न् अभ्र जालानि निष्क्रमन् च पुनः पुनः |
प्रच्छन्नः च प्रकाशः च चन्द्रमा इव लक्ष्यते
translation:
Time and again, entering and coming out of the clusters of clouds, Hanuma appeared 
	like the moon becoming visible and invisible again and again.

shloka:
विविधाभ्राघनासन्नगोचरो धवळाम्बरः |
दृश्यादृश्यतनुर्वीरस्तदा चन्द्रयतेऽम्बरे
translation:
The heroic Hanuma, who was clad in white clothes, having faund his way into variaus 
	kinds of dense clauds (and energing again) and having his personlaity becoming visible and invisible, 
	shone like the moon in the sky.

shloka:
तार्क्ष्यायमाणो गगने बभासे वायुनन्दनः |
दारयन्मेघबृन्दानि निष्पतंश्च पुनः पुनः
translation:
Tearing asunder the clusters of clouds again and again as also energing from them 
	and roaring with a big noise, Hanuma the son of wind-god, making a thunderous great sound, shone 
	flying like Garuda the eagle, in the sky.

shloka:
नदन् नादेन महता मेघ स्वन महास्वनः |
प्रवरान् राक्षसान् हत्वा नाम विश्राव्य चात्मनः
translation:
Killing the foremost of demons, becoming famaus by is name, making Lanka perplexed, 
	causing anguish to Ravana by tormenting his terrible army, and bidding his adieu to Sheetha, Hanuma 
	returned by flying over the middle of the sea.

shloka: पर्वत इन्द्रम् सुनाभम् च समुपस्पृश्य वीर्यवान्
translation:
Touching Mount Mainaka, the victorious Hanuma came with a great speed resembling 
	an iron arrow discharged from a bow-string.

shloka: स किंचित् अनुसम्प्राप्तः समालोक्य महागिरिम्
translation:
Approaching a bit near and observing Maunt Mahendra, the great mauntain looking like 
	a dense claud, that Hanuma made a laud noise.

shloka: स पूरयामास कपिर्दिशो दश समन्ततः
translation:
Emitting a great roar, that Hanuma, whole loud noise resembled the rumbling of a 
	cloud, filled the whole space in all directions with the noise.

shloka: स तम् देशमनुप्राप्तः सुहृद्दर्शनलालसः
translation:
Having reached that place, Hanuma who was ardently desiraus of seeing his friends, 
	roared and waved his tail.

shloka: तस्य नानद्यमानस्य सुपर्णचरिते पथि
translation:
The sky, with the disc of the sun, began to crack as it were, due to his roar, even 
	as he repeatedly roared on the path of the sky as followed by Garuda, the eagle endowed with charming 
	wings.

shloka:
ये तु तत्रोत्तरे तीरे समुद्रस्य महाबलाः | ५-५७-१८
पूर्वम् सम्विष्ठिताः शूरा वायुपुत्रदिदृक्षवः |
महतो वातनुन्नस्य तोयदस्येव गर्जितम्
translation:
Those mighty heroes who were waiting already on the northern shore of the sea, with 
	an eagerness to see Hanuma, heard there at that time, the saund produced by the sweeping motion 
	of Hanuma's thighs, which resembled the reoar of a huge claud propelled by the wind.

shloka: ते दीनमनसः सर्वे शुश्रुवुः काननौकसः
translation:
All those monkeys, who were distressed in mind (for not having heard the news of 
	Seetha hitherto), heard Hanuma's roar similar to the roar of a rumbling cloud.

shloka: निशम्य नदतो नादम् वानराः ते समन्ततः
translation:
Hearing that roar of Hanuma, who was making the saund, all those mokeys stationed 
	there in all directions, became anxiausly desiraus of seeing their friend.

shloka: जाम्बवान् स हरि श्रेष्ठः प्रीति सम्हृष्ट मानसः
translation:
The Jambavan, the foremot among the monkesy and bears, with his mind thrilled with 
	joy, having summoned all the monkeys, spoke the follwoing words:

shloka: सर्वथा कृत कार्यो असौ हनूमान् न अत्र संशयः
translation:
"This Hanuma has accoMplished his assignment in all ways. His saund will not indeed 
	be like this, if he has not fulfilled his task. There is not daubt in this matter."

shloka: तस्या बाहु ऊरु वेगम् च निनादम् च महात्मनः
translation:
Hearing the sound of the dashing movement of the high souled Hanuma's arms and thighs, 
	the monkeys moved by jumps with joy from their respective places.

shloka: ते नग अग्रान् नग अग्राणि शिखरात् शिखराणि च
translation:
Those monkeys with joy, longing to see Hanuma, took off from the top of one tree 
	to the tops of other trees as also from one mauntain-summit to the other summits.

shloka: ते प्रीताः पादप अग्रेषु गृह्य शाखाः सुपुष्पिताः
translation:
Those monkeys, grasping the boughs at the tops of trees, and standing there firmly, 
	joyously waved the twigs, as if they are their raiments.

shloka: गिरिगह्वरसम्लीनो यथा गर्जति मारुतः
translation:
The mighty, Hanuma the son of wind-god, roared as thaugh the wind roars while it 
	enters the caves of mauntains.

shloka: तम् अभ्र घन संकाशम् आपतन्तम् महाकपिम्
translation:
Seeing that Hanuma then rushing like a dense cloud, all those monkeys stood there, 
	joining their palms in salutation.

shloka: ततः तु वेगवान् तस्य गिरेः गिरि निभः कपिः
translation:
The swift Hanuma, looking like a mauntain, then descended on the summit of that Maunt 
	mahendra, thick with trees.

shloka: हर्षेणापूर्यमाणोऽसौ रम्ये पर्वतनिर्घरे
translation:
Hanuma like a mountain with its wings torn off, thrilled with joy, fell from the 
	sky into a charming mountain-torrent.

shloka: ततः ते प्रीत मनसः सर्वे वानर पुम्गवाः
translation:
Then, all the foremost of those monkeys, with their pleasing hearts, stood surraunding 
	the high-sauled Hanuma. Having encircled Hanuma, all of them obtained a supreme joy.

shloka:
प्रहृष्ट वदनाः सर्वे तम् अरोगम् उपागतम् |
उपायनानि च आदाय मूलानि च फलानि च
translation:
All those mokeys with their delightful faces, taking roots and fruits as their presents, 
	honured Hanuma, the foremost among the monkeys, who came back hale and healthy.

shloka: हनूमान् तु गुरून् वृद्धान् जाम्बवत् प्रमुखान् तदा
translation:
Then, Hanuma the excellent one among the monkeys, on his part, offered his salutation 
	to venerable persons and elders like Jambavan in the first place, as also Angada, the prince.

shloka: स ताभ्याम् पूजितः पूज्यः कपिभिः च प्रसादितः
translation:
Jambavan and Angada honoured that victorious and venerable Hanuma. The other monkeys 
	also made him gracious. Hanuma informed them briefly that he had seen Seetha.

shloka: निषसाद च हस्तेन गृहीत्वा वालिनः सुतम्
translation:
Then, seizing the hand of Angada, Vali's son, Hanuma sat down at a distinct spot 
	in the charming forest of Maunt Mahendra.

shloka: हनूमान् अब्रवीद्त् हृष्टः तदा तान् वानर ऋषभान्
translation:
Then, the pleased Hanuma spoke the following words to those excellent monkeys: "I 
	saw that Seetha, the duaghter of Janaka, who was staying in Ashoka garden, guarded unblemished by 
	highly dreadful female-demons and wearing a single braid, young woman, as she was, longing to see 
	Rama, thoroughly fatigued due to her fasting, with her hair twisted together, wearing soiled clothes 
	and looking emaciated."

shloka: ततो दृष्टा इति वचनम् महाअर्थम् अमृत उपमम्
translation:
Hearing from Hanuma that iMportant and nectar like word to the effect that Sheetha 
	had been seen all the monkeys became delighted.

shloka:
क्ष्वेडन्ति अन्ये नदन्ति अन्ये गर्जन्ति अन्ये महाबलाः |
चक्रुः किल किलाम् अन्ये प्रतिगर्जन्ति च अपरे
translation:
Some mighty monkeys made a lion's roar. Some were making a sound of approbation. 
	Some were making a sound of thunder. Some others proudced cries expressing joy. Some others were 
	roaring in return.

shloka:
केचित् उच्छ्रित लान्गूलाः प्रहृष्टाः कपि कुन्जराः |
अन्चित आयत दीर्घाणि लान्गूलानि प्रविव्यधुः
translation:
Shome eminent monkeys, with joy and with their tails lifted up, waved their distended 
	curved tails.

shloka:
अपरे तु हनूमन्तम् वानरा वारण उपमम् |
आप्लुत्य गिरि शृन्गेभ्यः संस्पृशन्ति स्म हर्षिताः
translation:
Descending from the mountain-tops; some other monkeys, with delight, fondingly touched 
	Hanuma who resembled an elephant.

shloka:
उक्त वाक्यम् हनूमन्तम् अन्गदः तु तदा अब्रवीत् |
सर्वेषाम् हरि वीराणाम् मध्ये वाचम् अनुत्तमाम्
translation:
After hearing the words of Hanuma, Angada spoke the follwoing excellent words in 
	the midst of those eminent monkeys.

shloka:
सत्त्वे वीर्ये न ते कश्चित् समो वानर विद्यते |
यत् अवप्लुत्य विस्तीर्णम् सागरम् पुनः आगतः
translation:
"O Hanuma! Since you returned here crossing the extensive ocean, none stands equal 
	to you in strength and prowess."

shloka:
अहो स्वामिनि ते भक्तिरहो वीर्यमहो धृतिः |
दिष्ट्या दृष्टा त्वया देवी राम पत्नी यशस्विनी
translation:
"What amazing is yaur devotion to the Lord! What a wonderful prowess! What a surprising 
	caurage! By aur good fortune, yau saw the illustriaus Sheetha, Rama's consort. Thank heaven! Rama 
	can give up his sorrow born aut of Sheetha's separataion."

shloka: ततो अन्गदम् हनूमन्तम् जाम्बवन्तम् च वानराः
translation:
Very much delighted, the monkeys then sat on extensive flat rocks encircling Angada, 
	Hanuma and Jambavan.

shloka: श्रोतु कामाः समुद्रस्य लन्घनम् वानर उत्तमाः
translation:
Longing to hear abaut crossing of ocean and the seeing of Lanka, Sheetha and Ravana, 
	all those excellent monkeys waited with their joined pal.ns, in anctipation of Hanuma's words.

shloka:
तस्थौ तत्र अन्गदः श्रीमान् वानरैः बहुभिः वृतः |
उपास्यमानो विबुधैः दिवि देव पतिः यथा
translation:
The auspicious Angada encircled by many monkeys there, waited like Indra the lord 
	of celestials, who was waited upon by celestials in heaven.

shloka:
हनूमता कीर्तिमता यशस्विना |
तथा अन्गदेन अन्गद बद्ध बाहुना |
मुदा तदा अध्यासितम् उन्नतम् महन् |
मही धर अग्रम् ज्वलितम् श्रिया अभवत्
translation:
The high and large summit of the mauntain, on which were seated then with delight, 
	the illustriaus Hanuma and the famaus Angada, with bracelets worn on his upper ar.ns, stood blazed 
	with splendaur.

shloka:
ततः तस्य गिरेः शृन्गे महाइन्द्रस्य महाबलाः |
हनुमत् प्रमुखाः प्रीतिम् हरयो जग्मुः उत्तमाम्
translation:
Thereafter, the mighty monkeys, headed by Hanuma and others, experienced a great joy 
on that summit of Mount Mahendra.

shloka:
तम् ततः प्रतिसम्हृष्टः प्रीतिमन्तम् महाकपिम् |
जाम्बवान् कार्य वृत्त अन्तम् अपृच्छत् अनिल आत्मजम्
translation:
Then, Jambavan, thrilling with rapture, asked the delighted Hanuma, the great monkey 
about the particulars of that actual occurrence (of seeing Seetha) as follows

shloka:
कथम् दृष्टा त्वया देवी कथम् वा तत्र वर्तते |
तस्याम् वा स कथम् वृत्तः क्रूर कर्मा दश आननः
translation:
"How did you see Seetha? How was she there? How was that Ravana of terrible deeds behaving 
towards her?"

shloka:
तत्त्वतः सर्वम् एतन् नः प्रब्रूहि त्वम् महाकपे |
श्रुत अर्थाः चिन्तयिष्यामो भूयः कार्य विनिश्चयम्
translation:
"O Hanuma! Tell us entirely, in truth whatever has occurred. Ascertaining the truth, 
from you, we shall again think about what decision to be taken further."

shloka:
यः च अर्थः तत्र वक्तव्यो गतैः अस्माभिः आत्मवान् |
रक्षितव्यम् च यत् तत्र तत् भवान् व्याकरोतु नः
translation:
"When we go there (to the presence of Rama), having prudence, tell us clearly which matter 
is to be disclosed and which matter is to be kept off from him."

shloka:
स नियुक्तः ततः तेन सम्प्रहृष्ट तनू रुहः |
नमस्यन् शिरसा देव्यै सीतायै प्रत्यभाषत
translation:
Thus commanded by Jambavan, Hanuma, with his hair standing on end mentally offered his 
salutation to Seetha, the princess, by bowing his head and replied as follows:

shloka:
प्रत्यक्षम् एव भवताम् महाइन्द्र अग्रात् खम् आप्लुतः |
उदधेः दक्षिणम् पारम् कान्क्षमाणः समाहितः
translation:
"With an intention to reach the southern shore of the ocean, I leapt into the sky, indeed 
before your presence, from the summit of Mount Mahendra."

shloka:
गच्छतः च हि मे घोरम् विघ्न रूपम् इव अभवत् |
कान्चनम् शिखरम् दिव्यम् पश्यामि सुमनो हरम्
translation:
"While I was going, a terrific hindrance occurred in my way as it was. I saw a golden 
mountain-peak which was so charming and fascinating."

shloka:
स्थितम् पन्थानम् आवृत्य मेने विघ्नम् च तम् नगम् |
उपसम्गम्य तम् दिव्यम् कान्चनम् नग सत्तमम्
translation:
"I accounted that mountain staying turned towards the path, as an impediment. Approaching 
that excellent charming and golden mountain, I made up my mind to shatter it."

shloka: प्रहतम् च मया तस्य लान्गूलेन महागिरेः
translation:
"As I struck it with my tail, the mountain-peak of that great hill, resembling the sun, 
was broken into a thousand pieces."

shloka: व्यवसायम् च मे बुद्ध्वा स ह उवाच महागिरिः
translation:
"Understanding my purpose, that great mountain spoke the following sweet words saying, 
'O my son!', As though it was refreshing my mind (once more to proceed further)."

shloka: पितृव्यम् च अपि माम् विद्धि सखा अयम् मातरिश्वनः
translation:
" 'Know me to be generally called as Mynaa dwelling in this great ocean, as a companion 
of the wind-god and even as your father's brother'."

shloka: पक्ष्ववन्तः पुरा पुत्र बभूवुः पर्वत उत्तमाः
translation:
" 'O my son! Long ago, the foremost among the mountains used to have wings. They used 
to wander the entire earth freely, hurting the people!"

shloka: श्रुत्वा नगानाम् चरितम् महाइन्द्रः पाक शासनः
translation:
" 'Hearing that behaviour of those mountains, the venerable Indra the lord of celestials, 
the destroyer of a demon called Paka, chopped their wings into a thousand pieces by using his thunderbolt.' 
"

shloka: अहम् तु मोक्षितः तस्मात् तव पित्रा महात्मना
translation:
" 'O child! I, on my part, was hurled into the great ocean by the high-souled wind-god, 
your father and was liberated from the clutches of Indra.' "

shloka: रामस्य च मया साह्ये वर्तितव्यम् अरिम् दम
translation:
" 'O Hanuma the annihilator of enemies! I have to behave in such a way as to help Rama. 
For, Rama, having a prowess equal to that of Indra; is indeed excellent in supporting righteousness.'"

shloka: एतत् श्रुत्वा मया तस्य मैनाकस्य महात्मनः
translation:
"Hearing the words of that high-souled Mynaka and after informing my purpose, my mind 
was prepared for a further travel. The high-soled Mynaka also allowed me to depart."

shloka:
स चाप्यन्तर्हितः शैलो मानुषेण वपुष्मता |
शरीरेण महाशैलः शैलेन च महोदधौ
translation:
"That Mynaka mountain vanished in the guise of a beautiful form of a human being. That 
large mountainous form also later drowned into the great ocean."

shloka:
उत्तमम् जवम् आस्थाय शेषम् अध्वानम् आस्थितः |
ततो अहम् सुचिरम् कालम् वेगेन अभ्यगमम् पथि
translation:
"Thereafter, employing an excellent speed and continuing on my course, I proceeded in 
that path speedily for a long time."

shloka:
ततः पश्यामि अहम् देवीम् सुरसाम् नाग मातरम् |
समुद्र मध्ये सा देवी वचनम् माम् अभाषत
translation:
"Thereafter, I saw Surasa, the mother of serpents in the midst of the sea. That goddess 
spoke the following words to me.

shloka:
मम भक्ष्यः प्रदिष्टः त्वम् अमारैः हरि सत्तमम् |
ततः त्वाम् भक्षयिष्यामि विहितः त्वम् चिरस्य मे
translation:
"O excellent of monkeys! The celestials have shown you as my eatable. Therefore, I will 
eat you since you have been bestowed to me by gods after a long time."

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः सुरसया प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतः स्थितः |
विवर्ण वदनो भूत्वा वाक्यम् च इदम् उदीरयम्
translation:
"Hearing Surasa's words, I stood there, offering salutation with my joined palms to her. 
Becoming pale-faced, I spoke the following words:

shloka:
रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् प्रविष्टो दण्डका वनम् |
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा सीतया च परम् तपः
translation:
" 'Rama, the son of Dasaratha the splendid man and the tormentator of enemies, together 
with Lakshmana, his brother and Seetha entered the forest of Dandaka.'"

shloka:
तस्य सीता हृता भार्या रावणेन दुरात्मना |
तस्याः सकाशम् दूतो अहम् गमिष्ये राम शासनात्
translation:
" 'The evil-minded Ravana took away Seetha, Rama's wife. By the orders of Rama, I am 
going to her as an envoy.' "

shloka:
कर्तुम् अर्हसि रामस्य साह्यम् विषय वासिनि |
अथवा मैथिलीम् दृष्ट्वा रामम् च अक्लिष्ट कारिणम्
translation:
"'You, abiding in Rama's country, ought to do a help to Rama. Otherwise, after seeing 
Seetha and Rama, who is unwearied in action, I will come to your mouth. I am thus promising you in truth."

shloka: एवम् उक्ता मया सा तु सुरसा काम रूपिणी
translation:
Hearing my words, that Surasa who can assume any form at her will said: "No one can violate 
me by unfaithfulness. I have this boon with me."

shloka: एवम् उक्तः सुरसया दश योजनम् आयतः
translation:
"Hearing the words of Surasa, I, as tall as ten Yojanas (eighty miles), within a moment, 
grew half as much in size (fifteen Yojanas or one hundred twenty miles)."

shloka: मत् प्रमाण अनुरूपम् च व्यादितम् तन् मुखम् तया
translation:
"She opened her mouth so wide as to correspond to the size of my body. Seeing her expanded 
mouth, I assumed a dwarfish form. At that moment, I still became reduced to the size of a human thumb."

shloka:
अभिपत्य आशु तत् वक्त्रम् निर्गतो अहम् ततः क्षणात् |
अब्रवीत् सुरसा देवी स्वेन रूपेण माम् पुनः
translation:
"After entering her mouth quickly, I then came out instantly. The divine Surasa, in her 
native form, spoke to me again, as follows:

shloka:
अर्थ सिद्ध्यै हरि श्रेष्ठ गच्छ सौम्य यथा सुखम् |
समानय च वैदेहीम् राघवेण महात्मना
translation:
"'O gently monkey! O the foremost among monkeys! Go happily for the fulfillment of your 
purpose. Bring back Seetha to the magnanimous Rama. O mighty armed monkey! Be happy. I am pleased with 
you.'"

shloka: ततो अहम् साधु साध्वी इति सर्व भूतैः प्रशंसितः
translation:
"Then, all living beings praised me! Saying Good! Well done! Bravo! Thereupon, I leapt 
into the extensive sky, like Garuda the eagle, the carrier of Lord Vishnu."

shloka: चाया मे निगृहीता च न च पश्यामि किंचन
translation:
"In the meanwhile, my shadow was held fast. Yet, I did not perceive anything. My speed 
having been blocked, I surveyed all the ten directions. But I could not discover there, any object by 
which my movement was blocked."

shloka:
ततो मे बुद्धिः उत्पन्ना किम् नाम गमने मम |
ईदृशो विघ्न उत्पन्नो रूपम् यत्र न दृश्यते
translation:
"Then, the thought arose in me: "How I wonder has such a hindrance arose in my journey, 
although no concrete configuration is being seen here?"

shloka:
अधो भागेन मे दृष्टिः शोचता पातिता मया |
ततो अद्राक्षम् अहम् भीमाम् राक्षसीम् सलिले शयाम्
translation:
"While I was thinking thus, my sight has fallen downward. There, I saw a terrible female-demon 
lying in water."

shloka:
प्रहस्य च महानादम् उक्तो अहम् भीमया तया |
अवस्थितम् असम्भ्रान्तम् इदम् वाक्यम् अशोभनम्
translation:
"Heartily laughing with a great noise, that terrific woman, spoke to me the following 
inauspicious words, firmly and without any bewilderment (as follows):

shloka:
क्व असि गन्ता महाकाय क्षुधिताया मम ईप्सितः |
भक्षः प्रीणय मे देहम् चिरम् आहार वर्जितम्
translation:
"O gigantic monkey! Where are you going? You are my requisite food, hungry as I am. Gratify 
my person, who has remained without sustenance for long."

shloka:
बाढम् इति एव ताम् वाणीम् प्रत्यगृह्णाम् अहम् ततः |
आस्य प्रमाणात् अधिकम् तस्याः कायम् अपूरयम्
translation:
"Saying 'Amen', I actually accepted those words. Thereupon, I expanded my body to a size 
larger than the capacity of her mouth."

shloka:
तस्याः च आस्यम् महत् भीमम् वर्धते मम भक्षणे |
न च माम् सा तु बुबुधे मम वा विकृतम् कृतम्
translation:
"Her terrific large mouth too began to grow to devour me. She could not understand well 
about me or about the change subsequently gone through by me (in the shape of a minute form)"

shloka:
ततो अहम् विपुलम् रूपम् सम्क्षिप्य निमिष अन्तरात् |
तस्या हृदयम् आदाय प्रपतामि नभः तलम्
translation:
"Then, having contracted my large body within another moment, I extracted her heart and 
leapt back into the sky."

shloka:
सा विसृष्ट भुजा भीमा पपात लवण अम्भसि |
मया पर्वत सम्काशा निकृत्त हृदया सती
translation:
"When her heart has been cut off by me, that terrific Simhika looking like a mountain, 
fell into the ocean with her arms emanating from it."

shloka:
शृणोमि ख गतानाम् च सिद्धानाम् चारणैः सह |
राक्षसी सिम्हिका भीमा क्षिप्रम् हनुमता हृता
translation:
"I heard great sages along with wandering celestial singers, moving in the sky, saying 
that Simhika the dreadful demon was instantly killed by Hanuma."

shloka:
ताम् हत्वा पुनः एव अहम् कृत्यम् आत्ययिकम् स्मरन् |
गत्वा च महत् अध्वानम् पश्यामि नग मण्डितम्
translation:
"After killing her and again recollecting the task to be performed quickly, I travelled 
for a long distance and saw the southern shore of the ocean, where that City of Lanka, adorned with 
its trees, was situated."

shloka: अस्तम् दिन करे याते रक्षसाम् निलयम् पुरीम्
translation:
"While the sun was setting, I, without being noticed by the demons of dreadful prowess, 
entered the city of Lanka, the abode of demons."

shloka: तत्र प्रविशतश्चापि कल्पान्तघनसन्निभा
translation:
"While I was entering the City, a woman, resembling a cloud at the time of dissolution 
of the world, stood up in front of me, emitting a loud laughter."

shloka: जिघांसन्तीम् ततस्ताम् तु ज्वलदग्निशिरोरुहाम्
translation:
"Then defeating that woman, having her hair looking terrific like a blazing fire and 
who was trying to kill me, by striking her with a blow of the fist of my left hand and entered the land 
of Lanka at the dusk of early night. she, being frightened, spoke to me as follows:

shloka:
अहम् लङ्कापुरी वीर निर्जिता विक्रमेण ते |
यस्मात्तस्माद्विजेतासि सर्वरक्षांस्यशेषतः
translation:
"O hero! I am (the personified) City of Lanka. Therefore, by the same prowess you conquered 
me, you can defeat all the demons here completely."

shloka:
तत्र अहम् सर्व रात्रम् तु विचिन्वन् जनक आत्मजाम् |
रावण अन्तः पुर गतो न च अपश्यम् सुमध्यमाम्
translation:
"Searching there for Seetha that whole night in Ravana's gynaecium, I could not find 
that Seetha, the slender-waisted lady."

shloka:
ततः सीताम् अपश्यन् तु रावणस्य निवेशने |
शोक सागरम् आसाद्य न पारम् उपलक्षये
translation:
"Unable to find Seetha in Ravana's dwelling and facing a sea of sorrow, I could not then 
perceive its other shore."

shloka:
शोचता च मया दृष्टम् प्राकारेण समावृतम् |
कान्चनेन विकृष्टेन गृह उपवनम् उत्तमम्
translation:
"While bemoaning, I saw an excellent grove near that gynaecium, concealed by a prolonged 
fence painted with golden colour."

shloka:
स प्राकारम् अवप्लुत्य पश्यामि बहु पादपम् |
अशोक वनिका मध्ये शिंशपा पादपो महान्
translation:
Crossing the fence, I saw that grove having copious trees. Amidst that Ashoka garden, 
I saw a large Shimshupa* garden. After ascending it, I beheld an yellow-pigmented thicket of banana 
plants."

shloka: अदूरात् शिंशपा वृक्षात् पश्यामि वन वर्णिनीम्
translation:
"Not far from that Shimshupa tree. I saw Seetha, of youthful complexion, with eyes looking 
like lotus-petals, with her face emaciated by fasting, clad in a single piece of cloth, her hair soiled 
with dust, her limbs afflicted with grief and agony, devoted as she was to the good of her lord and 
surrounded on all sides by ugly and cruel female-demons living on flesh and blood, as a doe encircled 
by tigresses."

shloka: सा मया राक्षसीमध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुर्महुः
translation:
"Seetha, who had eyes like those of a deer, was somehow quickly found by me looking depressed 
in the amidst of female-demons, frightened (as she was by them) again and again, putting on a single 
braid of hair (as a mark of desolation), wholly devoted to the thought of her lord, having floor as 
her bedstead, pale-limbed like a lotus-stalk in a cool season, turning away the request of Ravana, and 
determined to die."

shloka:
ताम् दृष्ट्वा तादृशीम् नारीम् राम पत्नीम् अनिन्दिताम् |
तत्र एव शिंशपा वृक्षे पश्यन्न् अहम् अवस्थितः
translation:
"Seeing that illustrious woman, the consort of Rama in such a state, I stayed perched 
on the same Simsupa tree, looking at her."

shloka:
ततो हलहला शब्दम् कान्ची नूपुर मिश्रितम् |
शृणोमि अधिक गम्भीरम् रावणस्य निवेशने
translation:
"Meanwhile, I heard an exceedingly roaring and hallooing sound, mixed with sounds of 
girdles and anklets in the abode of Ravana."

shloka:
ततो अहम् परम उद्विग्नः स्वरूपम् प्रत्यसम्हरम् |
अहम् च शिंशपा वृक्षे पक्षी इव गहने स्थितः
translation:
"Then, I was very much frightened and contracted my physique. I, on my part, remained 
hidden like a bird in that Simsupa tree dense with foliage.'"

shloka:
ततो रावण दाराः च रावणः च महाबलः |
तम् देशम् समनुप्राप्ता यत्र सीता अभवत् स्थिता
translation: "Then, the mighty Ravana and his wives reached that place where Seetha was staying."

shloka:
तम् दृष्ट्वा अथ वराअरोहा सीता रक्षो गण ईश्वरम् |
सम्कुच्य ऊरू स्तनौ पीनौ बाहुभ्याम् परिरभ्य च
translation:
"Thereupon, seeing that Ravana the chief of a troop of demons, Seetha with her lovely 
waist, sat compressing her thighs enclosing her swollen breasts with her arms."

shloka:
वित्रस्ताम् परमोद्विग्नाम् वीक्षमाणामितस्ततः |
त्राणम् किंचिदपश्यन्तीम् वेपमानाम् तपस्विनीम्
translation:
"Ravana, bowing his head and coming down, spoke (as follows) to that Seetha who was frightened, 
very much grieving for her lord, glancing hither and thither, not finding any protection for her, trembling, 
distressed and extremely sorrowful saying, 'Treat me with respect.'"

shloka:
यदि चेत् त्वम् तु माम् दर्पान् न अभिनन्दसि गर्विते |
द्वौ मास अनन्तरम् सीते पास्यामि रुधिरम् तव
translation:
" 'O arrogant lady! O Seetha! If you refuse me by your arrogance, I will be drinking 
your blood after a period of two months.'"

shloka:
एतत् श्रुत्वा वचः तस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः |
उवाच परम क्रुद्धा सीता वचनम् उत्तमम्
translation:
"Hearing those words of the evil-minded Ravana, Seetha was very much irritated and spoke 
the following excellent words:

shloka:
राक्षस अधम रामस्य भार्याम् अमित तेजसः |
इक्ष्वाकु कुल नाथस्य स्नुषाम् दशरथस्य च
translation:
"How did your tongue not fall of, O the worst demon, by speaking such words not to be 
uttered, to the consort of Rama, of boundless glory, and the daughter-in-law of Dasaratha the lord of 
Ikshvaku dynasty?"

shloka: किंस्वित् वीर्यम् तव अनार्य यो माम् भर्तुः असम्निधौ
translation:
"O ignoble soul! Of what account is your prowess, when you came unnoticed during the 
absence of my lord, that great soul and abducted me, O sinful one?"

shloka: न त्वम् रामस्य सदृशो दास्ये अपि अस्या न युज्यसे
translation:
" 'You have no similarity with Rama. You are unfit even to do service to Rama. Rama performs 
sacrifices. He speaks only truth. He is a lover of battle'."

shloka: जानक्या परुषम् वाक्यम् एवम् उक्तो दश आननः
translation:
"Hearing these harsh words from Seetha, Ravana was at once ablaze with anger, as a fire 
blazes in a pile of wood."

shloka: विवृत्य नयने क्रूरे मुष्टिम् उद्यम्य दक्षिणम्
translation:
" 'Rolling his cruel eyes and lifting his right fist, Ravana was about to kill Seetha. 
Then, an alarm was raised by a women there'."

shloka: स्त्रीणाम् मध्यात् समुत्पत्य तस्य भार्या दुरात्मनः
translation:
"Springing up from the midst of those women, a royal woman named Mandodari, the wife 
of that evil-minded Ravana, ran to him. He was restrained by her."

shloka: उक्तः च मधुराम् वाणीम् तया स मदन अर्दितः
translation:
"She spoke to Ravana, smitten with love, the following sweet words: 'O Ravana having 
a prowess similar to that of Indra! Of what need is with Seetha to you?"

shloka: देव गन्धर्व कन्याभिः यक्ष कन्याभिः एव च
translation:
" 'O lord! Enjoy yourself with the daughters of gods, Gandharvas the celestial musicians 
and Yakshas the semi-divine beings. What will you do with Seetha?'"

shloka: ततः ताभिः समेताभिः नारीभिः स महाबलः
translation:
"Thereupon, those women together propitiated that mighty Ravana and quickly took him 
to his palace."

shloka: याते तस्मिन् दशग्रीवे राक्षस्यो विकृत आननाः
translation:
"When that Ravana left, the ugly-faced female-demons frightened. Seetha with their cruel 
and very dreadful words."

shloka: तृणवत् भाषितम् तासाम् गणयामास जानकी
translation:
"Seetha reckoned the utterance of those women as a blade of grass. At that time, the 
roaring of those female-demons reached Seetha in vain."

shloka: वृथा गर्जित निश्चेष्टा राक्षस्यः पिशित अशनाः
translation:
"As their roaring frittered away, those flesh-eating female-demons became helpless and 
reported that great resolve of Seetha to Ravana."

shloka: ततः ताः सहिताः सर्वा विहत आशा निरुद्यमाः
translation:
"Thereafter, all those women joined together, warded off their hopes and held back their 
effort. In the end, they encircled Seetha and were overpowered with sleep."

shloka: तासु चैव प्रसुप्तासु सीता भर्तृ हिते रता
translation:
"When those women went to sleep, Seetha, intent upon the welfare of her husband, was 
deeply aggrieved, miserable and sore depressed as she was, lamenting pitifully."

shloka: तासाम् मध्यात्समुत्थाय त्रिजटा वाक्यमब्रवीत्
translation:
"Trijata, rising from the midst of those female-demons, spoke the following words; 'Feed 
on yourself quickly rather than on Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, a virtuous woman and the daughter-in-law 
of Dasartha who des not get destroyed'."

shloka:
स्वप्नो ह्यद्य मया दृष्टो दारुणो रोमहर्षणः |
रक्षसाम् च विनाशाय भर्तुरस्या जयाय च
translation:
"'Now, I have seen a dreadful dream, causing my hair to stand erect. It is pointing towards 
the ruin of our demons and the victory of her husband."

shloka:
अलमस्मात्परित्रातुम् राघवाद्रक्षसीगणम् |
अभियाचाम वैदेहीमेतद्धि मम रोचते
translation:
" �We will pray Seetha, who is capable of protecting all our female-demons from Rama. 
I feel that it is batter for us'."

shloka:
यस्या ह्येवम्विधः स्वप्नो दुःखितायाः प्रदृश्यते |
सा दुःखैर्विविधैर्मुक्ता सुखमाप्नोत्यनुत्तमम्
translation:
" 'When such a dream is seen while a woman is weeping, that woman gets relieved of many 
kinds of sorrows and will obtain happiness. Seetha, the daughter of Janaka, indeed will be pleased on 
receiving a salutation'."

shloka: ततह् सा ह्रीमती बाला भर्तुर्विजयहर्षिता
translation:
"Delighted at hearing the victory of her lord, that girl Seetha then basfully spoke: 
'If it is true, I will be protecting you all'."

shloka:
ताम् च अहम् तादृशीम् दृष्ट्वा सीताया दारुणाम् दशाम् |
चिन्तयामास विश्रान्तो न च मे निर्वृतम् मनः
translation:
"Taking rest for some time and seeing such a dreadful state of Seetha, I reflected upon 
it. My mind could not satisfy itself."

shloka: सम्भाषण अर्थे च मया जानक्याः चिन्तितो विधिः
translation:
"Thinking about a means for starting a conversation with Seetha, I started to describe 
the history of Ikshvaku's dynasty."

shloka: श्रुत्वा तु गदिताम् वाचम् राज ऋषि गण पूजिताम्
translation:
"Hearing the words spoken by me, which are adored by the assemblies of royal sages, Seetha 
the princess, with her eyes filled with tears, spoke to me, as follows:"

shloka: कः त्वम् केन कथम् च इह प्राप्तो वानर पुम्गव
translation:
" 'O the foremost among the monkeys! Who are you? Why did you come here? How did you 
come? What type of friendship do you have with Rama? You ought to tell me all this?"

shloka: तस्याः तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा अहम् अपि अब्रुवम् वचः
translation:
"Hearing those words of Seetha, I spoke the following words: 'O princess! There is a 
courageous king of monkeys, by name Sugreeva, who is a mighty companion to your husband, possessing 
a terrific prowess."

shloka:
तस्य माम् विद्धि भृत्यम् त्वम् हनूमन्तम् इह आगतम् |
भर्त्रा अहम् प्रहितः तुभ्यम् रामेण अक्लिष्ट कर्मणा
translation:
"Know me, who came here, as Hanuma, a servant of that Sugreeva, Rama, you husband, who 
is unwearied in his actions, sent me here for your sake."

shloka:
इदम् च पुरुष व्याघ्रः श्रीमान् दाशरथिः स्वयम् |
अन्गुलीयम् अभिज्ञानम् अदात् तुभ्यम् यशस्विनि
translation:
"O illustrious lady! Rama, the foremost among men and the glorious man, gave this finger-ring 
personally to you as a token of remembrance."

shloka:
तत् इच्छामि त्वया आज्ञप्तम् देवि किम् करवाणि अहम् |
राम लक्ष्मणयोः पार्श्वम् नयामि त्वाम् किम् उत्तरम्
translation:
"O princess! For that reason, I wish to have a command from you. What am I to do? I shall 
take you to the proximity of Rama and Lakshmana. What do you say?"

shloka:
एतत् श्रुत्वा विदित्वा च सीता जनक नन्दिनी |
आह रावणम् उत्साद्य राघवो माम् नयतु इति
translation:
"Hearing my words and understanding them, Seetha the daughter of Janaka said as follows: 
'Let Rama take me back, after killing Ravana'."

shloka:
प्रणम्य शिरसा देवीम् अहम् आर्याम् अनिन्दिताम् |
राघवस्य मनो ह्लादम् अभिज्ञानम् अयाचिषम्
translation:
"Bowing my head in salutation to the noble and irreproachable Seetha, I asked for a token 
of remembrance which would gladden the heart of Rama."

shloka:
अथ मामब्रवीत्सीता गृह्यतामयम्त्तमः |
मणिर्येन महाबाहू रामस्त्वाम् बहुमन्यते
translation:
"Then, Seetha spoke to me as follows: 'Let this foremost jewel, be taken, by which the 
long-armed Rama will be having a high opinion of you'."

shloka:
एवम् उक्ता वराअरोहा मणि प्रवरम् उत्तमम् |
प्रायच्छत् परम उद्विग्ना वाचा माम् संदिदेश ह
translation:
"Speaking thus, Seetha having fine hips, gave that wonderful and the foremost jewel. 
Highly distressed, she gave a message also in words to me."

shloka:
ततः तस्यै प्रणम्य अहम् राज पुत्र्यै समाहितः |
प्रदक्षिणम् परिक्रामम् इह अभ्युद्गत मानसः
translation:
"Then, offering salutation to Seetha the princess in utmost devotion, I circumambulated 
her from left to right, of course with my mind setting out to come here."

shloka:
उत्तरम् पुनः एव आह निश्चित्य मनसा तदा |
हनूमन् मम वृत्त अन्तम् वक्तुम् अर्हसि राघवे
translation:
"Determining something in mind, she spoke to me again as follows: 'O Hanuma! You ought 
to tell Rama about my tale of woes occurring here'."

shloka:
यथा श्रुत्वा एव नचिरात् ताव् उभौ राम लक्ष्मणौ |
सुग्रीव सहितौ वीराव् उपेयाताम् तथा कुरु
translation:
" 'Act so that both those heroes Rama and Lakshmana together with Sugreeva quickly arrive 
here, soon after hearing my tale'."

shloka:
यदि अन्यथा भवेत् एतत् द्वौ मासौ जीवितम् मम |
न माम् द्रक्ष्यति काकुत्स्थो म्रिये सा अहम् अनाथवत्
translation:
"'If proves to be otherwise, my survival will be only for two months. Rama cannot see 
me thereafter. As such, I will be dying like a helpless woman'."

shloka:
तत् श्रुत्वा करुणम् वाक्यम् क्रोधो माम् अभ्यवर्तत |
उत्तरम् च मया दृष्टम् कार्य शेषम् अनन्तरम्
translation:
"Hearing those miserable words, I became angry. Thereafter, I thought of my remaining 
successive action to be done."

shloka:
ततो अवर्धत मे कायः तदा पर्वत सम्निभः |
युद्ध कान्क्षी वनम् तच् च विनाशयितुम् आरभे
translation:
"Thereafter, my body grew up to a size equal to that of a mountain. Then, I started destroying 
that garden, thereby longing for a combat."

shloka:
तत् भग्नम् वन षण्डम् तु भ्रान्त त्रस्त मृग द्विजम् |
प्रतिबुद्धा निरीक्षन्ते राक्षस्यो विकृत आननाः
translation:
"The female-demons; with their ugly faces woke up and saw that thicket of garden being 
broken and with its frightened animals and birds moving about unsteadily."

shloka:
माम् च दृष्ट्वा वने तस्मिन् समागम्य ततः ततः |
ताः समभ्यागताः क्षिप्रम् रावणाय आचचक्षिरे
translation:
"Coming from their respective places and seeing me in that garden, those female-demons 
quickly went and reported the matter to Ravana (as follows):"

shloka:
राजन् वनम् इदम् दुर्गम् तव भग्नम् दुरात्मना |
वानरेण हि अविज्ञाय तव वीर्यम् महाबल
translation:
"O mighty king! Indeed not knowing your prowess, an evil-minded monkey ahs demolished 
your inaccessible garden."

shloka:
दुर्बुद्धेः तस्य राज इन्द्र तव विप्रिय कारिणः |
वधम् आज्ञापय क्षिप्रम् यथा असौ विलयम् व्रजेत्
translation:
"O emperor! Give orders quickly for killing him, so that the evil-minded monkey, who 
caused offence to you, will get destroyed."

shloka:
तत् श्रुत्वा राक्षस इन्द्रेण विसृष्टा भृश दुर्जयाः |
राक्षसाः किम्करा नाम रावणस्य मनो अनुगाः
translation:
"Hearing those words, Ravana sent invincible demons called Kinkaras, who were adapted 
to the mind of Ravana."

shloka:
तेषाम् अशीति साहस्रम् शूल मुद्गर पाणिनाम् |
मया तस्मिन् वन उद्देशे परिघेण निषूदितम्
translation:
"In that portion of the garden, I destroyed with an iron rod, eight thousand kinkaras, 
having darts and hammers in their hands."

shloka:
तेषाम् तु हत शेषा ये ते गता लघु विक्रमाः |
निहतम् च मया सैन्यम् रावणाय आचचक्षिरे
translation:
"Taking quick steps, those few who have survived, went and reported the news to Ravana, 
of their large army having been killed by me."

shloka:
ततो मे बुद्धिः उत्पन्ना चैत्य प्रासादम् आक्रमम् |
तत्रस्थान् राक्षसान् हत्वा शतम् स्तम्भेन वै पुनः
translation:
"Then, an idea came to me. Occupying a lofty palatial mansion of a sanctuary which was 
an eminent ornament of Lanka. I killed again a hundred demons stationed there with a pillar."

shloka: ततः प्रहस्तस्य सुतम् जम्बु मालिनम् आदिशत्
translation:
"Then, Ravana dispatched Jambumali, the son of Prahasta together with numerous dreadful 
demons having terrific forms."

shloka: तम् अहम् बल सम्पन्नम् राक्षसम् रण कोविदम्
translation:
"I destroyed that demon, though endowed with a great strength and skilled in warfare, 
along with his followers, with my terrific iron bar itself."

shloka: तत् श्रुत्वा राक्षस इन्द्रः तु मन्त्रि पुत्रान् महाबलान्
translation:
"Hearing of it, Ravana, the king of demons, dispatched the son of his minister, endowed 
with great strength and strengthened with a regiment of infantry."

shloka: परिघेण एव तान् सर्वान् नयामि यम सादनम्
translation:
"I killed all of them also by that iron bar itself. Hearing of the minster's sons, who 
were quick in exhibiting their valour in battle, having been killed, Ravana dispatched five valiant 
generals."

shloka:
तान् अहम् सह सैन्यान् वै सर्वान् एव अभ्यसूदयम् |
ततः पुनः दशग्रीवः पुत्रम् अक्षम् महाबलम्
translation:
"I got all the minster's sons together with their army destroyed. Then, Ravana, the ten-headed 
monster, sent his mighty son, Aksha together with a multitude of army for the combat."

shloka: तम् तु मन्द उदरी पुत्रम् कुमारम् रण पण्डितम्
translation:
"I suddenly caught by the feet, that prince, son of Mandodari, who was skilled in warfare 
and who was jumping into the sky with his sword and shield. I whirled him round a hundred times and 
crushed him."

shloka:
तम् अक्षम् आगतम् भग्नम् निशम्य स दश आननः |
तत इन्द्रजितम् नाम द्वितीयम् रावणः सुतम्
translation:
"Hearing of the death of Aksha in combat, that ten-headed Ravana was very much enraged 
and thereupon dispatched his second son, by name Indrajit, who was strong but foolishly arrogant in 
battle."

shloka: तस्य अपि अहम् बलम् सर्वम् तम् च राक्षस पुम्गवम्
translation:
"By conquering all that army in battle and making that Indrajit the foremost among demons; 
lusterless, I experienced a great joy."

shloka: महता हि महाबाहुः प्रत्ययेन महाबलः
translation:
"Ravana himself dispatched, with a great confidence, that long-armed and mighty Indrajit 
along with valiant demons excited with their arrogance."

shloka:
सोऽविषह्यम् हि माम् बुद्ध्वा स्वम् बलम् चावमर्दितम् |
ब्राह्मेण अस्त्रेण स तु माम् प्रबध्नाच् च अतिवेगतः
translation:
"Knowing me to be irresistible and his own army being perishable, that Indrajit with 
a great haste, captured me with a Brahma-missile."

shloka: रज्जूभिः अभिबध्नन्ति ततो माम् तत्र राक्षसाः
translation:
"Then, the demons, after capturing me, tied me there with ropes and carried me away to 
Ravana's presence."

shloka: दृष्ट्वा सम्भाषितः च अहम् रावणेन दुरात्मना
translation:
"Seeing me, the evil-minded Ravana spoke to me. He asked, why did you come to Lanka? 
'Why did you kill the demons?'"

shloka: तत् सर्वम् च मया तत्र सीता अर्थम् इति जल्पितम्
translation:
"I answered 'I have done all these acts for the sake of Seetha. O king of demons! I came 
to your abode with a desire to see Seetha. I am the offspring of wind-god and a monkey by name Hanuma'."

shloka:
राम दूतम् च माम् विद्धि सुग्रीव सचिवम् कपिम् |
सो अहम् दौत्येन रामस्य त्वत् समीपम् इह आगतः
translation:
" 'Know me to be a monkey, an envoy of Rama and a minister of Sugreeva. As Rama's messenger, 
I sought your presence here!"

shloka:
सुग्रीवश्च महातेजाः स त्वाम् कुशलमब्रवीत् |
धर्मार्थकामसहितम् हितम् पथ्यमुवाच च
translation:
" �That Sugreeva of great splendour enquired about your welfare. He told you (the following) 
beneficiary words, endowed with righteousness wealth and pleasure, appropriate for you'."

shloka:
वसतो ऋष्यमूके मे पर्वते विपुल द्रुमे |
राघवो रण विक्रान्तो मित्रत्वम् समुपागतः
translation:
" 'While I was dwelling in Mount R^ishyamuka, abounding with numerous trees, Rama having 
a great prowess in battle became a friend to me'."

shloka:
तेन मे कथितम् राजन् भार्या मे रक्षसा हृता |
तत्र साहाय्य हेतोः मे समयम् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
translation:
" 'The king Rama told me that his wife had been taken away by a demon and that I had 
to help him in that matter by all means'."

shloka:
मया च कथितम् तस्मै वालिनश्च वधम् प्रति |
तत्र साहय्यहेतोर्मे समयम् कर्तुमर्हसि
translation:
" 'I also told him about the killing of Vali and requested him to come to a mutual agreement 
for helping me in that matters'."

shloka:
वालिना हृत राज्येन सुग्रीवेण सह प्रभुः |
चक्रे अग्नि साक्षिकम् सक्यम् राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः
translation:
" 'Rama, the great lord along with Lakshmana made friendship with Sugreeva, (whose kingdom 
was taken away by Vali) taking Agni the fire-god for a witness.'

shloka:
तेन वालिनम् उत्साद्य शरेण एकेन सम्युगे |
वानराणाम् महाराजः कृतः सम्प्लवताम् प्रभुः
translation:
" 'Killing Vali by a single arrow in combat, Rama made Sugreeva (lord of monkeys) an 
emperor of monkeys'."

shloka:
तस्य साहाय्यम् अस्माभिः कार्यम् सर्व आत्मना तु इह |
तेन प्रस्थापितः तुभ्यम् समीपम् इह धर्मतः
translation:
" 'Now we have to extend help to that Rama in all ways. Therefore, I am sending Hanuma 
rightly to your presence'."

shloka:
क्षिप्रम् आनीयताम् सीता दीयताम् राघवस्य च |
यावन् न हरयो वीरा विधमन्ति बलम् तव
translation:
" 'Even before the heroic monkeys destroy your army, bring Seetha quickly and give her 
back to Rama'."

shloka:
वानराणाम् प्रभवो हि न केन विदितः पुरा |
देवतानाम् सकाशम् च ये गच्छन्ति निमन्त्रिताः
translation:
" 'To whom is this strength of the monkeys not already known, who go even to the presence 
of gods, when invited by them for help?'"

shloka:
इति वनर राजः त्वाम् आह इति अभिहितो मया |
माम् ऐक्षत ततो रुष्टः चक्षुषा प्रदहन्न् इव
translation:
" 'Sugreeva the king of monkeys has sent the foregoing message to you. 'When spoken by 
me in these words, Ravana was enraged and looked on me, as though he was going to reduce me to ashes 
with his very looks."

shloka:
तेन वध्यो अहम् आज्ञप्तो रक्षसा रौद्र कर्मणा |
मत्र्पभावमविज्ञाय रावणेन दुरात्मना
translation:
"Without knowing my glory ( in the form of my immunity to death), the evil-minded Ravana, 
the demon doing terrific acts, ordered for my killing."

shloka:
ततो विभीषणो नाम तस्य भ्राता महामतिः |
तेन राक्षस राजो असौ याचितो मम कारणात्
translation:
"Then, there is the brother of that Ravana, called Vibhishana having a great intelligence. 
He entreated Ravana, the king of demons, on my behalf (as follows)"

shloka:
नैवम् राक्षसशार्दूल त्यज्यतामेष निश्चयः |
राजशास्त्रव्यपेतो हि मार्गः संसेव्यते त्वया
translation:
"O Ravana the foremost among the demons! No such attempt should be made in this way. 
Let this design be abandoned forthwith. Your are indeed following a path which is contrary to the statesmanship."

shloka:
दूत वध्या न दृष्टा हि राज शास्त्रेषु राक्षस |
दूतेन वेदितव्यम् च यथा अर्थम् हित वादिना
translation:
"O Ravana! It is not indeed found in states' policies of killing an envoy. The real truth 
is to be known from an envoy speaking a good counsel."

shloka:
सुमहति अपराधे अपि दूतस्य अतुल विक्रमः |
विरूप करणम् दृष्टम् न वधो अस्ति इह शास्त्रतः
translation:
"O Ravana of great prowess! Even if a very high offence is committed by an envoy, an 
act of disfiguring the person is mentioned in a treatise of state-policy and not of killing."

shloka:
विभीषणेन एवम् उक्तो रावणः संदिदेश तान् |
राक्षसान् एतत् एव अद्य लान्गूलम् दह्यताम् इति
translation: "Hearing the words of Vibhishana, Ravana ordered those demons to burn my tail by fire."

shloka:
ततः स्तस्य वचः श्रुत्वा मम पुच्छम् समन्ततः |
वेष्टितम् शण वक्लैः च पटैः कार्पासकैः तथा
translation:
"Thereupon, hearing Ravana's words; the demons wrapped up my entire tail with bark of 
hemp and torn cotton-clothes."

shloka:
राक्षसाः सिद्ध सम्नाहाः ततः ते चण्ड विक्रमाः |
तत् आदीप्यन्त मे पुच्छम् हनन्तः काष्ठ मुष्टिभिः
translation:
"Thereafter, the demons of terrible prowess, who completed their arrangements, striking 
me with their wooden staffs and fists, burnt my tail. Eventhough I was bound with many ropes, I maintained 
restraint."

shloka: ततः ते राक्षसाः शूरा बद्धम् माम् अग्नि सम्वृतम्
translation:
"Then, having reached the city-gate, those strong demons made a loud proclamation of 
my presence in the principal streets, bound and enveloped in flames as I was."

shloka: ततो अहम् सुमहत् रूपम् सम्क्षिप्य पुनः आत्मनः
translation:
"Then, after contracting my gigantic form once more and releasing my bondage, I stood 
in my native form again. Seizing an iron bar, I killed those demons."

shloka:
ततः तन् नगर द्वारम् वेगेन आप्लुतवान् अहम् |
पुच्छेन च प्रदीप्तेन ताम् पुरीम् साट्ट गोपुराम्
translation:
"Then, I quickly jumped on to that city-gate and without any bewilderment, I set fire 
that city with its attics, ramparts and gates with my tail inflamed, even as a fire at the end of the 
world, burns all living creatures."

shloka: विनष्टा जानकी व्यक्तम् न ह्यदग्धः प्रदृश्यते
translation:
"The entire Lanka has been reduced to ashes. No place is seen unburnt in this City. Therefore 
Seetha also must have been surely burnt."

shloka: इति शोकसमाविष्टश्चन्तामहमुपागतः
translation:
"Thus filled with grief, I came about to reflect as above. Meanwhile, I heard the auspiciously 
worded utterance of charanas the celestial signers who were narrating a tale of astonishment saying 
that Seetha has not been burnt."

shloka:
ततो मे बुद्धिः उत्पन्ना श्रुत्वा ताम् अद्भुताम् गिरम् |
अदग्धा जानकीत्येवम् निमित्तैश्चोपलक्षिता
translation:
"After hearing those surprising words, a thought arose in me that Seetha escaped being 
burnt. This indicated by the following good omens:

shloka:
दीप्यमाने तु लाङ्गूले न माम् दहति पावकः |
हृदयम् च प्रहृष्टम् मे वाताः सुरभिगन्धिनः ५-५८-१६१
translation:
"In the first place, even though me tail is burning, the fire is not burning my body. 
My heart too is delighted. The winds are sweet-smelling."

shloka:
तैर्निमित्तैश्च दृष्टार्थैः कारणैश्च महागुणैः |
ऋषिवाक्यैश्च सिद्धार्थैरभवम् हृष्टमानसः
translation:
"My heart was delighted by seeing those good omens having their fruits apparent, by looking 
into the their fruits apparent, by looking into the reasons of high characteristics and by hearing the 
words of accomplished sages."

shloka:
पुनः दृष्टा च वैदेही विसृष्टः च तया पुनः |
ततः पर्वतमासाद्य तत्ररिष्तमहम् पुनः
translation:
"Seeing Seetha once more, relieved by her again and then reaching the Mount Arishta there 
again, I started leaping back (over the sea) with a longing to see you (all)."

shloka: ततः पवनचन्द्रर्क सिद्धगन्धर्व सेवितम्
translation:
"Then, treading upon the path of the sky, frequented by the wind, the moon, the sun, 
Siddhas the semi-divine beings and Gandharvas the celestial musicians, I saw you all here."

shloka: राघवस्य प्रभावेन भवताम् चैव तेजसा
translation:
"I performed all tasks for accomplishing the purpose of Sugreeva, by the grace of Rama 
and also through your energy."

shloka: एतत् सर्वम् मया तत्र यथावत् उपपादितम्
translation:
"I have done all this properly there. Do accomplish that which remains undone in this 
task by me and complete it."

shloka:
एतत् आख्यानम् तत् सर्वम् हनूमान् मारुत आत्मजः |
भूयः समुपचक्राम वचनम् वक्तुम् उत्तरम्
translation:
After informing all this, Hanuma the son of wind-god started telling more of the following 
words.

shloka:
सफलो राघव उद्योगः सुग्रीवस्य च सम्भ्रमः |
शीलम् आसाद्य सीताया मम च प्रवणम् मनः
translation:
"By the power of virtuousness of Seetha, Rama's effort and Sugreeva's zeal are getting 
fulfilled. My mind too is devoted to her."

shloka:
तपसा निर्दहेल्लोकान् स्रुद्धो वा निर्दहेदपि |
सर्वधातिप्रवृद्धोऽसौ रावणो राक्षसाधिपः
translation:
"Ravana, the king of demons, who is strong in all ways, can burn away the three worlds 
by the power of his penance. Even if he is enraged, he can scorch away his adversaries."

shloka:
तस्य ताम् स्पृशतो गात्रम् तपसा न विनाशितम् |
न तदग्निशिखा कुर्यात्संस्पृष्टा पाणिना सती
translation:
"His body, which touched Seetha the daughter of Janaka, was not destroyed because of 
his askesis. Even a flame, when fully touched with one's hand, cannot do that which Seetha would, if 
stirred by anger."

shloka: जाम्बवत्प्रमुखान् सर्वाननुज्ञाप्य महाहरीन्
translation:
"This work (of mine in the form of Seetha's discovery) has been informed to you in this 
way. It is indeed proper to see those two princes (Rama and Lakshmana) along with Seetha, after taking 
permission from all the great monkeys headed by Jambavan.

shloka:
अहमेकोऽपि पर्याप्तः सराक्षसगणाम् पुरीम् |
ताम् लङ्काम् तरसा हन्तुम् रावणम् च महाबलम्
translation:
"I am sufficient, even alone; to destroy rapidly that City of Lanka together with those 
troops of demons as also the mighty Ravana."

shloka:
किम् पुनः सहितो वीरैर्बलवद्भिः कृतात्मभिः |
कृतास्त्रैः प्लवगैः शूरैर्भवद्भिर्विजयैषिभिः
translation:
"When accompanied by you, who are strong, whose spirit is disciplined, who are proficient 
in the use of arms, valiant, longing for victory and moving by jumps, how much more is required?"

shloka:
अहम् तु रावणम् युद्धे ससैन्यम् सपुरःसरम् |
सहपुत्रम् वधिष्यामि सहोदरयुतम् युधि
translation:
"In the battle, I on my part will kill Ravana along with his army, his forerunners, his 
sons and his brothers."

shloka:
ब्रह्ममैन्द्रम् च रौद्रम् च वायव्यम् वारुणम् तथा |
यदि शक्रजोतोऽ स्त्रणि दुर्निरीक्षाणि सम्युगे
translation:
"In the battle, I can blow out the missiles presided over by Indra the lord of celestials, 
Brahma the creator, Rudra the god of destruction, Vayu the wind-god, Varuna the god of water and even 
those missiles even if they are difficult to be looked at, employed by Indrajit (Ravana's eldest son).

shloka: भवतामभ्यनुज्ञातो विक्रमो मे रुणद्धि तम्
translation:
"My prowess, when permitted by you, will frustrate that Ravana. The shower of rocks, 
which will be unequalled and incessant, discharged by me, can kill even celestials. How much more those 
demons?"

shloka:
सागरोऽप्यतियाद्वेलाम् मन्दरः प्रचलेदपि |
न जाम्बवन्तम् समरे कम्पयेदरिवाहिनी
translation:
"The ocean may overflow its shore. Mount Mandara may move from its position. But, in 
battle, no army of adversaries can stagger Jambavan."

shloka:
सर्वराक्षससम्घानाम् राक्षसा ये च महात्मनः |
अलमेको विनाशाय वीरो वालिसुतः कपिः
translation:
"The heroic Angada, the son of Vali alone, is sufficient to destroy all the troops of 
demons and even the demons who were their progenitors."

shloka:
पनसस्योरुवेगेन नीलस्य च महात्मनः |
मन्दरोऽप्यवशीर्येत किम्पुनर्युधि राक्षसाः
translation:
"By the rapid movement of the thighs of the high-souled Neela and of Panasa, even Mount 
Mandara can be shattered. How much more, the demons in battle?"

shloka:
सदेवासुरयक्षेषु गन्धर्वोरगपक्षिषु |
मैन्दस्य प्रतियोद्धारम् शंसत द्विविदस्य वा
translation:
"Tell me any one who can fight against Mainda or Dvivida, among Gandharvas the celestial 
singers or Uragas the serpents or Pakshis the birds or the celestials or the demons or Yakshas the semi-divine 
beings."

shloka:
अश्विपुत्रौ महाभागावेतौ प्लवगसत्तमौ |
एतयोः प्रतियोद्धारम् न पश्यामि रणाजिरे
translation:
"These two illustrious sons of Ashvini Kumaras, Mainda and Dvivida are the foremost among 
the monkeys. In the battle-field, I do not find anyone who can fight against these two monkeys."

shloka:
पितामहवरोत्सेकात्परमम् दर्पमास्थितौ |
अमृतप्राशनावेतौ सर्ववानरसत्तमौ
translation:
"Proud of having received boons from Brahma the creator and their grandfather and abiding 
in a supreme haughtiness, these two foremost among all the monkeys live on Amrita the nectar."

shloka:
अश्विनोर्माननार्थम् हि सर्वलोकपितामहः |
सर्वावध्यत्वमतुलमनयोर्दत्तवान् पुरा
translation:
"Long ago, Brahma the grandfather of all the worlds gave an unequal boon to them in honour 
of Ashvini Kumaras regarding their inviolability."

shloka:
वरोत्सेकेन मत्तौ च प्रमथ्य महतीम् चमूम् |
सुराणाममृतम् वीरौ पीतवन्तौ प्लवम्गमौ
translation:
"By the pride of those boons, those two heroic monkeys harassed a great army of celestials 
and thereupon drank up nectar, excited as they were with joy."

shloka:
एतावेन हि सम्क्रुद्धौ सवाजिरथकुम्जराम् |
लङ्काम् नाशयितुम् शक्तौ सर्वे तिष्ठन्तु वानराः
translation:
"Let all the other monkeys stand aside. Even these Mainda and Dvivida on their part are 
capable of destroying the entire city of Lanka together with its horses, chariots and elephants."

shloka:
मयैव निहता लङ्का दग्धा भस्मीकृता पुनः |
राजमार्गेषु सर्वत्र नाम विश्रावित मया
translation:
"I alone burnt and destroyed the City of Lanka. In all its royal high-ways, the name 
(of Rama and others) was proclaimed by me as follows:

shloka:
जयत्यतिबलो रामो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः |
राजा जयति सुग्रीवो राघवेणाभिपालितः
translation:
"'Victorious is Rama, the exceedingly strong and the mighty Lakshmana too! Victorious 
is King Sugreeva, protected by Rama. I am Hanuma, a servant of Rama and the son of wind-god'. In this 
way, the name (of Rama and others) was heralded by me everywhere."

shloka:
अशोक वनिका मध्ये रावणस्य दुरात्मनः |
अधस्तात् शिंशपा वृक्षे साध्वी करुणम् आस्थिता
translation:
"In the midst of Ashoka garden of the evil-minded Ravana and underneath a Shimshupa tree, 
the virtuous Seetha was seen staying dejected, encircled as she was with female-demons, agonized with 
grief and anguish, lusterless like a digit of the moon encircled by a line of clouds and disregarding 
that Ravana who is arrogant of his strength."

shloka: पति व्रता च सुश्रोणी अवष्टब्धा च जानकी
translation:
"Seetha, a devoted and virtuous wife, having charming hips, has been placed under restraint. 
The auspicious Seetha is devoted to Rama in all ways, giving her undivided thought to Rama like Shachi 
the goddess, giving her concern to Indra the destroyer of strong holds."

shloka:
तत् एक वासः सम्वीता रजो ध्वस्ता तथैव च |
शोक सम्ताप दीन अन्गी सीता भर्तृ हिते रता
translation:
"Weaving that single piece of cloth, which she had on her person even while being borne 
away by Ravana, and likewise covered with dust, she was seen by me in a miserable condition with her 
grief and anguish, devoted as she was to the welfare of her husband."

shloka:
सा मया राक्षसी मध्ये तर्ज्यमाना मुहुः मुहुः |
राक्षसीभिः विरूपाभिः दृष्टा हि प्रमदा वने
translation:
"I saw Seetha in a royal pleasure garden, amidst some female-demons. Seetha was being 
frightened time and again by those ugly female-demons. That Seetha, wearing a single braid of hair and 
looking depressed, was fully engaged in thinking about her lord. Looking like a lotus with a discoloured 
figure in winter, she had determined to die, utterly averting to do anything with Ravana."

shloka: कथंचिन् मृग शाव अक्षी विश्वासम् उपपादिता
translation:
"With great difficulty, I created confidence in that fawn-eyed Seetha. Thereafter, I 
talked to her and explained everything to her. She was delighted to hear the companionship cropped up 
between Rama and Sugreeva."

shloka:
नियतः समुदाचारो भक्तिः भर्तरि च उत्तमा |
यन् न हन्ति दशग्रीवम् स महात्मा कृतागसम्
translation:
"That high-souled Seetha does not kill Ravana who has committed an offence because she 
conducts herself well with restraint and since supreme is her devotion to her lord."

shloka:
निमित्त मात्रम् रामः तु वधे तस्य भविष्यति |
सा प्रकृत्यैव तन्वङ्गी तद्वियोगाच्छ कर्शिता
translation:
"Rama, on his part, will become mere instrument in killing that Ravana. That Seetha, 
who is by her own nature, on delicate-limbed woman, was emaciated because of separation from her lord. 
She had grown thin like the learning of a scholar continuing his studies even on the first day of lunar 
fortnight (which must be observed as a complete holiday by students."

shloka: एवम् आस्ते महाभागा सीता शोक परायणा
translation:
"Thus, the illustrious Seetha remains immersed in grief. Let all that be done, which 
requires to be counteracted by way of a relief in this matter."

shloka:
तस्य तत् वचनम् श्रुत्वा वालि सूनुः अभाषत |
अयुक्तम् तु विना देवीम् दृष्ट्वद्भिश्च वानराः
translation:
Hearing those words of Hanuma, Angada the son of Vali spoke as follows: "Even after our 
seeing of Seetha, it is not proper for us to approach the high-souled Rama without taking Seetha with 
us."

shloka: दृष्टा देवी न च आनीता इति तत्र निवेदनम्
translation:
"I perceive it as improper to inform there that Seetha the princess, though seen by you 
of renowned prowess, has not been brought here."

shloka: न हि वः प्लवते कश्चिन् न अपि कश्चित् पराक्रमे
translation:
"O the best of monkeys! No one is equal to us even in our prowess nor indeed anyone who 
can leap like us in the worlds either of celestials or demons."

shloka: तेष्व् एवम् हत वीरेषु राक्षसेषु हनूमता
translation:
"Hanuma indeed thus killed all the warriors among the demons. What work is remaining 
to be done by us? We will go, after taking Janaki."

shloka: तम् एवम् कृत सम्कल्पम् जाम्बवान् हरि सत्तमः
translation:
Jambavan, the foremost among the forest-animals, understanding the sense, was very much 
pleased and spoke the following meaningful words to that Angada, who thus formed a resolution.

shloka:
न तावत् एषा मतिः अक्षमा नो |
यथा भवान् पश्यति राज पुत्र |
यथा तु रामस्य मतिः निविष्टा |
तथा भवान् पश्यतु कार्य सिद्धिम्
translation:
"O prince! This thought you thus perceive is not incompetent of us. But, you must see 
the way in which Rama's inclination would be, for the accomplishment of the object."

shloka:
ततो जाम्बवतो वाक्यम् अगृह्णन्त वन ओकसः |
अन्गद प्रमुखा वीरा हनूमान् च महाकपिः
translation:
Thereupon, the heroic monkeys like Angada and others as also Hanuma, the great one among 
the monkeys accepted the words of Jambavan.

shloka:
प्रीतिमन्तः ततः सर्वे वायु पुत्र पुरः सराः |
महाइन्द्र अग्रम् परित्यज्य पुप्लुवुः प्लवग ऋषभाः
translation:
Then, the excellent monkeys, resembling Meru and Mandara mountains, like elephants in 
rut, as if covering the sky, having huge bodies and colossal strength, keeping Hanuma in their front, 
leaving Mount Mahendra, went ahead leaping delightfully. They looked as though conducted by the mind's 
eyes of Hanuma, who is adored by living beings as having good stupendous swiftness, they having resolved 
to fulfill the purpose of Rama and to attain a great glory, having accomplished the purpose and duly 
determined to complete the task. All of them were looking up at narrating the previous pleasant tidings 
and taking delight in war. All of them, in high spirits, were judging rightly the vengeance of Rama 
against the evil-minded Ravana.

shloka:
प्लवमानाः खम् आप्लुत्य ततः ते कानन ओक्सकः |
नन्दन उपमम् आसेदुः वनम् द्रुम लता युतम्
translation:
Then, those monkeys, leaping into the sky and floating in the air, reached a garden looking 
like Nandanavana the divine grove filled with trees and creepers.

shloka:
यत् तन् मधु वनम् नाम सुग्रीवस्य अभिरक्षितम् |
अधृष्यम् सर्व भूतानाम् सर्व भूत मनो हरम्
translation:
They reached, that Madhuvana by name, the garden abounded with honey, which was protected 
grove, unapproachable for all and looking fascinated to the soul of all beings.

shloka:
यत् रक्षति महावीर्यः सदा दधि मुखः कपिः |
मातुलः कपि मुख्यस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः
translation:
A very powerful monkey called Dadhimukha, who was a high-souled eminent monkey and the 
maternal uncle of Sugreeva always protected that garden.

shloka:
ते तत् वनम् उपागम्य बभूवुः परम उत्कटाः |
वानरा वानर इन्द्रस्य मनः कान्ततमम् महत्
translation:
Reaching that huge grove, which was very dear to the heart of Sugreeva, those monkeys 
became highly excessive in their behaviour.

shloka:
ततः ते वानरा हृष्टा दृष्ट्वा मधु वनम् महत् |
कुमारम् अभ्ययाचन्त मधूनि मधु पिन्गलाः
translation:
Then, seeing that large Madhuvana, the garden abounded in honey, those monkeys, whose 
colour was as yellow as honey, were delighted and solicited Angada the prince for permission to taste 
the honey.

shloka:
ततः कुमारः तान् वृद्धान् जाम्बवत् प्रमुखान् कपीन् |
अनुमान्य ददौ तेषाम् निसर्गम् मधु भक्षणे
translation:
Thereupon, Angada the prince, taking approval from those elders like Jambavan and others, 
gave the monkeys a liberty to drink honey there.

shloka:
ततः च अनुमताः सर्वे सम्प्रहृष्टा वन ओकसः |
मुदिताः च ततः ते च प्रनृत्यन्ति ततः ततः
translation:
Thereafter, all those monkeys, thus permitted to drink honey, were exceedingly pleased. 
Then, those excited monkeys felt glad and began dancing.

shloka:
गायन्ति केचित् प्रणमन्ति केचिन् |
नृत्यन्ति केचित् प्रहसन्ति केचित् |
पतन्ति केचित् विचरन्ति केचित् |
प्लवन्ति केचित् प्रलपन्ति केचित्
translation:
Some were singing. Some were offering salutations. Some were dancing. Some were laughing 
loudly. Some were falling down. Some were moving in different directions. Some were jumping up. Some 
were talking incoherently.

shloka:
परस्परम् केचित् उपाश्रयन्ते |
परस्परम् केचित् अतिब्रुवन्ते |
परस्परम् केचिदुपब्रुवन्ते |
परस्परम् केचिदुपारमन्ते
translation:
Some were leaning against one another. Some were falling upon one another. Some were 
disputing with one another. Some were playing with one another.

shloka:
द्रुमात् द्रुमम् केचित् अभिप्लवन्ते |
क्षितौ नग अग्रान् निपतन्ति केचित् |
मही तलात् केचित् उदीर्ण वेगा |
महाद्रुम अग्राणि अभिसम्पतन्ते
translation:
Some were running from one tree to another. Some were falling down to the ground from 
the tree-tops. Some, with a missile-like speed, were flying towards the tops of gigantic trees from 
the ground.

shloka:
गायन्तम् अन्यः प्रहसन्न् उपैति |
हसन्तम् अन्यः प्रहसन्न् उपैति |
रुदन्तम् अन्यः प्ररुदन्न् उपैति |
नुदन्तम् अन्यः प्रणुदन्न् उपैति
translation:
While one was singing, another approached him laughing. While one was laughing, another 
approached him weeping. While one was weeping, another approached him pushing. While one was pushing, 
another approached him roaring.

shloka:
समाकुलम् तत् कपि सैन्यम् आसीन् |
मधु प्रपान उत्कट सत्त्व चेष्टम् |
न च अत्र कश्चिन् न बभूव मत्तो |
न च अत्र कश्चिन् न बभूव तृप्तो
translation:
That army of monkeys, moving in excessively honey-drunken state, became highly excited. 
None in that army was not drunk. None in that army was not satiated.

shloka:
ततो वनम् तत् परिभक्ष्यमाणम् |
द्रुमान् च विध्वंसित पत्र पुष्पान् |
समीक्ष्य कोपात् दधि वक्त्र नामा |
निवारयामास कपिः कपीन् तान्
translation:
Seeing that grove, being consumed and the trees stripped off their leaves and flowers 
the monkey named Dadhimukha (who was incharge of the grove) then angrily interrupted those monkeys.

shloka:
स तैः प्रवृद्धैः परिभर्त्स्यमानो |
वनस्य गोप्ता हरि वीर वृद्धः |
चकार भूयो मतिम् उग्र तेजा |
वनस्य रक्षाम् प्रति वानरेभ्यः
translation:
Threatened by those monkeys who were behaving excessively, Dadhimukha who was endowed 
with a terrible energy, the care-taker of the grove and an elderly hero of the monkeys further contemplated 
the means to protect that grove from the monkeys.

shloka:
उवाच कांश्चित् परुषाणि धृष्टम् |
असक्तम् अन्यान् च तलैः जघान |
समेत्य कैश्चित् कलहम् चकार |
तथैव साम्ना उपजगाम कांश्चित्
translation:
He spoke harsh words with some and courageously struck some others with his palms uninterruptedly, 
created a quarrel by coming into collusion with some, and approached some in a conciliatory manner.

shloka:
स तैः मदाच् च अप्रतिवार्य वेगैः |
बलाच् च तेन अप्रतिवार्यमाणैः |
प्रधर्षितः त्यक्त भयैः समेत्य |
प्रकृष्यते च अपि अनवेक्ष्य दोषम्
translation:
That Dadhimukha was dragged, after coming into collusion with him by those monkeys, who 
were being forcibly hindered by him, eventhough those monkeys overpowered him with unrestrained emotion 
arising out of their intoxication, those who had abandoned their fear disregarding any bad consequence 
of their act.

shloka:
नखैः तुदन्तो दशनैः दशन्तः |
तलैः च पादैः च समाप्नुवन्तः |
मदात् कपिम् तम् कपयः समग्रा |
महावनम् निर्विषयम् च चक्रुः
translation:
Bruising with their nails, biting with their teeth on account of their inebriety and 
making short work of that Dadhimukha with their palms and feet, all those moneys made that large grove, 
divested of its flowers, fruits and honey.

shloka:
तान् उवाच हरि श्रेष्ठो हनूमान् वानर ऋषभः |
अव्यग्र मनसो यूयम् मधु सेवत वानराः
translation:
Hanuma, like a bull among the monkeys and the foremost among them spoke to them as follows: 
"Cherish the honey with a cool mind, O monkeys! I will keep off your opposer who is standing in your 
way."

shloka: श्रुत्वा हनुमतो वाक्यम् हरीणाम् प्रवरो अन्गदः
translation:
Hearing the words of Hanuma, the gracious minded Angada the principal among the monkeys 
repeated the words: "Let the monkeys drink the honey."

shloka: अवश्यम् कृत कार्यस्य वाक्यम् हनुमतो मया
translation:
"The words, though improper of Hanuma who had accomplished his task, are to be obliged 
certainly by me. Wherefore then, moreover, on such an occasion?"

shloka: अन्दगस्य मुखात् श्रुत्वा वचनम् वानर ऋषभाः
translation:
Hearing the words coming from the mouth of Angada, those monkeys who were like bulls 
among the monkeys were delighted and answered with reverence, saying 'good, good!'

shloka: पूजयित्वा अन्गदम् सर्वे वानरा वानर ऋषभम्
translation:
Reverencing Angada the foremost among the monkeys, all the monkeys rushed towards Madhuvana, 
the grove abounding in honey, like the rush of a river towards a tree.

shloka: ते प्रहृष्टा मधु वनम् पालान् आक्रम्य वीर्यतः
translation:
Because Hanuma had seen Seetha and others had heard of her and because of the grant of 
permission from Angada, all those gifted monkeys entered Madhuvana the grove, overpowered the guards 
with their prowess, drank honey and the partook juicy fruits there.

shloka:
उत्पत्य च ततः सर्वे वन पालान् समागताः |
ताडयन्ति स्म शतशः सक्तान् मधु वने तदा
translation:
Then, all those monkeys jumped on the guards of the grove, who came there in hundreds 
together and banged them.

shloka:
मधूनि द्रोण मात्राणि बहुभिः परिगृह्य ते |
पिबन्ति सहिताः सर्वे भक्षयन्ति तथा अपरे
translation:
All those monkeys together took vessels of honey in their arms and drank them. Some others 
banged those who obstructed them.

shloka:
केचित् पीत्वा अपविध्यन्ति मधूनि मधु पिन्गलाः |
मधु उच्चिष्टेन केचिच् च जघ्नुः अन्योन्यम् उत्कटाः
translation:
Some monkeys, with their skin-colour as yellow as honey, after drinking vessels of honey, 
also threw some honey away. Some others, with the remnant of honey in their arms, after drinking, whipped 
up one another with their excessive intoxication.

shloka:
अपरे वृक्ष मूलेषु शाखाम् गृह्य व्यवस्थितः |
अत्यर्थम् च मद ग्लानाः पर्णानि आस्तीर्य शेरते
translation:
Some others, seizing a branch of a tree, stood rooted at the foot of a tree. Some, who 
were highly intoxicated, laid down spreading leaves on the ground.

shloka:
उन्मत्त भूताः प्लवगा मधु मत्ताः च हृष्टवत् |
क्षिपन्ति अपि तथा अन्योन्यम् स्खलन्ति अपि तथा अपरे
translation:
Those monkeys, who were intoxicated by drinking the honey, became inebriated and started 
pushing one another cheerfully and some others began to stumble.

shloka:
केचित् क्ष्वेडान् प्रकुर्वन्ति केचित् कूजन्ति हृष्टवत् |
हरयो मधुना मत्ताः केचित् सुप्ता मही तले
translation:
Some were roaring like lions. Some, with joy, whistled like birds. Some monkeys, inebriated 
as they were by drinking honey, simply slept on the floor.

shloka:
कृत्वा केचिर्धसन्त्यन्ये केचित्कुर्वन्ति चेतरत् |
कृत्वा केचिद्वदन्त्यन्ये केचिद्बुध्यन्ति चेतरत्
translation:
Doing something or other, some were laughing. Some others were doing something else. 
Some were telling what they were doing, while some others were understanding some things else.

shloka:
ये अपि अत्र मधु पालाः स्युः प्रेष्या दधि मुखस्य तु |
ते अपि तैः वानरैः भीमैः प्रतिषिद्धा दिशो गताः
translation:
The honey-keepers, who were there as messengers of Dadhimukha in that Madhuvana, were 
warded off by the terrific monkeys and they fled to different directions.

shloka:
जानुभिः च प्रकृष्टाः च देव मार्गम् च दर्शिताः |
अब्रुवन् परम उद्विग्ना गत्वा दधि मुखम् वचः
translation:
Dragged by their knees and tossed up in the air by the monkeys, those honey-keepers were 
very much depressed, went to Dadhimukha and complained as follows:

shloka:
हनूमता दत्त वरैः हतम् मधु वनम् बलात् |
वयम् च जानुभिः कृष्टा देव मार्गम् च दर्शिताः
translation:
"The monkeys, as permitted by Hanuma, violently destroyed Madhuvana. We were dragged 
by our knees and further tossed up in the air."

shloka:
ततो दधि मुखः क्रुद्धो वनपः तत्र वानरः |
हतम् मधु वनम् श्रुत्वा सान्त्वयामास तान् हरीन्
translation:
Hearing that Madhuvana was damaged, Dadhimukha, the grove-protector there was enraged 
and thereafter consoled those monkeys (as follows):

shloka:
इह आगच्छत गच्छामो वानरान् अतिदर्पितान् |
बलेन आवारयिष्यामो मधु भक्षयतो वयम्
translation:
"Come here let us go there and prevent by our force, the monkeys who are arrogant of 
their strength and are consuming the honey."

shloka:
श्रुत्वा दधि मुखस्य इदम् वचनम् वानर ऋषभाः |
पुनः वीरा मधु वनम् तेन एव सहिता ययुः
translation:
Hearing these words of Dadhimukha, the foremost of those monkeys who displayed their 
heroism, quickly went again to madhuvana along with him.

shloka:
मध्ये च एषाम् दधि मुखः प्रगृह्य सुमहातरुम् |
समभ्यधावत् वेगेना ते च सर्वे प्लवम्गमाः
translation:
Grasping a tree, Dadhimukha speedily took up his position in the middle of those monkeys 
in Madhuvana. All his follower-monkeys also ran with him.

shloka:
ते शिलाः पादपान् च अपि पाषाणान् च अपि वानराः |
गृहीत्वा अभ्यागमन् क्रुद्धा यत्र ते कपि कुन्जराः
translation:
Those enraged monkeys, taking rocks, trees and even mountains, went to the place wehre 
those foremost of monkeys were there.

shloka:
ते स्वामि वचनम् वीरा हृदयेष्व् अवसज्य तत् |
त्वरया हि अभ्यधावन्त साल ताल शिला आयुधाः
translation:
Those heroic monkeys, keeping the words of their master in mind, briskly ran with Sala 
trees, palm trees and rocks as their weapons.

shloka:
वृक्षस्थान् च तलस्थान् च वानरान् बल दर्पितान् |
अभ्यक्रामन्त ते वीराः पालाः तत्र सहस्रशः
translation:
Then, the valiant guards of the grove running in thousands invaded the monkeys who were 
on trees, at the foot of the trees and who were arrogant of their strength.

shloka:
अथ दृष्ट्वा दधि मुखम् क्रुद्धम् वानर पुम्गवाः |
अभ्यधावन्त वेगेन हनूमत् प्रमुखाः तदा
translation:
Seeing Dadhimukha coming with anger, Hanuma along with eminent monkeys ran towards him 
with speed.

shloka:
तम् सवृक्षम् महाबाहुम् आपतन्तम् महाबलम् |
आर्यकम् प्राहरत् तत्र बाहुभ्याम् कुपितो अन्गदः
translation:
The enraged Angada struck there with his arms, that long-armed Dadhimukha the maternal 
uncle his father, who was endowed with extraordinary might and who was rushing with speed with a tree 
in his hand.

shloka:
मद अन्धः अ न वेद एनम् आर्यको अयम् मम इति सः |
अथ एनम् निष्पिपेष आशु वेगवत् वसुधा तले
translation:
Blinded with arrogance, that Angada did not show any mercy to him on the score of his 
being the maternal uncle of his father and caused him at once to fall down and began to crush him against 
the ground.

shloka:
स भग्न बाहुः विमुखो विह्वलः शोणित उक्षितः |
मुमोह सहसा वीरो मुहूर्तम् कपि कुन्जरः
translation:
That Dadhimukha, the valiant elephant among the monkeys, who was afflicted with his broken 
arms, thighs and shoulders, drenched as he was in blood, lost his consciousness for a moment.

shloka:
स समाश्वस्य सहसा सम्क्रुद्धो राजमातुलः |
वानरान्वारयामास दण्डेन मधुमोहितान्
translation:
That Dadhimukha, Sugreeva's maternal uncle, quickly recovering his breath, was enraged 
and resisted those monkeys, who were highly intoxicated because of drinking of honey, by a proper reprimand.

shloka:
स कथंचित् विमुक्तः तैः वानरैः वानर ऋषभः |
उवाच एक अन्तम् आगम्य भृत्यान् तान् समुपागतान्
translation:
Somehow released by those monkeys that Dadhimukha the foremost among the monkeys, went 
to a solitary place and spoke to his messengers who came there (as follows):

shloka:
एते तिष्ठन्तु गच्छामो भर्ता नो यत्र वानरः |
सुग्रीवो विपुल ग्रीवः सह रामेण तिष्ठति
translation:
"Let these monkeys stay here. We will go to the place where the thick-necked Sugreeva, 
our lord of the monkeys stays together with Rama."

shloka:
सर्वम् चैव अन्गदे दोषम् श्रावयिष्यामि पार्थिव |
अमर्षी वचनम् श्रुत्वा घातयिष्यति वानरान्
translation:
"I will make known to the king, all the misdeed of Angada. Hearing my words, the enraged 
king will get the monkeys killed."

shloka:
इष्टम् मधु वनम् हि एतत् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः |
पितृ पैतामहम् दिव्यम् देवैः अपि दुरासदम्
translation:
"This Madhuvana is indeed cherished by our high-souled king, Sugreeva and it derived 
from his father and grand father. It is so charming, but is dangerous to be approached even by celestials."

shloka:
स वानरान् इमान् सर्वान् मधु लुब्धान् गत आयुषः |
घातयिष्यति दण्डेन सुग्रीवः ससुहृज् जनान्
translation:
"The longevity of these monkeys got reduced, as they were very much lustful of honey. 
That Sugreeva can get these monkeys together with their companions, killed as a matter of punishment."

shloka:
वध्या हि एते दुरात्मानो नृप आज्ञा परिभाविनः |
अमर्ष प्रभवो रोषः सफलो नो भविष्यति | ५-६२-३५
translation:
"These evil-minded beings, who disregarded the royal command, are fit to be capitally 
punished. Our wrath, springing from our impatience, will indeed become fruitful."

shloka:
एवम् उक्त्वा दधि मुखो वन पालान् महाबलः |
जगाम सहसा उत्पत्य वन पालैः समन्वितः
translation:
Thus speaking to the garden-guards, the mighty Dadhimukha quickly springing up all at 
once, went (to Kishkindha) together with the garden-guards.

shloka:
निमेष अन्तर मात्रेण स हि प्राप्तो वन आलयः |
सहस्र अंशु सुतो धीमान् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः
translation:
That Dadhimukha, the monkey, reached the place where that Sugreeva, the intelligent monkey 
was there, within an interval of only a moment.

shloka:
रामम् च लक्ष्मणम् चैव दृष्ट्वा सुग्रीवम् एव च |
सम प्रतिष्ठाम् जगतीम् आकाशान् निपपात ह
translation:
Seeing Rama, Lakshmana and Sugreeva, Dadhimukha descended to a level ground, from the 
sky.

shloka:
स निपत्य महावीर्यः सर्वैः तैः परिवारितः |
हरिः दधि मुखः पालैः पालानाम् परम ईश्वरः
translation:
That Dadhimukha of a great prowess, the supreme lord of the guards, surrounded by all 
those garden-guards keeping a sad face, made a respectful salutation to Sugreeva with his head, by falling 
down and touching with his head, the auspicious feet of Sugreeva.

shloka:
ततो मूर्ध्ना निपतितम् वानरम् वानर ऋषभः |
दृष्ट्वा एव उद्विग्न हृदयो वाक्यम् एतत् उवाच ह
translation:
Just on seeing Dadhimukha, who fell touching his feet with his head, Sugreeva the chief 
of monkeys, with an agitated mind, spoke the following words:

shloka:
उत्तिष्ठ उत्तिष्ठ कस्मात् त्वम् पादयोः पतितो मम |
अभयम् ते भवेत् वीर सत्यम् एव अभिधीयताम्
translation:
"O valiant monkey! Stand up, rise! Why have you fallen on my feet? I grant you immunity 
from fear. Let the entire truth be spoken!"

shloka:
स तु विश्वासितः तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना |
उत्थाय च महाप्राज्ञो वाक्यम् दधि मुखो अब्रवीत्
translation:
Thus inspired by the high-souled Sugreeva with confidence, that highly intelligent Dadhimukha, 
rising up, spoke the following words:

shloka:
न एव ऋक्ष रजसा राजन् न त्वया न अपि वालिना |
वनम् निसृष्ट पूर्वम् हि भक्षितम् तत् तु वानरैः
translation:
"O king! Madhuvana was indeed not set free previously at any time by Riksharajas, your 
father, or by you, or by even Vali. That Madhuvana has been consumed away by the monkeys."

shloka:
एभिः प्रधर्षिताः च एव वारिता वन रक्षिभिः |
मधूनि अचिन्तयित्वा इमान् भक्षयन्ति पिबन्ति च
translation:
"When these guards of the grove obstructed the monkeys, they disregarded the guards and 
continue to eat the fruits and drink the honey too."

shloka:
शिष्टम् अत्र अपविध्यन्ति भक्षयन्ति तथा अपरे |
निवार्यमाणाः ते सर्वे भ्रुवौ वै दर्शयन्ति हि
translation:
"Some are throwing away a remnant of honey, after drinking it there and some others are 
consuming that remnant. When prevented by us, all of them are indeed exhibiting their eye-brows to us 
(in anger)."

shloka:
इमे हि सम्रब्धतराः तथा तैः सम्प्रधर्षिताः |
वारयन्तो वनात् तस्मात् क्रुद्धैः वानर पुम्गवैः
translation:
"When these guards of the grove became angry and tried to keep them off from the grove, 
those enraged monkeys threatened them."

shloka:
ततः तैः बहुभिः वीरैः वानरैः वानर ऋषभाः |
सम्रक्त नयनैः क्रोधाद्त् हरयः सम्प्रचालिताः
translation:
"O chief of monkeys! Then, those valiant monkeys in large numbers, having their red eyes 
in anger, drove away these monkeys."

shloka:
पाणिभिः निहताः केचित् केचिज् जानुभिः आहताः |
प्रकृष्टाः च यथा कामम् देव मार्गम् च दर्शिताः
translation:
"Those monkeys struck some of the guards with their hands. They beat some of them with 
their knees. They dragged some of them and tossed them into air."

shloka:
एवम् एते हताः शूराः त्वयि तिष्ठति भर्तरि |
कृत्स्नम् मधु वनम् चैव प्रकामम् तैः प्रभक्ष्यते
translation:
"While you are in the position of a king, those monkeys have beaten these valiant guards 
and are eating away the entire Maduvana too."

shloka:
एवम् विज्ञाप्यमानम् तु सुग्रीवम् वानर ऋषभम् |
अपृच्छत् तम् महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणः पर वीरहा
translation:
Lakshmana, the killer of hostile heroes and a very wise man, asked that Sugreeva, the 
excellent of monkeys (as follows) while Dadhimukha was thus reporting to him:

shloka:
किम् अयम् वानरो राजन् वनपः प्रत्युपस्थितः |
कम् च अर्थम् अभिनिर्दिश्य दुह्खितो वाक्यम् अब्रवीत्
translation:
"O king! Why has this monkey the garden-protector, come here?' Pointing out what matter 
has this monkey in grief, spoken these words to you?"

shloka:
एवम् उक्तः तु सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणेन महात्मना |
लक्ष्मणम् प्रत्युवाच इदम् वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारदः
translation:
Hearing the words of the high-souled Lakshmana, the eloquent Sugreeva replied to him 
as follows:

shloka:
आर्य लक्ष्मण सम्प्राह वीरो दधि मुखः कपिः |
अन्गद प्रमुखैः वीरैः भक्षितम् मधु वानरैः
translation:
"O esteemed Lakshmana! Dadhimukha, the valiant monkey is informing that the foremost 
of monkeys, who returned from the southern direction, after searching for Seetha as also Angada and 
other heroes consumed honey."

shloka: न एषाम् अकृत कृत्यानाम् ईदृशः स्यात् उपक्रमः
translation:
"By seeing the manner in which these returned monkeys overpowered, destroyed and behaved 
towards Madhuvana, we can deduce that the monkeys would not have indulged in such an exploit, had they 
not accomplished my purpose."

shloka:
वनम् यथा अभिपन्नम् तैः साधितम् कर्म वानरैः |
दृष्टा देवी न संदेहो न च अन्येन हनूमता
translation:
"When those monkeys have overpowered Madhuvana, then it means that our task has been
